§ 1026.01 SHORT TITLE.
   This chapter shall be known and may be cited as the “Street Tree Ordinance
of the Village of Jefferson” or just the “Street Tree Ordinance.”
(`80 Code, § 1026.01) (Ord. 1028, passed 10-21-68)
§ 1026.02 DEFINITIONS.
   As used in this chapter:
   (a)   ARBORICULTURE and TREE PRESERVATION mean and include the treating,
spraying, pruning, maintaining and any other care or work intended for the
strengthening of trees, and the removal and prevention of tree pests, blights
and diseases of any and all kinds.
   (b)   PUBLIC PLACE means any public street, public highway, public park or
any property owned or held by the village within the boundaries of the village.
   (c)   STREET TREE or TREE means a tree in a public place, except where
otherwise indicated.
   (d)   VILLAGE ARBORIST means the Village Administrator or such other person
as may be appointed by the Mayor and confirmed by Council.
(`80 Code, § 1026.02) (Ord. 1028, passed 10-21-68)
§ 1026.03 APPOINTMENT OF ARBORIST; AUTHORITY; DUTIES.
   (a)   Appointment. There is hereby created the office of Village Arborist,
who shall be appointed by the Mayor of an indefinite term, subject to
confirmation by Council.
   (b)   Scope of Authority. The Village Arborist is hereby given full
jurisdiction, authority, control, supervision and direction to enforce and
otherwise carry out the provisions of this chapter, to issue permits hereunder
and to delegate all or such part of his power and duties, with respect to
supervision and control of trees, to his subordinates and assistants in the
employ of the village as he may from time to time determine.
   (c)   Order to preserve or remove. The Village Arborist shall have the
authority and it shall be his duty to order the trimming, preservation or
removal of trees or plants upon private property when he finds such action
necessary to the public safety or to prevent the spread of disease or insects
to public trees and places.
(`80 Code, § 1026.03) (Ord. 1028, passed 10-21-68)
§ 1026.04 MASTER STREET TREE PLAN.
   There is hereby adopted for the village a Master Street Tree Plan showing
varieties of species of all trees to be planted in the public right-of-way of
all streets within the village. The Plan is on file in the office of the Clerk-
Treasurer in the Town Hall and is incorporated in this chapter by reference as
if fully set forth herein. No person shall hereafter plant, transplant or move
any public tree on or to any street in the village, except to a location where
it will be in conformity with the Master Street Tree Plan and the species or
variety therein designated.
(`80 Code, § 1026.04) (Ord. 1028, passed 10-21-68)
§ 1026.05 PLANTING, REMOVAL, ETC.; PERMIT REQUIRED; CONDITIONS.
   (a)   No person shall plant, remove, destroy, cut, prune, treat, break,
climb, injure or spray any tree existing on any public place in the village, or
authorize or procure any other person to do so, or remove or tamper with any
device placed for the protection of any such tree, or attach any rope, wire,
chain, sign or other device placed for the protection of such tree, or
authorize or cause the same to be done, without having first obtained written
authority from the Village Arborist to do so.
   (b)   Such permit, when granted for the planting of any tree to be located
on any public place in the village, shall designate the species of tree to be
planted, the required spacing and the required minimum planting size, as
specified in the Master Street Tree Plan, as such Plan now exists or as it may
be amended from time to time. No person shall guy any tree less than four
inches in caliper with wires or rope. For trees over four inches in caliper,
special permission must be obtained and the permittee must assume liability for
accidents occurring therefrom.
   (c)   The application for the permit herein required shall state the number
and kind of trees to be trimmed, sprayed, preserved, removed or planted, the
kind of treatment to be administered and such other information as the Village
Arborist finds reasonably necessary to a fair determination of whether or not a
permit should be issued hereunder.
   (d)   The Village Arborist shall issue the permit provided for herein when
he finds that the desired action or treatment is necessary and that the
proposed method and workmanship are satisfactory.
   (e)   The Village Arborist shall have the authority and it shall be his duty
to supervise all work done under a permit issued in accordance with the
provisions of this chapter.
   (f)   The Village Arborist shall have the authority to affix reasonable
conditions to the granting of a permit hereunder.
   (g)   No permit shall be required to cultivate, fertilize or water public
trees or shrubs. The Village Arborist may authorize any person to do any work
or act described in division (a) hereof without a written permit, whenever he
determines that such work or act will not be detrimental to the public interest
and will be in accord with the spirit and the specific requirements of this
chapter.
(`80 Code, § 1026.05) (Ord. 1028, passed 10-21-68)
§ 1026.06 ABUSE OF TREES AND SHRUBS; TRIMMING REQUIRED; OBSTRUCTION OF VIEW OF
MOTORISTS.
   (a)   No person shall, without the consent of the owner in the case of a
private tree or shrub, or without a written permit from the Village Arborist in
the case of a public tree or shrub, do, or cause to be done by others, any of
the following acts:
      (1)   Secure, fasten or run any rope, wire, sign or other device or
material to, around or through a tree or shrub;
      (2)   Break, injure, mutilate, deface, kill or destroy, or permit any
fire to burn where it will injure, any tree or shrub;
      (3)   Erect, alter, repair or raze any building or structure without
placing suitable guards around all nearby public trees or shrubs which may be
injured or defaced by, or where such injury or defacement may arise out of, in
connection with or by reason of, such an operation. The quality of the guard
shall be determined by the Village Arborist.
      (4)   Knowingly permit any unprotected electric service wires to come in
prolonged contact with any public tree or shrub; or
      (5)   Remove any guard, stake or other device or material intended for
the protection of a public tree or shrub or close or obstruct any open space
about the base of a public tree or shrub designed to permit access of air,
water and fertilizer.
   (b)   The Village Arborist shall, and he is hereby directed to, keep all
trees standing upon any public place in the village trimmed so that the
branches of such trees projecting over any public sidewalk or private drive way
or into any public street beyond the curb line shall not conflict with the
public welfare.
   (c)   All trees standing upon private property in the village, having
branches projecting into public highways or public places, shall, under the
supervision of the Village Arborist, be kept trimmed by the owner or occupant
of such private property to such an extent that the lowest branches of such
trees do not come within 13 feet of the ground where they overhang any public
sidewalk or public place or public highway.
   (d)   Notwithstanding any other provision of this chapter, no person shall
maintain, plant or permit to remain on any private or public premises situated
at the intersection of two or more streets or alleys in the village, any hedge,
tree, shrub or other growth which may obstruct the view of the operator of any
motor vehicle approaching such intersection to the extent that such operator is
unable to observe other vehicles or pedestrians approaching or crossing such
intersection. Any such hedge, tree, shrub or growth is hereby declared to be a
public nuisance.
(`80 Code, § 1026.06) (Ord. 1028, passed 10-21-68)
§ 1026.07 PENETRATION OF ROOTS UNDER PUBLIC PLACES; ABATEMENT OF NUISANCE.
   Any tree or shrub upon private property in the village in such close
proximity to any public place in the village as will permit the roots of such
tree to penetrate through or under the surface of any public place in the
village, is hereby declared to be a public nuisance and may be abated by the
Village Arborist as provided in §§
1026.03(c) and
1026.09.
(`80 Code, § 1026.07) (Ord. 1028, passed 10-21-68)
§ 1026.08 AUTHORITY OF ARBORIST TO TRIM AND REMOVE.
   The Village Arborist shall have the right and duty to trim or remove any
tree existing on any public place in the village.
(`80 Code, § 1026.08) (Ord. 1028, passed 10-21-68)
§ 1026.09 ORDERS TO CORRECT; HEARINGS; APPEALS; REMEDY OF VILLAGE FOR
NONCOMPLIANCE.
   When the Village Arborist finds it necessary to order the trimming,
preservation or removal of trees or plants upon private property, as authorized
in §§ 1026.03(c) and
1026.06(c), he shall serve a written order to correct the dangerous condition
upon the owner, lessee, agent, operator, occupant or other person responsible
for its existence.
   (a)   The order required herein shall be served in one of the following
ways:
      (1)   By making personal delivery of the order to the person responsible;
      (2)   By leaving the order with some person of suitable age and
discretion upon the premises;
      (3)   By affixing a copy of the order to the door at the entrance of the
premises in violation;
      (4)   By mailing a copy of the order to the last known address of the
owner of the premises by registered or certified mail; or
      (5)   By publishing a copy of the order in a local newspaper once a week
for three successive weeks.
   (b)   The order required herein shall set forth a time limit for compliance,
dependent upon the hazard and danger created by the violation. In cases of
extreme danger to persons or public property, the Village Arborist shall have
the authority to require compliance immediately upon service of the order.
   (c)   If the owner, lessee, agent, operator, occupant or other responsible
person is aggrieved by an order of an officer hereunder, and desires a hearing,
he may complain or appeal in writing to the Village Arborist within three days
from the date service of the order is completed, and the Village Arborist shall
investigate the complaint and shall fix a place and time, not less than five
days nor more than ten days thereafter, for hearing such complaint. Notice of
such hearing shall be mailed to the address of the aggrieved party as it is set
forth in the complaint or appeal.
   At the hearing, the Village Arborist may affirm, modify, revoke or vacate
such order. Unless such order is revoked or vacated by the Arborist, it shall
remain in force and be complied with by such owner, lessee, agent, operator,
occupant or other person within the time fixed in the order or within such time
as may be fixed by the Village Arborist at the hearing.
   (d)   Any person aggrieved by the final order of the Village Arborist as
made at the hearing provided for hereunder may appeal as provided for in R.C.
Chapter 2506. Any person adversely affected by a standard fixed or order made
pursuant to this chapter may appeal as provided for in R.C. Chapter 2506.
   (e)   When a person to whom an order is directed fails to comply within the
time specified by an order hereunder or otherwise upon appeal, the Village
Arborist shall remedy the condition or contract with others for such purpose
and charge the cost thereof to the person to whom the order is directed. The
person remedying a condition under a contract made hereunder shall be
authorized to enter the premises for that purpose.
   (f)   If the cost of remedying a condition is not paid within ten days after
receipt of a statement therefor from the Village Arborist, such cost shall be
levied against the property upon which the hazard exists as a special
assessment. The levying of such assessment shall not affect the liability of
the person to whom the order is directed to fine and imprisonment, as herein
provided. Such special assessment shall be collected in the manner provided in
R.C. §§ 727.30 to 727.38, with a forfeiture of 5% and interest for failure to
pay at the time fixed by the assessing ordinance.
(`80 Code, § 1026.09) (Ord. 1028, passed 10-21-68)
§ 1026.10 MOVING OF TREES; DEPOSIT OR BOND REQUIRED.
   All moving of trees upon any public place in the village made necessary by
the moving of a building or structure or any other private enterprise shall be
done under the supervision of, and with the written permission of, the Village
Arborist, and at the expense of the applicant or person seeking the removal of
such tree. Such applicant, as one of the conditions to obtaining such
permission, shall deposit with the village such sum in cash as the Village
Arborist may determine and specify to cover all of the cost of moving and
replacing such tree, if the conditions of such permission require the
replacement thereof. However, in lieu of such cash deposit, the Village
Arborist may, at his discretion, accept a good and sufficient bond in like
amount conditioned upon the payment of all of the cost of such moving and
replacing of the tree.
(`80 Code, § 1026.10) (Ord. 1028, passed 10-21-68)
§ 1026.11 RIGHT OF ENTRY.
   The Village Arborist shall have the authority to enter upon private premises
at all reasonable times for the purpose of examining any tree or shrub located
upon or over such premises and carrying out any of the provisions of this
chapter.
(`80 Code, § 1026.11) (Ord. 1028, passed 10-21-68)
§ 1026.12 INTERFERENCE WITH ARBORIST.
   No person shall prevent, delay or interfere with the Village Arborist or his
agents, employees or servants while they are engaged in carrying out any work
or activities authorized by this chapter.
(`80 Code, § 1026.12) (Ord. 1028, passed 10-21-68)
§ 1026.99 PENALTY.
   Whoever violates any of the provisions of this chapter is guilty of a
misdemeanor of the fourth degree and shall be fined not more than $250 or
imprisoned not more than 30 days, or both, for each offense. A separate offense
shall be deemed committed each day during or on which a violation occurs or
continues.
(`80 Code, § 1026.99)
CHAPTER 1027: PUBLIC GREENS
1027.01   Definition
1027.02   Green locations
1027.03   Management directives
1027.04   Regulations governing use of greens, parks and tree lawns
   CROSS REFERENCES
   Director of Recreation, Parks and Community Activities responsible for
maintenance of Greens, see ADM. §
243.01
§ 1027.01 DEFINITION.
   (a)   As used in this chapter, GREEN is defined to be an open area of lawn
and trees in public ownership; a grassy lawn, plot or similar area abounding
on, or covered with green growth or foliage.
   (b)   As used in this chapter, PARK means any area of land owned by the
Village of Jefferson and designated a park by the village.
   (c)   As used in this chapter, TREE LAWN is defined as the portion of the
street or highway right-of-way between the traveled and/or paved portion of the
roadway to the nearest line of any existing sidewalk or to the street right-of-
way boundary.
(Ord. 1924, passed 10-21-91; Ord. 2540, passed 4-5-04)
§ 1027.02 GREEN LOCATIONS.
   Village greens are established at the following locations:
   (a)   Northeast corner of Jefferson-Market Streets.
   (b)   Northwest corner of Jefferson-Market Streets.
   (c)   Southeast corner of Jefferson-Market Streets.
   (d)   Southwest corner of Jefferson-Market Streets.
   (e)   Northeast corner of Jefferson-Chestnut Streets.
   (f)   Northwest corner of Jefferson-Chestnut Streets.
   (g)   Southeast corner of Jefferson-Chestnut Streets.
   (h)   Southwest corner of Jefferson-Chestnut Streets.
(Ord. 1924, passed 10-21-91; Ord. 2540, passed 4-5-04)
§ 1027.03 MANAGEMENT DIRECTIVES.
   (a)   Open area. Open area means unobstructed in view; at street
intersections and approaches, having the value of aiding both pedestrian and
vehicular movement. Management will foster the open characteristic, as against
the presence of structures, signs (as covered by Chapter 1446), tree and shrub
growth, and other features detrimental thereto.
   (b)   Lawn and trees. Lawn and trees together display the green of life, in
contrast to the coldness and massiveness of brick, concrete, and asphalt.
Management will foster the use of native grasses, shrub, and tree species where
adapted to local climate and soil, together with the necessary care and upkeep.
   (c)   Aesthetics. Appreciation of natural beauty abides strongly in the
community. It has been a conscious force for participation in tree planting,
and beautification efforts. Management will promote and foster the aesthetic
value of these properties at all seasons of the year.
   (d)   Ownership. Land title to the named greens (§
1027.02) is recorded with the Ashtabula County Clerk of Courts, supported by
established boundaries, and with permissive uses set forth to abutting property
owners, where involved. It is the continuing responsibility of village officers
to assure adherence to established boundaries on the part of abutting property
owners. Familiarity and boundaries, alertness to change, and prompt enforcement
is the requirement.
(Ord. 1924, passed 10-21-91; Ord. 2540, passed 4-5-04)
§ 1027.04 REGULATIONS GOVERNING USE OF GREENS, PARKS AND TREE LAWNS.
   (a)   Persons using the greens shall observe all laws, ordinances, rules and
regulations pertaining to the public greens, and will do so at their own risk.
   (b)   Camping is not permitted on village greens.
   (c)   A pet shall not be allowed to cause a nuisance.
   (d)   Village greens shall not be used for illegal purposes. No person shall
suffer or commit any nuisance on these premises, nor use these premises in any
way, or for any purpose that may endanger the health, or disturb the peace and
quiet of other persons.
   (e)   Selling, vending, peddling and distributing of any merchandise or
property, and the placing or distributing of advertising matter, literature, or
other printed matter on village property without the issuance of a permit by
the Administrator, including any conditions, is prohibited.
   (f)   No person shall overtly and publicly consume or display the presence
of any beer or intoxicating liquor as defined in R.C. § 4301.01 in any area of
the village greens, tree lawns and parks; unless attending an event held
thereon the sponsors of which have obtained the proper liquor permit from the
Ohio Division of Liquor Control and the approval of Village Council. No person
under the influence of alcohol shall enter or remain on these public
properties.
   (g)   No person shall possess, use, or consume a drug of abuse as defined in
R.C. § 3719.011, in or on these public properties.
(Ord. 1924, passed 10-21-91; Ord. 2540, passed 4-5-04) Penalty, see §
202.99

CHAPTER 1029: PROPERTY NUMBERING SYSTEM
1029.01   Numbering map
1029.02   Numbering system

   CROSS REFERENCES

§ 1029.01 NUMBERING MAP.
   The property numbering map entitled “Jefferson Village Map, dated March,
1977, Ashtabula County, Ohio” is hereby adopted as the numbering map of the
Village of Jefferson, Ohio, and all property numbers assigned shall be assigned
in accordance with this numbering map, and no other property numbers shall be
used or displayed in the village, except numbers assigned in accordance with
the numbering map. The property numbering map shall be kept on file in the
office of the Village Administrator. Within 25 days of annexation, any new
property to the village shall be added to the map and numbers assigned to the
property in accordance to §
1029.02.
(`80 Code, § 1029.01) (Ord. 1949, passed 3-2-92)
§ 1029.02 NUMBERING SYSTEM.
   On the property numbering map, Chestnut Street is hereby designated as the
north-south axis and Jefferson Street is hereby designated as the east-west
axis, and all avenues, streets and alleys running generally north and south
shall be numbered from the east-west axis consecutively to the corporate limits
of the extremity of such avenue, street or alley. Avenues, streets or alleys
running generally east and west shall be numbered from the north-south axis in
the same manner. Wherever possible, 100 numbers shall be allowed to each block
so that the number of each consecutive block shall conform with consecutive
hundreds and one.
   One whole number shall be assigned for ever 50 feet of ground, whether the
same is improved property or a vacant lot, on every street within the corporate
limits, excluding the business district. In the business district, one whole
number shall be assigned for every 25 feet of ground, whether the same is
improved property or a vacant lot. Odd numbers shall be assigned to the west
side of the street on all north-south streets, and even numbers to the east
side. On east-west streets, odd numbers shall be assigned to the north side of
the street and even numbers to the south side.
(`80 Code, § 1029.02) (Ord. 1949, passed 3-2-92)
§ 1029.03 PURCHASE OF NUMBERS.
   Every property owner of improved property shall, on or before the fifteenth
day of March, 1992, purchase and display in a conspicuous place on said
property the number assigned.
(`80 Code, § 1029.03) (Ord. 1949, passed 3-2-92)
§ 1029.04 NUMBERS FOR FUTURE BUILDINGS.
   All residence and business buildings erected after the adoption of this
chapter shall be assigned a number in accordance with the property numbering
map and shall purchase and display such number as provided in §§ 1029.03 and
1029.06.
(`80 Code, § 1029.04) (Ord. 1949, passed 3-2-92)
§ 1029.05 DEFACING OF NUMBERS.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to alter, deface or take down any number
placed on any property in accordance with this chapter, except for repair or
replacement of such number.
(`80 Code, § 1029.05) (Ord. 1949, passed 3-2-92)
§ 1029.06 NUMBER SIZE, CONFIGURATION AND LOCATION.
   Each building to which a street number has been assigned shall have such
number displayed in a position easily observed and readable from the public
street. All numbers shall be Arabic numerals at least three inches (seventy-six
millimeters) high and one-half inch (thirteen millimeters) stroke.
   Numbers shall be in a position to be illuminated by exterior lighting if
lighting is provided on the structure. It is not required that the property
numbers be illuminated all night.
(`80 Code, § 1029.06) (Ord. 1949, passed 3-2-92)
§ 1029.99 PENALTY.
   Whoever violates any of the provisions of this chapter is guilty of a minor
misdemeanor and shall be fined not more than $100 for each offense. A separate
offense shall be deemed committed each day during or on which a violation
occurs or continues.

§ 1030.01 DEFINITIONS.
   As used in Chapters
1030 through
1036, unless the context specifically indicates otherwise:
   (1)   B.O.D. (denoting biochemical oxygen demand) means the quantity of
oxygen utilized in the biochemical oxidation of organic matter under standard
laboratory procedure in five days at 20ºC. expressed in milligrams per liter.
   (2)   BUILDING SEWER means the extension from the building drain to the
public sewer or other place of disposal. Specifically:
      A.   COMBINED BUILDING SEWER means a building sewer which conveys both
sewage and storm water or other drainage.
      B.   SANITARY BUILDING SEWER means a building sewer which conveys sewage
only.
      C.   STORM BUILDING SEWER means a building sewer which conveys storm
water or other drainage, but not sewage.
   (3)   C.O.D. (denoting chemical oxygen demand) means the quantity of oxygen
required to satisfy the carbon in a waste as determined by chemical oxidation
of the waste with a strong oxidation agent-acid solution.
   (4)   COMBINED SEWER means a sewer receiving surface drainage and run-off
from roof downspouts, exterior foundation drains, street drains, etc., and
sanitary sewage.
   (5)   COOLING WATER means water discharged from any system of condensation,
air conditioning, cooling, refrigeration or any other system, and has quality
characteristics of unpolluted water.
   (6)   DEBT SERVICE CHARGE means the charge levied on users to make principal
and interest payments required for the amortization of the cost of repairs and
improvements to the village of Jefferson's sewer system and waste water
treatment plant.
   (7)   GOVERNMENTAL USER means any Federal, State or local government user of
the waste water treatment system.
   (8)   GRAB SAMPLE means a sample which is taken from a waste stream on a
one-time basis with no regard to the flow in the waste stream and without
consideration of time.
   (9)   HOLDING TANK WASTE means any waste from holding tanks, such as
vessels, chemical toilets, campers, trailers, septic tanks and vacuum-pump tank
trucks.
   (10)   INCOMPATIBLE POLLUTANT means a waste constituent which interferes
with the operation and performance of the waste water treatment works.
   (11)   INDUSTRIAL USER means any nongovernmental, nonresidential user of the
publicly owned treatment works that discharges a trade or process waste.
   (12)   INDUSTRIAL WASTE means the liquid waste from an industrial
manufacturing process trade or business, as distinct from sanitary sewage.
   (13)   INSTITUTIONAL USER means an establishment which is involved in
social, charitable, religious or educational functions and which discharges
primarily segregated domestic wastes or waste from sanitary conveniences.
   (14)   NATIONAL POLLUTANT DISCHARGE ELIMINATION SYSTEM (NPDES) PERMIT means
any permit or equivalent document or requirement issued by the State water
pollution control agency to regulate the discharge of pollutants from the waste
water treatment works.
   (15)   NORMAL SEWAGE means sewage that, when analyzed, shows by weight a
daily average of not more than 280 parts per million of suspended solids, nor
more than 240 parts per million of B.O.D. and/or 500 parts per million of
C.O.D., nor more than eight parts per million of phosphorus, nor more than
eighty parts per million of ether-soluble matter (grease and oil). These
concentrations will be used for determining surcharges.
   (16)   OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE means all costs, direct and indirect, not
including debt service, inclusive of, but not limited to, expenditures
attributable to administration, the replacement of equipment, the purchase and
installation of new equipment and the treatment and collection of waste waters,
necessary to ensure adequate waste water collection and treatment on a
continuing basis.
   (17)   RATE means the charge levied as a function of the total material
water usage per unit of sewage.
   (18)   REPLACEMENT means expenditures for obtaining and installing
equipment, accessories or appurtenances which are necessary during the useful
life of the treatment works to maintain the capacity and performance for which
such treatment works were designed and constructed.
   (19)   SANITARY SEWER means a sewer which carries sewage and industrial
waste, from residences, commercial buildings, industrial operations and
institutions, to which storm, surface or ground water is not intentionally
admitted.
   (20)   SEWAGE means a combination of water- carried wastes from residences,
business buildings, institutions and industrial establishments, together with
such ground, surface or storm water as may be present.
   (21)   STORM DRAIN or STORM SEWER means a pipe or conduit that carries storm
and/or surface water and/or drainage, but excludes sewage and/or industrial
wastes. A storm drain or storm sewer may, however, carry cooling waters and/or
unpolluted waters.
   (22)   STORM WATER means any flow occurring during or following any form of
natural precipitation and resulting therefrom.
   (23)   SURCHARGE means the assessment, in addition to the service charge,
which is levied on those persons whose wastes are greater in strength than the
concentrations established as representative of normal sewage.
   (24)   SUSPENDED SOLIDS means solids that either float on the surface of, or
are in suspension in, water, sewage or other liquids, and which are removable
by laboratory filtering.
   (25)   USER means any person who contributes, or causes or permits the
contribution of, waste water into the village's publicly owned treatment works.
   (26)   USER CHARGE means a charge levied on users of the waste water
treatment works for the debt service charges and the operation, maintenance and
replacement costs of such works.
   (27)   WASTE WATER or SEWAGE means liquid and water-carried industrial or
domestic waste from dwellings, commercial buildings, industrial facilities and
institutions, together with any ground, surface and storm water that may be
present, whether treated or untreated, which is contributed into or permitted
to enter the publicly owned treatment works.
(`80 Code, § 1030.01) (Ord. 2044, passed 6-6-94)
§ 1030.02 TYPES OF ACCOUNTS.
   All accounts are continuous and shall be billed and paid monthly. All
accounts shall be divided into categories as follows:
   (a)   Domestic;
   (b)   Commercial;
   (c)   Industrial; and
   (d)   Governmental/institutional.
(`80 Code, § 1030.02) (Ord. 2044, passed 6-6-94; Ord. 2428, passed 7-15-02)
§ 1030.03 APPLICATION AND CONTRACT FOR SEWER USE SERVICE.
   (a)   An application for waste water treatment service of any of the types
set forth in §
1030.02, made in accordance with these rules and regulations, when accepted by
the village, shall constitute a contract. Service will be continuous so long as
these rules and regulations are complied with, until termination is requested
by the customer.
   (b)   Such application must be made at the office of the Village
Administrator on the forms provided. Such application shall be signed by the
person who is to be responsible for all charge arising from bills for sewer
service, or by his or her authorized agent. The customer, if a tenant, shall be
liable for charges for sewer use.
   (c)   In addition to making an application for waste water treatment
service, a new customer must pay to the village a security deposit of $40 to
ensure payment of future sewer charges. If sewer services are terminated by a
customer and all sewer bills have been paid in full by the customer, the
village will refund the sewer deposit. If sewer service is terminated and sewer
bills are not fully and timely paid, the village shall set off the amount of
the unpaid sewer bill against this deposit and refund the balance of the
deposit, if any, to the customer. No interest shall be paid to the customer on
the sewer deposit held by the village.
   (d)   The owner of the property shall be liable for any and all other
services, repairs and damages which, in accordance with these rules and
regulations, are the responsibility of the property owner.
   (e)   Information regarding a customer's application and/or account status
shall be strictly confidential and shall not be disclosed to any person except
authorized and properly identified agents of law enforcement and postal
authorities.
(`80 Code, § 1030.03) (Ord. 2258, passed 5-3-99; Ord. 2428, passed 7-15-02)
§ 1030.04 RESERVED.
§ 1030.05 BANKRUPTCY PROCEEDINGS.
   Whenever a customer is the principal in bankruptcy proceedings, the waste
water treatment service account shall be terminated and a final bill shall be
submitted to the customer. The waste water treatment service account shall be
considered as a lien against the property which has been provided the sewer
service and shall be certified to the County Auditor as a lien on such
property.
(`80 Code, § 1030.05) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82; Ord. 2428, passed 7-15-02)
§ 1030.06 DELINQUENCY SURCHARGE.
   Persons with premises connected to the sewer services of the village shall
pay an additional charge of 6% of any account for such services when such
account is not paid within 15 days after the date the invoice/bill for such
services is mailed.
(`80 Code, § 1030.06) (Ord. 1676, passed 2-4-85; Ord. 2428, passed 7-15-02)
§ 1030.065 DELINQUENCY LIENS.
   Unpaid sewer service charges shall constitute a lien upon property served by
a connection with the sewer services of the village. Council, under authority
of R.C. § 729.49, hereby authorizes the Village Administrator to certify all
delinquent sewer charges to the County Auditor as a lien against the real
property served thereby, requesting such delinquent amounts to be collected in
the same manner as other real estate taxes. The amount of delinquent sewer
charges certified shall be increased by 20% of the amount of the delinquent
account to reimburse the village for the 20% collection fee charged by the
Auditor for collection services.

result, in which case arrangements may be made for partial payments.

§ 1030.11 ADJUSTMENT OF BILLS; INACCURATE METERS; LEAKS.
   (a)   All water that passes through a meter shall be charged for water
pollution control use. The only basis for adjusting a bill is an inaccurate
meter or a documented water leak accepted by the water supplier and credited
against the water suppliers water service bill.
   (b)   If a meter fails to register or is found to be out of order, the
customer will be charged at the average consumption for previous comparable
periods.
   (c)   An allowance shall be made or rebate allowed to any sewer customer on
account of water leakage in the event the supplier of water services to the
sewer customer recognizes the existence of the water leak and gives the
customer a credit against the customer's water services bill because of the
leak. The amount of the credit against the sewer bill, because of a water leak
recognized and credited by the water supplier, shall be in accordance with the
amount of the credit granted to the customer by the water supplier due to the
water leak.
(`80 Code, § 1011) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82; Ord. 2428, passed 7-15-02)
§ 1030.12 CHARGE FOR DWELLING AND BUSINESS UNITS WITHOUT SEPARATE WATER METERS.
   There is hereby established a policy that the owner or occupant of each
dwelling unit and each business unit that does not have a separate water meter
shall pay a monthly minimum charge for the use of the sewerage system of the
village that is equal to the minimum monthly sewer charge for single-family
residences. In apartment units and multifamily units that are now connected to
one single water meter, the minimum charge shall be the minimum monthly charge
times the number of separate dwelling units connected to such meter.
(`80 Code, § 1030.12) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82)
§ 1030.13 REIMBURSEMENT OF FEES FOR WATER NOT REDISTRIBUTED.
   (a)   It is the intent of Council not to exact a sewer charge for water
bought, but not consumed and redistributed through the waste water treatment
system of the village.
   (b)   When water is purchased for uses such as industrial cooling or similar
purposes and is not redistributed in the waste water treatment facilities, then
upon delivery to the Clerk-Treasurer of an affidavit and evidence of such
nonusage, together with verification of such nonusage by the Village
Administrator, a rebate will be given for that portion of sewer usage fees that
is represented by such water retained and not redistributed.
   (c)   Where water is purchased by residential users for filling a swimming
pool, which water is retained within such pool and never redistributed through
the waste water treatment facilities, and such usage is verified in advance by
application to the Village Administrator prior to such usage, a rebate will be
made for such portion of the sewer usage fee that has been paid as a result of
water purchased for such swimming pool use.
(`80 Code, § 1030.13) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82)
§ 1030.14 RECOVERY OF OPERATION, MAINTENANCE AND REPLACEMENT COSTS AND DEBT
SERVICE CHARGES.
   The village shall review the sewer service charges on an annual basis. On or
before January 10 of each year, or at such other times as the Village
Administrator or Village Council deems necessary, the Village Administrator
shall submit a report of all expenditures of the waste water treatment system
for the previous year to Council. Thereafter, on or before February 1 of each
year, or at such other times as the Village Administrator or Village Council
deems necessary, the Administrator shall calculate and compare the operation,
maintenance and replacement costs and the debt service charges of the two
preceding years and projections of such costs and charges for the following
year and adjust the sewer rental rates to provide sufficient revenues to pay
for the projected operation, maintenance and replacement costs and the debt
service charges. The purpose of this adjustment is to annually reflect in the
sewer service rates the actual anticipated costs for the operation, maintenance
and replacement and the debt services charges of the waste water treatment
system, and/or any anticipated expenditures pertaining to the operation,
maintenance and replacement costs and the debt service charges, proportionately
among the users of the waste water treatment system. The portion of the user
charges attributable to the operation, maintenance and replacement costs and
debt service charges shall be calculated as such costs and charges divided by
the billable flow received in the system. The new rates, as determined by the
Administrator, shall be submitted to Council for its review and passage at the
first Council meeting in February of each year, or at such other times as the
Village Administrator or Village Council deems necessary.
   Following passage by Council, each user shall be notified, in conjunction
with a regular bill, of the rate and portion of the sewer service charges that
are attributable to the operation, maintenance and replacement costs and the
debt service charges of waste water treatment services.
(`80 Code, § 1030.14) (Ord. 2044, passed 6-6-94)

Wastewater Treatment Fund #520.

§ 1030.18 SEWER RATES.
   (a)   The rates or charges to be collected from all persons having premises
connected to the sewer service system within the territorial limits of the
village may be increased up to 3.5% per year as recommended by the Village
Administrator and authorized by Village Council in the manner set forth below.
      (1)   The Administrator is hereby authorized and directed to annually
propose for Council's review and approval a rate schedule for sewer rates.
      (2)   Council shall review the proposed rate schedule and make any
necessary changes prior to approval of the schedule but, in no case, shall the
rate schedule be approved later than the second regularly scheduled Council
meeting in January of each year.
   (b)   Bills shall be issued on a bi-monthly basis and have a minimum charge
for 200 cubic feet. Bills issued under this section may be prorated based on
move-in and move-out dates according to the rate schedule effective for that
billing cycle.
   (c)   The rates or charges to be collected from all persons having premises
connected to the sewer service system outside of the territorial limits of the
village are, as hereinafter set forth and are to be issued on a bi-monthly
basis.
      (1)   Charges outside the territorial limits of the village shall be as
provided for in division (a) hereof, plus an additional 75%.
      (2)   Connection to the sewer system by a user not located within the
village territorial limits is subject to Council's approval.
   (d)   An "EPA Compliance Fee" to fund mandated repairs and improvements to
the sewer treatment plant and collection system in order to comply with current
and future NPDES Permit requirements and discharge limits shall be added to
each bill issued by the Village of Jefferson.
      (1)   The EPA Compliance Fee shall be $4 per month and shall be collected
from all persons having premises connected to the sewer service system and paid
into the Sewer Improvement Fund #509.
      (2)   The EPA Compliance Fee and amount shall be reviewed annually and
adjusted by ordinance as warranted.
(`80 Code, § 1030.18) (Ord. 2044, passed 6-6-94; Ord. 2322, passed 2-20-01;
Ord. 2467, passed 3-3-03; Ord. 2517, passed 1-5-04; Ord. 2657, passed 9-18-06;
Ord. 2725, passed 10-15-07; Ord. 2815, passed 5-17-10; Ord. 2862, passed 4-4-

§ 1030.22 SPECIAL HOOK-ON PERMITS.
   (a)   (1)   No person shall attach a sewer to the manhole located at the
center of the intersection of East Erie and Sycamore Streets without first
obtaining a hook-on permit from the Village Administrator.
      (2)   No hook-on permit shall be issued by the Administrator, authorizing
any person to hook onto such manhole, until the Administrator receives from the
applicant such amount as is equal to the applicant's proportionate share of the
costs paid by the owners of property located at the northeast and southeast
corners of such intersection (on November 7, 1960). Any person availing himself
or herself of the service offered by such sewer extension and manhole shall
share equally in the cost, as paid by such owners.
      (3)   Such hook-on charges collected by the Administrator from persons
wishing to attach to such sewer extension shall be prorated back to the owners
referred to in division (b) hereof, and to any person who has subsequently paid
his or her proportionate share of the original costs. All of those properties
sharing in the use of such improvement shall share equally in its original
costs.
   (b)   (1)   No person shall attach a sewer to the sewer line on South
Cucumber Street between East Jefferson Street and East Erie Street, laid down
by the Jefferson Development Corporation, without first obtaining a hook-on
permit from the Village Administrator.
      (2)   No hook-on permit shall be issued by the Administrator prior to
payment to the Administrator of an amount equal to $2 per linear foot of that
property fronting upon such improvement which is to be served by an attachment
to the South Cucumber Street sewer.
      (3)   Such hook-on charges as may be collected by the Administrator
pursuant to this section shall be paid to the Jefferson Development
Corporation.
   (c)   (1)   Until January 1, 2018, no person shall attach a sewer to the
sewer line which runs from the manhole located at the intersection of West
Cedar Street and Westview Drive, thence westerly and southerly along a sewer
line easement of the village to a manhole located at the intersection of
Brittany Lane and Mulberry, without first obtaining a hook-on permit from the
Village Administrator.
      (2)   No hook-on permit shall be issued by the Administrator prior to
payment to the Administrator of hook-on fee in an amount equal to $65 per
linear foot of that property fronting upon such improvement which is to be
served by an attachment to the sewer line which runs from the manhole located
at the intersection of West Cedar Street and Westview Drive, thence westerly
and southerly along a sewer line easement of the village to a manhole located
at the intersection of Brittany Lane and Mulberry.
      (3)   Such hook-on fee as may be collected by the Administrator pursuant
to this section shall be paid Timothy G. Lemire, or his heirs and/or assigns.
      (4)   Until January 1, 2018, the village Administrator shall not issue
hook-on permits for that section of the village's sewer line described in
divisions (1) and (2) above, for more than five residential units which have
frontage upon said sewer line having a combined sewer effluent generating
capacity of 2000 gallons per day.
(`80 Code, § 1030.22) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82; Ord. 2177, passed 9-15-97)
§ 1030.24 MAINTENANCE OF SANITARY SEWERS.
   (a)   All sanitary sewers and appurtenances within public rights of way,
easements granted to the village or other public lands shall belong to the
village.
   (b)   The village shall be responsible for the operation and maintenance of
all sanitary sewers and appurtenances within public rights of way, easements or
public lands, with the exception of laterals from the main line sewer to the
user of the service, i. e. all sewers six inches or smaller, the operation and
maintenance of which shall be the individual user's responsibility.
   (c)   The user shall be responsible for repairs and damage to public rights
of way, easements or public lands as a result of the maintenance of his or her
lateral line, shall repair all damage caused by his or her actions and shall
secure all necessary permits required for this operation.
(`80 Code, § 1030.24) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82)
§ 1030.25 RIGHT OF ENTRY; INJURY OR LOSS WHILE ON PREMISES.
   (a)   Duly authorized employees and officials of the village, bearing proper
credentials and identification, may enter, at any time, all properties for the
purposes of inspection, observation, measurement, sampling and testing in
accordance with the provisions of §§
1036.16 and
1036.17. The designated supervisor of the Waste Water Treatment Plant or his or
her representative shall have no authority to inquire into any process,
including metallurgical, chemical, oil, refining, ceramic, paper or any other
industry, beyond that point having a direct bearing on the kind of sources of
discharge to the sewers, waterways or facilities for waste treatment.
   (b)   While performing the necessary work on private properties referred to
in division (a) hereof, the duly authorized employees of the village shall
observe all safety rules applicable to the premises established by the company.
The company shall be held harmless for injury or death to village employees and
the village shall indemnify the company against loss or damage to its property
by village employees and against liability claims and demands for personal
injury or property damage asserted against the company and growing out of the
gauging and sampling operation, except as such may be caused by negligence or
failure of the company to maintain safe conditions.
(`80 Code, § 1030.25) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82; Ord. 2019, passed 12-20-93)
§ 1030.26 POWER TO ENTER EASEMENT PROPERTIES.
   Duly authorized employees of the village, bearing proper credentials and
identification, shall be permitted to enter all private properties through
which the village holds a duly negotiated easement for the purpose of, but not
limited to, inspection, observation, measurement, sampling, repair or
maintenance of any portion of the sewage works lying within such easement. All
entry and subsequent work, if any, on such easement, shall be done in full
accordance with the terms of the duly negotiated easement pertaining to the
private property involved.
(`80 Code, § 1030.26) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82; Ord. 2019, passed 12-20-93)
§ 1030.27 POWER TO ACCEPT OR REJECT WASTES.
   The village shall make and enforce rules and regulations, establishing the
types and characteristics of sanitary sewage, industrial wastes and other
matter, not specifically covered in these rules and regulations, which shall
not be discharged into the village sewerage system, and the types and
characteristics of sanitary sewage and industrial wastes admissible to the
village sewerage system only after pretreatment.
(`80 Code, § 1030.27) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82)
§ 1030.275 RIGHT TO LIMIT CONNECTIONS.
   The village reserves the right to limit connection(s) to its sewer system
and refuse sewer service if, in the sole good-faith opinion of the Village
Administrator, the system does not have sufficient capacity to properly service
and treat the waste stream anticipated to be generated from the proposed
connection(s).
(`80 Code, § 1030.275) (Ord. 2054, passed 9-19-94)
§ 1030.28 SURCHARGE FOR SPECIAL WASTES.
   When necessary, by contract or ordinance, to establish additional rates to
be charged for specific types of wastes not covered in the surcharge
computation, the village shall determine a method by which to establish such
rates. Such rates or charges shall be subject to the approval of Council.
(`80 Code, § 1030.28) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82)
§ 1030.29 ADDITIONAL REGULATIONS.
   The village shall make recommendations and enforce all additional rules and
regulations relative to the discharge of water, waste or waste water to any
natural outlet, whether it is a river, lake, stream, creek, etc., as the need
for such additional rules and regulations arises.
(`80 Code, § 1030.29) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82)
§ 1030.30 REGULATING AND ENFORCING AGENCY.
   The village shall be the sole regulating and enforcing agency of water
pollution for the village.
(`80 Code, § 1030.30) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82)
§ 1030.31 APPLICATION OF REGULATIONS TO SYSTEMS OUTSIDE CORPORATE LIMITS.
   The provisions of Chapters
1030 through
1036 shall govern all sewerage systems outside the corporate limits of the
village that are connected to the sewerage system of the village.
(`80 Code, § 1030.31) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82)
§ 1030.32 WRITTEN NOTICE OF VIOLATIONS.
   Any person found to be violating any of the provisions of Chapters
1030 through
1036 shall be served by the village with written notice stating the nature of
the violation. The offender shall, within the period of time stated in such
notice, permanently cease such violation.
(`80 Code, § 1030.32) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82)
§ 1030.33 CITATIONS; ARREST WARRANTS.
   The village may issue citations and may request that a warrant be issued for
the arrest of any person violating any of the provisions of Chapters
1030 through
1036, unless the section in question makes provision for a specific action to
be taken.
(`80 Code, § 1030.33) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82)
§ 1030.34 LIABILITY TO VILLAGE.
   Whoever violates any of the provisions of Chapters
1030 through
1036 shall be liable to the village for any expense, loss or damage occasioned
the village by reason of such violation.
(`80 Code, § 1030.34) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82)
§ 1030.35 DETERMINATION OF DAMAGE COSTS.
   All damage costs shall be determined by the village and/or the Village
Engineer.
(`80 Code, § 1030.35) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82)
§ 1030.36 DETERMINATION AND PAYMENT OF FINES.
   (a)   All fines and penalties for citations may be determined by the village
and paid at the office of the Village Clerk.
   (b)   All fines collected for violations of the provisions of Chapters
1030 through
1036 shall be collected by the Clerk of Courts, paid to the Village Treasurer
and credited to the Sewer Revenue Fund.
(`80 Code, § 1030.36) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82)
§ 1030.99 PENALTY; COSTS OF LITIGATION.
   (a)   Whoever violates or fails to comply with any of the provisions of this
chapter shall be fined not less than $100 and not more than $500, or imprisoned
not more than 30 days. For each offense after the first offense, the minimum
fine shall be increased $50.
   (b)   In addition to the penalty provided in division (a) hereof, the
village may recover reasonable attorneys' fees, court costs, court reporters'
fees and other expenses of litigation by appropriate suit at law against the
person found to have violated, or found to have failed to comply with, any of
the provisions of this chapter or the orders, rules, regulations and permits
issued under this chapter.
(`80 Code, § 1030.99) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82)

§ 1032.01 WORK ON SEWERS; PERMIT REQUIRED.
   No unauthorized person shall uncover, make any connection with or opening
into, or use, alter or disturb, any public sewer or appurtenance thereto,
without first obtaining a written permit therefor from the Village
Administrator.
(`80 Code, § 1032.01) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82)
§ 1032.02 TAMPERING WITH MANHOLES; AUTHORIZATION REQUIRED.
   No person, without proper authorization from the village, shall lift, remove
or tamper with a manhole cover or lid or make any opening into a manhole for
the purpose of draining rain, ground or waste water or placing any material or
substance into any sewer.
(`80 Code, § 1032.02) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82)
§ 1032.03 INDEPENDENT BUILDING SEWERS REQUIRED.
   Where more than one building requiring sanitary sewerage is constructed on a
single parcel of land, a separate and independent building sewer shall be
provided for each building.
(`80 Code, § 1032.03) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82)
§ 1032.04 USE OF OLD BUILDING SEWERS.
   Old building sewers may be used in connection with new buildings, provided
that the sewers are all premium joint pipe and provided, further, that they are
found, on examination, to meet all the requirements of Chapters
1030 through
1036.
(`80 Code, § 1032.04) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82)
§ 1032.05 INSTALLATION METHODS FOR BUILDING SEWERS.
   The size, slope, alignment and materials of construction of a building
sewer, and the methods to be used in excavating, placing the pipe, jointing,
testing or backfilling the trench, shall conform to the requirements of the
Building and Plumbing Codes or other applicable rules and regulations of the
village. In the absence of Code provisions or in amplification thereof, the
materials and procedures set forth in appropriate specifications of the
American Standard for Test-Materials and Water Pollution Control Federation
Manual of Practice No. 9, as amended, shall apply.
(`80 Code, § 1032.05) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82)
§ 1032.06 ELEVATION OF BUILDING SEWERS.
   Whenever possible, the building sewer shall be brought to the building at an
elevation below the basement floor. In buildings in which the building drain is
too low to permit gravity flow to the building sewer, the sanitary sewage
carried by such building drain shall be lifted or gravity drained by a method
approved by the Village Engineer to discharge the sewage to the building sewer.
(`80 Code, § 1032.06) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82)
§ 1032.07 SURFACE WATER CONNECTIONS PROHIBITED; NOTICE TO CORRECT.
   (a)   No person shall make a connection of roof downspouts, storm water sump
pumps, exterior foundation drains, areaway drains or other sources of surface
run-off or ground water to a building sewer or building drain which in turn is
connected directly or indirectly to a public sanitary sewer.
   (b)   Any person violating division (a) hereof shall be given a first notice
to correct the connections to the specifications of Chapters
1030 through
1036 and have such work finished within 60 days. A second notice to correct the
connections shall be given if action in response to the first notice was not
completed within 60 days. If the connections are not corrected within 30 days
after the second notice, a third notice shall be issued and the violator shall
be guilty of a misdemeanor, punishable as provided in §
1032.99.
(`80 Code, § 1032.07) (Ord. 2065, passed 12-19-94)
§ 1032.08 REQUIREMENTS FOR CONNECTING BUILDING AND PUBLIC SEWERS.
   The connection of a building sewer into a public sewer shall conform to the
requirements of the Building and Plumbing Codes or other applicable rules and
regulations of the village, or the procedures set forth in appropriate
specifications of the American Standard for Test-Materials and the Water
Pollution Control Federation Manual of Practice No. 9, as amended. All such
connections shall be made gastight and watertight. Any deviation from the
prescribed procedures and material requirements must be approved by the village
prior to making such connection.
(`80 Code, § 1032.08) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82)
§ 1032.09 PERIODIC INSPECTIONS; COMPLIANCE WITH VILLAGE STANDARDS.
   All work prosecuted or performed by the sewer builder shall be subject to
periodic inspection by the village Engineer, or his or her designated agents,
during construction. All such work shall comply with the standard designs,
specifications and ordinances of the village and shall also comply with state
laws and regulations governing such work.
(`80 Code, § 1032.09) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82)
§ 1032.10 ACCEPTANCE OF SEWERS; FINAL INSPECTION AND TESTS; FEES.
   (a)   A new sewer or old sewer, where changes or modifications have been
made thereto, shall not be accepted by the village until a final inspection is
made and the sewer is approved for public use by the Village Engineer. The
final inspection for all sanitary sewers shall include a leak test, a T.V.
inspection and a visual inspection. A low pressure air test or water
exfiltration test shall be performed by the contractor.
   (b)   The fee for T.V. inspection and testing for leaks of all sanitary
sewers constructed in a new subdivision under a private contract shall be paid
for by the subdivider, directly to the village.
   (c)   On an assessed project, after completion of the sewer and prior to
acceptance of the sewer by the village, there shall be a T.V. inspection and
testing for leaks of the sewer. The fee for this inspection shall be charged to
the project and included in its cost.
   (d)   The fee for final sewer inspection, including T.V. inspection and leak
testing, shall be the total cost of the man hours worked by the inspectors,
including insurance and overhead.
(`80 Code, § 1032.10) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82)
§ 1032.11 SEWER SIZE.
   No main sanitary sewer line in the village shall be less than eight inches
in diameter. No lateral sanitary sewer service connection in the village shall
be less than six inches in diameter.
(`80 Code, § 1032.11) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82; Ord. 2216, passed 6-1-98)
§ 1032.12 GUARDING EXCAVATIONS; REPAIRING PUBLIC PROPERTY.
   All excavations for building sewer installations shall be adequately guarded
with barricades and lights so as to protect the health, welfare and safety of
the public. Streets, sidewalks, parkways or other public property damaged in
the course of the work shall be restored in a manner satisfactory to the
village.
(`80 Code, § 1032.12) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82)
§ 1032.13 PAVEMENT OPENING PERMIT REQUIRED.
   When excavations for building sewer installations are made in a hard surface
pavement, i.e. portland cement concrete or asphaltic concrete, the sewer
builder shall secure a pavement opening permit from the Village Administrator.
(`80 Code, § 1032.13) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82)
§ 1032.14 CONDITIONS OF SEWER PERMIT; CAPACITY OF SYSTEM.
   No sewer permit shall be issued for any new connection to the treatment
works unless there is capacity in all downstream sewers, lift stations, force
mains and the treatment plant itself, including capacity for B.O.D., suspended
solids and phosphorus.
(`80 Code, § 1032.14) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82)
§ 1032.99 PENALTY; COSTS OF LITIGATION.
   (a)   Whoever violates or fails to comply with any of the provisions of this
chapter shall be fined not less than $100 nor more than $1,000, and imprisoned
not more than 30 days, for each offense. Each violation shall be considered a
separate offense.
   (b)   In addition to the penalty set forth in division (a) hereof, the
village may recover reasonable attorneys' fees, court costs, court reporters'
fees and other expenses of litigation by appropriate suit at law against the
person found to have violated, or found to have failed to comply with, any of
the provisions of this chapter or the orders, rules, regulations and permits
issued under this chapter.
(`80 Code, § 1032.99) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82)

§ 1034.01 PURPOSES AND INTENT.
   The purposes of this chapter are to provide the legislative enactments
required under Public Law 84-660, and any subsequent successor legislation, as
set forth in 33 USC 1251 et seq., as amended, and applicable federal
regulations for the acceptance of construction grants, to prevent the
introduction of pollutants into the village waste water system which will
interfere with the operation of the system or contaminate the resulting sludge,
to prevent the introduction of pollutants into the village waste water system
which will pass through the system, inadequately treated, into receiving waters
or the atmosphere or otherwise be incompatible with the system, to improve the
opportunity to recycle and reclaim waste waters and sludges from the system and
to provide for an equitable distribution of the cost of the village waste water
system.
(`80 Code, § 1034.01) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82)
§ 1034.02 UNSANITARY DEPOSITS.
   No person shall place, deposit or permit to be deposited in an unsanitary
manner on public or private property within the village, or in any area under
the jurisdiction of the village, any human or animal excrement, garbage or
other objectionable waste.
(`80 Code, § 1034.02) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82)
§ 1034.03 DRAINAGE INTO SANITARY SEWERS DURING CONSTRUCTION.
   No person, in constructing a sanitary sewer or building or house connection,
shall leave the same open, unsealed or incomplete in such a fashion as to
permit storm, surface or subsurface water to enter such sewer.
(`80 Code, § 1034.03) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82)
§ 1034.04 DISCHARGE OF UNPOLLUTED WATER INTO SANITARY SEWERS; CLEANOUTS.
   (a)   No person shall discharge or cause to be discharged any storm water,
surface water, ground water, roof run-off, subsurface drainage, uncontaminated
cooling water or unpolluted industrial process water to any sanitary sewer. All
exposed cleanouts shall be plugged with an expandable plug and covered in a
satisfactory manner. A map showing all new lines and the location of cleanouts
shall be filed with the village at the time of construction thereof.
   (b)   Storm water and all other unpolluted drainage shall be discharged to
such sewers as are specifically designated as combined sewers or storm sewers,
or to a natural outlet approved by the village. Industrial cooling water or
unpolluted process waters may be discharged, with the approval of the village,
to a storm sewer or natural outlet.
(`80 Code, § 1034.04) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82)
§ 1034.05 GENERAL PROHIBITED DISCHARGES.
   No user shall contribute or cause to be contributed, directly or indirectly,
any pollutant or waste water which will interfere with the operation or
performance of the publicly owned treatment works. This general prohibition
applies to all users of the publicly owned treatment works, whether or not the
user is subject to National Categorical Pretreatment Standards or any other
national, State or local pretreatment standard or requirement. A user may not
contribute the following substances to any publicly owned treatment works:
   (a)   Liquids, solids or gases which, by reason of their nature or quantity,
are or may be sufficient, either alone or by interaction with other substances,
to cause a fire or explosion or be injurious in any other way to the publicly
owned treatment works or to the operation thereof, or which, as discharged to
the public sewer, shall constitute a hazard to humans or animals, create a
public nuisance or create any hazard in the receiving waters of a sewage
treatment plant, including, but not limited to, those metals or toxic
substances mentioned in §
1034.06. At no time shall two successive readings on an explosion hazard meter,
at the point of discharge into the system (or at any point in the system), be
more than 5% nor shall any single reading be more than 10% of the Lower
Explosive Limit (LEL) of the meter. Prohibited materials include, but are not
limited to, gasoline, kerosene, naphtha, benzene, toluene, exylene, ethers,
alcohols, ketones, aldehydes, peroxides, chlorates, perchlorates, bromates,
carbides, hydrides, sulfides and any other substance which the village, the
State or the Environmental Protection Agency has notified the user is a fire
hazard or a hazard to the system.
   (b)   Solid or viscous substances which may cause obstruction to the flow in
a sewer or other interference with the operation of the waste water treatment
facilities, including, but not limited to, grease, garbage with particles
greater than one-half inch in any dimension, animal guts or tissues, paunch
manure, bones, hair, hides, fleshings, entrails, whole blood, feathers, ashes,
cinders, sand, spent lime, stone dust, marble dust, metal, glass, straw,
shavings, grass clippings, rags, spent grains, spent hops, waste paper, wood,
plastics, gas, tar, asphalt residues, residues from refining or processing of
fuel or lubricating oil, mud or glass grinding or polishing wastes.
(`80 Code, § 1034.05) (Ord. 1584, passed 10-18-82)
§ 1034.06 SPECIFIC PROHIBITED DISCHARGES.
   No person shall discharge or cause to be discharged the following described
substances, materials, waters or wastes if it appears likely that such wastes
can harm either the sewers, the sewerage system or equipment, or the sewage
treatment process or equipment, or have an adverse effect on the receiving
stream, or can otherwise endanger life, limb or public property or constitute a
nuisance. In forming its opinion as to the acceptability of these wastes, the
village shall give consideration to such factors as the quantity of subject
wastes in relation to flows and velocities in the sewers, materials of
construction of the sewers, the nature of the sewage treatment process, the
capacity of the sewage treatment plant, the degree of treatability of wastes in
the sewage treatment plant and other pertinent factors. The following
substances are prohibited:
   (a)   Maximum Allowable Temperature into Sewers or Waterways. Any liquid or
vapor having a temperature higher than 140°F or 60°C;
   (b)   Maximum Allowable Ether Solubles. Any water or waste containing fats,
wax, grease or oils, whether emulsified or not, in excess of 80 milligrams per
liter ether-soluble or containing substances which may solidify or become
viscous at temperatures between 32°F and 140°F, or 60°C;
   (c)   Regulation of Garbage Grinders. Any garbage that has not been properly
shredded. The installation and operation of any garbage grinder equipped with a
motor of three-fourths horsepower (0.76 hp metric) or greater shall be subject
to the review and approval of the village;
   (d)   Local Limits. The total quantity of pollutants that can be discharged
from industrial users to the Village of Jefferson's publicly owned treatment
works is contained in the following table with contributions from individual
establishments subject to control in volume and concentration by the village of
the Ohio Environmental Protection Agency:
Material Quantity
