September 24, 1997
Meeting was called to order by Mayor McCune.
Roll of Planning Commission: Cufr, Hansford, Masirovits, McCune, Ward
Also Present: Wilma Herndon, Mark Edelmann, Art Aho, David Parker, Bev Finger,
Terry Finger, Cayce Baxley, Richard Row, The Gazette
Topic: Medical Clinics
Zoning District Change - Jefferson Geriatric Center
Amendments to Zoning Codes
The Planning Commission discussed the Ashtabula County Medical Center and the
request to rebuild the clinic. The Villages Zoning does not cover clinics in
the text. To cover clinics the Village will have to change the Zoning under the
B1 Business District to include clinics instead of using the clinic under
permissive use in the Residential District.
Administrator Weir explained to the Planning Commission that Medical Clinics in
the Zoning text are under conditional use in the RD District, which is a Multi-
family District in the Village. There is no provision anywhere in the Zoning
Code to allow a Medical Clinic. The only thing the Village can do is amend the
Zoning Code to permit Medical Clinics in the B1 Business District.
Mayor W. McCune explained that if the Zoning was changed to read Medical Clinic
in the Business District, medical clinics with the conditional use then would
have to be taken out of the RD District in the Zoning text.
Dr. Parker explained that the addition of the building would help service the
patients with more examining rooms, also services that you would have to go out
of town for would be available at the clinic.
Motion by Hansford to recommend to have Council adopt a new revised section of
1246.04 Of the Codified Ordinance.
2nd by Ward
Roll: Cufr, yea; Hansford, yea; Masirovits, yea; McCune, yea; Ward, yea.
Mayor W. McCune told the Planning Commission that the recommendation would go
back to Council then there will be a scheduled hearing by the Council for the
change in the Zoning, then it will go to the three readings of the Ordinance.
Planning Commission discussed the issue of the Jefferson Geriatric Center. They
have plans for a Medical Clinic west of the Jefferson Geriatric Center on a two
acre site. The property is zoned Residential and the property to the Geriatric
Center is on Residential property with a permissive use.
The discussion from the last Council Meeting, Council felt that the proper way
to work with the clinic situation was to change the zoning on that property
from Residential with a Permissive Use to Business one (B1), which will allow
the clinic with the parking in the front.
Hansford voiced his concern if the clinic was approved would it conflict with
the development of Sycamore Street.
Mayor W. McCune told the Planning Commission the Clinic presented plans that
will meet all zoning requirements, if the zoning change is approved from
Residential to B1 Business. The clinic will not conflict with the development
of Sycamore Street.
T. Finger stated to the Commission the only reason Council was concerned with
Sycamore Street was if the street was changed to a truck route, the owner of
the Geriatric Center stated earlier he was worried about fumes. With the new
clinics plans it will be closer to a industrial lot and truck route. The Zoning
Text the Village has now does not prevent industrial smelter. That is why
Council voiced a concern.
Mayor McCune told the Commission no matter what is built there it will still be
subject to fumes.
Motion by Ward to recommend to Council to change the Clinics Zoning from
Residential to B1 Business.
2nd by Masirovits
Roll: Cufr, yea; Hansford, yea; Masirovits, yea; McCune, yea; Ward, yea.
Ward told the Planning Commission the Buildings and Lands Committee has been
working on updating the zoning codes. There is a folder with all the
information on what they have been working on, which will eventually come to
the Planning Commission, the committee would appreciate any input.
Meeting Adjourn.
Respectfully Submitted,
Patricia A. Fisher

June 19, 1998
Planning Commission Members:
I've been on the Planning Commission for the past three years and I feel this
request is the most difficult to decide, so far. I would like to add to our
businesses and tax base, and I believe Ducro Funeral Homes would be a welcomed
business. Competition is good for all citizens of any Village - Unfortunately,
I am against this change because of the location and the amount of land that is
being requested to be changed. Since I've been on the Planning Commission we
have added to our B1 district and have changed the piece of land where the
Geriatric Center sits to B1 for a technical reason ( because they wanted to add
a small clinic), but, that development has been there for over 10 years.
I feel changing a large portion of land outside the B1 district could be
detrimental to the heart of the Village. Once we change the use, it is out of
our control. I've heard this statement a lot over the past three years. "It
could really change the way this Village looks." Well, this time I kind of
agree with it. It is this Planning Commissions decision, it could be overruled
by the Village Council. This decision could really effect this town. I am as a,
Councilman, Planning Commission member and a life long resident, urging a "NO"
vote - As I stated before, I would welcome Ducro Funeral Home to Jefferson, but
not under the terms we are currently reviewing.
Thank You,
Edwin J. Ward

Meeting called to Order by Mayor McCune
Roll: Cufr, Masirovits, McCune, Ward, Hansford.
Also Present: Terry Finger, Tim Lemire, Administrator Dan Weir, The Gazette
M. McCune - Asked Dan to explain the new Subdivision Regulations.
D. Weir - Explained the new version and how it brought the old zoning up to
date with new information, also incorporated information from sidewalks,
curbing etc. Added definitions where needed, soil conditions, flood plain,
erosion control, water supply, fire hydrant locations, sewers, testing methods,
what criteria is needed , traffic patterns, street names, blocks, geometric
designs, pavement widths, vertical alignments, subgrades, storm drainage, off
street parking, added a section in so that the Planning Commission has the
ability to look at possible growth near or adjacent to a new development, for
major growth. Surveying and monumentation, so everything is properly marked,
lot layouts, buffer - currently 40 feet, Residential vs. Commercial now we are
saying 100 feet. Also, asking that the developer provide at lease 2% of the
total acreage for public parks or green areas, so we don't get a situation with
all development, and no greenery. Tree planting, asking the developer to
provide some type of plan.
G. Hansford - Is this going to cause a upheaval, is there a grandfather clause?
D. Weir - Yes.
G. Hansford - Is this radical enough to open a bees nest?
D. Weir - I don't know.
G. Hansford - I understand , we need an upgrade. I would like to see us avoid
the same situation as we had with the Comprehensive Plan.
D. Weir - Now the property owner is basically responsible for the things that
they want done.
M. McCune - Changing this into this type of document, doing this will save
Council a lot of indecision, 20% want to pave, 40% don't, long meetings, etc. A
lot less of the people getting the Village to do this, now the people have to
do it. I don't think this is that radical. Once we adopt this document should
be the law in developing subdivisions. If we are going to adopt this, let's
make sure we are all on the same page.

Zoning Board
December 17, 1996 (Hearing)
Zoning Board Members Present: T. Colucci, Chairman, Walter Horowski, Wilma
Herndon, Linda Nemet, Brad Childs
Also Present: Mr. & Mrs. Lew Hayslett, Mr. & Mrs. Robert Cornell, Administrator
Dan Weir
Purpose of meeting: to review code for: Lew Hayslett for yard variance required
for construction of a personal storage warehouse.
L. Hayslett - A year ago May I bought the property. During the process of
buying the property I inquired to Dan Weir about using the property for more
mini-storages. He notified me on the facts that were required. Also we
discussed the possibility of changing the deed of that property to go in with
mini-storage, but we did not do it. We need 117 feet left from the house and
that would give me seventy-two hundred fifty-four feet we need for the lot. 72
hundred is required for the lot for zoning.
D. Weir - The lot that is there is a real narrow lot, it is only 62 feet wide.
The average building lot in the Village is at least 75 feet wide.
L. Hayslett - So, we have proposed with the Zoning boards approval a building
of six thousand and eight square feet building. I feel the building we already
have are an asset to the Village. We have paid about four thousand three
hundred dollars in real estate taxes in the last year plus income tax. I think
this is for the good of the property and the Village. The property is
commercial property already. If I have understood right, commercial property in
the Village you need to be five feet from the property line. We are asking the
side yard according to the zoning is twenty feet, we are asking to pick-up four
more feet.
T. Colucci - The five members of the board are not professionals. Our job is to
help the Zoning Commission on making decisions for Zoning Appeals. We use
common sense, no law tells us what to do. It is a matter of judgement on all
parties.
Mrs. Cornell - First of all Lew, I think Zoning Laws state for a resident at
least for commercial property you have to stay forty feet away from us because
we are a resident. That is not the thing of it, you said you would come no
further than our picket fence. Which would leave our small backyard open. With
the variance the fence will come one foot from our line. There is no angle from
our side yard or back yard that we will not see that building. We have no
problems if you just let us have our small backyard open, you can build
anything in the back.
L. Hayslett - Mrs. Cornell you said if we build a privacy fence that would be
okay.
Mrs. Cornell - I did not know what else to do. I did not understand the laws or
had anyone to talk to.
L. Nemet - Do you know how much feet back you are asking about?
Mrs. Cornell - Our fence is about forty feet back from our garage, and that is
where we asked him to have the building stop at.
L. Hayslett - If I do that I will not have very much of a building.
D. Weir - I think there has been there has been some confusion in regards to
the setback that is aloud for personal storage units under normal conditions in
a commercial district a five foot side yard is acceptable for any business. In
a B1 Business district you need a 40 foot front yard, five foot side yard and a
20 foot rear. Under what Lew is proposing the building would actually be part
of the existing buildings that are there. That would all be considered one lot
even though it is made up of three lots. The building would have a Cedar Street
address. He would have normally had to have a twenty-five foot rear yard, so
the variance would be nine feet in the rear. If the building would have a
Chestnut Street address and be separate from the other buildings he would have
had to have a twenty foot side yard requirement and he would be going for a
four foot variance. Under another section that tells what permissive uses are,
there is another section on storage units that require the side yard distance
shall be twenty feet exactly where residential use and then it would be forty
feet if you take all the requirements in there it narrows Lew's property to a
two foot wide strip down the center to build on. It is a very complicated
situation because of the special requirement, it is a tough zoning call.
T. Colucci - Things are changing around Jefferson, all the property zoned
around you is commercial.
W. Horowski - Is there anything wrong with making it smaller?
L. Hayslett - Before I could answer that question I would have to have her
actually stake off how far it would go. I would have to have accurate
measurements.
Mrs. Cornell - There is people in and out of there all the time, there is a lot
of traffic.
L. Hayslett - The basic lot will be fenced in. So we will not be having
problems with kids because they would be trapped in with the fence.
Mrs. Cornell - What is the actual variance?
D. Weir - It would be twenty-four foot on the South side and it then would be
twenty-four foot on the North side..
Mrs. Cornell - Then there is actually is not enough property there. You
wouldn't be willing to exchange your 30 foot building for forty-five feet of
storage.
L. Hayslett - I am saying before I say anything, I would have to measure before
I could commit myself. You will still see the building unless I put up a fence.
Mrs. Cornell - If you put up a fence, it will close us in with the fence.
D. Weir - We are going to run into this more and more of this, mainly because
all we have left for commercial property is redeveloped, there is no vacant
left for development. We will have business next to residential houses.
L. Nemet - Where is the land zoned commercial?
D. Weir - Commercial actually runs from Beech all the way to Mulberry street.
It varies, some places it is four hundred fifty feet most of the lots are three
hundred feet.
W. Horowoski - My suggestion would be that Lew work out something with the
Cornell's and come back . I can not see myself approving this, the variance is
too much.
D. Weir - You are asking for basically twenty-four feet.
L. Nemet - The reality of that is this is a piece of commercial property that
is waiting to be developed.
Mrs. Cornell - We are residential and by rights he can not come four feet from
our property.
Mr. Cornell - How far does he have to stay off the property line?
D. Weir - The Zoning Board of Appeals could make that determination. Under
normal conditions the business can be built from five feet from the property
line.
T. Colucci - Let me ask a question, Mr. and Mrs. Cornell, if Mr. Hayslett's
property fit within the zoning law and did not have to come to this hearing,
how would you feel?
Mrs. Cornell - If it would go the length of our property I would feel bad.
T. Colucci - You really do not want a building there?
Mrs. Cornell - I do not want the building in that forty feet by our back yard
and we do not want a privacy fence behind our picket fence. We want just the
picket fence to our house. All we ask is just that forty some feet so we have
an open yard.
L. Hayslett - The curbs will be set up so the water will stay on our property
and keep people from sliding into the fence in the winter. They will be within
thirteen feet from the line.
W. Herndon - Is there any other way you could put the building further East or
any other way you could appease their feelings?
L. Hayslett - No, not really because of the drainage and the water.
W. Herndon - We have never done a variance of this size before.
D. Weir - There is a lot of confusion under normal conditions. The section that
provides for set backs, if Lew's building would face Cedar Street under normal
circumstances it would be twenty-five foot set back rear yard and five foot
side yard. If he was going to let the building be a Chestnut Street address the
North line would be a side yard which would allow for a five foot set back. In
the Zoning Code it is really confusing how they have it set up. His building
applies to special set backs, which requires his side yard to be twenty feet
for a storage facility. Except for where there is residential use it is forty
feet. It goes according to what the property is to be used for. Basically what
we are looking at, Lew needs a forty foot set back from the North line of his
property which is next to the Cornell's. He is seeking a sixteen foot set back,
so he is actually requesting a twenty-four foot variance.
W. Horowoski - From what I can see the main purpose of the board is to protect
the property owner - if we would allow it there could be a kickback
(consequences) and the board could be sued.
B. Childs - We are supposed to be 50/50 and our main objective is for what is
best for the Village and property and work something out for everyone. If Lew
puts up a nice privacy fence no one will know the buildings are there.
Mrs. Cornell - There still will be the storage units on the other side, traffic
in and out. We should have some rights.
L. Nemet - This is still commercial property.
D. Weir - The powers of the Zoning board are to interrupt the zoning codes and
decide appeals where it is alleged that there is a error and order the required
decision made by the Zoning Inspector and permit variances and regulate the
Zoning Code with reasonable and sensible arrangements of buildings on a lot.
L. Hayslett - Are you saying if I took forty foot of the building I could get
it approved Mr. Cornell, the Zoning Board would give me the approvals.
Mr. Cornell - It would be from the fence, I really do not know the distance I
am not sure of the footage.
L. Nemet - What would the increments be, you can not just say I will take forty
feet off.
L. Hayslett - If I do this will the Cornell's accept this? I would have to come
back with new figures.
T. Colucci - Why don't we vote on why we are here today, on what we have there
is only one person next to his property that does not want the variance. There
is other people next to the property and they are not hear, so they are not
against it.
Mrs. Cornell - We are they only ones that will be effected with the variance.
L. Hayslett - I would consider taking the forty feet off, but I would have to
look at it.
W. Herndon - My concern is that this would be a twenty-four foot variance and
we are changing zoning. I suggest come up with another plan.
L. Nemet - Lew wants the new section to be treated just like the other
buildings.
Motion by Linda Nemet to accept the variance as it is written.
2nd by Childs
Roll: Nemet, yea; Horowski, nay; Herndon, nay; Childs, yea; Colucci, yea.
Meeting adjourn.
Respectfully Submitted,
Patricia A. Fisher,
Clerk/Treasurer

Visitors:
J. Fink - question on progress on complaints on property on North Market. The
Administrator said a little work had been done. Our Solicitor is preparing a
letter to the property owner regarding the complaints and setting a time limit
to respond with action. Fink asked if the removal of the building, which he
says is on his property, can be included in the clean up job. Building has been
there for years - years. Could it be cited as a safety or fire hazard and
approached in that manner. The Solicitor advised him that she doesn't see
anything in our code to give Council the authority to move the building, that
Fink may have a civil action through his own lawyer. If Council deems it a fire
hazard it may be approached in that way. The County Building Department has
some authorities also. Action is being taken - letter will be delivered to the
man with a time period to respond.
Debbie Brininger, representing the JayCee women and JayCees, presented Council
with documents stating the funds needed to run Safety Town and additional
teaching aids they would like to obtain, and was inquiring on securing funds
from the village to support the program. Free materials are no longer available
causing a financial problems; also would like to relieve the need to approach
the local businesses who have been very cooperative in the past. On reviewing
the list it was determined that the village could help with the paint and
striping, the police department could make copies needed, thus cutting some of
the expenses. Motion made by Roach to fund the amount of $625.00 requested for
additional teaching aids, from Federal Revenue Sharing Funds, second by Butler,
roll - Hruska, yea; Butler, yea; Nemet, yea; Herndon, yea; McCune, yea; Roach,
yea.
Committee Reports:
Wastewater Treatment:  
Work session held on Industrial Waste Survey. Motion made by Herndon to
authorize Jeffrey Pizel to purchase wastewater sampling equipment up to value
of $3,000.00, 2nd by Roach, roll - Roach, yea; Hruska, yea; McCune, yea; Nemet,
yea; Herndon, yea; Butler, yea. The village can utilize the engineers as
consultants. roll - Roach, yea; Hruska, yea; McCune, yea; Nemet, yea; Herndon,
yea; Butler, yea. Alarm system from plant to police department does not work
are looking into another system. Rodding maintenance program started today.
Utilities: 
Letter from Ohio Water Service on fire flows noted that new lines have greatly
increased the GPM - at Cucumber and Jefferson, from 260 GPM to 1280 GPM; at
Sycamore and Cedar from 75 GPM to 860 GPM.
Finance: 
Council by consensus approved the expenditure of $50.00 to the American Legion
for Memorial Day expenses. Council will be reviewing the recent Supreme Court
decision effecting overtime pay for employees of the village; also village
vehicle use as reportable to the IRS.
Safety: 
With the recommendation of Chief Johnson and the Mayor, motion made by Nemet to
approve the appointment of Okeylene Miller from the police auxiliary to a full
time police officer effective June 1, 1985 on probationary basis, second by
McCune, - Executive session was requested to discuss this personnel matters
return to regular session. roll - McCune, yea; Roach yea; Herndon, yea; Nemet,
yea; Butler, yea; Hruska, yea.
Light at 307/46/167 - will be up by July 4th. Comparator is in - Hopkins
completed schooling last week at London. Monthly activity report given to
Council.
Buildings/Land Use:
The Administrator is in process of running down people who have high grass at
residences or properties. He stated that there is a possibility of purchasing
some adjacent land at the Street Department garage area.
Service: 
Mulberry Street looks goods; Engineers will be reviewing for recommendation on
opening and accepting improvements. A copy of a petition sent to Dr. Behr of
the school system was given to Council. Signers of the petition object to the
use of Satin Street for school buses. Administrator will check with Dr. Behr.
Creek cleaning project involves quite a few properties, will be trying to get
easements, hope to get to in July during dry time.
Officials: 
Aerial maps are in. A zoning permit was issued today for a video shop in
Marie's Dress shop; proposed use of old Abernathy location not known yet; meat
market proposed for Village Boutique building; beauty shop will too to house in
the rear, Utterbacks building a new home on North Market; GE deal looks good;
nothing on Namco firmed up. The Mayor declared the week of May 20th as Poppy
Week.
The Clerk attended a meeting held by the County Health Department on setting up

stages with good prospects for development.

Visitors: 
Council received the financial report on the two phases of the water line
project completed by Ohio Water. Mr. Seese stated these have already made a big
difference in the flows, with the completion of the Market and Mulberry phase
flows will improve even more. The ISO has changed the fire class for the
schools through the efforts of Ohio Water and the retesting figures given to
ISO. Mr. DeArment stated that when the total program for the project is
completed the village may achieve a 4 rating. Ohio Water will be back in the
fall with suggestions to effect a better job.
Charles Thomas: - Thousand Trails submitted a letter to Council proposing the
construction of a line to tie into the Village Wastewater Treatment plant
services at Woodside. Proposal is to construct a 4" forcemain sewer which will
tie into the manhole located on Woodside Avenue, will transfer ownership of the
line to the village, but should any new development tap into this line they
would like to recoup a portion of their capitol investment in this line.
Council has scheduled a work session for Monday, June 24th at 7:30 PM with the
village engineer present to review the project, to review the current ordinance
requiring the annexation to have the service, the legalities of ownership
outside the village, etc. Mr. Borsukoff, as one of the developers who has put
money into the Sewer Improvement Fund for future update of the pump station,
stated their proposal makes a lot of sense and opens up for further future
development in the area. Thomas stated it was a matter of economics on their
parts with having to meet EPA criteria if they wish to expand their camp
grounds, and would not be able to use the lake if have to use their own
facility, and cited the expense of operator and operation.
W. Metzdorf-Margie Jones: Rich Butler and Rick Nemet met in a work session with
the Rec Board for the purpose of planning and determining the feasibility of
putting in a swimming pool for the villages land is under option adjacent to
the Village Park on East Jefferson Street, type of pool - for summer season
only - 15 x 25 meter size with fenced area and grassed area, 50% reimbursement
grant is available through the Ohio Department of Natural Resources. They are
asking Council to pass a resolution to apply for the grant of estimated
$250,000 on the $500,000 estimated cost of the pool. Application deadline is
July 1, 1985. There may be other grants around to come up with some of the
match. Council was told that even if grant comes, if we can't come up with the
money, we can refuse it. Even though the resolution used the term ‘the
Council of the Village of Jefferson, Ohio hereby does agree to obligate the
funds required to satisfactorily complete the proposed project and thus be come
eligible for Land and Water Conservation Fund Act financial aid of up to 50% of
the actual allowable reimbursement cost,’ the village would not be obligated.
Metzdorf stated that after review, if chosen, then we get further application,
at that time we can say no.
Questions raised were if village would have the funding to match, could a
community of this size support the operation of a pool, could it be put on the
ballot. Motion to hear the first reading of Resolution No. 1686, second by
Nemet, roll - Hruska, no; McCune, yea; Herndon, yea; Roach, yea; Nemet, yea.

Visitors:
Ken Ward, Jesse Fink, Sue Valek - concern is still with the clean up of the
Nizen property on North Market Street. What he has done looks good, asked
Council if this could be stepped up a little more. There are two cars there
yet, along with a semi trailer, rocks, cement blocks, branches not off yet. It
was reported that there are rats in the building and area, that the safety of
children is a great concerns that they would like to see clean up done before
school starts. They feel the time is overdue, he’s made it better, but that's
not what they petitioned for. Solicitor told Council that if we are at the
point where we feel we should take criminal action, then up to the police to
enforce the appropriate ordinance, warn him before issuing any citations. The
Mayor will meet with the Chief and pursue this issuev however, the Mayor stated
he does not like to take a hard nose approach, feels the man has done a lot.
Westfall also reported that Nizen has men working there.

Finance:
Safety: 
The village has been notified by the Ashtabula County Commissioners that
effective October 2, 1985, prisoner care rates will be $52.00 per day, village
also responsible for medical bills incurred by any prisoner. Ordinance! will be
prepared authorizinq execution of contract submitted.
McCune said he was displeased with the police coverage over the weekend with
the Street Fair, feels that concern for the village safety rather than concern
about overtime should be primary. The Mayor didn't feel they were doing that,
that we were short, with men on vacation and auxiliary not available. There is
a need to recruit more auxiliary people.
Buildings/Land Use:
The administrator will contact real estate agency on mowing lawn at the former
Connors place on West Satin Street.
The Mayor and council members reported receiving numerous phone calls on the
applying for grant funds for a swimming pool in the village, opinions were both
pro and con, some felt it is too much expense for the village, some a qeneral
no interests location questioned, could enough money be generated to run it,
how many months in use. Nemet asked if the people who called understood that we
donòt have to come up with the money. Butler stated that the public doesn’t
understand village funding. Stan Zwaduk told Council that if the park would
improve it would draw people to that area, he questioned where the pool was
planned for, since he was unable to get an answer from the director. He asked
questions on cost to maintain pool, was not provided with an answer; where is
money coming from, can we support it, will a levy be needed to maintain this
size pool. Since the need to better inform the public was apparent, a motion
was made by Nemet to table Resolution 1686, second by Roach, roll Nemet, yea;

Wastewater Treatment: 
Beds dried up, being cleaned. Sampler in. will be put to use soon. Village
Council reveived a letter from the Village Engineer regarding the proposal by
Thousand Trails to come into the village treatment system. His evaluation was
based on the flow data provided by 1000 trails, population figures from The
Ashtabula Planning Commission,and .his calculations. It is the engineer's
opinion that this connection will not limit unrestricted growth in the village.
The connection may be permitted under Chapter 1030.21(b) of the Codified
Ordinances of the village. Motion made by Herndon to agreement in principal by
Council, accepting sewage to the village Wastewater Treatment plant pending
agreement of Council and Village Engineer on specifics to be used, second by
Roach, roll : McCune, yea; Hruska, yea; Roach, yea; Herndon, yea; Butler, yea;
Nemet, yea. 1000 Trails will obtain needed agreements from the County and
Townships. County Sanitary Engineer Clutter has said that from environmental
standpoint, force main is preferable way to go. 1000 Trails will also agree to
time and materials basis to maintain the line.
Utilities: 
Ohio Water flushing in Jeffersonian Estates area. Question was raised on who
repairs streets damaged by trucks. With the construction of the mobile home
park, traffic has been heavier. Unless it can be shown that flagrant damage was
done, the village is responsible. Spots on West Jefferson Street that were
patched by Ohio Water are of temporary nature, permanent type patching will be
done.

Committe will review the possible purchase of the Hurst tool from the County.

occasions under mutual aid as needed.
Buildings/Land Use:
Council was advised that the Jefferson Planning Commission rejected the
proposed ordinance for the rezoning of two properties on West Walnut, as
requested by the County, because responses for concerns were not available. A
county representative was not able to attend the meeting. Concerns were for
drainage, use of building, parking, whether rear yard was to be paved, if
rezoned, what would be disposition of property if sold by the County. Council
was advised the building will be used for Eber Wright’s office for Ashtabula
County development, location convenient and handy to other County offices. In
his current office at the bank his hours are limited to bank hours. Butler
suggested that to ease the minds of people involved, have a conditional use of
the residence as an office, thus maintaining the residential zoning. This would
go through the Board of Zoning Appeals, with ten days notice needed for
hearing.
Motion made by Butler to approve application of conditional use submittal to
the Jefferson Board of Zoning Appeals,for two properties on West Walnut Street,
second by Nemet, roll - Herndon, yea; Butler, yea; Nelet, yea; Hruska, yea;
Roach, yea; McCune, yea. Rear yard of Duttons will not be paved.
Swimming pool - Marjorie Jones of the Rec Board and W. Metzdorf, Director again
tried to assure council and those present that the procedure in process is only
support to go after grant for funding, that the village does not have to come
up with any money, that if grant application approved, then up to Board to come
up with matching funds from other sources. Questions were still raised on
liability, on maintenance costs and who will pay, and how additional funding
will be obtained. If eligible, and grant approved, village can still say 'no'.
Solicitor verified that in her contact with ODNR, the word ‘obligate’ does not
mean village has to put money aside or come up with it. Nemet put Resolution
No. 1686 rack on the table. Motion made by Nemet to hear the second reading of
Resolution No. 1686, second by Herndon, roll - McCune, yea; Butler, yea;
Hruska, no; Roach, yea; Nemet, yea; Herndon, yea.

Stump chipper purchase - Solicitor checked with the Ohio Municipal League, they
stated that if Council can show a true emergency, it can waive the requirement
for bid advertising. If not, they recommended advertising for bid since total
cost would exceed the $5000 limit. The administrator was advised that if the
equipment can be obtained for $4999, then go ahead with the purchase, if not,
then ordinance to be prepared to advertise. With Federal Revenue Sharing monies
being used, it was advisable to follow the proper procedure.

Motion made by Butler to approve bills, second by Herndon, roll - McCune, yea;
Butler, yea; Hruska, yea; Herndon, yea; Roach, yea; Nemet, yea.
Visitors:
Jim Bowler and Duane Ball, represented Tele Communications. Recent and ongoing
problems in village cable reception resulted in their being asked to attend.
They advised council that a number of things cause problems - weather,
equipment failure, having to wait for parts sometimes. They stated there are
always going to be problems, when it does go out, people should call, company
will investigate and correct as soon as possible. According to their reports
complaints from the village have decreased to an average of three a day, which
is a big improvement over last year before all the changes were made. They were
advised that a number of complaints received are due to the response from the
company's phone answering staff, rudeness and indistinct answers. Company asked
that they be advised of any problems, that they would respond. They will also
check into some lines that seem to be low on Uselma, Willis, Mulberry, Erie,
and Elm, creating problems for trucks when they have to tailgate when plowing.

Motion made by Butler to approve the bills, second by Herndon, roll - Herndon,
yea; McCune, yea; Hruska, yea; Nemet, yea; Roach, yea; Butler, yea.
Visitors: 
JayCees representatives D. Brininger, L. Ewing and J. Baker presented plaques
of appreciation for services to Chief Johnson for the Police Department and to
Nemet for the Jefferson Volunteer Fire Department. Council, the village and
street crews were also thanked for their aid and support of the Safety Town
program this year.
R. Reitz asked if Halloween 'trick or treat' night could be coordinated with
other municipalities because of the large influx of kids when the nights are
different. The Mayor stated that the village has designated October 31st from
5:00 to 7:30 PM for 'trick or treat' night.
K. Ward/J. Fink attended council meeting to ask what's going to be done on
Nizen property. The building has loose shingles, still junk in yard and old
vehicles remain; that it is a safety hazard for children crossing his property.
The Administrator and the Mayor both stated they felt he has cleaned up the
place a lot and is working every day on this; that the things required by the
County Health Department have been done satisfactorily; commercial area is
being prepared so that Nizen can park his equipment there. It was stated that
people don't have any business on his property, they are trespassing, that the
parents should keep their kids off, not the village's position to do this. As
to the loose shingles - if anything interfered with the sidewalk or right of
way, then the village might have responsibility. Nizen's building does not. The
solicitor again stated that if there are criminal violations they should be
brought to the police department.

With the recommendation of the Administrator, motion made by Butler to accept
the bid of Koski Construction in the amount of $37,136.50 for the paving
project '85, second by Hruska, roll - Butler, yea; Roach, yea; Nemet, yea;
Herndon, yea; McCune, yea; Hruska, yea.
With the recommendation of the Administrator and the Street Foreman, motion
made by Butler to place Danny Hubbard on regular employment and off probation
in position as Driver-Laborer in the Street Department, second by Herndon, roll
- McCune, yea; Roach, yea; Hruska, yea; Herndon, yea; Nemet, yea; Butler, yea.
Council received letters from H. Frayer regarding the losing of village trees
due to mower damage. The administrator also expressed his concern on this with
mowers causing barking and scarring trees causing rotten spots which inhibit
tree growth or kills than. It has been recommended that a protective product
"LOREGUARD" be used next year along with a circle of wood chips around the
tree. Plans are to distribute brochures and letter requesting the property
residents to cooperate in our efforts to save the trees.
Clean up on the Market/Mulberry water line project is slow, stop signs also
need to be reset. Road is also breaking up quite a bit. Ohio Water Service and
contractor are responsible.
Wastewater Treatment 
A sewer jetting program for the whole village has been set up and will be
started shortly.

exception of the results of the psychological tests. Roll - Hruska, yea;

The Solicitor was requested to prepare proper legislation for executing fire
service contracts with the townships.
Buildings/Land Use: 
Council has received an application for a D3 permit from the Ohio Department of
Liquor Department for Gloria Jean Capone dba Wooden Nickel Saloon. A D3 permit
allows spirituous liquor for on the premises consumption only until 1:00 AM.
Architects J. Rembowski and Ray Bordwell, Bob Ross and Robert Maddon showed
drawings and plans on the current concept the Village Rec Board is considering
for a Community Center. Plan could be done in phases with gym an air-supported
enclosure along with support building as the first phase and multi purpose
structure as phase 2, a total of 15,000 sq.ft. or less as economics indicates.
The project is still in the pre-application stages, next step is the
architect's agreement which is a requirement of the FHA., next a legal service
agreement. Council concurred on the board's continuing to look for funding and
facts leading to an ultimate decision. The Solicitor has been asked to review
the architect's agreement and will also review the contract of the village with
Colpetzer-Thomas, Inc.- village engineers. The Solicitor was requested to
prepare legislation authorizing the village administrator to prepare
specifications and advertise for bids for a passenger vehicle for senior
transportation.

Present at meeting: Stan Zwaduk, Chief Ken Johnson, Gloria Capone, Dawn Capone,

Beacon
Visitors: 
Recently a resident in the Elliott Allotment built a three car garage on a lot
adjoining a lot on which his home is located. Mr. Niemeyer asked Council if
there was any way this could be prevented from occurring again. A Zoning Permit
has been issued under the village zoning regulations, but interpretation of
deed restrictions differ. Plans as presented to the Zoning Inspector indicated
the garage was located on the lot so as to build a home later, that deed
restrictions did not indicate house or garage be built first. Concern over the
upkeep of the property should the current move away and the possibility of
garages springing up on other lots were expressed by Mr. Niemeyer. It was
suggested that the homeowners in the allotment form an association as has been
done in other allotment to address these any any other problems they foresee
and to review their deed restrictions.
The Capones attended Council regarding the application they have into the
Liquor Control Department for a D3 permit. As an adjoining property owner,
Westfall voiced an objection, stating there has been an improvement, but there
have been occasions of fights outside, late, at times till 3 or 4 in the
morning, music overly loud and disturbing. The Capones purchased the Wooden
Nickel in the spring, they also live next to the business, and are trying to
respond to any problems there may be, and also realize they are in a
residential area. They intend to continue to address the problems. Chief
Johnson stated they have had very few complaints and minimum problems since the
Capones have owned it. Mrs. Capone told council the police are welcome anytime,
call if you have a complaint.
Gary Fusco of Ohio Water Service advised council that their crews are now doing
the clean up and finishing on the Market/Mulberry water line project, that they
hope to have it all connected by Friday. They have also assured property owners
that finish up will be done, in some areas in the spring for best results.
Marjorie Jones of the Village Rec Board requested an Executive Session to
discuss land acquisition. Return to regular meeting.

Buildings/Land Use:   
Motion made by Butler to hear the first reading of Ordinance No. 1701, second
by Roach. Discussion - The proposed ordinance was for the purchase of lane
adjacent to the present park on East Jefferson Street. It was McCune's feeling
that the village cannot afford a community center of the proposed cost and
magnitude, therefore we should not purchase the land. Hruska concurred. He was
in favor of expansion but at a pace and under a schedule the village can
afford. He also felt that the community center with proposed programccould not
pay for their proposal, thus village would have to make payments and jeopardize
village finances. Mrs. Jones stated that if the board didn't feel they could do
it, they wouldn't of proposed it; asked if the village had any money to put
forth and how much would village obligate. Council will have to review this
aspect. It was suggested that we still look for building or other than this one
proposed. McCune felt a total of $350,000 to $400,00 over a period of time
would be reasonable. Since there were not enough votes available for passage of
ordinance, Butler retracted his motion. It was suggested that we look at going
to the voters for acceptance. Nemet stated he could see both sides as did
Roach.

Two resumes have been received for patrol employment. Chief Johnson will be

Market/Jefferson Streets intersection, and advised to also be alert at other
intersections as well. The Mayor reported on a recent meeting with Senator R.
Boggs and F. Fisher and others from ODOT at which the village requested a
survey and recommendation for addressing the Market/Mulberry intersection,
where a number of accidents, problem, also to review other intersections on the
state highway system. Snow ban on parking is in effect, also plowing snow into
the streets is not allowed, nor is blocking of sidewalks with snow allowed.
Building/Land Use: 
The village has received a liquor permit application from the Ohio Department
of Liquor Control for a Jimmy Brown, address 113 North Chestnut, Jefferson,
Ohio.The address is the Miller Realty Company. Permit applied for is a "D5".
McCune felt we should request a hearing on this, that if the applicant intends
to use the permit outside of the village, it should not be allowed. Motion made
by Butler to advise the Ohio Department of Liquor Control that the village
requests a hearing on the advisability of issuing this permit, and that the
hearing be held in the county seat, second by McCune, roll - Roach, yea;
Butler, yea; Herndon, yea; McCune, yea; Hruska, yea.
The Rec Board reported that they didn't feel it was advisable to go to the
ballot in May, that information is not fully compiled. They also asked that the
village council make some definitive decision on support of a community center
- with land or monies.
The Mayor called an Executive Session on the matter of real estate.

up.
Wastewater Treatment:

The Mayor requested an Executive Session relative to personnel matters. Return
to regular meeting.
Two members of the Jefferson Police Auxiliary have submitted applications for
the vacancies in the police roster, Rick Titus and Tim Blon. Titus has
considerable experience in the field of law, is a paramedic also. With the
recommendation of the Chief and the committee, motion was made by Nemet to
approv the appointment of Rick Titus to a Patrolman III classification, under
the six month probationary requirement, second by McCune, roll - Herndon, yea;
McCune, yea; Hruska, yea; Butler, yea; Roach, yea; Nemet, yea.
With the recommendation of the Chief and the committee, motion was made by
Nemet to approve the appointment of Tim Blon to a Patrolman I classification,
under the six month probationary requirement, second by McCune, roll - Nemet,
yea; Herndon, yea; Hruska, yea; McCune, yea; Roach, yea; Butler, yea.
Both appointments are effective January 1, 1986. Several officers of the police
department recently attended weapons qualifications at the County Sheriffs
Department range. Maximum score was 240 pts. Blon - 200; Febel - 215; Titus -
213; Gollon - 203. Febel was only officer to fire and qualify in his department
uniform. In response to complaint last meeting on violations at the Market/
Jefferson intersection, the police department has been observing. A letter has
been received by the village from ODOT outlining some recommendations that
might possibly improve traffic control at the Market/Mulberry intersection,
including some different signs and trimming row of pine trees west of the
intersection.
Buildings/Land Use: 
The village has received a liquor permit application from the Ohio Department
of Liquor Control for extension of hours to 2:30 AM by the Wooden Nickle.
Motion made by McCune that we request a hearing be held locally, second by
Butler, roll - Butler, yea; Hruska, yea; Nemet, yea; Herndon, yea; Roach, yea;
McCune, yea. Letter received from Heritage Hills expressing concerns about what
they feel are inequities which exist between the development and the village of
Jefferson. Points will be reviewed for a future discussion with the development
residents.
McCune asked Council to consider the construction of a gazebo, possibly on one
of the village greens, which could be utilized by all in the village. Mr.
Frayer stated council could make such a decision, but 'where will it stop'
regarding the use of village green.
Letter from the Ohio Department of Liquor Control requested status of 113 North
Chestnut Street rendered on application of Jimmy Brown for a permit. They will
be notified that this property has been in the village since 1806.
Motion made by Butler to hear the first reading of Ordinance No. 1705, in toto,
second by McCune. Discussion: This ordinance as proposed would abolish the
Recreation Board and establish a steering committee, thus putting the operation
of the rec department under control of the administration and council, an
authority which they relinquished when board was first formed. Some feelings
were that this method will expedite plans for recreational facilities which the
board has been working so hard on, but have not been able to obtain a definite
commitment from council when it came right down to making a decision.It is
hoped that the rec board members would continue as part of the steering
committee, all the work they have done is valuable for future progression. A
temporary special committee of council has been set up, with McCune as
chairman, Butler, and Herndon. Legislation defining the duties of the director
needs to be acted on. It is hoped with the new format proposed an impetus will
be created with the two factions working together. The Grange also expressed
concern on where they stand, since their building is leased for the community
center. Committee and Rec Board, which will remain in control until such time
as other action is indicated. roll - McCune, yea; Roach, yea; Nemet, abstained;
Butler, yea; Herndon, yea; Hruska, abstained.

   MAYOR'S ADDRESS
During this past year we have accomplished much by drafting meaningful
legislation to protect and benefit our community, and to deal with the
complexities of the operation of this Village. The citizens gave us a vote of
confidence by passing several important levies, such as for operating Fire and
Police.
We saw a number of new businesses start up, such as several video stores, a
meat market, and a new title company to name a few.
After much time and negotiation spent by both Tim Westfall, myself and others,
the N.A.M.C.O. plant was sold. Hopefully in the near future it will employ some
of our citizens.
The General Electric plant sale is at a standstill, but I am not giving up as
yet. The door is till open.
I commend this Council on its decision to allow Thousnad Trails into our sewer
system, as they have indicated this will enable them to expand their operations
further which can add to our economy.
We saw the dedication of the A.C. & J. Railroad and already they have started
expansion.
An Industrial Development Day was organized and observed by us and the
community. We toured the various plants and learned something about the
products made here. This is something that should continue.
It also gave us a chance to let industry know we do appreciate their investment
and involvement in our Community.
The housing for the elderly at the Hudson properties is soon to became a
reality as they have broken ground and are now excavating.
PERSONNEL
We have seen some change in personnel but for the most part maintain about the
same number of people.
WASTEWATER TREATMENT
Jeff Pizel and crew have accomplished much by renovating #3 final tank. A new
sewer jet, which has been put into operation, has been used to clean out about
90% of the sewer mains. Also numerous repairs were made throughout the system.
SERVICE AND STREETS
Roland Ferguson replaced Al Hedberg as street foreman and is doing a
magnificent job at that position.
Some new equipment has been added to the Street Department; Case tractor used
to grade and used with the new stump chipper, along with mowing roadsides. We
now have a fine compliment of equipmment to better utilize and machinery.
We saw the cleaning out of the large storm ditch from Mulberry to Market
Streets, a much needed project, also a number of other storm sewer additions
and repairs mostly done by our Street Department personnel.
This year we will be doing more storm sewer improvements, including replacing
the old with a large culvert under the railroad near the mill on East Jefferson
Street.
We will continue our sidewalk repair program this year along with our paving as
laid out in our master plan to maintain and improve our streets.
Mulberry Street extension connecting Poplar Street and the High School has been
completed. I believe this was a good move, not only for the accessibility to
the sports complex and High school, but for the fact safety equipment will have
an alternate in case an emergency arises.
BUILDINGS & LAND USE
Much work was done on the entire building at the safety center, including a new
roof, dropping the ceilings, insulating in and out and Vinyl siding on the
exterior. This should make the building more energy efficient not to mention
improved maintenance.
Tim will be continuing the tree program again this year. By doing so enhance
the appearance of the Village.
Although some work has been done at the Village Hall there are extensive
repairs we should look at, such as repair or replace the roof, make it more
accessible for the handicapped, insulate, etc. This can be done in steps
setting priorities to projects each year.
PARKS & RECREATION
I would like to see all work completed on our Village parks, Jeffersonian
Estates, Community Park before we take on any more projects. A decision
pertaining to the future or the expansion of the Community Center will be
inevitable soon. The committee appointed have been working diligently and will
soon report on their findings or recommendations.
UTILITIES
I'm pleased to report that for the first time since I have been involved in
Village government I can see that our negotiations with Ohio Water Service is
now paying off. Almost 5,000 feet of new water mains were installed and are now
operating. This year, 1986, several thousand feet more of new lines and
upgrading will be done, according to contract. Truly this is a step in the
right direction.
Although Cable TV has made some improvement in reception, I still believe we
must keep a watchful eye on this utility.
SAFETY
New radio equipment for both the Fire and Police Departments purchased by the
Cleveland Electric Illuminating Company is now in service with some additional
equipment still to come.
A new police cruiser is on order and both the Fire and Police departments are
well equipped going into this year.
Although we have experienced a change in personnel in the Police department the
transition has been smooth and the highest standards in law enforcement has
been maintained. Both Chief Wayman and Chief Johnson have provided their
excellent service to this community and will continue to do so.
The four-way flashing light at Beech Street and Chestnut has added to the
safety of visitors and citizens of the community and we must do what we can to
eliminate any further problems pertaining to the safety of our citizens.
FINANCE
The financial outlook for the Village should be viewed with cautious optimism
as I have stated before. Not only are we experiencing some losses in local
revenues it is possible Federal Revenue Sharing may go by the roadside also.
This Council and Village administration has managed to accomplish much in spite
of declining revenues, but it is important that we manage wisely our budgets to
insure the services the people need and want.
I wish to thank the Community organizations, business groups, and civic groups
for their endless time and efforts in assisting us to better our community.
Without their help some things would not have been possible. We are all looking
forward to working together in 1986 to celebrate our Sesqui-centennial year.
I'm sure it will be a huge success because of the pride we all have for
Jefferson!
Finally, it has been a pleasure working with each of you, and I thank you all
for your continued support. I'm looking forward to this new year of challenge
and will work with this council, our local business leaders and industrialists
to actively pursue more new business and industry for Jefferson.
Respectully,
Kenneth Fertig
Mayor of Jefferson
Adjourn
Respectfully submitted,
Gertrude Armstrong
Clerk-Treasurer
Approved:
Mayor

relocation of the Town Hall offices - Lemire's on East Jefferson Street, Longs
on Wall Street, and Dearing's off North Chestnut Street. Committee will review
and recommend choice at work session scheduled for Wednesday March 5 at 7:00
PM. This work session will be for budget preparation purposes.

Utilities:  
A notice of intention to file for an increase was received from East Ohio Gas
Co. Notice from TeleCommunications was a notification that rates had been
increased for basic for non senior citizens to $8.92, senior rate to $8.13;
expanded basic tier increased to $5.00 per month effective March 1, 1986.
Council questioned the non-notification 60 days prior to the increase, will
contact other communities to see what they are doing on this matter. Telephone
crews worked on the problems in the village, still waiting for parts for some
of the systems.

Motion made by Hruska to hear the first reading of Ordinance No. 1715 in toto,
second by Bishop, roll- Bishop, yea; Herndon, yea; Nemet, yea; Hruska, yea.
1st reading in toto   ORDINANCE No. 1715
AN ORDINANCE AUTHORIZING THE MAYOR TO ENTER INTO LEASE FOR OFFICE SPACE FOR THE
VILLAGE OF JEFFERSON, OHIO, AND DECLARING AN EMERGENCY
Motion made by Hruska to suspend the rules on the second and third reading of
Ordinance No. 1715 second by Bishop. Discussion: L. Hayslett asked how much
space the village would be getting for the cost of the rental Response - cost
is 77¢ sq. ft. Hayslett asked if it would be possible to utilize space in the
buildings the village already owns, felt that some pretty nice offices could be
put in for the amount the rental would cost over the two years. Possibilities
mentioned were the village garage, and the finishing of the garage area in the
Town Hall. It was also discovered that the lease had no "out" provision for the
village before the end of the two years lease proposed. Council will review
possibilities and suggestions. Bishop withdrew his second, Hruska withdrew his
motion.

Appropriations Ordinance/Federal Revenue Sharing Funds
Motion made by Herndon to hear the first reading of Ordinance No. 1717, second
by Hruska.
Proposed use for the Federal Revenue Sharing funds were an estimated $49,000
for a truck for the Street Department, $7000 transfer to debt retirement for
Poplar Street, balance for operation/ maintenance/equipment as designated by
Council. Foreman Ferguson asked that Council give definite consideration to
replacing the truck as proposed this year.
In order to meet budget limits all areas of operation were cut, position
proposed to be re-filled was again eliminated. Insurance is now a very costly
item compared to prior years; other areas in the general fund, such as the tree
program were cut. Basically, we will do what we can with the funds that are
available. roll - Bishop, yea; Herndon, yea; Nemet, yea; Hruska, yea.

meet specifications
Five Star Truck Services      $52,931.00
   trade in    6,000.00
      $46,931.00
Bid #2 with plow and dump meeting our specifications. Snow plow to be installed
at dealer in Buffalo, New York; dump box to be installed at dealer in Winnber,
Pa.
Lake Truck Sales and Service Inc.      $55,300.00
   trade in   7,500.00
      $47,800.00
I am recommending that Council accept the bid of Lake Truck, Painesville, for
the amount of $47,800.00. This bid is higher than the next qualifying supplier,
however, we have dealt with Lake Truck and the equipment supplier, Jones
Equipment, Inc. in the past and have had very excellent service. Truck supplier
and equipment supplier are in the same building and everything would be handled
at one location in Painesville. The other supplier, the truck is supplied from
Erie Pa. and the snowplow is installed and serviced at a dealer in Buffalo,
N.Y. The dump box is installed and serviced at the dealer in Winnbar, Pa. I
cannot recommend taking a lower bid that may cost us much more in time and cost
to take it the long distances to have repairs or service to set up.
B.D. Westfall, Administrator
The administrator told council that the diesel powered truck would be more
efficient costwise both in fuel consumption and the mechanical maintenance and
repair. Truck has life expectancy of 12 to 15 years. Motion was made by Roach
to accept the proposed bid of Lake Truck Sales, second by Nemet. Discussion
followed on leasing and how village could purchase using Federal Revenue
Sharing funds. It was felt that the village would be further ahead to go to a
lease-purchase method for the truck, thus not depleting all proposed funding.
Lease figures given
were: 48 months @ $1170.94 per month    $56,205.00
20 qtrs @$2903.94    $58,078.00
4 annual @ $13,506.00     $54,024.00
5 annual @ $11,186.60    $55,933.00
Roach withdrew her motion. Motion then made by Roach to enter into a lease-
purchase agreement with International, through Lake Truck Sales for the four
year period at $13,506.00 per year providing it is stipulated that the village
can buy out after 2 or 3 years, second by Nemet, roll - Herndon, yea; Bishop,
yea; Nemet, yea; Hruska, yea; McCune, yea; Roach, yea.

Ohio Water representatives Bob Seese and Red Martin presented council with the

company in the village in 1986. Council will review the information for a
future meeting.
Durwood Newhard representing the Jefferson VFW post 3334, requested permission
to sell poppies on the streets in the village. No objection voiced by Council.
He also asked that the week of May 18 thru 24 be proclaimed for sale of
poppies.
Reports of Committees:
Wastewater Treatment: 
Road conditions to the pump station have been improved with the installation of
a couple drains across. The Thousand Trails line is at a standstill at the
moment till some change orders are finalized.
Joint Meeting - Township Trustees/Village Council.
Present from the Township Board were Ken Boczar, Vernon Hall, John Smolen,
Clerk Charlene Wise. Clerk of the Oakdale Cemetery Board was also present. It
has became apparent that the Cemetery will need additional funding to operate.
Trustees asked that the matter be tabled until some further review is done and
opinions obtained on the millage for the operation of the cemetery. Next
meeting June 2.
Visitors: 
Larry Meckley asked about dust control on the roads, and commented on the heavy
truck traffic on Spruce Street. The village has obtained a brine distributor,
EPA approved, for applying brine to village streets.
A group of residents from Center Street along with Chief Johnson told Council
of incidents occurring on Center Street that are terrorizing the residents,
vandalism, fights, drinking and excessive noiseness, foul language used,
mooning, and heavy traffic on the street. There have been cases cited into
court but no restitution for damages or other action has come of it. A meeting
has been scheduled for Wednesday May 7 at 9:30 AM Judge Varckette, Jo Bertone,
Ed Ptaszek and other officials involved in juvenile cases, for the residents to
discuss their problems.

Finance: 
The village has received notice from Blue Cross/Blue Shield of increase in
premiums by 20% single from 100.41 to 121.16; family from 250.71 to 301.34

July 1, 1986 - Special Meeting
Meeting called to order by President Pro tem W. McCune
Council members present: A. Hruska, J. Roach, F. Bishop, W. Herndon
Also present: Bud Brueggnan, Star Beacon
Steam engine acquisition: Brueggnan advised Council that plans are still in the
works for bringing a steam engine, which is hoped would be stationed in
Jefferson permanently, and passenger cars to provide train rides or other tours
for the area. The committee has received $5000 in pledges, however, more funds
are needed, up to $12,000 or $15,000. It is felt that the monies could be
returned within a short period of time after operation of the system begins.
Many benefits could be derived for the community and its businesses. People
willing to put up seed money would get their money back first. Council
previously had pledged $500.00. Motion made by Herndon to pledge an additional
$4500 to the train project, with agreement to be executed with the proper
parties, monies to be drawn from the Municipal Facilities/Capital Improvement
funds, second by Roach, roll - Roach, yea; Bishop, yea; Herndon, yea; Hruska,
yea; McCune, yea.
Programmer for the Community Center: Consensus was that with the center
activities being started up again, a need is there for a programmer. However,
it may be on a temporary basis pending success of programs.
Adjourn
Respectfully submitted,
Gertrude Armstrong
Clerk-Treasurer
Approved
President Pro tem

It has been determined that the Oakdale Cemetery finances need more funding;
that the Trustees will no longer put .68, which they say is part of the one
mill they would receive anyway, into the cemetery funds. A levy was proposed

Visitors: 
Prestons advised Council that they had signed an easement for the village to
have access to their property to install the Walnut/Sycamore culvert. They feel
that the erosion south of the intersection is the village's problem and should
be alleviated. Erosion is also occurring on the back of the Auvil property.
Bishop explained that the creek has wandered somewhat out of its original bed
but doesn't feel anything that the village has done has aggravated the
situation. Prestons stated that years ago that was all swamp, he has filled it,
now is eroding. He stated he was promised certain things by former
administrators that have not been done. Council however is not aware of this.
The administrator was asked to get with the engineers, let Council know what
has to be done, what if any, the village has contributed to their problem.
Auvil advised Council of a problem with septic tank overflow into the creek
during high water. Health Department will be contacted on this. Brown stated
that water runoff on North Sycamore Street washes out the road, creates a
problem with driveways, asked if the village intended to fix the road this year
yet- she was advised- we plan to.
S. Candela - regarding path on easement strip from Elliott Avenue to the High
School. She thought it was on her property, she posted "no trespassing" signs,
was asked to remove. The traffic on the pathway is more then students walking
to and from school - used by ATVs, people walk dogs, young people with their
boom boxes, etc. creating excessive noise, stones flying, which have broken
windows scaring her children. It was suggested that the developer be contacted
and asked if the easement could be moved south to the edge of the next lot,
create a 3' pathway for walking traffic only.
Douglas Edwards of Dominion Enterprises Incorporated presented Council with
literature on a pay phone installation which would make money for the village.
Council will review.

Visitors: 
E. Preston - The Administrator will check into obtaining state funding for
creek work at Sycamore Street project. Priority will be the work filling the
street in and alleviating the driveway problems on Sycamore. After a review of
the intermittent waterway by the County Soil and Water Conservation District.
District. District. District Manager Kim Coy, a letter with comments in regard
to its present condition and its potential maintenance was presented to
Council. It was readily apparent that this waterway is at present in need of
maintenance. Erosion from the channel bottom, banks and approximately 800 acre
watershed has caused siltation in the waterway. Vegetation and other debris,
some physically placed in the waterway as attempts to control erosion, have
also augmented channel erosion and siltation. This present state has been in
the formative process for many years. Upland development, urbanization, paving
and industrialization have all increased the amount of runoff water which
currently must flow through this channel. Accumulating brush deposited debris
and lack of channel maintenance have all acted to detract from the waterway's
carrying capacity. Increased runoff and decreased flow capacity together have
served to increase the velocity of water flowing through the waterway and hence
the rate of erosion of the waterway banks and bottom have similarly increased.
And so now notices the movement of the channel center-line which will continue
unless addressed by maintenance or reconstruction. The installation of the
eight foot diameter culvert under Jefferson Street enabled more storm runoff
water to move into the waterway in a shorter period of time. This served to
enhance the pre-existing channel movement. It is not the primary cause of the
channel movement. If the channel itself had been regularly maintained the
increased flow would not have been detrimental at all. Reconstruction of this
waterway would benefit all parties draining land into the waterway. The Ohio
State Legislature recognizes two distinct benefits to landowners within a
waterway's watershed: responsibility benefit and drainage benefit. Each person
whose land drains into the waterway is responsible for the runoff waters
leaving his/her land. Therefore, any channel improvement needed would some
degree affect and benefit that landowner and that landowner would then also be
partly responsible for the cost of such improvement. Any person whose land is
close enough to the waterway's channel to allow that person to artificially
enhance their land's drainage via ditches or tile would also accrue a drainage
benefit because of the water way's improvement. To this end he would hope that
all landowners affected and benefitted by this particular waterway's
improvement be involved. It is neither an individual landowner's responsibility
nor is it any public entity's sole responsibility. Mr. Coy also advised us that
the United States Corps of Engineers be contacted before anything else is done
as they are the authority on all natural waterways.
Jerry Shook and Dan Hulbert of the CEI were present to discuss issues as
presented in a proposed resolution presented to Council for consideration; said
resolution would ask that the Ashtabula County Commissioners and Governor
Celeste rescind the Perry Nuclear Power plant review of December 23, 1982 and
all previous and following approvals of the emergency plans for the plant,
which would effect the plant from operating above the 5% power level so that it
would not be a threat to the health, safety, welfare and economy of the
Northeastern Ohio area. The discussion with all present involved the statements
presented in the resolution- could the population within the 10 mile emergency
planning zone around the plant be evacuated in a safe and timely manner; the
ten mile zone limit was questioned; cost overruns being passed on to the
consumers, the seismic suitability of the site; financial reimbursement for
services rendered by personnel involved in the evacuation. Proposed resolution
will be reviewed by Council.

Visitors: 
Mr. and Mrs. Jim McIntyre are concerned with the evacuation plan as set forth
by the Illuminating Co. should there be an emergency situation at the Perry
Nuclear Power Plant, especially relative to our safety forces. Chief Johnson
stated that the forces have had and are continuing to have meetings with the
Disaster Services and other parties involved. He feels that our main purpose
would be to see over people evacuating into this area, feels that we have
sufficient personnel to handle this, but hopes it never happens. Our SOP's are
filed with Disaster Services. Council will be reviewing the proposed resolution
in a scheduled work session coming up.
Committee Reports:
Buildings Land Use:  
Public Hearing - to consider the request of Gene Crislip to rezone .375 acre on
Lot 87 East Jefferson Street from B 1 to RD.
Mel Ferguson, who lives across the street from the property, is displeased with
the way work was done in installing manhole and lines. Yard still not
corrected, doesn't feel he should be granted the request. Also questioned the
effect on the value of his property.
Roland Ferguson, a resident in the area, said he has gone to Crislip on the
open cuts in the road, was referred to Burns Construction who in turn referred
back to Crislip, repairs not made yet. McCune stated that the request is to
change from B1 to RD residential. This would give better control. If left
commercial - he would have a lot of leeway. RD or RS much more restrictive.
Ferguson - Being an apartment dwelling - will it be maintained? If Council
would have more control with the change granted, he would see no problem.

Utilities:
Motion made by Nemet to hear the first reading of Resolution No. 1736, second
by Herndon,
Discussion: Foote questioned whether this request by CEI is a duplication of
the one issued earlier. It is believed that the prior request had been
retracted by CEI, that this replaces it. Foote asked why oppose - if using same
rationale as use on the nuclear plant resolution, why didn't we object 10 years
ago. Hruska feels rates are high enough now. Nemet said in his opinion increase
is unjustified, area is one of highest paying as of now, opposes regardless of
what rate increase is used for - nuclear or otherwise. Herndon stated his
concern is cost of electricity, are pricing industry out of the area, we are
higher even than places with nuclear power, area can't afford it, feel in a lot
of ways they could cut. roll on motion and second - Hruska, yea, Nemet, yea;
Roach, yea; Foote abstain; McCune, yea; Herndon, yea.

November 14, 1986 - Special Meeting
Meeting called to order by Mayor K. Fertig
Council members present: Foote, Herndon, McCune, Hruska
Trustees present: Hall, Smolen, Boczar
Also present: Charlene Wise
As far as village is concerned, our levy passed, our contribution doesn't need
to be discussed. Prosecutor's office determined the village levy passed,
auditor has been advised to collect this village levy.
Township will fund their portion out of their General Fund since their levy
failed. They will possibly put it on the ballot in the spring. It was suggested
that an agreement should be drawn up for the five year period, with meetings
annually, since the township has to fund annually. Question was raised as to
the need for two full time men now with winter coming on. This will be
reviewed. The village will need a resolution to rescind the .10 portion
formerly a part of the Joint Resolution acted on annually. According to the
Prosecutor, a Joint Resolution not needed anymore.
No large expenditures anticipated at the cemetery anymore.
Gertrude Armstrong
Clerk-Treasurer

Service: 
Reitz reported a couple of places of obstruction in the village right of way
which hampers snow plowing efforts. One was at the Jefferson Courtyard
Apartments entrance where curbing was installed to the roadway; the other one
mentioned was at 155 Maplewood Drive where railroad ties are on the green. The
Administrator will contact the above parties and others involved in
obstructions in the right of way.
Council will be receiving a memo from the Administrator with comments on the
zoning regulations for installation of fences.
Rec: 
Motion made by Herndon to accept the recommendation of the Rec Board for the
appointment of James Spaulding to the position of Program Director, on
probationary basis, effective December 17, 1986, second by Roach; discussion
followed on whether position would indeed be available in light of the
liability insurance situation and the sovereign immunity ending on December 31,
1986. Solicitor said that the instructors ought to be hired by contract,
specify they are under independent contract status. When asked as long as the
department runs the programs are instructors and volunteers covered - response
no, if negligent, which has to be proven, it falls back on the village. Is
village any more liable than if Boy Scouts or such meet here? Those are
proprietary functions, only legally bound if in scope of Employment. By running
the programs the department is doing now, are we that much more liable?
Solicitor responded we are exposable, we will be just as bad off as we are now.
The proposed Program Director should be made aware that there is a probationary
period, and that there may not be a job along the line. It was the consensus
that the department continue running as it is now. Roll on motion - Foote, yea;
Hruska, yea; Herndon, yea; Roach, yea; Nemet, yea; McCune, yea.

Mayor speech - 1987
LADIES AND GENTLEMEN:
Another year has passed, and I am pleased to say we have accomplished much.
Most is noticeable but some is not.
While most of Ashtabula County seems to be dormant with a slow economy,
Jefferson Village appears to have a healthy outlook.
This year we saw a number of highlites in the Industrial community, such as the
purchase of the GE plant on W. Ashtabula Street and NAMCO on S. Cucumber
Street. We have purchased 74 acres on E. Jefferson Street for future Industrial
and Residential development. Champion Corp. was acquired by Stone Container;
Stone being an even larger Corp. than Champion. Several new businesses either
relocated here or started up here.
Three years ago when I took office I made a promise that I would work
diligently to help get the GE building and NAMCO building sold. Today that is a
reality, thanks to your efforts along with the Jeff. Development Corp. and
others.
By working together we have also seen new housing units built for the elderly
and handicapped on E. Jefferson St. These units were much needed and have added
to our community, showing our concern for our senior citizens. I would like to
see more of this caliber for the seniors. There has been more improvements in
our water service last year and we should encourage even more. There has been
more equipment added to better able us to maintain our streets and right of
ways. Storm sewers are continually being improved.
Our Safety forces have continued to serve this village and surrounding
communities with their outstanding services and professionalism, and I am sure
we will be just as proud of them in 1987. We have not had any reductions in
employees as other small communities have experienced, and I do not see any in
the near future. I contribute this to the watchful eye of our finances by all
of us in this administration.
Although we are a financially healthy community, we must continue to get the
most for our dollars, especially since there is no more Revenue Sharing and the
fact property taxes are being decreased some. I believe we made a good move by
bringing the Community Center to the Village Hall, but must look at this
department more objectively. In summary I would like to say you have been a
hard working Council and I have enjoyed working with each and everyone of you.
Together we can and have improved working and living conditions in Jefferson,
making this still a better place to live.
Thank you,
Kenneth Fertig
Mayor
Adjourn:
Respectfully submitted,
Gertrude Armstrong
Clerk-Treasurer
Approved
