Motion made by McCune to approve the bills, second by Roach, roll - Hruska,
yea; McCune, yea; Roach; yea; Foote, yea.
Visitors: 
In response to complaints of bad reception, poor color, etc. on cable tv, Mr.
Schultz asks that specific names and addresses be provided and they will be
checked out. Council was advised that service is available till 7:00 PM to
accommodate people who can't be home during the day. Schultz stated he was not
aware of any problems in the village. It would help if people would call. The
Mayor told him that people do call with no results, that they contact council
out of frustration. In areas where cable is on top of the ground, work is being
done to put these underground. Council was also advised that a 24 hr. answering
service has been made available by TCI, that emergencies can be responded to.
Mark Ervin of the GDNR Division of Forestry presented a slide review related to
street tree programs. His talk stressed the value of trees to an area both in
quality of life and monetarily. To have an effective tree program, a rotation
system of planting, maintenance and removal is needed. Mr. Frayer told Council
they have a responsibility to resolve policy for future direction to accomplish
and implement a system. Ervin has made his services available to work with
Council and committee set up for th is purpose.
Finance:  
Motion made by McCune to move Frank Bishop from probationary status to regular
status as village Administrator, second by Foote, roll - Roach, yea; Foote,
yea; McCune, yea; Hruska, yea.
Safety: 
Council had proposed two ordinance dealing with open burning. Last meeting both
were tabled, waiting for Chief Wayman's input. Ohio Revised Code along with EPA
states that certain combustibles, such as wood and cardboard can be burned at a
construction site. However, Wayman said that many materials are now treated,
some contain phosphene. Plastics, pre-finished wood, carpeting could pollute.
All these things are being burned at construction sites. He also didn't feel we
have a way of policing the activity, and would be a burden on the administrator
to enforce. He recommended that we leave things as they are.
Fire Department Errors and Omissions policy - It was requested that we look for
higher coverage. Current coverage expires February 5, 1987.
Street Foreman had asked that Council consider removing the STOP sign at
Mulberry and Elm. Consensus was to leave the signs to at least slow traffic
even if they don't always obey them. Motion made by McCune to hear the first
reading of Ordinance No. 1745, second by Foote, roll Foote, yea; Hruska, yea;
McCune, yea; Roach, yea.

Visitors: 
Robert Buckler of United Telephone was advised of problems with service such as
not being able to get correct numbers on long distance calls, even with
repeated dialing; noisiness in lines both local and long distance, static,
cross talk, trouble with service at the County Sheriffs department and not
being able to get immediate repair. Buckler advised Council that they have
already started to check out some of these problems, asked for specific a and
numbers. A lot of testing has to be done to resolve them. He was aware of
periodic problems but not aware of this many problems. Council was told that by
August '88 a digital switch will be in place in the Jefferson phone building,
which is now undergoing renovations. This will not eliminate all problems but
it will help. This change does not effect rates. Extension of free service to
other towns such as Austinburg would involve a rate change if people are
willing to pay.
Ohio Water Service: 
Wallace DeArment reviewed the program thus far in the updating of the village
water service, graphs show much improvement in the gallon per minute in most
areas. He feels that an ongoing annual program would mean continued
improvement, this accomplished by working with communities in the District.
District on rate structure, rather than going through the PUCO.

Motion made by McCune to approve the bills, second by Hruska, roll - Roach,

Visitors: 
B. Westfall and G. Althoff of A. Terra and T. Likovec of Burgess & Niple
appeared before Council expressing interest in becoming the engineering
consultants for the village. Westfall and Althoff, with an engineering/
surveying company in the village, stated they are familiar with the village's
needs and the village's area, and could be readily available. The
representative from Burgess & Niple stated they would also be available to meet
village needs. It was suggested that proposals from companies be reviewed,
along with the former contract to set up a contract suited to the village's
criteria.
Trustees John Smolen and Vernon Hall of the Jefferson Township and Clerk
Charlene Wise attended Council upon request from Council. They were advised
that the village will be pursuing some method of taking the village out of the
township. It is felt by Council that the close to $28.00 out of the inside
millage each year going to the township doesn't do anything for the village
tax-payers, also citing the fact that the village people passed a one mill levy
for cemetery purposes.
Up until last year the township had put .68 of the inside one mill into the
cemetery, but last year stated they were no longer willing to do that. Thus all
the village gains is the privilege of voting for the township trustees and
clerk. The current arrangement whereby the township puts in one mill of their
valuation, approximately $15,000, into cemetery will continue, and the Joint
Cemetery ownership still remains. Township will contact their legal counsel.
Committee Reports: 
Safety: 
Motion made by Nemet to pay the contract price, $50,696.00, plus $1430.00 for
added modifications to Eagle Air Systems for trailer mounted compressor/
generator equipment for the Fire Department, second by Nemet. Equipment
inspected and approved for acceptance by the Fire Chief. roll - Herndon, yea;
McCune, yea; Hruska, yea; Nemet, yea; Roach, yea; Foote, yea. Chief Wayman
stated that with the influx of inspections required due to the state not
covering the need anymore, some type of compensation for these duties needs to
be considered. Council has planned to address this issue with the
appropriations coming up. The Chief stated an alternative would be to go back
to 1965 way - become a fire suppression department again. It was felt that the
village people would like to see the department continue services as they are
now. The Chief also asked what the village stand is on the Perry plant. When
presented a resolution last year to oppose the plant operation, Council took no
action. The Mayor, however, said he would not send his police and fire
departments into a dangerous situation. If the departments have people
available and they want to go, they can go, but we will do what we can here,
prime responsibility is the village's needs.

Visitors: 
Kim Neill asked Council what is being proposed and when will it be started on
the erosion problem, tree lawn sinking, creek reroute and culvert placement or
replacement. She feels culvert may collapse leaving road in worse condition
than it already is. The Administrator said the County Engineer recommended
lifting top broken sanstone slab off and setting a concrete slab over the
culvert which would allow for good road repair, than“than” not “then” do
sidewalks and adjacent areas. On changing course of the creek, the
administrator stated we could move over 10 or 12' perhaps, if use existing
course, could possible repair and bank could be rebuilt. Tree lawn damage is
probably due to a broken tile. Question on grant movies available to address
the erosion problem was raised. None available at this time. Responsibility for
erosion and tree lawn was questioned. McCune stated the village will fix the
tree lawn problem, are not responsible for creek, is on private property. Kim
told Council she would like to work with the village in getting these problems
resolved in the best manner. Reitz noted that the village had put the cement
block on side in the '60s, is now washing in back of it.

Solicitor also advised Council on the question of road maintenance on Beverly
and Hillyer in the Elliott Allotment. Plat was recorded by the developers as
required under ORC section 723.03. Streets do not became village responsibility
for maintenance until they meet subdivision regulation and are accepted for
maintenance by the village. It is up to the developer to meet these
regulations. Question - do property owners have recourse on their own? - is a
private matter. Solicitor will prepare a letter of opinion on this matter.

Fiscal Officer's Certificate 
Funds for Rte 307 in cooperation with the State of Ohio Department of
Transportation
I hereby certify that the money, to wit: Five Hundred and 00/100 ($500.00)
required for the payment of the cost other than the part thereof assumed by the
State of Ohio;
whereas, the village has identified the need for and proposes the improvement
of a portion of the public highway which is described as follows: by applying a
leveling and surface course to State Route 307 from SR 46 to the village east
corporation limit, approximate distance 0.36 miles, full width and 0.12 miles ½
width; has been lawfully appropriated for such purpose and is in the treasury
to the credit of, or has been levied, placed on the duplicate and in process of
collection for the appropriate fund and not appropriated for any other purpose;
or is being obtained by sale of bonds issued on account of said improvement,
which bonds are sold and in process of delivery.
I further testify that this certificate was made, sealed and filed with the
legislative authority of Jefferson, Ohio, after said legislative authority
passed the ordinance/resolution in connection with the within described
project; and that this certificate was forthwith recorded in the record of
proceedings of said legislative authority, namely: Legislative Authority's
Journal volume 6, page 174.
In witness whereof, I have hereunto set my hand and official seal as said
fiscal officer, this 21 day of April, 1987.
Gertrude Armstrong
Fiscal Officer of Jefferson, Ohio

Re truck for the Fire Department - 1987 models no longer available; 1988 out in
September. Price quoted will be the same plus whatever increase in price GM
dictates for the newer model.
Buildings/Land Use  
The Administrator is obtaining quotes on some of the work. A request has been
received to erect a split rail fence across the opening of the unopened street
at Cedar and Chestnut; Council sees no problem as long as stipulation is made
that it must be removed if street is opened up in the future.
Request received from Bowdler's Super Duper that the village participate in
amount of $4000.00 for improvement of access to store which is on the village
green area. Solicitor feels the village has no obligation to do this, that it
would be improper use of taxpayer's money for his benefit. Agreement on use of
green area was negotiated with Bowdler's during village's claim to greens. He
is to be advised that the village does not want to participate on this
proposal.
On greens case - waiting for ruling on summary judgement notice regarding
Namey. Also no agreement reached with the County as yet.
Problem lawns in the village have been noted by the Administrator. It was
suggested that an unloader be used for the delivery of stone at the County
Garage, rather than having to haul stone from the yard. County Engineer had
requested use of streets with load limits, which his trucks exceed, for hauling
their stone from the yard
Hearing by the Board of Zoning Appeals scheduled for June 16th at 8:00 PM on
request for variance from Gastown for erection of a new building.
Steam train - no engine available yet - Brueggeman hopes to have a couple
passenger cars here for the fourth celebration - will pull with his engine so
tours can be offered.

Mayor Fertig arrived, and took over the meeting. Motion made by McCune to
approve the bills, second by Hruska, roll - Vance, yea; Roach, yea; Herndon,
yea; McCune, yea; Hruska, yea.
Visitors: 
Larry Bagley representing the petitioners for the paving of Mulberry Street
asked the status of the project. Price quoted at the last meeting was about
$37.00 a foot, which included storm sewers. The quoted price was not broken
down to the residential cost and the extra cost to construct road to handle the
bus and school traffic. After a lengthy discussion it was suggested by Housel
that the residents form a committee, meet with the administrator and engineer
to come up with an equitable solution and cost figure.
David Graper, representing a construction firm from Painesville introduced
himself and his brother to council. They are interested in constructing an
apartment complex at the corner of Rte 307 and Poplar Street, and that they
would be coming to the village with requests for a zoning change to multi-
family and same possible variances. This raised discussion on spot zoning.
Action on multi-family zoning requests have been considered on an individual
basis. The Mayor stated there is a need for apartments, that they could go for
the changes, when the presentation is made, all things will be considered.

New Business: 
Question has arisen on whether or not property on the northeast corner of
Jefferson and Elm Streets is hooked up to the sewer. Dye tests have been run,
see no indication that sewage is going into the sanitary line. Solicitor
advised that by Section 1034.13 of the ordinances requires hook up to the
sanitary. Question also from the property owners on monies they have paid over
the years for sewer service. Administrator still working on solution.

Larry Kraemer of the ACEDC told Council of various areas they are working on.
(1) working in start ups of small businesses - 2 in Jefferson, (2) help on
exports to markets overseas, (3) met with representatives of overseas
companies, citing advantages in our county for investing. These and other
activities rely on memberships, hence asked Council to renew their membership.
Mr. and Mrs. Ewing presented Council with the Mulberry Streets residents paving
proposal. They also asked that the catch basin be reinstalled at their corner,
as drainage has created a number of problems on their property. Ohio Water
Service will be contacted, since this was a result of the contractor not
reinstalling the catch basin when the new lines were put in that area.

yea; Nemet, yea; Roach, yea; Herndon, yea.
Safety:  
Note from Mayor - prefer that Ordinance No. 1763 not be passed. Letter from the
Ambulance Board requested a number of insertions of the word "fire" throughout
the ordinance: McCune, a member of the Ambulance Board, explained that the
squad members would be governed by the Board, workers comp would be picked up
by the board, while fire personnel would still be picked up by the village. It
was stated that a squad member would not have to be a member of the department.
Don Herndon told Council that all the members he has contacted don't want this
split, that the "employee" designation is not quite clear to him. He feels
problem stems from department election “splitting the department.”
Nemet asked that Ordinance No. 1763 be tabled till next meeting, as some
changes have been made and others may be made. Councilman Herndon agreed. Also
stated that after the article in the Gazette, he is not convinced the Mayor has
the desire or ability to dissolve this problem; time for Council to take over,
get department personnel together, let's find out what the problems are; get
this settled. Members of the department are to be notified that work sessions
will be held, Executive Sessions called, for Council and Fire Department
personnel - first the members then the chief. Monday the 27th of July at 1:00
PM and 7:00 PM so as to accommodate all shifts. It is to be noted that no
reprisals for anyone coming forth.
Buildings/Land Use: 
Three ordinances were presented to Council for consideration - 2 on zoning and
the other on weed control. The Solicitor suggested the zoning code be reviewed,
feels there are areas that need clarification. Committee to so do.

Reports on cruiser maintenance and use received by Council. Ordinance for fire
chief job description still on hold. The Administrator gave council memo on
possible replacement of copy machine at the police department. Executive
Session for fire personnel matters.
Return to regular session. After meetings and discussions Council feels
comfortable with the Chief at this time; are some things have to work with,
clear up same misunderstandings. Council feels this was blown out of
proportion. By laws are still intact, but are being revised and updated.
Ambulance service also in process of being returned to prior service. Both
services are starting a recruiting program.
No turn on red signs to be installed overhead at the Market -Jefferson Stress
intersection.

Motion made by Hruska to approve the bills, second by Roach, roll - Hruska,
yea; McCune, yea; Herndon, yea; Nemet, yea; Roach, yea; Vance, yea.
Visitors: 
Joseph Mallone, a councilman from Geneva, presented Council with a packet of
information relating to the purchase of the water system serving the Lake Erie
East district. It is stated the system could be run at less cost to the
consumer if locally owned. Council member Roach will be the representative to
future meetings on this issue. Council member Nemet will be the alternate.
Safety: 
Safety Committee met with Chief Wayman and the Advisory Board to review the
legislation on the fire chief position. Ordinance to be prepared for the next
meeting.
Executive Session requested for personnel matters. Return to regular session.
Meetings every other month have been set up by the Safety Committee and Fire
Department personnel.
New people on the department will be approved by Council periodically.
Buildings/Land Use: 
Council has received a Petition for vacation of a portion of Pine Street at the
Hall property. Planning Commission to meet on the requested re-zoning of the
Hall property on Tuesday the 18th. Council will then consider the petition
after commission recommendation on the property.
The administrator is trying to line up someone to cut down dead trees. Policy
of residents getting the wood for complete clean-up of the cut tree is still in
effect.
Path from Elliott to the school property is soft - needs some material.
Sanitary and storm sewer lines are being separated on the Post Office property.
Sink hole at 307 and Market has been repaired - found a void under the
pavement.
Spot repairs, where streets dug up by Ohio Water, are being repaired by Ohio
Water contractor. Administrator to check out report of an open drain behind an
East Erie residents property. No further word on the paving of East Erie or
Mulberry streets. Preliminary engineering work is being done on Mulberry Street
project.
Culvert work on East Erie started last Thursday, will continue as work force is
available.
Service:
Wastewater Treatment:  
Poured three beds before fair - no problems. Changing of doors at the plant's
garage will be done to let two vehicles in the building, thus accommodating the
new truck. Painting and sealing of the interior of the street department garage
and awning over front door will be started soon.
Utilities:  
PUCO hearing on CEI rate increase request - 8-26-87, 6:30 PM, KSUAC. At recent
meeting with Ohio Water Service it was learned there will be no increase in
rates in 1987 and probably not in 1988. Problems with Channel 18 reception and
the difficulty in reaching TCI were expressed.
Finance: 
Bids to be sought for compilation of personnel handbook and job descriptions.
Village’s Budget hearing- 8/25/87 - 2:00 PM - Courthouse Conference Room.
Clarification of the Permissive Auto Tax proposal is needed. Village is being
audited at this time. Income Tax ordinance renewal next meeting. Prior East
Erie Street engineering bill is still outstanding.
Possible County participation in the paving of the street will be looked into.
Officials:  
McCune expressed his upset with the Beacon reporting, felt fire department
problem was sensationalized on the front page, but when resolved was not on the
front page.
USEPA hearings on Poplar Street Laskin Oil subject - 7:00 PM, 8-26-87, Comm.
Conference Room Covered Bridge Festival Committee have requested permission to
display covered bridge model on one of the greens up town - no objections
voiced by Council.
Little League Banquet 8-27, 6:00 PM, VoEd school
Old Business: 
Executive Session requested by the Solicitor re personnel matters.
New Business:
Adjourn
Respectfully submitted,
Clerk-Treasurer

1st reading title only   ORDINANCE NO. 1770
AN ORDINANCE AMENDING THE ZONING OF APPROXIMATELY 2.73 ACRES IN BEECH STREET
LOT NO. 2 AND PART OF ASHTABULA STREET LOT NOS. 1 AND 3 FROM RESIDENTIAL (RS)
(SINGLE FAMILY) TO RESIDENTIAL (RD) (TWO FAMILY OR MULTIFAMILY)
Motion made by Roach to hear the first reading of Ordinance No. 1771, second by
Herndon.
Nemet voiced objection - are changing something and setting a precedent, we are
not sure this developer will build all these units. Planning Commission went
along with it- reasoning is it is in the northwest corner of village and there
are no areas zoned RD. Concern was expressed that if do for one, would have to
do for another. Vance felt this was too much to ask of Council, is a 32%
reduction in our zoning. It was stated that the density is not changed -
changed the square footage. roll on motion - Vance, yea; Roach, yea; Nemet, no;

felt that the settling damage ought to be over by now, that the village is no

Visitors: 
Marion Schultz, TCI representative, was asked to appear at council meeting to
address a number of complaints on unstable picture, service and box deposits.
Unstable picture should not be happening, may be bad box or converter. New dish
should improve the AMC channel reception. A number of complaints related to
service - not being able to reach the office, time span before response to
service and for hook-ups. To improve the system the company is currently or a
continued maintenance program, they will be starting to rebuild the system
which should greatly improve the reception, should be ready by end of '88. On
delayed service calls, the company has a large back-log. another number for
customers to call - 1-800-423 4634 - call goes into the office during regular
working hours. Mark Nelson, representing the amateur radio community, noted
interference on Channel 18 caused by amateur radio transmission. He is licensed
on the 146.715 frequency which is also near the cable system, has caused
problems with the Sheriffs Department. Schultz and Nelson will work this
problem out.
Jim Kelley, representing the Jefferson Rotary, requested Council permission to
place a container for aluminum cans somewhere uptown. Proceeds go towards the
Rotarians Polio-Plus world wide program. No objections from Council. Kelley to
get together with the Administrator on location.

to the next meeting

Nemet, yea; Hruska, yea; McCune, yea; Herndon, yea; Roach, yea; Vance, yea.
Door operator installed, garage project near completion.
Public Hearing - (1) rezoning certain properties from RS to RD (2) amend zoning
regarding density requirements
Additional attending: Ed Curie, Lynette Hall, Vern Hall
The original proposal was for 32 units on 2.73 acres. With the acquisition of
an additional 1.3 acres the unit number was upped to 48. Planned are 6 units
with 8 apartments each, would start with one or two buildings. Further
development would depend on the market for apartments. Acquisition of the
additional land also improved the parking and eliminated the need for a set
back variance formerly asked for. At present have no desire to sell the land,
but things could change and would be forced to sell, could then possibly have
deed restrictions to have future building be of quality as the Graper
construction, but Graper said they would hope to complete the project. When
asked if they could live with the present zoning density Graper said no,
eventually want to build 48. Graper also stated he would have a 25 to 30
thousand dollar investment in putting in a sewer line. Vern Hall asked if there
had been any negative input. Council member answer was yes, from contractors
and residents. Density at 5000 sq. ft. has been agreeable to developers before.
Once changed, it would change for the whole village from now on. Ed Curie told
Council this is the second most devastated county in the state, we have to
progressive - new ideas, younger people coming in, whole area has to became
more progressive, changes have to be made. If project goes, it may bring in
more development. The Graper projects are of good quality, not a detriment to a
community. He felt there are still ways to protect the village, when zoning
request made council could refuse. Question asked by Al Graper - if can have
spot zoning change, why not spot density change. Solicitor opinion was that
such action would create further problems, that if change made it has to be
made in the zoning code and a requirement for all future building. It was noted
that the Jefferson Planning Commission had reviewed and approved the project as
was presented to them. The answer was 'no' on question if the project was State
of Federal funded. Would it be for adults or families. Project would have areas
designed for children and area for adults. Initially for adults, later for
playgrounds and children. Each building would have one and two bedroom,
possibly three bedroom apartments. Graper asked when the last apartments were
built in Jefferson - between nine and ten years ago - material and labor costs
have changed a great deal, water bills are astronomical; based on average rent
here, can get higher in Painesville, where one of their projects is located.
However, land costs and taxes are lower in Jefferson. Consensus of Council was
for the zoning change from RS to RD.

Buildings/Land Use: 
Weather permitting, finish work to be done on East Erie Street culvert. CEI
will be in Tuesday to cut down some trees and trim others. Administrator has
had no indication on when sidewalk program will start.
Wood off Cucumber Street on property abutting owned by Cowgers: Question raised
on procedure in this situation. Although there is no ordinance, village policy
has been to take down a tree on the tree lawn, with the abutting property owner
having first chance at the wood, but they have to take all and clean up. On the
tree lawn strip abutting Cowger's property - 17' x 600', there are many trees,
would be quite an expense to the village to take down as opposed to one or two
trees. The Administrator was also unaware til a week and half ago that the
property abutting on the west side of the street also belongs to Cowger. He
would like the wood from there also. Consensus of Council was that the village
should not go in and cut them all down for Cowger, that it is the
administrator's responsibility to get trees cut down and out of there at the
least cost to the village, so stump removal and ditching under current contract
can be done. Administrator to meet with Cowger and work out.
No objection from Council on the Jaycees use of green for Christmas tree sales,
Sohio corner has been used in prior year.
Salvation Army box to be moved from current placement.
Service: 
More information needed before can proceed with West Mulberry Street proposal.
Forestry:
Old Business: 
Village Greens committee will be meeting at 9:00 AM on November 18th, have
proposal from two defendants who have been holding out.
Roach met with CEI on use of poles for Christmas decorations- will get back to
us.
New Business:
Old church building almost relocated on the Depot property.
Adjourned:

apartment complex. Graper stated they would go with the 40, if they can get

granted to the village.

AN ORDINANCE AMENDING SECTION 1252.01 (a) OF THE CODIFIED ORDINANCES OF THE
VILLAGE OF JEFFERSON, OHIO, 1987, TO REQUIRE MULTIPLE UNITS, TWO STORY, IN THE
RD DISTRICT TO CONTAIN A MINIMUM LOT AREA OF 4000 SQUARE FEET AND REPEALING THE

Motion made by Herndon to suspend the rules on second and third reading of
Ordinance No. 1771B, sector by Roach, roll - Nemet, abstain, Roach, yea;
Hruska, yea; Vance, yea; McCune, no; Herndon, yea.
Motion made by Herndon to adopt Ordinance No. 1771B, second by Roach, roll -
McCune, no; Herndon, yea; Vance, yea; Nemet, abstain; Hruska, yea; Roach, yea.
McCune stated he had no problem with this developer's quality of work and
integrity, but was his concern was for what this could bring in in the future,
that council could then not control future development. At the work session a
copy of "Planned Unit Development" was offered to Council. This concept would
provide a tool for control over further development if put into our zoning.
Solicitor reviewed, feels it is an excellent tool for the village to consider.

1988 Village Council Meeting Minutes
January 4, 1988
Meeting called to order by Mayor S. Nizen
Pledge of Allegiance
Roll: Council members present: R. Nemet, J. Roach, B. Vance, W. Herndon, K.
Buell, A. Hruska
Also present: H. Frayer, S. Febel, K. Johnson, R. Ferguson, T. Lekovic, J.
Pizel, C. Powers, Solicitor B. Larson, Administrator F. Bishop, Prosecuting
Attorney's officer Phillips, J. Koziol of the Gazette, W. Dillaway of the
Beacon
Mayor's address:
Forty two years ago I took my first oath of office as your Mayor and I then
held office for five terms. At that time I had a very good Council to work with
and we had many accomplishments, but that is history and we will not dwell on
it. There have been many changes in the operation of our community since that
time. I have been able to keep up with the changing times and I feel that I
will be just as capable to handle the village affairs now as I was then. As I
look at my Council, Clerk, Administrator and Solicitor I feel that I have an
excellent and highly dedicated group to work with. I will make every effort to
cooperate with our Council and I will make sure that everything we do will be
in the best interest of the Village of Jefferson. At this meeting the Mayor is
supposed to report to Council on the affairs of the Village and make
recommendations on legislation that I would deem appropriate to solve village
problems. If I took it upon myself to make such a report and recommend such
legislation, I would only be kidding you and myself. It would be impossible to
do these things after being in office only four days. After reading such rules,
I can see why we have so many false political promises and phony politicians.
Again I will only work for the good of the Village of Jefferson and I refuse to
draw promises out of thin air. I want to work with the people of Jefferson for
the common good of the village. My door will always be open to my constituents
and I hope that we will be able to convince more people to attend meetings and
take a more active roll in helping us manage our community. I thank you for
letting me make these remarks and now we will get back to the business at hand.
Executive Session requested by Officer Phillips on Narcotics Task Force.
Return to regular session. Councilman W. Herndon was sworn in by the Solicitor.
The Mayor and Councilman K. Buell were sworn in on December 29th, 1987.

Mulberry Street - Residents have been informed on what they would be
responsible for in the paving of their street. They now have an opportunity to
make a decision on whether to proceed with the project. Vance suggested that
the village undertake the sidewalk program this year, contract out the mowing
and greens care. The Mayor concurred.
Wastewater Treatment:  
New flow meter in operation. Pizel doing investigating on new testing required
by the EPA. Village is meeting ammonia criteria, but will have test for
phosphorous.
Department is putting together a general plan to submit to EPA for approval.
Estimated cost for new lab equipment needed - $10,000.
Likoves from Burgess & Niple told Council they do not require a retainer but
work with each project - submitting estimates for village to accept, modify or
reject - or take a portion of.
Utilities: 
Roach expressed a complaint on Ohio Water billing for excessive late charge.
Administrator will be meeting with the Ohio Water and the cemetery sexton on
work being done on Market Street. Scheduling is in place for TCI to rebuild
wiring system in Jefferson.

Annual report from the Fire Department was presented to Council. Department was
commended for excellent report and their services.
Lenox Township Trustees Harry Smith, Tom Waltenmire and Gary Lewis approached
Council on the amount needed for continuance of fire service contract. Their
five year one mill levy expires this year. Chief Wayman said he didn't foresee
any drastic increase in the next two or three years, but perhaps some increase
after that. Trustees will propose renewing the levy for three years and address
further upon expiration. On coming into the Ambulance District they were
advised to meet with the Ambulance Board.

AN ORDINANCE AUTHORIZING THE VILLAGE ADMINISTRATOR TO RESCIND THE CONTRACT WITH

The Administrator would like to advertise for bids to replace the '81 Ford
truck in the Street Department. It would cost considerable to make all the
repairs, and has cost considerable in the past several years.
Tree trimming and cutting - nothing more as yet.
Ventilation for meeting roam to be looked into.
Welcome to Jefferson signs are still under consideration.
Contractor for Ohio Water Service installing water line on Market Street has
done a miserable job. Problems surfaced over the weekend with wash out in road
and at cemetery creating about a one foot drop. Village will probably get some
expenses submitted for damages to cars, lost hubcaps are at Police Department.
Ohio Water Service did care and repair. Further damage to lines in street was
also discovered when crews dug up.
Wastewater Treatment:  
Plan for EPA was completed and submitted. Ohio Water Service has backed off on
former letter advising Village of discontinuance of billing and collecting, are
proposing increase for services from 3.35 to 3.75%. Village will go ahead with
update and repair estimates of computer offered by the Community Center.
Random topics brought up by the Mayor: Merger of Jefferson Village and
Township; consideration given to the minimum security prison, Town Hall
building in the future.
Utilities: 
Hruska noted increases from East Ohio Gas and the Illuminating Co. If anyone
sees street light out, it should be reported to CEI.
Rec: 
The Community Center has hired a temporary program director- James Spaulding.
Ad for a full time van driver will be running. Rec Board terminated J.
Wasilewski. Department will be advertising for a program director.
Forestry: 
Committee wants to get together with the Administrator, Mr. Frayer and the
Mayor to go over street tree plan.
Ohio Municipal League seminar for officials - March 26 at Marriott Inn at West
150th Street in Cleveland. Those who wish to attend to advise at next meeting.
Registration $35.00 per.
Two police officers, Titus and Febel, are at the Physical Evidence schooling.
Old Business: 
Need to advertise for sale of Scott air packs as authorized by ordinance last
year. John Fazio will write a more definitive contract for the Employees
Handbook compilation.
New Business:  
There are parking problems at the Justice Center. Mayor will contact
commissioners with some ideas. Letter from Commissioner Mackey relative to lab
update and testing will be discussed with Pizel. Meeting with the Jefferson
Township trustees being planned.
The Mayor requested an Executive Session to discuss greens case under
litigation.
Adjourn:
Respectfully submitted,
Clerk-Treasurer

Justinian Publishing submitted a more definitive agreement for the village
consideration, Village Personnel Handbook project cost not to exceed $5000.00
totally. Motion made by Roach to authorize signing of agreement, second by
Buell. Discussion: The Mayor questioned why spend $5000.00 for this, could we
do this ourselves. It was explained that Council had tried to accomplish this
on their own for several years but found it overwhelming. This way we have been
given insight into other entities policies and the legal aspects on employee
matters. Solicitor also felt this is an important project, will work with
Council to complete. roll: Nemet, yea; Roach, yea; Herndon, yea:, Buell, yea.
Future work sessions to be scheduled to work on handbook contents.

Council was advised that a charge back on the performance bond could not be
made because no claim was made, there was no completion date in contract, and
provisions to act if work not carried out.
Wastewater Treatment: 
Motion made by Vance to approve the attendance of J. Pizel at the Annual
Wastewater Workshop in Columbus on March 2nd and 3rd, registration fee and
normal expenses, second by Roach, roll - Roach, yea; Vance, yea; Buell, yea;
Nemet, yea.
Electrical problem at plant appears to be CEI problems in their line; main
source of electricity wore out, shorted out in the conduit. Further problems
added when CEI employee used thumper without notifying our crews to shut off
anything. Village hopes to recoup costs from CEI,
Solicitor was asked to write a letter to CEI on this matter. Gammon told
Council Mr. Cole is looking into a devise for emergency shut off of equipment
when such problems occur. Crews were commended for their attention to the needs
arising from this problem, and acting quickly. Sewer rates for apartment
complexes was brought up for review.
Utilities:  
Letter from TCI Cablevision of Ohio, Inc. stated they are exercising their
first option on renewal of contract for five years in the village. Income from
franchise for 1987 is $4,506.86.
Rec: 
Community Center to be advised that the Council room is off limits except for
Mayor and Council and Township officials.
Forestry: 
Administrator is in contact with the Urban Forester and CEI on tree work.
Committee reviewed tree situation recently, noting work to be done.
Finance:  
Motion made by Vance to hear the third reading of Ordinance No. 1784, second by
Roach, roll - Nemet, Buell, yea; Roach, yea; Vance, yea.

3rd reading title only   ORDINANCE NO. 1785
AN ORDINANCE AUTHORIZING THE VILLAGE ADMINISTRATOR TO PREPARE SPECIFICATIONS

Motion made by Vance to adopt Ordinance No. 1785, second by Buell, roll -
Vance, yea; Roach, yea; Nemet, yea; Buell, yea.
Administrator ready to meet with committee, clerk and Mayor on budget.
Officials: 
Memo from the administrator on tax abatement received by Council. Pros and cons
of tax abatement were discussed, with the Mayor feeling it is unfair to
localize it. Ordinance does provide for review of the plan.
Old Business: 
Agreement with Ohio Water Service for fee on billing and collecting sewer
accounts will be brought up at next meeting. The feeling is to get computer set
up to do this ourselves.
Electric heaters in the offices at the Street garage may have been the cause of
a high bill.
Alternatives to be looked into.
Chamber of Commerce has offered to build a gazebo on the Southwest green at the
Chestnut/ Jefferson Streets intersection, with Metal Sales providing much of
the material. If built by the Chamber at that sight, they will finance. Mayor
suggested building a picnic shelter on green at Market/Jefferson streets
intersection. He would also like to consider burying the CEI lines along
Chestnut. Council approved the Mayor's going ahead with the Chamber proposal.
New Business: 
Discussion held on village crews doing sidewalk program, hiring out the keeping
of the parks and greens for a several months period. Green on the Northwest
corner of the Market/Jefferson intersection is a tremendous mess from football
games, hard to get back in shape. It was suggested that restrictions be put on
use of the greens. Administrator to check out with Chief Johnson on use of
green and damage to village properties.
Tree planning should be started within next couple or three weeks,
administrator intends to buy a few different types.
Tax Administrator appointment forthcoming.
Adjourn
Respectfully submitted,
Gertrude Armstrong
Clerk-Treasurer
Approved
Mayor

Visitors:  
Paul Butler, Butler Landscaping, had submitted a proposal to the village for
grounds maintenance on greens and parks, is looking to improvement of village
appearance. Council is taken the proposal under consideration, will also seek
other quotes.
Herb Locy, Ashtabula County VoEd, told council of plans to promote voter
registration and to emphasize the freedoms we have in this country. Primarily,
he asked for Council support and approval for one phase of the project, a
Berlin wall uptown for a week end in October. Plans for the construction of a
memorial at the school was given to Council. After Council reviews, the Mayor
will contact Mr. Locy.
Reports of Committees
Buildings Land Use:
Speedway, formerly Gastown before expansion, has applied for a C1, beer in
container carry out by application to the Department of Liquor Control. The
Administrator told Council that at the time of application to expand, they were
asked if they intended to have beer carry out - the answer was 'no'; also were
asked if they planned to extend hours - answer was 'no'. They now have done
both, being open 24 hours. The Administrator to ask them to trim shrubbery down
and remove flags from the curb area. Vance reported very loud music late at
night; ordinances to be checked on this. Their engineer will also meet with
Buckeye Masonry to check out noise problems coming into a neighbor's (Mrs. Cox)
home. Motion made by Roach to voice no objection to the C1 beer carry out
permit, second by Nemet, roll - Roach, yea; Nemet, yea; Vance, yea; Hruska,
yea; Buell, yea.
The Mayor will set up a committee to look into conformity in signs and building
improvements, mainly in the business district.
Service: 
A number of views were expressed on the replacing of a truck in the Street
Department, with the Administrator, Nemet and Ferguson favoring replacement,
the Mayor with opposite views.
Issue to be reviewed further.
Vance recommended going with the Butler proposal for grounds maintenance,
however, Solicitor will review contract submitted, other proposals to be
sought.
Wastewater Treatment:  
Letter from EPA requesting changes in general plan has been addressed by Pizel.
Further details to be worked out and re-submitted. CEI engineer will look at
damage at plant from recent electrical problems. Insurance company was down,
say that problem is not covered by our insurance. Pizel thought the single
phasing may not be, but the other damage after that should be, feels it was
failure of CEI to cover all bases.
Utilities: 
Motion made by Buell to authorize the Mayor to sign agreement with Ohio Water
Service for billing and collecting sewer accounts with rate at 3.75% for
service, second by Nemet, roll - Buell, yea; Hruska, yea; Nemet, yea; Roach,
yea; Vance, yea.
TCI advised the Village by letter that premium rates for cable will be
increasing.
Rec: 
Motion made by Vance to remove James Spaulding from temporary Programmer
Director position to full time status effective March 7, 1988, second by Roach,
roll - Nemet, yea; Hruska, yea; Buell, yea; Roach, yea; Vance, yea.
Forestry:  
Buell has been checking street trees in the village, will finish up soon, had
list of trees that need attention, given to the administrator. A company will
be coming in to check out work that needs doing and will give estimate. ODNR
will also be in with recommendations.

Reports of Committees
Buildings/Land Use:
Letter received by the village from County Commissioners informed Council that
the per capita charge for administering the building code is to increase to 25¢
per capita, up from 10¢ per. Council received copies of junk ordinance to
review.
Service: 
Quotes are being obtained for tree work.
Wastewater Treatment: 
Herndon recommended approval for attendance of Pizel and Gammon at the Apple
Scientific lab workshop in Cleveland on March 25. There is no charge for this
event which will address the new testing requirements from Ohio EPA.
Letter from Ashtabula County Sanitary Engineer had several questions on sewer
service to the township areas: Will the village extend sanitary sewers into the
township area to provide service to customers without the annexation of that
territory? If financing construction by County is required, would village be
willing to contract with the county to provide sewer service? What charges are
levied relative to the charges in the village for wastewater treatment? Are
there any other factors that they should know in dealing with potential sewer
customers outside the village? It is Herndon's and Pizel's opinion that at this
time we do not have the capacity to accept any more outside the limits of the
village, and do not have real estate to expend the plant. We also have to
consider the development of the acreage acquired, along with other uncompleted
developments before further acceptance. Word has been received that property
owners on North Market Street's East Side and north of Beech Street are
considering annexation. The Mayor and Council were not in favor of proposal
being considered by the Commissioners and property owners. The village has not
been formally petitioned on this matter.
Utilities: 
Illuminating Co. requesting 50% increase to be apportioned over ten years. It
has been suggested that the village look at generator system for the wastewater
plant.
Hruska reported cable reception problems.
Rec:
Forestry: 
The Administrator has done some shopping for trees - sugar maples are $50.00
per - feels this is too high, also stated that sugar maples are susceptive to
road salt. Crews will be planting from current stock when the weather is
conducive. Conference on Urban Forestry is being offered by the Illuminating
Co. and the City of Cleveland Division of Urban Forestry. Bishop and Herndon
will attend on March 25th.
Buell has reviewed a couple more streets with some recommendations for removal,
also suggested planting of ornamental tree by the students at the elementary
school grounds on Arbor Day. Pine tree on the southwest green near Sohio is
getting out of hand. Council to consider what we can do with this matter.
Finance:

Council received schedule of rental charges for use of town hall rooms proposed

Herndon reported letter received from insurance company stating the power
problem at the Wastewater Treatment plant is not allowable under the village
coverage as it is considered a mechanical failure. Herndon feels problem is in
CEI lines, installed by CEI when plant was built, could be defective
conductors, feels line could not deteriorate in the time since plant was built
- is strictly CEI material failure.
The Mayor will contact parties involved for information on the next meeting
relative to the Geneva OWS buyout.
New Business: 
Council voiced no objections to the Agricultural Society request to close a
portion of North Popular Street during Fair Week - August 9 thru the 14.

while culvert replacement over Three Breathers Creek is being done.
Council granted permission for use of Council Chambers twice a year for the Eye
Clinic, but not for storage of commodities. Requested by the Community Center
director.

department. All have at least 80,000 miles - '85s are $3645, '86s are $4350.

18 thousand dollars to get three cars ready to roll. Letter will be sent to the
State requesting the necessary approval for the purchase of 3 used highway
patrol cars as they become available. Department instructed to go ahead and
order needed equipment. The Chief was also given approval to purchase a new
copy machine.

Visitors:
Lois Blank of Lois Blank and Associates, through whom we obtained health
coverage with Community Mutual Blue Cross/Blue Shield, gave Council various
rates. There has been a dramatic increase by all companies in health insurance.
The Village's current coverage increases from 71.79 to 107.67 for single,
203.01 to 339.38 for family. Other alternatives presented were with HMO -
105.00 for single, 271.00 for family - have to report to the Ashtabula Clinic,
must go to their doctors, and have to have at least five in group. Blue Cross
of Northern Ohio, not even equal to our current coverage, 136.75 for single,
353.00 for family. Up front deductibles would decrease rates. Further quotes on
rates with deductibles will be obtained. All rates quoted were per month.
James Lemieux would like Council to entertain and welcome annexation of
annexation to the village, currently for six properties on the eastside of
North Market Street --- extending from Beech Street to northerly end of the
tavern property. The Health Department and EPA have cracked down on the tavern
establishment to meet their standards - existing system update would cost an
estimated $40,000. If criteria can't be met, tavern owner may lose his
business.
Both the Mayor and some Council members stated they would be more receptive to
annexation of properties on both sides of the road, and all the way to Route
46. Problems can arise with road maintenance with a half road situation.
Lemieux stated his willingness to get other property owners involved, will be
back at May 2nd meeting.

Visitors:
J. Lemieux and David Carlson - Lemieux advised Council that he has contacted
property owners on proposed annexation for area on North Market Street. He will
return to next meeting with more detailed proposal. Also he will respond to
question on whether the village will be permitted one more bar in the village.
R. Titus, speaking for the police department, stated they were upset with the
increase in hospitalization taken out of their pay checks, upsetting their
budgets, and not been aware there was to be an increase. They were advised that
Council is looking at other companies and plans, that Council had very short
notice of the increase also. Chief Johnson asked Council to meet with
employees, stating ‘we have no rights as employees on raises and benefits, we
are told what we are to get without asking the employees their thoughts’;
stated that he wants Council to be realistic on wages, are forcing employees to
go into a union situation. He also questioned village expenditures for other
departments, giving money to other places rather than the raises he feels he
and his people should be getting. He felt Council should be picking coverage,
that all the other communities are doing it, also citing wages of other
entities that are higher than our police get.
J. Collisse wished to advise Council that he is pursuing a program for
installation of flashing 20 mile zone signs for access roads to the elementary
school. To date best estimate of cost is $5000. School Board has seen the need
and are moving in support of this project. He asked that Council also express
support for this effort. The 'walk light' issue has come up again and will be
reviewed by the state.
The Jefferson Township Trustees did not respond to notification of Joint
Meeting for cemetery purposes, will reschedule for May 16th meeting.

May 9, 1988 - Special Meeting
Meeting called to order by Mayor S. Nizen
Pledge of Allegiance
Roll: Council members present: R. Nemet, B. Vance, W. Herndon, K. Buell, A.
Hruska
Also present: Solicitor B. Larson, W. Dillaway of the Beacon, J. Koziol of the
Gazette
Purpose of meeting: village/township inside millage, town hall status and
related governmental matters
Motion made by Vance to call an Executive Session, second by Herndon, roll -
Herndon, yea; Vance, yea; Buell, yea; Nemet, yea; Hruska, yea.
After executive session the Township Trustees J. Smolen, K. Biczar and Vern
Hall, and T. Harris joined the Council session.
It is apparent that there was a lease, as it is referred to numerable times in
the minutes. Harris stated that at a meeting in the County Commissioners'
office, the village had arrived at three points - the township would retain .32
millage, the village would retain .68 millage, lease of Town Hall for 20 years
with village agreeing not to seek secession in that time, and the township not
seek increase from the .32 millage. The Township was asked if they had
considered a price on the property. They had not considered this and were not
prepared at this time to talk about, but would look into. It was suggested that
the Mayor and Smolen, along with their counsel, hold sessions to discuss these
things. In the meantime we will work out lease agreement and hold in lieu of
purchase agreement. Other items to be considered as part of the lease should
cover maintenance, and an agreement termination option. There were no
objections to the Village maintaining the property as they have for the last 59
years, with a lease back to the Township to use the Council room as needed as
long as it did not conflict with Council activities. Harris will prepare lease
with the following a part thereof - Township will retain .32 of inside mill,
Village will retain .68 of inside mill, term of twenty years with 10 year
option with agreement termination notice set at one year, village will continue
to maintain inside and outside township will have use of Council room as needed
but not in conflict with Council activities, that the Village will not petition
for secession in the twenty years; that Township will not seek increase from
.32 mills during the same period, if extend would preclude also.
Motion made by Buell to accept terms for preparation of lease, second by Nemet,
roll - Vance, yea; Nemet, yea; Boczar, yea; Hall , yea; Smolen, yea; Hruska,
yea; Buell, yea; Herndon, yea.
Joint Union Cemetery: Motion made by Hall to approve preparation of proper
legislation to place a one mill levy for joint village and township on the
ballot for November 1988 election, for cemetery proposes, to be for a term of
five years, second by Boczar, roll - Herndon, yea; Buell, yea; Hruska, yea;
Smolen, yea; Hall, yea; Boczar, yea; Nemet, yea; Vance, yea. If the levy
passes, the current one mill levy from the village will be removed.
Motion made by Nemet to approve the appointment of Herndon to the Cemetery
Board, second by Buell, roll - Vance, yea; Herndon, yea; Buell, yea; Hruska,
yea; Nemet, yea.
Adjourn
Respectfully submitted,
Gertrude Armstrong
Clerk-Treasurer
Approved

Paving project: Streets not designated as yet. Mayor suggested that
intersections at gravel roads be paved back 50 or 100'. He has talked with the
County Engineer on cooperating on getting East Erie Street paved Market to
Sycamore. Estimates forthcoming.
Frame on plow on International Truck is sprung - estimated cost to repair
$800.00. Mayor will check out. '84 Ford cruiser work to be assessed.
Dearing, Asbestos Abatement Co., will be asked to attend to plywood in front of
window leaning out over the sidewalk.
Driveway from Peoples Bank to Satin Street: The Administrator has requested the
bank manager to have signs posted "no thru traffic" and " bank traffic only".
Complaints had been received that traffic was becoming quite heavy and at
excessive speeds. Traffic bumps were also suggested.
Sidewalks: Consensus of Council was to have village crews remove bad blocks,
set forms, then hire contractor to pour and finish. He had contacted contractor
who would come in with two men @ $60.00 per hour. Property owners would pay for
the concrete. The other suggestion was to offer rebate to property owner at so
much per block.
Issue II funding: Mahoney suggested we prepare of projects we want to apply for
funding for.
Grant application for EPA/OWDA has to be in August 3rd.
Wastewater Treatment: 
Application plan for sludge ready for Mayor signature. Meeting in Columbus with
Ohio EPA July 26th.
Utilities:  
East Ohio Gas has applied to PUCO for a small increase. Cable system still
being worked on, hopefully will correct problems with reception.
Rec: 
Ordinance to be prepared donating the Jefferson Community Park land to a
private organization as a site for a Community Center, with two year limit to
commence, if nothing happens, will revert back to the village. The Board has
been told that we’ll support financially with wages and benefits the balance of
this year and hopefully next year, but cannot assure beyond that. (funding for
three full time employees) Fitness Trail being improved, well tested.
Special: Forestry:  
Tree at Treen's on South Market to be checked out by the Administrator. Crews
are stuffing, and ditching.
Officials:  
Storm sewer project : The Administrator has talked with Rev. Brandis and
followed this up with a letter regarding the proposed route for the storm line
for the church council to review. Alternative route could be through Herndon
property and along Satin Street on the treelawn.
Old Business: 
Our crews are hauling stumps out of the Cucumber project area to the County
Fair fairgrounds, rather than putting in the ravine area. The Mayor can obtain
an engineer to make a study for drainage and culvert need at the site, $35.00
per hour. This work should be done when leaves are off the trees.

Visitors:
Robert Seese, enjoying his first day of retirement, introduced Warren Morgan,
the new manager for Ohio Water Service in Geneva office.
Dr. E. Rice informed Council that he felt we had a near riot on Center Street,
the problem has been going on for four or more years, that people on the street
are fearing for their lives and property; seems as though nothing is being
done. The Mayor advised him that we are in better shape to handle the
situation, have it under control now and are working to resolve the problem. B.
Westfall expressed his concern over the Joe Nosse development site, drainage
was not a part of the plan submitted when applied for zoning permit. He does
not want to create a hardship on anyone, but also doesn't want a hardship
created for him with the added flow coming onto his property. Mayor and
Administrator to talk with Nosse on providing plans for drainage.
Reports of Committees:
Safety: 
Bid notice ready for publication for the fire truck changeover. Air compressor
has to go back to North Carolina for some major re-design, would like to take
new cab and chassis to take the compressor down and back. No objections voiced
by Council.
Cars blocking sidewalks and parking on tree lawns being checked by police.
Truck parked in school parking is creating visibility problems coming off Satin
Street. Council was advised that we have ordinances covering loud vehicle
noises. Chief Wayman feels Council should address fireworks ordinance - like to
see all small stuff off the store shelves and unavailable to children.
Solicitor to further check out ordinances on this matter. Administrator to
check for 'no parking' signs on West Satin and speed limit signs on Pine
Street.

district, will be passed on to the Jefferson Planning Commission for review and
recommendation.

Asphalt Specialists, was the low bidder, but they did not come up with options
as requested, one of which was the two 1" layers. The Mayor stated that Koski
Construction came closer to our specifications, and would do the two 1" layers
on specified streets for an additional $500.00. It was his recommendation that
the village accept the Koski proposal, which also offered a 2% discount if
total package accepted. Motion made by Nemet, that the village accept the bid
proposal of the Koski Construction at $51,927.50, with the added $500.00 for
the 2 1" layers, second by Roach, roll - Vance, yea; Roach, yea; Nemet, yea;
Hruska, yea; Buell, yea.
The Mayor advised Council that the planed off material becomes Koski property.
Village will be starting on their sidewalks soon.
Drainage situation between Jefferson and Satin to Market to be reviewed
further. The Mayor noted that on inspection after a hard rain there was only
about 2" running through tile, but the street had excessive water running over
it.
The Solicitor will prepare proper legislation governing the installation of
parking lots in the industrial/commercial areas. Hopefully, in this way the
village can designate the drainage requirements.
County Engineering is doing the engineering work to obtain estimated cost for
the paving of East Erie Street east of Market Street.

Visitors: 
Robert and Tony Bucci appeared before Council responding to letter informing
them of the rejection of their bid proposal for the paving project proposed.
The letter stated that the options were not addressed, and a separate bid for
each of the locations was not submitted. The Bucci's stated that if they did go
by the quantity amounts estimated by the village to come up with their total.
If the village had worked these out, they would have come up with the Bucci
total. They said bid did not address manholes or water boxes - is a no pay item
for these. They stated they bid the same as Trinidad, that Koski did not bid
planing. They feel the bid the correct way, that the way they bid would save
the village about $2800. The Mayor stated that the village did ask for separate
bids so we could select one or all and asked for proposal on 1" or 2" layers,
and manholes adjustment. We do not intend to go into your bid and figure each
street out, 'Notice to Contractors' stated "Please submit a separate bid for
each of the locations, and a lump sum bid for the whole project. The Village of
Jefferson, Ohio reserves the right to non-perform any and all of the individual
projects." Koski did follow what we asked for, also the options of 1" or 2".
Bucci again stated that if we add up quantities, would cane to pretty much what
we bid, you can't abuse discretionary powers by accepting the bid higher than
ours. Mayor stated that he and the Administrator and then Council selected the
bid which was the best for the Village. Bucci stated he will write a letter to
the Ohio Contractors Association, asked for copies of the other bidders and
names of members of Council.

Residential Districts.

There was no public present for input. Return to regular session.

Visitors: 
At our last meeting council questioned the application for a D1 permit for
Jefferson Amoco Shop. Mark Lyden, Jim Stoops and Bob Santor from Lyden Oil Co.
appeared at this meeting to respond to Council. Why D1 permit? Santor stated
that at the time they considered purchase of the property a C1 was available,
however, after purchase of property the C1 was no longer available. A D1 was.
Communication with Senator Boggs confirmed this, so the application for that
permit was made. The company does not encourage consumption on the premises,
will not advertise nor list as available, but if it is asked for they will have
to oblige. The store will be set up with one booth for food and beverage.
Manager and employees, probably local people, will have class training for
operation of the business. Hours - proposed 6 AM to 12:00 midnight. After
further discussion by the Mayor, Solicitor and Council the company agreed that
if we permit D1, C1 will remain on file and when available the company will
give up the D1; keep price on single drink reasonably high -is a minimum but no
ceiling on what can be charged. Lyden Oil Co., dba Jefferson Amoco Food Shop,
will affirm this agreement by letter.
Motion made by Vance that Council "do not request hearing" for application for
D1 permit for Jefferson Amoco Food Shop, second by Roach, roll - Hruska, yea;
Buell, yea; Herndon, yea; Vance, yea; Roach, yea; Nemet, yea.
Carl Taft, re drainage problems from abutting apartment property on South
Market Street. The Mayor assured him that something will be done. Dunford will
be asked to be at next council meeting to address the issue. Jefferson Webelos
were welcomed to our meeting.
Reports of Committees
Wastewater Treatment
Tanks are in an operating, started last Thursday AM , tested out, are now below
state limits and can show EPA we can meet requirements. Pizel reported that
when jetting, line got stuck under a concrete driveway, indicating probably a
broken tile. Crews will check out and repair. Further repairs are planned for
the lines on East Jefferson Street.
Utilities: 
PUCO has scheduled public hearings in various communities, one at Kent Center
is on December. A request for increased lighting on North Chestnut at Dr.
Rice's and at Brakin' Joes will be reviewed.
Rec:
Special: Forestry: 
A number of trees have been felled in the village, and trimming done. The Elm
Tree program will be checked out with the local Boy Scout group. Council was
receptive to the program - municipal cost $200.00 per year for 100 elm
seedlings per year for five years, scouts would tend and plant when proper
growth.
On disposal of wood from cut trees - policy has been to approach abutting
property owner first, if can't use, would go to a 'wood' list of village people
first. If none, can dispose otherwise.

reviewed. A lowering of speed limit on West Jefferson Street to 25 mph was
suggested.

positive ventilation equipment, ram

of the bridge on North Chestnut Street. The Mayor will confer with ODOT on
various items such as detour and haul street plans.
There has been a rash of sign thefts. Village replacing then at quite an
expense. Trucks stopping on North Chestnut and other streets for short periods
is to be checked out by the police department. Administrator and the Mayor met
with OWS manager Martin on the village requirement for patching streets. Gazebo
construction on hold.

Mayor's Report to Council
   It is my opinion that we had a successful 1988, with a number of
accomplishments. The high points are that we did get a number of streets
resurfaced. We also were able to start our sidewalk program. Our wastewater
treatment plant was improved to meet E.P.A. requirements for the moment. The
Walnut/Sycamore intersection was filled and brought up to a much more usable
grade. The tree lawn portion of Satin Street storm drain project was installed.
A sizeable tree trimming and removal program for the year was completed. We
also planted a number of new trees to help replace those we lost. We purchased
three additional cruisers to give us a more suitable fleet which I hope will
last us, at least, into 1990 without further major expenditures. We also
purchased new copiers for the village hall as well as the police department. A
new fire truck chassis was purchased for the fire department. All in all we had
a good year in the village, but we were not able to accomplish all of the
projects that I had hoped we would. I am proposing to Council that we organize
better and attack our projects with more vigor. The committees for the various
village departments should confer with the Mayor and Administrator more
frequently and insist the projects that are to be completed will be kept on a
closer schedule.
   We had a number of major expenses which were a drain on our financial
resources. I have listed them as follows:
   Improvement in wastewater treatment   23,588.00
   Sidewalk repair program      4,360.00
      (we should collect back about 935.00 of this expense)
   Walnut/Sycamore intersection project   6,500.00
   Storm drain on Satin Street      5,331.00
   Street resurfacing program      52,063.00
   Overrun of costs - Cucumber Street      5,500.00
   Tree trimming and removal      4,000.00
   Police cruisers      19,000.00
   Copier for village hall      1,975.00
   New fire truck cab/chassis-apparatus removal/replace   59,914.00
   Insurance increases      12,236.00
   Payroll increases      44,745.00
   As you can see these expenditures represent a large amount of money. These
figures are in addition to our regular operating expenses.
   We are not reaching a fiscal emergency, but because of our large
expenditures for last year we will have to be extremely careful with purchases
through April, 1989. At that time we start receiving our 1989 tax settlements.
   It will be necessary to put a lot of thought into our 1989 budget. We cannot
be as liberal as we would like to be. A little bit of conservatism "make do" is
in order.
   I am listing below a number of suggestions that I believe would work well
and would help us reach our goal in improving efficiency.
1.   Consider the advantage of changing to a charter form of government.
2.   Establish central purchasing for all departments.
3.   Establish a parts and supply inventory.
4.   Reorganize our work forces for more efficiency.
5.   Raise sewer rates.
6.   Continue in-house mechanical repairs.
   Doing our own mechanical repairs has resulted in getting the work done
sooner as well as having a saving in costs. I know that instituting my other
suggestions would be equally successful.
   Projects that I would like to pursue for 1989:
1.   Start procedures for procurement of a permanent Village Hall.
2.   Complete East Erie and Sycamore Street paving projects.
3.   Start improvement of Cucumber Street project as well as considering a name
change for the street.
4.   Completion of mid-block drain for Satin Street.
5.   Completion of intersection of East Walnut and Sycamore Streets.
6.   Completion of culvert and guard rail project on East Erie Street.
7.   E.P.A. mandated improvements to wastewater treatment plant.
8.   Complete land use proposal for Cucumber Street development.
9.   Continue sidewalk improvement program.
10.   Implement an annual street resurfacing program.
11.   Complete a 5 year infrastructure study for the needs of the village
including an inventory of existing infrastructure conditions. This information
will be necessary to make a good application for Issue II monies.
12.   Start a program to beautify the downtown section of the village, such as
burying of wires, elimination of poles, install street light posts (to also be
used as decorative posts), replace oversize trees in narrow tree lawns with
decorative dwarf trees.
13.   Start implementing a drainage program for entire village.
14.   Accelerate a program to eliminate storm water entering sanitary system.
   (Issue II money can be used for this)
15   Lay out a work program with completion dates and have progress reported at
each Council meeting.
   I realize that this appears to be an ambitious program, but it can be done
if we really try.
   In spite of the fact that we had some heavy expenditures in some of our
funds, such as an increase of $44,745.00 in the amount spent for wages, we were
able, with the help of a conservative clerk to hold our expenditures to less
than we spent in 1987.
   Our clerk will provide you with our fiscal balances. Please study them
thoroughly. We will start putting our 1989 budget together very soon. If you
have any requests or suggestions, please let us know as soon as possible.
   I would like to take this opportunity to thank our Council, our Clerk, our
Solicitor, our Administrator and our department heads for a good year and a
year of cooperation. I am looking forward to a great year this year.
Thank you.
Stanley P. Nizen, Mayor
Adjourn:
Respectfully submitted,
Gertrude Armstrong
Clerk-Treasurer

M. Schultz of TCI - TCI is in process of turn on to new system, hope to
actually start individual boxes to new system January 23rd., with possible
completion of project April 1.Boxes that do not have a 36 channel capacity will
be replaced. An 11 x 14 gray box is to be mounted on the outside of the house
close to the power service. New channels will be part of the new system,
including arts/entertainment, C Span, TNT, and Discovery. No increase in rates
at this time. System includes a stand by power supply which will cover for a
short time when regular power is off. Finish up ground work will be done in the
spring. TCI is also working with the VoEd school to set up access for community
activities viewing. Non reception at times is due to the changeover in cables.
This process is unavoidable. On notifying property owners when work is being
done, he stated this is difficult to do. Notices of when will be working in
areas will be noted in the newspaper and on Channel 6.
G. Cole of East Ohio Gas: On January 10th EOG applied for a 1.1% increase in
rate, with average costs to users of $1.13 per month more.

work. At this time Dunford is willing to do work needed, but feels the other
property owners should share in the costs. Administrator to keep on this
project for completion.

work.

With the recommendation of Chief Wayman, motion made by Buell to make final

have been coming our way on service and response time.
At this time the Mayor designated the committee assignments for Johns - he will
chair the Wastewater Treatment committee, be on Buildings/Land Use and
Forestry, and replace Herndon on the Jefferson Planning Commission.
Letters received from the Police Chief: suggested the Police Chief be
responsible on decision of need for promotion within the department; would
recommend to Mayor and then to Council for approval. The Chief requested the
promotion of Patrolmen Febel and Titus to the rank of Sergeant. He asked for
the appointment of David M. Liggett to the Police Auxiliary. Copies with the
request underlined the fact that the Mayor makes the appointment, does not need
Council approval. The Mayor did designate said appointment.
Buildings/Land Use: 
Solicitor to check out village responsibility on opening up a dedicated street
and installation of utility lines. Interest has been shown in property along
West Cedar between Chestnut and Elm Streets.
Service: 
Discussion ensued with alternative thoughts on the development of northeast
quadrant and Cucumber Street, providing truck access to the industrial section
through another route, possibly Spruce or Sycamore Streets. The Jefferson
Planning Commission needs to address these and other land use issues.
Ferguson, Street Foreman, recommended we stop using cinders, go totally to
salt; also cited problems in catch basins with the use of cinders. Salt is
quite expensive, same companies are coming up with substitutes. Cinders are
hard to get anymore. Dirt roads are in need of repairs, reed to be graded down.
Wastewater Treatment: 
It seems probable at this time that the minimum sewer rate will be returned to
the $5.33 minimum, with other usages raised proportionately. Improvements at
the plant demanded by the E.P.A. and increased cost of implementing all the
requirements have made apparent the need for an increase. We are currently
talking with engineering firms on the next phase of improvement- the digester.
Issue II monies may be available for some of the cost. A meeting on Issue II
applications is scheduled for February 13 with EDATA and the County.
Utilities: 
PUCO accepted the proposal for the Illuminating Cos. increases over the next
three years.
Rec: 
Gates at the park entrance have been modified.
Forestry: 
Boy Scouts of Jefferson will not be implementing the national elm tree project
- is too long a process. Other options of tree procurement were mentioned.
Bishop reported briefly on Urban Tree conference, will follow up with a written
reccap.

Have guard rails - need posts and spacers.
Mayor: 
Enterprise Zones: The Economical Development Council is trying to establish
enterprise zones. The village has established such a zone, council gave no
indication of participating in the county proposal. Most companies are more
interested in good employees than in abatement. Nemet cited the effect on the
schools if abatement extended. He thought perhaps it might have some positive
aspects for smaller businesses which have a hard time starting in these times.
Income tax: the State legislature has some bills in the works which would allow
the school systems to vie for the local income tax dollars, which would hurt
community governments. Officials are urged to express there concerns to the
state on such measures.
Laskin clean-up: E.P.A. talking use of an incinerator, would be extremely
noisy, and have other drawbacks - emissions, use of village streets for access
and maintenance of same.
Mayor will be contacting officials on this matter.

February 13, 1989 - Special Joint Meeting
Meeting called to order by Mayor S. Nizen
Council members present: R. Nemet, J. Roach, B. Vance, W. Johns, K. Buell, A.
Hruska. Township Trustees present: John Smolen, Ken Boczar, Vern Hall.
Also present: M. Franklin, C. Wise, J. Bauwin, B. Wise, The Star Beacon, The
Gazette.
Purpose: Cemetery funding:
Over the years the village and township had funded the cemetery, until now
suddenly find out there is no funding from the township. Hall explained that
the township no longer has the funds at the $15,000 level, since the secession
move took a portion of the millage away from the township.
Mr. Franklin stated the Ohio Revised Code has no clear distinction on how a
joint cemetery should be funded, and that he has not had sufficient time to
research this further. He had prepared a legislation for putting a joint levy
on the ballot in May, which the township understood was what Council wished to
do after discussion at the prior Monday joint meeting. If this legislation is
enacted this meeting, it still would not address the funding for this year.
Question raised on budget of cemetery $54,000 last year, with the township
trustees feeling is more than should be spent there. They talked of cutting
expenses by laying off one man for, part of the year, leaving only one man,
which is not economical in the long run. The option of the township putting a
levy on the ballot on their own was suggested, then could borrow against
anticipated revenues. It is apparent at this time that along with the one mill
the village is paying in, the village will have to fund the balance from what
the township comes up with if less than the $15,000 from the one mill. The
township was asked if they wished to dissolve the union cemetery-negative.
After a lot of further discussion on the same matters, and on why the joint
levy failed, a motion was made by Roach to hear the first reading of Resolution
to place Joint Levy for Cemetery purposes on the ballot in May, second by
Buell, roll - Nemet, yea; Johns, yea; Buell, yea; Hruska, yea; Smolen, yea;
Boczar, yea; Hall, yea; Roach, yea; Vance, yea.
Motion made by Roach to suspend the rules on the second and third reading of
said Resolution, second by Buell, roll - Vance, yea; Roach, yea; Hall, yea;
Boczar, yea; Smolen, yea; Hruska, yea; Buell, yea; Johns, yea; Nemet, yea.
Motion made by Roach to adopt said Resolution. Discussion again on funding for
1989, with township stating they will fund whatever is mandated by ORC. If
there time the trustees will discuss putting their own levy on to try for
funding. Consensus of Council at this point was that the township go for their
own levy, possibly to expire at the same time as the villages. Mr. Franklin
reminded those present that they should look to going as a district and at what
is in the best interest of said district - this is a joint meeting and should
act as joint interest in the cemetery. Buell seconded the motion to adopt. roll
- Vance, nay; Nemet yea; Johns, nay; Buell, nay; Hruska, nay; Smolen, yea;
Boczar yea; Hall, yea; Roach, yea.
Respectfully submitted,
Gertrude Armstrong
Clerk-Treasurer
Approved:
