Motion made by Buell to approve expenditures, second by Hruska, roll - Nemet,
yea; Hruska, yea; Vance, yea; Johns, yea; Roach, yea; Buell, yea.
Visitors: 
The Carlsons re annexation: If annexation goes through, is it mandatory for
sewer to go in right away? What would time frame be for doing so? Council and
Mayor to review and respond at next meeting.
Jason Bauwin of Scout Troop 41: Jason is working on his Community Service
badge, one requirement was to attend a Council meeting.
T. Likovec of Burgess & Niple: Criteria and funding has changed on installation
of traffic lights. Village was inquiring for intersections at Rte 307 and
Market, Jefferson and Chestnut, and Poplar and West Jefferson Streets. Police
department will come up with more data on accidents at these intersections,
then can find out eventual cost and what funding available from Department of
State Highways and ODOT.
Reports of Committees
Buildings Land Use: 
Rear door at fire hall in, weatherstrip work being done. Council reviewed
drawing of Chamber of Commerce's proposed gazebo. Council had authorized the
Mayor to go ahead on the project to be located on the southwest green at the
Jefferson/Chestnut intersection. The Administrator was directed to issue the
zoning permit.
Questions again raised on what can be done to relieve eyesores in the village.
Solicitor advised that unless property owner starts damaging or it becomes a
hazard, we have no authority to demand beautification.
Service: 
Check on Community Development Block Grants availability. Ditches being dug on
Hillyer - two new homes going in. Mayor proposed shutting off truck traffic on
Poplar Street.
Council concurred with the proposal.
Wastewater Treatment: 
Motion made by Johns to approve Pizel attendance at the 26th Wastewater
Workshop in Columbus on March 15-16, with mileage, meals and lodging, second by
Buell, roll - Johns, yea; Vance, yea; Roach, yea; Buell, yea; Hruska, yea;
Nemet, yea.
The Mayor and Pizel have met with Likovec of Burgess & Niple to review needs
for improvement required by the E.P.A.. Mayor advised we need an engineering
firm now. Quote for initial work up to bid opening and recommendation on award
is $18,000. Agreement presented to Council would be for services as required
and requested by the Village, not binding to all projects.

Visitors: 
Mr. Lemieux, re the annexation proposal, stated that they have enough property
owners that want to annex, however, the properties at the intersection of
Market and Beech Streets do not want it. The Solicitor will look into whether
an annexation can be done if lands are not abutting the village. They were
advised that there is not a set policy on time to come into sewer system, but
when done it would be at the annexed property owners expense.
Sergeant Febel introduced the Police Auxiliary members, which has a roster of
11 at this time.
Reports of Committees:
Buildings/Land Use:
Service: 
Nemet asked that lists of things, that Council feels needs to be done, be
submitted to committee to review. Stumping, ditching and maintenance are
continuing.
Wastewater Treatment:
EPA has given approval for one-time deal for spreading sludge since we have to
clean out the digester. Janson has 63 acres in area where he can dump it. EPA
is waiting for soil samples and ration per acre before continuing. Cost is .05¢
per gallon, plus a $500.00 pump fee, estimate cost $6500.00, gallonage estimate
130,000.

in Denmark resulted in an estimated loss of $3000.00 of department equipment,

that tank inspections will also fall to local departments.

advised to double check problem origin before charging. We will have to go into
an industrial pre-treatment and sampling line program. So far we have been able
to work with companies to avoid problems.

coming up. Mayor and County Engineer have been discussing East Erie Street

info coming on village use of said machine to prepare and repair needed streets
before paving. Nemet asked that contact with residents regarding sidewalk work
be started. Administrator is keeping check on lawns not being mowed, notices
have been published advising the public of the criteria on mowing.

Visitors: 
Mabel Gogul - Gene Crislip, owner of lot abutting 223 East Jefferson, has not
mowed his lot this year as yet, did little last year. The Administrator stated
he has sent notices but Crislip does not respond to his orders. Last notice
sent May 19th for lot to be mowed by Memorial Day. By ordinance, if owner fails
to cut and destroy weeds, etc. by May 15th of the year the Administrator has
the authority to destroy such growth and owner shall be indebted for the cost,
and has thirty days to pay costs or indebtedness can go on tax duplicate. Gogul
stated that there are residents in the senior complex have breathing and eye
problems caused by weeds. M. Schossler - With new apartments going up in back
of Franley's, she is concerned about drainage, is concerned where
responsibility lies. A number of years ago, while she was out of town, creek
was diverted around her property, is no bank on one side. During recent heavy
rains yard was like a pond. When Poplar Street was raised, large tile was put
in, which may need cleaning out. She stated that her sidewalk was ruined years
ago with snow plowing - is exasperated with what is happening to her property.
Mayor will review the property.
C. Powers - Some attendees are here about request to Council about "open land"
for recreation; if some land not preserved, some as historical, the lands will
lost for all time; and also some are concerned about the maintenance of the
park - mowing - , some are for support of the community center.
R. Lewis, 271 East Jefferson Street, abuts the park area, objects to the
community center being placed there, feeling it is a 'bad deal', that we are
inviting trouble ahead. He asked if there was other land available, if sewer
system would have to be updated. . It was suggested he submit his views and
objections by letter to be on record, and that he could attend the next SOCC
meeting.
On mowing park - The Mayor had stopped it, stating that the village no longer
holds deed, thus is private property. Laidley, from SOCC committee, stated by
charter they are to raise money and construct, not to maintain. A few years ago
the village took over the parks, rec board was to do the programming. Four
council members said that they recall by a sort of gentlemen's agreement, to
maintain the park. The Mayor said the question is the legality. Motion made by
Nemet that the village take care of the land, mow at the community park, second
by Roach, roll - Hruska, yea; Buell, yea; Vance, yea; Johns, yea; Nemet, yea;
Roach, yea.
Support for the proposed Community Center was expressed by several, citing the
opportunities offered, the monies generated in the community from increased
participation from all areas. Amount of open land will be considered. Public
input is encouraged.
Mabel Gogul - What happened at cemetery - was not as has been in past years.
Johns said that for past nine years a good job was done and no praise, this
year had three fewer men, had equipment breakdown, rain most of May, but did
the best they could. Chairman of the Cemetery Board would not not support
hiring of more people, would not allow volunteer help, nor allow overtime. A
Clerk-Treasurer for the Cemetery Board started June 1st - Judy Maloney

Housing Amendments. As of the thirteenth of March landlords are no longer

Gary Pascarella, owner of properties on Franley Drive, told Council he took on
a project which turned out a bigger one than anticipated. To eliminate ditch
ten sections of 20' pipe were installed with another basin still to be
installed by the village. It will take a lot of dirt to cover, asked if any
would be available.

upgraded along with the planned bridge replacement already in the plans. The
village however should act on ordinance presented at this time and accompany it
with a letter on changes sought.

Motion made by Buell to approve the expenses, second by Roach, roll - Nemet,

Vance, yea; Johns, yea; Buell, yea; Hruska, yea.
Visitors: 
Gary and Barbara Pascarella-Over the past three months the Pascarellas have
tried to complete a tile project in front of their properties. They were
advised by the administrator on type and size of pipe to purchase. After a
number of delays, the pipe was laid but not as yet covered. Heavy rains washed
much dirt back into the ditch, caused the pipe to float and hampering drainage,
thus yards were flooded on the properties they own on Franley Drive. The Mayor
at this time became aware of the problem, advised them that this was the wrong
size and type of pipe. They feel a mistake was made through no fault of theirs,
asked that the village correct the situation. After a lengthy discussion on
resolution to the problem, a motion was made by Nemet that since it was our
mistake, the village is to correct the drainage problem front of the
Pascarella's property, to do it as it should be done at village expense, with
the village taking the pipe they bought and replacing it with proper type,
second by Vance, roll - Johns, yea; Buell, yea; Hruska, yea; Nemet, yea; Roach,
yea; Vance, yea. The village will do this as soon as possible.
David and Linda Masirovits: They had sewage in their basement again on June
22nd, insurance has over $5000 in this, they have $600 in it, are planning to
put furnace in and need correction to their problems. When asked if they had
had put in back up protection, they responded that no one had ever told then to
put back flow protection in. Such a protection is not the village's
responsibility. The village has been tv'ing the line, will be smoke bombing to
determine corrections needed to be made. The Mayor has also proposed putting a
ditch in the back of the properties to better route surface water to proper
channels. Village will do their part to help them put in a back flow protector.
They asked if any of the $600 they have spent out of pocket could be recovered
from the village.. The Mayor stated he would check with the solicitor but
didn't feel we good legally do this.
Mabel Gogul - Weeds on property abutting the senior complex - some was cut
today, more needs to be done; asked why sidewalks going east of town from the
tracks aren't being done; will there be open area at park. On weed cutting,
Mayor will check with administrator, on sidewalks, we are doing the high
traffic areas at the present, will branch out at later time; there will be open
area required by anyone who develops the northeast area, but not 20 acres as
rumored.
John Lightner - The building of a new home on West Cedar Street has caused
water to drain into the neighboring yards. The Mayor advised them he will find
out if village has the power to make the builder make satisfactory arrangements
for drainage. Other alternatives were mentioned to be reviewed.
Jack Felde, resident on W. Walnut Street - All West Jefferson Street properties
drain off to the West Walnut properties. At one time their was a ditch between
the backs of the properties. Mr. Felde was requested to try and obtain
permanent easements so village can do the ditching necessary.

Pascarella pipe out, ditch cleaned out. Herndon asked why we are doing the
Pascarella drain at village cost. It was explained that the installation done
by them was as specified by the administrator, after installation it was
determined to be the wrong pipe, flooding conditions also ensued. Council felt
it was a village error, village should fix. Herndon still felt it was wrong for
the village to absorb this expense. He stated that under a 1987 directive
village cleaned ditch and set grade only. Johns noted that village crews were
helping a resident on Woodside to cover pipe. Administrator will check this
out. The Mayor showed Council the drainage plan drawn for the Westview
allotment area. Incorrect storm connections came under discussion, noting
builders installing and covering up before inspection. Ordinance or directives
relative to installation, type of material required and inspection on storm or
sewer lines are to be considered, possibly next Council meeting. In the
meantime Administrator is instructed to follow up on requests for ditch
cleaning, grading and pipe installation with an inspection and instruction. In
the matter of proceeding with work in the Westview Allotment, the Solicitor
will check out procedures for getting storm drain work done.
Wastewater Treatment  
Inspection of the empty digester was scheduled for this day, but engineer's men
not available. It may be another week away. Pizel advised Council that the
digester has been pumped out, that a lot of grit was found in the bottom,
necessitating the use of a lot of water to be able to pump out. Ordinance gave
a 130,000 gallon limit, contractor would like to be paid for 150,000 to 160,000
gallons. Motion made by Vance to approve payment for the additional 20,000
gallons sludge removal from the digester, second by Roach, roll - Nemet, yea;
Roach, yea; Vance, yea; Johns, yea; Hruska, yea.
TV ing of line on Cucumber and Jefferson Streets is continuing. Vance called
Council attention to chapters in the Codified Ordinances relative to collecting
delinquent sewer accounts. The authority is granted to the Administrator to
place uncollected sewer charges on the tax duplicate and collected as all other
property taxes. (1030.06, 1030.065)

The gas rate increases about 2.7% for the next three months. The Mayor and
Clerk attended the TAG hearing in Orwell on the 17th. Most concerns expressed
were relative to bringing in out of state garbage. Transcripts of the hearing
will be available after all the processing of discussions.
Recycling - Mr. Kangas has found a suitable building, has trailer under
construction, has containers on order.

Visitors: 
L. Meckley - road and ditches on South Spruce not taken care of. Mayor replied
that they are partially taken care of, that we need to build up berms, will be
done before bad weather sets in. Meckley also stated that he is working with
the health department on the sewer into ditch problem in the area. Ferguson
commented that the problem on that road is not just because the grading, has
been a problem before that.
M. Gogul - weeds are still not down. Someone is burning garbage in the area at
night. She was advised to call the police department to check out burning.
Mayor feels there is a problem with the weed ordinance, can't ask that all
areas be mowed, we have fields and open land areas, not all lawns.
G. and B. Pascarella - they were advised that the village would start within
the next couple days to get partly done on pipe installation; there are other
steps that need to be done before completion for proper drainage. Mr.
Pascarella stated their names were mentioned in article in the Star Beacon
article, implying, in Pascarella's opinion, that the administrator lost his job
over this particular incident, asked that the Beacon retract the story. The
Mayor assured them this incident had nothing to do with the Bishop dismissal.
W. Herndon -Satin Street drain - Pipe is on hand, will be done as soon as we
can get someone to do it.
Reports of Committees
Safety: 
Committee received activity reports from Police and Fire departments. Meeting
with Fire department included discussion on resurfacing parking lot and
necessary painting.
Buildings/Land Use: 
We still have problem with areas of grass and weeds. At this time Mr. Crislip
addressed council on the 'weed' situation which has been coming up every week
at our meeting. It stated he has no problem with the ordinance, but if one has
to mow, all should have to mow. He cited areas, such as village owned property,
that are not mowed. He mows 250' from the road and side yards on his
properties, can't see mowing hay fields. He has not paid the bill for mowing
ordered done by the administrator. Committee to review ordinance.
Village is to pay Greg Lachey for three billings not paid for by the property
owner as yet; also one submitted by Maloney's.
Service: 
Contractor has scheduled paving for the last week in August. Trees are being
taken down. Procedures on disposal of wood was defined by Ferguson. Property
owner abutting tree lawn, where trees are being taken down, are contacted
first. If they don't want the wood, we go to 'wood list' of villagers who can
come and take the whole tree; after that the village hauls to property owners
who have no means to haul.
Question on tree removal at 18 East Satin to be addressed by the to be
appointed arborist.
Wastewater Treatment:  
Backflow protection installed for Masirovits property. Problem with fish kill
in Cemetery Creek being checked out by Jim Kelly and other proper authorities.
Strong odor problems were reported at the Childs residence on Woodside. It is
felt problem stems from pressurized line coming in from Thousand Trails.
Solutions being worked on.
The Mayor warned against the further use of pressurized lines in the village.
Utilities: 
Council by consensus approved the installation of two more lights on Hillyer
Drive.
Rec: 
Council received summer activities report. We have been notified that Debi
Johnston, Senior Coordinator is resigning, she is commended for an outstanding
job.
Forestry: 
Mr. Frayer and committee went to tree farm and have come up with a purchase and
planting plan. Trees are container grown, assuring a good root system. Plans
are for planting 12 trees this fall, 50 in the spring. With the rental of the
auger, estimated cost is about $1400.00. Residents will be asked to care for
tree. Committee was encouraged to proceed.
Motion made by Nemet to approve the appointment of Hume Frayer as Village
Arborist, second Buell, roll - Hruska, yea; Nemet, yea; Roach, yea; Buell, yea;
Johns, yea; Vance, yea.

Visitors: 
J. Lightner questioned progress on drainage problem on West Cedar, which was
brought to village attention in April. The Mayor told him we are spending a lot
of time on this and it will get done, that we are ahead of schedule compared to
time it would take if an engineer were hired. B. Brueggeman asked permission to
close Center Street on September 2 from 3:00 to 11:00 PM for a street party. He
was advised to submit a letter noting agreement by all the neighbors. Council
saw no problem with granting the request if this is done. Police department
will be notified. Emergency vehicle access is assured. Brueggeman also asked
about sidewalk in front of Smokin' Joes. The company has agreed to fix it.
G. Pascarella granted the drainage job was started in front of their property,
but couldn't understand why the work on it had been stopped, most sensible
thing would be to finish the job, but nothing done. The Mayor told him that his
job was part of the other gentleman's job (Lightner). When we come up with the
right way to solve the whole problem, the job will be done. There are
priorities, have street job has to be done also.
Mable Gogul talked of weeds again on abutting property. On garbage burning
complaint, she said it is coming from Sycamore Street direction, she had called
police, but burning continued. Mayor will check out. There is a dead tree on
the tree lawn at 223 East Jefferson Street.
Committee still working on weed ordinance.
Janet Pallo is planning a museum of Victorian carriages at 26 East Cedar
Street, asked if sign could be posted on right of way of unopened West Cedar
Street. Sign ordinance prohibits signs on public right of ways. Consensus of
Council was not to change ordinance, it would create too many problems. It was
suggested she contact abutting property owners on right of way for permission
to post a sign. Mrs. Pallo asked that Council consider this for the future,
make stipulations for allowances in certain situations.
C. Powers didn't understand Council refusal on a/c last meeting, asked for
reconsideration. The issue was misunderstood by Council when presented last
meeting, therefore, motion made by Vance to approve purchase by the Village of
an air conditioner, second by Buell. Cost quoted was $351.00, village will own,
roll - Vance, yea; Buell, yea; Roach, yea; Hruska, yea; Nemet, yea. Mrs. Powers
presented figures on how much money is generated by the money the village puts
into the Community Center, stating their per centage of input is higher or
equal.
M. Gogul asked where money coming from for new town hall, and why do we need a
new town hall. It was explained that the building and land belongs to the
Township, village has spent all the money to fix up, with sore large expenses
still anticipated, township has put nothing in.

Motion made by Nemet to approve the expenses and expenditures, 2nd by Hruska,
roll - Vance, yea; Johns, yea; Roach, yea; Nemet, yea; Hruska, yea.
Visitors: 
Joe Nosse asked about his request for street lighting. He was advised that CEI
has been contacted, we are waiting for their recommendations. Further
discussion dealt with portable signs, whether or not or how to regulate, what
is appropriate, set backs, etc. The Council asked for input from businesses and
residents, which will be considered in formulating an ordinance. Also in
question are yard sale signs and such.
Reports of Committees:
Service: 
Street paving will possibly start on Thursday. All missing street name signs
will be replaced. The Mayor will contact Skidmore & Chah on needed work on
Beverly and Hillyer Drives. Village maintains and plows, but does not supply
materials for such work.
Hruska commented on the good use being made of the equipment purchased for the
street department grader, paver, roller, etc. Nemet stated that all the roads
are not as they would like them to, but will be done within a program.
Wastewater Treatment: 
Electrical problem at plant has been corrected.
Utilities: 
Complaints have been received on water - non clarity and bad odor.
Rec: 
New Senior Program Coordinator - Vicki Sockman, had nice turnout for soccer and
baton.
Trick or Treat hours set for October 28th, 5:00 to 7:00 PM, Community Center
party on the same night - 7:00 PM to 9:00 PM. Spook Forest will also be held on
the 28th.
Forestry: 
Revisions near completion on Master Street Tree Plan. Report received on white
oak tree on East Jefferson Street stated the tree is estimated to be 400 years
old with value of over $23,000.00. Proposals on how to prolong its life were
also part of the report.
Placement of trees at certain distances from driveways, intersections and the
like should be addressed.
Finance: 
Motion made by Vance to approve payment of $2334.34. to Nicholson & Pontius for
legal services; second by Roach, roll - Nemet, yea; Hruska, yea; Roach, yea;
Vance, yea; Johns, yea.
Safety: 
No problems in fire department. Police Dept. got those responsible for
elementary school break-in.
Buildings/Land Use: 
Committee will be putting time in on sign ordinance, hoping for public input. A
prepared weed ordinance was given to Council for review. Good job on sign
posted across from Abernathy's. Hardee's moving right along. Village got most
of the top soil and the bricks. Money for the Anderson property is in escrow.
Officials: 
State has not responded on study of Rtes. 46/307/167 intersection. However, we
were notified that drainage project across Rte 307 near Washington Blvd. would
be the village's responsibility, as we own both sides of the road.
Old Business: 
The Covered Bridge Committee will be working in cooperation with the Fair Board
on signing for the closing of Poplar Street during their festival - hours
probably 9:00 AM to about 7:00 PM. Mayor felt everything is in order, consensus
of Council approved the action.
Council approved proceeding with the Erie Street project to be done by the
County. Total cost $21,527.00 with the village share being $3114.00. Figures
will be given to Don Treen to circulate among the property owners on the street
effected.
Study on generator installation at the wastewater treatment plant is in
process, would like to work it in with the rehab work proposed.
Adjourn:
Respectfully submitted,
Gertrude Armstrong

Reports of Committees:
Service: 
Paving of two streets, drive to pump station and fire hall lot are complete.
Crews to do berming and drive aprons. Village has five more culverts scheduled
to do yet. Lightner was contacted and advised the village is still working on
getting drainage resolved on West Cedar Street section. Erie Street paving
scheduled for June of next year. CEI will be in on Tuesday to take down some
trees, village crews to do clean up of same. Ferguson was advised to go ahead
with service on heaters in the village garage, if repairs needed, get prices as
opposed to new heaters. Crews have took out 16 stumps, more to go. Council was
advised that reflector signs for bridges are in and will be installed.
Wastewater Treatment: 
With the recommendation of Superintendent Pizel, motion made by Johns to
advance Greg Copeland to Mechanic/Laborer - 6 mo. status, at $7.31 per hour,
second by Roach, roll - Johns, yea; Vance, yea; Buell, yea; Roach, yea; Nemet,
yea; Hruska, yea.
There were no objections from Council on request for Pizel and Ferguson to
attend a Heavy Equipment show for a half day on October 19th, with pay.
Utilities:
Rec:
Forestry: 
Master Street Tree Plan revisions have been reviewed by committee and Frayer,
are ready for submission to be typed for Council review. Next spring we plan to
plant 50 trees in designated areas.

Chief Johnson and Sgt. Febel accepted a Pedestrian Safety award for Jefferson.
Said award indicates the village had no pedestrian fatalities, and has
participated in an ongoing pedestrian safety program. Council was also advised
that Lowell Masirovits and John Smolen, Sr. will be going to Columbus for a
Governors award for the ambulance district - have had no accidents since the
inception of our ambulance service. Police department is keeping a check on
tree lawn parking.

lawn and exterior building appearances in some areas.

Wastewater Treatment:
Utilities: 
Recycling project - Use of the cans is being abused. Some customers are not
cleaning out cans, bottles and other containers, dirty diapers have been found,
etc. It was suggested that door hangers be used to remind people of the proper
uses. Residents on bag service, those who live in apartments and non NE
Disposal customers will not be getting cans. There are no current plans to
extend the recycling to the east side of the village.

CHARGE AGAINST DONALD HERNDON
PURSUANT TO OHIO REVISED CODE SECTION 733.35
To the Council of the Village of Jefferson, Ohio:
I have reason to believe that Donald Herndon, a volunteer fireman with the
Jefferson Fire Department and a member of the Jefferson Rescue Squad, has been
guilty, in the performance of his official duties, of gross neglect of duty,
misconduct in office and nonfeasance, as follows:
   A.   He has failed to undertake the required hours of training for his
duties as a Fireman.
   B.   He has failed to answer 10% of the fire calls.
   C.   He has failed to undertake the required hours of training for his
duties as a member of the Rescue Squad.
   D.   He has missed more than 4 out of 12 business meetings of the Jefferson
Volunteer Fire Department and has missed 3 consecutive such business meetings
without a good cause.
   E.   He does not reside and is not employed within Jefferson Fire District.
I charge the foregoing and request that Donald Herndon be dismissed as a
volunteer fireman for the Jefferson Volunteer Fire Department, and as a member
of the Jefferson Rescue Squad. It is further requested that the City Council of
the Village of Jefferson conduct a hearing upon the charges against Donald
Herndon at its regular meeting on December 4, 1989, at 7:30 P.M. or as soon
thereafter as the Council may hear the same.
Service of this charge shall be made personally upon the said Donald Herndon
and return shall be made thereon as is provided for the return of the service
of summons in the civil action.
         THE VILLAGE OF JEFFERSON, OHIO
         BY:                                                                
          STANLEY P. NIZEN, Mayor
         DATE:                                                          
      (Return of service to be completed by Chief of reverse)
STATE OF OHIO   )
         ) SS:
ASHTABULA COUNTY   )
   I certify and return that on  November 21 , 1989, I received this charge and
served it by delivering to Donald Herndon personally true and correct copies of
the charge at 1188 Forman Rd , Ohio, on  November 26th , 1989.
Austinburg Twp.
   BY:  Chief John Wayman

the violators is. The Mayor will talk with Serwatka on this issue. It was also
stated that the 18 wheelers are still using Popular Street, law not being
enforced. It was also noted that the whole town has a problem with snowmobiles
now, atv’s in the good weather months. Registration of vehicles and banning
were suggestions to try to curb the problem.

New Business:
   MAYOR'S ADDRESS
   The Village of Jefferson has completed a successful year in all respects.
   We have completed a number of projects in the village which include the
completion of the mid-block storm drain through the Nazarene Church property.
This project was successful because it has eliminated much of the flooding in
that area. A new larger culvert was installed under Woodside Drive at the
intersection of Susan Drive. This project has also eliminated flooding in that
area. Increased drainage capacity and re-routing of storm water at the
intersection of West Erie Street and Franley Drive has eliminated the flooding
conditions in that area. Considerable storm drainage work was done on East Erie
Street. The area ditches were improved and many damaged driveway pipes were
replaced. The culvert pipe under Dorset Road at the intersection of Market
Street was replaced because it had deteriorated badly.
   We have purchased additional street maintenance equipment such as a roller,
spreader box and motor grader. The addition of this equipment was badly needed
and made it possible for the street department to do a much better job of
maintaining and repairing our existing blacktop and gravel streets. With the
use of this equipment we were able, with our own crew, to remove bad sections
of blacktop, repair the base material, and replace the portions removed with
new asphalt. Even with a late start we were able to make these repairs on both
Woodside and Westview Drives. We were than able to have a contractor put an
overlay of two one inch layers of asphalt on both streets. The repair work that
we did to these streets before the blacktop overlay could foreseeably double
the life of the new blacktop on the streets. We also improved the drainage and
base work on the driveway to the Woodside lift station and had the driveway
blacktopped. We were also able to repair the catch basin on Wall Street and
install a new storm across the village parking lot on Wall Street. After a very
bad start, due to an extremely wet spring and early summer, our village crew
was able to get our normal maintenance program completed as well as do most of
the work previously mentioned. It is my opinion that with some changes our
village now has an excellent, well organized and managed work crew who take
pride in the work they do. During 1989 it was a pleasure working with them.
   The Village again made considerable progress on our sidewalk program, but
due to poor weather we were unable to accomplish as much as I had planned on.
   We have completed our agreement with the County to pave East Erie Street
from Market Street through Sycamore Street and Sycamore Street from the tracks
south through the intersection with Erie Street. The Erie - Sycamore
intersection will be widened to permit heavy truck traffic. This project is
scheduled for completion in early June.
   We appointed Hume Frayer as Village Arborist and he has done an excellent
job of reviewing the Street Tree Program. Unfortunately 1989 was not a good
year for the village in the street tree program. We lost more trees than we
were able to replace. With the tree program now well established, I feel that
during 1990 we will be able to turn this failure around.
   During 1989 much work was done on plans to improve our sewage disposal
system. The plans were completed by our consulting engineers and have been
submitted to the E.P.A. for approval. We feel we will be able to advertise the
job in February 1990. I feel that our wastewater treatment employees have done
an excellent job and should be commended.
   The Village is financially strong and we have been able to end the year in
the black with no problem. Our Clerk-Treasurer, Trudy Armstrong, has done an
excellent job of keeping me informed on our finances and has handled our funds
very efficiently. Through careful handling of our village monies, she has been
able to earn in interest for the village nearly $65,000.00. This is more than
an additional two mill tax would have brought in. I feel that we have handled
our fiscal responsibilities very well.
   Our Police Department has done a commendable job of protecting the village
and have done a good job of trying to stay within their budget.
   Our Fire and Ambulance Departments are some of the best in this area and we
are very fortunate to have them.
   It is my feeling that the cooperation between the various departments in the
village is excellent and it shows that teamwork can get the job done better.
This also shows up in the support that the citizens of our community give us.
When we asked for the 1.75 mill operating levy renewal, the voters approved it
with no problem. At this point I want to thank the public for their support of
the village and our administration.
   Our village has continued to grow. We issued 44 zoning permits in 1988 and
this number increased to 59 in 1989. I an also assured of some further
industrial expansion in the near future.
   There are still many things to do and there always will be. After a good
1989, I grant to see the following projects for 1990:
   1: For the year 1990 I want to see drainage problems in the southwest end of
the village resolved. Our plans are pretty well in place and I hope that we'll
be able to start them soon.
   2: We still have a serious drainage problem on the east side of the village
and I would like to see this corrected during this year.
   3: We also have other drainage problems throughout the village and I hope to
eliminate than as soon as possible.
   4: We have purchased the property at 11 South Market Street for a possible
town hall site and we must have a move in that direction completed during this
year.
   5: We have several streets, especially in the Westview section that must be
repaired and resurfaced this year. We will go as far as our budget will permit
in that direction.
   6. We have a drainage problem and some street repair in the Jeffersonian
Estates section to be addressed. At least the drainage problem must be handled
this year.
   7. Finish the East Erie Street culvert west of Market Street and remove the
abuttment bridge over the creek on Market Street south of Satin Street.
   8. I would like to see the balance of Jefferson Street sidewalks repaired
and go as far as funds will allow in Chestnut Street.
   9. We must address the Street Tree Program this year and turn the program
around so that we plant more trees than we remove.
   10. Proceed with the East Erie Street improvement program in June as
planned.
   11. Improve the drainage on both West Walnut and East Walnut Street.
   12. Rebuild the digester at the wastewater treatment plant.
   13. Build an addition at the village garage to make sheltered storage for
ice control materials.
   14. Replace 2 police cars with used cruisers.
   15. Replace village pickup truck and village one ton dump truck.
I am proposing a sizeable program, but I think that we will be able to
accomplish it.
Adjourn:
Respectfully submitted,
Gertrude Armstrong
Clerk-Treasurer

Motion made by Buell to approve expenses and expenditures, second by Johns,
roll - Fertig, yea; Buell, yea; Johns, yea; David, yea; Roach, yea; Nemet, yea.
Visitors: 
Powers advised Council of a 'brick' selling campaign that SOCC will be
conducting, cost per commemorative brick is $10.00. In pledges and donations,
$56,700 has been slotted for the new Community Center.
Lew Hassled, representing the Ambulance Board, showed Council a plan in the
works for expansion of the ambulance section of the Safety Center. Council
supports the improvement. Funding for such expansion is borne by the ambulance
board.
Danny Hubbard cited a problem with trucks coming out of gates at the former GE
plant and coming onto sidewalks and into his yard to make their swing. It was
noted a similar problem exists at the Busch property to the north of the plant.
The Mayor and Roland will check out.
The village could possibly look into enlarging radius.
Special Joint Meeting: 
In attendance: Trustees John Smolen, Sr., C. Rippons, K. Boczar, Clerk Charlee
Wise and all on prior listing.
With the resignation of James Bauwin from the Cemetery Board, a new appointment
was needed to fill the unexpired term. Roach nominated Ed Utterback, second by
Smolen. Nominations closed by Johns, second by Smolen. roll - David, yea;
Roach, yea; Nemet, yea; Smolen, yea; Boczar, yea; Rippons, yea; Fertig, yea;
Buell, yea; Johns, yea. Utterback elected by unanimous acclamation. There will
be an election by the board at the regular Joint Meeting in May for term to
start January 1, 1991. Discussion ensued on the funding of the cemetery. A
decision needs to be made on this year’s funding from the township, whether it
be by valuation or trustees board decision. A resolution authorizing the
placement of request for one mill levy to be put on the ballot this November
will be presented at the next Joint Meeting. Suggestions for future facility
improvements at the cemetery included starting a perpetual care fund, laying
out sections with plates, develop land across the road, a small chapel,
complete water system layout and road work.
Adjourn.
Return to regular meeting of Council.
Reports of Committees:
Buildings Land Use: 
Committee working on best use and layout for village offices at the house.
Service: Village payment to the County for the Sycamore/Eries Streets
intersection will be 3152.36. Village will buy the material, estimated at $3800
delivered. Legislation authorizing agreement with County will be presented at
the next meeting. Fertig reported receiving calls stating need for attention on
Mulberry Street. Village will be grading at the appropriate time. Skidmore &
Chah have been contacted on improvements an Beverly and Hillyer. Parking on
East Walnut to be reviewed and proper signs posted. Commissioners are be
contacted again on parking for their people. Parking all day on Chestnut has
hampered parking availability for businesses.

Johns to approve said appointment, second by David. Ferguson stated he had not
done anything like this before, was willing to look into, wanted it clear that
if he can't handle or would rather not handle, he would like out of it without

thoughts. roll - Fertig, yea; David, yea; Johns, yea; Nemet, yea; Roach, yea;

Motion made by Johns to approve bills, second by Roach, roll - Nemet, yea;
Roach, yea; David, yea; Fertig, yea; Buell, yea; Johns, yea.
Visitors:
Jim Kelly, representing the Rotary Club, presented Council with a proposal to
erect 'welcome' signs with appropriate landscaping at entrance points of the
village. Signs and area to be maintained by the Rotary Club. Council concurred
that this was a nice gesture and voiced no objections. Appropriate permits will
need to be obtained.
D. Oblich had sent letters to Council relating to a drainage problem on their
property. Mayor and Street foreman will handle the situation.
Reports of Committees:
Service: 
Committee as given the Mayor a list of streets the committee is recommending
for paving this year. Sidewalks marked on W. Jefferson Street and portions of
Chestnut Street for repair. The State has closed Rte 307 for bridge improvement
west of the village. Plans for culvert under Rte 307 near Washington Blvd. are
being finalized. TCI has been called on their placement of cable in ditches in
Westview allotment, were asked to remove them.
Village Clean-up day to be coordinated by K. Fertig. Free disposal days have
been set by the Doherty Landfill.

Utilities: 
Mr. McLaughlin and CEI crew have replaced the lights on North Chestnut Street
to meet village request.
Rec:
"Brick" campaign going well. Roach wanted to make a formal declaration that we
will continue to support the Community Center as far as wages are concerned.
There was not a concurrence of Council on this matter. One stated that the
village has budgeted for this for 1990, not sure about further funding. Another
stated if funds were not available, rec might be the first to go.
Forestry: 
Listing of proposed street plantings has been turned over to the Street
Foreman, augur has been purchased by the village to do the tree work. Fertig
asked to be taken off the Forestry committee as he has not been asked to
participate or make any decisions.
Finance: 
The quote for higher limits coverage on Uninsured motorist was received from
Glazier Insurance Agency. It was felt quote was too high and was rejected.
Community Mutual Insurance rates for term starting May 1, 1990 are $151.4.0 for
single, 405.24 for family coverages.

Utilities:
Rec: 
Council received memo from the Rec Board expressing concern by Village
Council's seemingly lack of commitment to the Recreation Department, noting
minutes of February 5th and April 2nd. They state that recreation is a bonafide
department of the Village, they would like documented assurance that if and
when financial cuts become necessary that they will be made throughout all
departments and not be directed toward one specific department and that
recreation will continue to be supported financially by Village Council.
Nemet stated he did not agree with cuts throughout all departments, have to go
with priority for village needs. David wanted to go on record, that police,
fire street, and sewer are needed services, if funding not there, rec dept.
would go. During the discussion it was suggested going on the ballot. Near end
of discussion Nemet said we have no plans to cut funding, but if there is a
money problem, - don't know about next years budget - doesn't mean 1991 budget
isn't going to change that. Fertig asked at what point is Community Center
going to be self sufficient; we can't commit for next ten years for example.
Any change coming up will be up for discussion.
Forestry: 
List of trees and stumps for removal has been received from Arborist Frayer. 11
trees and 10 stumps. The white oak at 372 East Jefferson Street will have to be
added to this list. The village will use a part of history with removal of this
tree. Frayer likened the loss of this tree to the fire at the Town Hall.

areas. The Mayor noted we have no place, at this time, for truck parking. The
village owns a lot north of the 4H building at the fairgrounds. He will work
with the County to consider this a possible location for truck use.

Question asked - if accept a bid does it bind us to purchase only from the
particular company? This based on requirements of agreement. Village agreement
does not bind village to a company alone, only binding at a price quoted by a
company and accepted from that company.

and concrete, second by Roach, roll -David, yea; Roach, yea; Nemet, yea;

Council felt there was no need for an agreement with Ainsley Oil Co., since
prices would fluctuate anyway.
Culvert at one time proposed to cross Rte 307 at Jeffersonian Estates will not
be done, would not be effective way to resolve particular drainage in that
area.
There are some bad driveway pipes on Franley Drive, hampering drainage flow.
There are lawns in the village which need attention. These will be noted,
owners contacted. On the inquiry by Pizel if we have ordinance prohibiting
putting leaves and grass clippings in ditches - answer yea. Plat sure where
'officials' started.
St. Joseph is planning to increase parking area, will blacktop to library
parking lot. Village needs to go in and finish extended storm drain back of
church and the school offices to the Society Bank lot. Other drainage problems
in the village will be worked out as soon as we can. The Mayor said we are to
re-advertise for the part-time clerical position, also will be advertising for
police chief position. Letter from the Jefferson Police Auxiliary and four
regular officers asked that promotion be made from within the department.
Officers within department will have to apply also when ad run. Solicitor has
recommended the ad procedure be followed. Council will interview four
applicants, Ron Garvey, K. Settles, D. Lathrop and Bud Brueggeman, and any
others that carne forth, on May 30th starting at 7:00 PM.
Council expressed their thanks for the “welcome” signs put up at entrances to
the village. Fertig stated he has not changed his opinion on the Joint Cemetery
levy, but realistically, we have to push for that joint levy, only way to
insure the township participation. If not passed village may have to pay not
only our share, but also their share.
Council had no problem with request from Jefferson Junior Grange to sell
flowers at the village green next to Thorne's.

Safety: 
Village will be advertising for police chief position and other position. Mayor
was asked to contact the Police Dept. again on junk vehicles. Memorial Day went
well, forces did good job.
Buildings/Land Use: 
Plans for set up of offices at house are in the works; will have to have
handicap access, repair wiring, and some other items. Junk collecting around
buildings to be addressed by Mayor and Police Chief. Street Foreman will check
on posting of Zoning Permits on new housing construction. Parking lot at the
Kampf property is under construction.
Service: 
County crews worked on Sycamor/Erie Streets intersection on Saturday, under
authorization of the Mayor broken and collapsed tiles were replaced. D. Hubbard
of the Street Dept. will be undergoing surgery, will be off for a while. The
Mayor recommended hiring another full time person for that department. Question
on how to fund was raised, Mayor feels that sufficient funding is available.
Complaints on dust from streets - village has been brining.
Wastewater Treatment: 
Lines on Chestnut and Satin Street were TV'd, will review when received. Pizel
said he received a verbal quote of $19,000 from Burgess & Niple to oversee the
digester renovation job. It was suggested we go another way, hire someone
ourselves to do the job. Catch basin cleaning is done along with some work at
the wwt plant. They ended up doing the 112 basins; plus 20 more at no
additional cost.
Officials: 
The Clerk-Treasurer gave notice, last day will be July 31. 1990.
Councilman Settles was appointed to Buildings/Land Use committee with Chairman
David, and to the Wastewater Treatment committee as Chairman.
Old Business: 
Herndon made reference to sign and weed ordinances in the works- need control
on banners such as Dominos have been using all over the village.
New Business: 
Letter to be sent to the Rotary acknowledging the new signs at the access
points of the village. It was also mentioned that Mr. and Mrs. Blanche; on
their many walks, pick up litter. Village will check on obtaining additional
trash cans; as current number are overflowing. Paving plans are being worked
on. Cedar from Elm to Chestnut may be opened up by interested developer.
Drainage in Elm and Cedar area is being worked on now.
Fertig will check with Ohio E.P.A. on extent of work anticipated at fair time.
Letter from Ashtabula County Agricultural Society, requesting the closing of a
section of Poplar Street during the fair in August has been received by the
Village.
Letter of commendation to be sent to the Chamber of Commerce; David Carlson and
those involved in the street flag displays.
Adjourn:
Respectfully submitted;
Gertrude Armstrong
Clerk-Treasurer

communications changeover are being obtained by the Mayor.
Service:

Street for replacement. Gogul asked when village would get to East Jefferson
with areas of no sidewalk left. At rate village is going it will be many years
for sidewalk work to be completed. Herndon asked `how many blocks budgeted for
this year?' - answer - more than we'll get done. Committee was asked to work on
weed and junk vehicle ordinances. Most of east end of Erie prepped. Three
hundred feet of new sewer line was installed by Housel, at no cost to the
village, on East Erie from Sycamore to the tracks. Intersection is complete,
waiting for county to start cutting top off street. Driveway at north of County
Seat driveway is sunken. This may be a catch basin. Bad places in Nizen plaza
lot will be fixed this week. Village needs to get Poplar Street in shape before
the EPA comes in for Laskin project. Pictures are then to be taken showing
condition, EPA will need to bring road to condition during and after completion
of their project. Preparation of specs for one ton truck to be presented at
next meeting.

Motion made by Buell to approve the expenses and expenditures, second by Roach,
roll - Roach, yea; Fertig, yea; Buell, yea; Settles, yea.
Visitors:
Reports of Committees:
Finance:
Public Hearing for Estimated Budget for 1991 is on next regular meeting.
Safety:
End of month cruiser logs received by Council. Interviews for Police Chief
position will be conducted on Tuesday July 3rd - have five applicants. Problems
with skate boarding continues on East Walnut Street, it is felt parents are as
much to blame as the kids. Mayor will check on enforcement of ORC and village
ordinances for this problem and junk vehicle situation at Taylor's. Police have
received a new radar - working well. Department commended for their work during
Jefferson Days.
Buildings/Land Use:
Growth Partnership has applied for re-zoning of property at 36 West Walnut from
residential conditional use to commercial; will be submitted to the Planning
Commission.
Wastewater Treatment:
Preconstruction meeting for plant project was held, contracts were finalized.
There will be a waiting period of 8 to 12 weeks before actual construction
work, waiting for parts needed. Satin Street project being worked out. Copeland
took Class I exam, expressed appreciation for the opportunity and for expenses
paid.
Utilities:
Letters were received from TCI on rate increase for basic cable service.
Letters received from Ashtabula City Council President inviting village
officials to a meeting with other communities on July 19th. Cable tv will be
one of the subjects on the agenda.
Service:
Erie Street graded, manholes raised. County will put first 2" on, two or three
weeks later the next coat. Village also working on extending paving further
east and on getting the ditching done by the County. Crews will start on
sidewalks next Tuesday. Sotu Elm catch basins done. Walkway from Ellioot top
school needs attention. Water needs to be redirected to avert washout that is
happening at bulkhead on Woodside. Crews will do on Monday. Work session
scheduled after Special Joint meeting on July 9th - to work on weed and junk
ordinances. Solicitor was asked to prepare ordinances for purchase of a one ton
truck and for sale of '82 pick up.
Recreation:
Motion made by Roach to approve the appointment of Virgie Butcher to the Rec
Board, second by Fertig, roll - Fertig, yea; Buell, yea; Settles, yea; Roach,
yea; Nemet, yea.
Forestry:
Mr. Frayer resigned position of Village Arborist, but has agreed to assist
Buell in an advisory capacity. Committee is spotting places for all tree
planting.
Officials:
Paving plan for this year - next meeting.
Old Business:
Mayor has been in contact with Skidmore & Chah - will ask the company for 4"
added material after scarifying current surface on Beverly and Hillyer Drives.
Motion made by Nemet to approve the Mayor's appointment of Norman David to the
Zoning Inspector position, retaining Roland Ferguson as Assistant, second by
Buell, roll - Nemet, yea; Roach, yea; Fertig, nay; Buell, yea; Settles, yea.
New Business:
Applications for Clerk-Treasurer have been received. Two applications for
Council seat also received.
Adjourn:
Respectfully submitted,
Clerk-Treasurer

1st Reading Title Only   RESOLUTION NO 1881
A RESOLUTION FOR THE SUBMISSION TO THE ELECTORS OF THE VILLAGE OF JEFFERSON,
ASHTABULA COUNTY, OHIO ON THE 6TH DAY OF NOVEMBER 1990 OF THE QUESTION OF A
RENEWEL LEVY OF 1.00 MILLS PER YEAR FOR FIVE YEARS, FOR EACH DOLLAR OF THE
TAXABLE PROPERTY WITHIN THE VILLAGE OF JEFFERSON, OHIO FOR THE PURPOSE OF
PROVIDING AND MAINTAINING FIRE APPARATUS, APPLIANCES, BUILDINGS OR SITES
THEREFOR, OR SOURCES OF WATER SUPPLY AND MATERIALS THEREFOR, OR THE
ESTABLISHMENT AND MAINTENANCE OF LINES OF FIRE ALARM TELEGRAPH OR THE PAYMENT
OF PERMANENT, PART-TIME OR VOLUNTEER FIREMAN OR FIRE FIGHTING COMPANIES TO
OPERATE THE SAME IN THE VILLAGE OF JEFFERSON, OHIO IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE
PROVISIONS OF SECTIONS 5705.19 and 5705.25 OF THE REVISED CODE OF OHIO. SAID
LEVY TO APPEAR UPON THE TAX DUPLICATE OF THE VILLAGE OF JEFFERSON, ASHTABULA
COUNTY, OHIO FOR THE TAX YEARS 1991 to 1995, INCLUSIVE.

against. Will vote on rezoning. Open hearing closed at 8:15 P.M.

October 22, 1990 - Special Work Session Village and Township
Meeting called to order by Marty KUHLA
Members present: Council: R. NEMET, K. FERTIG, K. BUELL, K. SETTLES, L. BRAGGA
J. ROACH
Township: J. SMOLEN, K. BOCZAR, C. RIPPONS
Visitors:
Nola LARSON, V. SKIDMORE, G. PYLE, A. PYLE, P. HAINES, W. BRAINARD, E. RICE, M.
PRACHTKO, D. AKINS H. BRUGEMAN, F. KID, J. HALL, N. DAVID, G. HOUSEL, STAR
BEACON, GAZETTE, B. DURAY, W. OBEYMEYER J. MYERNICK
KUHLA: We have been working with Worthington since March 1990, originally
looked at Coffee Creek but soil conditions were not favorable, then began to
look at Jefferson area.
Review of Questions:
Q: Why not locate in the present Industrial Zone on Route 46 North?
A: Sewer, water, infrastructure, need 45 acrea. EPA discouraging package
plants, to run sewer line from Jefferson would be 5500 ft cost would have to be
assessed as well as water lines $150,000 cost. Wetland permits hard to get and
the time required. At 307 site less than 1000 feet to connect.
Q: Water table?
A: Mr BOGGS has been working on this with the State
Q: Spot Zoning?
A: Contiguous Industrial Zoned area (County Comprehensive Plan) spot zoning not
an issue.
Q: Traffic patterns?
A: ODOT Region IV Ravenna has been contacted by Mr. BOGGS
DURAY: If Bob LUCE had not passed away where would it have been located? No
other area met all the requirements of Worthington.
What guarantee do we have that the next industry that comes along you won't do
this again? What site will be available then? KUHLA: Your officials need to get
together to make plans for the future.
DURAY: We want Worthington but don't want less desireable plants. Tax
Abatement?
5 year 75%- Virgil Wynland said this was discussed and the intent of the
Village was to insist on annexation. Tap in fee instead of annexation. A letter
was sent a week ago to the company. Mayor Nizen: We will need a rate ordinance
insure that Worthington will pay tap-in fee and rates which will be fair to the
other residents of the Village. A letter was prepared a month ago. Annexation
was required at that time, according to the concensus of the Council (telephone
contact) BRAGGA said he had met with Hugh THOMAS on this. At the time he felt
the Village should get some piece of the pie.
Residents would be willing to rezone for Worthington only-if they don't come
rezone it back. MEYERNICK: You can't do a conditional zoning change for one
company, you would have to go back through the whole process of rezoning.
FERTIG: At one time this area was zoned industrial.
Water? What if we have to go off our wells? Do we have to take sewer in order
to get water? Do we have to annex in order to get water? Mayor NIZEN No, the
Village doesn't own the water company.
Spruce Street is already bad. We need some speed limit and load limit
regulations. Let's do this before they come in. Need patrols during peak
traffic hours. Need sign -No thru truck-children playing. This is a formal
request to you and the Trustees Mr. SMOLEN. 750 cars leave here every day we
need signs on Route 307.
SMOLEN: Prosecutor was contacted. Need some answers from Zoning Commission,
either yes or no on rezoning Special meeting tenatively scheduled for 10/23/90.
MEYERNICK call it for Wednesday at 7:00 PM if possible.
MEYERNICK: Worthington asked him to talk to the residents who signed the
petitions. There were 113 signatures. 75 people were contacted 38 were not. 65
signers have requested that their signatures be removed. NEMET asked if
priority will be given to Township and Village residents on jobs? a thought for
abatement talks. RIPPONS would like a copy of the letter sent to Worthington.
Mayor NIZEN will discuss this at next council meeting.
KUHLA: The Township should designate an industrial park with abatement.
OBEMEYER the Zoning Commission was approached 10 years ago were told by the
County Planning Commission to roll back our industrial area.
MEYERNICK -What was suitable then is not necessarily suitable now because of
Wetlands legislation
MEYERNICK: Where do we go from here? Village Sewer-Township Zoning. Plant to be
operational by Nov 1991
NIZEN: The Village is ready and willing to welcome Worthington.
SETTLES: Considering the time frame it took Worthington to decide Coffee Creek
was not a viable area for locating its plant there and the short time frame it
took for the Village and Township to act should give them a very good
impression of the Jefferson area.
Adjourned at 9:30 P.M.
Respectfully submitted:
JUDITH A. SELZER Clerk/Treasurer

Mayor's Report to Council:
1990 was a very busy year in the Village. We had many accomplishments, but for
various reasons we were not able to complete some of the projects that we had
hoped to do. Considerable ditching and drainage was completed as well as a
number of new catch basins and culverts were installed. Erie Street paving was
completed from Market east through the intersection with Sycamore. Sycamore was
paved from the tracks south through the intersection with Erie. A completely
new Erie and Sycamore intersection was built to accomodate large trucks that
serve the County Highway Department, and our industrial section. The Erie
Street project was in the planning stages for many years, but was to costly to
proceed with. With the help of the County Highway Department and our own crew,
we were able to cut the cost of improvements to an acceptable level and the
project was completed in 1990. From now on the residents in the neighborhood
will be able to enjoy a dust free area to live in. Our maintenance costs of the
street should be reduced considerably. I would like to recommend that the
Village make plans to improve Sycamore Street South to SR 307 as well as the
balance of Erie Street from Sycamore to Cucumber. This improvement should be
constructed to serve as a truck route for our industrial area. When completed
we will be able to eliminate most of the truck turning traffic at the Square as
well as the truck traffic at the Elementary School intersection. I have been
very concerned with the truck turning hazard and congestion at the Square as
well as the danger of the truck and traffic congestion at the Elementary School
where our heaviest foot traffic and crossing problems exist.
Our Village crew installed a new storm sewer on South Market Street in front of
the school property. We have had drainage problems in this area for some time
and discovered that someone had removed sections of our storm sewer line and
did not replace them. I can only guess that this was done by one of our utility
companies or a private contractor. I wonder where our inspector or
administrator was a that time. The reopening of the storm sewer line will
eleiminate many of the water problems at the school because the school is once
again connected to a working storm sewer line.
Our Village crew was trained in a new process of pavement crack sealing and
this past fall, as the equipment became available, we started a crack sealing
program. We were able to seal the cracks on several streets before we had to
return the equipment. This system of crack maintenance will probably increase
the surface life of our streets by 5 years. Our plan is to rent the equipment
as soon as possible this year and hopefully crack seal the balance of the
streets. This program will save the Village a considerable amount of money by
prolonging the surface life of the black top streets.
Our own crew also removed bad portions of Poplar Street, repaired the base and
replaced black top with new material. In previous years, project such as these
were either contracted out or not done. It shows that with good help, proper
equipment and a good work attitude we can accomplish a lot and at the same time
cut costs.
Our Wastewater Treatment Plant renovation contract was let and work has been
progressing very well. The project should be completed in the very near future,
and hopefully will meet EPA requirements for sometime to come. In addition to
their regular work of operating the Sewage Plant, our wastewater employees have
been very busy with keeping the sewer and storm sewer lines free from
obstructions and eliminating other problems. With the cooperation of the Street
Department we were able to redirect the storm water from the fairgrounds so
that it is no longer washing out the footings under our overhead line North of
the Fairgrounds. Our Wastewater crew, over the year, has been able to eliminate
many instances of storm sewer infiltration into our sanitary system. Our
sanitary lines are getting old and in some areas deteriorating very badly. I
have applied for and am assured of getting $80,000.00 grant from Issue II Funds
to help the Village correct a large part of this infiltration problem. We hope
to be able to start this program by Spring and completed this year.
We appointed a new Police Chief, Steve FEBEL, and I feel that our choice was a
good one. He is handling the job very well and as with all departments he is
faced with many new regulations which he must familiarize himself with and also
insure that his other officers are kept up to date. Traffic control has
improved. In my opinion we have a very good Police Department and they do an
excellent job of serving the Village.
Our Fire and Ambulance Departments are doing an excellent job. New equipment is
being added and I would say both Departments are very well managed and second
to none in the area.
I would like to take this opportunity to thank all our Village employees for a
job well done. Especially the Department Heads, Roland FERGUSON, Jeff PIZEL,
Steve FEBEL, and John WAYMAN. I have had their complete cooperation and I in
turn did everything I could to cooperate with them. The Departments cooperate
with each other perfectly as well as the Cemetery Board. At this time I feel
that each and every one of our employees knows what his job is and takes pride
in doing it. We have a very dedicated group of employees who are proud of this
community. I would also like to thank Norm DAVID for being my right arm. He has
been a big help to all Department Heads.
I feel that our Department Heads are now well enough versed in their duties,
that I could leave for an indefinite period of time and they could carry on
with no problem.
Our fiscal condition is very strong. Again we have been able to strengthen our
balances over previous year. We have been able to pay for our sewer plant
improvements without borrowing. We have been able to accumulate enough cash
balance in our Municipal Facility and Capital Improvement Fund to build a new
Town Hall without borrowing money to do it. Through fiscal responsibility and
proper investing of our cash balance we have been able to collect an additional
$75,000.00 in interest. This amounts to approximately 2 1/2 mils of Real Estate
Taxes. If we are able to cooperate and continue to handle our fiscal
responsibilities correctly we should be able to institute a Real Estate Tax cut
in the near future. Maybe we could set a precidence showing our State and
Federal Governments shameing them into a little fiscal responsibility.
We were not able to accomplish everything that I wanted to get done in 1990. We
failed to correct some of our drainage problems. Especially in the Southwest
area and in the Eastern part of the Village. We have had set backs in our plans
and I hope that we soon will be able to correct them. I also hope we will be
able to solve some of our drainage problems in the Jeffersonian Estates area.
Our plans call for an early start on our sidewalk program this Spring.
We plan on expanding our street black topping as soon as possible weather
permitting in the Spring.
I would like to see our sanitary sewer water infiltration program completed
this year.
In 1990 we planted 88 new trees and took down 22 trees a gain of 66 trees. That
was a big step in the right direction and I would like to see it improved upon.
I am going to try to provide funds in the next budget to replace the 1981 Ford
Dump Truck.
It is necessary to build additional covered storage at the Village Garage for
ice control materials.
We must finish the Erie Street Culvert Project.
Prepare plans and build a new Town Hall that we as a Village can be proud of.
It should be part of our Civic Center at East Jefferson and Market Streets.
Thank you,
S. P. NIZEN Mayor

Regular meeting adjourned at 8 P.M. Joint Meeting in Session:
SMOLEN concerning the Townhall, does the Village want to continue lease?
RIPPONS the people are not in favor of selling the Townhall at this time. We
want everything on the table as soon as possible. Mayor NIZEN we are waiting
for more reports. SETTLES we know the building is structurally sound. Why did
you decide not to sell? RIPPONS because the people do not want to give up the
Town Hall as their meeting place. The Village pays the insurance for the
Townhall, who is the beneficiary? Mayor will find out. RIPPONS also wanted to
know what is going on with the 350 acres North of town and why aren't the
Township Trustees notified about negotiations and must read them in the paper?
Mayor I do not have to make my negotiations public until the decission is made.
RIPPONS that is what causes the difficulties between the Village and Township,
maybe they could be resolved if we communicated more readily, then these
problems would deminish. Mayor I have no intentions to divulge information
prematurely. RIPPONS if you wait too long, then the residents feel as though
nothing can be done to stop it. ROACH perhaps we can include the Township in
future negotiations i.e. professional courtesy/consideration. BRAGGA asked
Solicitor how the anexation process works. Solicitor explained process. Mayor
that is why I talk merger rather than annexation, less problems. Bonnie DURAY
wanted to know about Joint Committee. She wants to resign so that residents can
form their own committee. What is latest on Worthington. RIPPONS will break
ground in April. Mayor called last week everything is moving along. Motion by
SETTLES, seconded by ROACH to adjourn. All in favor.

COMMITTEE REPORTS
Finance:
Bids on Village insurance received. Will need a work session to decide carrier
and best agency for Village. Work session and special meeting called for 7 p.m.
3/25/91. Press present. Clerk to call Auditor and make arrangements concerning
first reading and send it in unapproved, then pass retroactive legislation.
Local grant funds? Solicitor could have 3 special meetings, 6, 7, 8 p.m. if
necessary. Clerk to contact press. Glazier - Village insurance due 4/2/91;
April 1 meeting would be o.k.
Wastewater Treatment:
Settles - Pizel has gone to seminar. Introduced Al Nottage about cogeneration
at plant. The heat generated from generator could be used to reduce the drying
time in the sludge beds 50-60%. CEI tests are about the same as he conducted
last year. Generator at New Castle was estimated to run for 12,000 hrs. prior
to service, has now run 320,000 hrs. (Waukasua). Took 3 years to recoup
investment. Economics good for Jefferson. $78,000 for one 165 kw. Nottage to
send Settles list of plants currently on line locally.
Utilities:
Fertig attended a meeting in Ashtabula; 8-9 municipalities represented. Wants
to form a consortium with 12 members to share in cost ($12,000) of legal fees.
Ordinance will provide regulatory rules for cable. Recommends we hold off until
more information received. Mayor - our Administrator has good knowledge of
cable. Will work with the committee. Fertig - received a letter from
Northeastern Disposal. Effective 4/1/91, rates will be increased due to his
increase from landfill. Nemet read about some recycling in Cleveland, will
investigate.
Recreation:
Roach - Rec. Board & SOCC are continuing to work on the fund raising campaign.
Saw a video on Boys & Girls Club. The local club is progressing well.
Forestry:
Bragga attended the briefing on Gypsy Moth eradication at Rush Creek property.
Spraying should be started in May after we decide which form of pesticide to
use. Received a letter from U.S. Army Corps concerning Wetlands. Recommends we
hold report until needed. Mayor states that there is new legislation in
Congress which may overturn current Wetlands issue.
Service:
Nemet - letter from AC Planning Commission to proceed with Worthington Cylinder
Project. Mayor spoke with him today. One-half the funds for engineering are to
come from JDC. Will contact John Lampson 3/19/91 to make sure funds are
available. Bragga concerned about the project at Busch's garage. He wants to be
sure that tree lawns are not being replaced by parking spaces. Berm is for
turn-around only, no parking allowed.
Buildings/Land Use:
Rippons wanted to know if the Village has a timetable to move yet. Mayor - not
yet, but hopes to have something at their meeting this week. Part of the lease
was for maintenance of the Town Hall. Can we have an agreement for the Village
to pay for this before the move.
Safety:
Nemet - two police officers have attended a seminar. Chief Febel states they
are having problems with heavy trucks on Spruce Street. Will attend a meeting
at Lakeland College concerning new state regulations for weapons
qualifications.

with recommendations for the Clerk and Administrator to complete.

corrected before paving. When will the paving project be bid out? Mayor will
meet with Jeff Pizel and the Administrator next week on this. A steel feeder
line at the Wastewater plant needs repair. The Mayor will check this out and
possibly have it done by summer. Bragga asked about the Worthington extension.
Mayor - all is going according to plan. Pizel went to a workshop in Columbus
which was very informative. He wanted to thank Council for sending him.
Utilities:

Forestry:

chemical to use on the gypsy moth. The current preference is Demelin, and a

Service:
Nemet - Heritage Hills is having problems with rusted and crumbling culverts

pool. The lighting is adequate. Some improvements have been completed since the

before these streets can be accepted. Fertig - reported that the FCC license

Motion by Roach, seconded by Meehl, to pay current bills. Roll: Settles, yea;

Visitors:
Cayce Baxley - Jefferson is not a retirement community; there are a lot of
children here. To. Fleming - There are ambulances at different stores during
all hours. John Meehl will check it out. D. Serwatka is in favor of a tax levy
for the Community Center.
Utilities:
Fertig - We're supposed to have prior notification from Ohio Water Service for
digging. Have they started doing that yet? Weir - A letter has been sent. Now
they are notifying us. Weir also said he would call tomorrow about start dates
on the paving projects.
Recreation:
Roach - Summer playground has started; we have 100 swimmers signed up, and on
the 10K run, there were 110 participants. There are 25 senior citizen meals
served a day. Resolution #1918 - Roach included an amendment to add an
operating tax levy -- millage to be determined later. Motion by Roach, seconded
by Settles, to approve the amendment. Meehl - Finance Committee met to discuss
Resolution #1918. He presented a list of possible amendments to consider, with
the recommendation to place an operating levy on the ballot in November, 1991,
to cover the costs of operating the proposed Community Center, with the
contingency that no tax dollars would be collected until after the Community
Center is built and accepted by the Village. Bragga - Is the intent of your
recommendation to restructure present funding of the Community Center? Nemet -
yes, but salaries were not discussed, just operation of the new building.
Bragga - How much will it cost to operate the building? Settles - about $35,000
per year. Joint Recreational District discussed; Village and Township now,
additional districts later. Meehl - Would the Township be willing to discuss a
Joint District? Rippons - No problem. Meehl - Would be willing to work with the
Township on this. Bragga-What if we want to buy some property in the future? It
would be cumbersome to put everything on the ballot. Roach - We are trying to
address everyone's concerns with this amendment. It's feasible and we have the
money. Nemet - I like the idea of putting this on the ballot. Nizen - The
Village will be involved whether we like it or not, but we should place a
construction levy on the ballot. C. Baxley - You'll have title to the building.
What do you have to lose? M. Lehnert - One year ago it was $500,000 to build
the Community Center. Now it's $675,000. If we wait, the costs will go up
again. We have collected over $100,000 as of today; we have 500 signatures for
30 acres for a park. Fertig - Why don't you get 500 signatures for this
Community Center? M. Lehnert - Over 270 people have donated money. J. Laidley -
The $200,000 will open doors for the matching grants. This will be a village
asset, getting a $675,000 building for $200,000. Energy efficiency will be
incorporated into the building. With expanded programs we feel we can operate
it. It's an investment in the future. T. Fleming - We need an operating levy.
Why are you talking about a construction levy? Nizen - It's supposed to be
unfurnished; what about furnishings? The Township needs to discuss this. We
should table this. Roach - Read the amendment again. Roll: Settles, yea;
Bragga, yea; Roach, yea; Nemet, yea; Fertig, nay; Meehl, yea. I would like to
see the levy passed before the construction begins. Roach - We can make
additional changes on the third reading, if necessary. Bragga - It will not
change the commitment of the $200,000. Motion by Roach, seconded by Settles for
a second reading of Resolution #1918. Roll: Settles, yea; Bragga, yea; Roach,
yea; Nemet, yea; Fertig, nay; Meehl yea. Motion passed.

Recreation:
Roach - SOCC Board meeting last Thursday, K-Run had 110 participants, while the
Ashtabula Y only had 91. All classes are going well. Motion by Roach, seconded
by Settles, for the third reading, title only, of Ordinance 1918. Bragga - We
should specify a date for the operating levy. Roach - We don't see the
necessity of a November, 1991 vote, because it will confuse the issue. Meehl -
What would happen to the millage if the resolution becomes null and void?
Solicitor - We could repeal it. Settles - Operation of the building will be
about $30,000. Fertig - What about salaries? Bragga - Present salaries were not
addressed. B. McCune - Why can't the tax levy money be given to the Community
Center for these salaries if the resolution becomes void? Meehl - Suggested a
joint district with the Township for recreation. Settles - How about a levy at
a specific later date - when all the funds are in place? Nemet - There is a lag
time for taxes. We may have to wait for two years. B. Topper - There will be a
school levy on the ballot. We should check our priorities. M. Lehnert - We
should have an operating levy, but not until the building is there. J. Laidley
- Construction in the Spring; ballot in May. Fertig - We should ask the people
first. J. Laidley - We have over-whelming support of the people -- over
$100,000 in donations. Fertig - What about the school levy? Settles - Board of
Education has endorsed the proposal. Bragga - The school levies are both
renewals. K. Powers - All programs pay for themselves. Bragga - Increased
programs mean increased revenues. This should cause the Village share to
decrease in the future. Meehl suggested using only unappropriated funds-
$96,000 from 1991 and $104,000 in 1992 when the building will be built, rather
than $200,000 now. Motion by Roach, seconded by Settles, to amend Resolution
1918. Roll: Bragga, yea; Roach, yea; Nemet, yea; Fertig, nay; Meehl, yea;
Settles, yea. Motion passed.
Amendment to Resolution No. 1918
BELIEVING SOCC WILL BE SUCCESSFUL IN RAISING THE BALANCE OF THE CONSTRUCTION
COST, AS SET FORTH HEREIN ABOVE, THEN THE VILLAGE OF JEFFERSON, OHIO, SHALL
PLACE BEFORE THE VOTERS OF THE VILLAGE A SPECIAL TAX LEVY, IN NOVEMBER 1991, IN
A MILLAGE TO BE DETERMINED AT A FUTURE DATE, FOR THE PURPOSE OF SAME BEING TO
RAISE SUFFICIENT ANNUAL REVENUES TO OPERATE THE JEFFERSON COMMUNITY CENTER.

Reports of Committees:
Service:
Nizen - The solution to Heritage Hills is to draw up an agreement to plow the
roads and install street lighting this year; next year, replace the culvert;
then pave 1,200 feet of the street at a cost of $32,000. The program would be
for four years, each year the residents will pay half of the costs for the
culvert and the paving. Motion by Nemet, seconded by Meehl, to enter into an
agreement with Heritage Hills to incorporate plowing, street lights, and street
maintenance. Roll: Fertig, yea; Nemet, yea; Roach, yea; Bragga, yea; Settles,
yea; Meehl, yea. Nemet - Residents near Maple and Westview have been
complaining about low spots in the paving. Ferguson - We did what we were
instructed to do. Some of the asphalt we took out was 5 inches thick. We'll go
back and even these up. Nemet - Beverly and Hillyer--There are some problems
with a few of the people about money. Administrator was directed to send a
letter to those people by September 23rd so that efforts can be made to
complete the project this year. Roach - Will the proposed truck route be
suitable for traffic? D. Weir - It will be o.k. except for the culvert and the
catch basins. Regarding the culvert by the school - there is enough fall for 15
inches, but if we put another 15 inches in, we'll only have 18 inches going
out. Fertig - Can we swale that toward the culvert? D. Weir - You can do that
for part of the way. The schools have agreed to purchase the pipe along the
road. Nizen - We have a request to cut about 50 feet of curb out at the depot
for parking. D. Weir - There should be no problem removing the sidewalk and the
curbing.
