Motion by Settles, seconded by Bragga, to pay the current bills, excluding the
Koski bill in the amount of $1,188.27. Roll: Settles, yea; Bragga, yea; Roach,
yea; Nemet, yea; Fertig, yea; Meehl, yea.
Visitors:
Hoffman - We received a letter from the Township regarding maintenance on the
Town Hall. What has been done about this? Nizen - There is no decision yet. It
is on the agenda. John Puskar, of CEC Consultants, made a presentation on
cogeneration for the East Ohio Gas Company. This would generate a savings at
the WWT Plant of $29,362 the first year. The total cost would be $130,000 and
would pay for itself in 4 1/2 years. He said that this would include an annual
maintenance fee and a fund for overhauls. Caperpillar is the manufacturer.
Settles - We are interested in this type of cogeneration in the near future.
Bob Zufall, of East Ohio Gas Company, asked Council to send someone to visit
one of their plants in Pittsburgh during the week of December 9th and see this
system in operation. Settles - Let us know what date is best for you and we
will get someone there.
Wastewater:
Settles - We have a problem with the Antonella Apartments on Satin Street. D.
Weir - Several building are tied together to one sewer line. There are 12 units
in each building - two new buildings, and one existing building. Each apartment
building should have a separate sewer line. It will cost $1,800 for a
contractor to install separate lines. The Village will pay for the contractor,
and the owner will supply the materials. Settles - The Mayor told the owner he
could tie everything to one line, so a compromise was negotiated in order to
comply with our ordinance which requires a separate line to each building.
Motion by Settles, seconded by Meehl, to accept the Administrator's
recommendation that the Village hire a contractor to install the lines
according to Village Ordinances. Fertig - If a permit had been issued from the
Building Department, could this problem have been avoided? D. Weir - No. The
Health Department inspects after the fact. Roll: Bragga, yea; Roach, yea;
Nemet, yea; Fertig, yea; Meehl, yea; Settles, yea.
Utilities:
Fertig - What about the Satin Street lighting? D. Weir - The lights should be
staggered every other pole. One will be moved and one added in order to do
this. Beverly Drive needs one and Hillyer needs two additional lights. Service
Committee will study and make recommendations.
Recreation:
Information was passed out regarding the Rec. Board. There will be a Christmas
Parade on December 7th followed by an Open House with Santa. The play "Greater
Tuna" was a success. Motion by Roach for the Second Reading, Title Only, of
Ordinance No. 1927, seconded by Settles. Roll: Bragga, yea; Roach, yea; Nemet,

ORDINANCE NO. 1927
AN ORDINANCE ESTABLISHING THE POSITION OF TEMPORARY PART-TIME PROGRAM
SUPERVISOR FOR THE RECREATION DEPARTMENT: AND, DECLARING AN EMERGENCY
Since the last meeting we have determined that we do need a Program Director
right away. K. Powers - We would like to advertise for this position or hire
someone as soon as possible. The Recreation Department will pick up the cost of
the part-time temporary as soon as the full-time person is hired. Bragga -
Would like to see a historical progression of the Recreation Department. K.
Powers will put one together. The Rec. Dept. has applied for a state grant for
a Senior van. The state will advertise for bids, etc. It can get a better
price. The Village will need to provide 15% matching funds for the van. Motion
by Roach, seconded by Settles, to commit 15%, not to exceed $4,000, on the
application for the grant for a new senior van. Roll: Settles, yea; Meehl, yea;
Fertig, yea; Nemet, yea; Roach, yea; Bragga, yea. Bragga cautioned about the
budget and unplanned expenditures.
Forestry:
Bragga - Dan will be meeting with a representative of the Ohio Department of
Natural Resources on December 10th, to re-evaluate and re-apply for the tree
grant for next year.
Service:
No report.
Buildings/Land Use:
Fertig - Have we done anything on the greens at Market and Jefferson Street? D.
Weir - We need a survey to locate exact boundaries of the greens. Nizen - We
laid out plans for fence posts to be installed. K. Ward - A 1983 judgment is in
conflict with this plan. D. Weir - Council should consider having an actual
survey before we construct such a fence. Bragga - We haven't received any
complaints on this, nor can I recall recommending that a fence be built.
Settles - The Buildings/Land Use Committee did not recommend this. We should
check the court order and do a survey. K. Ward - In 1978 there were complaints
about property on North Market. Letter was sent again in 1990. The house is
still not finished. Nizen - We will remand to committee. Fertig - With regard
to the Township letter - we are not ready to make a recommendation. Bragga -
The Rec. Board meeting was pertinent to this in my estimation. I need to hear
the results of that meeting before I can make a decision. Committee will meet
and discuss. Meehl - Would encourage the Committee to have a recommendation by
the next meeting. D. Weir - Repairs need to be made to the boiler at the Town
Hall. I have two quotes and would like to have it repaired as soon as possible.
Nizen - Why not give the Township the money and let them decide to fix or
replace it? Motion by Settles, seconded by Bragga, to spend up to $300 to fix
the boiler at the Town Hall. Roll: Meehl, yea; Fertig, nay; Nemet, nay; Roach,
yea; Bragga, yea; Settles, yea. Motion passed. C. Rippons - The Township letter
was received 6 1/2 weeks ago. What is the timetable for these 6 1/2 weeks?
Nizen - We have been trying to get some information. This is tied to the
Recreation Board and the Township lease. G. Hoffman - What was Council's
attitude on the letter? Meehl - I think most of these things could have been
done without coming to Council. Bragga - I think that the whole concept of the
Town Hall can be resolved. I like the old Town Hall, and I like the idea of
working together with the Township on this.
Safety:
Meehl - A quote was discussed for the Caution light at Poplar and West
Jefferson. D. Weir to get another quote. Febel thinks a traffic light would be
a better choice than a Caution light. Will get prices. Motion by Meehl,
seconded by Nemet, for the First Reading, Title Only, of Ordinance No. 1928.

Wastewater
Settles - Smoke testing has shown problems in 30 areas. The program will begin
in January to contact residents and initiate repairs.
Utilities:
Fertig - We should hear from CEI about the street lighting by next month.
Recreation:
Roach - The Community Center has been approved for the new van.
Forestry:
Bragga - D. Weir and Hume Frayer met with Al Sievert, Ohio Dept. of Natural
Resources regarding the tree grant. We will re-apply in 1992. He gave us a lot
of good advice for a Master Tree Plan.
Service:
D. Weir reported on paving of East Ashtabula Street. In the past, the Village
has paved the intersection up to the right of way, plus 2% of the total
improvement for the balance of the road. D. Weir recommended that the Village
pay the bill and then charge Mr. Utterback and the Oakdale Cemetery $458.13
each for the asphalt. E. Utterback said that the paving was done after approval
from the Service Committee and Dan Weir. He said that Larry Bragga also
approved the aprons to the cemetery, the parking lot, and the street. Bragga
objected to this. R. Ferguson said that Mayor Nizen approved the project and
then told them to do it as soon as possible; to let something else go. Settles
- It was never mentioned in the budget. Utterback - It was a good deal for
everyone. Settles - If this was such a good deal, why was it not brought to
Council for approval? Why scramble around like this? Roach - Did we pay for 100
ft. On Beverly and Hillyer? Settles - No. Nemet - We provided for emergency-
type expenditures in the budget. Settles - The difference between this and
other emergency repairs is that this was a capital improvement, not an
emergency repair. Motion by Settles, seconded by Roach, to bill Ed Utterback
$458.13 and forgive the Cemetery Board its portion because it is jointly owned
by the Village. Roll: Bragga, yea; Roach, yea; Nemet, yea; Fertig, yea; Meehl,
yea; Settles, yea. Motion by Settles, seconded by Meehl, to pay Koski
Construction their bill in the amount of $1,88.27 for asphalt for East
Ashtabula Street. Roll: Settles, yea; Meehl, yea; Fertig, yea; Nemet, yea;
Roach, yea; Bragga, yea.
Buildings/Land Use:
D. Weir - Underground storage tank has been in the ground for 20 years. The
State Fire Marshall suggested removal before June because of new EPA
requirements. Our Fire Chief can issue a permit now for their removal, but in a
couple of months only the state can issue the permit. The Health Department can
check the soil. Nizen - The Village doesn't own the tank. D. Weir - Ainsley
says that they don't own it. Settles - What we need to do is take care of it
now, and we won't have to go through the EPA. Motion by Bragga, seconded by
Nemet, to table this matter to the next meeting. Roll: Settles, yea; Meehl,
yea; Fertig, yea; Nemet, yea; Roach, yea; Bragga, yea.
Officials:
New Business:
Bill McCune would like to move our first Council meeting in January back to the
Town Hall. D. Pontius agreed that, in his interpretation, the lease is still in
effect on a month to month basis, as long as we continue to pay the bills and
occupy the building. The consensus of Council was that the Council Chamber be
moved to the Town Hall.
Old Business:
Meehl - What about the Poplar caution and traffic lights? D. Weir - The caution
light would cost $4,483.00, the red light would be $9,000, and the flashing
yellow, $3,000. We are waiting for more information on this.
Motion by Nemet, seconded by Roach, to go into Executive Session to discuss
personnel. Roll: Settles, yea; Meehl, yea; Fertig, yea; Nemet, yea; Roach, yea;
Bragga, yea.

State of the Village - Mayor William McCune
January 1992
The Village of Jefferson is in fair condition with good people working in all
departments. My goals, with Council's approval, are several for 1992:
I believe the Administrator of the Village, Dan Weir, has the knowledge and
ability to run the every day operations of this village and he should do so.
The Mayor and Council are here to give him direction (not directions).
The Clerk's office has to be updated with a computer so that the Mayor and
Council can have better control over the finances and operation of the Village.
With a computer added to the village, we could do our own billing of sewers and
possibly village income tax which would save on these outgoing costs.
The Fire Department has some of the best equipment available, and excellent
support by the volunteers. I think the Village can be proud of them.
The Police Department has been directed by me to get the traffic in the Village
under control, with speed limits and traffic signal rules enforced.
The Recreation Department is part of the Village and some type of permanent
financing has to be made available.
The Sewer Department generates revenue for its operation. I believe this
revenue should be used to upgrade the plant with cost-saving improvements.
Also, the old sewer lines in various sections of the Village should be
upgraded.
The paving of the Village streets is an important item along with the sidewalk
program. The Street Department has some good equipment with the addition of a
new truck last year. The people working for the Street Department should be
used for the every day maintenance of Village property, not for paving and
excavating projects.
As far as our meetings are concerned, I would like to continue to hold them
here - there's more room to accomodate visitors and we're not in the way of the
Fire Department. I do expect Council to be prepared for the Council meetings
and to be here on time. With Council's help, cooperation, desire to serve, and
expertise, I believe we should have a productive 1992. Thank you.
Old Business:
Motion by Nemet, seconded by Roach, to rehire Nicholson & Pontius as Village
Solicitor for one year at the same contract as before except for a retainer of
$4,500. Roll: Bragga, yea; Roach, yea; Nemet, yea; Fertig, yea; Settles, yea;
Blevins, yea.
Adjourn.
Respectfully submitted,
Judith Selzer Clerk-Treasurer
Approved: Mayor

needed to bring the Charter up to date and then give the Village the streets.
Heritage Hills cannot maintain these roads on its own, and they may
consequently deteriorate, causing the area to be unattractive. If made public,
the rear property can also be developed. We thought an agreement was reached on
October 24th with the previous administration. Certainly there was a meeting of
the minds on this issue. I urge you to reconsider. Visitor - We pay our taxes
and get no services in return. McCune - It's a costly item to bring streets up
to code and then accept them. This is not the usual procedure. Fertig - Let's
have our engineer make a recommendation. Motion by Blevins to have our

to committee to study, and then give us some direction at the next meeting.

Recreation:
Bragga - We are waiting for the Board of Elections to give us the ballot
language for the 2.5 mil recreation levy.
Forestry:
Fertig - Went to see the trees that were cut down on the cemetery tree lawn.
The base of most of the trees looked pretty good. Why were these trees cut
down? Bragga - There was discussion at a meeting about the trees, but I can
find nothing in my notes about any decision to contact the Village about them.
H. Frayer - All of these trees would have leafed out this spring. One was
questionable, but all would have performed this year. J. Maloney - Mr. Frayer
and the Cemetery Board were instrumental in saving those trees in the past.
Fertig - I would like the Clerk-Treasurer to send a letter to the Cemetery
Board to inform them of the proper procedure when contemplating cutting down
any trees in the village. D. Weir - This was unauthorized. No one contracted
me. McCune - At the Cemetery Board meeting, only trees inside the cemetery were
discussed. Frayer - What does the word discussed entail? A vote of the Board?
Bragga - No, nothing was approved, just discussed. I am working toward a better
procedural system at the meetings. Nemet - We need to get those trees replaced
as soon as possible. Fertig - The trees we planted last year are doing pretty
well. We will start planting again in the middle of April.

March 10, 1992 - Special Meeting
Meeting was called to order by Mayor William A. McCune
Roll: Blevins, Fertig, Nemet, Dietrich, Bragga, Roach, Smolen, Rippons, Boczar
Meeting opened with a prayer led by Philip Dietrich.
Also present: E. Utterback, Michael Franklin, Richard Barlo, Steve Cusp, Ed
Flack, Tim Skidmore, Z. Copelan, Fred Hinkle, V. Hall, Stanley Nizen, Donald
Serwatka, A. Roe, Roy Stainfield, Reid March, Gabriel Demshar, Jr., Dana
Armstrong, Dorothy Armstrong, D. Mead, Jane Mead, Kathryn Hoffman, G. Hoffman,
J. Maloney, J. Lemieux, Fred Martin, Steve Febel, Phyllis Larsen, Wilma
Herndon, R. Ferguson, D. Pontius; Village Solicitor, N. David, Hume Frayer, D.
Dvorak, Charlene Wise, D. Weir, Administrator; R. Selzer, Star Beacon, Gazette,
WFUN.
McCune - There are several reasons for the Special Meeting of the Joint Board.
The first concern is the removal of the trees from Village property. Where is
the authorization? Smolen questioned the ownership of the tree lawn at the
cemetery. He informed those present that the Cemetery Board took out six trees
last year. Rippons - Who authorized cutting down the trees last week? Smolen -
The Cemetery Board at regular meetings. Rippons - When? Roach - The trees
weren't dead. Bragga - The trees referred to at the meetings were inside the
cemetery property. I did not know anything about these trees. I didn't
authorize this. Edward Utterback then read a prepared statement stating, in
essence, that the trees were cut down as part of the routine maintenance
procedure of the cemetery. McCune - The concern is not maintenance or tree
trimming. These trees were on Village property, and they were cut down. D. Weir
- Out of all the trees, only one was bad enough to be taken down. Smolen - If
those were Village trees, then the Village can pay for them. Why didn't Bragga
tell us this? McCune - Lax Minutes and procedures were the problem. Visitor -
What regulations are there? McCune - The Ohio Revised Code rules the Board.
Fertig - It's a known fact that the tree lawn is owned by the Village, but the
home-owner mows the grass. M. Franklin, Attorney for the Cemetery Board, stated
that the Joint Board has given the authority to the Cemetery Board to do as
they see fit. Rippons - What can we do? Franklin - Right now, you have working
trustees, who do some of the work at the cemetery. If you want more control,
then triple the budget and hire professional caretakers. Solicitor Pontius
recommended that a motion be passed to require that the Cemetery Board get
permission for any major maintenance on the tree lawn. Fertig - We bypassed
those trees when we ran a sewer line to the Geriatric Center. He referred to
Ordinance No. 1028. The damage is done. We can't bring the trees back. Now we
have to think about replacing them. I hope soon. Those trees were not taken
down for the state highway. Boczar - Everyone agrees now that these were your
trees, but they didn't know it at the time. Can we go on to something else?
McCune - The Cemetery Board was established and never given any direction by
the Joint Board. I will entertain a Motion concerning the drawing up of
regulations for the Cemetery Board. Smolen - Why don't we wait for the May
meeting to finish this discussion. That will give everyone a chance to think
and present their ideas. There were no objections to this suggestion.
Adjourn.
Respectfully submitted,
Judith A. Selzer Clerk-Treasurer
Approved: Mayor

* Adjourn to Joint Cemetery Board Meeting
Mayor McCune called the meeting to order. Smolen - We are adding a 30-foot
addition to the west side of the building. There will be a large door on the
south side, and another door on the north side. It should cost about $5,000. An
additional $5,000 will be spent to pave some roads. Utterback - There is
drainage work to be done as well. Rippons - Requested copies of financial
statements and Minutes of Cemetery Board meetings. Dvorak - We took in $64,000
in 1991, and expended $62,000. Smolen - We bought a tractor and mower. Dvorak -
The financial summary is done yearly. Bragga - We met with an arborist who
checked out the trees at the Cemetery and gave us some valuable information for
our Fall planting schedule. Utterback suggested planting small trees in the
field, and then replanting them in the cemetery after a few years. Smolen - We
need to elect a new Cemetery Board member. Mayor McCune nominated Phil
Dietrich. Ken Boczar seconded the nomination. Bragga informed the meeting that
he has enjoyed his tenure on the Cemetery Board. The Mayor said that he needs
Larry on other committees; i.e. Recreation, Finance, etc. Motion by Bragga,
seconded by Blevins, to close the nominations and call for a roll. Roll:
Bragga, yea; Rippons, yea; Nemet, yea; Fertig, yea; Boczar, yea; Smolen, yea;
Dietrich, yea; Blevins, yea. It was brought to the Board's attention that Phil
Dietrich will serve the term which commenced January 1, 1992, as Bragga's term
had expired on December 31, 1991. His term will expire on December 31, 1994.
Questions were raised as to the legality of the Board's actions since Bragga
continued to serve unaware that his term had expired. The matter was turned
over to the Solicitor. A Special Joint Cemetery Meeting has been set up for
June 1 to discuss this. McCune - Referred to a letter from M. Franklin. We are
not interested in retracting our letter regarding the cutting down of Village
trees. We want it kept in the file. Smolen - The crypt must be opened before
any repairs can be done. Rippons - Requested some information be prepared by
the Cemetery Board for the June meeting. Mayor - Specific information such as,
"Does the Board follow the Ohio Revised Code? What are the rules and
regulations regarding such matters as bids, payment of bills, and so forth?
What are the procedures? Who decides what to buy and when?" Utterback - We are
in the process of computerizing the Cemetery records. Motion by Bragga,
seconded by Blevins, to adjourn the Joint meeting. Roll: Dietrich, yea; McCune,
yea; Bragga, yea; Rippons, yea; Nemet, yea; Fertig, yea; Boczar, yea; Smolen,
yea; Blevins, yea.

**Zoning Hearing:
D. Weir gave a brief explanation of the Divine application. The Planning
Commission has recommended denial of his request. Larry Divine spoke about his
plans - two one story duplexes which he intends to occupy himself; otherwise,
inexpensive single family homes will be built. Questions were asked from the
visitors about size of the lot, noise, traffic, too many people, and drainage
problems. Some expressed concern over property values declining if Mr. Divine
should move out and sell the property. Blevins - We can't allow spot zoning for
this and then turn down the next applicant. L. Divine - Why now? The
neighborhood has apartments and multiple family units all over. Bragga - But we
can't go back and change what's already done. L. Divine - I wasn't notified of
the Planning Commission meeting. If I had been there, the decision may have
been different. Roach - Looked over the area and agrees with Mr. Divine. This
will be an asset to the neighborhood. Bragga - Agreed that Mr. Divine should
have been notified, and that the Planning Commission may want to look at this
again, but meanwhile Council shouldn't second guess the Planning Commission
without good cause. Motion by Bragga, seconded by Blevins, to support the
decision of the Planning Commission. Roll: Blevins, yea; Bragga, yea; Roach,
nay; Nemet, yea; Dietrich, yea.
D. Weir gave a brief description of Ron Fulwiler's application, which was also
turned down by the Planning Commission. He wants to use the former Agape chapel
for a mortgage company. Residents in the area are worried about leaving the
property vacant, vandalism, traffic near the school, and inadequate parking.
One resident suggested the property be purchased by Village and the building
torn down for greens. Motion by Bragga, seconded by Blevins, to uphold the
recommendation of the Planning Commission. Roll: Bragga, yea; Roach, yea;
Nemet, yea; Dietrich, yea; Blevins, yea.
**Adjourn to regular meeting.

***Joint Cemetery Board Meeting:
Roll Call: Bragga, Rippons, Nemet, Boczar, Smolen, Fertig, Dietrich, Blevins.
Also present: E. Utterback, D. Dvorak, M. Franklin. Motion by Blevins, seconded
by Bragga, to elect Mayor McCune to chair the meeting. Roll: Bragga, yea;
Rippons, yea; Nemet, yea; Boczar, yea; Smolen, yea; Fertig, yea; Dietrich, yea;
Blevins, yea. McCune - Larry Bragga served on the Cemetery Board for
approximately 18 months. Larry was appointed to the Board in 1990 by the
previous Mayor. A Joint Session was necessary to approve his nomination. This
never happened. The Joint Board needs to figure out a way to approve his tenure
and make it official. M. Franklin suggested a resolution of the Joint Board to
accomplish this. Motion by Blevins, seconded by Boczar, to approve Larry
Bragga's tenure on the Oakdale Cemetery Board from August 6, 1990, through
December 31, 1991. McCune - Do we need something in writing or are the Minutes
sufficient? Solicitor - The Minutes will be sufficient. M. Franklin agreed.
Roll: Blevins, yea; Dietrich, yea; Fertig, yea; Smolen, yea; Boczar, yea;
Nemet, yea; Rippons, yea; Bragga, yea. Smolen - The Joint Board needs to decide
what to do about the remains presently in the crypt. Blevins - Do we have names
or dates? D. Dvorak - Records show these are members of the Hawley family.
Blevins - Are any relatives alive? Smolen - No. Fertig - Is it worth fixing?
Dietrich - One casket is caved in, and the other is totally open. It shouldn't
cost too much to repair, $400 to $600 approximately. We can put up a plaque
with names on the outside. Hume Frayer - The vault area has some historical
significance. Motion by Rippons, seconded by Nemet, to begin restoration
proceedings by providing cost analysis and investigation into the families of
the deceased. Fertig - Should we remove the door or cover it over? Blevins -
Suggested restoration to original appearance. Dietrich - We don't need to open
the door at all. Bragga - Why is the Joint Board making this decision? M.
Franklin - The authority to disinter and re-inter lies with the Joint Board.
Bragga - Perhaps we should eliminate the Oakdale Cemetery Board if the Joint
Board needs to make these decisions. Haven't we had four or five meetings so
far this year? M. Franklin - We already have this Board, so why go into this
question? Bragga- Why, after the fact, is this Joint Board involved? Utterback
- We didn't know the remains were there at the time. Do you want us to spend
this money on a private burial place, or should we bury them somewhere else? H.
Frayer - Expressed reservations as to the competency of the Cemetery Board.
Rippons: We need a recommendation from the Cemetery Board. Roll: Bragga, yea;
Rippons, yea; Nemet, yea; Boczar, yea; Smolen, yea; Fertig, yea; Dietrich, yea;
Blevins, yea. M. Lehnert - In the 1870's the Hawley family were very prominent,
appearing often in the social pages of the newspapers. Smolen - Should we
continue to allow sledding in the cemetery? Bragga - If we eliminate sledding
there, maybe we should offer it on other village-owned land; but what would
this accomplish? The liability would still be there. Motion by Blevins to allow
sledding during daytime hours and make arrangements for another suitable place.
No second. Solicitor - If you allow it, you have to make it safe and
controlled. Bragga - Let's research this and come back with a recommendation.
Discussion followed regarding terms of Cemetery Board seats. No additional
action was taken. Motion by Nemet, seconded by Dietrich, to adjourn. Roll:
Blevins, yea; Dietrich, yea; Fertig, yea; Smolen, yea; Boczar, yea; Nemet, yea;
Rippons, yea;. Bragga, yea.

November 16, 1992
Meeting was called to order by Mayor William McCune.
Roll Call of Council: Roach, Fertig, Nemet, Blevins, Dietrich, Bragga
Also present: Anthony DiMarino, Mike Wehner, Larry Gollon, S. Nizen, Norm
David, John Meehl, Madge Lehnert, Wilma Herndon, William Salin, Larry Divine,
Dave Fine, Bill Cunningham, Kathy Cunningham, Darla Zawacki, Ed Flack, Stella
Stroke, Lowell Hines, Mary Jane Hines, Linda Harnist, R. A. Jones, Steve Febel,
Jeff Pizel, D. Weir, Administrator; D. Pontius, Solicitor, Star Beacon,
Gazette, WFUN
Zoning Hearing 7:30 p.m.
Larry Divine, Corner of Satin & Poplar Street:
Blevins gave a short description of the application for a zoning change from
Residential-Single Family to Residential-MultiFamily. Mr. DeMarino, speaking
against the change, wanted to know why Mr. Divine was allowed to re-apply for
it. He spoke of the dangers of traffic congestion, population density, and need
for additional parking spaces. He wanted to know where the blueprints are for
Divine's buildings. McCune - explained that spot zoning would be a change from
residential to commercial or industrial. He said that the reason Divine's
application had been turned down was because of spot zoning. That was not a
valid reason in this case. M. Wehner - Why the change of heart? McCune - The
plans were good otherwise. They fit the criteria for the area. D. Weir - The
precedent for Multi-Family has already been set in the area. Bragga - The
Planning Commission unanimously recommended the change to Multi-Family. Blevins
- We called Columbus to make sure of the correct definition. Motion by Roach,
seconded by Blevins, to approve the recommendation of the Planning Commission
in the application of Larry Divine to change the zoning from RS to RD. Bragga,
yea; Roach, yea; Nemet, nay; Fertig, yea; Dietrich, nay; Blevins, nay, Mayor
McCune, yea. Motion passed.
William Cunningham, 3-1/2 acres on Erie St. through to Cedar St.:
Blevins explained that the application was for a zoning change from
Residential-Single Family to Residential Multi-Family. Mr. Jones spoke against
the change, bringing up potential sewage problems, that it is a single family
area, and noise. Blevins - Sound barriers are being put up, and the traffic
problem has been addressed. Drainage problems were brought up. Nemet - What
about a playground for the children? Mr. Cunningham said he will address this
as the need arises. Motion by Blevins, seconded by Roach, to approve the
recommendation of the Planning commission in the application of William
Cunningham to rezone 3-1/2 acres from RS to RD. Roll: Bragga, yea; Roach, nay;
Nemet, nay; Fertig, nay; Dietrich, yea; Blevins, yea; Mayor McCune, yea. Motion
passed.
Return to Regular Session.
Minutes were approved as written.

Roll Call: Blevins, Dietrich, Fertig, Boczar, Smolen, Rippons, Nemet, Roach,

meeting has been called to address the problem of the mausoleum. We received a
letter from Michael Franklin. Smolen - We can't find anyone to do the work.
Dietrich - Related some interesting details of the Hawley family history.
McCune - The Council consensus is to fix the crypt. Dietrich - We can find a
bricklayer and cave in the top, bring in more dirt to contour, brick it in,
leave the sandstone as it is, block up the door, put up a wood front and
install a plaque to explain some pertinent history. I think this whole job can
be done for $1,000. This will maintain the historical value of the crypt. H.
Frayer - Was pleased with a positive approach to the problem. This does have
historical significance. Motion by Rippons, seconded by Bragga, to have Phil
Dietrich get a proposal with figures together to look at. Utterback - Who will
clean the bricks? What about the foundation? McCune - Will send out a
bricklayer who will be able to handle this. Fertig - Why not use new brick?
Let's get it repaired and get it over with. This could cost a lot in liability
if we wait around. Roll: Blevins, yea; Dietrich, yea; Fertig, yea; Boczar, yea;
Smolen, yea; Rippons, yea; Nemet, yea; Roach, yea; Bragga, yea. Motion by
Blevins, seconded by Roach, to proceed with this plan if it is under $1,000.
Roll: Bragga, yea; Roach, yea; Nemet, nay; Rippons, yea; Smolen, nay; Boczar,

Mayor's Report:
1992 is over. I'd like to review the many projects that we've accomplished.
One of the major accomplishments of 1992 was the purchase of the Town Hall. I
believe this historic building should be preserved and play a role in our
community.
Another accomplishment was the computerization of the Clerk's office. We can
now access records and get current balances. We are also establishing a
purchase order system to better control the spending of the departments. There
are several things we are able to do with this computer that will help
streamline the village operations. The clerk's staff is working hard to enter
all the information on the village into this computer.
Accomplishments in the Street Department include the purchase of a new backhoe
through the state bidding process, which saved the village thousands of
dollars. We shall look to this process for future purchases to save taxpayer
money. Issue 2 money enabled improvements to East Jefferson Street, including
new curbs. Other Street Department projects included the paving of North Market
Street, the topping of East Erie Street, the replacement of a culvert on East
Erie Street, an extension of the sidewalk program, and several smaller projects
too numerous to mention. In all, I'm very proud of the Street Department's
accomplishments and their versatility.
In 1992, the Police Department solved several crimes in the village. They
should be commended for their good police work. In the department we upgraded
their fleet of cars and purchased a computer system for them. We have also
created a lieutenant's position to help the smooth operation of the department.
New scheduling of shifts puts two patrolmen at a time on the street during the
busiest times to better serve the people. I'm very proud of the cooperation and
teamwork shown by the members of the Village Police Department this past year.
The double failure of the Community Center levy was a major disappointment in
1992 and has forced Council to reconsider the construction of a Community
Center. The continued hard work of the Recreation Board and the SOCC Board will
be needed to move this department forward.
An engineer has now been hired to help us comply with all EPA regulations in
the Wastewater Department. A few small pieces of equipment have been purchased
for this endeavor.
The Fire Department stressed maintenance of their equipment for 1992, with very
few purchases needed. We thank them for the volunteer work done and for their
dedication to the safety of this community.
In general, the implementation of tax abatement created a few jobs in the
village when Plasticolors moved a small division to Sycamore Street. Hopefully,
the continuation of the tax abatement program will bring additional jobs.
With the hiring of Aerocon, we have started a topol and overlay of the entire
village to better serve our own departments and any possible developers.
One project which we are still working hard on is the extension of Cucumber
Street to relieve the truck traffic in the center of our village. The high cost
of this project has instituted an extensive search for state and federal
grants. The continuation of this project is very important to the village not
only for safety reasons but for the saving of our streets from the excessive
wear and tear of these trucks.
All of these projects for 1992 have been done with the expertise and under the
watchful eye of Dan Weir. His research in cost saving ideas has saved the
village much money.
There are several projects for 1993.
With the upgrading and improvements needed at the sewer plant, this could be a
costly year.
The fire station is in need of storage and office space and has proposed an
addition. I hope we can find the money in the budget to comply.
The continued influx of storm water into our sewers will have to be looked at.
Relocation, cleaning, and resetting of culvert pipes and catch basins is an
important factor in this problem.
The drainage and paving projects for 1993 are Erie Street from Market to
Franley and all streets in Jeffersonian Estates. Additional paving projects are
possible if the budget permits.
The sidewalk program will continue in 1993 along with the start of curbing on
West Jefferson Street.
A new roof on the Town Hall is desperately needed in this year's upgrading and
maintenance of this facility (which has been sorely neglected for so long).
Several pieces of equipment will be upgraded or purchased for the various
village departments on an as-needed basis.
Let's all work together to improve the Village of Jefferson in 1993.

Recreation:
Roach - We did get a reduction in the Boys & Girls Club annual fee. McCune -
Suggested Council go with a bond issue and build the new Community Center. It
should cost about $50,000/ year at 5% for 15 years for a $500,000 building. No
additional cost to the residents. We can use our present income tax to pay for
it. With a larger facility, we can generate an additional $28,000 to $40,000 a
year. This will help to defray the expenses of the new building, and possibly
some salary expense. We have come up with a new design. He described the layout
and announced that grants are possible from the Boys & Girls Club, and that
grants for Seniors are also possible. This building will be more cost effective
than the other one. The S.O.C.C. Board will stay in existence. They will
continue to raise money as the building goes up. With more space we can do
more. This will keep our kids here and out of trouble. Bragga - Agrees finances
are no problem based on his experience serving on the Finance Committee. The
Community Awareness Group has indicated that we could use more facilities and
more programs. This certainly would be a step in the right direction. Nemet -
Would like to see the facts and figures before a decision is made. Dietrich -
Our new Director is educated. If we don't provide him with the facilities to
grow and do a good job, we may lose him in a year or so. Jefferson is growing
and we should move forward. McCune - Now is the time, while interest rates are
low. The Solicitor will continue to investigate the various types of bond
issues available to the village.

Roll: Bragga, yea; Blevins, yea; Dietrich, yea; Rippons, yea; Smolen, yea,
Boczar, yea, Nemet, yea; Roach, yea. McCune - The first order of business is
the budget for the cemetery. D. Dvorak answered questions about the budget
reports. Bragga - Questioned the $60.00/hour charges for an attorney. McCune -
Why was the attorney hired? E. Utterback - The Cemetery Board has no legal
help. McCune - If the attorney is being used for bringing suits against the
Joint Board, then I am against having one. Bragga - Agreed. Rippons - I'd like
to know what cases the attorney has been used for and what answers he has come
up with. Smolen - It often takes too long for answers when we go to the
Prosecutor's office for advice. McCune suggested the Cemetery Board use the
Village Solicitor for ordinary legal questions. If a matter looks complicated,
a joint meeting will be called to determine who will pay or it. Motion by
Rippons, seconded by Bragga, to direct the Cemetery Board to use in-house
resources for legal services (the Solicitor and the Prosecutor) effective
immediately. Roll: Blevins, yea; Dietrich, yea; Rippons, yea; Smolen, yea;
Boczar, yea; Nemet, yea; Roach, yea; Bragga, yea. Boczar - Questioned the
$15,000 paving item on the budget. Bragga - It also opposed to paving at the
cemetery. We should plant more trees instead. Smolen - Thinks snow removal will
be easier if the roads are paved. E. Utterback - Maintenance will be less
expensive, too. Gravel costs about $1,200 per year. Dietrich - There will be
more maintenance with blacktop. There is upheaval and cracking unless you put
in drain tile, etc. The roads look beautiful the way they are. The Chardon
cemetery has ruts down both sides caused by cars going around parked cars and
two-way traffic. Skateboarding will be another problem if roads are paved.
Hinkle - Most people who come in have had no objections to the paving. E.
Utterback - As for more trees, we have plenty of trees available for
transplant. We don't have to spend a lot of money on this, but every tree in
the old section must be planted on a grave. Motion by Bragga, seconded by
Roach, to approve the budget with the exception of paving. This amount is to be
put into the projected balance. Dietrich - What about the bid opening? The
Board voted to accept the paving bid of $11,782.00 per attorney approval, if
within percentage. Motion by Blevins, seconded by Roach, to table this motion
to allow the Solicitor to check into this. Roll: Bragga, yea; Roach, yea;
Nemet, yea; Boczar, yea; Smolen, yea; Rippons, yea; Dietrich, yea; Blevins,
yea. A special Joint Meeting was set for May 17th at 8:00 p.m. to continue
discussion of the budget. Motion by Dietrich, seconded by Bragga, to have the
cemetery clerk contact Michael Franklin to hold up on the contract. Roll:
Blevins, yea; Dietrich, yea; Rippons, yea; Smolen, yea; Boczar, yea; Nemet,
yea; Roach, yea; Bragga, yea. The Minutes of the Joint Meeting regarding the

Visitors Comments:
Mr. Durward Newhard, VFW Post #3334, presented a Loyalty Day Award to Mayor
McCune. On Loyalty Day, May 3rd, a flag was presented to the school. On May 2,
1994, the VFW plans to hold another Loyalty Day. Bragga - The Service Band has
been requested for next year.
Mr. Richard Simpson, of Bricker & Eckler, Bond Counsel, gave a short
description of the process involved in selling municipal bonds for capital
improvement. General Obligation bonds are supported by the property tax. One
may not intend to use the tax to pay them, but they must be provided for,
nonetheless. Revenue bonds are supported by certain revenues such as water or
sewer fees. Usually Recreational facilities are done with General Obligation
bonds, either 1) Negotiated bonds, or 2) Publicly sold to the lowest bidder.
Bond Counsel: Drafts all ordinances or resolutions necessary for the issue, and
prints the bonds. The counsel is also liable for correct procedure. Our costs
would be about $4,000. He then explained the process of public sale of short-
term notes, ordinarily sold to cover the construction period. After all costs
are in and the building is paid for, then long-term bonds are issued.

accusing Phil Dietrich and Dan Weir of not abiding by the statutes. He also

a conflict of interest in running a summer camp at Buccaneer Campground.
Dietrich responded that he has not decided yet whether to give up his home here
in Jefferson. He has lived here all his life and still does. Blevins defended
herself by responding that the summer camp she runs is not in the Village and
is mostly for latch-key children. She stated that her opposition to building a
new Community Center is based on her belief that the Village cannot afford it
at this time. Dan Weir said that it is true that he is not yet a resident of
the Village, but that he is a Village taxpayer and has been looking for
affordable housing here since taking the position of Village Administrator.

Service:
Hugh Thomas distributed some information regarding House Bill 592 (Ashtabula
County Solid Waste Management Plan). Grants are available at 25% of total
expense to local districts for mobile and stationery recycling drop-off
centers, curbside recycling, and/or back yard composting. This will eventually
be done on a county-wide basis. Larry Meaney said that there are to be two
public hearings to gather public input on the Plan. He reviewed dates and
deadlines required by the EPA, if we are to be separated from TAG. The Village
will have to set up its own recycling stations, etc. Eventually, if we can't
keep up, the district will help. Sample Ordinances will be provided for Council
approval by September 28, 1993.

September 7, 1993
Meeting was called to order by Mayor William McCune.
Roll Call of Council: Fertig, Roach, Bragga, Nemet, Blevins, Dietrich
Also present: Dan Weir, Administrator; Jerome Lemire, Solicitor; Sharon Graper,
David Graper, Cayce Baxley, Richard Buchanan, Gene Crislip, Michael Carins,
Molly Gogrd, Sue Materles, Betty Evans, Mildred Bixil, Joe Adams, Antoni
Trzaska, Theresa Trzaska, Bill Stone, Mark Mansfield, Ed Flack, Steve Febel,
Gazette, Beverly Cowles, C. Rippons Star Beacon, WFUN
***Public Hearing:
1.   Hudson Hanover - An application to rezone a parcel of land adjacent to the
west side of the existing Jefferson Courtyard Apartments on East Jefferson
Street from RS (Residential single-family) to RD (Residential multi-family).
The Planning Commission recommended that the request be denied due to
inadequate square footage of lot area to establish a 32-unit senior housing
complex. R. Buchanan - Said he has sent a letter to the Village indicating that
he will comply with the current zoning regulations with regard to density, set-
backs, and parking. This is a change from his original position. John Nemeth -
Thinks his property will be devalued if more apartments are placed there.
Several Seniors who live there said they are very pleased with the apartments,
the maintenance, and the laundry and recreational facilities. C. Baxley - Said
that these apartments are nicely kept and she enjoys having the seniors there,
but plans should be made for landscaping if more units are to be built. Gene
Crislip - Owns this and the next property over - They have a waiting list for
the Senior housing. These properties are kept in first class condition. Nemet -
How many will this property hold? D. Weir - 24 units. Fertig - Seven years ago,
when this project was going on, we went along with it because it was for
Seniors only. They are well built and comfortable. These apartments won't lower
the value of anyone's property. Hudson Properties has a site at Middlefield,
too. These are top-notch quality. Roach - We all agree we need more Senior
housing, but right now we need to deal with two issues - The zoning regulations
and whether or not to rezone. Bragga - Said the Planning Commission has
rejected the application. If Hudson Properties wants to change the number of
units, they need to go back to the Planning Commission. McCune - Suggested an
ordinance be prepared for the next meeting. The Planning Commission can then
meet and re-evaluate this with the changes. B. Cowles - Which issue are we
looking at? Solicitor - Explained that Council needs to decide whether to
approve or disapprove the Planning Commission's recommendation. In order to
change zoning, it requires five votes of Council to go against the Planning
Commission's recommendation. Motion by Bragga, seconded by Roach, to approve
the recommendation of the Planning Commission. Roll: Bragga, yea; Roach, yea;
Nemet, yea; Fertig, yea; Dietrich, yea; Blevins, yea.
2.   Trzaska Apartments: An application to rezone a parcel of land located on
the southwest corner adjacent to the intersection of Washington Blvd. and
Linden Street from RS (Residential single family) to RD (Residential multi-
family). The Planning Commission recommended the request be denied due to
inadequate square footage of lot area to establish a 12-unit apartment complex.
Mrs. Trzaska - This parcel was zoned multi-family in the past - then it was
changed to single family. We just want to change it back. We are willing to
change our original application from 12 units to 10 in order to meet the zoning
requirements. B. Stone - Asked that the property not be rezoned because of the
problems in the neighborhood the additional multi-level units will cause. Mrs.
Trzaska - Said she will go back to the Planning Commission with revised plans.
Motion by Dietrich, seconded by Roach, to approve the recommendation of the
Planning Commission. Roll: Blevins, yea; Dietrich, yea; Fertig, yea; Nemet,
yea; Roach, yea;, Bragga, yea.

Visitors Comments:
In reference to the fatal accident at the West Jefferson and Poplar
intersection: Donald Serwatka - Lost a son in a 1985 traffic accident.
Suggested the speed limit on Poplar from 307 to W. Jefferson should be reduced
from 35 to 25 m.p.h. This intersection is dangerous. There are many close calls
there. Evan Howe read a resolution requesting installation of a traffic light
at the intersection of Poplar and West Jefferson streets, and the use of police
to ensure traffic rules are followed. Robert Wisedale - Has done autopsies of
children killed in traffic accidents. He urged Council to do anything possible
to prevent future tragedies. Kathy Selzer - There are squealing tires there all
day and night. Something needs to be done. Mandy Hanyok - Aren't the lives of
the people we love worth the price of a traffic light? Cayce Baxley - Asked why
the light wasn't installed last year. McCune - The traffic patterns and
accidents there did not warrant a traffic light. There were other intersections
that were ruch worse. We also felt that a light would add to the congestion
there. It was never a question of money. Other Visitor's Comments: Barry Harper
- The construction on East Jefferson Street has left mud holes. D. Weir - This
will be fixed before the contractors leave. Barry Harper - What about the
senior housing? McCune - We are waiting to hear from Hudson-Hanover Properties.
Safety:
Roach - The Safety Committee met today regarding the recent accidents at Poplar
and W. Jefferson streets and what to do to prevent more. We are going to have a
traffic study done immediately and we'll do everything we can to prevent this
happening again, but the fact remains that the drivers need to pay attention to
the road. There are double "Stop" signs there already. This is not a high
accident intersection. Bragga - Doesn't want to wait for a traffic study. Has
felt the need for a traffic light there for some time. We should also lower
speed limits, and more "Stop" signs should be installed immediately. Fertig -
Several years ago we put a flashing light at the bottom of the hill at a cost
of almost $5,000. We still have accidents, but the flashing lights do help the
situation, especially at night. Motion by Bragga, seconded by Fertig, to:
1)   Install a traffic light at the intersection of W. Jefferson and Poplar
streets.
2)   Reduce the speed limit on Poplar Street to 25 m.p.h.
3)   Reduce the speed limit on Jefferson Street to 25 m.p.h.
4)   Install a "Walk" button to cross Poplar on the south side of Jefferson,
and to cross Jefferson at the east side of Poplar street.
5)   To have a 3-way stop at the intersection of Poplar and Walnut Streets.
6)   Install a "No Right Turn on Red" during school hours at the intersection
of Poplar and W. Jefferson.
7)   Place a "School Zone - 20 m.p.h." from the high school to Jefferson
Street.
Bragga - This will cost about $25,000 to $30,000. Each of these items must go
along with the uniform traffic codes. Roll: Bragga, yea; Roach, yea; Nemet,
yea; Fertig, yea; Dietrich, yea, Blevins, yea. McCune - We'll do as much as we
can now. The rest will be done as soon as possible. R. Ferguson - Cautioned
that too many signs may cause a visibility problem. Blevins - Parents should
obey the speed limits and signs in order to set a good example for their kids.

Wastewater:
Dietrich - J. P. Bergren visited our wastewater plant to demonstrate a polymer
feed system at a cost of around $20,000. It causes the sludge to thicken up.
Eight EPA people and the County Board of Sanitation were there to see the
demonstration. Last week we visited Madison to see a sludge press demonstration
at a cost of about $105,000. We are looking for a sludge management process
that is the most reasonable and efficient one for us. Herb Housel will be
putting in a new tank in the holding area. Dietrich - The Wastewater Committee,
the Mayor and the Administrator have come forth with a recommendation for the
re-organization of the wastewater treatment plant. Some positions will be
eliminated, others will be renamed. The Village Administrator will head up the
Department, and he will name a supervisor in his absence. The next two-three
years will be crucial to the operation of the plant. Motion by Dietrich,
seconded by Blevins, for the First Reading, Title Only, of Ordinance No. 2019.
Discussion followed regarding supervisor compensation. Roll: Blevins, yea;
Bragga, yea; Roach, yea; Nemet, yea; Fertig, yea; Dietrich, yea.

Mayor's State of the Village Address - 1993
Last year was very busy with various projects started or completed in all
village departments.
One project done in 1993 was the installation of a new roof on the Town Hall.
With this continued upgrading, we are trying to follow a plan to make our Town
Hall a nice building that everybody can be proud of.
The storm water drainage system in the village is in very poor shape. We
installed new pipe on West Erie Street and East Jefferson Street. The Street
Department did the work on West Erie Street and a fine job they did. The East
Jefferson Street Project was contracted out and paid for with Issue Two money.
The paving will be completed in the spring. We have a lot more work to be done
with the drainage systems in the housing allotment off West Beech Street, on
West Walnut Street, in Elliot Allotment, and at various other places in the
village.
The paving projects done in the village for 1993 were Erie Street, both east
and west, East Satin Street, and the parking lots at the Fire Hall and Town
Hall. Several more streets will be done in 1994.
We are still trying to complete work on the sewer plant, so we can be in
compliance with the EPA permit. This is a very costly project and will take
some hard work by the sewer committee and sewer department.
The Police Department was very busy upholding traffic laws in the village and
trying to make our village a safer place to live. The addition of some new
equipment helped them do a very good job. Continued upgrading of that
department will ensure a safe town with a professional staff.
The Fire Department again operated very efficiently and effectively. The men of
this department volunteered even more of their time for additional state-
required training so as to be ready for any type of emergency. I would like to
thank them for all the time that they donate to the citizens of this village.
Village Administrator Dan Weir has again provided this village with very able
leadership. He has spent a large part of the past year handling residents,
village workers, contractors, and EPA officials. With his administrative skills
and engineering expertise, he directs this village on a sound professional and
economic course.
Robin Walker and Gail Keefer, the village office staff, do an excellent job at
the village office. They keep our office running smoothly and keep Council and
me aware of our daily obligations.
Judy Selzer makes sure that tax money is invested profitably and that village
finances are handled correctly.
I want to thank the 1993 Council for their support and for their dedication to
the Village of Jefferson. I also would like to welcome the new Council members
to the 1994 Council.
New Business:
None.
Adjourn.
Respectfully submitted,
Robin Walker Deputy Clerk
Approved, William A. McCune, Mayor

Public Hearing: Comprehensive Plan
Blevins explained that Council decided to have a Comprehensive Plan
professionally done in order to provide for orderly growth. The Planning
Commission has worked with the Consultant, Roger Reese and they have approved
the Plan in its present form. Now the Council will decide whether to adopt it
as it is or to make changes before final approval. After the Plan is adopted,
the amendments to the Zoning Codes and Subdivision Regulations will each have
separate public hearings. Bragga opened the meeting to comments from the
public. Terry Finger, W. Jefferson St. - Why does the plan call for new multi-
family mixed in with residential? Blevins - Multi-family is residential.
Traffic patterns need to be considered for multi-family areas, so they are to
be placed on collector streets. Mr. Finger - The Gazette has stated that the
commercial district on West Jefferson St. runs from Poplar St. to the railroad
tracks. Bragga - This is incorrect. It stops at the Gazette on the South side
and at Fleming Funeral Home on the North side of the street. Durward Newhard,
S. Elm St. - Concerned about W. Mulberry St. The school agreed to put up a
barrier. This is not a through street. If paving is to be done to bring this up
to a Class A street, who is going to pay for it? Why would W. Mulberry be a
collector Street? Blevins - This is a future plan. Bragga - It will be assessed
to owners. Roger Reese - We will need a wider street if new homes are to be
built in that area. Mr. Newhard - Will this be extended to Cedar St? Why should
we pay to benefit one or two people? Reese - We can't allow the area to be
developed if we don't make plans for traffic flow. When the Council decides
whether to allow development there, the developer may be asked to share in the
cost of the roads. Jackie Lemire, 333 S. Elm St. - You can bypass Woodside and
Elliot via Mulberry. This may bring in truck traffic to the residential area.
To the South is the Township. Will we be assessed for the Township side of the
street? Bragga - This is an area where your village government may have to
contribute to the cost of a collector street. Ms. Lemire - Elliot is a dirt
road. If this street were paved, it would help alleviate the traffic problem
there. The plan calls for multi-family on my property. This was never discussed
with me. Roger Reese - The individual property owners are not considered in
terms of zoning. This does not prohibit you from using your property for single
family. This will allow you to use it for multi-family, too. The Plan calls for
20 acres for multi-family, in 4-acre lots dispersed throughout the village.
George Hoffman, W. Mulberry St. - School buses were routed down W. Mulberry to
alleviate traffic congestion. The Village was approached about paving W.
Mulberry, but they said it needs to have all new sewer lines and upgrades to
handle the school buses, so the cost was prohibitive. If this will now be a
collector street, why should the residents pay for this? Bragga - If the Plan
requires this, I think government should help pay for it. Jim Donathan, 337
Susan Dr. - Multi-family is not wanted there. Will the sewer lines be extended
on W. Jefferson? Bragga - This hasn't been discussed. Mr. Jana, Susan Dr. -
Will these be condos or one story high buildings? Bragga - They will have to
conform to our building codes for multi-family. The meeting was interrupted to
announce that there are more people waiting in the hall. Bragga - We appreciate
the interest in the Comprehensive Plan. It looks as though we will need to hold
another hearing 30 days after publication of the notice of the meeting. Jim
McIntire - We need the maps at the library. Sheila Hedding, 957 Doyle Rd. - Can
we write to you to convey our opinions on this? Bragga - I prefer to hear what
you have to say, but you are welcome to write to us, care of the Village
office.
Adjourn.
Public Hearing: Trzaska Apartments
Blevins said the Planning Commission has approved the application for a zoning
change from single-family to multi-family for a ten unit apartment building on
Washington St. This is located on a collector street, and it meets all of the
zoning codes for multi-family units. Bragga opened the meeting to comments from
the public. Jackie Roach, 210 Linden St. - As spokesman for the 100 people who
signed petitions in the Jeffersonian Estates, she requested denial of
application because 1) lack of a play area, 2) increased traffic flow on narrow
streets, and 3) Additional construction will cause more drainage problems
there. We now have the apartments, the allotment and behind us is the trailer
park. Jerry Finger, W. Jefferson St. - Asked how this complex fits in with the
Comprehensive Plan. Bragga - This was allowed for as the Plan was developed.
Peggy Gassis - The owners could build a couple of houses with six kids in them.
There are going to be kids in that neighborhood. Charla Deems, N. Linden -
Washington Street is the only way out of the allotment. Adding more cars to the
street will cause more congestion. Patrick Burns, 424 Washington St. - We
welcome single family. You can only put so many apartments in this area. Bob
Jones, 238 Linden St. The trailer park also causes traffic congestion in the
area. Terry Evans, Linden St. - 20 years ago, this was a nice, quiet
neighborhood. We were promised two playgrounds. Now, the neighbors are too
close on all sides. There is too much light coming from the apartments. George
Hoffman, W. Mulberry St. - Doesn't think the property taxes will make up for
the costs of schools and village services which will be increased. Patrick
Keen?, 418 Washington Blvd. - Paved roads are buckling there because of the
water problem. R. Anderson, 234 Jackson - Lights from the apartments do light
up the whole area. Heat ducts fill up with water. Jim Lemieux, attorney for
Trzaskas, 531 E. Beech office - This project conforms to the overall scheme.
There is a need for more housing in Jefferson. These will be Townhouses similar
to the ones on Erie and Market. The Trzaskas will live in one of them. Vern
Murdock, 414 Washington Blvd. - Garage floods all the time. Where is the water
going to go? This water is supposed to go to Rt. 46. Cayce Baxley - These were
zoned single-family originally. Lemieux - This was multi-family and is now
single-family. The Trzaskas just want it chaged back to what it was before. Jim
Cufr, 96 Linda Lane - We don't need anymore multi-family. David Deems, 267
Linden - Presented a petition with original signatures against the zoning
change. Gabe Demshar, 949 Eagleville - We fought this 20 years ago when I was
on Council. These people were cheated 20 years ago, they should not be cheated
again. Motion by Blevins, seconded by Cowles, to approve the recommendation of
the Planning Commission.
Discussion followed. Cowles wants a compromise. Drainage will be worked on this
summer. Bragga - We have a request for a zoning change. We must act on it.
Dietrich - Promises were broken in the past, things were changed. Linden Street
and out to Rt. 46 is terrible. We need to be careful with these areas. Mary
Stasny - Lives in an apartment. Jefferson needs to have more apartments. Mrs.
Trzaska - We have improved our properties. Why should we be punished because of
the developer? Piper - Against new apartments until the drainage problem is
addressed. Roll: Blevins, yea; Dietrich, nay, Cowles, yea; Piper, nay; Stasny,
yea; Bragga, nay. Motion failed.
Adjourn.
Return to Regular Session.

Recreation:
Piper - Sent a letter on February 9th asking Ken Kaminsky to join the United
Way Council of Agency Executives. An Easter painting project for adults is
scheduled for March 7 at $6.00 per person.
Building/Land Use:
Cowles - Received new plans from Hudson Properties for the additional Senior
housing units. Will send to the Planning Commission meeting which has been set
for February 28th. Roger Reese, Planning Consultant, will introduce some
changes to the zoning codes at that time. Cowles - The Planning Commission
should be doing more. She requested a job description for members. Motion by
Cowles, seconded by Blevins to draft a memorandum to the Planning Commission to
explain their duties. Bragga - Disagreed with this contention. The Commission
Members have served diligently and expended much energy and effort over the
years. They do know what their responsibilities are. Cowles - Nothing has ever
been established in writing or by ordinance to tell them what they are charged
with doing. We need to set down rules and regulations for a planning
commission. Bragga - Suggested a committee be formed to include members of the
Commission to study this issue. Motion and second withdrawn. Motion by Cowles,
seconded by Blevins, to have the Solicitor draft an ordinance for the Hudson-
Hanover zoning amendment. Bragga - Said that the zoning codes may need to be
upgraded with respect to multi-family and single-family requirements. Dietrich
- Agreed. If the square footage requirements are upgraded, we will create a
better atmosphere, larger apartments and less chance of too many units in one
area. Solicitor - Drafting the ordinance will not show approval or disapproval.
It is a requirement of the statute that an ordinance be sent to the Planning
Commission for their review. Cowles - Suggested that this project be put on
hold, notify everyone that no decisions will be made until the Comprehensive
Plan is completed. McCune - This project has been in front of us for nearly two
years. It was first presented before the new upgraded square footage
requirements for Senior housing went into effect. Since then Mr. Buchanan has
had some health problems. This is the third time this request has been back
here. We should follow the procedures and give this gentleman an answer, one
way or the other. Roll: Bragga, yea; Stasny, yea; Piper, yea; Cowles, yea;
Dietrich, yea; Blevins, yea. McCune - Explained that the Comprehensive Plan is
not set in stone, it is a living document to be added to or subtracted from as
our needs change. It is not legislation. It doesn't change zoning. Its just a
Plan. Discussion followed regarding newspaper coverage. McCune - Change does
not come overnight. Mr. Reese is a professional planner. Bragga - We will need
public hearings and ordinances must be passed before any zoning changes can be
implemented. Solicitor - Recommended the Plan not be adopted unless zoning
ordinances are to be adopted to implement it.

conflict of interest.

March 22, 1994 - Public Hearing
Meeting was called to order by Mayor William McCune.
Roll Call of Council: Blevins, Bragga, Cowles, Dietrich, Piper, Stasny
Also present: Jerome Lemire, Solicitor; Daniel Weir, Administrator; Roger
Reese, Planning Consultant; Star Beacon; Gazette; WFUN
Public Hearing:
Purpose: To review the updated Comprehensive Land Use Plan
Jackie Lemire - Commended Council for trying to protect and preserve the small
town atmosphere of the Village by adopting a Comprehensive Plan. She urged
Council to change and omit parts of the Plan before adopting it. Specifically,
the re-zoning of land without consulting the property owners is unfair and
presumptious. Multi-family housing which has been scattered thoughout the
Village on the proposed Plan will destroy peaceful residential areas. A public
playground has been placed in another quiet residential neighborhood with no
provision for security. Changing West Mulberry St. to a Collector Street will
cause a by-pass of our commercial area.
Jim McIntyre - The Plan designates Industrial zoning on Cucumber. This would be
a mistake. This area should be scenic residential. We should include the
Township in our plans. Reject this plan. Growth is not everything.
Marguerite Schossler - Someone at the Village office said that everyone in the
Village was sent a letter explaining the Comprehensive Plan. This proved to be
not true. McCune - No letters were sent out. Selzer - Will look into this.
John Meehl - Suggested looking to the Township for possible dialogue as to the
sites for future Multi-Family housing. McCune - We have been looking at the
number of multi-family units here in the Village. There is the question of how
many are really needed for a village of this size. Council will look long and
hard at this.
R.A. Jones. Asked about the County property which is designated as
recreational. Reese - This property is actually zoned Industrial, but used as
recreational. No changes are proposed for this area.
Terry Finger - Wants us to stick to our present zoning codes. Any changes
should be taken to the voters. Also, the codes should be adhered to. He
referred to the duplex on North Poplar which was allowed in a neighborhood
zoned for single-family. He said that if the Village adopts a Comprehensive
Plan and it's going to vary the zoning, then the Village residents should vote
on that zoning.
Jim Donathan - There has been a 31% increase in multi-family units in Jefferson
in the last 10 years. This is a lot for a small village. Opposes the rezoning
of the Elliott Allotment to multi-family. Has brought a petition of more than
100 homeowners from the area who oppose it. This will lower property values in
the area. This will increase the student population, which is already
overcrowded. If we do allow multi-family, it should be one-story with garages
in back and a buffer zone in the middle. Quality rather than quantity.
Rod Butcher - Residents against multi-family at Elliott Allotment. Cited
traffic congestion, more taxes for streets and public services. McCune - Multi-
family is not being solicited by Council. Every year some property owners come
to us and we have to look at their applications. In order to control density,
we have increased the requirements in square footage for Senior housing. Reese
- Two-family homes and converted single-family homes are not differentiated on
this map. They show up as single family residential.
Charlene Kusar - She and her brother own several rental properties in
Jefferson. They live in the Township. She thinks landowners should be allowed
to vote on zoning issues. Renters are good people, too. There is a very high
demand for rental properties. Not everyone can afford to buy a home. Taxes are
high here in Jefferson. Bragga - There will be hearings and notices to property
owners if individual properties are rezoned.
Mark Mansfield - We don't need to seek out growth. We need to worry about the
overcrowded schools. McCune - We are trying to control growth with a plan.
Cayce Baxley - we need good strong zoning and enforcement. There are 1,378
residential lots here in the Village; 519 lots left. Industrial land is already
owned by someone. Highest prices are for Industrial. We don't need this plan at
all. Throw it out and start anew. Brought forth a petition to reject the
Comprehensive Plan in its entirety.
Ken Fertig - Something has been done right; rental units go like hotcakes. You
don't even need to advertise. Historical District is too restrictive. Maybe if
you start with a small section in the center of town, you could try to control
change. It used to be legal to build multi-family units in areas zoned
commercial. That may be how all the converted homes came about. We do need a
Comprehensive Plan, because we are growing, and we need to control this growth.
George Jones - The Comprehensive Plan should address the costs of services
necessary for the possible growth.
Deb Foote - West Mulberry is a dirt road. We love it as is. We don't want it to
be a Collector street. It will cause more traffic to be routed to our street.
McCune - Mulberry St. was put in to give a double access to the High School in
case of emergency. This goes to private property (the school). The map will be
corrected. West Mulberry will not be a Collector Street. Reese - In the year
2000 to 2010 traffic pattern problems will develop with the potential growth of
the Elliott Allotment and the subdivision to the south. The growth of the
Junior/Senior High School complex, which is the main social center of the area,
will also add to severe traffic congestion if provision is not made for an
additional outlet away from Jefferson St. Even though the Village does not own
the right of way at Mulberry, as development occurs in the southwest quadrant
of the community, the increased traffic will require the Village to look at the
possibility of improvement of Mulberry in the future.
Questions and comments from the audience:
The flooding in Elliott. What are you going to do about it?
McCune - We are cleaning the ditch and developing an access road to alleviate
this flooding.
If a developer is annexing his property to build a subdivision, the developer
should pay for the street.
What is a Collector Street? Reese - A collector street collects traffic from
smaller streets and moves it to a main artery, in this case to the State
Highway.
Converted houses all over town. No one does anything about them. The Village
owns acreage north of Jefferson St. Why zone it Industrial? Are we going to
sell it? This is choice, precious land. We don't want it zoned Industrial: we
want it zoned residential.
We have a fine town here already - We don't need any changes. Don't louse it
up.
Fertig - Of the 75 acres the Village bought for $75,000, only 30 acres of it is
buildable for homes.
Adjoining landowners have no say so in zoning changes.
Over 20 school buses a day go by West Mulberry now. Worry that a collector
street will turn into a truck route.
No drainage is addressed in the Plan. What about the Jeffersonian Estates?
McCune - This Plan is far from finished. There will be more hearings to get
more input from the community. We will be looking at this this very carefully.
Adjourn.
Respectfully submitted,
Judith A. Selzer Clerk of Council
Approved: William A. McCune Mayor

Cowles - Referred to a letter from the Board of Education requesting paving of
the tree lawns at the Elementary School, which are now being used for parking.
McCune - We don't pave tree lawns because we may have to put them back later.
They now have a conditional use permit for the parking. Council consensus was
to decline the request. A letter will be sent.
Cowles - Has a problem with the plans Hudson-Hanover rezoning applications.
According to her figures, this is only enough square footage for 14 units.
Doesn't think the density regulations should include the driveway. D. Weir -
There were two areas which were noted when the zoning permit was denied:
setback and square footage. There will be a Public Hearing on May 16th for
Hudson-Hanover. Cowles - Asked why multi-family was discussed at the last
Planning Commission meeting. Blevins - The need is to provide for approximately
25 acres of buildable land for multi-family construction. Our present zoning
allows for no multi-family areas, except for those that already exist. But in
the commercial areas, there are 25 acres which do not exclude it. Cowles -
Suggested the zoning updates and upgrades be passed as soon as possible. These
have nothing to do with any changes related to the Comprehensive Plan. These
zoning amendments will be separated out, placed in a new format, and presented
again.
Cowles - A Bldgs/Land Use committee meeting will be held on Tuesday to discuss
the Comprehensive Plan.
Bragga - Suggested some changes be made to the Plan now. We can iron out some
of the problems right here and now. Then at the next Hearing, we can work on
the other things which we haven't decided on yet. For instance, lets adjust the
multi-family section now. Cross it off. Cross off Mulberry as a Collector
Street. We should not need to have separate committee meetings for this. Motion
by Cowles, seconded by Bragga, to delete West Mulberry as a Collector Street
(Recommendation No. 1.) Blevins - Reminded Council of the future traffic

Visitors Comments:
Mr. Richardson, representing the Ashtabula County Medical Center, gave a short
summary of the proposal to join with the Ashtabula Clinic and build a medical
facility here in Jefferson. Five acres of land are needed for the project. This
will allow for future expansion. We also need to be able to hook into both
water and sewer McCune - The Cucumber Street property is being considered. We
need an emergency 24 hour facility with x-ray and lab, not just another doctors
office. Mr. Richardson - No x-rays will be available at the present time. Blood
will be drawn and sent to the lab in Ashtabula. There is a possibility that
EKG's will be provided here. Blevins - Will there be a helicopter service? Mr.
Richardson - Surface transportation will be more readily available. Bragga -
Will the zoning need to be changed? D. Weir - We will need to rezone the
property in order to build a clinic as opposed to a hospital. Richardson -
sewer and water is necessary to us. Cayce Baxley - What are you offering that
we don't already have? Richardson - Just primary care - no mammograms. Dietrich
- Asked why we should subsidize just another doctor's office when the other
doctors here in town have paid to set up their own practices. Hours will be
regular office hours, no emergency services.

Recreation:
Bruce Thompson gave a brief summary of the Recreation proposal to build a new
Community Center. Madge Lehnert went over the history of the Jefferson
Community Center from 1976 to the present. At the present time, there are still
several foundations and agencies willing to provide grant money for the new
building if the community shows a willingness to support it. Dona Borsukoff
presented a list of donors including 56 businesses and over 200 individuals.
The donations range from $20,000.00 down to $3.00. Ruby Blanche reported on the
current balance in the S.O.C.C. treasury: $89,832.00 plus pledges to a total of
$100,632.00. Virgie Butcher said applications to C.D.C. for $100,000.00 and to
the Ashtabula Foundation for $40,000.00 have been sent. We are going to apply
to the State for a 1084 grant for $40,000.00, and to the CDBG for $26,000.00.
We need $500,000.00 in Councilmanic bonds or a bank loan to support our
Community Center. Wilma Herndon explained about how various fund raisers will
raise about $6,000.00 this year. Cowles - Explained about the plans. These are
very preliminary. The estimated cost will be between $500,000.00 and
$600,000.00. This is a guess. A lot more work will need to be done to get a
true estimate. Madge Lehnert - There are 15 members of S.O.C.C. Board and they
have all worked very hard to put this proposal before the Council today. She
introduced Ike Snell, Regional Director of the Boys and Girls Clubs of America.
He explained that the Boys and Girls Clubs provide not just recreation, but
things to do to improve the quality of life for our children. In New York City
they have been around for 135 years. The Jefferson Community Center services
the young and the Seniors. This is a positive program, here. Barb Heath said we
have no programs for junior and senior high school students because we don't
have the facilities. This is not good. Our children deserve good things. This
plan provides for a workable facility. It is easy and inexpensive to maintain,
just the basics.
Bragga - If we set our priorities differently, we can do this. If we crunch the
numbers, the dollars are there. The 2.5 mil levy was political, the next one
was battling two school levies and it still almost passed. Solicitor - We need
to get the project totally in focus, with the architect's budget. At the 6%
current rate, a loan of $550,000.00 for twenty-five years will be $3,543.66 a
month. Bragga - $40,000.00 a year is not a problem. Dietrich - We need a
finalized set of plans complete with all costs. McCune - Beverly can get these
figures as time goes on. We need to build it big enough. Solicitor - The
question is whether Council will support borrowing the money for this. Cowles -
Will continue to donate her services and work with Council and the S.O.C.C.
Board to move this project forward. After discussion, Council agreed to a
building cost budget of $550,000.00. This figure is expected to be defrayed by
possible grants, donations and fund raisers. They also want an addendum to
include an indoor swimming pool. Blevins is philosophically opposed to the
building. Motion by Dietrich, seconded by Bragga, to have Beverly Cowles bring
in a total proposal, including the money needed, size of the project, and
finalized plans; this is an expression of Council's willingness to borrow the
money needed for this project. Roll: Bragga, yea; Stasny, yea; Cowles, yea;
Dietrich, yea; Blevins, nay. Motion passed. Cowles - Read a letter of
resignation from Kenneth Kaminski, Director of Recreation. Motion by Dietrich,
seconded by Bragga, to accept the resignation. Blevins, yea; Dietrich, yea;
Cowles, yea; Stasny, yea; Bragga, yea. Cowles - Read a letter from Barbara
Heath requesting the position of Acting Director. Motion by Cowles, seconded by
Dietrich, to appoint Barbara Heath as Acting Director, with probationary
salary, for up to a six month period. Roll: Bragga, yea; Stasny, yea, Cowles,
yea; Dietrich, yea; Blevins, yea.
