**Public Hearing: Hudson-Hanover Senior Complex
Purpose: To review a request by Hudson-Hanover Company for a zoning change from
Single-family Residential to Multi-family Residential in order to build a 24
unit Senior Housing Complex.
Richard Buchanan, President of Hudson-Hanover, explained how the small shortage
of square footage could be compensated for by adding the adjoining driveway to
the plan. He then asked Council to approve his plan for Phase II of the Senior
Housing Complex. John Nemeth said we already have too many multi-family units
in Jefferson. Barry Harper asked if the housing complex will be strictly for
the elderly. R. Buchanan - Yes, only the elderly and the handicapped. These
will be financed by the FmHA. No modifications to the present use are allowed
for twenty years. We can't sell the property without FmHA approval, and any new
owner must rent these only to the elderly or the handicapped. Cayce Baxley said
there is not enough parking space provided, and the two bedroom apartments are
not big enough. A current tenant said there are no problems with parking. This
is the biggest and best apartment I've ever had. The Manager of the complex
said the apartments are beautiful, each apartment has a mailbox in the hallway,
so the Seniors don't have to go outside for the mail. J. Nemeth - Property
values will decrease for the adjacent property owners. C. Baxley wants Council
to go with the most restrictive codes, and stop bending the rules. Solicitor -
Explained that Council's role is not to approve this project.
They must decide whether to rezone the land. Bragga - Asked about the fire
safety codes. D. Weir - The Fire Chief has checked this out and has no
complaints. Bragga expressed the opinion that the zoning codes should should be
adhered to. More discussion followed with the Seniors in the audience
expressing their approval of the project. Cowles - Said the owners should come
back with a plan that meets our zoning codes. Gene Crislip asked why the zoning
code provides for variances if none are allowed. Motion by Blevins, seconded by
Stasny, for the First Reading, Title Only, of Ordinance No. 2046. Roll: Bragga,
nay; Stasny, nay; Piper, nay; Cowles, nay; Dietrich, nay; Blevins, yea. Motion
failed.

Visitors Comments:
Charles Jeffords, Superintendent of Jefferson Schools - Explained the need for
a new school in Jefferson to house grades 5, 6, 7 and 8. The Elementary School
has 1,000 students. Normal enrollment for elementary schools in the State of
Ohio is 400 to 600 students. Part of the school was built in 1870 and the rest
in 1905. It is at the end of its useful life. The above ground tanks at the bus
garage are inadequate and obsolete. The High School also has a lack of
sufficient space and homerooms. Some years ago, a consultant recommended a
middle school. We are still in the planning stages. Brainstorming and comments
from the public are welcomed. We need to move forward. We need a plan ready for
a bond issue on the November ballot. He announced another School Board meeting
to be held on Thursday, June 30, at 8:00 p.m. Terry Finger - Asked about the
rumors concerning the Community Center as part of the new Middle School. Mr.
Jeffords said this was never part of the building plan; this was just one of
many items suggested at one of the school board meetings. Eva Heidecker - There
were many good suggestions at that meeting. We just can not do everything.

Solicitor - Regarding the West Cedar Street petition, Council has the authority
to improve this street if they want to, but they are not obligated to do so. We
can accept this petition as a petition for improvements, through the assessment
process. We can issue bonds, improve the street, then place the charges on to
the tax duplicate. If the Village pays to improve this street, it will set a
precedent. In his opinion West Cedar has not been accepted as a village street.
Ben Godleski - Complained that the residents of the street have paid taxes as
if the street was improved. The Village needs to pay only $10,000.00 to
$12,000.00 to open the road. Jerry Lemire, Solicitor - If the residents agree
to a petition for assessment, we would be forced to open it. The Mayor asked
for a vote on the matter. Motion by Cowles, seconded by Blevins, to accept the
petition as presented and open West Cedar Street at the expense of the Village.

Motion by Bragga, seconded by Cowles, to pay the current bills. Roll: Cowles,
yea; Dietrich, yea; Blevins, yea; Bragga, yea; Stasny, yea; Piper, yea.
Visitors Comments:
Jim Collise complained about parking on front lawns. Ben Godleski had several
requests of Council regarding water lines, sewer lines, and improvements to
West Cedar Street, at the expense of the property owners there. Solicitor - The
Village should maintain the road if it meets specs. Solicitor - normal
acceptance of a street is by ordinance. Motion by Blevins, seconded by Piper,
to commit overselves to accept the street if it meets specs and is inspected
and approved by the Village Administrator or his designee. Motion by Blevins,
seconded by Bragga, to table the motion until we receive these requests in
writing. Roll: Bragga, yea; Stasny, yea; Piper, yea; Cowles, nay; Dietrich,
yea; Blevins, yea. Bob Jones said the Jeffersonian Estates area needs sidewalks
on Route 307 more than they do in the subdivision. Park can not go forward
until the drainage project is completed.
Recreation:
Piper - The CDC has requested a current resolution of support from Council in
regard to the two salaried positions and the utilities for the new building.
Motion by Cowles, seconded by Piper, to resolve to continue to pay the salaries
of the Director and the Program Supervisor and to pay the utilities for the new
Community Center. Roll: Bragga, yea; Stasny, yea; Piper, yea; Cowles, yea;
Dietrich, yea; Blevins, yea. A letter will be sent to the Civic Development
Corporation to this effect. D. Weir - 87 applications have been received for
the Director position. Mccune - Two members of the Recreation Board and the
Recreation Committee will go through and select the four best applicants to be
reviewed by Council. Dietrich - Suggested we hire an area resident for the job.
Buildings/Land Use:
Motion by Cowles, seconded by Blevins, for the First Reading, Title Only, of
Ordinance No. 2049. Roll: Blevins, yea; Dietrich, yea; Cowles, yea; Piper, yea;
Stasny, yea; Bragga, yea.
First Reading, Title Only   Ordinance No. 2049
AN ORDINANCE ACCEPTING THE ANNEXATION OF LAND TO THE VILLAGE OF JEFFERSON
Blevins - Has had several complaints about people parking on front lawns. J.
Collise has gone to other towns to find out how they enforce their laws
regarding this. They start with warnings and deadlines to remove the cars from
prohibited parking areas. Blevins - Said some of these people have built
parking spaces on their front lawn. Solicitor - Building parking spaces on the
lawn is clearly a violation of our present ordinance, but the problem of
parking on the lawn is still not addressed. Motion by Blevins, seconded by
Cowles, to have an ordinance drawn up to prohibit parking on front lawns. Roll:
Cowles, yea; Piper, yea; Stasny, yea; Bragga, yea; Blevins, yea; Dietrich, yea.
Cowles - Read a letter from a property owner on Spruce Street who is against
the truck bypass along their street. Dietrich - Suggested Sycamore Street; no
residents there to complain. Cucumber Street will have residents if we open it
and zone it residential. Cowles - Regarding the Comprehensive Land Use Plan,
updates will be reviewed for next meeting.
Cowles - Asked Bob Jones for cost estimates for the park at the Jeffersonian
Estates. B. Jones - The fence will cost approximately $10,500.00. We need a
survey, first, at a cost of about $400 to $500. Then we need asphalt for the
Basketball court. A grant from the Ashtabula Foundation is a possibility. The
Vocational School will do the work on this. Drainage and survey need to be done
first. McCune - The budget for this year has no money for this project. He
suggested we do some preliminary work which will not cost too much actual cash.
Motion by Bragga, seconded by Blevins, to fill the pond, set the pipe in the
ditch for drainage and order the survey. Roll: Bragga, yea; Blevins, yea;
Dietrich, yea; Cowles, yea; Piper, yea; Stasny, yea. Cowles - Was asked to
choose colors for the village buildings. The color schemes will be at the
Village Office for Council's input. McCune - The painting project should be bid
both ways, all white or with colors. Motion by Dietrich, seconded by Blevins,
for an addendum to the bid documents for colors. Roll: Bragga, yea; Stasny,
yea; Piper, yea; Cowles, yea; Dietrich, yea; Blevins, yea.
Safety:

Finance:
Bragga - Explained that with the renewal of the 1.75 mill General Fund
operating levy, the Village will continue to receive about $42,000 a year for

will be an auction at the Vocational School-Complex B on August 8, 1994. We
need any and all donations for the event.

Resolution No. 2051
RESOLUTION IN SUPPORT OF THE JEFFERSON AREA RECYCLING CENTER'S GRANT REQUEST
FOR THE PROGRAM "RECYCLING EDUCATION FOR STUDENTS AND TEACHERS (REST)"
Blevins - We requested a grant of $22,000.00 and they gave us $11,000.00. The
grant will reimburse us for the transportation and box rental charges. She
again requested a worker be hired for 4 to 8 hours on Saturdays. McCune - We
need a track record, first. We don't want to hire anyone until we know how many
hours are need in the winter months. Bragga - Agreed. We can use our own people
to get a track record. This should be taken from the Recycling Budget. Motion
by Bragga, seconded by Stasny, to approve the overtime needed for the remainder
of 1994 for the recycling effort. Roll: Blevins, yea; Bragga, yea; Stasny, yea;
Thompson, yea; Cowles, yea; Dietrich, yea. Blevins - Bob Burton of Uselma
Avenue was the 1,000th person to use the recycling center. He received a free
load of wood chips.
Blevins - The proposal from Mr. Godleski for West Cedar Street has been
received. D. Weir - The sewer line needs the proper procedure to be followed
before it is accepted. We inspected it and a few things still need to be done.
We need to televise the line. Solicitor - He will build the water line all the
way through. The tap-in fees will be over and above the $500.00 tap-in fee for
sewer. Motion by Blevins, seconded by Stasny, to allow Mr. Godleski to proceed
with the road and accept it when it meets specifications. Cowles - Has a
problem with a partial road. Roll: Bragga, yea; Blevins, yea; Dietrich, yea;
Cowles, nay; Thompson, yea; Stasny, yea. D. Weir - Charlie Miller is retiring
in September. We need to advertise for the position. Bragga - This is a part-
time position. We may be able to integrate this position with the hours
necessary for recycling.
Old Business:
Cowles - There will be a committee meeting on the painting of the buildings.
The Mayor read Carrie Heath's letter of resignation. Bragga - Met with CDC
people about the grant application for the new Community Center. We should get
$100,000 or more from them, but we need to have everything ready. We should put
a cap of $400,000 on the first phase of the building plans. McCune - Explained
that we can build one big room as a start. The offices can be separate from the
building in the beginning. Bragga, the Village may not need councilmanic bonds
or a levy. It is very probable that we can get approximately $320,000.00 of
this money from grants and gifts. Then we will only need to budget $80,000 for
the building. The CDC needs an answer by August 25th.
New Business:
Mayor McCune read a Proclamation: "Key Bank Neighbors Make the Difference." On
Tuesday, September 13, 1994, Society Bank will close and their employees will
work for the community. They will volunteer to help out Senior citizens and
others who need work done and are unable to do it themselves.

Ordinance No. 2052
AN ORDINANCE AMENDING SECTION 876.01 OF THE CODIFIED ORDINANCES OF THE VILLAGE
OF JEFFERSON TO REGULATE TRANSIENT DEALERS.
Motion by Stasny, seconded by Bragga, for the First Reading, Title Only, of
Ordinance No. 2056. Dietrich - This is just another example of the government
taking control of our personal liberties. We already have compulsory school
attendance, and truant officers. Our Police Department already has the
authority to pick these kids up. Bragga - We are addressing other people's
kids, coming into our town. We should build up more protection against these
kids. Cowles - Asked why expelled children are specifically excluded from this
ordinance. Solicitor - This ordinance is only to address children who belong in
school. Other questions were raised about home schooling and juvenile court.
Chief Febel - In every case it will be left to the officer's discretion. Bragga
- Some people don't want to be bothered with their children; they want someone
else to control them. This will put teeth into the laws already on the books.
Roll: Stasny, yea; Thompson, yea; Cowles, yea; Dietrich, nay; Blevins, yea;
Bragga, yea. Motion passed. The Solicitor gave a brief explanation of the
proposed amended D.U.I. ordinance, which will now conform to the Ohio Statutes
with regard to D.U.I. and includes immediate suspension of license and
forfeiture of vehicle upon the second offense. Motion by Stasny, seconded by
Bragga, for the First Reading, Title Only, of Ordinance No. 2057. Roll: Stasny,
yea; Bragga, yea; Blevins, yea; Dietrich, yea; Cowles, yea; Thompson, yea.

Solicitor - Regarding the request for exclusive rights for Norma Jean's Sleigh
Rides, Council has the authority to grant exclusive rights, but we need to
worry about the liability aspects of a contract. If we do nothing, she can do
this, but with an exclusive contract, the liability presents itself. Norma Jean
has $100,000.00 liability insurance for this. Solicitor, this is somewhat
unusual for a village to do. Exclusivity for sleigh rides, on the face of it,
doesn't benefit the village as a whole. McCune - The routes have been drawn up
by the Police Department. Cowles - Suggested she try it for a year, without the
exclusive rights, and see how things work out. Cowles - There are cracks in the

able to patch the stucco. Thompson - There is standing water in the basement,

G. Pascarella complained about the proposed daytime curfew for young people,
the proposed parking ban for front lawns, and the proposed new Community
Center. He also said that curbs and sidewalks in the center of town should be
put on hold until a truck route is designated. K. Fertig said the schools
should be responsible for truancy. The police already have the authority to
stop kids who are walking around during the day. We don't need this ordinance.
Blevins - If parents don't watch their kids the community must. Bragga - Gang
members have tried to enroll in our school. R. Titus - Ashtabula gang members
came here last year, burglarized some homes and raped two women. J. Kusar -
Asked about the conversions of single-family homes. Who will pay for the
lawsuits? How can you tell when these conversions took place? Solicitor - It
will be difficult to trace. On July 6, 1976, the zoning code was passed. Any
conversions prior to that date were grandfathered. We could look into requiring
permits for additional electric meters. B. Stone - Asked when the drainage
project on Washington Blvd. will be finished. D. Weir - The ditches there will
be open late this fall. The job was much worse than expected. McCune - This was
addressed as soon as was possible.

Buildings/Land Use:
Cowles - We have received two letters from the Planning Commission. They
recommend Council deny the zoning change request from Gary Van Slyke. A hearing
will be held on November 7, 1994. The Planning Commission has approved the
revisions to the Comprehensive Plan except for recommendations No. 4 and 5,
which they feel need more public hearings. No. 4 is to open North Cucumber
Street and designate it as a truck route. No. 5 is to change the zoning along
North Cucumber Street to a Light Industrial District. Bragga - We do need a
viable truck route. Cucumber may be the best choice. Funds may be available to
open the road if it were zoned Industrial. We need to hear from the public
about how this area should be zoned: Residential or Industrial. Cowles -
Council has already decided against Nos. 4 and 5, so why should we need to have
public hearings on this? We need to revise the Plan so people can see the
changes, and then we'll have a hearing. She suggested more discussion about
this at the next meeting. Motion by Cowles to eliminate public hearings on
recommendations No. 4 and 5. No second. Solicitor - The Planning Commission has
voted to make this recommendation to the Council. You will need to have five
votes of Council to go against their recommendation. Bragga - Asked how much it
will cost to have Mr. Reese make the revisions to the Plan to date. D. Weir -
He will revise it one final time at no cost. After that, there will be a
charge. Motion by Cowles, seconded by Bragga, to table the recommendation of
the Planning Commission until the Plan has been revised. Roll: Stasny, yea;
Bragga, yea; Blevins, yea; Cowles, yea; Thompson, yea.

No Report.
Wastewater:
Dietrich - Burgess & Niple is working on the plans. Bids will be solicited for
a new truck, 6 cylinder, heavy duty. McCune - The Township trustees, Mr.
Nassief, Dan and I had a meeting last Tuesday. West of the dealership, Nassief
wants to build between 20 and 80 homes. They want to tap in to our sewer system
without annexation. I told them annexation is required to tap in. We need the
tax dollars to support the sewer plant. Tap-in fees are not enough. Does
Council have any different opinions on this? C. Rippons - If you charge
$5,000.00 for each tap-in, times 80 homes, you will bring in $400,000.00 just
for this, plus outside village sewer rates. We invited you to this meeting just
to evaluate the merits of this proposal. K. Fertig - We will not receive the
income tax from these people, even though they will be benefitting from our
sewer system.
Utilities:
Thompson - Spoke to a representative from the East Ohio Gas Company about the
rate increase. The reason for the increase is to upgrade the value of their
stock, and to upgrade their technology. The contract was signed for a smaller
amount, but before the public hearings. The gentleman encouraged everyone to
attend the hearings anyway, to express their views. Blevins - TCI is
implementing another rate increase. CEI has changed their procedures with
regard to street lighting. A meeting will be held Wednesday, October 19, 19994,
to go over these changes. Dan will attend. McCune - Ohio Water Service will no
longer reimburse property owners for water line installation costs. Thompson -
You can recoup it yourself from the lot buyers as you sell them.

*** Public Hearing: Van Slyhe Zoning Change Application
Gary and Elida Van Slyke have applied for a zoning change from RS (Residential
single-family) to RD (Residential multi-family) in order to build a two family
home. The Planning Commission has recommended that Council deny the request.
Jim Reuschling, their builder, presented plans for the Council to study. He
said the Van Slykes will wait until these plans can be reviewed by the Planning
Commission. Bragga - Suggested a vote be taken now, and then they can reapply
to the Planning Commission with the proper plans. Motion by Bragga, seconded by
Cowles, to deny the zoning change. Roll: Blevins, nay; Dietrich, yea; Cowles,
yea; Thompson, yea; Stasny, nay; Bragga, yea. Motion passed.

Wastewater:
Dietrich - We have had several meetings with Burgess & Niple, our engineering
firm. Things are now moving along on schedule. If we can eliminate some of our
I & I problem, we will be able to use a smaller detention basin. This will save
us some money. We have a list of about 100 possible violators. D. Weir - During
a heavy rain, about 96,000 gallons of water per hour goes into the sewers from
illegal downspout connections. We need I to disconnect these downspouts from
our sanitary sewer system. Solicitor - Our ordinance requires a prolonged
procedure of notices and warnings. We don't have the time to waste. He
suggested we try a voluntary compliance letter. Offer them something in return.
Dietrich - We will also need an amendment to the ordinance. We need this done
by March or April of next year. Bragga suggested using incentives during
legislation. D. Weir - We could offer to pay the $45.00 cost involved. Dietrich
- Disagreed. Hardship cases, only. Property owners should pay for their own
repairs. D. Weir - The EPA has assured us that the permit to install has been
approved. We can start the bidding process soon.
*** Adjourn to S.O.C.C./Recreation Board meeting.
The Mayor referred to a letter from the S.O.C.C. and Recreation Boards. D.
Binkley - Asked who is responsible for hiring an architect if Beverly isn't
able to continue to devote her time to this. The Mayor asked Beverly if she
will be able to meet the December 25 deadline. Cowles - Will meet with the
committee and have an answer by next meeting. Solicitor - The S.O.C.C. Board
can hire their own architect because they have their own money. The O.R.C.
provides for the Rec Board to spend the money which it generates. The confusion
arises when the money for the building comes from other Village funds. M.
Lehnert - The S.O.C.C. Board would welcome the Village's interest in this
matter. McCune - Explained that a referendum petition has been filed with the
Clerk to block Resolution No. 2055. This Resolution authorizes the Village
Administrator to file for Issue 1 funds from the State for the new Community
Center. It also commits the Village to fund the project for a maximum of
$168,000. Solicitor - We are still in the ten day period required for the
petition to be open for public viewing. Some people are taking advantage of the
time to remove their names from the petition. McCune - Prior to 1992, Council
had set aside $200,000 of Village funds for the new Community Center. We are
trying to get this money from Issue I funds. It is somewhat confusing that the
same people who were going to spend $200,000 two years ago are now trying to
stop the grant procedure. If we get the total grant, the Village will not have
to spend anything. Dietrich - Asked how much money the S.O.C.C. Board has
without the Village involved. M. Lehnert - We may lose our grants. Ashtabula
Foundation has a deadline of December 31st. C.D.C. and ODN&R also have
deadlines. Stasny -Asked why they want to stop this. S. Nizen - The voters
should decide whether we spend taxpayer money on this. C. Baxley - It looks
like we'll stand to lose a lot of money if this goes to referendum. McCune - A
short while ago, we received a grant for handicapped access, but we had to turn
it down because we didn't have enough money committed. They said to apply again
as soon as we are ready. D. Weir - A Community Block Grant is also a
possibility.

Mayor's State of the Village Address - 1995
1994 was an interesting year. A lot of work was done on various projects
throughout the Village.
1995 will be an expensive year because we need to bring the sewer plant into
compliance with new EPA regulations. The plans are ready and hopefully the bids
will be received and accepted in the first quarter of 1995 for these repairs. I
know that our Administrator, Dan Weir, will put our sewer plant in compliance
and keep it that way for many years to come. This is a very difficult part of
the Administrator's job.
The Street Department worked vigorously on the storm drainage system on West
Walnut Street and in Elliott Allotment and Jeffersonian Estates. There are
still several areas to work on in our continuing attack on the storm drainage
problems. The Street Department also received a prestigious award from the
Chamber of Commerce this last year when they were honored with the Community
Service Award.
The Police Department continued their duties in keeping the Village safe and
solving crimes that occurred.
The Fire Department continued their duties in extinguishing fires and being on
the scene of accidents.
The Recreation Department is still struggling to build a new Community Center.
We have another new Director who, I hope, will present to Village Council all
the needed figures to enable us to help with this.
The Clerk and her staff have begun the sewer billing through the Village
office. This will save the Village Sewer Department money that can go into the
required sewer improvements.
In all, the Village is running smoothly. I expect to continue the repairs of
sidewalks and streets and other various projects in the Village this coming
year.
I would like to thank Council for their hard work and support in 1994. I look
forward to working with you and all the employees and citizens of the Village
in 1995.
Adjourn.
Respectfully submitted,
Judith A. Selzer, Clerk of Council
Approved: William A. McCune, Mayor
January 5, 1995 - Public Hearing
Meeting was called to order by Mayor William McCune.
Roll Call of Council: Blevins, Bragga, Cowles, Dietrich, Stasny, Thompson
Also present: Toad Childs, Bill Douglass, Jeanne Douglass, Virgie Butcher,
Sharon Mayernick, Bev Finger, Terry Finger, Eleanor Ferguson, Wendell Ferguson,
Jackie Lemire, Jim McIntyre, Cayce Baxley, Ken Fertig, John Nemeth, Barb Heath,
John Kusar, Stan Nizen, Jerome Lemire, Solicitor; Daniel Weir, Administrator;
Roger Reese, Planning Consultant; Star Beacon; Gazette.
Public Hearing:
Purpose: To review the Revised Comprehensive Land Use Plan with Emphasis of
Discussion on Recommendations Number 4 and 5.
Roger Reese, Planning Consultant, gave a brief description of the Comprehensive
Land Use Plan as he was hired to proceed with it. The recommendations of the
Planning Commission included (1) designating Cucumber Street as a truck route
and the adjacent land to be zoned Light Industrial; (2) upgrade Mulberry Street
so as to use it for a collector street; (3) to allow for multi-family housing.
Items (2) and (3) have been struck down by the Council and the Planning
Commission agreed to these changes. The issue here today is Cucumber Street.
The Planning Commission wants more public input as to the use of this area.
Jackie Lemire - Why does the revised Comprehensive Plan still have the same
recommendations as the old one? Reese - This is a guideline, these alternatives
are still available. Toad Childs - Why can't the Plan be rewritten? McCune -
The Plan will be rewritten and open for public viewing before Village Council
approves it. Terry Finger - Asked about Poplar Street. McCune - There will be
no changes to Poplar St. Cayce Baxley - Read some old minutes regarding truck
routes. Ordinance No. 2001 was passed for delineation of Cucumber Street. She
said this was the plan before the planner was hired. She brought up the park
land ordinance. She wants a vote of the people on the use of this property. D.
Weir - We're here now to further discuss recommendation numbers 4 and 5 -
Zoning along Cucumber Street, and whether it should be designated as a truck
route. Solicitor - Zoning should follow the Comprehensive Plan eventually. If
we have a Comprehensive Plan first, we are better able to defend our future
zoning laws. Ed Flack - Will the sewer plant be able to handle the industrial
expansion if this area is zoned industrial? Dietrich - Without a doubt. Stan
Nizen - Cucumber Street should remain Residential, its a dead-end street,
anyway. Let's leave the truck route alone until the State pays for it. McCune -
Sycamore Street is also a dead-end street. Jim McIntyre - The State can
relocate Route 307 to Spruce Street. Stan Nizen - Jefferson Township and
Jefferson Village should be one governmental entity with a Charter. Jim
McIntyre - This is the last piece of nice land in the village for homes. The
industries want vacant flat land. Look at the BP of Jefferson. They put up a 30
foot sign, and took a beautiful tree down. He feels the best use of this land
is not Industrial or Light Industrial. We can use Sycamore Street if needed. We
sold the water system. Now we have the second highest water rates in the state.
We need to save Cucumber Street. Stan Nizen - This land is best suited for
residential single-family construction. John Nemeth - We should make Cucumber
Street a truck route. There are no homes there, yet. If we don't do something
now, while we have the chance, we'll end up in the future with no truck route.
Ken Fertig - Cucumber Street is the most logical road to open for a truck
route. Traffic is backed up every day in the center of town. Stan Nizen - Any
money spent on Sycamore Street will not be wasted when the State opens Route
307 to trucks. Cayce Baxley - This was a small price to pay for the beautiful
area we own. Thompson - This area is a wonderful combination of Man's
destructiveness and Nature's natural beauty. Jim McIntyre - Truck route or
Industrial zoning - What is the question here? McCune - Grant money is
available for Industrial construction only. We need the truck route, and the
grants will pay for it if we zone this area Industrial. This is how the idea
came about.
No further comments from the public.
Mayor McCune - The Council will take the comments from the public under
advisement and will make the Comprehensive Plan available to the public again
before final approval.
Adjourn.
Respectfully submitted,
Judith A. Selzer, Clerk of Council
Approved: William A. McCune, Mayor

Buildings/Land Use:
Dietrich - The revised Comprehensive Land Use Plan has been distributed.
Solicitor - Explained that the Planning Commission has the final word on the
Land use Plan, according to the Ohio Revised Code. They are the body who does
the planning process. The Council has the final word on any zoning changes.
Ideally, any zoning changes should follow the plan adopted by the Planning
Commission. C. Baxley - Complained that three readings were promised, and now
it is not necessary. Solicitor - The Plan can not, of itself, change anything.
Only Council can change zoning through the process of hearings and ordinances.
Council can also adopt the Plan if they desire. K. Fertig - Asked who enforces
the Comprehensive Plan. Solicitor - According to the zoning laws, the Planning
Commission decides an issue. Council then concurs by passing an ordinance or
over-rides the Commission by a 3/4 vote of Council. Bragga - The intent was to
hear it three times, but this Council has gone above and beyond the statute.
Solicitor - The Planning Commission has the power to refuse the input of the
Council on planning issues.

accessibility. We need to pass two motions to satisfy the County Building
Department. Motion by Dietrich, seconded by Thompson, to clarify the Job
Description of Village Employees who work at the Jefferson Wastewater Treatment
Plant to require that all such employees not be wheelchair bound. This
requirement is imposed due to the physical skills needed to adequately perform
the work required of an employee at the Wastewater Treatment Plant and because
of the inherent danger from the equipment operated at the Plant to a wheelchair
bound individual. Roll: Blevins, yea; Dietrich, yea; Cowles, yea; Thompson,

policy regarding public access to and public tours of the second floor of the
Wastewater Treatment Building, which contains the belt filter press for
dewatering of sludge. No public access and/or tours shall be allowed, due to
the dangerous nature of the machinery employed and the potential health dangers
that arise out of the sludge dewatering process. Roll: Blevins, yea; Dietrich,
yea; Cowles, yea; Thompson, yea; Stasny, yea.

September 21, 1995 - Special Meeting
Meeting was called to order by President Pro Tem Esther Blevins.
Roll Call of Council: Blevins, Cowles, Dietrich, Stasny, Thompson
Also present: Star Beacon, The Gazette.
Blevins - This meeting has been called in order to interview the candidates for
the vacant Council seat of Larry Bragga. The term for this seat ends December
31, 1997. Some of the applicants are already on the ballot running for a four
year term, as opposed to the two years and three months remaining of Mr.
Bragga's term. If this presents any problems, we may be able to eliminate some
of the candidates. If anyone has questions which would require an Executive
Session, then Council has the authority to adjourn to a closed session for this
purpose. Motion by Cowles, seconded by Stasny, to interview all candidates who
applied for the vacant seat. All in favor.
Kathleen Baxley, Edwin Ward, Terry Finger, James Noyes, and John Kusar were
interviewed individually. Walter Olson was not able to attend, but still wished
to be considered. Arthur Aho removed his name from consideration because he is
a candidate for the four year term. Discussion regarding candidates. James
Noyes name was eliminated because he has not been a Village resident for one
year or more. Motion by Dietrich, seconded by Stasny, to elect Terry Finger to
the unexpired term of Larry Bragga. Roll: Stasny, yea; Thompson, yea; Cowles,
yea; Dietrich, yea; Blevins, yea. Motion passed. Mr. Finger will be sworn in at
the October 2, 1995 meeting.
Motion by Thompson, seconded by Stasny, to send a letter to each candidate to
thank them for their time and commitment to the Village. Roll: Blevins, yea;
Dietrich, yea; Cowles, yea; Thompson, yea; Stasny, yea.
Blevins - Reminded everyone of the upcoming Candidates' Night.
Adjourn.
Respectfully submitted,
Judith A. Selzer, Clerk of Council
Approved: Esther H. Blevins, President Pro Tempore

Planning Commission was asked to make a recommendation. There will be no cost
to the property owners to upgrade the road for a truck route. Jan Pallo - Is
against the strip mall. I live in the house where my business is. Our property
values may go down. A suggestion was made to change the zoning from Commercial
back to historical. The neighborhoods should be preserved. Any old thing is
being put up. Barry Harper - We don't want or need a new strip mall. Mrs.
Cornell - We do need more stores and we do need more places for people to work.
We do support it. Mr. Thorne - This is not a huge project, about six stores. We
just want to grow with the Village. Cayce Baxley - Asked Mr. Thorne for maps
and plans. Thorne - We have no plans completed, yet. This project will add to

Wastewater:
Dietrich - Asked about the figures for the bi-monthly billing with actual
readings. Selzer - There will be savings for postage and bill printing charges
for six billings. Even though the extra two meter readings per year will cost
more, we will still realize a savings of an additional $500 a year. This will
not affect our cash flow too much. The Seniors could pay half each month if
they have problems with a two month bill. So far, no one has complained to the
office about problems with a two month bill. McCune - Said he was sorry he
asked the Clerk to do this in the first place, because nothing she does is
right. First, it was to be done every month, now she wants to do it every two
months. What's next? Selzer - Originally, everything was set up for quarterly
billing with actual readings. After we were set up and ready to go with it,
Council decided they wanted monthly billings. This was still feasible if we
went for two estimates and a catch-up bill. But as we move forward with this,
we find that people are not happy with estimated bills, and the billing takes
much longer because of the adjustments. McCune - Complained that the minutes
are not caught up, either. Selzer - Without any help, I will continue to get
farther behind. Dietrich - Why can't you just come in early, work together, and
save the Village $10,000? Selzer - If I come in early, the Secretary leaves
early. Thus, I have to deal with the public all day and stay all the longer at
night in order to get the work done. I work weekends because 3:00 to midnight
is not enough time to do all of the work. I am not here to help the part-time
secretary. I have too much work to do, and my work has to be done.

ordinance. Motion by Finger, seconded by Stasny for the First Reading, Title

too. This was not in the original proposal. Cowles - Front yard parking of most
vehicles is aesthetically unpleasing. If you must park there, do so according
to the exceptions allowed. J. Collise - Some people believe that once this is
on the books, it will fall by the wayside. It shouldn't. Daily use of the front
yard for parking is what we are addressing here. This is an affirmation of your
rights as a property owner. This is a positive step forward. R. Titus - If we
get a complaint, we will act on it. Solicitor - The Zoning Inspector will be
able to cite, and there are penalties provided. Also, the neighbors can get
relief through the zoning inspector rather than the police department. There
were complaints from the public about junk cars, and household garbage allowed
to pile up on people's porches. There are ordinances on the books for this, but
they are not being enforced. Roll: Finger, yea; Stasny, yea; Thompson, yea;
Cowles, yea.

*** Public Hearing:
A request from John Herrmann for a zoning change from Residential Single-Family
to Residential Multi-Family, located on South Sycamore Street and known as
being Lot No. 10 and 15 of the Eastwood Subdivision.
Jim Reuschling gave a short description of the plans to build a duplex on the
property which has Industrial zoning to the east of the lot. This will be a
$130,000 duplex. He read from a list of home sales near other multi-family
units to show that home values have not depreciated. There is no provision for
Multi-Family zoning in the Comprehensive Plan. Ken Fertig - We could open the
75 acres the Village owns to houses and duplexes. McCune - The area sewers need
to be replaced. Reuschling - The effluent from one house will certainly not
have the same effect as storm water. McCune - It will be fixed this year. Why
not wait until then? Reuschling - Sewer problems and zoning are two separate
issues. It will take some time to build, anyway. Finger - The Planning
Commission has denied this request because of the sewer problems. Motion by
Finger to approve the recommendation of the Planning Commission. No second.
Motion by Cowles, seconded by Thompson, to table this request until after the
budget meetings to deal with the sewer problems in the area. Roll: Thompson,
yea; Cowles, yea; Dietrich, yea; Blevins, yea; Finger, yea; Stasny, yea.

Mayor's Address:
THE STATE OF THE VILLAGE OF JEFFERSON, OHIO   JANUARY 2, 1996
The sewer plant was the major expenditure of village and borrowed money (which
will be repaid by the increase in the sewer usage fees over the next twenty
years.) This sizeable investment will enable our hard-working sewer plant
employees to comply with the EPA regulations. The repair of the sewer lines,
both storm and waste water, will continue to make the water treatment plant run
more efficiently.
We continued our sidewalk replacement program with several interested
homeowners wanting this service. In years to come, we plan to replace the rest
of the sidewalks that need it.
In the last two years, we have doubled the amount of street paving that we
normally do in a year and hope to have the repaving program back on schedule
soon.
Our street department was involved in these important repairs to our village
infrastructure. I can't give them enough credit for the wonderful job they do.
The police department has done an exemplary job keeping crime down and the
village safe. The recent purchase of new automobiles, instead of the old
Highway Patrol cars, should cut maintenance and operating vehicle costs in half
or better. The continued training and community involvement by this department
is a fine example to all.
The fire department continues to answer calls with some of the best response
times in the county. The volunteers work hard to keep this department and its
equipment in top shape. Some of the older fire department equipment will need
replacement in the next couple of years.
Our recreation department has developed several new programs for all ages. They
have increased their income this past year, although the department still needs
village support. It is may hope that this department will eventually become
self-supporting and have their own facilities. I'd like to urge everyone to
support the recreation department by using the programs and the SOCC and REC
boards by supporting their plans. If you have any suggestions, please contact
them.
All village departments and programs are overseen by our village administrator,
Dan Weir, and his secretary, Michelle Ashley. They do an excellent job making
sure that the equipment and materials are there for the various projects and
they help me run the village efficiently, making my job much easier.
With the continued support of Council, I'm looking forward to a prosperous and
productive 1996.
Adjourn.
Respectfully submitted,
Judith A. Selzer Clerk of Council
Approved: William A. McCune, Mayor

M. McCune - Any questions?
A. Aho - Has this been reviewed by Legal Council?
J. Lemire - Yes, this is a take off of the policy that was adopted by the
County, complied with rules and regulations.
D. Weir - By State law we have to alcohol and drug test the employeees that
drive motor vehicles or have a CDL. This portion is our drug and alcohol policy
for our employees.
A. Aho - The reason I ask, is that I questioned some of the wording. (Part B)
D. Weir - These are random drug and alcohol tests, we are part of the Health
Occupational Services Consortium, where they do the selection by social
security number, along with 250 other people.
B. Thompson - What happens if someone gets injured on a first offense?
What would happen to the employee?
J. Lemire - We would follow our personnel policy.
B. Thompson - What if they damage property, but no one is hurt, will they be
terminated?
J. Lemire - We would have to follow policy?
D. Weir - We have an obligation to an extent to help an individual who may have
a drug or alcohol.
B. Thompson - How may people are in these random tests?
D. Weir - 8
J. Lemire - Personnel policy does have language in it that we agree that drug
and alcohol abuse is a disease and that is required treatment. There is a big
section on that, these guidelines were suggested by the State to us.
D. Weir - The Federal Law requires specific statements in regards to this as a
program.
B. Thompson - So 4 out of the 8 will be tested?
D. Weir - It could be all, it could be 2, could be none of them. It depends on
how the selection goes.
J. Lemire - These are the minimum requirements by State Law.
M. McCune - The computer selects the people.
B. Thompson - What if you are on medicine?
M. McCune - They will ask you to bring all that in before your test.

OFFICIALS
D. Weir - The board needs to reorganize, there has to be a motion for this.
There is some confusion between the Administrator and the EEC. Board, the
director has to answer to one.
J. Lemire - The Rec. Board serves as an advisory board, it reviews and
addresses problems.
M. McCune - It is confusing between EEC. and SocC. Boards what meeting are we
having, some people are on both boards and it is run by the same person. When
the Rec. Board runs out of money they come to Council. They need to control
spending. In 1972 the board was established it was to support itself. They keep
saying they are making money, but not once have they ever paid and electric
bill, insurance, or any other utilities. If the Village has paid it all. I
recommend the Rec. Department pay 250 a month rent and we will put it into a
fund to go towards the new Rec. building. We never received a dime.
N. Stasny - We need to have a recommendation for the Rec. Board.
B. Cowles - What are the alternatives, we don not have votes?
M. McCune - There are 2 from the school, 3 from Council, they are appointed.
B. Thompson - How is confused arrangement, we have a board they have power.
M. McCune - Under the Ohio Revised Code the Rec. Board is set up so it has it’s
own money. Our Rec. Board shows no money.
B. Cowles - The Rec. Board can make money.
J. Lemire - We have to check the stature to eliminate confusion. If you want to
eliminate confusion, eliminate the Rec. Board. The SOCC Board can still be out
there to try and raise money for the center. The Rec. Board would be a
committee, like an advisory board.
B. Thompson - The Director would then answer to the Village Administrator.
D. Weir - According to the reorganization, the stature is still Rec. Board and
that is a problem.
T. Finger - How do other Rec. Boards raise money in other towns?
J. Lemire - They put it on a Levy.
B. Thompson - Their names are Joint Rec. district. Then you can have several
members from Council and the Board, they can put funds on the levies to be
voted.
J. Lemire - There is a joint district in the stature we do not have that, we
have our own Village Board so we have the worst of both worlds.
M. McCune - Read the Settles report and we will discuss it all in the meeting
on May 2, 1996.
J. it that a Councilman is appointed to a committee, goes to the meetings,
doesn’t have a vote but comes back with a recommendation to Council?
J. Lemire - Make sure the Rec. and SOCC Boards have some reports.

VISITORS COMMENTS:
M. Misnick - Came to Council about his written proposal for the annex of the
sewer line. Discussed the possibilities of an Entertainment Center located on
N. Market Street, approximately three acres adjacent to the land that the
Little League is building their new complex on. The Center will be a Family
oriented center, expressed that the center is needed. He explained that he was
working with the EPA to find out about the Water and Sewer regulations for the
center. Also, he explained what was going to be in the Center, Batting Cages,
Concession stands w/ pizza and pop and much more. Porta Johns can not be used
for a place like this on a year round basis, I don’t know what the little
league is going to do.
P. Fisher - My Husband is on the Little League Board and they are going to use
Porta John.
M. Misnick - Thanked Council for their time in listening to the proposal.
J. Lemire - First we just put 2 million into a new sewer plant, second you are
so far out you probably could not get annexed anyway. Third we would have to
run sewer lines out, which is approximately 1 mile out, at about 55 dollars a
foot, which is about a quarter of a million dollars.
M. Misnick - If the property is annexed the cost is to the property owned.
J. Lemire - If we were to put a sewer line to the property, yes the property
owners would have to put sewer on their property within two years.
M. Misnick - What other costs are there?
J. Lemire - Explained what the additional costs were, and what was involved.
M. Misnick - Would the 250 Thousand be split by the property owners?
J. Lemire - It would go by front footage. 2 to 3 years ago Harassments wanted
sewer lines, they tried the procedure but the residents were not interested.
M. Misnick - Can we get annexed?
J. Lemire - For an annexation the boundary lines have to touch it. Usually the
township contests it, normally townships do contest annexations.
M. Misnick - Is that the only route?
J. Lemire - That is the only route that the Village will allow.
T. Finger - Could they put in a Treatment Plant.
M. McCune - The EPA will not allow it.
M. Misnick - Is the railroad annexed?
M. McCune - The boundaries are 100 ft. on both sides of the railroad when it
leaves the Village it is then in the Township.
M. Misnick - Without annexation it is no go.
M. McCune - Yes, I am sorry that is the Village rule, somewhere we have to stop
and think about where the Village will be in 20 years, a lot of property will
be annexed.
A. Aho - Your request is not the only one.
J. Lemire - The Village can not make people annex, they have to come and ask
Council.
B. Thompson - Did you have a talk with the trustees, since it is their
property.
E. Flack - Also talk with the County Board of Health.
M. Misnick - The water line is so close to the surface, that is another problem
also with the EPA. They do not care where the water comes from as long as it
meets the standards.
M. McCune - For water, if you put a well out there, you will still have the
same problem.
M. Misnick CSo if we can’t get the sewer we can’t get the water. It would be
nice to be out there with the Little League.
Visitor - Asked about the status on Issue II Money.
M. McCune - Explained that we have not applied for Issue II Money.

E. Ward - Memo from the Solicitor explaining the predicament the Village
Council is in with the laws and requirements with the Rec. and the SOCC board,
also the hiring of the new director, he will be confused as to what
administration he should go to. The Rec board or the Village Administrator.
Right now the status in the ORC clearly states, if you have a REC board, they
can hire because they are a legislative group. The Rec board has the power to
raise funds, our Rec board has never been self funded or it has never been put
on a tax levies or raised bond monies. The Village Rec board has always come to
Council for funding, the Village has never wanted to give up control of the Rec
department.
T. Finger - We should not give up control of the Rec board as long as they are
not self supportive.
J. Lemire - My opinion is that we do away with the Rec board which is a body
that is empowered with stature in the ORC. Or we let the Rec become totally
self supportive.
M. McCune - If we dissolve the Rec board could they be an advisory board?
J. Lemire - There is no statute stating that the Rec board could not be a
committee or an advisory board, but we have to be careful of how we word what
the board will be called. If they are an advisory board they will be a
committee with no powers.
T. Finger - The other school of thought is we keep the Rec board and they
become totally self sufficient.
B. Thompson - If they are self funded they can put levies on and can generate
funding.
J. Lemire - We have a confusing mess which should be straightened out buy
making an Ordinance which conforms with the laws.
B. Thompson - I really do not think the Rec board understands the ramifications
of Jerry’s research.
M. McCune - We will meet with the Rec board on June 6 at 8:00 p.m. to discuss
if we the Village will be in control or the Rec become self funded. We became
responsible for the Rec funds because the State Auditor came in and said that
someone had to responsible for the funds. So we took care of the money, making
the Rec department accountable for their money. The Village has always given
the Rec department funds for capital, utilities, insurance and salaries.
K. Fertig - If we divorce the Village from the Rec department it would make
them accountable for their funds.
T. Finger - For the meeting between the Council and the Rec, can we have
something put together in regards to what the Village is actually spending on
the Rec department (PERS, insurance, salaries etc.)
B. Thompson - Discussed the problem with the tennis courts, concerning the
condition they are in now. On November 27, 1974 the school board accepted a
tennis court from the Jefferson Village Council. The school board accepted an
agreement to assume and maintain the responsibility of the courts for 15 years.
In 1986 they meet the terms and carried it ten years longer. There are four
main uses for the courts:
1. Gym classes
2. Tennis team
3. Community center
4. General public
Two of the main uses are used in the Village. The Courts are being used by the
community and safety is a main concern right now. The Village had helped before
to fix it, I feel we should go into a partnership with the school and fix the
courts again.
K. Fertig - Voiced his opinion on what the Village had spent to build an
maintain the court and his concern that every time the court needs fixed they
will come back to the Village. He agreed we have to help the school fix it.
B. Cowles - Brought up that we exchange the fees they charge us for the use of
the building to fixing the court.
M. McCune - Has the school given us a cost figure before we discuss it anymore,
we should get the cost figures on what needs to be done.

2nd by Thompson
Roll: Aho, yea; Cowles, yea; Finger, nay; Thompson, yea; Ward, yea.
C. Baxely - Voiced her opinion that Council should be more open with the
public, stated that she would have liked to haven seen the appraisal of the
building and she was shocked out of her shoes at the price and the way that is
was arrived at, using square footage of a comparable building. Wanted to see
figures on what the roof was going to cost.
J. Lemire - Explained the changes in the contract and what it consisted of.
Also stated that the Village of Jefferson and Thornes Bi Lo will have a
forcible agreement, which will be a building contract. The issue on financing,
there have been two firms contact me on bonds and notes. They are Bucker &
Eckler of Columbus and Calfee Halter & Griswold of Cleveland. When you use
public funds by issuing a municipal department, you need to have an outside
attorney from a firm that the Community respects. Bucker & Eckler and Calfee
Halter and Griswold recommend we issue notes instead of bonds, notes are short
term, bonds are long term obligation The best way to issue notes to finance the
project as when the project is completed go to bonds which is long term
financing, a Ordinance would have to be passed for this.
There are three ways to place the note.
1.   Place notes with a bank that you have a working relationship with, without
any shopping around.
2.    Take all local banks in town and give them a chance to make the best
offer on the interest rates.
3.    Put notes issuing on a list that circulates through the State of Ohio to
get a much broader bidding on the notes insurance.
The Buckler & Eckler Firm services for doing notes is $750.00 and the Calfee,
Halter and Griswold firm charged $3,000.00 for the same work. My recommendation
is to use the Buckler & Eckler Firm. Let me know what route you would like to
go with this.
P. Fisher - The Key Capital Market, which is through Key Corp. a gentleman
named Stephen Szanto came to the office and gave some prices on what it would
approximately cost and the best way. He said to start out the Village should
use notes to buy the building. Then after the building is purchased and what
the cost figures are to bring the building to useable standards
P. Fisher - for the Village. The best thing is to transfer the bonds, notes are
for the first year. This is just one banks ideas.
A. Aho - Should Council recommend a bond Council or a note Council.
J. Lemire - The company that issues notes will most likely do the bonds, notes
float and bonds are fixed.
Motion by Thompson to retain the Buckler & Eckler firm for the note issue.
2nd by Ward
Roll: Aho, yea; Cowles, yea; Finger, yea; Thompson, yea; Ward, yea.
J. Lemire - Buckler & Eckler will draw up an Ordinance that will authorize the
issue of the notes. Council will then vote on the Ordinance. When the Ordinance
is passed we will have to wait 30 days to make it legal. During the 30 days
window the citizens of the Village can make a referendum to challenge the
Council decision. Then the decision would have to be put on a ballet for the
citizens of the Village to decide if the money should be spent.

Regular Session
C. Rippons - How did Council get the Seven Hundred Thousand Dollar figure
needed for the Community Center?
A. Aho - To purchase the building is Five Hundred and Fifty Thousand, the other
One Hundred Fifty Thousand was to allow the Village additional costs for
maintenance, we will be getting some money from SOCC.
M. McCune - The Seven Hundred Thousand Dollars is the max figure we are going
to use. It depends on the expenses. We will go ten years on the loan for the
building.
A. Aho - Our master plan for the Village is the business district and it is in
the center of town. The Thornes Bi Lo, when it moves the building will be
empty. It is adjacent to the town hall. A good location for the community
Center.
C. Rippons - What major work needs done on the building?
M. McCune - The roof needs worked on. We have had estimates from 30 to 50
thousand on it. We have a 26 page appraisal on the break down of the Thornes Bi
Lo building. We are buying the building for the Community and the Recreation
Department.
M. Lehnert - Expressed her feelings that the Village has been waiting years for
a Community Center. There is a lot of people who have donated time and money
for the building. There is a lot of people who want this for the Community.
H. Childs - I am not opposed to the Community Center as long as it is self
supportive. I also just wanted to let people vote on it if they want it.
M. McCune - If the Community feels the Council and Mayor have done something
wrong in buying the building, there is a procedure to put it on the ballot. We
are going to continue as Council to buy the building, because if we do not the
building will be bought by someone else.

forestry, and we are required to have a proclamation and a Arbor Day Program.

D. Weir - The trees in the Village all have root stress. What happens is the
root system develops as much as it can develop. When the tree starts to grow it
puts stress on the roots and the roots can not keep up with the tree, which is
why the trees die from the top down.
A. Aho - Trimming and pruning is not the answer.
M. McCune - The Village will take care of the trees in the tree lawn.

Finger - Questioned if we have to stay with the ten dollars per read for finals
and a five dollars per read for all swapped meters because the water company
was told by the PUCO.
M. McCune - Quoted that Janet Henery told Dan Weir that the Water Company is
not supposed to be charging those prices. The PUCO never told the Water Company
to charge us. We are going to pursue the water company.
Finger - We have a contract at 60c~ per read with no reference to the extra
charges.
M. McCune - If we follow the contract to the letter then they are going to go
back to quarterly reads because that is what the contract states. It would be
quarterly reads instead of every two months. We are going to limp along with
the agreement, then when we get them at the table we will continue to talk to
them. I am going to put the water rate case right out to the public. We are
trying to negotiate with Consumers Ohio Water Company over rates. We could get
nowhere with them, so we went with the procedure of intervening which cost us
money. We have done everything to help solve the problem. The PUCO does not
want to be the bad guy, Consumers Ohio Water does not want to be the bad guy,
either. The Intervener we hired after we have spent all this money, says maybe
we better negotiate with them(Consumers Ohio Water). I think if we sat down to
negotiate we are backing down and Consumers Ohio Water is telling us now, if we
do not negotiate they are going to hit us with a rate shock. Twenty four
percent right off the bat. And we the Villages will be the bad guys because we
caused them to do it. If we sat down and talked with them, the whole rate
increase would only be thirty two percent.

little roads in the Village are not made for trucks.

Roll: Aho, yea; Cowles, yea; Finger, yea; Stasny, yea; Thompson, yea; Ward, yea
Rob Kagler and Jack Howe of the Ashtabula County Planning Commission presented
to Council the plan of the Ashtabula County Transportation plan. They explained
the routes, what loops they would take in each city. Told Council that
Jefferson would be the hub of the South County and every two hours there would
be routes coming and going in Jefferson. This is a public transit and could not
provide the service that the Community Center does, but this transportation
system provides service to everyone. The transportation does get State funding,
but 40% of the funding will come from the local communities. The cost to the
Village would be about four thousand dollars annually. The fairs would range
from .50 cents to $1.50.
Aho - How are you interfacing with act 2000? We are being solicited by both
groups.
Howe - Act 2000 has twelve goal areas and transportation is just a small part.
Transportation is anyway you move. The Countys comprehensive plan has three
parts: Land use, Services, Transportation. We have been meeting with the County
Planning Commission and we are trying to make it one and have all parts of the
Community involved together.
Ward - If any part in the Jefferson area does not want to participate in the
system where would the money come from to support the system.
Howe - It is done through public support money, would come from the communities
that support It.
M. McCune - Said this would be turned over to our service committee and we will
let you know if we are interested.
VISITORS COMMENTS:
B. Flack - Thanked Dan Weir and the Streets Department for coming out and
cleaning the road ditch on North Spruce Street.

2nd by Thompson

yea.

Directors job description. Because in the title it is Rec Director/Social
Service Director. Do we need social service on our job title?
D. Weir - Stated that in our paper work, that is how the job description was

J. Lemire - Said we could redescribe our title of the Rec Director. It is
within Councils power to redefine the Directors job description. Take out
Social Service Director if it is what Council wants. We can look at the
Ordinance and modify it.

SAFETY:
No Report.
BUILDINGS AND LAND USE:
M. McCune - Council has received a copy of all the conversions in the Village
of Jefferson. This is your answer to the questions. When a person goes to buy
the house that has been converted, if the conversion is illegal, before the
house can be sold it has to be turned back to the way it was before the
conversion.
D. Weir - We received calls from Realtors when a house is for sale with
questions regarding houses when it was converted, can it be converted if it is
grand fathered in? We always tell them the right procedures of what to do.
J. Lemire - What is illegal in conversions is any house that has been converted
after the Ordinance in October of 1976. Our stature provides for continuing
existence or continuing use unless they are abandoned . If you stop using, you
can lose that preexisting use.
B. Cowles - We could have a monthly or yearly update that comes into the
office.
M. McCune - It would be like a safety inspection. But, then in a sense we would
be condoning the conversions and we do not want that to happen. Then if we
inspect one house we better inspect them all.
J. Lemire - It would then be time consuming and costly if you get into a
routine house inspection, on top of the alleged violation inspections.
M. McCune - Basically, if you are going to do inspections as far as multi-
family the we may just as well do the building inspections too.
T. Finger - Should we change our Zoning mal)?
J. Lemire - No, it should not be changed. They have a preexisting usage, the
district does not change and we should keep a file on this.
T. Finger - We keep doing a count of properties that fall into the RD
classification. These 37 homes keep falling out and do not get counted into the
percentage of properties in the Village that are truly RD. or being used as RD.
J. Lernire - If the Village was challenged on that, we do not have enough RD.
We could bring that to defend the Village. So these are legal nonconforming
uses.
C. Baxley - It is also clear that if the structure is destroyed more than 60 %
by fire, they revert to the original classification.
M. McCune - That overrides the grandfather clause and is in our zoning text.
D. Weir - We have a letter from Burgess & Niple and they have had conversations
with ODOT regarding the truck route. In the letter it states that it is
unlikely functional classification revisions will be approved prior to the year
2000. We will not see anything happen until then.
B. Cowles - Is there any way we can study the potential or developing that land
for light industry on one side of Cucumber Street to help pay for the route.
M. McCune - We have tried every avenue for funding. When you propose industry
for part of it they are not interested in funding unless you use all the land.
B. Cowles - Why can’t we as a village try to get industries to come into the
Village. We can advertise what we have to offer, we should create and develop
the property the way we want and solicit for industry.
M. McCune - Other than basically making it marketable, is by putting a road
there so there is frontage then you have to put in sewer, gas, water and
electric. There is no other way to market the property. This would take a lot
of money to get it done.
B. Cowles - We have no room to grow with industry that is also not helping us
with the truck route. We have been talking for two years now on rerouting the
trucks from the center of town. I have brought it up before about putting signs
up on Route 11, rerouting the trucks. But nothing ever seems to get done.
M. McCune - We are working, trying to relieve the problem in the center of town
with a new traffic signal and setting back some parking spaces. This will help
temporarily.

W.   Herndon - Representing SOCC. Board, wanted to thank everyone and Council
for the support of the Thornes Building. Also I am behind Council one hundred
percent of their decision with the Community Center.
M.   McCune - We finally have our Community Center after many years. It took
total support by the Community to get the building.
V. Butcher - I am here on behalf of the S.O.C.C. Board and support of our
Community
Center.
SERVICE:
A. Aho - Mark surveyed the Seniors that are using the Senior Van. They like the
point to point service and the price structure. They stated that if we got into
a scheduled service they would like to have the service we have now continued.
When I look at the planned service myself I still question the plan. Point to
point is more effective for the individual needs in our community, for those
who do not have transportation. The county is trying to create a scheduled
service on a county wide basis. I am wondering why we are trying to finance it
by the Villages in the County. When all we will be is a transfer point, It
seems like all the residents in the County should help pay such as townships
and other Villages and cities. They are looking at a three year program. I do
not think we need three years to see if it will work. Therefore, my
recommendation is no to accept the program as it has been presented to us.
B. Cowles - It takes a lot to absorb everything, it has taken a lot to plan
everything. I think it is also important to save our natural resources where we
can use buses for work and pleasure on a more regular basis. I understand that
it will take a long time for something like this to happen and we have to take
it step by step. Maybe this is the first step. Is there a long range plan to
have a bigger system in the future?
R. Kagler - We have been looking into the future trying to get more support and
trying to get more grants. The only way to get funding right now is to go to
the County. We are hoping in the future that we have the entire County support
and the program will grow.
A. Aho - In speaking of natural resources; first of all people have to be able
to get on the bus, and what we have now is a bus that goes to the houses and
picks them up and takes them to the mall. Our trips to the mall have been
booked, we may have to expand that service. That hardly justifies a scheduled
service.
B. Cowles - I think you misunderstood what I meant. I was saying that this
would be a great way to conserve fuel. I think the transportation system is
better off serving a larger mass of people. I am not totally convinced we need
to spend the money.
M McCune - At this point in time we do not have to give our answer. It is
something to think about and if the transportation system will be used.
FORESTRY:
A. Aho - Discussed master plan with our tree planning program. In our master
plan, we have large trees for shade and I can not agree with that. There is too
many problems in maintenance and root problems. Our biggest problem right now
is our mature trees and we will continue to have the problems if we keep on
planting trees that when they mature are seventy to eighty foot trees.
Ornamental trees are what urban foresters recommend for utilities and electric
lines. These trees will grow twenty five or thirty foot. The trees we should
try to keep away from are the big trees.
RECREATION:
E. Ward - Discussed a new idea regarding the Rec. Scholarship Fund. It will be
put on the back burner for more ideas. I will take any new ideas or comments.
Told Council about Christine Litwilwer’s seminar summary. Thanked everyone
involved in the Thones Building.
SAFETY:

building. We do not have any sidewalks up to the new building.
D. Weir - There is a process you have to go through for being able to put
sidewalks down, it is a special assessment. The residents will have to agree to
pay their portion.

Thornes. We are going through with listing the notes for public sale through
the Ohio Municipal League. We will get bids for the note and obtain the lowest
interest rate. Our Bond Council is Buckler & Eckler they are out of Columbus,

RESOLUTION OF JOINT BOARD OF OAKDALE UNION CEMETERY DATED DECEMBER 30, 1996
A RESOLUTION REPEALING ORDINANCE NO. 1690 OF THE JOINT BOARD OF THE OAKDALE
UNION CEMETERY PERTAINING TO THE MANAGEMENT OF OAKDALE UNION CEMETERY
Whereas, the Joint Board of the Jefferson Village - Jefferson Township Joint
Union Cemetery believes that the management of the Oakdale Union Cemetery is
best left to the Trustees of that Cemetery; and
Whereas, on August 5, 1985 , the Joint Board of the Jefferson Village -
Jefferson Township Joint Union Cemetery adopted Ordinance 1690 which
established various restrictions on the sale of cemetery lots and on interment;
and
Whereas, the restrictions contained in Ordinance 1690 conflict with ongoing
policies of the Trustees of the Oakdale Union Cemetery.
Now, Therefore, be it ordained by Joint Board of the Jefferson Village -
Jefferson Township Joint Union Cemetery, that:
Section 1: Ordinance 1690 and the contents shall thereof are hereby repealed.
Section 2: That this Resolution shall take effect and be in full force at the
earliest period allowed by law.
Vote

State of the Village Address:
Mayor W. McCune - 1997 will be a busy year, especially for the Recreation
Department with the purchase and remodeling of the Bi Lo Building. Our
Community Center Director, Marc Glotzbecker has many excellent ideas for
additional programs in our larger facility. We look forward to the utilization
by the whole community of the new Community Center, which should be open by
late Spring or early Summer. At that time, the Village Offices will return to
the Town Hall for the convenience of Village residents.
The Sewer Department continues to meet EPA requirements and do everyday
maintenance at the plant. The repairs to the addition of water retention tanks
and digester have increased our capacity for development well into the future.
The Maplewood and Cedar Street sewer line replacements have removed the influx
of storm water to our sanitary sewers in that area. We plan to replace the
sanitary line on Market Street upon receipt of an applied for grant. Once this
project is completed, the sanitary sewer line problems in that area should be
eliminated. We will continue to repair storm water intrusions as mandated by
the EPA.
The Village streets and sidewalks are in fair condition. The repairs and
maintenance programs will continue by the members of our hard working Street
Department.
The Safety forces, both Fire and Police, are continuing their good jobs for the
residents of this Village. We are budgeting for needed equipment replacement in
both departments.
The Administrative Office is finally running smoothly with the addition of our
new Clerk, Patty Fisher. Her dedication and knowledge of computers has helped
immensely in the everyday operations of the Village. Her helpfulness to
everyone os refreshing. The sewer billing is running more smoothly and, as of
this month, payroll is again being done in-house. Our Administrator, Dan Weir,
has taken on additional responsibilities with the Water Task Force and
Recreation Department, but continues to handle the everyday operation of the
Village with expertise.
The legislation has been started for the repurchase of our water system. This
will stabilize the rates and also bring quality service to the customers. We
plan to finance the purchase of the water system by extending water lines for
future development and increasing the customer base.
All in all, the Village of Jefferson, Ohio, is in fair condition and our
finances are adequate to handle all projects on this sixth day of January,
1997.
J. Kusar - Asked about the Water system, how long will it take?
Mayor W. McCune - A couple of years.
A. Aho - Mentioned that we are not alone in taking back the water system. He
has noted articles of other places doing this in the paper.
Adjourn.
Respectfully Submitted,   Approved:
                                                           
    William A. McCune, Mayor
Patricia A. Fisher,
Clerk/Treasurer

annexation. The Jeff. Dev. Corp. wants to put together an agreement between the
Village and the Township that no annexation is required for sewer. They want to
develop the land outside the Village, they want me as Mayor to appoint someone
from Council and someone from the Township to J.E.D.D. The main drift from the
whole this is sewer lines.

good for them but I do not think it is a good agreement for the Village of
Jefferson.

councils feeling on this?
