B. Thompson - Had a questions regarding the Salary Ordinance for the Clerk and
wanted clarification.
J. Lemire - I discussed the Ordinance this afternoon with Patty. It is a bunch
of extensive changes. I told her to hold on to the Ordinance till we had a
chance to discuss the Ordinance further. In its current form, I think we need
to clarify where the Council is going. Before we do any modifications.
T. Finger - Should we table the Ordinance or have a open discussion here?
J. Lemire - I think this is an appropriate time to discuss this, the whole
issue in the pay increase is because there seems to be a lot of conflict and
undesciseveness about the issue. We have to be on the same page if we are going
to get any further with this issue. Let me just point out as your legal advisor
on the whole subject of pay increases. In your packets there is a memo from the
Law Director of the Village of Oak Harbor on in-term pay increases for the
Clerk Treasurer dated February 6, 1997, also there is a document dated April
30, 1993 for in-term increases for Village Officials and another document dated
1983 opinions on the same subject. For the last meeting I gave you a memorandum
stating my position. I believe that the in-term pay increases for the Clerk
Treasurer were unlawful in violation of the statute. That memo came up after
the first reading of the Clerks pay increase in salary. Some people raised the
issue if it was legal, that is when Dan called me to do the research. Concluded
from my research that given the state of law right now, we did not have the
authority to give Patty a in-term pay increase. And I have taken a look at the
other things in the packet, my position still remains as it was in the
memorandum. I am going to try to outline why that is with that confusing law.
There are two statutes that govern this whole subject. One, the Ethics section
102.03 of the Ohio Revised Code, the whole section deals with ethic matters and
provides for the Attorney General to issue opinions, to give public officials
guidelines on what is and what is not ethical. The ethics of that statute is
that anytime there is the appearance of a conflict or where someone is
controlling something that would lead to a benefit. The official is in that
position where they can make a decision that would lead to a possible benefit
to the official. This is a conflict of interest situation, which is a violation
of the Ethical Statutes. Most of the opinions that are out there are talking
about wether or not in-term pay increases to a Clerk Treasurer or any other
Village Official. Does the person who is giving the pay raise have some say so
on weather or not they should get that pay raise?
J. Lemire - Some of the ethical analysis in that section of the revised code
and opinions clearly say that in the case of the Clerk and the Mayor do not
have any power over voting decisions. There is nothing unethical about them
having a in-term pay increase, but there is a whole other section of law that
we have to deal with. Other sections of the Revised Code, one of which is
731.07 a real simple statute. That says you can not do it, you can not give in-
term pay increases to Village Officials. The Ethical Statute interprets the
Clerk could have a in-term pay raise that wouldn’t violate any ethical
statutes, but then you have Section 731.07 which says you can’t. B. Thompson -
A question, would some of the argument for or against in-term pay raises if the
Official in question was elected or just an employee?
J. Lemire - It really does not matter. The issue from the Ethical analysis is,
does the person getting the pay raise have the ability to cause that pay raise
to happen or have an impact on that decision. As long as from a ethical point
of view the Official can not effect that decision because they are not a voting
body. They are not in violation of the Ethical breach. If you look at 731.07 it
reads, The salary of any Official of the City shall not increase or decrease
during the term he was elected or appointed. This section does not prohibit the
payment of any increase cost of continuing to provide the identical benefits
provided to a officer at the commencement of his term of office. 731.07 of any
officer of the City shall not be increased or diminished during the term for
which he was elected. The Village Clerk is a Official that was elected and is
covered by this section of the law. There was a case that was decided back in
1982, it was a court of appeals case. It was the Village of Bellview versus
Beil a case which was out of Richmond County. In that case they were simply
arguing under home rule concepts under our constitution there are some elements
of local call that the State can not interface with, you have home rule power.
This court of appeals ruled in this case, that the State Statute (731.07) was
overstepping the bounds of the legislation. There for this current statute says
you can not give in-term pay increases to the Village Officials. This court
says that this is not constitutional because of home rules and these are areas
only the local officials should consider and should be limited to the local
government not by the legislature in Columbus.
B. Thompson - Is this where the Officials actually voted on the increase while
they were in office?
J. Lemire - I believe that to be true. The bottom line is the court of appeals
said you could grant in-term pay increases. So this crowd forgot about what
731.07 meant, because now we have one opinion on record that said we could do
that, no matter what the statute says. There was another case in 1992 Creed
versus Hubbard, it is noticed because it is more recent. But more importantly
it comes out of our appeals district 11th court. Any case that is decided in
our common pleas will go to the 11th district of appeals. In this case there
was a question about a Mayor getting a in-term pay increase in a town in
Trumbull County. In the Court of Common Pleas level the pay increase was
approved, but at the Court of Appeals level which is higher up, they said no,
that it was improper to grant such a pay increase because of 731.07. This Court
of Appeals decision was appealed to the Ohio Supreme Court and the Ohio Supreme
Court refused to listen to the appeal. They can decide if they want to, to hear
the case or not, and they decided no to take the case up on appeals, they
simply did not want to listen to the case. Which disrupt this opinion to get
good law. We now have a split. We have the 11th district saying Mayors can not
get in-term raises. The Mayors position is almost the same as the Clerk. But
they are not part of the legislative authority that governs pay increases. So
we have the 1982 case that says you can have a in-term pay increase and a 1992
11th district court saying no to the in-term pay increase. That was the status
of the law until recently. In 1994 the same citizen who challenged the Mayors
increase demanded that the Mayor give back the money. That he was paid
deficiency rendered. This case was litigated all the way up to the Court of
Appeals. The Court of Appeals ruled that the Mayor did not have to give back
the money. That he had good faith, reason to believe that there was a
legitimate argument for the increase. This decision was appealed to the Ohio
Supreme Court and in 1996 the Ohio Supreme Court ruled that the Mayor had an
argument to support his belief that it was legal.
J. Lemire - He in good faith accepted the money and did not have to give it
back. Because there wasn’t any bad faith involved in the payment. The Supreme
Court didn’t say they were ligament pay increases. It simply said it already
had endorsed a 11th district decision by refusing to hear the 1992 appeal. But
on the issue of wether the Mayor had to pay the money back, they didn’t
overturn that decision. Let the old decision stand. The Mayor had a reason to
accept the money in good faith reasons. We are in the 11th district area in
this district it is in question that law in this subject is that you can not
give a Mayor and by my status the Clerk a pay raise because they are elected
officials. The Ethics commission based on where they are coming from, he stated
that they only look at the 102 statute. They said that no way is their opinion
that in fact it is not a ethical breach doesn’t mean that it is legal and
approvable type pay raise. They are supporting that it is not a ethical lap to
allow such a pay increase to go through. We have two splits of opinions, the
11th district and Richmond Court of Appeals. We should in my opinion follow the
11th district and in my opinion we can not give an elected officials in-term
pay increases. We are in a district where there has been clear law and we are
stuck with it. That led to how we find a way to work within the law and to give
Patty the additional compensation because she puts in so much time and works so
hard. Look at what the Clerks duties are and if she is doing things that are
not statutory mandated. There is nothing wrong with the creating of this
position. That in fact provides for her to do other things that she is not
statutory mandated to do. And pay her for those services. This has come up in
another local Village, they came up with the same conclusion to solve this
problem. They passed a Ordinance creating a separate position handling Utility
Billing. It doesn’t appear that Utility Billing is a mandatory duty for the
Clerk. Therefore if you want to compensate the Clerk for all her work she has
done and do it by law. We are not giving her a Clerk pay increase, but we are
letting her perform another job that someone else could be hired to do and if
she refused to do it voluntary you will have to hire someone to do it. Anyway,
the only issue is that in conflict in office. The basic idea of office in
conflict is that one office supervises the other, and so therefore that Patty
reports to the Village Administrator. My opinion still stands as I wrote in my
memorandum.
B. Thompson - That was very comprehensive.
T. Finger - There was so much information around that, brought confusion.
J. Lemire - The courts’ themselves are confused, even they differ.
B. Cowles - Will this increase bring Patty up closer and equal with everyone?
J. Lemire - I do not know that, but there was suggestion that we do that for
her work and motivation.
D. Weir - I think and this is my opinion, she does a good job, and has a lot of
responsibility and she is underpaid.
T. Finger - In the Finance meeting we have talked about a Ordinance re-setting
the wages for the Clerk based on where the Clerks job requirement by statute
are. That is one issue. It should be put in the books for future reference. The
second part is now that we have it in the books can Patty get the increase.
Based on what I have heard we can not give her that increase. But I still think
that Ordinance needs to be on the books before the next election.
J. Lemire - We can not change the Ordinance for this term. But it can be
changed prior to the next Election.
B. Thompson - I think we have a route in which we can take now and I have no
problem with that.
J. Lemire - In creating a Ordinance for it to be effective for the next term, I
will need more information on what you want to draft it up.
T. Finger - There is only one problem, then it looks like in Ordinance 2116
that we granted a illegal raise with the 6 ½ percent pick-up with P.E.R.S.
J. Lemire - In the research we have done, I would question wether or not if
that was appropriate.
I was probably a violation.
Mayor W. McCune - That was done in 1994 when they added the P.E.R.S. It was
done over a two or three year period. We didn’t do it last year. It was done in
a percentage rate.
B. Thompson - That is not necessary interpreted as a pay raise. It is a benefit
as apposed to a direct increase in the salary.
Mayor W. McCune - It is basically a no cost. It doesn’t cost the Village
anything or the employee anything. It would have been spent one way or the
other. Either by given salary and taken back out in the percentage or by being
paid directly in the percentage. Those Ordinances concerning P.E.R.S. started
in 1994.
D. Weir - That Ordinance was done based on the A.G.S. opinion done in 1993.
J. Lemire - That was when the research on State Law began. These laws had not
really been checked and throughly researched until most recently. Because there
was not all these bodies of law and ethics law, and court of appeals law, also
the County law. This was done when the Council believed there was no problem in
doing it. The practical point of view is you have a Clerk that probably feels
she is working for below minimum wage when she adds up her time. And that is an
issue that should be addressed. Or you risk the Clerk retention back to a time
limit that is reasonable to the pay.
C. Baxley - Patty is conscientious and all that but should we rewrite the job
description.
J. Lemire - The problem is the position is statutory defined. She is accepted
as a elected official.
This body really doesn’t have the authority to tell what to do or not to do.
A. Aho - That is why I think we are better putting in the position as Utility
Clerk. Because it still gives Council and the Administration some control.
J. Lemire - If she took the Utility Clerks position she would be under the
Administrator.
Mayor W. McCune - What are we going to do, let’s not just drop this issue.
T. Finger - We will go to a Finance Committee meeting and solve two issues. One
will be a Ordinance to increase the salary for the Clerk before the next
election. The second part will be creating the Utility Clerk position.
W. Herndon - When will you be doing all these changes. I hope not six months
from now. If it is not done soon, you might lose your Clerk.
B. Cowles - Will her hours cut down in the future?
P. Fisher - Right now we are doing a lot of changes. We have put in a new
budgetary program.
The first of the year we brought back the payroll and we are putting in a new
utility program for the sewer billing and for the water in the future, if we gt
the water system back.
Mayor W. McCune - I think things are coming together with work the work that
Patty is doing and the long hours. Number one, she doesn’t pound her chest. She
took back the payroll. It was done in an hour and a half last time. It is been
done right and to date. ADP couldn’t get it done over the phone in an hour and
a half. It took them three days and it was wrong.
Mayor W. McCune - She basically is putting a lot of hours in. And the computer
now has all the information it needs to do it quickly. She is now on the next
phase in the programing. Eventually she will get a breather. It will not be
along one, I do not think there will ever be a slow period in the office. But
it has been so intense. If we amend this Ordinance, this position will make her
responsible to the Administrator. We will have to pass this Ordinance as an
emergency. We can not let this Ordinance go past April 1. Or we will shut down
the Village wages. We can not do a Ordinance as an emergency on the third
reading. It needs a 30 day window after it is passed if we do not do it as a
emergency.
J. Lemire - We do an Ordinance as an emergency it eliminates the 30 day window.
30 days after the Ordinance is passed it becomes effective. There is two ways
not to have three readings, one is be waving Council rules. That Ordinance
becomes effective 30 days in the future. Emergency Ordinances are different ,
the need to continue the work force would follow under emergency. So you
probably have the authority to adopt it as a emergency, which means it becomes
effective right away. Or you can adopt it tonight after waving the third
reading. My opinion, there is enough of a problem to designate this as an
emergency. We can table the Ordinance to get away from the issue and adopt it
on the second reading as a emergency then you would eliminate the question.

A. Aho - We had a Forestry Committee meeting tonight at 7:00 p.m. Our Arbor Day
recognition will be April 25th 1997 at 12:00 Noon in the Courthouse Park. The
program will have a presentation on the proper planting maintenance and care of
trees. We will plant two Crab trees donated by Tree Tyme Nursery. The trees
will be planted next to the Case property on the west side next to the
fountain. They will be planted in the north and south end of the property to
help balance the trees in the park. Also in the meeting we discussed the
request of the Rotary Club with the removal of the Crab Apple Tree in the park.
It was agreed upon the removal of the Crab Tree because of the unbalance in the
architectural of the trees and the area. The tree is to remain on the green
until the middle of May after the blossom. In the Fall we will still plan our
dead wood removal and the Fall planting of trees.

have we made that decision as a Council? I don’t feel that we have.

the formula to come to an agreeable price.
T. Finger - We have a problem. As a member of Council I don’t believe I have
ever agreed to proceeding.
Mayor W. McCune - You proceeded to sign the agreement with Brickler & Eckler
and it was never hidden to you that is what we were doing.
T. Finger - When I go to my lengthily discussion before the third reading.
Mayor W. McCune - Which was what I had told you, I wouldn’t sign a agreement
until Council were comfortable with it. And I have not signed a agreement yet.
We are going for a joint setting with Geneva, Geneva-on-the-Lake and myself

proceed.
T. Finger - Without any input from Council?
Mayor W. McCune - You already had the input when we passed the three readings
in the Ordinance of hiring Brickler & Eckler.
T. Finger - No, I disagree.
Mayor W. McCune - If all of you were not voting on proceeding to purchase the
Water Company, what were you voting on?
T. Finger - We voted on the Ordinance, as a member of Council I have not agreed
to proceed to buy the Water Company.
A. Aho - The Ordinance we passed says that we would look into a study.
Mayor W. McCune - The only place the studies came from was the people that were
saying we were spending 250 thousand to do a study. There is no reason to do a
study. It is a procedure to buy back our water system.
J. Lemire - Normally when you appropriate property there would need to be a
Ordinance passed to go forward the appropriation of property.
T. Finger - It said we were going to hire them to study and advise us on the
financing of purchasing the Water Company.
Mayor W. McCune - Brickler & Eckler are a law firm they don’t do studies. They
are lawyers, engineers do studies.
J. Lemire - Retaining services of Brickler & Eckler Attorneys. Whereas the
Village of Jefferson is considering the possibility of acquiring the water
distribution facilities to serve the residents.
Whereas the firm of Brickler & Eckler has experience in advising public bodies
in connection with the acquisition and financing of public water facilities.
Now therefore be it resolved by the Village Council of the Village of Jefferson
that: The law firm of Brickler & Eckler is hereby retained to represent and
advise the Village of Jefferson with respect to acquisition and financing of
public water supply facilities. I would not read this as a decision.
Mayor W. McCune - It will come back to you when the price is established. It
will then come back to Council to basically purchase at that price and continue
to negotiate or whatever.
J. Lemire - What was meant, we are going to proceed in the direction of buying
the water company. But there has been no formal decision made by anybody at
this table to actually purchase. We are proceeding along the path. When the
minutes say we are going to proceed with buying the Water Company that may be
strongly worded. Because this Council hasn’t fully committed itself to doing
that yet. We have hired a law firm to advise us. And the group has decided to
go forward toward that effort. But the ultimate decision to actually purchase
it has not been made.
T. Finger - That is what I was struggling with, that in the wording. It sounds
like we have made up our mind, lets buy it and lets go.
Mayor W. McCune - We basically made up our mind that there is no study needed.
The study was done along time ago.
T. Finger - For me as a Council person and a member of Utilities, I would like
to see some facts and figures.
Mayor W. McCune - You will get them because Brickler & Eckler already has them
in hand. But they will not release the funding until we sign the agreement to
continue. I understand the concern. I will not sign the agreement until Council
is comfortable with it. And we all will sign the agreement together, all the
Villages. But the study to buy the water system shows it is feasible to go
ahead.
B. Cowles - We are proceeding with Legal Council. We are moving with Legal
Council to a more serious direction.
J. Lemire - In order for this Village to buy this utility it will take a
Ordinance passed by this body
(Council).
T. Finger - The only reason that I questioned this is a public foreman and the
press has said certain things and there are people who are arguing and saying
us crooked politicians made their minds to purchase. I am just a little
sensitive to make sure we are in agreement where we are headed.
B. Thompson - The articles you are referring to, Do not include the fact that
the municipalities in the State of Ohio have the right to take the course of
action to obtain the law firm. I am satisfied with the process up to this
point. Because we have been advised all along.
Mayor W. McCune - I should have said to proceed in the direction of buying the
water company.
Minutes to the last meeting were approved with the corrections of. We are going
to proceed in the direction of buying the Water Company.

Mayor W. McCune - We have had about three different parties looking at the
roof. We have had Brinningers Roofing, Building Technologies and the Engineers.
They completely inspected the roof. Part of the roof is in excellent shape. The
main roof itself needs replaced. They suggested we do it as soon as possible to
save the integrity of the building. Also, we have a letter from CT Consultants
stating a complete replacement of the roof is required. Building Technologies
gave us information stated we did not have to completely remove the entire
roof. They stated the insulation was still dry, if we got to it soon enough, so
it didn’t get saturated.
B. Cowles - What exactly is this Ordinance saying we need to do with the roof?
Mayor W. McCune - We are basically going to go by the engineers suggestions to
the roof. Each bidder will have the same level of playing field. Everyone will
know what is being bid on when the bids go out.
J. Lemire - The statute that is quoted in the heading of the Ordinance is a
statute that authorizes an emergency to proceed without bidding.
Mayor W. McCune - We are going to get prices for bids on the roof.
D. Weir - I would think that before we did anything, if we need the complete
removal of the roof, we would want justification. I would want the engineers to
take another look and let us know if it is absolutely necessary to replace the
entire roof. We will solicit the bids out to everyone.
I myself feel uncomfortable recommending we replace pieces and parts of the
roof. If we are going to put the investment of putting thousands and thousands
of dollars on the interior of the building, I think we should replace the roof.
Mayor W. McCune - We will put everything out to each bidder the same. All
bidders will receive information on what needs to be done on the roof.
E. Ward - Could I ask to get a summary report from the bids.
Mayor W. McCune - If he gets the bids quick. They will be here next meeting and
Council will be informed on what is going on. Let me explain one thing very
throughly to the six Council members. We are not going to do anything behind
your backs. Everything that is done in this Village will be brought to you six
people. And you will be comfortable with it before we vote on it. We have never
spent a dime without bringing it back to Council first. We will tell you what
is going on with everything we do.

VISITORS COMMENTS:
R. Ferguson - I am here for Ordinance 2169, my feelings on that Ordinance it
that it effects every employee. I have spoke with everyone on Council and asked
them to review it, and see if Council can do something different with the
Ordinance in regards to the way it is written.
I would like to see it revert back to the way it was before. The only exception
for the overtime was sick leave. We were told that this Ordinance did not
effect our Department, I read it effects everyone.
J. Lemire - A generic Ordinance applies to every employee.
R. Ferguson - We used to have it, if we were off sick then it did effect our
overtime. But the new Ordinance reads it will effect the overtime with any time
off. I do not think we plan to take vacation and then work over. I do not think
that my department has ever abused it. Also, I feel April 1st we passed a
budget and gave us a raise, then before May 1st we lose , something I was told
by Council, there was not intent for that.
T. Finger - You feel like this is to take away the increase.
G. Copeland - I don’t understand what brought this about or what the Village
has to gain by doing this. Why take this away from us. It seems like we are
being punished.
J. Lemire - What the Ordinance proposes to so is to change our current
Ordinance and Personnel Policy, which currently provides if you are employed
for more than forty hours a week you are entitled to overtime. What the change
would do would change the wording to say that if you work more than forty hours
a week, then you are entitled to overtime which is time and a half.
I was told that until recently that was always the way it had been. That you
had to work forty hours a week before you got overtime. When the statute was
reviewed and the use of the word employed. When someone is out on vacation or
on sick leave, they are employed, even though they are not working and so the
current Ordinance seems to read; that you are entitled to overtime anytime you
have been employed at the Village for more that forty hours. Be it vacation
sick leave, seminar or any other causes are entitled to overtime pay. I was
asked to draw up an Ordinance to change that and make sure that you had to work
before overtime pay kicked in. We did check with the Fair Labor Standards Act
that governs overtime pay, that law does not mandate overtime pay for anything
except for over forty hours of actual work. It does not require we pay out
overtime for vacation and etc. This is the decision for Council to make. There
is nothing illegal for doing it either way. The current policy we have now is
more generous than the Fair Labor Standards Act requires. I was told that the
old policy was that you had actually work forty hours before you were entitled
to time and a half. The current law Federal law that governs this does not
require we stick with this. This is the decision for Council to make.
D. Weir - If we had an employee that attended a seminar, he would be considered
working.
J. Lemire - Not under the way we have the current Ordinance before Council.
S. Terry - Then what is our incentive to go to a seminar? To learn and benefit
the Village and our careers. If we go to a seminar, we get compensated, but the
next day we work over our regular time, that time is straight time.
J. Lemire - The way the Ordinance before this Council is. You would not be
entitled to overtime unless you had already put in forty hours of work.
B. Reitz - It would work the same for us during the winter if we are on
vacation. If there was a snow storm we would have to work a lot of hours before
we would get overtime. But yet, we came in to benefit the Village.
C. Baxley - I think the only thing you need to do to make this proper and
justifiable, strike the work that does not include in the two places in the
Ordinance. Because we do not pay our workers enough. They earn every penny. As
far as the labor practices it doesn’t seem like a very good way to do business.
You should try and please your employees. I don’t think it is giving anyone
anything that any one of us in our work force does not already have.
J. Lemire - Most employers strictly comply with the Fair Labor Standards Act,
and would not give anything in the overtime area, only what the law demanded.
S. Terry - I feel vacation time is earned time. There are many times when we
are on vacation and we get called to work for court. If I am on vacation and
get called to work it is not overtime. That is not fair to us. This will be
straight time, what then is our incentive? What is our incentive to do our jobs
if you are going to take everything away. Sick time, I can agree with that but
vacation and seminar time I disagree.
Chief Febel - We provide a service to the community. In our line of work we
have to take some time off to keep our heads on straight. We have not really
put in a lot of overtime. When there is a storm in this Village you have the
Police, Streets and the Wastewater departments working arm in arm to clear the
streets. All we are asking for is a fair shake. We are all hear to provide
service for the Village and I feel we provide good services. It has been
working for many years the same way. I do not know what the problem is. We are
not a company to make money. We are here to provide services for the people of
the Village. I feel my people do a good job. We have a good working
relationship with all the other departments. It is disheartening when we get a
raise and then the next thing we get something taken away from us, that hurts.
B. Thompson - My understanding of this was certainly that no one was being
punished. On that past practices had been changed. It appeared to me that a
couple of words had been changed to comply with the law.

in that week. The old policy was that you didn’t count sick time as worked time
and therefore, you weren’t entitled to the overtime, if your week extended
forty hours that old policy didn’t fit with our Ordinance because, you are
still employed even when you are out on sick time. After we look at the
Ordinance we concluded we had to start paying overtime even of you were out on
sick time because of the way the Ordinance was worded. The current stature is
very broad, it states anytime you are employed for more than forty hours, you
are entitled to time and a half. This new Ordinance gets very specific about
what you gotta do in order to earn overtime pay.

VISITORS COMMENTS:
R. Ferguson - I am here for Ordinance 2169, I know it is tabled. Council asked
us at the last meeting for the department heads to come together and come up
with some solution. We did, and it was in Council packets.
Mayor W. McCune - Let me explain, I am the generator of this Ordinance. In 1986
we wrote a personnel book. We wrote the book up at the advice from our
Solicitor at the time. Because a person was fired and we almost had to go to
court over it, because we had no personnel file (Personnel Rules and
Regulations Handbook), at the time we wrote the book up. I left Council,
several people that were behind the book left Council. A different Mayor came
in and it got tabled. When I came back as Mayor the first thing that I asked
was “do we have a Personnel File”? It has never been acted upon. At that time I
asked Council to look it over and act upon it.
Which then we would come up with rules and regulations for the Village. Our
Solicitor lookedit over and everything seemed to be in line then. The overtime
came to issue when I was looking at the list of payrolls from our packets, I am
seeing regular hours, vacation hours, and overtime hours. Basically my thought
was that I had put a clause in the personnel file, that caused people to get
overtime when they shouldn’t have. When I realized what was going on, I tried
to correct it. First question asked, how do we come up the number of days
employees have off? The Federal Regulations for Holidays paid, so we must
follow the Federal Regulations for overtime, which overtime is paid after you
work forty hours. I had Patty research it and ask the previous Clerk (Trudy
Armstrong). She said this was the practice when she was Clerk, also. Some of
the things that were put in the minutes, I take exception to. When I came in as
Mayor, since then you people have gotten over two dollars an hour in raises,
just from my time. It doesn’t take long to calculate in a five year period, you
have increased your pay by three hundred and sixty dollars a month. I was just
trying to close a loophole that I thought I had created. I do not want to
create a hardship for the taxpayers. And I believe you people that work for the
Village shouldn’t create a hardship, it is tabled now and what happens is up to
the six Council people.
T. Finger - There was a lot of good discussion in your absence. Believing that
it came from you, we did not feel it was appropriate to second guess. It was
tabled until there could be a open discussion and look at what problem we were
trying to fix. At the time of the first reading all of us were under the
impression that there was abuse in overtime. It excluded Seminars and when we
vote to send someone to a seminar for the benefit of the Village. I think that
is work.
Mayor McCune- It was not set up to punish someone when they went to a seminar.
If we bring back the Ordinance I think we should take in consideration
everything that was discussed with the employees and Council. We should look at
the intent of what we are trying to fix and get in agreement that everyone can
live with.
J. Lemire - The practice of including sick time only just came upon in the last
year. That clearly is our current policy of paying overtime for time taken off
when sick time is taken. The document given to Council by the employees states
they would find it acceptable to exclude sick time from the overtime
calculation. The problem came about when we adopted a different language. When
we adopted the Personnel Policy, when it was read and looked at it didn’t seem
to allow us to exclude sick time, because of the words used.
Mayor W. McCune - That is where the Ordinance came from. If I caused a
uncomfortable feeling to people that work for the Village I am sorry. I thought
as Mayor I have been a pretty vibrant fighter for the wages. As far as I am
concerned it is a dead issue, the issue is tabled.
B. Cowles - Don’t we still have to amend our Policy Manual?
Mayor W. McCune - The rules are already established in the employees hand book.
I was just trying to clarify the handbook.

BUILDINGS AND LAND USE:
E. Ward - We have a request from the Merchants Committee to allow them to use
banners for the Community Night Sale. I have no problem doing this.
Mayor W. McCune - I was under the understanding the banners that fly at the
North and South end of town were part of a group or organizations that
advertises the Community. It will no be disallowed.
E. Ward - In the Codified Ordinances states that you can not hang anything over
the right of ways with the exception of Banners. We are working on the sign
Ordinance and we will bring it to Council hopefully by the next meeting.
T. Finger - As it stands right now, in our Ordinances, temporary banners are
allowed. This is a community project the banner will be up 7 to 10 days prior
and taken down after the sale.
E. Ward - We have a new Ordinance on signs to fix a problem with existing signs
in the tree lawn. We want to eventually, eliminate all the signs in the tree
lawns.
Mayor W. McCune - I was on Council when the first Ordinance was written up. The
intent of the Ordinance was, if the business was still in business and the sign
was knocked down, the owner could erect the sign back to its original place. If
the business changed hands and the sign was going to be changed then it had to
conform to the Zoning Code which has a set back from the tree lawn, and not
hang over any right of ways. That was our intent of writing it. In 1997
basically, it is now a loophole.
Council - Discussed in the Ordinance, when do we want to have the signs removed
and how to correct the verbiage, when the signs is blown down or when it is
removed or both. Also, questioned and discussed areas where there is no other
place to put the sign but on a pole hanging over the sidewalk. Talked that
signage can effect everyone, business owners and residents.
A. Aho - There is many considerations that take place, the way we can do
anything with signs is to take one thing at a time and pass it.
B. Cowles - Brought it to Council, that if we say that your sign is blown down
or removed you can not re-erect it in a public right of way and then we try to
do the next step of legislation and find out there is no place for this
property owner to put the sign, and maybe there is come places we have to allow
signs in the tree lawn. Then we will have to go back and rewrite this law.
Mayor W. McCune - Our concern, why we did this back in the Eighty’s was that
everyone was suing everyone. Our insurance carrier at the time asked if the
sign blew down, who was at fault.
Even though it wasn’t our sign we were told we would be at fault because the
sign was hanging over the right of way. That is why Council brought the
legislation across. Before we jump into any new Ordinance, if we have to set
back for two more weeks. Let’s make sure we don not put a clause in there that
we are right back where we started from. Lets set down with the Solicitor, the
Administrator and talk with the Merchants. To see what they can live with
concerning the signs. I think that would be a better idea than ending up with
the same thing we already have.

P. Fisher - What we have been trying to do is have the customer call the water
company if there is a question on their bill. If the customer calls they will
not be charges any fees. For the final water bill, we have the customer bring
in the final read to get the consumption. We have been doing it this way to
help avoid the extra charges from the water company. Even before we bought the
new billing program, Dan, Bill and I discussed which way would be cheaper, to
have the water company do it or we continue to do the billing. In conclusion it
is still cheaper for us to do the billing and we have more control of it.
Mayor W. McCune - When the water company did the billing, the water company
sent a bill for sewer and water together. If a person sending in a check does
not pay the full amount, the water would get paid first and the sewer a
percentage. I think the new system we are going to have will help with a lot of
the programs, and we will know what is being billed and what money is coming
in.
Motion by Finger that we will continue to do our own sewer billing at the rate
of 95¢ per meter read.

UTILITIES:
T. Finger - Last meeting we were faced with the decision with Consumers Ohio
Water Company that in June of 1997 our sewer billing contract was up. Consumer
Ohio Water declined to extend our contract another four years. In the new
contract they raised the meter reading rates from 60¢ to 95¢ a reading. That is
the way the Village wants to go. The other option given to Council was 4½
percent of the total billing. When you compare 4½ percent even against the
increased rate the Village saves about fifteen thousand dollars a year. From
utilities stand point we are not happy with consumers Ohio for rasing the meter
reads from 60¢ to 95¢. That is why I think it is in the Village’s best interest
to purchase the water district. So we can control the kind of costs and not be
at some private individuals fancy. This is an ongoing battle and the Village is
to control the costs, we are sticking with our decision to continue with the
purchase of the Water Company.
D. Weir - We contacted the Water Company and expressed our interest in
continuing with the existing contract we have with the rate of 60¢ per read.
Their response back was that they had no intent to continue with the contract.

AN ORDINANCE AMENDING SECTION 1446.03 OF THE CODIFIED ORDINANCES OF THE VILLAGE
OF JEFFERSON TO REGULATE EXISTING SIGNS.
J. Lemire - This Ordinance is a very strongly worded Ordinance. It will
eventually do awaywith signs in the tree lawn and right of ways.
A. Aho - This Ordinance is not being unduly harsh considering the depreciation
table on the existing signs. It will allow the functional signs to continue on.
T. Finger - Under existing zoning text the intent of zoning usually is to
grandfather out those non-conforming conditions. This is a movement in that
direction.
J. Lemire - It doesn’t effect existing signs.
T. Finger - But it doesn’t allow them to exist forever.
Mayor W. McCune - The outside of the Town Hall has been reconstructed. It has
brought out some of the character of the building. This is the last thing we
will do on the outside. It still complies with the historical aspects.
OFFICIALS:
Mayor W. McCune - I have a Proclamation to read. July is “Parks and Recreation
Month”.
In 1984 - 1986 Council spent all their extra time writing a Personnel Policy.
The Personnel Policy was established by recommendation of our Solicitor at that
time, to protect the Village and Employees. In 1992 when I came in as Mayor I
asked where the Personnel Policy was, it had not yet been passed, we did not
have any rules, guidelines and nothing to follow on any kind of discipline
action or anything. Council at that time brought it forth again. About twelve
Council people through the years worked on this Personnel Policy. They changed
it before it was ever adopted. The Personnel Policy is a living document. We
changed it, adjusted it, we tried to make it work for the Village of Jefferson.
The Personnel Policy is there to protect everyone, administration and the
employees also. If anyone has a problem with the Personnel Policy bring it to
Council so it can be worked out.

AN ORDINANCE AMENDING PERSONNEL RULES AND REGULATIONS PERTAINING TO HOLIDAY
COMP TIME AND USE OF TIME CLOCK
T. Finger - This Ordinance is about compensation time not being a allowed
practice of the Village. Also, it is reinstating that the employees are using
time clocks, per the Personnel Policy. This is a modification of the rules. We
believe it to be in the best interests of everyone.
A. Aho - What is the application if someone is request to work during their
lunch time period?
Mayor W. McCune - It would be considered overtime. If a employee doesn’t take a
lunch and works through it. That time will be considered overtime. This has to
be for an emergency reason only, it just can not be practice.
B. Thompson -In the Ordinance it does allow for flexibility and the supervisors
would have control over that.
J. Lemire - For the Patrolmen, the Chief questioned the impractibility of half
hour lunches for Police Officers because they are always on call. The Chief
wanted me to look into the Workers Compensation, if they are covered when they
are on lunch. He wanted to know what happens during that lunch period if a
Patrolman will be covered when they are called out. But if he is injured on his
own he is not, but he is still in uniform. So maybe this situation should be
looked into more. There is still a lot of issues that should be looked into.
T. Finger - It is my understanding that everything we are talking about right
now relating to hours worked and lunches are covered nowhere in this Ordinance
nor in the handbook. We are talking about a issue that is not in writing.
J. Lemire - We are amending the Personnel Policy to add the requirement to
clock in and out at lunch time.
T. Finger - When a officer takes a vehicle home with him, if he gets into an
accident on the way home the same question will apply there as when he is out
to lunch if he is covered under Workers Compensation.
J. Lemire - Workers Compensation is factual, it all depends. Whether he is
covered or not, it depends on what happened.
Chief Febel - We just have some questions we need answered. The book says to do
it this way and that is what we are going to do. But situations come up and we
need some answers.
A. Aho - The actual question is do the Police have a 7½ hour day or a 8 hour
day with a half our lunch when they work.
J. Lemire - I will look into it more, how a patrolman is covered under these

that basically has come up, that we feel the building would have to be torn up
to fix, we are going to do the repairs now. We will contact the asbestos
removal ourselves and have the building ready to be started.
W. Gallagher - We are in the process of working with the Commissioners on the
CDBG Funding to allow the Village of Jefferson to administer all the CDBG
monies independent of the County offices. It has been done in other counties.
So we are trying to get Ashtabula County to do this. Legal agreements will have
to be executed within the parties for approval of this work. In closing we are
hoping to get construction started on September 1997 and completion of the
building in mid December 1997 before the end of the year. A new building of
this magnitude which this building is over 12 thousand square feet of useable
space with additional 5 thousand square feet of storage space. The total
building is about 15 thousand square feet. The building has a brick exterior
and is maintenance free. If a new building was less than a hundred dollars a
square foot, I would be surprised. A new building would be about 1.5 million
dollars and that and that is only a new building, it does not include
utilities, land and parking lots. We still have time to corporate any changes
that are needed.
Mayor W. McCune - Anybody that has time can go down to the Village office and
look at the plans, feel free to do so. If there is something in the plans that
we have forgotten or you think we need to change let us know.
FINANCE:

amend the budget from the amended certificate received July 3, 1997 for Issue
II monies. We also received the month end figures for April and May of 1997.

Mayor W. McCune - We have applications out for grants . The date when the

SAFETY:
A. Aho - We had a safety committee meeting last week discussing several things
concerning the Fire department. One issue is whether our Volunteer Firemen are
employees to the village and subject to the employee procedures and employee
manual. The issue is worker compensation, are they covered if we didn’t pay
them as employees . The Solicitor is going to look into that issue. As being
employees and receiving a wage for the call out the payroll tax implications
that is being reviewed. We did note that the Volunteers have been appointed
according to state law. They are recommended by the Mayor to the Council to be
approved. Even though they are not employees the Village is exercising certain
amount of control over the Fire Department at the meeting many of the Volunteer
Firemen expressed their concerns and most concerns were communication and what
council was doing. I affirmed to them that all our meetings are public meetings
open to everyone. This is a little new to them that the Village has to follow
laws as a Village fire Department. They expressed their opinions that they
didn’t even care if they were paid. That is the extent of their volunteering.
Mayor W. McCune - My suggestion as Mayor, the ramification of pay with the Fire
Department, the pay came before the change. The change should have been that
the Jefferson Volunteer Fire Department no longer be volunteer. That is to be
changed by the Mayor and Council and be a paid organization. You can not be
paid and be volunteer too. If you do pay with the rules in effect today there
is a lot of cost to the Village. There is several items that go with the pay of
a Volunteer Fire Department. Right now we are breaking our rules as Council and
we can not do this. That is why I asked the Safety committee to try and
structure it. We are not restructuring the Fire Department it will stay the
same, the issue is the spending of monies the spending of tax payer monies and
it will be solved so it is right and voted on council to be done right. When it
comes down to misappropriation and miss spending of money. Patty and myself
could get into trouble. We will not let this happen, we are going to do this
right. The mileage we receive for the Fire Department and equipment is not
enough. We boost the operation of the Fire Department with tax money, we want
to make sure that everything is done correctly so we have the money to fight
fires. That is what the Fire Department is for.
A. Aho - The other articles of discussion is the fire inspections, how they are
being conducted. And who contracts the inspector to do fire inspections.
Mayor W. McCune - You as a Council should know who the inspector is because as
Council you should have voted on hiring the inspector. This was never brought
to this Council through myself. As Mayor I appoint the Fire Inspector and then
bring it to Council for approval. I have never appointed a Fire Inspector. The
memo sent to the Fire Chief on the fire inspections was sent because the fire
inspector was not properly appointed by the Mayor or Council. Fire Inspections
were not to be stopped the memo was sent out to follow procedures, no to stop
fire inspections.
A. Aho - The Chief has issued a order not to give fire inspections by Jim
Yancey because he is not properly appointed. The question is now are we not
going to do fire inspections.
B. Cowles - I think we should continue with our fire inspections, have a fire
inspector and pay them if we have to. Make sure the person is certified and
keeps track of all inspections that are being done.
Mayor W. McCune - I have no problem with that, by my situation is money. If we
are going to appoint a fire inspector under contract we have to know where the
money is coming from. The inspections are done in the Village and the Village
district of the Jefferson Volunteer Fire Department. I think we should set up a
rate schedule with the Village getting preference because they pay the taxes to
us and then the Townships that have contracts with us.
J. Kusar - Couldn’t you just appoint someone for now for a time period to cover
all basics until you hire someone permanently.
E. Ward - Couldn’t we make a motion to hire Jim Yancey and have him bring his
certificates for fire inspector?

lot due to the Police Department, and voiced that citizens in the Village would
be outraged if the Police Department was eliminated.

prices for certain hours being patrolled. This is just a cost figure. We need
to know if we are in line in what we are spending for the protection of the
Village of Jefferson. We have a personnel handbook in the Village. It is there
to protect the employees and the Village. We have to have every department in
the Village in line, they all have to follow rules. The Police Department did
not have a time clock, which in the policy book states the Police Department is
required to punch in and out. A time clock was put in, the Police Department
did not like it. But it is in our rules and regulations and we will follow the
rules.
M. McCune - The scheduling of our Police officers is now set so they can have
breaks and have coverage. We are going to fix our policy book and Ordinance for
all that matters. And it will be done right and legal. When we find a area in
the policy book that is wrong or needs to be fixed, we will correct it.
T. Finger - As a member of Council we all should keep a level head and stick
together. We all have heard criticisms of the Mayor. The Mayor is doing what
the Mayor should. He is regulating and controlling the safety forces this is
his job. It is Councils job to give him the regulations he has to follow. If
something is wrong in the Ordinance it will come forth and be fixed as needed.
Mayor W. McCune - We have front yard parking and we have a situation with the
Ordinance and how it is worded. The violations go under traffic and zoning. The
fines can go from 5.00 dollars to 100.00 dollars depending upon the judge. We
need to look into and decide what violation we are going to do. I want the
safety committee to look into it and bring this back to
Council.

Mayor W. McCune - This Ordinance is brought forth concerning the use of the
time clocks and Holidays. We have been talking about this for along time. We
need to clarify our Personnel Policy. So it is written down in black and white,
so there will be no misunderstandings.
Motion by Thompson for the first reading of Ordinance 2180.
2nd by Stasny
Questions on Ordinance 2180
J. Lemire - This Ordinance is a revision of the prior Ordinance attempting to
get around the problems of Police Officers on call. We have learned from the
wage and hour people that any policeman on call has to be paid for their lunch
hour. We are trying to clearly delegate that the policemen are not on call
during their half hour lunch period. We were told by the wage and hour people,
that a policeman is on anytime he is in his uniform.
T. Finger - Going back to the last meeting, the provision because the Police
Department works a rotating schedule, can we change the Police Departments work
week to 43 hours before it goes to overtime.
J. Lemire - The Federal and Hour law that governs overtime compensation states
that unless a Police Officer works more that 43 hours a week we do not have to
pay that overtime compensation. However, our Ordinance does not follow that
law. We have a more generous Ordinance that provides clearly that if a police
officer works more than 40 hours he gets paid overtime. The 43 hour work week
does not effect whether or not they are working or not during the half hour
lunch .
Mayor W. McCune - We have changes the shifts in the Police Department so they
are staggered so everyone can take a half hour lunch. We have established a
lunch hour after four hours of work. They punch out for lunch so they are not
on call or duty . Our Police Officers are asked to work 8 ½ hours, take a half
hour lunch and get paid for 8 hours. If there was a emergency during their
lunch period, they would get paid time and a half with the approval from the
Chief . They did not want that they want to work 8 hours period.
T. Finger - Even acting on this Ordinance we still do not have a good clear
path.
B. Thompson - In this Ordinance it says except in circumstances where the use
of the time clock would be grossly inconvenient and unpractical. We are
allowing for those situations that may arise where it would be impractical.
This Ordinance allows for situations that may arise. It also allows for if a
officer wants to go home for a half hour and not be on call during his lunch.
A. Aho - I have a question with the Holiday pay. In the section 30.09 where it
states the employees work schedule is other than Monday through Saturday, he or
she shall be entitled to holiday pay for holidays observed on his or her day
off. I am not to sure what that says.
Mayor W. McCune - It says if you are working 24 hours, seven days a week and
your day off falls on the Holiday you get paid for it.
A. Aho - Don’t we already say that everyone get paid if you are a full time
employee with 60 days of service, is that being redundant?
J. Lemire - It sounds like it to me, maybe we should look into at that section.
A. Aho - We should still go forward with this Ordinance on the use of the time
clock. Amend the Holiday section that if one of the above holidays falls within
an employees vacation period the employee shall receive holiday in addition to
the vacation pay. Also, a employee must work all scheduled hours the last day
before the holiday and the first scheduled work day after the holiday even
though it is in a different work week except when a employee is off due to
vacation.
Mayor W. McCune - Let us remove the holiday section 30.09 in this Ordinance and
bring a Ordinance forward with just holidays. So we understand everything under
holiday and no oneis confused.
B. Thompson - Removed his motion for the first reading of Ordinance 2180.
M. Stasny - Removed her Second Motion for the first reading of Ordinance 2180.
Motion by Thompson to remove section 30.09 out of the Ordinance to amend
Holiday Comp Time and use of Time Clock.
2nd by Stasny

VISITORS COMMENTS:
D. Wassie - Representing the Police Department with comments on two Ordinances
being read tonight. One that effects the Police Department directly is
Ordinance 2180, pertaining to use of the time clock. My primary concern with
this Ordinance is it is written to require the Police to be off duty during
assigned lunch period. This puts each of the officers in a civil liability
risk. A officer can be sued civilly for failing to respond to a call in a
timely matter to the emergency. We are being placed in a position where fellow
officers will be off duty during a time period and if we end up in a situation
where we will not be able to respond in a timely matter. The other concern have
and also citizens of this Community, is do we have to look at our watches when
we call 911 to decide if someone is going to be there or not or will they have
to wait a half-hour for someone to decide to be there. In this Ordinance it is
mandated that after four hours of work a lunch break be taken. We are now
publicizing when a officer is on break or off duty. It was stated at the last
Council Meeting that there were schedule adjustments to cover the lunch break.
That only covers 7 of the 21 lunch periods in a week. In the weeks we have
someone off sick or on vacation there will be no coverage.
David Wassie - Also, when the person has to take the lunch period after four
hours of work it cuts the person covering both shifts lunches down to one
because of the Ordinance. So this will also reduce coverage further. As to why
this is being sone I am not even going to guess. My understanding was a Village
employee and a Council member, we are hear to provide the best service possible
for the residents of the Village. I think this Ordinance goes against that. We
are taking people off duty and unavailable in the case of a emergency. In
concerns that we are doing our job. We have a small handful of officers that
answer 3,500 complaints within two to three minutes and have a 95% closure on
all cases, that speaks for itself. When people are walking the streets
exercising or walking their dogs at 5 a.m. in the morning . I guess that means
I am doing my job. Because citizens of the Village feel safe. Never in the past
have we had complaints about our lunches. If we are counting on the Sheriffs
department to do back up on our lunches maybe we should see what their response
and ours is only two to three minutes from the Sheriffs time. The next
ordinance which is the fire Ordinance they go hand in hand. It was quoted that
there was not authorization for two fire units to respond to a fender bender.
When I have a traffic accident, there is a lot of traffic going through the
intersection and traffic is being blocked because of the accident. I am tickled
to death when those two trucks get there with nine people. The thing that makes
this Village different from any other place I have worked. The fire fighters do
not have to say a word, they get on the truck and go to work. I do not have to
say anything everyone goes to work and gets the job done. I have never seen a
group of municipal workers that produce the service as they do here. That is
why I am here. I saw a group of people that work together like I have never
seen before. If we have a storm go through this town and trees are down and
wires down and services are out, there is no question as to who’s job it is to
do. We have people from every department in the Village out working together to
get the job done. That doesn’t happen in other Village’s, everyone is saying
that is not my job. They work until the job is done. When I put on my uniform
and come to work, I am expected to come upon situations most people would never
think about.
D. Wassie - Every single time a fireman gets on a truck to go to a fire they do
know that may not ride the truck back. They are willing to make that comment to
people of the Village. Instead of writing resolutions to say thank you. You are
writing Ordinances up to punish us for doing our job.
Mayor W. McCune - Let me answer your questions, as we go first of the
situations with the lunches. It was confusing to me as to when you were on duty
and when you were in the coffee shops taking lunch. I want to know so I could
figure out what the Police Department was doing. That is correct, you can
respond to any call in the Village in two to three minutes from coffee shop and
that is what was going on. I asked very, very nicely to the Chief several times
to get the men out of the coffee shops and get them on the streets. I said I
don’t want to see the car in front of the shops anymore, so then the cars went
behind the shops. I want the Police Department to do their job for eight hours
as far as the half hour lunch periods, I will pay you for the half hour.
I want to know when you are in the coffee shop, it is for lunch. The people
deserve a Police Department to be on the street not in coffee shops, for hours
at a time. The other reason is why do we have to specify when you have to take
it. Because the Police Department went an got an attorney and said basically we
did not have a set time for lunch breaks. So we wrote the Ordinance to give you
lunch breaks after four hours of work. All I have asked point blank is you do
your job. This is not a joke, it is tax payers money we are spending.
J. Kusar - The question with the half hour lunch break. The police department
has brought a good point. We are now publicizing when their lunch is. Right now
we do not have a lot of crime in the Village. But how many times has the Mayor
stated himself remember what you do today because it will effect us twenty
years down the road. I asked the Sheriff’s department what would be the
response time when police are not on duty for lunch breaks. They could not give
a definite answer because of the fact where the Sheriff’s car is when the
problem arises. I have asked the Police Department if there is enough coverage
for lunches and I was told there is not enough coverage.
John Kusar - There will be no coverage for second and third shift. There are
few businesses open twenty-four hours in this Village. One is Dairy Mart and
the other my motel. So if someone robs Dairy Mart we do not have any
protection, if someone tries to come and rob my motel at two thirty in the
morning. Now I will have to wait ten to fifteen minutes for a police officer.
Mayor W. McCune - There would be no problem because the midnight shift would
only work eight hours. The Ordinance has not passed yet and we are making sure
everyone gets paid for whatever they are working. The main point that everyone
has missed is the time that the officers are spending in the coffee shop.
Citizens of the Village have complained about the time the Police were spending
in the coffee shops. We will probably go back to the eight hours, but I want to
know when you are on lunch. All I want is eight hours of work from the Police
department.
D. Nelson - With a 95% solving rate of crime in the Village, you are saying the
Police are not doing their job.
Mayor W. McCune - We have heard the Police departments concerns. We will come
to some conclusion that will probably benefit all of us.
J. Wayman - The main concern the Fire Department is here tonight, the last
Council meeting a Ordinance was read to cut the Fire departments wages are
going back to a dollar a year. We are not happy about that and we want to know
why.
Mayor W. McCune - Basically, I want to know what I am supposed to be paying
for. I am paying right now for accidents, fires, and misc. Basically, you are a
volunteer Fire Department. When we pay the firemen all the paperwork says is
runs. I will pay the hour for a fire, I have no problem with the money. But I
do have a problem with fender benders, heavy rescue we are into, we have the
equipment to do it. But every time we have an accident we have pieces of our
equipment running, those trucks are fire trucks for fires. And we should save
them for that.
J. Wayman - We have to depend on what comes out of the 911 call, what we send
out. We are in a society, first thing we do is dial 911 and send out the fire
department because they can take care of everything.
Mayor W. McCune - My problem is when we have a fire. I want the trucks to be
able to respond to the fire. I was told by dispatch that the Fire Chief wrote a
letter and told to dispatch trucks to all accidents.
B. Thompson - To answer Chief Wayman’s question, we have to make a decision to
make the Fire Department volunteer or employees. There will be deductions taken
out of every check that is issued to you.
M. Stasny - Some of the men at the fire committee meeting said they do not want
to be employees. But they have been ever since the Ordinance passed in 1962.
J. Lemire - The Fire Department were employees before and they are still
employees. At the meeting there was discussion that they would rather not be
employee and not paid than an employee and paid. This Ordinance will reduce the
pay and they still are employees.
Mayor W. McCune - I drafted the Ordinance because we were spinning our wheels.
In the minutes of the meeting they said they pay did not mean anything to them.
D. Locy - If we were not a employee of the Village, we were asking if we were
going to be employees of the Village, we would go back to $1 a year, if we
weren’t employees. This Fire Department has done a lot for this Village.
Mayor W. McCune - The question is proper procedures with what we are doing and
what we are paying for. I do not want to loose any firemen , I just want to
know what we are supposed to be paying. And I want it kept to date, so the
Clerk can take care of the pay the way it is supposed to be done, and we know
who is doing what, so that everything is document. The money that is levied for
the Fire Department and the money we get for the fire levies is for fire use
only. We have General Fund money and Capital Improvements money. That goes into
the fire fund to boost it. We probably are over budget with the monies we have
spent.
R. Gregg - How can we be over budgeted if we had a carry over?
Mayor W. McCune - My job as Mayor is to take care of the money. And my job as
Mayor is to make sure the Clerk has all the information and everything she
needs, so she can properly handle the money. The next and most important thing
is to make sure the Village of Jefferson has money.
K. Fertig - Mayor, we can argue back and forth about money. I depend on these
people (Fire and Police Department). When I go to bed at night I know I am safe
and I do not care what it costs. Without these people this is not the town to
live in.
A. Aho - This all started out to get us in compliance with the tax law. Also
determine whether or not the Fire Department were volunteers. And whether they
were subject to taxes. For our Village to have a Fire Department it will not be
a Volunteer Fire Department, because they are employees and all payments will
be subject to taxes.
Mayor W. McCune - The money is not the subject, we have to follow proper
procedures. No matter what you make the proper deductions have to be made.
J. Wayman - We can argue points all night the Fire Department and Council have
decisions to be made. What we would like is Council to repeal the Ordinance and
go back to the way it was and accept all deductions.
Mayor W. McCune - We have not passed this Ordinance. We never pass anything in
an emergency. We want the discussion, you will have three readings to discuss
any problems. It is open to the public. The main thing no matter what you get
paid, we have to follow procedures and take out the proper deductions.
T. Finger - We keep sating Volunteer Fire Department. People who work in the
fire department are employees of the Village no matter what else happens. This
Council passes status that comes from committees or administration.
D. Locy - Questioned the policy book, which states that if we are a employee of
the Village you can not be employed by anyone else.
J. Lemire - When the personnel policy was adopted no one thought the issue of
part time or Volunteer employees. If we are going to make the personnel policy
book work we will have to look at the personnel policy and we will have to
detail the Fire Policies and the Village’s Personnel Policy together.
T. Finger - This Council has been working trying to fix these inconsistences in
the Personnel Policy. By statute the Fire Department are employees of the
Village. We do not want to kill the volunteers or spirit of the Fire
Department.

and so that the Clerk can properly record it for payroll.

BUILDINGS AND LAND USE:
Councilman Ward spoke with Council about the zoning text and different
situations that have come up on zoning. There are two medical clinics that want
to build in Jefferson. The Zoning text does not include medical clinics. They
can be built in the Residential area with a conditional use.
Council discussed the difference of the two medical clinics. One clinic wants
to build on property that is in Residential Zoning with a permissive use. The
other wants to change to a B1 Business Zoning, this property is the Jefferson
Geriatric Center. The main issue on both clinics is Jefferson’s zoning does not
have clinics in the Zoning. Medical Clinics are only under Residential Zoning
with a permissive use. In Residential Zoning front yard parking is not
permitted.
Council discussed a great concern about Medical Clinics in Residential Zoning.
There fear of Medical Clinics in this area could mean any type of Medical
Clinic on a Residential Street.
Councilwoman Cowles expressed her concern that if we change the zoning to fix
the needs of the medical clinics we will have to change it for everyone. If
people want to build they should abide by our zoning. We should not do spot
zoning in the Village.
Councilman Finger explained to Council that when we say Residential Zoning with
a Permissive use it is not conditional use and any type of Clinic can be put in
Residential Zoning with a permissive use and no restrictions.
Motion by Ward to move the Jefferson Geriatric Zoning change from Residential
to B1 Business to the Planning Commission for a recommendation.
2nd by Thompson
Roll: Aho, yea; Cowles, nay; Finger, abstain; Stasny, yea; Thompson, yea; Ward,
yea.
Motion by Ward to move the Ashtabula Clinic Zoning change from Conditional Use
in the RS District, to the Planning Commission for a recommendation.
2nd by Thompson
Roll: Aho, nay; Cowles, nay; Finger, nay; Stasny, yea; Thompson, yea; Ward,
nay.
Motion by Ward to move the Ashtabula Clinic Zoning change to B1 Business with a
Permissive Use to the Planning Commission for a recommendation.
2nd by Thompson
Roll: Aho, yea; Cowles. Nay; Finger, yea; Stasny, yea; Thompson, yea; Ward,

PUBLIC HEARING:
Administrator Weir explained to Council that the Jefferson Geriatric Center is
looking to build a Medical Center on Beech Street and North Sycamore Street.
Presently the zoning that is there is RS Single Family that does not allow
Medical Clinics. They are looking to rezone the parcel of land to B1 Business
which would permit the Geriatric center to build a Medical Clinic providing the
other Ordinance is passed to allow medical clinics is in the Multi Family
District and in the District it is a conditional use.
Administrator Weir -The other Ordinance in front of Council is to allow medical
clinics in the B1 Business district. This would allow the Geriatric Center and
the Ashtabula Clinic to build their projects.
Councilwoman Cowles expressed her concern that Council did not receive the
plans drawn up for the new clinic.
Administrator Weir told Council the plans are not a issue. The meeting with the
Planning Commission was to discuss the rezoning, the parcel of land. The
Planning Commission was given the plans to review them prior to making their
decision. Council makes their vote on changing the zoning text itself. It has
nothing to do with the building that is being built.
Councilwoman Cowles stated with the zoning change this would allow Medical
Clinics in the whole B1 Business District. Her concern with the zoning change
is there are still residents in the B1 Business District. With this rezoning
there could be any type of medical clinic next to a residential house. She
stated that she did not disagree with the new building, but was concerned with
the residents in the B1 Business District.
Councilman Finger stated the whole issue at hand is the rezoning of the B1
Business District to add a class of business in that district.
Councilwoman Cowles expressed she did not have a problem with the Clinic
building. Her concern was changing the entire district instead of just changing
a particular lot.
Mayor W. McCune explained to Council that if we continue to use our zoning with
conditional uses we are creating more problems in the future. If we make a zone
specifically zoned for that area in which clinics should be designated clinics
will be in the B1 Business District area because it has high traffic, and not
in another zoned area under conditional uses.
Motion by Finger to go back into regular session.
2nd by Ward
Roll: Aho, yea; Cowles, yea; Finger, yea; Thompson, yea; Ward, yea.

OFFICIALS:
Mayor William McCune read the State of the Village 1997 to Council:
The State of the Village of Jefferson, Ohio, January 5, 1998
1997 was a very busy year with the remodeling of the former Bi Lo Building and
the anticipation of the finished Community Center for the entire Village. With
the completion of the remodeling, we will have a wonderful place to hold a
variety of functions and a larger area to provide for Mark’s planned expansion
of programs. I would like to applaud Mark and Dan for all the extra work in
addition to their regular duties that this project has involved. They have
dedicated many hours to help make this a reality.
In the coming year, we will turn our attention to the interior of the Town Hall
to return it to the center of Jefferson Village Government. This project will
take us a few years to complete.
The Street Department did a good job in all of the various tasks that we’ve
added over the years. I would like to thank Rollie and his crew for their hard
work and dedication to the Village of Jefferson.
The Sewer Department continues to do a good job in meeting all the EPA
requirements and taking care of all the sewage needs of the Village residents.
There were a lot of problems with understanding the rules and regulations in
the Safety Departments this past year. The rules that the Village Council
adopts will be observed by everyone. If it’s a state regulation, we will follow
it. I hope that in 1998 the Safety Departments will become familiar with the
rules. If questions arise, please ask the Committee people, or Dan Weir, or Me
for clarification.
The Administration of the Village is being handled excellently by Dan and
Patty. With their watchful eyes on finances, the Village of Jefferson shall
prosper and the services that the residents have come to expect will continue.
I’d like to thank Council for their hard work in 1997 and, with a warm welcome
to our new Councilperson, Wilma Herndon, I look forward to a challenging 1998.

Motion by Thompson to adopt Resolution 2204.

Mayor McCune explained that we were to have the first reading of our
appropriations tonight.
The County Auditor faxed some figures to us because we have not received our
amended certificate. The Administrator worked out some figures. It shows our
estimated resources which is our actual numbers we will receive. The sheet also
has all our appropriations for each department as one total figure. After
everything is added up we have a balance $60,190.03.
The next meeting we will have the first reading of our appropriations. The
second reading of the Ordinance, I hope we go ahead and suspend Council Rules
and pass. When the Clerk gets back, it will be broken down into the proper
funds.
Councilman Finger - Again I have been vocal about the process. On January 11,
1998, we received a 1998 year end figure of $3,937,919.00. The new budget
summary states we will end the year with 60,000.00. Someone please tell me
where the $3,877,000.00 went. The first document I received was from the
Ashtabula County Budget Commission dated 8-11-97. The money they say is
available is $6, 296,000.00 On 1-30-98 we received a revised certificate from
the Auditors Office which states we only have $2,950,000.00. Somewhere between
August and January there is a $3,345,000.00 less in that fund that is
available.
Mayor McCune stated somewhere there is figures duplicated. Because the balance
of the Village has never been 6 million dollars. The figures you have there
come from the Auditors Office. On Wednesday, I called Bob Beacon from the
Auditors Office and asked him if he had the figures done. He stated they were
done, not approved. He faxed us the new amended certificate. The figures you
are looking at, dated 8-11-97, are not correct. The signatures on the paper
work is not signed by us.
Councilman Finger questioned duplicates in personnel on the worksheet and
stated Council did not approve of extra person.
Mayor McCune explained that the Clerk broke down the person wages from the two
separate funds. Part is from the general fund and part is from the Wastewater
Treatment. The employee does the sewer billing for the Wastewater Treatment
Plant, so the Clerk is taking funds from the Wastewater instead of all from the
General Fund.
Motion by Thompson to direct the Administrator to communicate further with the
County Auditor and provide us with some concrete figures.
2nd by Herndon
Roll: Aho, nay; Finger, yea; Herndon, yea; Stasny, yea; Thompson, yea; Ward,
yea.
Councilman Aho noted that each of the funds should stand alone for the services
rendered.
So when we have to analyze something we have sound numbers to make our
decisions upon.
I think the utilities for the Recreation Building should be changed to that
fund and not Lands & Buildings as it in the Budget.
Mayor McCune explained that we need a track record to know where we are going.
The Recreation Department will cover it’s own weight as much as it can. We do
not know the actual costs for that building yet. We can not put figures in the
appropriations for the Community Center Utilities without having the knowledge
if it will generate enough funds. There is not any department in the Village
that is not boosted by the General Fund. The only department generating funds
to run on its own is the WasteWater Treatment. What is being done today with
the appropriations, we are amending our certificates when it is needed, we are
not transferring money from fund to fund. The answers are not at this table.
The answers are setting right down with the Clerk and with the Auditor and
talking to them. Let them explain it. That is the only way to learn finances.
Councilman Finger - I take offense at your comments. I have worked 30 years
with budgeting.
Mayor McCune stated that is great, but you work in business budgeting, not on
government.
A dollar in government is totally different than a business dollar. And until a
person sits down and understands how the government financing and
appropriations are worked there will be confusion. Everything will be given to
Council the Friday before the next meeting in the packets.
If there are any problems we will call a special meeting.
