DISCUSSION:
Solicitor Lemire told Council we did not need an Ordinance to bring income tax
back in house. There is already a Ordinance in place that authorizes the Clerk
Treasurer to contract with Central Collection Agency. There is already
authority in place for the Village to do income tax. The Village needs a motion
from Council to bring it back.
Councilman Finger expressed his opinion, he wanted more of a study done from
the committee about pro’s and con’s.
Mayor McCune expressed to Council ; with bringing the collection back in house
the Village can take control of the Village’s own destiny as far as income tax
money being slipped away by people not reporting. CCA only accepts people who
pay, they do not go out and find the people who are slipping away. We will be
able to cross reference the people who should pay with our sewer billing master
file.
Councilman Aho questioned why we are bringing income tax back. Doesn’t CCA do
that?
Clerk Fisher told Council that CCA give a list with the numbers to the Village,
they do not actually know the names. When you talk to CCA you get a different
person every time.
CCA will only do the people that file if you do not file they will never catch
you. If the Village brings back the collection we will save money. The Village
will know when a person moves in or out. People will be able to pay at the Town
Hall. If a person has a question instead of calling CCA they will come to the
Office to get answers. The first year some money will be saved but the Village
is looking at increases as we look at the years ahead. There are figures from
other Villages around us that show they bring in more money when the collection
is done in house.
Administrator Weir told Council if the Village does the income tax we can
simplify the forms and put together our own income tax process that will
simplify the procedure and make it more efficient.
Councilman Thompson expressed to Council that he lives, works and pays his
taxes in the Village. He would like to see everyone paying their taxes.
Bringing the collection back will surely affirm this.
Councilwoman Herndon told Council that at the special Finance Meeting we had
four out of six Council people there and the consensus was to go forward.
Mayor McCune told Council that there is a motion on the floor and we have to
take a vote.
Roll: Aho, nay; Finger, nay; Herndon, yea; Stasny, yea; Thompson; yea; Ward,
yea.

March 16, 1998 - Public Hearing
Public Hearing.
Regular Meeting was called to order by Mayor William McCune.
Roll: Aho, Herndon, Stasny, Thompson, Ward
Absent: Finger
Also Present: Ed Flack, Gary Cole, Marc Glotzbecker, Chief Febel, Stephen
Szanto Huntington Bank, Administrator Dan Weir, Solicitor Jerry Lemire, The
Gazette.
Mayor McCune introduce Stephen Szanto to Council. Told Council that Mr. Szanto
will tell Council what he does and what he can do to help the Village with the
Bonds.
Stephen Szanto told Council he represented Huntington Capital Corporation, he
is a investor and underwriter for bond issues. He has worked with tax exempt
debts since 1980. The expertise he has deals with mostly municipalities.
Huntington Capital bought the Village’s Notes for $700,000 dollars in December.
Mr. Szanto explained who is involved with bond issues. He explained the Village
will have a Bond Council, that drafts the legal documentation for the bond
issue, does the specs, ordinances, resolutions and a tax exempt legal opinion
that is presented to all buyers of the bonds. The Bond Council also puts
together the official statement or offering document. Any bond issue that deals
with over a million dollars the F.C.C. requires the Village the have a official
statement. The lawyers put it together from a legal standpoint. A underwriter
helps put it together from a sales standpoint and highlight the parts that
appeal the most for the buyers. The underwriters will help you structure the
transaction, how many years the bond should be for, how to put the bond issue
together and which rating agency to use. A underwriter is like a intermediator
broker to the bond market. The bond issue the Village wants to sell can be done
in two ways. The competitive sale, and that is done by underwriters or the
client and the Bond Council put it together. Mr. Szanto explained to council if
they choose to have a underwriter do the bonds for the Village, Huntington
Capital would by the bonds thirty days after the third reading of the Ordinance
( which this is a negotiable sale). Huntington Capital would choose what day
the sale of the bonds would be, this is done to get the best rate. Draw up the
official statement, working with the rating process and help answer all
questions that are asked.
Mr. Szanto also told Council that the Village’s rating would probably be a BAA
rating, for the area the Village is located in, that is not a bad rating. To
get ratings you need to look at three years of financial statements, type of
payback in respects to the department, what activities go on in the Village,
building permits, assessed value and income tax receipts. Other parties
involved in buying bonds are a printer that prints up the perspectives and a
registered paying agent that makes sure the people who buy the bonds get paid.
Solicitor Lemire asked Stephen Szanto if the bids were done competitively would
there have to be an underwriter.
Stephen Szanto told Council if the bond was bided out competitively and there
was an underwriter involved he would do the biding. Whatever underwriter has
the lowest bid the Village would pick. Whether you pay someone to negotiate the
deal or take the bid out competitively, there is always a fee. Both the
underwriters and the Bond Council are always involved in the transaction of
selling bonds. The decision is where the Village wants them in the transaction.
Mr. Szanto explained that his fee to be the Village’s underwriter would be ten
thousand dollars.
Councilman Aho asked Mr. Szanto what efforts would be put forth in the attempt
to get an A rating.
Stephen Szanto explained there is two ways to apply for a rating. 1) You look
at everything there is, then have a conference call. 2) Or you go to New York
and do a formal presentation.
Whatever is needed is done to the best rating. The only problem in getting
through the steps, the Village is a small community.
Mayor McCune expressed his thanks to Stephen Szanto and told him Council would
digest it then get back with him.
Minutes to the last meeting were approved as written.

April 6, 1998
Regular Meeting was called to order by Mayor McCune
Roll: Aho, Finger, Herndon, Stasny, Thompson, Ward
Also Present: Gary Cole, Ed Flack, Cayce Baxley, Kelly Ward, Bev Finger, March
Glotzbecker, John Kusar, Ashtabula County Prosecutor Thomas Sartini, Chief
Steve Febel, The Gazette, The Star Beacon, Administrator Dan Weir, Solicitor
Jerry Lemire.
Mayor McCune introduced Ashtabula County Prosecutor Thomas Sartini to Council,
the presentation he introduced to Council was concerning a five year narcotics
task force levy.
T. Sartini asked Council for the approval of a Resolution in support for the
passage of a 0.7 mill narcotics task force levy. Mr. Sartini told Council in
dealing with drug cases, drug dealers, and the drug culture. This is a
different type of crime, not the run-of-the-mill that local police agencies are
geared up and trained for. Mr. Sartini explained to Council that the funds
raised by the levy are badly needed by the Ashtabula County Drug Task Force.
This money will help do the work that is necessary to infiltrate the drug
culture in the county. In the process of infiltration the drug culture, long
term surveillance is needed, with this levy this will be able to be done in
Ashtabula County. The budget for the task force operates on about $140,000
which $85,000 is a grant. Matching funds are contributed from all of the local
communities, and seizures and forfeitures. Figures released by Chief Febel
contained the operating expenses that the Task Force levy operates with. The
budget is $109,973 which employs one special full-time agent and three part-
time special agents. Sartini stated to Council, if the levy is passed a
director would be hired along with additional agents. The levy if passed would
generate about $773,000. Sartini explained that someone with a $100,000 home,
the levy would cost them about $22.00 per year.
This is a levy that will not cost a lot to the homeowners, but it is needed
very much to help rid of drugs in the County.
Minutes to the last meeting were approved as written.

Councilman Aho discussed with Council Resolution 2006 the 2 mil. levy for Roads
& Bridges.
The Levy will expire at the end of the year. Council debated whether they
should renew or replace the levy.
Administrator Weir explained to Council that the levy money is used for
services, road materials, wages and equipment. Together that helps maintain the
roads.
Clerk Treasurer Fisher told Council the 2 mil levy right now (1998) brings in
$74,805.50.
Councilman Thompson asked Administrator Weir what the future needs were for the
Village Streets and if the milage would be enough. If the needs do not extend
the milage, he recommended the levy be a renewal at the present rate.
Administrator Weir told Council over the last few years the Village has gone
heavy with paving with most of the streets in town. The Village will maintain
the streets with a crack seal program and resurfacing when necessary. Weir told
Council that the plans for the streets department in the future, the levy money
would be enough. Also, the Village subsidizes some monies from the general
fund.
Councilman Aho expressed to Council that four levies are coming up in the next
two years that need to be replaced. The Village should just renew this levy
because the funds in this levy are not needed as much as in the other levies.
Motion by Thompson to bring a Ordinance forth next meeting for a 2 mil levy to
renew Resolution 2006 for Roads and Bridges.

Mayor McCune expressed to Council and the Village that the Village has a set
way of paving the streets, especially dirt roads. The set way is certain
specifications of asphalt. It is not chip and seal nor pug mill. The residents
that live on dirt roads pay a one time fee to hard surface these roads.
The taxpayers of the Village of Jefferson maintain the roads forever. We are
paying a lot of money to keep our roads in good shape. The dirt roads in the
Village, if a resident wants to have them paved, please follow the correct
procedures and the Village will go forward with the request.
Councilman Finger questioned the new developments of subdivision regulations,
and having them be dirt roads. He questioned the consistency in asking the
developers on paving the roads.
Mayor McCune told Council that our subdivision regulations are set up for the
Village specifications for paving roads.
Solicitor Lemire explained to Council about the roads in the Village, that
border against the Township and methods of payment. He explained the payment of
the funding with the Township.
He stated that the Village would have to create a special improvements
district. This would allow the Township residents to get together and pave
roads where they both border, but this takes citizens wanting to do this.
Mayor McCune told Council if the residents approve it there is a way the paving
can be assessed to taxes over a certain amount of years. But it has to be
approved by the property owners on that street.
E. Flack brought up the issue of dust control for the Village roads.
Mayor McCune told Council that salt brine is being applied to the dirt roads
and he assured that it is being done in the best timely fashion possible. The
Mayor stated that brine has been hard to get a hold of in the past, but the
Village has made arrangements with Clarence Tussel this year for brine
application.
E. Flack questioned the Ordinance for the 2 mil levy for the roads and bridges.
Clerk Treasurer Fisher told Council the 2 mil levy brings in money for
maintenance of roads and street maintenance, street department equipment. It
pays for asphalt to pave the streets, the wages for the streets department,
salt and cinders during the winter and curbing of the streets.
Councilman Finger stated for the record the proper policy to pave the roads is
as follows:
The owners pay the first time. The Village residents who want the roads paved
61 percent of them bring forth a petition for paving it is then added to a
list. There is step for the roads that borders the Township and the Village,
through a special improvements district. The Village has the means to get the
paving done, but all the citizens must agree or want it done. It will never be
Councils actions to declare it be done.
FORESTRY:
No Report.
OFFICIALS:
Councilman Thompson commented the appreciation of the Memorial Day Observance
and all the organizations that worked together for the Memorial that was built
in honoring local Veterans of War.
OLD/NEW BUSINESS:
No Report.
Meeting Adjourn
Respectfully Submitted,
   Approved:
                                                                     
Patricia A. Fisher, William A. McCune, Mayor

option for development. Also, told Council the Village can either take off the
restrictions or can install sewers and pass the cost on to the property owners.

told Council the USA Waste has bought out Northeastern Disposal and they are
being charged tipping fees. (Landfill fees) That is why they are asking for the
increase, he also stated Geneva Landfill and USA Waste are one in the same.
Weir told Council that the Village has two options. One is to accept the
increase to the residents of the Village or terminate the contract. After
discussion Weir told Council that the competition is being bought out by USA
Waste and there is not competition out there.
Mayor McCune explained to Council that the Attorney General is looking into the
merge with USA Waste.
Council discussed the increase, landfill fees and the contract. Stated the
monthly fee has been low since the Village started bidding out the service in
1992. Council instructed Administrator Weir to get the information on increases
and tipping fees, work out and negotiate a new contract with USA Waste. No
decision will be made until more information is brought back to Council.

RESOLUTION ACCEPTING THE AMOUNTS AND RATES AS DETERMINED BY THE BUDGET
COMMISSION AND AUTHORIZING THE NECESSARY TAX LEVIES AND CERTIFYING THEM TO THE
COUNTY AUDITOR.
Councilman Finger questioned if the Finance Committee checked the numbers
against last years . Based on time spent on last years figures, the 1998
Estimated income from other sources was 2 million, the new sheet states our
estimated income from other sources for next year will be 3 million.
Clerk Treasurer Fisher told Council that the difference is from the Bond money.
The Tax Budget was done before Council approved the Ordinance on the Bond
money. The Budget will be amended at the end of the year and the money will
then be put in the 1998 certificate of Estimated Resources when the county
Auditors approve the new amended certificate.
Councilman Finger still questioned why the money was put in other sources
instead of the unencumbered balance.
Clerk Treasurer Fisher told Council that Council had not approved the Ordinance
for the Bond money in 1998 yet. So the money had not been unencumbered so far
in 1998. When the Bond money was approved by Council, in the Ordinance it was
sent to the County Auditors office for approval. We will then get a new amended
certificate with the new figures in January of 1999. I will send the year end
figures with the Bond money and in the 1999 new estimated certificate it will
show the correct figures. The County Auditors Office has to have the Resolution
to prove that we are accepting the money they are giving the Village.
Councilman Thompson told Council of receiving the monthly fund reports and year
to date totals up to August 1998.
Clerk Treasurer Fisher told Council that the Codified Ordinances for the
Village of Jefferson, two companies have received the last year and a half of
Ordinances and Resolutions and the company with the best price is the company
we will go with. At the beginning of 1999 the Ordinances will be codified up to
July of 1998.
Councilman Thompson asked if there had been some progress with the wish lists
from each department. Asked if everything could be finalized by the first week
in November.
Councilman Aho questioned the amortization schedule for the bonds. The top of
the sheet sates 5.11 percent. But when you look at the schedule of payment ir
shows different percentages.
Clerk Treasurer Fisher told Council that is what the percentage averages out to
be. That is how the Bond council set it up. Told Council that she would get in
touch with Brickler & Eckler to find out the answers to Councils questions. The
interest rate was set up based on what is owed at the time of payment.
Mayor McCune told Council that the first part of the bond is locked in at the
interest rate that was quoted. The long term payback is set up with different
interest rates.

SERVICE:
Administrator Weir talked to Council with the disposal contract. Told Council
that he had spoke with Bill Skidmore of Waste Management (USA Waste) and Louis
Popovich of County Disposal. Told Council with the proposal from Waste
Management they put a cost factor for their service over the next three years,
which calculated out to about a five percent increase per year. County Disposal
has offered the same service for $9.00 with a minimum of 3% increase per year
which is the cost of living increase.
Councilman Aho stated Waste Management has the language in their contract
stating that they could reopen the contract anytime for additional costs.
County Disposal stated they would absorb the costs themselves. Aho also
questioned if the Village would not agree to the current contract would it have
to be put to bid again.
Administrator Weir told Council that the Village would not have to bid out the
garbage contract again because the expenditures do not come from the Villages
money. The residents of the Village pay for the garbage service.
Solicitor Lemire told Council he reviewed the statute and it requires bidding
only when there is a expenditure of more than 10,000 dollars of Village funds.
Bill Skidmore of Waste Management addressed Council and stated that his company
and USA Waste services merged together in July of 1998. USA Waste came to the
Administration and requested a $1.00 per month price increase. The Villages
contract started in July of 1996 and there is one year left in the contract.
Told Council that they have serviced the Village for over 30 years and
continues to service the Village. The two bids between the companies are not
different. Told Council their (Waste Management) numbers are based upon the
current specifications and that specifications call for a 100% Performance Bond
There is costs that accrue in getting the Performance Bond. Stated that they
have insurance requirements and equipment requirements. Questioned Council if
in the contracts were apples for apples. Suggested that Waste Management is a
large company with financial resources to do great things. Told Council about
House Bill 592, concerning taxes on Landfills, which is a surcharge.
Asked Council if the district increased that tax, wanted to know if it could be
passed onto the Community for 1.00.
Louis Popovich of Country Disposal addressed Council stating that Waste
Management is big, but he has been in the business since 1976 and has a record
to be very proud of. Told Council his trucks have only missed one day and that
was in 1977 due to snow, nobody could get out. Financially, the business has no
problem. Said both companies record for record are about the same, pointed out
2% is not much and no one knows when the landfill prices will increase.
Informed Council that Country Disposal is working out a contract with a
landfill, if he gets the contract then he will be locked into a contract for
five years, which guarantees a rate. Stated if the landfill rates and State Tax
rates go up, he will take the loss. Informed Council, if his name is put on a
contract Country Disposal will give the best possible service .
Council discussed with the Contractors landfill areas, the contracts and bid
specs. Discussed type of service and how the residents would be treated for
special needs. After discussions with both contractors, Council decided the
Service Committee would meet and then come back to Council with the decision,
Council announced a service meeting Thursday, September 10, 1998 at 6:00 p.m.

Lincoln Morris of West Cedar Street spoke to Council and asked for the Villages
approval. Discussed the responsibility of the residents. Went over what it
would cost, each lot owners for their share of the paving. Told Council the
residents of the street would cover costs for the two lots that the residents
from the street would not pay.
Administrator Weir explained to Council what the costs would be for the

Council asked Administrator Weir where the expenditures would come from.
Administrator Weir replied, the B24 Fund which is Capital Improvements and

VISITORS COMMENTS:
Marilyn Aho commented to Council about the sign for the Perambulator Museum .
The attention was brought to Council by a letter from a resident of the Village
stating it was the Villages responsibility to place a sign advertising
historical and educational sights within the Village. Other places in Ohio have
visitors signs but the resident did not indicate how the signs were placed by
local government. The green signs placed along public highways are controlled
by the Department of Transportation. There is criteria that must be met in
order to place a sign in the Village. The primary rules is that the facility
must be open 7 days a week with a specified minimum number of hours to be open.
Most tourist sites in Ashtabula County meet that criteria including the
Perambulator Museum, which is only open Wednesday and Saturdays during the
summer months and winter months until January just on Saturdays. Ashtabula
County has a organization called the County Convention Visitors Bureau which
promotes tourist activities in the County . Mrs. Aho also stated that she was
not in favor for the Village taking on the responsibilities of promoting
tourist sights within the area and if the Council does decide to do so, she
suggested a uniform type of sign be placed at all historic sites in the Village
of Jefferson.

regulations. Council discussed that the subdivision regulations in the Codified

October 5, 1998
Regular Meeting was called to order by Mayor William McCune
Roll: Aho, Finger, Herndon, Thompson, Ward
Absent: Stasny
Also Present: Madge Lehnert, Cayce Baxley, Harlin Wade, Dave Schiele, Tim
Lemire, Jason Pearis, John Wayman, Chief Febel, John Patterson, Solicitor
Lemire, Administrator Weir, The Gazette, The Star Beacon
Steering Committee:
John Patterson, Dave Schiele and Dr. Harlan Wade represented the School
District with a video advertisement in seeking support to the Jefferson Village
Council for the 9.95 mill bond issue to build a new high school that will be on
the November Ballot. The Steering Committee told Council that the new school
would include 20 new class rooms, four science labs, four special education
classrooms, a word processing computer lab, and a media center. There would
also be separate labs for food, clothing, arts, music graphics and space for a
industrial art and vocational agriculture. There would also be a gymnasium,
auxiliary gym, wrestling room, weight room, locker room areas, a 10,000 square
foot cafeteria and a kitchen, a guidance and administrative and clinic area.
The new building would be designed for 900 students but could hold 1200
students. The Steering Committee discussed the estimate of expenditures to
operate the new high school. Told Council based on the current tax valuation
the school would need an estimated 530,000 dollars to run the school , which
would require about 3.7 mills. Also, stated that the cost would be lower in the
future because the school districts tax lease would continue to grow. Indicated
to Council that the cost to borrow money is low right now, which is a ideal
time to build the new school.
Councilman Aho questioned to the Steering Committee with the afford ability to
the tax payers in the County. Questioned the operating costs and the costs of
the levy. Told the Committee that he was in favor of the levy but still wanted
some questions answered. Asked the Steering Committee to look at the total 22.5
mills and wanted a total breakdown of space for the classroom, instructional,
Administrative and Multi Purpose rooms.
The Steering Committee told Councilman Aho they would get the figures for all
his questions.
Mayor McCune asked the Steering Committee what the total millage would cost for
the tax payer of each household.
The Steering Committee told Council the market value of a house that is 100,000
dollars the thirty-five percent of that value would be $350.00 a year but it
would only be about $259.00 year because most people can deduct the cost of the
real estate taxes in the form of their income the end of the year. In some
cases it may even be lower if you claim the homestead exemptions.
Councilman Finger questioned what bearing his income tax had on his property
tax.
The Steering Committee told Council when a person files his income tax at year-
end you deduct the income tax credit. The Committee went over with Council
everything with the school size and the student needs , told Council it falls
within state statutes.
Councilman Finger questioned that the mileage that the Steering Committee is
asking for is for a bond issue for the building and when the bond issue passes
for the building, will the school have to come back and ask for more, for
operating the building.
The Steering Committee told Council most likely in the future there would be a
possibility of it. But if the growth factor goes the way it should with the new
students and State, it may not cost more.
Administrator Weir told Council that with the new allotment, there is a
possibility of 88 new households in the Village, in the future.
Cayce Baxley a citizen of the Village, told Council a building does not make a
school. It is excellent teaching., books, and equipment. With the operating
costs now in Jefferson , we are not taking care of our kids now. The school is
already being heavily subsidized by organizations in the Community. Cayce did
agree that the community did need a new school. But we should make the State
pay more in the role for a new building for a new school. Also, noted to
Council a 28 year bond issue puts a burden on the residents now but will also
be passed on to our children. Mrs. Baxley stressed her major point to the
Steering Committee as; if the school system can not equipt our school with up
to date materials and teaching aids how can the system think about the future.
The Steering Committee responded back stating that the information and figures
were put together with the best interests for everyone involved. If this
project is not done we will end up short changing our kids.
Minutes to the last meeting were approved as written.

SERVICE:
Councilman Aho presented council facts from the committee meeting concerning
the Solid Waste Hauling contract. The Committee reviewed all submitted
proposals from Geneva Disposal Company , All County Disposal, Country Disposal
and Waste Management. After reviewing the contracts in their entirety. The
committee discarded Geneva Disposal because of the high costs. All County which
came in at $8.40 a month was discarded because of incomplete information
provided. All County had nothing about ensulry services or what maximums on
what they would take. The Committee considered what is happening in the
disposal industry with the consolidating and lack of possible options in the
future, made the Committee feel a locally owned company would give the Village
an alternative to Waste Management. There are residents in the Village that are
not happy with Waste Managements service since they have taken over USA Waste .
Waste Management is the company that broke the existing contract with the
Village. If we sign a new contract with them they may break it again.
A recommendation was made by Councilman Aho from the Service Committee to
recommend Country Disposal as the Solid Waste hauler for the Village of
Jefferson. With the Administrator entering negotiations with them to get the
best possible deal and enter into a contract.
Councilman Finger wanted clarified why All County Disposal's proposal was
rejected.
Councilman Aho told Council in the proposal they stated $8.40 a month no bag
limit was mentioned, they were referencing the Villages exhibit.
Randy Dearing of All County Disposal addressed Council stating the way the bid
was filled out was, after a discussion with the Administrator. The discussion
that took place was in regard to a standard weekly amount. There was no
discussion of a senior situation or smaller bag amount. There was nothing in
the bid stating what amount was being hauled a week. He also questioned that he
did not understand what the Village meant when they said the proposal was not
filled out out properly.
Solicitor Lemire recommended to Council that there was no need for any voting
from Council until a contract was in place. There is a recommendation from the
Committee to Council and a suggestion from the Committee to have administration
pin down more details in the agreement before being reviewed by Council.
Councilman Thompson questioned if Council should reconsider the recommendation
from the Committee because new information was given from all Country Disposal
.
Solicitor Lemire told Council that they ultimately decide who will receive the
contract and also if it should go back to the committee.
Administrator Weir questioned Council and the Solicitor if the Council is
required to take the lowest bidder?
Solicitor Lemire told Council they did not have to take the lowest bidder.
Administrator Weir also told Council that the Village was not even dealing with
a bid process. He also stated to Council that there are three other contractors
that can come and talk to Village Council and can all say they were not treated
right. We can do this process forever.
Councilman Aho told Council that the proposals have been advertised twice and
everyone has been given a chance.
Administrator Weir questioned Randy Dearing of All County Disposal as to where
the Villages' trash would be disposed.
Randy Dearing replied that All County uses two different sites. One which is
Lake County Bailer and the other USA Landfill . Everything is done on which one
gives us the better price.
Councilman Finger questioned All County if the amount quoted was for normal
household refuse.
Randy Dearing stated it was for normal refuge only.
Councilwoman Herndon questioned if individual bags were sold.
Randy Dearing stated that All County sold bags at twenty dollars for ten bags.
Councilman Finger reminded Council that there was still a recommendation from
the committee open on the floor to have Country Disposal as the Villages Solid
Waste Hauler.
Motion by Finger to accept the Committees Recommendation.
2nd by Aho
Roll: Aho, yea; Finger, yea; Herndon, nay; Stasny, nay; Thompson, nay.
Councilman Finger told Council as it stands right now, Waste Management is
still the Villages hauler until July 1999 at $9.00 a month.
Administrator Weir told Council that the Village is still under the current
contract that can change at any time.

hearing, may amend, supplement or change the subdivision regulations. The
Subdivision Regulations that will be acted upon are the ones dated 1961. The
new regulations will bring everything up to the 1998 - 2000 standards. It is
ultimately the Planning Commissions responsibility to bring back a Ordinance to
this Council. After that there will be a public meeting. As a result from the
public meeting a Ordinance will be brought back to Council.

J. Shouvlin from Second National Bank presented Council with information
regarding the financing for the purchase of a new fire truck for the Fire
Department. Explained to Council the availability to finance the truck and
spread the purchasing price of the truck over a 2 year period. Which then would
help with fund balances for the Village. What the Village would do is put a
cash percent down finance the balance and make principal payments with interest
over the next two years. Also told Council the minimum that could be financed
was 15,000.00 dollars. Stated that there is no fees charged to municipalities
which included points and closing costs.

Councilman Finger questioned two bills on the list of bills, which were
Governmental Systems Bill and the American Legal Bill.
Clerk Treasurer Fisher explained to Council the Governmental System Bill
included the first step of the income tax on purchasing the system. The rest of
the bill included software support for our programs through them. The American
Legal bill includes a program for putting the minutes of folio views and
converting the minutes from 1996 until August of 1998 into the program. Some of
the pages were converted from disk and some were scanned. This is the beginning
of a maintenance the Village will be doing for record retention. Eventually,
the Village will have all the old minutes, police reports and Ordinances on
disk which can be used for the permanent record retention in the Village.

SERVICE:
Mayor McCune discussed with Council the situation with our garbage haulers.
Discussed low bids and contracting haulers. The bid with the garbage haulers is
not a low bid contract. The Village is just trying to get a better rate and
make the Village exclusive to a garbage hauler who gives us the best prices for
the residents. Mayor McCune expressed to Council of having the Village do the
billing instead of the waste hauler, asked Council and the Service Committee to
reconsider rebidding the Waste Hauling contract again with the possibility of
saving more money to the residents. The Village would then have a one stop
situation for residents to pay their bills.
Councilman Aho commented to Council that at the last Council meeting Council
voted understanding that the Waste Hauler contract was not being bid out. The
Committee presented Council with a proposal and council elected not to go with
the recommendation from the Committee. Stated he felt the mayor was not sure
which way he wanted to go with on the bids; use lowest bid or best bid. Because
of past experience on using Waste Management which in the last contract was
Northeastern Disposal and they were not the lowest bidder.
Mayor McCune explained in the past we always took the lowest bidder and
Northeastern was not, we accepted that bid. The only reason the Village is
involved with the bidding contract is to save the residents of the Village
money.
Councilman Aho asked the Solicitor for a legal opinion. Stating the Village had
a contract with USA Waste which was assumed by Waste Management. They raised
their rates which gave the Village right to rescind the contract. The Village
chose to entertain other contracts to do our hauling. At what point has the
Village accepted their terms of a increased rate?
Solicitor Lemire told Council Waste Management raised the rates which they has
a right to do. Which in turn gave the Village the right to cancel the contract
and no one has done that. There is no termination on that cancellation right.
If Council wants to cancel the contract and go with someone else the Village
still has the right to do it.
Councilman Aho asked if the Village did the billing, would it help the
citizens?
Mayor McCune told Council, billing ourselves, now the residents can walk in and
pay the bills.
Councilman Aho stated he would like to see direct debt to the residents,
checking accounts if possible.
Clerk-Treasurer Fisher told Council that she has a meeting set up with the bank
on Thursday for that option. Stated it would also help with the billing for the
garbage hauling.
Administrator Weir told Council if we did do our own billing it would lower the
rates that the contractor charged the Village.
Councilman Finger questioned who would tell the waste hauler to pick up the
garbage?
Administrator Weir told Council the new people moving in and out would have to
contact the waste hauler and then the hauler would have to give the Village the
information.
Clerk-Treasurer Fisher told Council when a person moves in they have to come to
the Village and sign up for sewer, so they could also sign up for garbage.
J. Kusar questioned if a tenant does no pay his garbage bill could it be tacked
onto his taxes, also, how do we know if the person is delinquent on their
garbage bill?
Clerk Treasurer told him it could be assessed to his taxes just like the sewer.
But the system will run from the same program as the sewer billing. We will
have the capability to send out delinquent garbage bills.
Mayor McCune told Council that if we bid out the contract again. That it have
everything in the contract that the Village wants.
Councilman Aho questioned, two years ago the proposal had it to do collections
and Council choose not to do collections, Council choose not to go with that in
the contract.
Clerk Treasurer Fisher told Council the system at that time for sewer billing
did not have the capability of doing the garbage billing and there was still a
lot of problems with the sewer system at that time.
Councilman Aho told Council the Village runs under a statutory form of
government not charter. As such, the Village Clerk is elected. Councilman Aho
expressed his concern that we are giving all these administrative things onto
the Clerk and then we come in with a new elected person. We then do not have
any continuity to maintain these administrative type services. Councilman Aho
also stated he wished the law read that we could hire a clerk. No reflection on
our present Clerk, if anything it is a reflection of her ability. Councilman
Aho stated the situation will go back to the Service Committee and be
discussed.

year contract. Also in the bidding process the Village will use the old bid

incorporate the changes recently proposed in the changed contract. For example;
the change of hours and two day collection. The bid spec will be available to a

FORESTRY:
Councilman Aho asked for volunteers to help him on Saturday to trim the lower
branches on the younger trees. This will be done with the direction of a
volunteer arborist.
RECREATION:
Councilman Finger questioned rate increases at the Recreation center and asked
if Council was going to have input with them?
M. Glotzbecker said there would be rate increases effective January 1, 1999.
Mayor McCune said there would be a recommendation coming from the Rec
Department but all prices will be effective January 1, 1999, even if Council
does not approve the rates to a later date. The rates will be retroactive back
to January 1, 1999.
Mayor McCune also stated to Council that the Village residents pay taxes to
support the Community Center and that they pay for the programs or for anything
that goes on at the Community Center, it should be different from what people
pay who do not live in the Village.
FINANCE:
Mayor McCune explained the Income Tax memorandum from the Solicitor. It stated
that the Village can go back legally six years to the people who have not filed
income tax. The tax is collectable back to six years. Central Collection Agency
is basically our contracting agency and they do not have the right to go back.
They just give the Village a list of tax payers who owe.
Councilman Finger questioned if this would fall under the Tax Administration
Department to prepare the lists and the audits, then turn it over to the
Solicitor?
Clerk Treasurer Fisher told Council the way it is set up. The Tax
Administration prepares all information, gets audits and then gives all the
information to the Income Tax Board. They make a recommendation on what to do
then the Solicitor takes legal action.
Solicitor Lemire told Council that some process should be developed which will
provide for notification and a chance to pay their delinquent taxes before
legal actions are taken. CCA does collect the Income Tax for people but they do
not collect the delinquent taxes. That is up to the Village.
Clerk Treasurer Fisher told Council that there is a Income tax questionnaire
that will be going out to all tax payers of the Village by the end of the year.
The employers of the Village will have to give the Village a list of all their
employees.
Councilman Finger asked, now that the Village has determined that it is the Tax
Departments responsibility to follow up with those tax payers who have not
filed or paid. Questioned how is this going to be done?
Clerk-Treasurer Fisher told Council the first step is the questionnaire. When
the information is imputed from the questionnaire we will cross reference that
with the list CCA will give to the Village at the end of the year Then it will
be Councils decision what to do after every thing is cross referenced. Everyone
that lives in the Village will get a form. In the Villages Ordinances it is
mandatory filing for every resident that lives in the Village. When anew person
moves into the Village and comes in to sign up for sewer we have them fill out
the questionnaire. So we have all the information on a new person that moves
into the Village from day one.
Mayor McCune told Council with the local control that the Village will have
with the Income Tax the Village should be 95% successful. We do know that not
everyone that files owes money.
Councilman Aho questioned the questionnaire; stated that in the exemption
certificate we did not have what year the person would be claiming for, and
that there was not a provision for spouses.
Clerk-Treasurer Fisher stated to Council, on the form there is a section for
the spouse at the residence.
Mayor McCune told Council every resident will only get one questionnaire. The
questionnaire when filled out, will give us both the husbands and the spouses
social security numbers. That will then be put into the system.
Clerk-Treasurer Fisher with the exemption section in the questionnaire it is
just for the year. It is mandatory that every resident of the Village file
every year. The residents that are on the Villages file will get a form every
year.
Councilman Aho told Council in our code exemption from our Village income Tax
would be if a person worked outside the Village. A person must file for each
year they are exempt, the form does not state what year.
Mayor McCune said according to the Villages Ordinances the person that pays
taxes in another town receives a 100%credit of anything that is one percent or
more and the resident is liable for anything under one percent.
Councilman Aho still questioned the exemption certificate section on the
questionnaire. He stated if a person filled this out and it states exemption
certificate, when the forms are mailed out in January, they will not file
because they already filled out the exemption certificate from the
questionnaire. The section on the questionnaire is for the Senior Citizens or
any one under the age of 18.
Clerk-Treasurer Fisher told Council that this form is just a questionnaire to
set up the files in our system, they will still have to fill out the mandatory
filing form.
Solicitor Lemire told Council he would look over the questionnaire and get with
the Clerk-Treasurer about any changes.
Councilman Thompson mentioned to Council that the next Ordinance and
Resolutions tonight will be the first reading, but the second meeting in
December the Finance Committee would like to suspend Council rules and pass
them before the year-end.
Motion by Thompson for the first reading of Resolution 2231.
2nd by Stasny
Roll: Aho, yea; Finger, yea; Stasny, yea; Thompson, yea; Ward, yea.

AN ORDINANCE TO AMEND THE APPROPRIATIONS FOR CURRENT EXPENSES AND OTHER
EXPENDITURES OF THE VILLAGE OF JEFFERSON OHIO, DURING THE FISCAL YEAR ENDING
DECEMBER 31, 1999.
Councilman Finger questioned the changes and asked with all the changes we are
adding an additional 313 thousand dollars to the appropriations for the year.
Clerk-Treasurer Fisher explained we are expanding the encumbrance and the
appropriations so funds will not end the year with a negative balance.
Councilman Finger expressed his worry that if every dime is spent that is
appropriated the Village will end the year 1998 with 168,000 dollars so January
1, 1999 will begin with only 168,000 dollars.
Clerk-Treasurer Fisher explained not all appropriations we are amending will be
spent in 1998. There are purchase orders out for various items, the monies will
be spent out in 1999 not 1998.
Councilman Finger said he would rather see fund transfers than increasing that
total appropriations. Also expressed, Bond Council said the Village should have
a 20% margin.
Mayor McCune told Council one year the Village ended the year with $15.00
because of the paperwork in one sense we have it in another we do not.
Mayor McCune also stated that if all the bills come in before December 31, 1998
we would only have 168,000 left. But all the bills will not, they will move
into 1999 and the Village will be receiving new revenues.
Councilman Finger said his age old argument is, we turn in a budget and
appropriations and nothing ever matches.
Mayor McCune told Council that it is hard to match because the monies come in
at different times and it is expended at different times also. In the political
entity it is not like regular business.
Councilman Finger questioned the budget that was done in July 1998.
Clerk-Treasurer Fisher told Council the Tax Budget done in July was for Revenue
only. It did not have anything to do with expenditures. The estimated
expenditures given to the County Auditor is just estimated figures, what the
Village thinks it will spend next year.
Mayor McCune explained to Council the July Tax Budget (wish list) is sent to
the Auditor of the County. Regardless of what we turn in, the Auditor issues us
money according to their prescribed calculations. They tell us what monies we
will receive. The expenditures are just estimated they are not a budget. It is
not stone. Mayor McCune asked Councilman Finger to sit down and talk to Bob
Beacon. All the figures and paperwork were approved at the County Auditors
office , if there are any problems in the process, they tell us how to do it.
Clerk-Treasurer Fisher told Council if she made a mistake she would admit it.
Council approved the tax budget and so did the County Auditors office . The Tax
Budget is only for the Revenues of the Village. The expenditures will be done
when the Village receives the estimated certificate after January 1.
Councilman Finger expressed that he was on vacation when the Tax Budget was
approved and he would talk to Bob Beacom.
Motion by Thompson for the first reading of Ordinance 2234.
2nd by Stasny
Roll: Aho, yea; Finger, yea; Stasny, yea; Thompson, yea; Ward, yea.

Solicitor Lemire explained the three ways of adopting Ordinances and
Resolutions:
1.) Normal way, three readings, it will become law after 30 days after the last
reading.
2.) Suspend council rules and adopt after one or two readings, it will still
become effective thirty days after the adoption.
3.) If it is declared an emergency, it will become effective as soon as it is
passed.

Citizen Kusar questioned the sewer department if it made or lost money on a
yearly basis, how much is left over at year end and, what the percentage
increase is spent on in regards to improvements?
Mayor McCune told Council the sewer department has a General Fund which pays
all the general obligations of the sewer. It also has a Capital Improvements
Fund which pays the note for 2.3 Million and any major improvements that are
needed at the Sewer plant.
Clerk Treasurer Fisher stated she would have the appropriate figures at the
next meeting which would show what the Wastewater Treatment Fund ended with and
what the Sewer Improvement Fund balance is. Told Council that she would give
John Kusar a report after she finishes her year end figures.
Mayor McCune told Council the payment for the sewer notes is paid bi-annually.
The money that is built up is for the loan payments and any Capital
Improvements that is needed. The sewer payments paid by residents are broken
down by a percentage to the Wastewater Fund and Sewer Improvement Fund.
Clerk Treasurer Fisher told Council that the Village spent about 100 thousand
dollars on the lab renovations in 1998.
Administrator Weir told Council that in 1999 the Village will anticipate in
doing 189 thousand dollars in line repairs. Other improvements that have been
done include South Market Street, Maplewood Drive and East Cedar Street. Also
stated that any repairs that are done, the equipment is not cheap and there is
money put aside to buy it.
Citizen Jim Reuschling expressed to Council his concern with the Resolution on
the Subdivisions regulation. Told Council he felt that with the changes that it
would increase the costs of lots, because the Village is adding sidewalks,
curbing and storm sewers. When the lot increases up 110 thousand dollar ranch,
jumps up to 150 thousand dollars. When a subdivision is built in Ashtabula
County it can not be priced like you are building a house. The cost must be
projected with a ten year cycle.
Mayor McCune told Council that if each developer sat in a Council seat and
listened to the residents of the Village, that are living on dirt streets in
developments, that they bought with the promise that it would be paved after X
number of lots were sold. Now, instead they have to pay to have it paved.
Citizen Jim Reuschling questioned the sewer laterals and the distance from the
sidewalks to the sewers also questioned if sidewalks were necessary. Wanted to
know in the new subdivisions, who was going to take care of the green spaces.
Mayor McCune explained that the Village has always taken care of the greens and
will continue to do so. The subdivision regulation are being changed to protect
the residents and set up lots that will be able to put a nice sized home with a
garage on them and have a subdivision with sidewalks, curbing and storm sewers.
Citizen Jim Reuschling told Council no matter what the subdivision regulations
are changed to, as a contractor he will build them and still make money.

Visitors Comments:
Bill Skidmore of Waste Management of Chardon Ohio addressed Council about the
bid that was submitted last week, passed out a hand out about the bid. Told
Council that Waste Management was the only bidder to submit a complete bid.
Referred to section 9 of the specifications that required bidders to submit a
bid for the contractor to provide cards. Stated that the Orange Bag program was
35 cents less than the next closest bidder. Also expressed that Waste
Management has the strongest financial position in the industry. The service
expectations has set those standards of service for the Village of Jefferson
pertained in section 14 and 19 of the bid.
Introduced the drivers that do the Jefferson Contract. Told Council that Al
Dodge has worked 32 years hauling trash and is a resident in the Village and
does the Villages contract. Introduced Robert Hamilton, who is also a resident
of the Village and is working on the contract that does the Villages hauling.
Introduced Russ Wiles of the team that does the Villages contract, told Council
that he has worked with Al Dodge for eleven years. Stated that Waste Management
has a fleet of over seventy pieces of equipment. 30 which can specifically
service the Village. Reminded Council that three years ago they awarded
Northeastern Disposal the contract which was 20 cents per month higher than the
next closest bidder because of their service. Now that company is Waste
Management. Northeastern Disposal was bought out by Waste Management last year.
Told Council that they provided the Village with the best and most qualified
bid.
Citizen John Kusar expressed his feelings about Waste Management, stated that
he got rid of his commercial account because of their service. Told Council
that they should look at the lowest and best bid. Stated that he felt Waste
Management is a huge corporation and you will never talk to the same person
twice and money does not provide good service.
Louis Popovich of Country Disposal told Council he crossed every T and dotted
every I in the contract. Stated he was legal and presented everything to the
Village that they asked for. Said to Council in violating the Villages
contract, if he did he would loose a lot of money. Expressed to Council he
would lose his bond money. Expressed that he only has 4 trucks but only one is
needed to do the Village. Also stated if the need ever happened, he would go
out and get the garbage himself to make sure the Village garbage was picked up.
Stated his references speak for themselves and also stated if his service is
not good enough to please the Village then the Village can break the contract
anytime. All the tax money stays in Ashtabula County.
Bob Pifr of Country Disposal said he has been driving truck for Country
Disposal for over ten years and their service is second to none. They take the
time to put the lids back on the cans and put the cans four feet away from the
road. If there is a complaint, the driver calls the customer back, they are
just a phone call away to solve the problem.

2nd by Herndon
Roll: Aho, yea; Finger, yea; Herndon, yea; Stasny, yea; Thompson, yea; Ward,

Citizen John Kusar still had questions on the 33% increase in sewer rates which
was done when the Treatment Plant was updated and a OWDA Loan was taken out.
Questioned that the Village carried over for 1998 $117,759.79. Stated it was
almost enough for the loan payment. Asked where is the 33% increase going and
what it is going to? And why are we carrying over so much.
Councilman Finger told Council that in 1998 the Sewer Improvement Fund started
the year out with $253,238.40 received in, $195,641.20 spent, $374,604.14 if
the fund is run down to nothing there will not be money in 1999 to spend
$180,000 to fix the sewers in the Village. Councilman Finger also stated that
money is carried over until there is enough to take on big sewer project
repairs or etc.
Citizen John Kusar asked the Clerk to get information on how much money did the
sewer fund carry over before the 33% sewer increase was put into effect.
Questioned when the increase was done it was done to pay for the improvements
to the loan.
Solicitor Lemire stated to council that the EPA loan could not be passed
without updating the the sewer rates.
Administrator Weir told Council that the 33% rate increase was done basically
to cover the cost of the construction. A rate has to be shown to the EPA that
will show the Village can repay the loan and maintain the plant and add capital
Improvements.
Councilman Aho told Council that this fund is a propriety fund, the monies that
go into that fund stay in that fund and do not go into any General Revenue. If
that fund was to get too large of a balance it could cause a rate reduction or
if there is a deficit a rate increase in the future.
Citizen John Kusar said to Council , maybe the increase was needed a few years
ago but right now the more gallons that are being put into the system is making
it more cost effective. The plant is running at 50% capacity and when new
houses are coming on line they are generating more money.
Administrator Weir told Council that to run the Sewer Plant cost a lot of money
and the Village has never gone in the other direction in spending less money or
staying the same.
Citizen John Kusar also asked Council to look at the Ordinance pertaining to
the consumption use in the water to the billing in sewer based upon water
usage. Even if the water does not go through the sewer plant. The Ordinance
that the Village has now states if it went through the water meters you have to
pay. But the Ordinance protects the Village if the meter does not work.
Questioned why it would not work if a pipe breaks for a customer. Asked the
Wastewater Committee to look at the Ordinance to see if when a water pipe
breaks there can be some help to the customer with the sewer bill.
Councilman Finger told Council there would be a Wastewater Committee meeting in
the near future. Asked to have all figures for the last five years from the
Wastewater Funds.

Wastewater Treatment:
Councilman Finger discussed the draft for the update on the Phase II
Improvements, told Council that this draft updated the report dated September
1992 to give the Village current costs to what it would be to finish sewer
lines in the Village. The update went through November 1998. The only change
from the last draft was the map. The change was in the cross hatch patterns in
the area I and on West Jefferson. This shows the ability to extend sewers in
that area. The difference in the cross hatch patterns is it shows what is in
the Village and what area is Township. The Village is looking at the ability to
develop that area for Village purposes. The position of the Village is it not
going to pay to develop sewer. It is up to the person in that area to pay if
they want to develop the area for sewers.
Administrator Weir told Council that the Villages Master Sewer Plan has also
been updated to reflect the same changes so everything is current and up to
date.
Administrator Weir told Council that the Village has the preliminary plans for
the sewer lining project. A application has been submitted to small governments
for funding. In April the Village will find out if the project will be funded
through small governments.

Service:
Councilman Aho questioned the recycling center.
Administrator Weir stated that the hours were generally 5 days a week, weekends
people can drop items off but there is not anyone at the center. He explained
the bins and how they are separated.
Roland Ferguson explained that we separate the magazines which should be tied
in bundles, cardboard, and newspapers in brown paper bags, we accept No. 1 and
No. 2 clear and colored plastics , no lids; tin cans, aluminum cans. Basically
the center is open 24 hours a day, we do not encourage people to use the center
at night, because no one is there, but the County is going to install a light
at the center. Daytime is the best time, there are pamphlets at the Town Hall
with information about the center.
Councilman Finger noted that the center is a County site, anyone can use the
recycling center.

AN ORDINANCE TO PROVIDE THE APPROPRIATIONS FOR CURRENT EXPENSES AND OTHER
EXPENDITURES OF THE VILLAGE OF JEFFERSON, OHIO DURING THE FISCAL YEAR ENDING
DECEMBER 31, 1999.
Councilman Finger questioned some of the figures from last years appropriations
to this years increases and decreases. The questions included the Street
Maintenance Fund going from $63,750.00 down to $54,250.00, the Solicitors -
Attorneys Fund - asked why it was $70,000.00 more that last year; Capital
Projects Sidewalk Road Fund last year it was $300,000.00 this year it is at
$177,781.00; State Highway Improvement Fund last year was at $8,000.00 this
year it is at $38,000.00; Special Fire Apparatus Fund last year $91,000.00 this
year $193,179.09.
Clerk-Treasurer Fisher explained to Council that the Street Maintenance was
lower this year because the wages were moved to some of the other Street Funds,
so it would not be taken mostly from the General Fund. The attorney fund is
higher because of the legal fees for the process with the Water Company. The
Capital Projects, Sidewalk, Road Funds were lowered because the Village is not
paving as much this year because of the amount of paving done in the last
couple years. The State Highway Improvement Fund is higher because of the
purchase of a new truck for the Streets. Half would be taken out of this fund
and half will be taken out of the Capital Improvements Fund. The Fire Apparatus
Fund is higher because of the purchase of the new Fire Truck Cab and Chassis.
Motion by Thompson for the first reading of Ordinance 2243.
2nd by Herndon
Councilman Finger questioned the Wage Ordinance ; why there was not a wage
increase for all the positions in the Wage Ordinance?
Clerk-Treasurer Fisher told Council there was not a wage increase put in the
Wage Ordinance in the positions that were unfilled. Told Council that the
procedure had been followed the same way it was done last year.
Councilman Finger expressed his disagreement with the procedure and said the
positions will start to overlap in time.
After a long discussion Council decided to give all positions the same wage
increase even if the position is unfilled.
Motion by Finger to amend Ordinance 2243 to have all positions with a 45¢ wage
increase.
2nd by Aho
Roll: Aho, yea; Finger, yea; Herndon, yea; Stasny, yea; Thompson, yea.

purchasing the expenses will be charged under Administration.

Department and the Wastewater Department; the supplies are taken out of the
Administration Department because of central purchasing. The Departments in
their budget do not get appropriated monies for supplies.
Councilman Ward commented to Council, in regards to the Police; there was a
pager case and the Police do use pagers. Stated that this should be added to
part of the equipment for the Police uniform and updated in the codified
ordinances.
Visitors Comments:
Resident Cayce Baxley expressed her opinion on the Village getting involved and
making an Ordinance for the smoking problem at the school. Stated that the
problem has been going on forever and that the school asking the Police
Department to help has gone too far. Noted that it is not the Villages place to
control the students, it is the school authorities place to suspend students
and site if need be.
Mayor McCune told Council that the Police Chief and the Safety Committee are
looking over that problem.

Committee Reports
Buildings/Lands -
Councilman Finger discussed the new zoning map. Stated that the new map will
show all the
annexed properties. There are sections on the map that show nonconforming
properties, there
are almost 45 properties that are nonconforming . The properties could be
Multi-family, Residential, or Commercial. About 42 of the 45 properties that
are multifamily are located
in commercial or residential properties. The next to the last of nonconforming
properties
will be to put what it is zoned for and what the non-conformity is. The non-
conforming
properties pre date the existence of zoning. The laws protect the properties
with the way they
are zoned. The Village should notify these property owners and tell them they
do have a non-
conforming property and tell them what their rights are.

Administrator Weir explained to Council that all the parcels reflect what is
current now in the way the parcels are in the Village. The map was then build
up to scale showing how everything is
zoned such as commercial property, multi-family, residential, the business
district and all of the
nonconforming properties and conditional properties. Everything shown on the
map is up to date.

Solicitor Lemire expressed that the Village should tell the non conformed
property owners what
the status of their property is. The other issue that has to be talked about is
there are several
properties that do not have legal non conforming status. These properties do
not fall in the
non conforming definition under the code of the Village. The Village should
make the zoning code fit to the reality of the zoning that was approved.

Councilman Finger expressed to Council that there were permits issued to some
property
owners in violation of the zoning text.

AN ORDINANCE AMENDING SECTION 248.08 OF THE CODIFIED ORDINANCES
OF THE VILLAGE OF JEFFERSON PERTAINING TO THE POLICE DEPARTMENT
UNIFORM ALLOWANCE.

Councilman Finger questioned that shoe allowance for the Police Department had
been taken out in the last Ordinance because of the steel-toe shoe. He also
questioned if the Village was going to
specify the type of shoe and make it part of the uniform , if not we are giving
the department a blanket of $150.00 for shoes.

Councilman Ward stated to Council than in the Codified Ordinance book it is
part of the uniform.

Solicitor Lemire read section 248.08 b of the Code book. It read that
standardized uniforms to be worn by the Police Department. The uniform includes
both equipment and clothing necessary
for normal daily and season requirements. The department head determines the
make up of the
required uniform in consolation with department members and the Safety
Committee of Council.
Solicitor Lemire stated that the uniform requirement had a loose definition and
the Chief has a lot
of the determination what the uniform is. Also, he stated with the new
Ordinance it is implying
that shoes are not in the uniform Ordinance. We are making a new Ordinance just
for shoes.

Mayor McCune explained to Council the separate section in the uniform allowance
for shoes was to make certain that there would be an allowance for shoes
because it was just left in the uniform
section of the Ordinance "boots" would be left out by the patrolman and this
would make sure
the patrolman has correct shoes.

Councilman Finger expressed his concern that there was no restriction on the
150.00 dollars allowance for shoes they could buy what they wanted.

Motion by Thompson for the first reading of Ordinance 2257
2nd by Herndon

Roll: Aho, yea; Finger, yea; Herndon, yea; Stasny, yea; Thompson, yea; Ward,
yea.

AN ORDINANCE AMENDING SECTION 60.01 OF THE VILLAGE OF JEFFERSON'S
PERSONNEL RULES AND REGULATIONS PERTAINING TO PHYSICAL EXAMINATIONS; REPEALING
ORDINANCES, RESOLUTIONS, RULES AND REGULATIONS IN CONFLICT THEREWITH AND
DECLARING AN EMERGENCY.

Councilman Finger questioned what the emergency was.

Mayor McCune explained to Council that if we go through the three readings and
30 days; physical examinations can come back very costly to the Village, just
like a few have already done so. The Ordinance will state exactly what the
physical will cover.

Councilman Finger questioned the source from which the points covered in the
new Ordinance
came from.

Solicitor Lemire stated it came from the Committee.

Mayor McCune told Council that this basic physical examination should just
identify if there is any problems. Then the employee will go to their doctor
under our health care plan and get it diagnosed. What has happened now a single
examination turned into a blown out diagnostic exam which then costs the
Village money.

Clerk Treasurer Fisher told Council employees covered under the Villages plan ,
a basic physical
is covered for $10.00.

examinations as an emergency to set some stipulations on physicals to prevent a
routine physical turning into a major examination. Council agreed that this
Ordinance would be looked over and have all areas addressed with certain
provisions.

President Pro Temp Thompson addressed the Council and Residents of the Village,
stating
that the Village Council understands that there are concerns and questions in
the new refuse
collection. Stated for the record that the problem began in 1993 with Ordinance
2002. The
questions brought up were residents with concerns that the Council had passed a
Ordinance
requiring all residents who own single, two or three family residents, that
they would be required
to put their garbage out and have it picked up. The facts are the Ordinance was
passed in 1993
with one amendment which was to give residents one year to make the transition
from the
previous collector to the collector that the Village had a contract with. A lot
of the concerns
that have surfaced since the change of the new collector and lower refuse rates
have come
about, since the Village is doing the billing. Council is aware of the concerns
and the Council
will address and work on the problems.
Visitors Comments:
Citizen Kusar addressed Council with his concerns with the present Ordinance.
Stated the
Ordinance requires him to pay for a commercial dumpster and also pay for his
residential refuse
because he has a commercial dumpster and it is not contracted through the same
contractor
as the Village uses. Also expressed concern that if the refuse was not paid,
that the Village
could assess the property taxes or take the land owner to small claims court.
Told Council that there should be some considerations to the Ordinance. If a
person does not have refuse because they have other means of getting rid of
their refuse , the Village should not
bill them if they do not use the service.

Administrator Weir addressed Council stating that the trash Ordinance that was
passed in 1993 was done to reduce the cost for the majority of residents in the
the Village that have single family homes. In doing so, the Village has saved
residents of the Village about 67 thousand dollars the first year to date the
residents have saved about 300 thousand dollars in trash hauling and about 99%
of the people are happy.

Council discussed the issue of a replacement or a renewal of the 1.75 mil for
the current
operating expenses. The Finance Committee recommended that the Village should
go with a replacement.

Councilman Finger questioned why the Village was going with a replacement and
stated that this would be a increase in taxes.

President Pro Temp Thompson expressed to Council that in the Finance Committee
meeting the Committee chose to do a replacement because every person that the
Village does business has
locked their prices and the cost of living goes up every year.

Clerk - Treasurer Fisher explained to Council the General Operating Levy which
is a five year
levy at 1.75 the Village receives in tax revenues about $46,782.62. The
assessed valuations
since the levy was voted in has gone up. The assessed valuation of real estate
property in 1997
is $44,457.55. The County Auditors Office told the Village today, if the levy
was done with a
replacement the Village would receive in taxes about $75,369.00.

Clerk-Treasurer Fisher told Council at the last Finance meeting the Committee
chose to do a replacement because the operating expenses of the Village keep
going up every year and to
run the Village properly the extra revenue would be needed.

Roll: Aho, yea; Finger, nea; Herndon, yea; Stasny, yea; Thompson, yea; Ward,
yea.

Buildings/Lands -
Solicitor Lemire explained to Council the Special Improvements District. The
process that the two public entities will take; included in the two entities
are the Township and Village explained what they will have to do. The steps
that the residents on West Mulberry street will have to follow now, since they
have turned in their petitions and the process in which the Special
Improvements District needs to follow. Lemire told Council that it was going to
take time, money and involvement from Council and the Residents on West
Mulberry street. Lemire explained
that once the Village has the petition the Special District has to also bring
forth to the Village Article of Incorporation and a plan, the Village then has
the duty to react within 60 days to approve or disapprove of the District.
Council discussed the issue and expressed concern with
costs that will occur with attorney fees. Discussed if the attorney fees could
be assessed and who should pay for this up front. After a long discussion it
was recommended that the Building and
Lands Committee have a meeting to discuss all the issues and send a letter to
all the residents
of West Mulberry Street, what steps have to be followed.

Councilman Finger announced a Building and Lands Committee meeting, Monday, May
10,
1999 at 7:00 p.m. Subject will be to discuss the Special Improvements District.

Administrator Weir explained to Council that the Village is going to try to get
some Issue II
finding or small governments.
Safety -
Councilman Ward explained to Council that a lot of time was put into this
Ordinance enacting
comprehensive regulations pertaining to tobacco products and information was
collected by
all different sources. Ward expressed to Council that right now there is no
State laws that
regulate the use of the possession of tobacco products by minors. Stated that
this Ordinance
would give the Village Police the means to try and correct a problem that is
out there.

Motion by Ward for the first reading of Ordinance 2261.
2nd by Herndon

Councilman Finger asked Council why do we think that making criminals out of
youngsters
that posses and smoke tobacco products, is going to cure the problem.

Councilman Ward stated to Council, right now there is no law that can help the
police officers.

Councilman Finger told Council that the State of Ohio has chosen not to make it
a crime, and we,
the Village, are now saying that we choose to make it a crime. Finger expressed
that the
Village is trying to do positive things for the youth and in doing this, it
would be a negative towards the youth. Also stated, the Village is putting a
social implication on smoking that is
no where else in criminal law.

Councilman Aho expressed to Council the concern that the law would make it all
right for a minor
to smoke in the Township but as soon as the minor would cross into the Village
the minor would
be sited for violating the Ordinance. Noted that not everyone entering the
limits would know the laws.

Councilwoman Herndon told Council that the Village should start somewhere.

Citizen Cayce Baxley told Council that the law would hurt the parents not the
kids. Also,
note that the parents would be the one paying for the fines and having to take
the child to court.

Roll: Aho, nay; Finger, nay ; Herndon, yea; Stasny, nay; Thompson, yea; Ward,
yea.

Councilman Finger explained to Council the zoning district change for the
Jefferson Fraternal
Order of Eagles Building on 152 East Erie Street. Explained that they want to
tear down the existing building and rebuild a new Eagles Building . This
property is currently zoned residential
and is a non conforming use in the residential area. Under the existing code
they can improve the
structure by 10%. The only way they can tear down the building and rebuild is
to the zoning changed from residential to industrial. The reason that this
zoning change involved being changed
to industrial is if it were changed to commercial the Village would be doing
spot zoning. If it
is put under industrial, commercial can be in under industrial.

Councilman Finger questioned the paragraph on page four with the Clerk-
Treasurer concerning the 1.75 milage.

Mayor McCune explained to Council that he had discussed the 1.75 milage with
County Auditor. The original evaluation was done in 1996 and with a evaluation
taxes do change. When a levy is
renewed the taxes still stay the same as when the levy was originally passed
and the milage then will be given to the Village at the assessed evaluation
rate of when the levy was passed. The
1.75 milage levy that we are talking about was originally passed in 1976. The
mileage today,
if the levy is replaced will be about $75,000.00. The number that was given to
us from the County Auditors Office were correct. Each time the property is
evaluated the taxes will not change unless the milage is replaced. A renewal
will make the taxes stay at the same as when the levy was passed. This is noted
in these minutes to correct the minutes from the last meeting.

Councilman Finger also stated on page five of the minutes; he could not let
citizen Cayce Baxley
explanation stand, because it is also incorrect information. Citizen Cayce
Baxley's comment
stated that a replacement levy would only hurt people buying a new home or
people building
a new home.

Mayor McCune told Council the everyone will be taxed at the new evaluation when
the
replacement levy is passed. So the taxes will increase to the new assessed
evaluation.

Councilman Finger told Council the 1.75 milage ordinance is a replacement which
will cause a
increase in revenue to the Village.

Citizen Cayce Baxley told Council what she was referring to was the cost of
houses have gone up considerably within the last ten years, and with that in
building and buying homes, the base price
has increased.

AN ORDINANCE AUTHORIZING THE JEFFERSON VILLAGE ADMINISTRATOR TO ENTER INTO A

Motion by Ward to adopt Ordinance 2265.
2nd by Thompson.

Roll: Aho yea, Finger yea, Herndon yea, Stasny yea, Thompson yea, Ward yea.

Councilman Finger gave to all Council people, a copy of the first draft in the
zoning text, from Building and Lands Committee meeting. Told Council that there
were a lot of definition changes in the new zoning text, to help with problems
that face the Zoning Inspector. He explained that the major areas of change
were in section 1242-04, which covers all new construction in residential and
commercial areas to include sidewalks. Stated the enforcement area had wording
changes that could be used by the Village Planning Commission to address the
architectural review process. This gives our Planning Commission the
opportunity to look over plans and cause negotiation to the builder. Went over
the area with the changes in the home occupation section. Noted the new changes
in the signage section. Asked everyone in Council to be sure to look over and
read it before it goes forth into Ordinance form. Solicitor Lemire told Council
that it is a zoning change so it would go to the Planning Commission for a
review, then back to Council with a public hearing, to have input from the
residents.

Council discussed the Planning Commissions roles and powers that they have in
the building process with the developer.

Solicitor Lemire explained to Council the new wording in the zoning text that
would allow the Zoning Inspector to send a zoning permit to the Planning
Commission to look over the plans and make sure it meets all the criteria. Then
they would send it back to the Zoning Inspector for a permit after approval.

Council set up a work session for Thursday, July 8, 1999, at 8:00 p.m. to go
over the new zoning text.
Public Hearing -
Clerk - Treasurer Fisher explained to Council the tax budget process. Stated
that this budget is really a wish list. That figures are given to the County
Auditors office. The County Auditors gives the Village revenue figures that are
allocated to the Village by the formula that is set up for the break down of
revenue. Expressed to Council that what figures the Village gives to the
Auditors office, the Village will only receive what they allocate from that
formula. They do not give by showing a need for the money. Clerk - Treasurer
Fisher told Council that a budget hearing will be set up by the
County Auditors office in August, to go over the tax budget. An Ordinance will
then come back to
Council to accept what revenue is given to the Village by the Auditors office.
