A RESOLUTION ACCEPTING THE UNDIVIDED LOCAL GOVERNMENT & REVENUE ASSISTANCE
ALLOCATIONS.

Motion by Thompson for the second reading of Amended Ordinance 2266.
2nd by Herndon.
Discussion
Councilman Finger told Council the current salary of the Clerk - Treasurer is
20,000 dollars plus
6 ½ percent of the PERS pickup, to equal 21,300 dollars. According to Ordinance
the new Ordinance will increase the salary to 33,000 dollars plus the 6 ½
percent pickup of PERS to equal 35,140 dollars, for a 13,845 dollar a year
increase. This amounts to 6.92 an hour and the newspaper said it would be less
than a dollar an hour.

Mayor McCune explained to Council that the new Ordinance will set the salary
for the up coming elected Clerk - Treasurer. He told Council that the Clerk -
Treasurers salary was set back in 1992. Council had set it at what they felt
the Clerks position was worth. April 1, 1997 all of Council agreed to give the
Clerk a raise because of the job being done. But because the position is
elected, law prohibits intern raises. So Council decided to put in a salary for
the Utility Billing Clerk, to increase the Clerks salary. April 1, 1997 it was
increased by 5,000 dollars. April 1, 1998 it was increased by another 1,000
dollars to make it 6,000 dollars and April 1, 1999 it was increased another
1,000 dollars to make it 7,000 dollars. The pay of our Clerk & Utility Clerk
totals 27,000 dollars. Each employee for each of the last four years, has
received a 996.00 dollar raise. When broken down the Clerks is about 1083.00
for twelve years if you would go back to the last pay increase for the Clerks
position.
The next raise for the Clerk will be April 1, 2005. With the passing of this
Ordinance the Utility Billing Clerks position will be abolished. The Clerks
combined salary will increase from 27,000 dollars to 33,000 dollars, which is a
six thousand dollar increase over the four years. The Clerk is the Utility
Billing Clerk, she is the supervisor over the billing.

Citizen Caycey Baxley questioned the abolishment of the Utility Billing Clerk
because by law you can not add duties to Clerk-Treasurer and combining the
duties ten years from now another Clerk could say they are not doing the extra
duties.

Mayor McCune told Council that the Clerk - Treasurer has job descriptions
mandated by the Ohio Revised Code. Also stated again she is the head of the
utility billing.

Councilman Thompson told Council that in his mind the Clerks salary was 23,000
dollars. We have been working on this for four years. The Finance Committee
came up with the salary with recommendation from the Mayor.

Councilman Aho discussed the survey for the Clerks salary and the Villages
population. Stated the survey is invalid with only the response of three people
and twice as many Villages reported the Clerks position as part time. Stated he
is not arguing the hours but asked what does the Village need, a full time or
part time clerk.

Councilman Ward stated to Council all that is needed by the Clerk is to get the
job done regardless of what hours it takes.

Citizen John Kusar asked Council to leave the Clerk - Treasurers salary at one
rate and keep the Utility Billing Clerks position. Because what if someone else
runs and wins and then we are back to a Clerk that only works three days a week
and is getting paid 33,000 dollars. Council cannot define the Clerks work hours
because it is an elected position. The Village is lucky now that they have a
good clerk and she wants to work with everyone.

Roll: Aho nea, Finger nea, Herndon yea, Stasny yea, Thompson yea, Ward yea.

Public Hearing
Mayor McCune told Council that the public hearing was set up for the rezoning
of the Jefferson Fraternal Order of Eagles. The rezoning would change from
residential to industrial if approved by Council. The address of the Eagles
Club is 152 East Erie Street.
Solicitor Lemire swore in all parties interested in speaking at the public
hearing.
Jeff Otto, representing the Jefferson Fraternal Order of Eagles expressed that
the club wanted to build a new building. Stated that the club is not just
another bar. The members of the club donate many hours to programs in the
Village and outside the Village to help people young and old. Told Council that
adding to the building would also help the community. The hall would be able to
be used for festivities, such as open houses, weddings, family reunions, etc.
Asked Council to consider the facts of the project and give the Eagles Club the
opportunity to help themselves also.

Richard Jones spoke to Council with opposition to rezone the Eagles Club from
residential to industrial. Spoke of concern as to what it would do to the
property value of residents in the area. Expressed to Council that residents
have put storm sewer pipes in to make tree lawns and the residents in the area
want to keep it beautiful and safe for their families. Also noted in the last
couple of years that they have already rezoned property around the area of the
Eagles Club to fit needs of the land owners. Told Council if this was changed
they would be approving spot zoning and there would be an industrial strip in
the middle of a residential and park area. Richard Jones told Council he was
not against the Eagles Club building a new building. What he was concerned with
is the rezoning within the Village and changing residential to industrial. Also
asked why the property is operating under a nonconforming use.

Terri Toukenon Spoke to Council representing the Ashtabula Construction Co. as
the builder for the Eagles Club. Spoke about the size and plans for the new
building. Explained to Council that the parking area was why the Eagles had to
rezone the property. Told Council that the new building would beautify the
area. Before applying for a zoning permit the Eagles Club sent the plans to the
Eagles Chapter for approval for the new building. Stated that before it became
the Eagles Club it was the American Legion. There has been a private club
located on that property for 47 years. Terri also said with the new building
there would be a new alarm system installed and that the Eagle Club wants to
help the community by renting it out to the public for parties etc. Also
expressed that with any new plans for building that the Eagles Club needs to
get the maximum use of space and monies being spent.

Residents of the Village spoke up with concerns of traffic noise and safety,
with the issue of putting in another driveway on Cedar Street.

Terri Toukenon told Council that if the residents were concerned with another
driveway, that the Eagles Club may consider a deed reduction.

Councilman Ward commented that information was provided to the Planning
Commission that was not accurate concerning the zoning, on the property owned
by the county. That the outcome of the vote may have been different had the
Planning Commission been given the correct information regarding the fact that
a portion of the county property was zoned residential. Councilman Ward
commented that the correct information would have been a factor with his vote.

Councilman Finger commented on the Planning Commissions vote and recommendation
also.

Administrator Weir commented to all present, that no one else other than he was
responsible for unintentionally misinforming the Planning Commission and agreed
that more than likely the outcome of the vote by the Planning Commission would
have been different had the Planning Commission had the correct information.
Discussion preceded regarding a possible lot split and retaining a portion of
the lot on E. Cedar as residential and providing a deed restriction to prevent
access to East Cedar Street.

Councilman Aho told Council that the issue before them is zoning not the plans
or the intention for how the building is being used.

Buildings and Lands:
Councilman Finger noted in the Council packets there was a re application for
the Eagles property. In the application it calls for the property to be split
into two parcels. One parcel being the fronting on Erie Street to be industrial
and parcel two on Cedar Street, leaving the parcel that joins up with the
county property, as residential which is the size of 133 feet by 200 feet.

Administrator Weir told Council, in talking with the applicant they have
started the process of splitting the property. But they do not want to follow
totally through with the split until they are reasonably sure that they will be
approved for the zoning change.

Councilman Finger questioned the restriction that was discussed at the public
hearing.

Administrator Weir stated that the restriction was not included with the
application.

Councilman Aho commented that Council should not send the application to the
Planning Commission until it is complete (the separation of parcel and the
covenant in place).

Administrator Weir told Council he suggested to the applicant to have all of
that in place prior to the application being processed.

Mayor McCune told Council that once the application is filed the village has 30
days to act on the application.

Councilman Finger brought up the discussion that took place in the public
meeting, the citizen input for concern was spot zoning residential area and
traffic pattern extended to Cedar Street. The new application addresses one
issue by the citizens and at this point does not address the second issue.

Council discussed the issue with the application and stated if the parcels were
separated and the covenant put into parcel two, preventing the driveway, they
may be for the zoning change and sending it onto the Planning Commission. It
was discussed that previously the Planning Commission agreed to propose to
change the entire property to industrial. Council then voted it down. Question
was brought up, if the Commission approves it this may happen again. It was
then agreed by Council that they would have to hear public opinion again and
have the deeds and paperwork all completed before being sent back to the
Planning Commission.

Motion by Ward to send the rezoning application for the Eagles Club back to the
Planning Commission.
2nd by Finger

Caycey Baxley expressed concern to Council that the Eagles Club should split
the land and change the parcel then go to the Planning Commission, not make the
changes if and when the Planning Commission approves the application.

Mayor McCune expressed to Council that when the Planning Commission approved
the rezoning, they acted in good faith to what was the best way for the Eagles
Club to build on their property.

Administrator Weir told Council that he recommended to the Eagles Club that
when they come in to reapply for the zoning change to have the lot split before
it went to the Planning Commission.
Administrator Weir also explained to Council that if there is a district that
splits a lot, the district line then does not follow the lot line. The Zoning
Board of appeals then has the power to extend the district to the nearest lot
line.

Councilman Finger, after discussion withdrew his second motion.

August 16, 1999
Meeting was called to order by Mayor McCune

Roll: Aho, Finger, Herndon, Stasny, Thompson, Ward.

Also Present: Daniel Allman and son, Beverly Finger, Marilyn Aho, Jerald March,
Terri Toukonen, Bob Lister, Mike Bittner, Jeff Otto, Gazette, Star Beacon, News
Harold.

Councilman Finger wanted changes in the Minutes dated July 19, 1999. On page
six, the sentence which says so much is set up for the Clerk-Treasurer and
still have the Utility Billing Supervisors position. Take out the word
supervisor and only have the Utility Billing Clerk. Councilman Aho questioned
the Minutes dated August 2, 1999, if there were Minutes for the executive
session.

Solicitor Lemire told council that he would have to look into whether there
should be Minutes for the executive sessions.

Councilman Aho brought the questioned Council, Mayor and Solicitor if the
executive session at the last meeting was done properly. Stated that the
session was done improperly under Section 122. It does not allow you to go in
simply for personnel reasons. The Attorney General has made a statement that
you must be more specific than personnel.

Solicitor Lemire explained to Council the statue that governs it all. It states
that when councils go into an executive session under personnel reasons,
council needs to state the purpose and not specify the person. There should be
a more specific statement such as executive session for personnel for pay
increases, personnel for a possible reprimand, the statue gives you a set of
adjectives that should be utilized when councils actually go into an executive
session for personnel reasons.

Councilman Aho also questioned the motion that was passed after the executive
session whether it was proper. Because the motion asked for a special audit,
which is a financial matter not a personnel issue in which the executive
session was asked for. Also expressed to Council that executive sessions should
be done by law and followed properly.

Solicitor Lemire told council that in the last executive session council did
not designate a proper topic. The statue provides the following items are
suitable for discussion in the personnel area:
Appointment, employment, dismissal, discipline, promotion, demotion,
compensation of a public employer or official, and investigation of charges or
complex. One of these topics should be mentioned when you call an executive
session for personnel. This was not done in the last executive session so
Council was in violation of the statue.

Councilman Aho also stated to Council when going into an executive session you
cannot use the persons' name but once you are in the executive session you can.
The person could request a public hearing that the executive session was called
for.

Councilman Finger asked to have the discussion of the parallel that was drawn
to the Nemet property added to the minutes. Added from the meeting is the
discussion.

Administrator Weir explained to Council that on the Nemet property the district
line did not follow the lot line that actually split the lot. So the Zoning
Board of Appeals has the power to extend that district to the nearest lot line
unless the lot is split off. This issue is that one parcel was split into two
districts. This is the fear that Council has if the Eagles Club is zoned into
two separate parcels.

The Minutes will stand as written with the additions.

Administrator Weir explained to Council that the application is different from
the last one. They are rezoning less of the parcel than originally planned. The
new ordinance reflects the changes that were submitted.

Councilman Finger explained what was being submitted to the Planning Commission
is one parcel of land with split zoning on that parcel. The north end is being
asked to be rezoned industrially with the south end of the parcel being left
residential. Expressed to Council that if they approve the zoning changes there
is nothing to stop the industrial piece from being extended all the way
through.

Terri Toukenon explained to Council that in the Eagles application the proposal
is to split the parcel into two separate parcels. They will redo the deed so
there is a deed for the residential section that faces Cedar Street and another
deed for the parcel that would be industrial. There will not be any
restrictions added to the deed that has a residential parcel. The Eagles Club
would like to have the Planning Commissions approval before the split is done.
So when it comes to Council for a vote it will be two separate pieces of
property.

Councilman Aho noted to Council that council does not overturn without five
votes. The ultimate authority is Council but the Planning Commission has a lot
of power.

Councilman Ward questioned the solicitor. What council sends to the Planning
Commission isn't necessarily what comes back from the Planning Commission, is
that correct?

Solicitor Lemire told Council when someone applies for a zoning change, Council
has the duty to send it to the Planning commission for review. The Planning
Commission will review and make a decision to approve or disapprove it. When it
comes back to Council for their decision, to overcome what the Planning
Commission has decided, a five vote margin is needed. To adopt what the
Planning Commission has voted on you need a majority vote.

last Monday of August.

September 7, 1999
Meeting was called to order by Mayor McCune

Roll: Aho, Finger, Herndon, Stasny, Thompson, Ward.

Also Present: Madge Lehnert, Terri Toukonen, Larry Bragga, Caysey Baxley,
Jerald March, Marc Glotzbecker, Beverly Finger, Richard Jones and First Merit.

Councilman Ward questioned page five of the minutes. The statement made by the
solicitor "What council sends to the Planning Commission isn't necessarily what
comes back from the Planning Commission." He wanted to make sure the
Solicitor's statement was correct.

Solicitor Lemire told council what he stated in that paragraph was true.

Councilman Ward then asked, if his statement is true, can the Planning
Commission act on something other than what council has sent to them.

Solicitor Lemire told council "no" the Planning Commission cannot act on
something other than what council has sent them. He also told council that the
Planning Commission has a duty to act upon what has been presented to them for
decision. The Village transmits the application to the Planning Commission. The
Planning Commission reviews the application, presents it and makes a decision.
Then sends it back to council for a final decision. Council has the power to
approve the decision by a majority vote or make another decision with a five
vote margin.

Councilman Ward expressed to council the concern that when council presents the
Eagles application to the Planning Commission the property was not split and
then at the Planning Commission there was another Ordinance with the property
stating it would be split. The next day the property would be sent to the
recorders office to be split.

Mayor McCune told council that the Planning Commission acted upon what was
brought back from the Building and Lands Committee the second time.

Solicitor Lemire told council that the Ordinance was transmitted to the
Planning Commission.

It was discovered that the ordinance had inaccuracies in it. So the corrected
ordinance was then given to the Planning Commission. They reviewed and acted
upon the new ordinance.

Councilman Finger expressed to council that his understanding and his complaint
about the ordinance was that council had talked about. Council wanted it known
that the applicant was given the opportunity to bring back to council an
amended application with two parcels. That did not happen because of the
obligation to pass the information on to the Planning Commission. Council
passed on exactly what was submitted to council. When the Planning Commission
met
there was an ordinance that showed a difference in the acreage and parcels. The
planning commission acted on something different than what council had voted to
send.

Administrator Weir told council the only difference in the ordinances was, the
actual acreage contained in the rezoning, which was incorrect. The parcel that
was included in the first application was incorrect. The second one that was
submitted was corrected. The parcel as far as the residential, did not change.
The application did not change and the intended use for the parcel did not
change. Administrator Weir told council that you want to vote on what was
corrected not on something that is incorrect. Solicitor Lemire told council his
view is that as long as the ordinance that was finally acted upon by the
commission properly reflected what the application was about, then he felt
council's decision was okay. The ordinance only put everything in legal form.
The key item is the application for the amendment to the zoning code. The
Village Council has a duty to pass on to the Planning commission an ordinance
that properly reflects what the applicant wants amended. The Planning
commission reviews that and makes a decision then sends it back to council and
council votes on that decision to approve the decision or deny it.

Councilman Finger wanted change on page two the last sentence of the second
paragraph. The sentence should be: This is the fear that council has if the
Eagles club is zoned into two separate districts.

Minutes will stand as written with the change added.

time goes on and they change poles in other areas they will go with the taller
poles. The new poles actually cost about $1.00 more per pole. The reason the

installation costs. Weir also explained to council that the roads are
accessible to the public and this is a safety problem if we do not have
lighting. The roads are not accepted by the village yet but the public does use
the roads.

Visitors Comments:
Larry Bagley, owner of the BP gas station in town, expressed his concern with
vehicles parking for a long and short term at his station. This parking
situation has been going on for sixteen years and wanted to know why after all
this time is it being brought to his attention that cars should not be parked
there for long terms. Asked council to look into the situation with the short
term parking.

Mayor McCune told Larry Bagley that the long term parking was the problem and
any questions regarding the no parking signs or short term parking he would
have to talk to the zoning inspector or the solicitor on the legalities.

Administrator Weir explained the easements with the property of the BP station.
The easement is a stipulated judgement entry in regards to the complaint that
the village filed with all adjacent property owners that had use of any green
areas in the village. The judge ruled that the village owned the property and
did grant some permissive uses that are stipulated within the judgement entry.
Which does not include the BP or Standard Oil.

Larry Bagley questioned why the parking was still allowed for all these years
after the lawsuit was filed.

Mayor McCune stated that the laws were probably not enforced. Now we have
citizens in the village with watchful eyes. Since we have been enforcing front
yard parking, citizens have been calling the village and informing us of other
illegal parking issues.

Council discussed and agreed that the laws time period for parking and lot
deeds, should be looked into concerning the issue of what the area was deeded
for.

Administrator Weir expressed to council, concerning the parking issue, that
there should be no exclusive right to anyone to park on the green. Weir stated
that council can pass a motion if they want to change the status of parking on
that green.

Mayor McCune stated the issue would be put forth to the safety committee and
buildings and land.
If there is going to be a change in zoning have it in written form. Everyone
will be notified of what decision has been made.

Ed Flack expressed the conditions of the road on North Spruce. Stated that the
road was in bad shape.

Administrator Weir told council he would look at the condition of the road but
felt it was in good shape because he had just driven down the road.
Committee Reports
Recreation - no reports
Buildings and Land -
Councilman Finger made note to council of the letter from Terry Toukonen asking
to have the zoning application corrected with the proposed use of the Eagles
Club. The change would be corrected from Philanthropic Club to a Personal
Service use listed in section 1246.04 (a). Finger questioned the amendment and
asked if this could be done.

Solicitor Lemire stated it is phrased as a correction to the application not an
amendment. The statue states it can be amended anytime during the process.
There is nothing improper about the method that has been done to implement the
change. Lemire also stated to council that this was done because of the issue
that was brought up at the last meeting. That a Philanthropic Club was not an
appropriate use in an industrial zoned lot.

Discussion went on for a lengthy time discussing the issue of the zoned usage
for the Eagles lot. Lemire expressed that this is based on peoples opinion. The
final decision would have to come from a court rules decision if an agreement
could not be made. There is no clear statue that tells what is what for the
usage. Expressed his opinion that the personal service use does fit the
appropriate usage.

Councilman Ward expressed his disagreement with the solicitors opinion. Stated
that there is nothing that specifies where corrections can come from. He felt
that the village was not being fair to the citizens that would want to address
the issue.

Councilman Ward also made note to Ordinance 1547 which is an amendment to the
zoning text, that put number 12 in under industrial. Number one in industrial
is, everything is allowed under
B-1. Number 12 is out in left field. Commented on minutes regarding the zoning.
The sentence stated that "this action will be retaining industrial for
industrial purposes."

Solicitor Lemire read section 246.05 of the code. Talking about permissive
usage number one. It states any non residential use is permitted in a B-
1 district and number 12 is, any use permitted in a R-S district or B-
1 district is permitted on currently existing properties in an I district for
reconstruction. Lemire stated he read that you are aloud to reconstruct a B-
1 and build a B-1.

Council in discussion agreed that all of council should have a copy of the new
amended application.

Mayor McCune told council the zoning inspector would make up a press release
for the paper to inform the public of the change in the zoning application for
the Eagles. The Mayor also expressed to council and the residents that this
Eagles situation has brought up so much controversy over one piece of property
changing in their zoning. This issue is a zoning change of property asked by
the property owner. The Planning Commission has acted twice on the zoning
change. This will go to a Public Hearing and council will vote on the zoning
change. For council to overturn the Planning Commission decision the vote must
be five votes to do something other than what the Planning Commission voted on.
Four votes to adopt what was presented to council. This issue will be discussed
at the Public Hearing on October 18, 1999.

Councilman Finger discussed the solicitors opinion from the memo he wrote on
the parking in a residential lot. Finger expressed that he disagreed with the
solicitors opinion which he read.
The fact that parking spaces are not listed as a permissive or conditional use,
does not in my opinion mean that parking spaces are not permitted in a
residential district. Finger then read on adding adult entertainment is not
listed as a permissive use, therefore, if it is not listed then it is
permitted. He went on and added, drive in theaters. Finger stated that this
opinion makes no sense. The fact that it is not listed means it is okay. If it
is listed in our zoning text says that what is permitted.

Solicitor Lemire asked councilman Finger if he took his interpretation as
saying a person could not park at all in a residential zone. Lemire stated that
none of the districts listed parking as a permitted or conditional use. There
is a separate chapter that deals with parking. Parking spaces in the zoning are
not listed as conditional or permitted uses. 1254.03 governs the issue of
parking away from industrial use. 1254.03B which is the section that follows
the authorization to have parking spaces within 300 feet of the use. It does
not say anywhere in that sections that is has to be only on a similar lot. But
it goes on to say in section B no parking space may be located in the front
yard of any residential district. The implication of that statement is that if
you can not park in the front yard, you must be able to park in the side or
back yard. But this is just an opinion.

Administrator Weir stated a zoning inspector that he supported his opinion
because that is how he interprets the zoning text and parking ordinances.

Council went on with discussion about the zoning text and parking in business
use.

Councilman Finger stated the issue is the business and industrial parking in a
residential lot. How this is interpreted effects every piece of residential
property that abuts commercial or industrial to a parking lot.

Council agreed that the issue should be checked into further.

Councilman Aho also expressed his disagreement with the solicitors opinion
based on the same issues.

Forestry -
Councilman Aho wanted read into tonights minutes the minutes from the forestry
committee submitted at the last council meeting.

The committee reviewed the location, size, species and condition of the trees
in the tree lawn of the proposed Drug Mart development site on Chestnut and
Satin streets.

The best condition trees which were of 18" caliper and less were mostly located
where the approved curbs and driveways will be. Mr. Furst wants to remove all
trees in the tree lawn and replant after the site is developed. Although the
Committee members are generally against the removal of mature trees the
following facts were considered:
The removal of old gas pipes will be very close to the roots of many trees. The
driveway cuts will take some of the best trees. Damage by heavy equipment
during demolition and construction can be minimized by barriers, but may result
in the damage of some trees.

Three large trees are of no value and will need to be removed at village
expense in the near future if they are to remain after development.
Mr. Furst will accommodate all neighbors with the planting of hedges or fences
between adjoining properties.
If Mr. Furst is allowed to remove all the trees, he will be required to replant
at least eight new trees, the actual number will be determined after the
building is erected. Red Maples will be required on Satin Street. Mr. Furst
requested that Japanese Maples be planted on Chestnut Street. This species is
too small a tree to acceptable to the village. The Committee believes that an
alternative species other than our Master Tree Plan could be acceptable, but
the choice of species will remain with the village. Mr. Furst will replace
trees as directed by the village.

The alternative to removing all the trees is to remove only those in driveways
and work around the others. Considering the facts above, it is the
recommendation of the Committee that:

The request before council for the removal of twelve trees be granted with the
following conditions:
   1. Minimum of eight trees be planted. Size of each tree will be consistent
with          our current tree planting program.
   
   2. Red Maples will be required on Satin Street, except the tree nearest to
         Chestnut Street.
   
   3. Alternative species for Chestnut will be at council will.
   
   4. Hedges will be planted on adjoining neighbors property if desired by
   neighbors.
   5. Acceptable fencing as an alternative to hedges will be erected and
maintained    by the developer between the development and the neighbors. The
fence will be       on the property of the developer.
   
   6. Removal and disposal of all trees will be at the expense of the
developer.
Utilities -
Councilman Aho brought council up to date on the acceptance of the light poles
in the new division and they cost more than what the village is paying now.
What the village is paying now. The new ones are about 17.95 versus the cost of
8.00 to 12.00 for the maintenance of our current poles. Wanted to know if the
village is paying for the amortization of the cost purchase or is it just
maintenance.

Brett Harley of Illuminating Co. told council the village is set up with
municipal lighting program with the cost of about $8.95 up to $12.00 per month
being the charge for the street light outside. The overhead lighting is cheaper
than the colonial fiberglass post lights that are being requested for this
allotment. What is done in the municipal lighting program is they take total
cost of the fixtures and estimate the maintenance cost and raw fuel cost, which
is about $1.39 per month, and break it down into 120 payments. That is how they
come up with a figure. The contract is then continued over another ten years
based on replacement. The colonial lights that are being requested for this
development do cost more. Most of the lights are mercury vapor light. But the
government energy conservation program is phasing out mercury lights and going
to high pressure sodium, which is more efficient.

Councilman Aho questioned if Brett Harley could break down the cost of the
amortization of the purchase cost of the fixture. Aho told him that the village
is not in the business of development. But the village will maintain, operate
and replace roads, ditches, sidewalks to some extent and lights. We will not
pay for the purchase portion of the new lights. Aho stated that the contractor
(developer) would pay for the fixtures and the village would maintain them.

Brett Harley stated it was not impossible but he would look into it and get
back to council with the breakdown of costs.

Administrator Weir expressed to council that the municipal lighting agreements
are standard around the state and the rates are governed by the PUCO.

Councilman Thompson asked council if the Income Tax Ordinance could be put on

Solicitor Lemire explained to council the difference between the proposed
Municipal Income Tax Ordinance and the prior Earned Income Tax Ordinance. He
explained that most of the changes were clarifications and additions to the
definition section. Also told council that the new ordinance expressed a
clearer clarification to what income was and was not exempt from the village
income tax. Told council that the new ordinance brought everything up to date
with the present Ohio laws. Also expressed that this ordinance is in compliance
with the Ohio Revised Code. Told council to compare the old ordinance to the
new one. Expressed to council that he felt there should be a council meeting of
the whole to go over this.

Recreation -
Councilwoman Herndon made a statement to council concerning Marc Glotzbecker as
Director of the community center. She stated that he has done a fantastic job
for the Village of Jefferson in youth programs but there are management
problems at the recreation center. Herndon then referred to the Administrator
to explain his suggestions and recommendations.
 
Administrator Weir explained to the council his two recommendations. The first
one is for the reorganization of the community recreation center, which would
include a business manager and rearrange the existing employees. Weir
recommended to council that the Village create three new positions and
eliminate three existing positions. Weir stated the necessity is because the
village needs to have someone in the position to manage the operation with a
business background. Weir went on to say that Director Glotzbecker has done a
wonderful job with the community and the programs that he has established. He
also expressed the villages gratitude with his participation and dealings with
the youth and families within the community in general. His degree is in
recreation and his abilities are more toward providing programs instead of
managing the dept. Currently the recreation dept. is lacking support personnel
because, the program supervisor is maintaining the front desk and does all the
clerical paperwork. This has created a problem for the director, because he has
to manage the programs. Doing this he lacks being able to do the directors job.
The intention of the new plan is to offer Marc Glotzbecker the assistant
director/program coordinator position. Then offer Barb Heath the full time
clerical/program advocate position. Weir wanted to make sure that council
understood that a lot of the problems with this set up that the village has
now, is that the administrator does not have the time to spend at the comm.
center. Weir also expressed to council that the reorganization has nothing to
do with any disciplinary action of any personnel or the situation that is going
on at the recreation center. Weir then stated that he felt this was best for
the operation of the recreation dept.

Citizen John Kusar asked what the pay would be for the new directors full time
position.

Administrator Weir said the probationary director would start at $26,000, after
six months increase to $27,000 and at one year $28,000. Weir said with the
reorganization the wages would increase about $14,000 but the benefits would be
more.

Councilman Finger stated for clarification that the recreation dept. with the
reorganization, would have four full- time positions and one part- time
position, there would still be five employees. Currently there are three full-
time and two part- time employees .

Administrator Weir told council that the extra money would have to be discussed
with the Finance Committee. He stated that this is just a plan to get the dept.
back on track in regards to what is a sensible operation.

Councilman Aho questioned what hours the new director would work and if it was
a forty hour a week job.

Administrator Weir stated that it was a salary position just like any salary
position in the village based on a forty hours a week. But the person works
when he or she is needed. Weir also stated that the positions could be held
open to all village employees or any member of the public that would want to
apply. Weir then stated to council that he had a recommendation for the
directors position and he felt the position should be filled quickly to keep
the dept. running properly.

Councilman Ward expressed concern that maybe the director was trying to do two
jobs and maybe the village should hire a new program coordinator and clerk and
let him be the director.

Administrator Weir commented that Marc Glotzbecker told the Administrator that
he was not good with finances and the directors position has financial
responsibilities.
Administrator Weir told council his recommendation to hire Mark Hellmer was
because he has savvy in regards to business and has some background in
recreation. He is also familiar with the recreation center. He is more suited
for the financial part of the department.

Director Glotzbecker handed a letter to council and the mayor at this time.

Mayor McCune read the resignation letter as director to council. The letter
stated that Marc Glotzbecker would work until October 22, 1999 and then he
would take a weeks vacation and his resignation would be effective November 1,
1999.

Councilman Finger made a motion to adopt the plan and codify at a later date.
2nd by Herndon.

Roll: Aho yea, Finger yea, Herndon yea, Stasny yea, Thompson yea, Ward yea.

Motion by Finger to have the Solicitor bring forth an ordinance to codify the
plan.
2nd by Herndon

Roll: Aho yea, Finger yea, Herndon yea, Stasny yea, Thompson yea, Ward yea.

Motion by Finger to advertise for a position of a business manager/director at
the community center.
2nd by Herndon

Roll: Aho yea, Finger yea, Herndon yea, Stasny yea, Thompson yea, Ward yea.

Mayor McCune announced that the meeting would go out of regular session and
into the public hearing for the Eagles Club.

Administrator Weir explained to council that in July the village had received a
second application from the Eagles Club to rezone a parcel of land at 152 E.
Erie Street. The application was to rezone 1.417 acres of the two acre parcel,
leaving a section off Cedar Street as residential. The 1.417 would be rezoned
industrial which would allow the Eagles to build a new facility. This has gone
to the Planning Commission and the Planning Commission approved to have the
parcel rezoned. It is now back to Village Council for the Public Hearing.

Solicitor Lemire swore the residents in, who wanted to testify at the hearing.

Mayor McCune told council and the residents for the hearing the Village would
hear one side for and then one side against.

Solicitor Lemire told council the side in favor should go first.

Citizen Terry Toukenon 175 West Jefferson Street spoke for the Eagles Club. She
presented two petitions to the Mayor. One petition is a general petition
circulated throughout the Village for people in favor of the zoning change. The
second petition is from people that live on Erie Street which will be affected
by the change. The only way the Eagles can build a building on their Erie
Street lot is to have the property rezoned from residential to industrial. Area
residents and council have said that they are against the Eagles. Toukenon
asked if anyone new of any way other than rezoning the property, that would
allow a new building to be built and the Eagles to continue to operate. The
courts have certain criteria that need to be asked and answered. The first
question states: will the proposed zoning alter the caricature of the
neighborhood? The Eagles have been operating in this neighborhood since 1982
and prior to the Eagles was the American Legion which was established in 1952.
The residents new the Eagles Club was there when they bought their home. On the
Erie Street petition 10 of 13 residents are in favor of the change. They
believe their neighborhood will change for the better. This represents 77% of
the people who will be directly affected by the zoning change. The second
question is, is the request reasonable? Yes it is. This is not spot zoning.
Erie Street currently has mixed zoning. The Eagles are asking to extend the
industrial 132.65 feet to the west. The third question to be asked is, will the
Eagles get a reasonable return on their investment? The Eagles have two
residential lots that could be sold. The property was purchased in 1982 for
75,000 dollars. The current value listed with the auditor is 87,620 dollars.
Toukenon presented a letter from Ed Curie stating the property at 152 E. Erie
Street owned by the Eagles is valued from 7,500 to 10,000 dollars appraised as
a residential piece of land. The fair market value for the land zoned as
industrial would be 27,500 to 30,000 dollars. Toukenon expressed concern to
council with their duty not to destroy economical value of peoples property.
The most economical use for the property is to allow it to continue to be used
as it has been for the past 47 years, as a social club. The zoning change will
allow the Eagles to construct a new building and continue to operate as they
have for the past 17 years.

Richard Jones of 134 East Cedar Street spoke against the zoning change. Jones
spoke to the elected officials stating they have made many good and difficult
decisions for improvement and protection of our community in the
administration. Jones notes to council if the application would mean a further
encroachment of industrial property into residential area, we believe
( petition signers against the Eagles) that this is not a good zoning practice
and respectfully urge the council to vote down the application as they did the
first time.

Jeff Otto of 15 East Satin Street spoke for the Eagles Club. Stated to council
that they are not trying to do anything different with the property than what
is presently being done at the Eagles Club and has been done for the past 20
years. Otto stated that the Eagles Club is only trying to improve the facility.
Otto addressed the Solicitor, asking if there could be a contingency put into
the zoning. Stating that it could be industrial and an addendum put on the deed
that if the Eagles ever lose or sell the property it would go back to
residential. Stated that this would solve some of the fear. Asked if Jefferson
Village has something in the zoning.

Solicitor Lemire stated that in the Village code there is no such mechanism in
place.

Caysey Baxley of 245 E. Jefferson Street against the zoning change. Stated to
council that this zoning does not affect one street, East Erie. It affects
Cedar and the corner of Market also. On East Cedar alone out of 12 properties,
11 of the property owners signed the petition against the zoning change. It
seems if you have one parcel and one owner, if two are against it this is a
democracy. Each council person was voted in by public and you were put there
and expected you to go with a majority. This is the basis of our whole
government. Petitions can be filled with names for or against. You have to look
at who owns the property. There is an overwhelming majority of people that are
not in favor of the zoning change. Baxley noted to council it was up to them to
make the right decision and vote how the majority of the people want the
zoning.

Jeff Otto of 15 E. Satin Street. Expressed to council that when the petitions
were gotten, yes there were both husbands and wives because they are separate
votes. Yes, some of the people do rent but they are voting residents of
Jefferson. When the Eagles got the petitions they got voters that were involved
and live on the street.

Fran Jones of 134 E. Cedar Street opposed to the Eagles Club. Stated that when
the apartment houses were put on Erie Street and Cedar Street there was
opposition to it. But it was in good faith that it would be kept residential.
If the Eagles go in with a new building this is now going to be a party center.
It would then not be residential in any way.

Walt McCasskey of 812 Rt. 46 S. for the Eagles zoning change. Expressed to
council that the Eagles Club will be there whether you approve the zoning or
not.

Kimberly Faulke Durkovic of 146 E. Cedar Street is against the zoning change.
Asked council to consider if the Ealges Club upgrades there property, what will
it do to value of the residential property owners. Expressed concern with
noise. Also asked council to listen to the people that live around the Eagles
Club, who are concerned for their children, sound, traffic and for their future
and safety.

Richard Hummel of 114 E. Erie Street against the zoning change. Questioned
council about the zoning permits and building permit to tear down the building.
Also questioned the trees.

Amended Ordinance 2283.
An Ordinance Amending Chapter 890 of the Codified Ordinances of the Village of
Jefferson, to Clarify Ambiguities, Amend Dates and Conform the Chapter to
Existing Ohio Law.

Councilman Thompson explained to council at the next council meeting he would
like to suspend council rules and have the ordinance passed so there will not
be two tax policies in place January 1, 2000.

Councilman Finger questioned why are we paying to have the code updated when
council rules say we will update once a year and there are sections of the
update that are still wrong and not up to date. ( such as the seven people on
the Planning Commission instead of five.)

Solicitor Lemire explained that when the ordinance was changed for the Planning
Commission there was an oversight in the ordinance and that section was not
amended. But the new section has the correct Planning Commission members. The
solicitor stated that it was an oversight or drafting error on his part. But he
stated that in the ordinance it was changed to a five member committee and not
an error on the codifier.

Clerk-Treasurer Fisher told council that before council changed council rules
to have the ordinances codified once a year, it was set up with the
codification co. once a year (Aug. to Aug.)
This year we will have to codify twice to make it go from January to January
each year.

Mayor McCune stated that when the council rules were changed there was still
September to December of the previous year. So somewhere they had to make up
those months because of the split.

Clerk-Treasurer Fisher told council as soon as the ordinances are codified the
book is outdated because a new ordinance has already been passed. Fisher also
stated that if council wanted the ordinances codified monthly or quarterly
instead of yearly, American Legal would do it. But the fees would be more.

Councilman Finger questioned the review log and stated he did not care if the
Village had to go back to the beginning of time to make sure ordinances are not
missed.

Clerk-Treasurer Fisher told council that there is a log of the ordinances. Also
before that last code update the Administrator and herself went back before
1996 and still found ordinances not codified.

Councilman Finger stated at some time we have to start from the beginning and
codify all the ordinances to make sure everything is in the code book.

Mayor McCune suggested to council to have American Legal come in and research
the ordinance from the beginning to make sure all the ordinances are codified.
Asked the Clerk to get figures on what it would cost. McCune also told council
that they would have the legal expertise that is needed.

Administrator Weir explained that to research the ordinances and codify takes a
lot of time.

Solicitor Lemire told council that the ordinance only reflects the replacement
dated October and there is a replacement dated August too. The ordinance will
have to be amended to reflect both updates or table the ordinance.

Motion by Finger to table the Codification Update Resolution
2nd by Herndon

Roll: Aho yea, Finger yea, Herndon yea, Stasny yea, Thompson yea, Ward yea.

Councilman Finger questioned the emergency of the resolution.

Solicitor Lemire explained to council that these are actually the laws of the
village but people do not know because they have not been codified. The
ordinances are in effect but the emergency is to let people know the laws and
have the ordinances all in a book to avoid confusion.

Councilman Finger then questioned if the ordinances should be codified more
frequently.

Motion by Finger to change Rule 37 in council rules and have the village
ordinances codified quarterly instead of yearly.
2nd by Herndon

Lands & Buildings -
Councilman Finger discussed with council the revision to the Jefferson zoning
code. Stated there are sections that have been revised concerning regulations,
controlling value, material, etc and asked the solicitor to explain.

Solicitor Lemire explained to council that the new ordinance has a section that
is called a site plan review which is done by the zoning inspector. The new
chapter 1256, would have a review of permits for RD, I and B1 district
construction projects. Lemire stated that all of council should review the
changes. This does not deal with architectural review situations but it does
give the zoning inspector some leverage to negotiate and talk with the
developers. It does have a referral to the Planning commission for a review of
the location of a proposed building. This method does formalize the process and
makes it more specific and outlines issues the inspector should review when he
does a site plan. There are also changes in the ordinance dealing with sings.

Councilman Finger suggested a committee of the whole meeting to review the
ordinance.

The meeting was set for Thursday, November 11, 1999 at 7:00 p.m.

Councilman Thompson announced a Finance meeting Tuesday, November 23, 1999 at
6:00 p.m. in the committee meeting room.

Councilman Ward discussed with council the proposal from the Jefferson
Emergency Rescue District. Told council that the JERD was interested in
swapping the vacant property, which is now a parking lot owned by the village,
for the 1,836 sq. ft. building and office space the JERD is now using and owns.
The land was kept for expansion of the safety center in the future. Noted to
council that the Fire Station needs room for the equipment.

Councilman Aho told council that this would be a win win situation for both
parties.

Councilman Ward stated he felt with the ambulance on the property it would be
beneficial for everyone. Along with the growth in the village it would be in
the best interest for the village to keep all safety departments together.

Tim Bojanowski legal council for the JERD stated appraisals on the current
building have been done and the value of the building is comparable to that of
the vacant lot. Told council that he would discuss the matter with anyone on
council.

Mayor McCune stated his only concern was lack of parking for the adjacent
Jefferson Volunteer Fire Dept. Told council that this is simply a request to
consider the trade and if council did not approve the trade the district would
have to look elsewhere.

Tim Bojanowski stated that in drawing up the new plans they would make sure to
put in as much parking space as allowed by the building code for the size of
the property.

Solicitor Lemire stated that the next step would be that Bojanowski , legal
council for the JERD, would submit a written proposal.

Councilman Ward told council that he would like to incorporate the need for
parking in the plan that is drawn up between council and the JERD.

Councilman Finger noted to council that the building space the JERD is in is
owned by the JERD but the land is owned by the village and there is a lease
agreement in place. If the JERD decides to move out of that building the
village has no rights to the building.

Mayor McCune explained to council that the JERD is an entity all by its self.
The village has a representative and the township has a representative. Neither
entity controls the JERD the board controls it. Any change in that operation
would have to go to the public for a vote.

After a long discussion council decided to make a motion to agree with the
preliminary discussion.

Motion by Finger for a roll of council for those who are in favor of the
village and JERD swapping properties.
2nd by Ward.

Roll: Aho yea, Finger yea, Herndon yea, Stasny yea, Thompson yea, Ward yea

Mark Fuerst, the contractor for Drug Mart, addressed council telling them that
the color of the bricks used for the building will be changed to a red block.

Councilwoman Stasny asked Mark Fuerst if the high arch in front of the building
was going to stay.

Mark Fuerst explained to council that it was there so when people get out of
their car they have something to walk under.
Mark also presented to council a resolution for the liquor license that is
being applied for now.

John Kusar asked council for help with a problem of an old sewer bill, from
1996-97, that was not paid by an old tenant. Because the bill was not paid the
amount was going to be assessed to his taxes. Kusar stated that he had talked
with Michelle Ashley, she said she would not assess his taxes and she didn't.
But to this day the amount that is owed, he has not been told by her. Kusar
also told council that he had talked with councilman Finger and Clerk-Treasurer
Fisher about the problem. Michelle Ashley told Kusar that they were not her
boss and she would handle it. Kusar stated to council that all he wanted was to
get the problem solved. Since he has questioned Michelle Ashley he has also
stopped receiving landlord letters stating who has not paid their sewer.

Mayor McCune told John Kusar he would get all the information and make sure
that he was given a correct answer.

Administrator Weir commented to council that John Kusar had just brought this
to his attention last week.

Citizen Lisa Hawkins asked Mark Fuerst why the fence that Drug Mart was putting
up, ends at their pole barn? Asked if it could be extended to the sidewalk so
the lights from the cars in the parking lot would not shine in their house.
Also worried about their children and privacy.

Mayor McCune told council and the public again, that the builder and the
developer have met all requirements of the village, dealing with the zoning. He
said we cannot tell the developer to extend the fence farther.

Mark Fuerst told council that the stockade fence will go to the pole barn and a
picket fence will go along the backyard. The reason for this is, if a stockade
fence was extended to the sidewalk it would block the view of cars pulling in
and out, putting people in danger.

Citizen Don Hawkins asked Mark Fuerst if they could put up a different fence or
extend it farther to block lights and give privacy.

Council then agreed to leave the issue with the fence open until after Drug
Mart was finished.

Administrator Weir told council that the zoning code would allow the builder to
run a fence to within a foot of the sidewalk.

Mark Fuerst asked council if they would pass the resolution and get the process
moving forward for the liquor permit.

Councilman Thompson stated to council that the resolution has to come from
committee and then be presented to council. An ordinance of resolution has
never been accepted from a member at large.

Solicitor Lemire stated the Resolution is an endorsement for the application of
a liquor permit.

Mayor McCune told council that a resolution has never come to council to
support the issue of a liquor license. There has to be a resolution to renew a
license.

Mark Fuerst explained they are just asking for a resolution of support. In the
past they have even had letters written from the mayor.

Solicitor Lemire told council that he would like to look over the statue and it
should be assigned a committee for review and brought back to council.

Mayor McCune told the solicitor has was the committee and get with Mark Fuerst
to go over all the information.

Solicitor Lemire told council that the village has no jurisdiction, the state
controls the liquor licenses and the number of permits approved for the
communities.

Mark Fuerst explained to council that in applying for a liquor permit in this
are, Jefferson is a saturated area. If applying for a license in a saturated
area, if one is not available, a permit can be taken from another saturated
area.

Mayor McCune told council, after the solicitor has looked over everything and
he approves, it will then be presented to council.

Amended Ordinance 2286
An ordinance amending ordinance 2243 providing for increases and/or adjustments
in pay for salaried, hourly, and part-time employees of the village of
Jefferson, Ohio, providing for a $.50 hourly additional compensation to
employees acting in a supervisory capacity; providing for a pickup of employee
contributions to the pension funds; repealing all other ordinances inconsistent
herewith.

Councilman Thompson explained to council that there are seven ordinances
declaring an emergency. When declaring any ordinance as an emergency is has to
have an explanation. It is to meet the December 31st deadline. When there is a
motion to suspend rules it takes five votes, 3/4 and a move for passage is 2/3,
four votes.

Motion by Thompson to suspend council rules for ordinance 2287.
2nd by Herndon.

Solicitor Lemire explained, normally there is a first reading then a motion to
suspend rules and adopt.

Councilman Thompson explained in rule 26 in 2201.01, it does not mention the
first reading if it is an emergency and you have 3/4 votes.

Councilman Finger questioned the temporary appropriations.

Clerk-Treasurer Fisher explained that the temporary appropriations are for the
first quarter of the year 2000. The figures are based on the first quarter of
1999. This is to run the village until all the appropriations and ordinances
are passed before April 1, 2000.

Solicitor Lemire read the village council rules to council. It states that if
it is an emergency ordinance, the presiding officer, after it is read, shall
entertain a motion to suspend rules. The villages traditional way it to have
the first reading then suspend the rules.

Councilman Thompson then withdrew his first motion.

Councilwoman Herndon withdrew her second.

Motion by Thompson for the first reading of ordinance 2287.
2nd by Herndon.

Recreation:
Motion by Herndon to accept the interim Directors recommendation to raise the
mens adult Basketball fee for village residents to $35.00 and $40.00 for non
residents to participate in the league. This would help defer the costs for
referees, scorekeeper, time keeper, t-shirts and the use of the High School
gymnasium so that the program would be cost effective to the village.
2nd by Stasny.
Roll: Finger yea, Herndon yea, Maloney yea, Stasny yea, Thompson yea, Ward yea.
Councilman Finger questioned if the Village was going to go back and have it
retroactive or make the adjustment for future programs.
Mayor Bragga stated that Basketball runs two programs during the winter. The
fees would go into effect the second half of the season.
Councilwoman Herndon explained to council that the recreation committee is
looking over the applications for the recreation department. They will then
have interviews from the best applicants. After the interviews are completed
the committee will then bring a recommendation to council. Councilwoman Herndon
read a letter from the Administrator suggesting the Administrator bow out of
the process of candidate selection for the newly created positions at the
recreation center and request that the recreation committee perform the
process. This would avoid criticism of fair hiring practices and non partial
selection for the position.
Councilwoman Herndon then told council that the process for hiring the new
director would be completed in the early part of February.
Mayor Bragga suggested to council that the final person selected for the
position, have a security check done. He also wants council to interview the
top three candidates.
Administrator Weir told council that the clerical position was not advertised
because the Village personnel manual states that when an employee is laid off
from the department and there is an opening, they could be placed in that open
position if they are interested.
Administrator Weir then told council that there are two employees interested in
that position.
Administrator Weir referred back to the rates and fees that are charged next
door that council approves by motion. He explained that the motion to raise the
basketball fee is a good example of why council should keep the rate structure
out of an ordinance. Explaining that when there is a need to change the fees
all council has to do is pass a motion, instead of going through three readings
of an ordinance.
Councilman Finger suggested to council that there be a rate sheet with all the
fee structures and have it updated each time there is a change, for auditing
purposes.
Mayor Bragga told council that at the recreation committee meeting he suggested
that for each program there be a cost analysis sheet done to show if the
program is feasible.
Building/Lands:
Councilman Finger discusses the memorandum that the solicitor wrote up
explaining the land trade for the building with Jefferson Emergency Rescue
District.
Council discussed the land appraisal to the value of the building. Tossed
around if the situation with the building that Jefferson taxpayers have paid
for with tax dollars and the same issue with the vacant property. Agreed that
in the contract drawn up, that council can put in whatever stipulation they
want.
Solicitor Lemire explained to council that the JERD wants to trade the land for
their section of the building. Also told council that this was just a proposal
drawn up by there attorney. Council can decide what they want.
Mayor Bragga expressed to council that it is councils decision to look over the
process and make sure the taxpayers dollars are being spent wisely. Council has
to think the issue through. He also told council that the appraisal for the
property is a very good one. The property was purchased in the early ninetys
for $69,000, verse the appraisal of $103,000 for the vacant lot today.
Councilman Ward told council that in the JERD plan the general cost per square
foot for the building is estimated at $63.50 and could go up to $100 per sq.
foot. Also noted that in the 20% depreciation of the building is just
estimated. The JERD has upgraded the building in many areas to be able to have
personnel in the building 24 hours.
Councilman Finger questioned that both the building and the land is taxpayers
money. If at some point in time after the building is done, the JERD would go
disban or private, they would have to buy the property from the taxpayers.
Solicitor Lemire explained to council that there is a statutory process when an
emergency district disbans that it governs the district. He told council that
he does not know the whole process but he could look into it if they approve
the process.
Motion by Finger to have council go ahead with the proposal and have the
solicitor draw up an ordinance with a memorandum explaining the process and
legal issues to protect the taxpayers.
2nd by Ward.
Roll: Finger yea, Herndon yea, Maloney yea, Stasny yea, Thompson yea, Ward yea.
Forestry:

codification in the council rules. Also expressed that council was not
following their own rules. So a change has been made in rule 36 to change the
phrase from. The council rules may be amended or altered or new rules adopted
by a vote of the majority of all the members elected at any meeting of council,
on the report of a committee to which the subject has been referred at the
previous meeting. The new amendment would state: these rules may be amended or
altered or new rules adopted by a vote of the majority of all elected members,
at any meeting of council.
Motion by Finger for the first reading of ordinance 2295.
2nd by Herndon.
Roll: Finger yea, Herndon yea, Maloney yea, Stasny yea, Thompson yea, Ward yea.

Mayor Bragga read to council the Mayors address for the year 2000.
As the year 2000 begins. I reflect on the past six weeks as I have begun to
prepare to once again serve our community. I am amazed at the complexities that
exist in a seemingly simple task of managing our village. It is the charge and
responsibility of this collective body to address each issue through study,
preparation and communication while approaching each task with professionalism
and completeness, with as much expedience as the process allows. We should work
to help each other to understand and address each situation as we conduct the
business and affairs of our village.
Some of the items and issues that are on the table or under consideration may
include:
* The current revision and continuous review of the zoning text.
* The reorganization and operation of our Jefferson Recreation and community
Center. Realizing the fantastic potential of all current and future programs
designed to serve the recreational needs of our public.
* The continued scrutiny of the utilities providing services to the community.
A current issue involves the position of the community and how to provide
efficient and cost effective water services.
* The management of our industrial areas and the need to address and solve the
material and supply routes for that area. A truck route is needed to provide a
safe, logical and efficient delivery system for the industrial portion of our
community.
* The possible expansion of our emergency rescue services and facility.
* Develop a short and long range plan for the use of the 80+ acres of village
porperty in the northeast quadrant of the village (Rush Creek Clay and Tile
Property).
* Move forward with the Joint District formed for the improvement of Mulberry
Street.
* Continue the sidewalk improvement program.
* Study and review the necessity of improving the culvert on South Market
between Satin and Erie Streets.
* Study and review the necessity of improving the storm sewer system on North
Chestnut St. from Jefferson St. to Cemetery Creek north of town.
* Study and review the necessity for a traffic signal at the Chestnut and
Walnut Street intersection.
* Expect a Jefferson Village web site. The plans include a community events
calendar, historical information, demographics, recreation programs, agency
phone numbers, village boards and committees and village council news.
The village of Jefferson has to give thanks for many things. The ingredients
for a great place to live are evident on a daily basis in our community.
We’ve been blessed with quality and diverse churches and church families.
We have been privileged to have a quality school system for our children.
Our safety forces (police, fire, rescue) provide a safe and secure environment.
Our street department and waste water treatment department provide efficient
and expedient services for our community.
We have a beautiful, historic, well managed and well maintained Oakdale
Cemetery.
We are fortunate to have a quality public library providing excellent resources
for us.
We have an abundance of adult and student oriented civic, social, and
recreational organizations, clubs and groups for our citizens.
Our public has always been positive and eager to support the many and varied
components and ingredients it requires to create a great and wonderful place to
live and raise a family.
We are truly blessed with quality people whose diverse thoughts, opinions and
work ethics, continue to make Jefferson a most desirable place to call HOME!
Old/New business
Councilman Ward discussed the resolution from the last meeting dealing with the
liquor license for the new DrugMart. All present council members voted against
supporting them in their application for a liquor permit. Then Mayor McCune
signed a letter for DrugMart in his support for the liquor permit and it was
sent to the state. Councilman Ward then proceeded to state that council voted
it down. He felt that council should send a copy of the minutes, letter and
resolution to the state. Telling them that the village council is against
supporting their liquor permit.
Motion by Ward to have the solicitor draw up a letter stating the village is
against it along with the mayors letter and a copy of the minutes and
resolution.
2nd by Thompson.
Discussion
Councilwoman Herndon stated to council that it is a worthwhile thought, but
they have liquor license at other stores. The state is going to give them the
license no matter what the village states.
Councilman Ward noted that it is just the point and council was forced to act
on it and it did not matter what council voted.
Solicitor Lemire clarified to council that the resolution that council voted
not to adopt was a resolution that expressed no objection. Council is saying
different, they do not support the liquor license transfer of a permit into the
village which is labeled a saturated area.
Councilman Thompson stated to council when the resolution was put on the agenda
it was made a legislative matter and it was up to council to decide. Mayor
McCune relinquished his authority when it was given to council to vote on.
Mayor McCune then sent his letter of approval after it was voted down.
This is an issue that has never come to council before and we voted upon it as
a council in not supporting it.
Councilwoman Maloney expressed that the DrugMart is a drug store not a liquor
store and not having the liquor license should not have a negative impact on
the development.
Council had a long discussion on the issue and decided to withdraw the first
motion.
Councilman Ward withdrew his motion.
Councilman Thompson withdrew his second.
Councilman Ward made a motion objecting to the transfer of the liquor permit
into the village of Jefferson which is already a saturated area.
2nd by Thompson.
Roll: Finger yea, Herndon yea, Maloney yea, Stasny yea, Thompson yea, Ward yea.

Mayor Bragga expressed to the public that at the beginning of the meeting in
visitor comments they can speak and express concerns. If they have a concern or
want to address council, asked if they would look at the agenda and let the
Mayor know prior to the meeting so that they could be added to the agenda.
Visitors comments:
Mayor Bragga announced that the DrugMart issue would be moved from old business
to visitors comments.
Councilman Finger told council that he had gotten some new facts that question
the letter to the state liquor board. Said that the CVS and Rite Aid both have
liquor license. Council has voiced concerns of having too many liquor license
in the village. Also stated that this procedure was new to council, having a
letter brought forth for approval and no objection to the license.
Council voted at a council meeting not to support the approval of the liquor
permit by a majority voting down the resolution. Then at the next council
meeting council voted to even support the disapproval of the liquor permit by
having the solicitor draw up a letter that council was opposed to the transfer.
Councilwoman Maloney expressed to council that DrugMart doesn’t need support
but needs a statement saying we have no objection to the permit. This would
enable them to do their business.
Council then questioned why they felt they needed the license to better their
business in a drug store.
Mayor Bragga stated that it is councils pleasure. Council requested the letter.
Councilman Thompson made a motion to vote on the letter and have it read.
2nd by Ward.
Discussion.
Councilman Finger told council that the buildings and lands committee had a
meeting. The committee chose not to discuss the letter. The meeting was set up
to discuss what the developer was going to do with the property. The developer
stated at the meeting that he was willing to work with the village and be a
good neighbor and change the design to satisfy the residents. This would
address all the issues. The developer then stated for them to proceed they
would like some consideration on the letter. We have two drug stores in this
village with liquor permits. Also the village was never asked to support the
license and why is the village putting a restriction on a business in the
village.
Dale Markowitz explained to council why everyone is hearing about this permit
and not others.
Mark Fuerst stated that the reason is under Ohio statue that DrugMart is
seeking the transfer of a permit outside the county. The State Department of
Liquor Control then asks for comments on the permit before the hearing is
started. CVS and Rite Aid did not get permits that are called Trek permits
which is a transfer from outside the area. When you have this type of permit
you have to have a resolution or letter from the village sent to the
Deparatment of Liquor Control. If the persons asking for the permit can prove
that this permit would economically benefit the community, the permit then
would be allowed to be transferred. There is another process which could go
through a public hearing and you have to go to Columbus for that.
Dale Markowitz then went on to say the reason DrugMart is asking for a
resolution was it would say that there is no objection to the Dept of Liquor
Control beginning the process. There would still be time later to object the
process if something happened. This is where the village can have a position
with a resolution or a letter from the Mayor of Chief of Police. The letter
from Mayor McCune is being sent back to Mark Fuerst for the Village of
Jefferson. This is what was asked at the last meeting.
Mayor Bragga did express that if council had known some of the information from
the beginning there may have been different thoughts on the issue. The Mayor
explained to council the motion that is on the floor is the letter council
asked the solicitor to draw up which shows opposition to the liquor permit.
Motion by Finger to go into executive session to discuss possible litigation.
2nd by Herndon.
Roll: Finger yea, Herndon yea, Maloney yea, Stasny yea, Thompson nea, Ward yea.

resolution the county will then sign the contracts with all the terms along
with the agreement. He also told council that the agreement would not carry
over to another business if Vision Plastics would dissolve their lease. This
would be a two party agreement which is recommended by the State of Ohio. Brian
then told council that there is an annual review board that looks over the
performance date and votes if the abatement will go on through the abatement
period, as long as they are meeting all the terms.
