Visitors Comments:
Mark Fuerst of DrugMart asking for council to reconsider the denial of the
liquor permit. Expressed to council that he has complied with all the zoning
codes. He even stated that he has gone the extra mile to say he would put up
the fence and change the color of the brick. Fuerst then stated to council he
had plans drawn up for the drainage at the DrugMart that would more than exceed
the retention plan. Also expressed that they paid a bond for cutting down the
trees. He went on to say to council that he has done everything that council
has asked. Fuerst presented the letter from the old Mayor that was signed
stating no objection to the liquor permit and then proceeded to ask council to
reconsider their letter of objection to the liquor permit. He said if the
permit is not granted, the drug store conglomerate will pull out of the deal
and not locate here. Fuerst went on to say that he has $800,000.00 sitting on a
corner and cannot make payments on vacant land. I have one of two choices,
either I can build a DrugMart or I can build a service station. He then stated
he was coming back to council one last time. DrugMart will bail out if they do
not get the liquor license.
Solicitor Lemire read Marks contract with DrugMart and agreed that if DrugMart
does not get a liquor permit they can pull out.
Mark Fuerst then presented a Western Reserve look plan for DrugMart stating he
would change his plans again and said he was prepared to do what everyone was
asking but he needed one thing and that is a liquor license. To get a C1 or CT
Trex liquor license which is a liquor license brought in from another city, I
need a resolution from council not objecting to the liquor permit. There is not
a DrugMart in the chain that does not have a liquor permit.
Mayor Bragga asked council if there was a desire of council to prepare a
resolution.
Councilman Finger asked council what are we trying to prove by denying a liquor
license to DrugMart? When there are liquor license all over town.
Councilman Ward told council that he was not against the sale or consumption of
alcohol. When the resolution was brought to the Village, council voted not to
send the resolution. The previous Mayor then sent a letter that he had no
opposition to the liquor permit. The intent at the last meeting was to correct
what the previous Mayor did. Stating that the village council does object to
the transfer of liquor license.
Motion by Herndon to introduce a resolution that states that the village
council has no objection to the transferring of a liquor permit into the
village.
2nd by Ward.
Discussion
Councilman Thompson expressed his feelings that enough citizens of the village
came to him and said we would hope you would not approve of such a thing. This
is not my own personal preference. Councilman Thompson also noted to council
that the State Liquor License Board makes the final decision not the village.
Mark Fuerst told council that the State will not start the process with a
letter from the village objecting to the permit. He went on to say that he
would not be here in front of council if he did not need a letter of approval
from council or the Mayor.
Solicitor Lemire told council that there are no regulations other than standard
of practice, that attorneys have gotten used to dealing with when they go for
the permits. The statue simply says that this can be done, getting a permit
from another area, which is called Trex. No business has ever gotten the permit
if they did not have the proper letter or resolution in place.
Mark Fuerst said the package is an economic development, which includes the
plan to build and have a two year performance on the company and what it will
create for the town. If this is not done the State will not even look at the
paperwork. If I get the resolution, council will not hear from me again. But I
would like to have it passed as soon as possible so he could get on with his
plans.
Councilman Finger told council if we are denying this liquor permit we are
making a statement to all other developers that are seeking a liquor permit.
Mayor Bragga told council that it was 8:00 p.m. and the council would have to
have the joint session meeting.

Roll: Finger, Herndon, Maloney, Stasny, Thompson
Absent: Ward
Also Present: Bob Reitz, Cayce Baxley, Joyce Friend, Virginia Schaffner, Robert
Sawyer, John Kusar, Jerry March, Tony Tulajew, Richard Hummel, Roland Ferguson,
Star Beacon and Gazette.
Minutes to the last meeting were approved as written.
After a brief discussion regarding the bills no changes were made.
Motion by Finger to pay the current bills as of March 6, 2000
2nd by Herndon.
Roll: Finger yea, Herndon yea, Maloney yea, Stasny yea, Thompson yea.
Visitors Comments:
Citizen John Kusar presented council with a hypothetical proposed building and
questioned if a zoning permit would be issued. He told council that he would be
building a Quonset hut used for a mini mall. Noted to council that these
hypothetical building plans would follow all of the Village zoning codes. He
then went on to comment on the new proposed zoning code. That with the new code
the Village is leaving too many of the decisions up to the zoning inspector and
his personal preference. Asked council to give a written response to his
proposal. Told council he agreed with them in having an architectural review
board. Said the Village does need to have some control in the commercial
development. But it must be cast in stone. Told council that he knows they are
working on the zoning ordinance but what is going to happen while they are
making changes in the text?
Recreation:
Motion by Herndon for the second reading of ordinance 2303.
2nd by Stasny.
Roll: Finger yea, Herndon yea, Maloney yea, Stasny yea, Thompson yea.
Resolution 2303
A Resolution accepting the donation of equipment and materials from the SOCC
Board.
Councilwoman Herndon made a motion for payment of $230.00 to the Jefferson Area
Local Schools for use of the gym.
2nd by Stasny.
Discussion
Council discussed the bill. Was concerned that the proper procedures and rules
were not followed. Which is mandated by the Ohio Revised Code. Stated that
Vickie Crompton should be held accountable. Along with the fact that
compensation had been given to the person and the bill has not been paid.
Mayor Bragga told council that the intention from the clerk was to pay the
bill. Then at a later date this would be discussed by legal council to be
reimbursed by Vickie Crompton, for payment of the bill.
Clerk/Treasurer Fisher told council that this issue of payment of the bill was
brought to council to help keep the open relationship that the Village has with
the school. At times we are allowed to use the building for free if it is for
the grade school children. This baton program was an extracurricular activity
so a fee is charged to the Village. This issue is something that reflects back
to what the old director had done by not deducting the fees from the
instructors pays. Legally there should have been a contract drawn up for the
Village using the school and there never has been.
Solicitor Lemire told council that this was an administrative mistake. The
Village should look at the business aspect of it. We do have an ongoing
relationship with the school. Legally the Village is not obligated to pay the
bill, because there was not a contract written up. If we do not pay the bill it
may cause future problems with the school system. The Village does have the
option of going against Vickie Crompton in the future for recovering this
payment.
Councilman Finger wanted noted in the minutes that the Village at some point
will make every effort to recoup the money.
Roll: Finger yea, Herndon yea, Maloney yea, Stasny yea, Thompson yea.
Lands/Buildings:
Councilman Finger reminded everyone there is a public hearing on March 20th at
8:00 p.m. This meeting is to review the zoning changes in public forum.
Forestry:
No report
Utilities:
Councilwoman Stasny discussed with council the transmitted sheet from the
Illuminating Co. regarding the Oakwood Development Light. Told council that
when Elliot Allotment was started the Village chose number two of the plans.
Brett Harley of the Illuminating Co. explained the three programs that were
available.
Dan Weir explained to council that Mark Skidmore from Skidmore and Chah
expressed his feeling. He said that item three in the transmittal would not
help the situation in the street lighting, because they are asking for the
Village to accept the streets now. Number three states that Skidmore enter into
a five year private outdoor lighting contract that can be transferred to the
Village when the roadways are dedicated.
Council discussed the issue, went over all three scenarios and decided that
number two was the best issue for the Village and Skidmore and Chah. Number two
is that council enters into a contract under the Municipal Streetlighting
contract which is approved through the PUCO. This cost to the Village would be
$17.84 per month per light for a total of $4709.76 per year. Brett Harley told
council that this contract would be a five year contract and at the end of the
contract it could be extended.
Councilman Finger noted to council that scenario two cost the Village $863.00 a
year more than scenario one -forever. Then went on to say that basically the
developers cost of the street lighting is falling back onto the Village.
Brett Harley told council that if something happens to the street light poles
in the development, the Illuminating Co. will fix them under the contract.
Councilman Thompson told council if we agreed to this contract the Village
would have to look at the lighting levy to make sure it would cover the cost.
Councilman Finger told council that the new development will bring in more tax
dollars when the houses are built.
Motion by Stasny to accept number two which would be council enters into a
contract under the municipal street lighting contract.
2nd by Maloney.
Roll: Finger yea, Herndon yea, Maloney yea, Stasny yea, Thompson yea.

The residents have been asked to call the police when the dogs are barking. The

Finance:
Councilman Thompson set up a finance committee meeting for March 14, 2000 at 7:
00 p.m.
Council discussed the letter from the Ohio Dept. Of Transportation regarding
pre-application for Issue II funds. They agreed that there are going to be
engineering costs for the Mulberry Street/Special Improvement District project.
Solicitor Lemire told council that there has been a Special Improvements
District which is now incorporated. The district was set up to empower the
assessment on both township and village properties to pay for the costs that
are not covered by grants. There is a time frame in which to get these grants.
The engineering is needed to get these grants and if the village does not front
the money for the costs, most likely we will not receive any grants. If we do
not receive any grants the residents of the street will not want to be assessed
for the cost of the project.
Dan Weir told council in submitting the pre-application one major aspect is
that the engineering be already done. The village should go out for bids for
the engineering soon, to get the designs done in time to apply for the grant.
Motion by Finger to fund all of the engineering costs up front. Then have the
administrator solicit quotes for the selection of the engineering firm.
2nd by Herndon.
Roll: Finger yea, Herndon yea, Maloney yea, Stasny yea, Thompson yea.
Solicitor Lemire told council that there is a provision in the statue that the
village could recoup the funds back for the engineering fees.

2nd by Finger

Mayor Bragga told council that next year when the budget is being done he is
requesting the department head be at the finance meeting when there department
is looked over by the Finance Committee. 8:00 p.m. Motion to adjourn from
regular meeting for public hearing. Take consideration of amendments to the

Motion by Thompson to move the meeting into public hearing.
2nd by Maloney
Roll: Finger yea, Herndon yea, Maloney yea, Stasny yea, Thompson yea.
Solicitor Lemire swore in Arthur Aho, Cayce Baxley, John Kusar and Terry
Toukenon to speak during the public hearing.
John Kusar of 132 N. Chestnut Street, Jefferson, expressed his concern about
the letter he sent to council. In the letter he was concerned with the proposed
zoning changes. Specifically, the site plan reviews. Stated that he had great
concern dealing with the idea that the zoning inspector has such powers to
determine what could be used. Asked council to look at the manufactured home
zoning and consider amendments be done before the new zoning code is changed.
Cayce Baxley of 245 East Jefferson Street, Jefferson, told council that the
zoning change has been a long process. It is better for the Village to toughen
the standard and fight for the right issues ahead of time rather than have the
zoning issues come to us at the time when a permit is being applied for and the
interpretation differs. The council must look at the future of the Village to
make sure it is kept up to the standards for the residents.
Terry Toukenon of 175 West Jefferson Street, Jefferson, questioned section
1242.04 of the code.
Discussed sidewalks in a new development, subdivisions with the new
construction site. Concerned that the village was putting the whole burden of
new sidewalks to the land owner. Questioned that with the replacement of
sidewalks, the village helped the resident and in a new development it was up
to the land owner. Toukenon expressed concern with number 14 page four. The
certificate of occupancy for a building. Asked how this could be done if the
building is already occupied and construction is being done on the building.
Asked council to look it over and possibly change the manufactured home
requirements in the new zoning code. Change it from 1000 sq. ft to 980 sq. ft
and amend the new ordinance.
Mayor Bragga told council to think over and consider what was brought up in the
public hearing.
Said that the information would be passed to the Planning Commission.
Councilman Finger expressed that this zoning code will have changes when the
issues come up. The zoning code is a working document and it will be amended
when needed.
Solicitor Lemire explained to council that when amending the new zoning
ordinance, there has to be five yes votes in order for the changes to go into
effect.
Motion by Thompson to close the public hearing and return to regular session.
2nd by Stasny.
Roll: Finger yea, Herndon yea, Maloney yea, Stasny yea, Thompson yea.

monthly report would be given to council.

Resident John Nemeth discussed the truck route issue that was discussed at the
Planning Commission Meeting. Expressed concern that the Village spent money to
have Burgess and Minutes of the Jefferson Village Council Meeting Held April
17, 2000..Niple do a study stating that Cucumber Street was the best possible
road for a truck route. It was also stated that funds from the state were not
available until 2020. Nemeth told council that when the talk of the truck route
came up again that Sycamore Street was stated as possibly being the truck
route. Stated that it would hurt the property values and be a safety issue with
children crossing the truck route to go to Memorial Field and community park
for activities.
Earl Preston told council that the factories are on Cucumber Street. Why would
we route trucks to another street when they still have to get to the factories
on Cucumber. Also when the study was done it was going to be more costly to use
Sycamore Street.
Mayor Bragga said that the main concern is the trucks in the middle of town.
Also noted that there would always be trucks in the middle of town because of
the businesses. With the center of town being a state route we will never be
able to force the trucks not to go around town.
Sycamore Street is a straight route that goes through to 307 and Cucumber does
not. The issues dealing with the truck route are just discussions on the
studies that have been done and will need to be updated. Along with all the
minutes and discussions that were done in the past. It will effect property
values whatever street is picked for the route. Funding for the route will have
to be looked into such as State Issue II money and any other grants for road
funding.

May 8, 2000
Special Meeting
Roll:   Herndon, Maloney, Stasny, Thompson, Ward

Also present:   Administrator Pauley; Solicitor Lemire; Art Magee; Al Savline;
Gary Heefer; Walter Peskur; Gary Fusco
Representatives of the Consumers Ohio Water talked to the Council concerning
the overview of Consumers Ohio Water Company. Stated that the company bought
out the Villages Water System in 1968 and the Franchise agreement with the
Village expires in 2008. Explained to Council that Consumers has done
improvement to the system since it was purchased. They have maintained the line
with the service that was needed. There has also been waterline (new/
replacement) to the amount of $513,000 along with other system improvement to
$970,000 with a total of $1,483,000 in system improvement. With one of them
being a new water tower in the Village, along with booster, meters, valves,
hydrants, and other services.

Council discussed with Consumers Ohio Water Service Company one main concern;
the quality of water and water flow through the lines. Stated the lines were
old and there has been water breaks in areas more than once. (Especially next
to the Elementary School)

Council also questioned some hydrants in town If all worked and if there was a
fire, could enough water come from the hydrant to put out the fire. Asked when
was the last time Consumers Ohio Water Service did a test on all hydrants and
main line flows.

Consumer Ohio Water Company told Council that in all water lines there is
tuberculation which is build up in the lines and it reduces the water flow.
Consumers wen on to tell Council that in 1999 they did $51,300 in waterline
repairs, and in 2000 there will be $175,000 in developer projects which is
funded by the developers. But Consumers has $75,000 in capital waterline
projects projected, with supply projects of over $222,000. It was assured by
Consumers that Jeffersons water lines were being taken care of, but also
explained that the water system is a regional system and everyone pays for any
costs to Consumers

Consumers set up goals with Council which included:
Reasonable Rates
Prompt Service
Quality Water
Fire Flow Status
Community Partnership
Growth in the Community
Successful Lake Shore Division
Joining Lake & Ashtabula Counties Together

Council still issued a concern with Consumers with the water rates and the
figures were on the increase that was done in 1996; quality of water; and fire
hydrant pressures (flow meter tests). Consumers gave the Village a copy of the
scheduled tests.

Consumers told Council that the first priority is to have a strong commitment
with the Village Council and the customers. They agreed to have flow meters
tests done around the Village and anyone questioning the quality of water, they
would test it for the consumer. The rate increase that was done in 1996
Consumers told Council that the PUCO approved the increase and a rate increase
had not been done in years.

Consumers Ohio Water told all of Council if they had any questions they would
be glad to answer questions anytime.

Council and Consumers agreed to set up another meeting to go over all questions
and get figures and answers.

Respectfully Submitted,

Patricia A. Fisher
Clerk-Treasurer

rates.
Mayor Bragga told council that he met with the Clerk and Administrator this
morning for a while. The carry over balance in 1997, 98, 99 decreased and for
the year 2000 it will not carry us through the year-end. It has decreased from
450,000 to 50,000.We need to determine what has happened. The old ordinance
needs to be looked at. The carry over is depleting and we need to rectify that.
The auditor has stated that the Village have a 20% carry over, and by mid 2001
we could be down to zero. This is not a good projection and it needs to be
looked into. This includes both of the funds for the Waste Water Department.
Administrator Pauley told council some of the problem dealt with the billing
cycles not being sent out on time. This dealt with the sewer and refuse.
February and March should have been sent out in April but was sent out May
19th, adjusted to be due by June 19th. The next billing cycle should be sent
out June (June & July sewer) the adjusted due to August 3rd, this would get us
back to a normal billing cycle.
Councilman Finger questioned with this projection and changes in the billing
cycles makes the refuse back on track? What we're spending versus what we're
taking in?
Administrator Pauley told council the dollars if you were to look at this
year’s budget; your expenditures are greater than what we anticipate in our
revenues. Regardless, of what cycle we're on, rolling year not necessarily
January to January. Always have that 20,000-dollar difference. (We're
collecting ahead of time). And We’re collecting insufficient revenue.
Administrator Pauley Explained part of the problem stems from the fact that we
have assumed the responsibilities and duties for collection and billing and the
contracting of our vendor. We are liable for those debts. The bad debt should
have been the contractor’s responsibility.
Councilman Finger asked what do we do to get out of this? I'm not in favor of
the Village subsidizing 20,000 to the garbage hauler.
Administrator Pauley- You do have the escape clause within the contract, where
you can shift that responsibility back to the single franchise vendor. Within
the contract, there are some specific time periods. Example: If the landfill
raised its fee to us, it could pass that fee on to us with a 90-day notice and
10 days notice .We have assumed all collection responsibilities.
Clerk Treasurer Fisher –told council that she was working with Country Disposal
right now. Trying to make them be more accountable. Like they should have been
in the beginning.
Administrator Pauley Stated that they’re supposed to provide us with certain
information such as: starts, stops, vacancies, changes in service. In practice
we have supplied them. (It should be the other way) Part of the problem is that
so and so moved in and the billing never got here for six or seven months, etc.
Exemptions for seniors and business owners, some still being billed and should
have never been.
Councilman Finger expressed that a procedural issue is set up to help us all
understand what its going to take to get the Village out of the business of
subsidizing this. I don't think it was ever intended that way. However, we got
there we should make plans as quickly as possible to get out of it.
Mayor Bragga Stated we find ourselves in several situations, for example we
recently talked about wastewater treatment and the fact that our carry over is
depleting our income is not increasing at the rate that it needs to set a
profit. That’s an issue that needs to be dealt with. We found out a couple
issues in other areas, which we're still dealing with the special audit,
waiting for that to happen. Now we're looking at refuse collections that
everybody’s touched on for the last few months. We're going to fix it; it’s
going to take some time.
Mayor Bragga said to council you have to understand that there's a certain
amount of record keeping and trust that has to balance. We're doing the billing
they're doing the collection. When you have that kind of an arrangement there's
room for error. If they do the collection and they do the billing there's less
room for error, theoretically. If we do the collection and the billing there's
less room for error. We have two entities trying to run one service. It's not
an easy task.
Administrator Pauley told council the original contract did provide for him to
do the service, the collection, billing and record keeping. For whatever reason
the contract was modified so that he provides the service, but the Village has
assumed the record keeping, the billing and the collection.
Councilman Finger said the thing that bothers me is that, some of us that were

Ordinance2321
An Ordinance Amending Title six- Administration, chapter 232,section232.05
Pertaining to the Secretary
Councilman Thompson questioned usually our ordinance has what the old text was
included in it. This Ordinance does not please tell me what changed?
Administrator Pauley it is just a different style of drafting. When I draft
ordinance I normally do not put the old language in.
Administrator Pauley explained to council the old ordinance read, a secretary
should be employed to assist the Village Administrator. Reporting directly to
the Mayor and Village Council and shall be directed in duties by the Village
Administrator.
The old one said, she takes direction solely from the Village Administrator.
The new one reports to Mayor, Village Council and Administrator.
Mayor Bragga told council I couldn’t speak for Administrator Pauley but suppose
the person worked a 40-hour week. Lets suppose a portion of that time was
devoted to refuse billing, our Clerk Treasurer is responsible for the financial
ins and outs of the district, of the Village, in the absence of the
Administrator, or doing business in that account the Clerk Treasurer needed
that person to do a particular job then that employee would in that case could
possibly have more than one boss.
Councilman Thompson expressed his concern saying that was part of the problem
that got us where we are. The fact that there was a description reflecting this
and that support was eliminated.
Administrator Pauley expressed to I don't agree somebody has to be the
supervisor of the employee, responsible for giving directions and writing
performance evaluation, discipline and recommending raises and everything that
goes along with being the supervisor of the employee. The direction of work is
something different.
Mayor Bragga told council maybe that is s what it needs to reflect. The
Administrator is the supervisor. However, the person will work for or assist
when needed.
Administrator Pauley said we can accomplish that simply by a job description
and not designate this position specifically within the ordinance because if
all else fails and the budgets go in a hand basket, there are 3 positions that
would be defined within the code that would be: the Administrator, the
Secretary, and the Chief of Police and the Chief of Fire.
Administrator Pauley stated those positions are defined within the code, if
budgets went down to zero, and we had no money, those are the 3 that would have
to be employed for the Village. You could take that out of the code and simply
have this position enabled by the creation of the job description and by
funding of the position that had the responsibility defined by the job
description. The job description, currently says title of supervisor - Village
Administrator and reports directly to the Village Administrator.
Mayor Bragga said to Council a secretary should be employed to assist the
Village Administrator, The Mayor, and Village Council.
Mayor Bragga stated I don't object to adding the Clerk Treasurer in the list of
people that they can do work for. I object to the removing of the last
sentence. That says, clearly defines, the Village Administrator as having the
responsibility of supervising the person.
Councilman Thompson said add back in "shall be directed by Village
Administrator. Leave as was.
Administrator Pauley explained we are only adding to the list of people the
Clerk Treasurer, the old list did not have Clerk Treasurer.
Clerk Treasurer Fisher said to Council the only problem this pertains to that
she has fiscal responsibility and that was where we came into a major problem
with our utilities department in the past.
Administrator Pauley said we are where we are with regard to a couple of
finance accounts because we lacked a step in the process in a direct
involvement of the Clerk Treasurer with that particular person.
Bragga? - Billing Clerk was written in to do the kinds of things that we're in
trouble with right now and the discussion was that after we got out of this
cycle somebody would assume that responsibility.
Mayor Bragga told council I'm not going to argue that point but the point is
that what has been happening didn't work. This previous Council had for want of
a better agreed that the Clerk Treasurer would oversee that particular portion
of financial information that was required of the Village, but in fact it
didn't happen because I don't know why, it didn't happen. And consequently
we've got some problems with regard to sewer billing and sidewalk billing and
refuse collection etc. because of that. I just want to solve the problem.
Councilwoman Maloney told council this doesn't say work for, it says assist and
provide assistance to the Mayor, Village Council, and Clerk Treasurer. Assist
doesn't mean boss.
Administrator Pauley noted to Council I think Councils intend when they created
the position, and put it within the code was to provide assistance to the
Administrator, and provide assistance to the Mayor, Members of Council and the
Clerk Treasurer. So yes, by virtue of my responsibility as Administrator, I
have direct responsibility for all employees except for police, fire and legal.
Those are put outside. Within the job description this person reports directly
to me. In the code as was written prior to this, it took out the ability for
the Clerk Treasurer to have any influence over this person. I think that
looking back at the history and what happened since we are trying to rectify
that problem by putting that additional ability back in there. That one person
still being under my supervision, their sole purpose in life is to provide
assistance to me and to assist the Council and the Mayor and the Clerk
Treasurer. In my case I have two bosses. On Legislative matters I respond to
the Council as a whole on Administrative matters I respond to the Mayor. I
would love to have one boss but by the nature of the business it doesn't
happen.
Clerk Treasurer Pat Fisher expressed to Council my main concern is about the
problems that have been going on.
Mayor Bragga read a letter addressed to the Clerk Treasurer dated (August 25th
1999), copy sent to prior Mayor. It read
To: Clerk Treasurer, Pat Fisher from Dan Weir, the Administrator.
In accordance with ordinance number 2064, the Administrative Assistance is
under the direct control of the Village Administrator; to prevent any further
conflicts between your office and mine, discontinue with Michele assisting with
your elected duties and inherent responsibility. So that’s what I don't want to
have happen again. That’s what prompted this whole discussion.
Mayor Bragga - Again, I wasn't here. Nor was Administrator Pauley. We're just
trying to put a piece of documentation in place that is going to give the
proper people and the proper offices the ability to oversee the matters that
need to be observed and supervised.
Administrator Pauley this would give us two signatures on every deposit and all
receipts that are needed per the auditor’s recommendation.
Mayor Bragga said to Council I'm confident that the current Clerk and the
current Administrator are going to have the ability to communicate, work
together. I hope I'm correct in that statement, I believe that. Ergo, if we put
in the statement that the Administrator supervises in charge at this point, I
don't see a problem. You always have the possibility of a change in Clerk
position or Administrator position.
Councilwoman Herndon - Mr. Mayor, I suggest we delete department heads leaving,
Administrator, Mayor and Clerk Treasurer and Village Council, but we do not
have as much input as far as work is concerned. I agree with using assist as a
good word for the situation.
Administrator Pauley commented to council one of the things that led to the
rift before was the fact that her job description says I have to do only what
is in the code and the code said I don't have to talk to that side of the hall.
Clerk Treasurer Fisher explained to Council another problem is that she still
takes money that’s a big issue, with a problem in checks and balances. The
Administrator said she could do it the way she wanted but there are proper
procedures that have to be followed. Proper procedures have not been followed.
Most people under utilities, in Villages and smaller towns are under the
Finance Director, with the small amount of people, we have to work together. We
have procedures and steps that have to be taken for cash balancing and double-
checking and with this happening it has not happened.
Councilwoman Maloney made a motion to amend Ordinance 2323 section 232.05 of
Secretary
(Which reads a secretary shall be employed to assist the Village Administrator,
the Mayor and the Village Council and shall be directed in her duties and work
responsibilities solely by the Village Administrator)
Second – Finger
Roll Call - All Yea Motion Carried
Motion by Thompson to make the Income Tax position full time
Second – Herndon
Discussion
Councilman Finger said to council basically, she would be 1/2 time income tax
and 1/2 time something else. We started out with the understanding that
bringing Income Tax back to the Village was only going to cost us 25 hours a
week. We are already up to 78 every 2 weeks. Do we have a job description?
Administrator Pauley noted to council there is a point there that Income Tax is
not daily. This position would obviously assist. It is badly needed.
Mayor Bragga stated in an organization like this village. When an organization
chooses to take on an additional work and additional responsibility in this
case waste collection and refuse collection. Those two responsibilities in my
opinion were not properly in place before the action occurred. One of the
reason were having a special audit regarding the Recreation Dept. Proper
procedures were not in place prior to the adoption of the action. Now we find

to go back and make sure we have people in place to do these kinds of things.
When you add a position a good percentage of the time you got it.
Mayor Bragga said it is going to take some time. When those actions occurred
proper procedures that are in place today were not in place then. If they were,
we would not be in the position we are in now.

Leaf bags from Ashtabula County Environmental Services - Recycling Program were
presented by Street Forman Ferguson. These are biodegradable clear bags, 30
gallon and are completely recyclable. These bags will cost the Village $.10 per
bag. We plan on getting 7200 bags this year and they will be distributed free
to village residents. Bags may be picked-up at the town hall or community
center, with proof of residency. This is a trial and all leaves must be in the
clear bags to be picked-up . The village will not pick up any bags other than
the clear bags. Residences will be notified of this change through the
newspaper and on the sewer bills.

Seconded by Finger
Roll: All Yea. Motion Carried
Visitor comments:
Citizen Casey Baxley questioned the gas and electric deregulation, wanting to
know what the Village was doing regarding the aggregation.
Administrator Pauley and Mayor Bragga explained that the Village passed an
Ordinance to put the aggregation legislation on the November ballot. The voters
will be asked to decide whether the Village of Jefferson will have the
authority to aggregate the electric for the Village. If passed, the resident
will still be able to opt out of the aggregation if they choose.
   The Village is discussing and will vote on joining a Northeast Ohio Mayors
and Managers Association to group together to get the best possible rate for
electricity. It was explained that council is putting all efforts to
electricity now, and it is foreseeable the same may happen for gas as it has
for electricity, in the future.
Citizen Bill Johnston questioned if there would be a mess with electricity as
there is with sewer.
Mayor Bragga assured him that the Village is joining in a pool to get the best
rate. The Village would not be involved in collection and billing.
Department Reports:
Administrator Pauley announced that Village residents will be able to pick up
leaf bags starting September 20, 2000, at the Recreation Center and Town Hall.
Drivers License must be shown for proof of residency. The schedule for leaf
pickup is October 23rd, October 30th and November 13th. Only the biodegradable
bags will be picked up. Also, noted was that the last brush pick up will be
October 2, 2000.

DEPARTMENT REPORTS
Administrators Report
Administrator Pauley reminded everyone that the last brush pick-up will be on
October 2, 2000. He also said that the leaf bags are available at the Village
Hall and Community Center. The leaf bag scheduled dates for pick-up are October
23, October 30 and November 13. The Bio Bag provided by the Village will be the
only ones picked up.
Administrator Pauley told Council that attached to his report was the current
rate/rental agreement for Council to look at. He had received the plans from
COWC for installation/replacement for E. Erie Street and he forwarded to Chief
Wayman for comment on W. Mulberry Street and Poplar Street. These replacements
would need Councils approval.
He has had numerous zoning inquiries regarding Bed & Breakfast or Museum sites.
Since neither are addressed in Planning and Zoning Code, he recommends this
issue be referred to committee.
Administrator Pauley told Council that an information sheet about transient
vendors was distributed to area businesses/merchants.
A request was received for the closure of North Polpar Street for the Covered
Bridge Festival on October 14th and 15th, 2000 from 10:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.
Along with the road closing, no parking signs were asked to be posted along
North Elm Street.
Administrator Pauley requested the approval of the Disposition of Surplus
Property. He recommended a public auction be held Saturday, October 28, 2000 at
10:00 a.m. at the Village Streets Department Garage. The Ohio Revised Code
allows municipal corporations to sell equipment, vehicles or machinery which is
no longer needed to another municipal corporation. The equipment, vehicles or
machinery must have a written contract and the transfer must be sold at fair
market value. Discussion followed. Council agreed, working with other
municipalities is good public relations.
Motion by Finger to approve the disposal of surplus property no longer needed
for municipal purpose in the form of an auction. Seconded by Maloney.
Roll: All Yea. Motion Carried.
Motion by Finger to accept the Village Administrators recommendation to sell
surplus equipment to municipalities as noted. Seconded by Maloney.
Roll: All Yea. Motion Carried.

Permissive Auto Fund. She told Council the transfer of the monies from Capital
Improvement and General Fund would restore the Permissive Auto Fund to a
positive balance. Fisher requested $10,000 from Capital Improvement Fund and
$20,000 from the General Fund. (Action taken in Finance Committee)

Visitor Comments:
Kelly Batanian of 137 West Erie Street asked Council what was going to be
resolved with the Sewer blockage that originated in the Village lines on Friday
October 13, 2000 which resulted in damages to numerous homes in the Village
including her basement and her neighbor’s basement. Was told by the Village
Administrator that it was beyond the Village’s control. Ms. Batanian wanted to
know why there isn’t maintenance that checks the lines and why there isn’t
something in the Village’s insurance to protect the property owner when
situations like this happen. Her insurance picked up some of the costs but not
all and wanted to know if she could get help from the Village.
Ms. Batanian questioned the increased sewer cost to the villagers. Asked if the
sewer increases cover the cost of maintaining the sewer lines Told Council she
was told the sewer lines in the Village are a self maintained systems, asked
how could something like this happen. She presented a petition to Council
asking for restitution to the families involved by the Village of Jefferson for
damages incurred.
Citizen John Powers of 131 West Erie Street raises the same concerns as Ms.
Batanian however his insurance does not cover all of the costs which are
approximately $2,600. He also expressed concern over the way he was handled by
the Village’s insurance representative, Cheryl Connor, her attitude and
approach to the problem with Mr. Powers was in a nonprofessional manner.
Mayor Bragga informed Council and residents that the sewer increase is needed
to run and maintain the Wastewater Treatment Plant. Also, the State Auditors
suggested the Village should have a certain percent carry over at the end of
the year in case something catastrophic should occur at the plant. He also
suggested for the Village to check into their insurance policy to see if
coverage exists or can be added for situations like this. Mayor Bragga asked
the Wastewater Treatment Committee to look into this situation further.
Cayce Baxley asked Council to look at the trees planted at Drug Mart to see if
they were according to specifications. Her concern was they will not, during
her son’s lifetime, be of sufficient size to give shade.

Administrator Pauley explained to Council that Custodian / Utility Maintenance
A position is a permanent, part-time, 25 hours per week position. Also,
Custodian / Utility Maintenance B position is a permanent, other than part
time, 8 hours per week position. The rates for both are: Starting - $7.25/hr;
Completion of 6 month probation - $7.75/hr; and 1 year anniversary - $8.25/hr.
He also stated that for Custodian/Utility B position, because the person works
less than 520 hours per year the Village is under no obligation to supply
medical benefits and after they acquire 2080 hours they will be able to get
prorated hours of sick time, holiday time, and vacation time.

Council suggested a letter be sent to Ohio Consumers Water Company requesting

installations.

Visitor Comments:
Mark Fuerst addressed Council with concerns regarding the trees at the new Drug
Mart. Stated he received a call from the Mayor explaining Council was
questioning the release of his bond on the trees. Fuerst told Council he felt
he had followed the agreement that he had signed with the Village regarding the
trees in his development. Explained he removed the designated trees that the
committee had agreed upon. Saved what trees he could, even when there were
problems with trees falling in conjunction along the water line. He contacted
the Village to inform them that trees were damaged when the hole was dug.
Stated he only planted eight trees because he did not cut down all of the trees
that were originally planned with the committee. Told Council he planted trees
in the lot that follows the Village tree plan. Council referred back to minutes
dated October 4, 1999 which explained in detail what and how many trees that
were to be torn down and replanted. Council at this time told Fuerst they felt
the trees planted were not what was agreed upon. Council questioned the size of
trees that were planted and asked why only eight trees were planted.
Mark Fuerst explained he planted only eight trees because he did not cut all
the trees down that were originally planned. Councilwoman Maloney said that
Allen Stewart, the Urban Forester, came and looked at the trees that were
damaged from installing the water line. He stated he felt the trees were
severely stressed and did not feel they would make it through the winter. Mark
Fuerst told Council if the trees did not survive he would replace them. He also
told Council that he has done whatever they have asked him to do.
Mayor Bragga explained to Council he contacted Mark Fuerst to keep an open
communications with the issue and try to resolve things in a good nature.
Rejine DeSalvatore spoke to Council in regards to the acceptance of Brittany
Lane for maintenance purposes. She told Council that the Lemire Estates has
followed all recommendations that the Village had indicated in the engineer’s
inspection.
DEPARTMENT REPORT
Recreation Committee Report
Jefferson Community Center Director Hellmer told Council that the Recreation
Department is prepping up for Christmas. Told Council in conjunction with all
the activities involving the Christmas Parade and Merchants Sale; the Community
Center will have a Craft and Antique Sale from 10:00 a.m. until 4:00 p.m. From
one p.m. to three p.m., children will be able to make Christmas ornaments that
will be taken and put on the Christmas tree in the gazebo. From three p.m.
until four p.m. there will be a storybook hour and at six p.m. is the parade.
After the parade Santa will come back to the Community Center to have his
picture taken with the children. December 9, 2000 from nine a.m. until eleven-
thirty at the Community Center you can have breakfast with Santa. December 16,
2000. The Kids Theater will put on a show for anyone who wants to see it at
four p.m. at the school.
Recreation Director Hellmer told Council that he made a plot of the Village
marking all trees that had fallen down or were cut down along with the new ones
that were replaced. A total of fifty-five trees had come down in the Village.
Thirty-five have been replanted this fall. Fifty-five more will be planted in
the spring. Any resident that is interested in having a tree planted in their
tree lawn, please contact the Village Office or the Recreation Department.

offered at Kent State. The extension of the East Erie Street sanitary sewer is
complete. Administrator Pauley asked Council to consider the E-Mail and

Wastewater
Council discussed at length the Sewer Rate Ordinance. Some of Council expressed
concern again that 11.5 percent was still too high. Did not feel comfortable
passing this on to the residents of the Village. Felt that the Sewer Rate
Ordinance should be tabled until after the conclusion of budget appropriations
for 2001.
Administrator Pauley reiterated to Council that a 11.5 percent increase was
necessary to insure enough revenues to meet expenditures if the new budget is
capped at the 2000 budget levels. Stated this will only preserve the fund, not
increase any surplus in the fund reserve. Also expressed concern again to
Council without an increase the reserve could possibly be totally depleted in
the first quarter of 2001.
Motion by Finger to table the Sewer Rate Ordinance No. 2322 until at such time
as the 2001 appropriations are completed to see what actual revenues are needed
to operate the fund. 2nd by Maloney.
Roll: All yea. Motion carried.

December 4, 2000
Held Town Hall Council Chambers
Meeting was called to order by Mayor Bragga at 7:30 p.m.
Mayor Bragga offered opening prayer.
Roll: Finger, Herndon, Maloney, Stasny, Thompson
Absent: Ward
Also present:
Administrator Pauley, Solicitor Lemire, Clerk-Treasurer Fisher, Gazette, Star
Beacon, News Herald, Cayce Baxley, C. Pengel, John Wayman, R. A. Hummel.
Minutes of the November 20, 2000 Regular Council meeting were approved with the
change on page 3 under bills remove the P.O. number in right column.
Minutes of the November 20, 2000 Planning Commission meeting were approved as
written.
Motion by Maloney to approve the list of bills for December 4, 2000. Seconded
by Herndon.
Roll Call: All Yea. Motion Carried.
Visitors Comments:
Casey Baxley complemented the Village as a whole in the support that was given
to the whole community on December 2, 20000 with the annual Merchants Sale and
Christmas Parade.
Richard Hummel asked Council questions regarding the Electric Deregulations
with rates opting out and what involvement the Village would have. Mayor Bragga
explained that the Village is involved with the Northeast Ohio Public Energy
Council. This happened with the Village residents choosing to vote yes on the
November ballot. With Jefferson in the NOPEC as a group, we will purchase
electricity power at the lowest cost possible. Each resident of the Village
will get a mailer explaining the NEPEC. Every citizen in the Village has the
option to choose if they want to stay with the Village’s choice or opt out and
pick their own electric power company. As a Council the per kilowatt cost has
not been determined yet. The local representative for the Council in the County
is Tony Zempredo. Administrator Pauley explained that there will be two County
Public Hearings regarding NOPEC. The hearings will be December 14, 2000, at 7:
00 p.m. at Eastlake Community Center and December 18, 2000, at 7:00 p.m. at
Brecksville Community Center. Explained to everyone also that any person could
go in the NOPEC web page to find out more information. In January the NOPEC as
a whole will have more information and figures.
Department Reports:
Administrators Report:
Administrator Pauley told Council that the Service Department has been working
hard all over the Village in preparation for the holiday decorations. Expressed
the Recreation Department has a full schedule of events going on at the
Recreation Center for the holiday. The Village received the results on the
District 11 Area Agency Contract and Evaluation. The Village was in compliance
in all areas. Administrator Pauley informed Council of the resignation letter
from Lisa Hamper regarding her gymnastic class. Informed Council that she now
has opened her own gym and her last day would be December 16, 2000.
Administrator Pauley asked Council to look over his memos regarding the Ohio
Bicentennial Commission with the Village’s involvement, along with the
Northeast Ohio Public Energy Council legislation with its adoption.
Administrator Pauley thanked First Class Construction for the donation of the
tree-planting bond to the Tree Planting Program.
Announced the Public Hearing of the Bethel Bible annexation on December 14, 11:
30 a.m. at the Commissioners’ office.
 Chief Wayman Fire Department:
Chief Wayman addressed Council with his concerns regarding the dwindling of
enrollment in the Jefferson Volunteer Fire Department, which has a lot to do
mostly with the previous administration and lack of involvement in people
today. It takes a lot of time to be a fire fighter and people today do not want
to put the time in, they would rather be doing other things. Chief Wayman went
on to tell council of the report on the departments Insurance Service Office
Rating. The Department met with the ISO representative in June. Spent four days
reviewing record keeping, conducted test of pumps, fire engines, hoses, Village
water supply at hydrants and other required checks from the Fire Department.
Results are not in, but all looked good except for weakness in the number of
personnel responding to major fires. State enrollment is down from 38 to 20
volunteer members. Chief Wayman expressed concern that in the future the
Village will probably be looking at a full paid or part paid department. Chief
Wayman moved to the discussion of repairs that need to be done on the 1983
Pierce Arrow. Mostly involving an engine refurbish. The repairs the engine
needs include: a pump assembly, repairing the leaking water tank, installation
of a transmission lock out system and the enclosure of the rear compartment,
with some of the repairs involving safety issues. Other items would include
painting of the truck, replacing window cracks, and relining the cab. The total
refurbishing would cost as much as $90,000. To replace the truck it would cost
$275,000.00, but the truck has low mileage and is a good quality truck.
Chief Wayman also informed Council that the Village should look into possibly
replacing the 1975 truck.
Councilwoman Moloney questioned the water pressure in the Village and asked if
all the flow test had been done on the fire hydrants in the Village. Councilman
Finger questioned if the Chief would have the figures in writing for the
finance committee meeting. Chief Wayman said he would have a rough draft.
Council Maloney asked how many more years we would get from the truck when it
is repaired. Chief Wayman told Council about 15 years.

permits. Discussion continued with zoning codes and its interpretation. The
final outcome lead to whatever is written in the zoning codes what will be

VISITORS’ COMMENTS (none)
DEPARTMENT REPORTS
Administrator’s Report
Administrator Pauley told Council that the Service Department is working hard
keeping the streets clean with all the snow and ice that the Village has
received in December. He reminded all residents that the Village would collect
Christmas Trees January 2nd, 8th and 16th of 2001. Administrator Pauley asked
that the trees be put at the curb, preferably without bags around them. He told
Council that the holiday programs are still continuing at the Recreation
Center. Expressed to Council that there were repairs done to the Woodside lift
station which included the thermal overload contactors.
Administrator Pauley requested Council to approve the ICMA University Training
E-Government, E-Commerce, and E-Lectorate training on February 24, 2001 at the
Dublin Windham hotel in Columbus, with registration costs of $75.00.
Administrator Pauley noted his memo to Council regarding the recommendation
from the Planning Commission on Museum uses.

AN ORDINANCE AUTHORIZING A PENALTY CHARGE FOR THE ISSUANCE OF A CHECK ON A BANK

Councilman Thompson discussed with Council the memo from Clerk Treasurer
regarding the Recreation Dept. with its shortfall for revenues in 2000.
Councilman Finger referred to the year to date Summary Funds Report. Questioned
that the anticipated revenue amount does not meet the actual revenue amount,
there is a short fall.
Clerk-Treasurer Fisher explained this happened in the B-4 Recreation Account
because in the middle of the year all expenditures were moved to the B-
4 Recreation Fund. This was done because the fund was set up in the middle of
the year as an Enterprise type fund. The Recreation Fund is not a true
enterprise fund because it is subsidized by the General Fund. Clerk-Treasurer
Fisher explained the memo regarding the Recreation Funds. Told Council that as
of December 15, 2000, the Recreation Fund was $19,666.05 in the negative.
Explained that the Recreation Fund was not over expended but the Revenues that
were anticipated for the year were falling short.
Mayor Bragga told Council that the Clerk-Treasurer had come to him earlier with
the information. Also explained that the Recreation Fund would never be a true
enterprise fund and be self-sufficient. Expressed that maybe Council should
rethink how we set up the Recreation Fund. Be it an Enterprise Fund or part of
the General Fund.
Councilwoman Maloney expressed Council did not request the Recreation Fund to
be an Enterprise Fund. The Auditors suggested it. All Council wants is a way to
track the revenues against expenditures.
Councilman Thompson told everyone, on a positive note towards the Recreation
Department, right now they are running the Recreation Department generating 60%
of the fund and only 40% of the funding coming from the General Fund.
Councilman Ward told Council he would like to set up a work session with the
Recreation Committee and Council. Suggested January 8th at 7:30 p.m.
Councilwoman Herndon expressed to Council that the Recreation Department would
never be self supporting. Asked Council to consider an operating levy to help
with the costs of operating the Department.
Motion by Thompson for the first reading of Resolution 2343 with the amount of
$20,000 transferred from the General fund to the Recreation Fund.
2nd by Finger.
After a lengthy discussion Council decided to change the amount of transfer
from $20,000 to $22,000.
Councilman Thompson withdrew his first motion on Resolution 2343.
Councilman Finger withdrew his second on Resolution 2343.
Motion by Thompson for the first reading of Resolution 2343 with the amount of
$22,000 transferred from the General Fund to the Recreation Fund.

Officials
Mayor Bragga read his State of the Village for 2001 to Council.
Tuesday, January 02,2001
The year 2000 proved to be a very interesting, insightful and fast-paced year.
I appreciate the communication and the support of many members of our
community. The administration has
made significant efforts to promote a more professional and business-like
approach to the
operations of the village.
I want to mention just a few of the many positives that have occurred in a few
short
months.
Because of the interest and effort and dedication of our local American Legion
Post 3334 as well as community wide support our police department has a K-
9 officer and a trained and certified K-9 handler.
Through the partnership effort with our Jefferson Chamber of Commerce, the
village
administrator, several citizens, and some cooperative council committees, we
are now on-line, with a web page and e-mail addresses. Our citizens are able to
view council and commission agendas on-line prior to the meeting,
Because of improving organization and planning, we now post our council agendas
in public places (at the village hail, community center and police station)
prior to council meetings in an effort to keep our public informed.
Our administrator, in cooperation with the clerk/treasurer, has revised and
updated many procedures and forms that relate to the daily operations of the
village ... from billing procedures to applications for various permits.
Weekly department head meetings are occurring to help insure a means of
communication and team-work among all village departments.
Thanks to the cooperative efforts of council and the approval of some personnel
changes and a positive approach of village employees our village offices are
more customer friendly.
Our council and administration has addressed some serious and unfortunate
financial issues with class and professionalism.
I could go on and on relating the many positive issues and changes that have
occurred in 2000; but, I must press forward and suggest and encourage this
village to address a variety of
issues and challenges that face us in the next few years beginning in 2001.
We have made significant strides to create proper accounting procedures and
checks and balances for our daily collection accounts in recreation, refuse and
waste water. We must continue to monitor and formally adopt proper daily
accounting and reconciliation procedures.
This council needs to review and revisit our refuse billing procedures and be
certain our efforts are not only beneficial and convenient for our residents ,
but also are meeting all costs involved in our management of the program.
A decision with respect to our waste water treatment charges to our customers
needs to be made. Our public needs to be apprised of the complete and total
operation, maintenance and improvement needs of our WWTP and the requirements
in meeting all state, local and EPA rules and regulations. We need to regularly
adjust and visit our plan for growth and development. We need to communicate,
study and plan for continued maintanance and improvement of our systems sewer
lines and plant operations. We need to be reminded of the problem areas of our
storm sewer lines as well.
With the continued growth and complexities of our village and unfortunate past
situations described in recent audits, I will be recommending a standing audit
committee for our village.
Some of the Audit committees responsibilities may include:
1. meeting with independent auditors before and after each audit
2. monitoring the progress of the financial and compliance audit
3. evaluating the results of the audits
4. ensure internal control and legal compliance issues are promptly addressed
and effectively remedied.
With members to include the mayor and one member of council appointed by the
mayor and one citizen member appointed by the mayor.
To continue with my thoughts on the financial side .... we need to be aware of
our assets with proactive planning and procedures and NOT continuous crisis
management . Let us create a clear vision, mission statement and commitment to
a strategic capital plan. We need to plan on using our assets related to such
things as; recreation center and programs, WWTP as a utility, refuse collection
as a utility, the Rush Creek parcels as potential assets, and addressing
planned and surprise growth as it relates to our total financial plan.
There are some safety issues we must address in 2001 and beyond.
We need to once again be pro-active in our discussion, study and approach to
fire service in the future. Like it or not, several factors ( factors like
continuous growth and development and changes in society) dictate we attack
this important issue in 2001.
We need to aggressively seek state of Ohio attention and financial support for
additional traffic controls at the intersections of 307 on both north and south
Chestnut (46). Additionally, we should not forget the needed truck route in an
effort to improve safety and efficient access to our industrial areas of the
Village.
The village needs to be continually aware of its potential for growth and
development planning and zoning regulations need to remain open and improving
documents that support and reflect what we want for our village and what we
believe this village should be and grow into.
We must continue to learn and gain knowledge with respect to electric and
natural gas utilities and hope that our membership in NOPEC for electric
deregulation will prove to be beneficial to the budgets of our citizens. As it
proves a correct decision, we will direct a positive approach with NOPEC to
proceed with natural gas aggregation and purchasing.
We need to continue to explore our influence and communication with Consumer
Ohio Water Service as they provide water service to our village.
The table is full but constantly changing .... and I have mentioned only some
of our many and varied issues and concerns I would be remiss if I failed to
emphasize two most important pieces of our total community .... a thanks to our
churches , their leaders and church families that create the fundamental stable
foundation for a quality community,,,, as I relate a basic premise to my simple
philosophy, “our community is no better than our churches and our schools” We
Must get involved in the necessity of supporting, improving and becoming
knowledgeable about our local school system.... and become involved with the
powers at the state level who daily affect operations , regulations,
legislation and funding decisions and mandates that directly impact our local
educational system the very system that is responsible for providing the
education for our students and, in turn ,affecting the attitude, image and
perception of our village and total school district.
Finally, I thank this council for your patience, cooperation, knowledge,
communication and support .... my prayer continues to be that we work together
in an effort to continue to improve in making our village a safe and beautiful
place to live, work and raise a family.

the changes going on with Adelphia Cable. The changes include prices on analog
cable rates which dropped from $13.50 to $9.95. Talked that digital cable is
available to all residents of the Village of a monthly fee. The residents would
have to pay additional costs for the digital box. Told Council of new channels
available to the Village, and said that internet access ability would be
available to all residents in late spring or early summer.

withdrawal the adoption of amended ordinance 2322. Pertaining to Rules of
Council rule number 27: which states when an ordinance is amended on the third
reading it must proceed back to the second reading. Then at the next meeting
have a third reading and adoption.

Department Reports
Administrator Pauley told Council that the maintenance of the gravel roads are
continuing along with pothole patching.
Administrator Pauley asked Council to approve his request for the purchase of a
mid mount mower and acceptance of the trade in.
Administrator Pauley told Council on March 6, 2001 at the Senior Lunch Chief
Febel will have an orientation session regarding the Severe Weather Alert
Siren. Also told Council that the testing of the siren is scheduled for March
14th at 11:00 am
Administrator Pauley told Council that the Recreation Committee summary updates
and recommendation for the Community Center programs that were given to Council
should be considered for acceptance and approval.
Administrator Pauley told Council the recommendation for the Amendment to
Section 1030.15 Sewers – pertain to the distribution of collection fees need to
be looked over by Council and action taken. Legislation for the amendment will
set both inside Village and outside Village user to the same distribution of
funds.
Administrator Pauley told Council included in the Council packets was a
resolution regarding the urging of Natural Gas Aggregation. This legislation –
County Commissioners are urging local government to pass. This would allow
local government to aggregate natural gas in the same manner as electric
aggregation.
Administrator Pauley also told Council before them there is also a resolution
urging the support of NOPEC and City of Cleveland’s complaint to PUCO regarding
allocation of MSG. This is a complaint to the PUCO in the First Energy’s method
of allocation of Market Start up Gerneration (MSG).
Administrator Pauley also updated Council on the NOPEC Energy agreement. The
agreement is a letter of understanding with Green Mountain Energy Co. of
Austin, Texas to provide electricity to NOPEC’s residential customers. The
contract would be a six year contract with the savings of 6-8 percent from the
amount customers were paying for electric last year.
Administrator Pauley told Council the bid openings for the refurb of 412 will
be March 9, 2001 at noon.
Mayor Bragga told Council Chief Febel would give his report later in the
meeting as he had a prior engagement.
Fire Chief John Wayman responded to Council with the questions that were
brought up at the last meeting regarding Ryan Otto’s training and the pancake
breakfast. He told Council that last summer Council approved the training but
Ryan could not attend it then. Also told Council that the pancake breakfast was
put on by the Firemen’s Association which $138.00 was collected to feed the
fire fighters during structure fires.

Finance
Councilman Finger questioned the memo regarding the transferring of funds from
the E9 fund to the E2 fund. Asked with this change would it reflect the sewer
rate that has been discussed since last year.
Clerk Treasurer Fisher told Council when the appropriation figures were entered
into the financial charter of account worksheet the totals for the E2 Waste
Water Treatment Fund did not correspond to the summary page totals taken from
the budget worksheet done for 2001.
Administrator Pauley told Council when the drafts were being done for the
appropriations for 2001, in one of the first drafts when the budget was reduced
$17,000 was subtracted within the fund on the total summary page. It was
inadvertently subtracted twice. So when the Clerk Treasurer put in the figures
that Council approved, the figures did not align. He assured Council that the
budget had not been changed and this would not have any effect on the sewer
rate adjustment that was just approved by Council.
After a lengthy discussion it was agreed to amend the appropriation Ordinance
and transfer funds from E9 Sewer improvement to E2 Waste Water Treatment. With
this amendment of appropriations ordinance, it will have to revert back to the
second reading, per Rule of Council for the Village. The third reading would be
done on March 19, 2001. This would be done in time for the Ohio Revised Code
requirement for the adoption of the Budget by April 1st.
Mayor Bragga told Council that a lot of work was put into the budget
preparation and did not want this error to have any reflection on the
accomplishments the Village had done in preparations.
Motion by Finger to amend Ordinance No. 01-O-2345 and add $17,000 to the E2
Fund line.
2nd by Thompson
Roll: All yea, motion carried.
Motion by Finger for the second reading of Ordinance No. 01-O-2345, as amended.
2nd by Thompson
Roll: All yea, motion carried.

Visitors Comments:
Mayor Bragg told Council that Township Trustee Tim Skidmore had talked with him
earlier in the week regarding the application for annexation by Nassief
Properties. Mayor Bragga had extended the invitation for all the Township
Trustees to address Council regarding annexation in general and this parcel in
particular.
Trustee Tim Skidmore addressed Council with a short discussion regarding
Cooperative Economic Development Districts (CEDD’s), a type of development
district that was approved by the State in 1999. He indicated that the Township
would still have legislative authority over the properties, but the Village
could charge higher service rates for the sanitary sewers. He indicated that
the sewer issues were still the same as they were 10 years ago when discussions
were centering on Worthington Cylinders, and he felt that the Village and
Township should work cooperatively.
Councilmember Thompson indicated that the Village was not opposed to sitting
down with the Township, but CEDD’s (authorized by Section 701 of the ORC) are
different than JEDD’s (authorized by Section 715 in the ORC) and was not sure
if residential areas could be included.
Trustee Skidmore indicated that the Nassief proposal includes approximately 120
homes, and septic fields are not feasible on this site.
Councilmember Maloney indicated that she felt that the Wastewater Committee
should look at the sewer issue and should make a recommendation to Council.
Mayor Bragga reminded all that the Village has not solicited any annexation,
that the annexations have occurred because sewer services are not available by
the Township.
Councilmember Thompson indicated that he could look at it from the Township’s
perspective, and felt that CEDD’s could be looked at.
Councilmember Finger asked that the annexation process be explained, and is the
Village required to pass a resolution of availability of services.
Solicitor Lemire explained the annexation process, and stated that the
Commissioner’s have a very specific guideline that they must follow.
Township Trustee Martha Demshar stated that she was not in opposition to the
development of the Nassief Property, but was opposed to annexation in general.
She indicated that the Township has only 5 major employers, and felt that if
the Nassief Property were allowed to annex, the adjoining areas would also
annex. She indicated that this would harm the schools and overtax the Village’s
sanitary sewer system. She indicated that she felt that the young people were
leaving, and she owed it to the community not to annex. She indicated that the
Township could oppose the annexation on the grounds that this would create an
island of territory that the Township could not provide services to, as well as
the size of the parcel involved.
Councilmember Ward indicated that he had questions about the applicability of
CEDD’s.
Trustee Demshar indicated that she had asked Mr. Joe Mayernic of the Ashtabula
County Growth Partnership, to contact the Village and Schools regarding CEDD’s;
and the possibility of the Township participating in the Mulberry Street
Special Improvement District.
Solicitor Lemire reminded the Council that the Commissioners make the approval
for annexation; the Village must pass a resolution of services available. If
the Commissioners approve the annexation, the matter comes before Council for
final acceptance.
Councilmember Ward indicated that he felt there would be no difference in the
effect on the schools, and he was opposed to JEDD’s, the Village should not
giveaway services.
Councilmember Maloney read a portion of the Commissioner’s transcript for the
Bethel Bible annexation, indicating the Township voiced no opposition to the
annexation.
Trustee Demshar stated that she was all for Christian education, and didn’t
oppose what Bethel Bible Baptist was doing.
Village Resident Gary Helfer stated that he felt that the Village should take
care of what they have first.

Forestry
Councilwoman Maloney commented on the seminar of North Coast Urban Forestry
Conference.
Councilwoman Maloney stated that our Tree Ordinance does not meet the State
recommendations for planting. We need to revise our Tree Ordinance in order to
qualify for grants. They want us to be more diversified.
Administrator Pauley noted that they want us to be more appropriate on the
species according to the location. There was a shift on the emphasis for the
Grants program, no longer funding the planting programs they are looking for a
well rounded program for tree maintenance and preservation.
Mayor Bragga questioned whether it was worth changing to meet their
specifications rather than do what we want to do for our community.
Maloney felt that they had valid points to their statements. The original plan
was set up back in the 60’s and things have changed over time. CEI doesn’t work
with us as they used to. The Village wants trees that will look nice and not
have CEI making them look bad. The Village cannot afford to lose 100 trees if
something comes through and kills all of that species. They are trying to help
us put up trees that will last. We don’t have to change but we want to look
into it.

Mayor Bragga presented Auxiliary Lt. Keith Ford with a Proclamation for his 30
years of service to the Village.
Chief Febel presented Auxiliary Lt Keith Ford with a gold plated retirement
badge for his 30 years of service.
Visitors comments:
Jeff Hope of 334 West Cedar St. talked to Council concerning building his house
in Elliott Allotment. Hope told Council that Larry Divine and himself are the
only two lots left to develop in the Allotment. The new zoning laws that were
passed requires them to put sidewalks on the property. Stated that the new laws
are good for new developments, but there will only be two lots in the Elliott
Development with sidewalks. Asked if this was fair, and if the Village would
plow them. Stated he felt this would also down grade the neighborhood.
Mayor Bragga explained that there was no provision in the zoning for waiving
the zoning requirements for these certain residents. Explained only Council can
change the Ordinance.
Judy Divine also expressed her concern to Council about the sidewalks in the
Elliott Allotment asking Council for a variance concerning the issue.
Jeff Hope also expressed concern to Council about the fire hydrant being only
six feet away from his driveway. Explained that if a sidewalk were put in; the
hydrant would be in the way. Got figures to move the hydrant and it would cost
$2,000. Stated all other hydrants are on the property line and over 100 yards
apart.
Councilman Finger expressed to residents that the issue would be considered and
an answer would be given. Also explained that any change made in the zoning
would not be done soon. The legal process has to be followed to amend the
Ordinance.
Councilman Thompson told everyone that when the Zoning Ordinance was changed
the thought was for new developments not the existing developments.
Councilman Finger referred to the solicitor and his memo on sidewalk
requirements.
Solicitor Lemire explained the request to review the legal requirements
regarding sidewalk construction in the Village. He reviewed the Subdivision
Regulations contained in Chapter 1224 of the Codified Ordinances of the Village
of Jefferson. He reviewed Section 1242.04(i) of the Village Zoning Code. He
also reviewed Chapter 1024 of the Village Code that deals with sidewalks.
The Subdivision Regulations govern new subdivisions built in the Village after
February 19, 1999, the effective date of the new Subdivision Regulations.
Section 1224.09(f) requires that the subdivider construct sidewalks on one or
both sides of the street, as required by the Planning Commission. It further
requires the sidewalks to be constructed one foot inside the right of way, be 4
feet in width, and not less than 4" thick (6" where crossing driveway). The
sidewalks shall be constructed when 80% of the lots on a street are built upon.
Chapter 1024, Sidewalks, provides a mechanism to reimburse owners who make
their own sidewalk repairs in accordance with the detailed specification set
forth therein.
Section 1242.04(i) of the Village Zoning Code, effective May 17, 2000, requires
that all new construction in RS, RD and B1 districts include installation of
new sidewalks along the front yard line, one foot inside the right of way, in
accordance with detailed specifications set forth in the statute.
Section 1242.04(i) seems in conflict with Section 1224.09(f), in that the
Subdivision sidewalk requirement only becomes effective upon 80% completion of
the Subdivision. Also, the Planning Commission retains the right to require
sidewalks on only one side of the street in the subdivision setting.
However, since Section 1242.04(i) is a general zoning requirement governing all
new construction in RS, RD and B1 Districts, and was passed after Section
1224.09(f) of the Subdivision Regulations, in my opinion, Section 1242.04(i)
overrides Section 1224.09(f) and all new construction, even in subdivisions,
must comply with the sidewalk requirements contained therein. There is no
provision in the Jefferson Zoning Code that permits a variance from this
requirement. The only relief available to a person who desires to avoid this
sidewalk requirement is amending this provision of the Zoning Code.
Councilman Thompson told Council he would like the issue referred to the
Building Lands committee. A committee meeting was set for Wednesday, April 4,
2001 at 7:15 pm. to discuss the issue.
