Visitors comments:
Officer Steven Terry of the Jefferson Police Department gave a demonstration to
the Jefferson Village Council with Apollo, his K-9 partner. Apollo demonstrated
the search for marijuana, hidden in boxes. Officer Terry talked to Council
about the areas of training in which he and Apollo have been working. This
includes certified tracking, passive aggression, aggressive search, patrol work
and handler protection. Officer Terry explained to Council that the two have to
work together as one to be a strong team. Apollo has proven to be a strong team
player and partner.
Ray Sapporito of the Ashtabula County Health Commission talked with Council on
SB 105 Septic Bill. The Ohio Department of Health has established a review
schedule for Chapter 3701-29 of the Ohio Administrative Code (Household Sewage
Treatment Rules) as required by Section 119.032 of the Ohio Revised Code,
commonly referred to as the Five Year Rule Review. There are about 15,000
septic tanks in the county, most are inspected annually. The new bill that had
gone to the Senate and passed, was defeated in the House. The new rules, if
passed, would have a major impact on residents. Under the new rules the
homeowner could not install a septic system. An NPDES permit would be required
for all new homes also. This would increase the cost for installation of septic
systems.
Councilman Finger questioned the opposition to controlling human sewage waste.
Ray Sapporito told Council that the county does random inspections. Stated that
there are about 4,000 residential septic tanks in the county, of those about
100 a year are replaced by residents, on there own. The county is promoting
public health and looking into any improper discharges. Sapporito also told
Council that the Ohio EPA rated the Grand River in excellent health. Reports of
endangered species are surviving in the river.
Rick Hoyson a representative of the Jefferson Falcon Pride Committee talked to
Council on promoting the Jefferson School levy (Issue 17) that will be on the
ballot May 8, 2001. Hoyson spoke to Council stating that the Jefferson Schools
need this levy to run and operate the schools. The teachers pay in Jefferson
are at the bottom 10% of the state. To keep the quality of teachers and
education in Jefferson the levy needs to be passed. Hoyson told Council that
the levy is a 6-mil levy for operations at the school. Also said that in
November of this year a 3 mil levy previously passed will expire. So the levy
will not be as large as it seems. Rick explained to Council that the campaign
funding to promote the school levy comes from community donations.

Safety
Councilman Finger discussed the memo from Solicitor Lemire regarding legal
requirements for borrowing money to pay the cost of the refurbishment of the
1982 Pierce Pumper.
Ohio Law provides that a Municipality may borrow money through the issuance of
voted or unvoted bonds. The procedure for issuing unvoted and voted bonds is
the same, excepted that voted bonds can be issued only after approval by the
voters, and the principal and interest payable on unvoted bonds must be paid
from taxes levied within the ten-mill limitation, while the tax for debt
service refurbishing the 1982 Pierce Pumper Fire Truck, operated by the
Jefferson Volunteer Fire Department on voted bonds is without limitation. In
order to issue unvoted bonds, there must be available leeway within the ten-mil
constitutional tax limitation. When the Village issued bonds for the
acquisition and construction of the Community Center, leeway under the ten-mil
limitation for the issuance of unvoted bonds existed.
To issue municipal bonds, either voted or unvoted, the services of bond counsel
are usually required. The role of bond counsel is to examine applicable law,
prepare authorizing and operative documents, consult with the parties, review
certified proceedings and render an objective legal opinion with respect to the
authorization and issuance of the bonds. In today's market, banks will normally
not purchase municipal bonds without a Legal Opinion from recognized Bond
Counsel that the Bonds are correctly authorized and issued.
In the past, the Village of Jefferson has utilized the services of Attorney
Richard Simpson of the Law Firm of Bricker & Eckler for Bond Counsel Services.
Other firms have solicited the Village's Bond Counsel Business and could
perform the service.

2nd by Maloney

John Kusar spoke to Council with his concerns with the Ordinance to waive the

not available.
Mayor Bragga told Council that Council does have the authority to waive the
residency requirement. Also said the Administrator has a pager and cell phone
to get in contact with him in the case of an emergency. Bragga also explained
to Council that in the past other Administrators have superceded the length of
time to move into the Village.
Solicitor Lemire told Council before them was the wrong ordinance and the
ordinance to be read tonight is supposed to be an updated version, stating the
residency requirement would be for a period of two years not the duration of
the Administrators contract.
Councilman Ward told Council it is not an issue with the Administrator. It is
an issue with residency within the Village. I still believe the residency
requirement needs to stick.
Ken Fertig told Council in the past the residency requirement was extended for
the Administrator to sell his house. Stated the Administrator should live
within the Village and if he lives in the Village he will have some impact to
what taxes are in the Village and what effect it will have on the residents.
Jane Stone told Council when he applied for the job he told Council he would
move here and he should uphold what he said.
Richard Hummel told Council that he is doing a good job. But he still should
have residency in the village and be the same as the Mayor with a residency
requirement.
Mayor Bragga read the correct Ordinance.
ORDINANCE WAIVING RESIDENCY REQUIREMENT
FOR THE VILLAGE ADMINISTRATOR FOR A TWO YEAR PERIOD
WHEREAS, Ohio Law provides that a Village Administrator must become a resident
of the Village he administers within six months after taking the position
unless the residence requirement is waived by ordinance, and
WHEREAS, The Council of the Village of Jefferson believes that it is in the
best interest of the Village to waive the residency requirement for Village
Administrator Robert A. Pauley for a period of two years;
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE COUNCIL OF THE VILLAGE OF JEFFERSON,
COUNTY OF ASHTABULA, AND STATE OF OHIO, THAT:
   SECTION 1:This Council hereby approves the residence of Robert A. Pauley
outside the Village of Jefferson while he holds the position of Village
Administrator for a period of two years.
   SECTION 2: Officials of the Village of Jefferson are hereby authorized to
amend the Employment Agreement with Robert A. Pauley, to amend the residency
requirement to provide that residency in the Village shall be established
within two years of the commencement of employment.
   SECTION 3: That this Ordinance shall take effect and be in full force after
the earliest period allowed by law.
Roll: Finger yea, Herndon nea, Maloney yea, Stasny nea, Thompson nea, Ward nea.
Four neas to two yeas, motion failed.
Motion by Maloney for the third reading of Ordinance No. 01-O-2361
2nd by Finger
Roll: All yea, motion carried.

Council discussed the memo from the Administrator regarding the Sanitary Sewer
Capacity.
   As discussed at the last Council meeting, the following are pertinent facts
relating to the Village’s wastewater treatment plant and collection system, as
it currently exists. This assumes that there are no improvements to the plant
or collection system such as reduction of I&I flows (inflow and infiltration)
or elimination of connected downspouts, footer drains or sump pumps.
·   Nominal plant capacity 1.0 MGD
·   Monthly flows range from .456 MGD to .642 MGD; average daily flow is .501
MGD
·   Customers on system currently 1382 (including out of Village and sludge
received from Roaming Shores and Rock Creek treatment facilities)
·   Average customer is 266 Gal per day (.000266 MGD)
·   New single family zoning permits issued range from 3 per year to 7 per year
(last 8 years reviewed)
·   Oakwood allotment vacant lots -   56
·   Lemire Estates allotment (Brittany Lane) vacant lots -   16
·   Scattered throughout Village – 16
(areas that are presently sewered, with probable sell-off / development by
landowner
Includes the following streets:
   Beech   Pine   Ashtabula   Walnut   Maplewood
   Erie   Satin   Westview   Cedar   Franley
   Chestnut   Elm   Poplar   Market   Sycamore
   Linda   Elliott   Woodside   Hillyer   Beverly
   Kathleen   Susan   Center   Willis   Uselma
If full build-out of the following areas, at the current per-customer average
daily loading, were to occur instantly, the wastewater plant loading would be:
   Wastewater plant average         501,000 gpd (.501 MGD)
   Oakwood   56 x 266 gpd = 14, 896 gpd       14,896
   Lemire Estates    16 x 266 gpd = 4,256 gpd       4,256
   Village scattered 16 x 266 gpd = 4,256 gpd       4,256
              Total                  524,408 gpd (.524 MGD)
If all of the proposed Nassief development were to occur instantly, the loading
would be:
   124 x 266 = 32, 984 gpd          32,984
   Total                  577,392 gpd (.557 MGD)   
Councilman Finger explained the contracts with Rock Creek and Roaming Shores
could be cut off if the sewer capacity was getting too high.
Council discussed the letter from Ed Curie regarding the proposed Nassief
Development stated that if accepted the subdivision would be an ongoing
development in three phases.
Council asked to have the letter inserted into the minutes. (follows
immediately)
Dear Council,
   The Nassief proposed residential subdivision is going to be developed in
three phases:
Phase I: The south side (44 lots) will take 5-10 years to sell out.
Phase II: The north side (44 lots) will take 10-20 years to sell out.
Phase III: The west end (30 plus lots) with take 20-30 years to sell out.
   As you can see this subdivision will take up to 30 years or more to sell. As
you all know the front part of Elliott subdivision took 39 years to sell and
Westview subdivision took 37 years to sell.
   I strongly believe that the Nassief proposed subdivision is necessary for
healthy growth over the next 3 0-40 years in our village as well as new tax
revenue. The village must continue to grow to keep the schools and local
businesses and industry from stagnating.
   This project will not strain our sewage package plant as the engineer has
pointed out to everyone concerned.
   I could not make this meeting in person as I’m the head of the Council at
St. Joseph Church and we have a very important meeting at 7:00 tonight also.
   Please vote for our future and growth, as I want my 3 grandchildren to have
a reason to come back to Jefferson to live & not relocate in some other city.
Sincerely,
   
Edward R. Curie
Real Estate Developer & Broker

Regular Session 8:26 p.m.
Finance 
Solicitor Lemire explained to Council that the Income Tax Ordinance would need
changes to reflect statutes in the Ohio Revised Code. Told Council the Finance
Committee directed him to change the penalty for not filing a city income tax
return from a flat fifty dollars to 2-½ % of what is owed up to a maximum of
fifty dollars. Explained also the change in the mandatory filing of every
Village resident to residents who have taxable income. Solicitor Lemire
explained that a new ordinance has to be passed in order for these changes to
go into effect.
Motion by Finger for the first reading of Ordinance No. 01-O-2369
2nd by Thompson
Discussion
Council discussed the new Ordinance, which would increase the pay for Council
from seventy-five dollars per meeting up to a maximum of thirty-two per year,
to a monthly salary of three hundred dollars with a pick up of six and one half
percent of the PERS.
Council agreed that to be a good Councilperson a lot of hours must be put in
along with meetings. The Village is growing and time must be put in to endorse
new and old legislation.
Councilman Thompson told Council the increase is long over due. According to
the OML Cities and Villages Salary Survey, this salary is average compared to
other cities our size.
Councilman Finger told Council that the salaries would increase from 2,400
dollars to 3,600 dollars a year. Council agreed the increase would only effect
the Officials with terms starting January 2002.
Roll: All yea, motion carried.

of Jefferson, to Provide for a Monthly Salary for the Position of Council
Persons of the Village of Jefferson, Ohio.

Ordinance No. 01-O-2370
An Ordinance Accepting the Annexation of Land Owned by The Bethel Bible Church
into the Village of Jefferson.
Council discussed the petitions for annexation from Herbert C. Housel and
Yvonne M. Housel for 2.291 acres and from Kathleen M. Housel for 2.853 acres.
Questioned the owners intent of the property if the annexation were to pass.
Solicitor Lemire explained to Council, the Village is required by the Ohio
Revised Code to pass an ordinance stating what services would be available if
the annexation is approved. Told Council passing the Ordinance for the
availability of services does not approve annexation. The hearing on the
petition for annexation will be held on July 24, 2001 at 2:00 pm. and one at 2:
30 pm. in the Commissioners Conference Room.
Council asked the Solicitor to invite the Housels to the next Council meeting
held on June 4, 2001.
Motion by Thompson to have the Solicitor draft a Resolution of available
services for the two annexation submitted to Council on May 21, 2001 by Herbert
C. Housel, Yvonne M. Housel and Kathleen M. Housel.
2nd by Maloney
Roll: All yea, motion carried.
Council discussed the zoning for the annexations. All agreed the properties at
this time are zoned residential in the township. If annexed it would be zoned
the same.
Council discussed the sidewalk issue for new construction in previously
approved developments and isolated lot completing buildout in developments.
Members of the Planning Commission and the Building and Lands Committee all
agreed to relieve the requirement for sidewalks for new construction in the RS
and RD district, except where adjacent abutting properties, on either side of
the new construction, currently have sidewalks. The requirement for sidewalks
for new construction still stand in the B1 district. The requirement for
sidewalks as part of the subdivision requirements still stands.
Councilman Finger expressed his concern with the change and stated the Village
should develop a plat that reflects where sidewalks are currently in the
Village.
Motion by Maloney to have the Solicitor draft legislation to resolve the
conflict regarding sidewalks on new construction in previously approved
developments and isolated lots completing buildout in developments, platted but
unopened streets in the Village.
2nd by Thompson
Roll: All yea, motion carried.
Bruce Chapman of Western Reserve Farm Coop, discussed the revised fuel bid.
Explained that fuel prices change daily and rates will fluctuate from where
ever the fuel is bought. All fuel has a 22 cent State Tax but governments are
exempt from Federal excise tax.
Councilman Finger stated he felt the Fire Chief should feel comfortable with
the grade of fuel he puts into the Village fire trucks. He knows what grade of
fuel causes gumming and what fuel the fire truck will run the best on.
Councilwoman Herndon questioned the placement of signs for yard sales and if
there had been any discussion to have a central location for all yard sale
signs and recurring yard sales.
Councilwoman Herndon asked the solicitor to look into the legalities of
recurring yard sales and the length of time they can be run.
Mayor Bragga told Council there is an existing ordinance that deals with yard
sale signs.
Solicitor Lemire told Council he would look into the village ordinance on
recurring yard sales.

22-24th, for the Jefferson Days Celebration. The street would be closed Friday
from 7:00 pm to 12:00 midnight, Saturday from 12:00 noon to 12:00 midnight and

beer permit for the up coming Jefferson Days.
2nd by Maloney.
Roll: All yea, motion carried.
Herb Housel and Kathy Housel talked with Council regarding proposed annexation
of properties located in Jefferson Township. Explained the reasons for
annexation is to receive all of the current Village services. These are only
available if they annex into the Village. Herb explained that his property is
zoned commercial and he doesn’t currently have any plans for the property.
Kathy’s property is now zoned residential and if annexed, would like to have it
rezoned B-1, but also does not currently have any plans for the property.
John Kusar addressed Council concerning his letters addressed to the
Administrator and letters received from the Administrator. He told Council that
he filed an application for a zoning permit and was refused. Kusar stated that
Administrator Pauley told him, that he would have to request guidance from the
Solicitor on the proper interpretation and application of the code.
Administrator Pauley also questioned if the parcel was one lot or split into
two lots. The letters also addressed issues concerning the construction of a
pond on John Kusar’s property.
John Kusar questioned why he had to bring a copy of his deed and survey to get
a fence permit. Kusar stated that he asked the Administrator if he had
requested this of other residents requesting a permit. Kusar then questioned
the issue of his pond. Told Council that seven months prior he had come to the
Administrator with questions on the code concerning the digging of a pond on
his property. Kusar said he was advised that there was nothing in the code to
prohibit the digging of the pond. Kusar told Council that upon questioning the
Administrators residency he then received the letters from the Administrator
concerning the fence permit and pond.
After a lengthy discussion between the Administrator, Council, Mayor and John
Kusar it was agreed that as originally suggested by the Administrator, a
meeting would be set up between the Administrator and John Kusar with the
Solicitor to clarify the issues.
 
John Kusar told Council that there has been a lot of controversy over his
property from the beginning, even when it belonged to the Eagles.
Mayor Bragga told John Kusar that the Administrator has been consistent with
all the zoning applications he has given out. If the Administrator is asking to
see the deed and he felt it would solve the confusion, he would stand by the
Administrators decision.

Persons of the Village of Jefferson, Ohio
Councilman Finger questioned the spreadsheet with the YTD summary fund report
and asked why some departments had a negative balance.
Clerk Treasurer Fisher explained to Council that the B4 Village Recreation
Dept. was in the negative because the dept. was lacking in revenues compared to
its expenditures. Explained the B10 Permissive Auto fund was in the negative
because the local government revenues are lacking. This fund is used to buy
salt and cinders, we were buying Rock Salt in March because of the long winter.
The fund will balance out as the Village receives more revenue throughout the
year. The E10 Refuse Fund is in the negative because of the bi-monthly billing
cycle. In May the fund will balance out with the revenue for that month.

informational session regarding the new medical insurance. Enrollment forms
were given out to all employees. Information will be given to the Finance
committee and a recommendation will come forth to Council soon.

Public Hearing 8:00 pm.
Mayor Bragga told council that the public hearing is to listen to comments
concerning the following request for zoning district change to SL
46,47,48,49,50, and 51 Loomis Lot. The zoning change would be from (RS)
residential to (B1) business.
Solicitor Lemire swore in any interested parties that wanted to testify during
the hearing. Parties included: David Smith, Paulette Piper, Dave Dvorak and
Lewis Hayslett.
David Smith of 230 S. Chestnut St., Jefferson, told council that himself and
his wife Mary Lou Smith were opposed to the zoning change for the said lot.
Council was presented with a letter from David Smith, Mary Lou Smith, Robert
Cornell and Donna Cornell. Stating what they would be in favor of compromising
for the zoning change.
RE:   Application for Zoning District Change
   (S/L 46, 47, 48, 49, 50, 51 Loomis Allotment)
Dear Mayor Laurence Bragga, Council Members. Robert Pauley:
   Per your memo dated April 12, 2001, Dave Dvorak, property owner of S/L 46,
47, 48, 49, 50, 51 Loomis Allotment, is requesting a zoning change for the
noted parcels from a RS - Residential to B-I Commercial. Mr. Dvorak has
indicated that the proposed use includes the sale of the lots to Lewis Hayslett
for the expansion of the adjoining Jefferson Mini-Storage. I and my wife, Mary
Lou Smith, currently own the property which abuts and is West of the noted
lots, further known as 230 S. Chestnut St., Jefferson. Our property is zoned B-
1 hut currently the use of the property is residential. The drainage of the
properties located at 230 and 234 S. Chestnut St. drain to the creek which is
to the East across the noted lots presently owned by Dave Dvorak.
   We, David L. Smith and Mary Lou Smith, are OPPOSED to the zoning change for
the said lots. We would be in favor of the following:
   a.   We would be in favor of a “use” variance. The zoning of the property
would remain RS -Residential;
   b.   The “use” variance would permit the construction of one storage
building of similar construction to the existing storage building owned by
Lewis Hayslett;
   c.   The proposed storage building would be built on S/L 46, 47, and on a
portion of 48;
   d.   The proposed storage building would he in line with and containing the
same setbacks as the existing storage buildings located on Cedar St. The
proposed storage building will not extend behind the properties located at 230
and 234 S. Chestnut St.;
   e.   The proposed storage building would not be constructed farther North
than the existing storage buildings located on Cedar St.;
   f.   Fencing to match the existing fencing will be erected around the
proposed storage building.
   g.   The remaining S/L 51,50. 49, and the portion of 48 will remain in its
“as is” vacant condition. The removal of the trees will be prohibited from
these lots and will serve as a landscape buffer. S/L 51, 50, 49 and the portion
of 48 will not be used for the storage of any vehicles or materials in the
open. A gravel parking area will be prohibited on S/L 51, 50, 49, and the
portion of 48;
   h.   Lighting for the building site will be shielded to protect the
properties located at 230 and 234 S. Chestnut St.;
   i.   A shared twenty foot (20’) permanent and dedicated storm drainage
easement will be granted for the drainage of the lots located at 230 S.
Chestnut St. and 234 S. Chestnut St. to the creek in the vicinity, The shared
drainage easement will begin at the Southeast corner of the property located at
230 S. Chestnut St. and the Northeast corner of the property located at 234 S.
Chestnut St and extend to the creek. The construction of any storage building
in the stormed drainage easement will be prohibited. The proposed storm
easement may be utilized for any commercial or residential development of the
properties located at 230 and 234 S Chestnut SL;
   j.   If ever the use of BOTH lots located at 230 S. Chestnut St. and 234 S.
Chestnut St. are changed from the present residential use to a commercial use,
then an additional storage building may be built on S/L 51, 50, 49 and the
portion of 48. Any additional storage buildings will not be located in the
storm easement;
   k.   Zoning ordinances regulating the construction and use of storage
buildings are binding to the proposed lots;
   l.   S/L 46, 47, 48, 49, 50, and 51 must be sold as a unit and be binding to
the agreements herein; and,
   m.   The conditions noted herein will be binding in the event that the
properties would be sold and the “use” variance is granted for the construction
of a storage building. Such agreement shall be recorded on the property deed
and enforced by Jefferson Village and the Zoning Inspector.
Paulette Piper of 38 E. Erie St, Jefferson, told council that she was opposed
to the zoning change. Told council that they had worked had to improve their
property and felt the mini storage building would not improve their property.
Dave Dvorak of Mill Creek Road, Jefferson, told council that he was the
previous owner of the lots now owned by the Smiths. Told council that he had
offered lots 50 and 51 to both the Cornells and the Smiths but they showed no
interest. Dave told council he agreed to sell the property to Lew Hayslett if
the zoning request was approved by council.
Lewis Hayslett of 117 Maplewood Dr., Jefferson, told council he owns the
adjoining mini storage building next to the Dvorak property. Told council if
the zoning request change was approved he was going to expand one more building
and possibly two. Hayslett told council that both the Cornells and the Smiths
were offered the property, they chose not to buy the lots. Hayslett told
council he assured the Smiths he would control the water. Hayslett also told
council that the Cornells have their house listed with the realtor. With the
zoning change to B1 business this would bring in more tax revenue to the
Village.
Councilman Thompson questioned the impact of adding of more storage units would
have on the creek near the lot.
Lewis Hayslett told council that their would be not interruption to the creek.
David Smith asked council if they had any questions with the letter and if it
was clear enough.
Councilman Finger questioned the Solicitor if the council had the power to do
any of the changes that were referred to in the letter.
Solicitor Lemire told council no they could only approve to rezone and it had
to be done by ordinance.
Administrator Pauley showed council the lots on the zoning map.
Public Hearing closed at 8:23 pm.

The general consensus from the planning commission was that CT Consultants

developing zoning and land use issues in the Rush Creek area.
Mayor Bragga told Council the vision for Rush Creek area include a light
industrial, residential and potential redevelopment of the area. With the
redevelopement of the area, it would increase tax value to the property, which
in the long run would bring tax dollars to the Village.
Council agreed the planning commission has made much progress and felt the
Village should move forward with the plans.

Visitors Comments:
Gene Crislip, a property owner and landlord, questioned Council regarding his
delinquent sewer bill from a renter. Crislip presented Council with minutes
regarding questions on his delinquent sewer account dated March 12, 1998. In
the minutes he talked with Council about his delinquent sewer bills from his
property at 215 East Jefferson Street. After the Council meeting in 1998 when
he talked with Council he was under the impression that landlords would be
notified if sewers were in arrears. Crislip told Council that he did give a
list of his renters to Michelle Ashley. He called and questioned how the
account was doing. Ashley told Crislip that the account was being taken care
of. After the renter was evicted he found out only $45.00 had been paid on her
account. Crislip asked Council if the Village was going to accept the
responsibility for the negligence of Michelle Ashley.

Visitors Comments
Ed Curie spoke on Nassief Property development and proposed annexation. He gave
an estimated time for subdivision to build out the project. Would be broken
into phases. Phase I is on the south side and has 56 lots, expect 7 years to
sell 75%, Phase II has 56 lots, expecting 17 years for 75%, and Phase III 20 –
25 years to sell out completely. No professional engineering was done because
there is a significant cost involved. They want to be sure the project flies
before spending the money.
Talking with Dick Burns or Ed Burke on easement access to the sewer line. If
they cannot get easements from the neighbors they will have to come up State
Route 46 and get right of way easements from the State.
The State will require that the road entrance will have to be wide enough to
accommodate two fire trucks at one time.
Need annexation because of utilities. Then they may come to Council wishing to
change the zoning to Industrial. Ed stated that the village only has 43 lots
left. Will need to approve annexation to grow over the next 10 years. But it is
Nassief’s decision on zoning.
Councilman Finger questioned what is the current Township zoning. This will
come in at current Township Commercial property. Planning Commission will make
recommendation to keep or change current zoning based on proposed use.
Discussion as to what zoning was believed to be best for the Village.
Gene Crislip came in to ask for action on his request from July 2, 2001
meeting. He had addressed Council concerning 456 Mulberry St. Crislip said he
was told at a prior Council Meeting that if he gave Michelle a list of renters
that he would be notified of delinquent accounts. He had called Michelle and
questioned the balance of the account and was told it was being taken care of.
Crislip feels Council is responsible for the village employees. He stated that
if Council does not act upon this, and it is put on his taxes, he will have to
take legal action.
Mayor Bragga asked the Waste Water committee to look into the issue before the
August 1, 2001 assessment to taxes.
Councilperson Herndon asked for the Solicitors advice.
Solicitor Lemire told Council that there is nothing in the code stating that
the Village has to notify the property owner of delinquent accounts. It states
that the property owner is responsible. If we give this special attention, we
are setting a precedent.
Mayor Bragga stated that he is looking for closure on this issue.
Council discussed how to handle Gene Crislip and the situation. Agreeing on no
relief for the property owner’s responsibility for the sewer usage.
Mayor Bragga will a send letter to Mr. Crislip.

Forestry
Council discusses the century oak tree on 341 South Elm Street. The tree split,
dropping a significant limb. After examination and due to the extent of the
rot, it was decided that the tree would need to be removed.
Administrator Pauley discussed the cutting of trees within Village right of
way. The Village Arborist received a complaint that a tree at 71 West Erie
Street was being cut down, and the tree was within the Village right of way.
The resident of 71 West Erie Street cut limbs from the tree and stated he was
going to contract someone to do it. Administrator Pauley informed the resident
that the tree was in the Village’s right of way and permission needs to be
obtained from the Forestry Committee before it could be removed. The Village’s
Street Tree Ordinance requires permission from the Village prior to removing
any tree from within the right of way. Section 1026.99 does state that whoever
violates the provision of this chapter is guilty of a misdemeanor of the fourth
degree. Council discussed the issue and agreed that the Solicitor and
Administrator should look over the legal issues and review the legislation.
Council agreed that the dry weather has hurt several species of trees.
Residents are encouraged to water and fertilize the trees.

Waste Water
Council discussed the memo regarding the sludge – land application with Keith
Palmer of 2670 St. Rt. 6, Cherry Valley, Ohio. In the proposed agreement it
would permit the Village to dispose of pressed sludge from the Waste Water
Treatment plant to 6 application sites approved by the OEPA. Along with the
removal of sludge, the Village will coordinate the purchase of the appropriate
sludge applicator (manure spreader). The term and fees for the contract will be
payable August 15, 2001 in the amount of 2,500 dollars. For 2002 thru 2004, two
installments each year totaling 7,500 dollars, and for 2005 thru 2006, two
installments per year totaling 8,500 dollars. Council agreed that cost of
alternative sludge disposal could run about 32,000 dollars a year for the
Village.
Administrator Pauley told Council monies for the manure spreader and $2,500 for
sludge removal are in the budget.
Motion by Herndon to have the Solicitor draft legislation on the land/sludge
application.
2nd by Maloney
Roll: All yea, motion carried.
Councilman Thompson asked the Administrator in the future if he would prepare
specs and advertise for sludge receivers.
Councilwoman Herndon reminded everyone of the Waste Water Plant Open House for
September 8, 2001 @ 9:00 am.

Councilman Thompson questioned the Water Advisory Group minutes. Asked why
minutes were not submitted by the Administrator or someone from Council.
Solicitor Lemire told Council that the Water Advisory Group is not a standing
committee of the Village. The committee is just an advisory group working
together. Minutes are taken to inform Council what was discussed during the
meeting. No action can be done during this meeting and they are not a permanent
record of the Village until the discussion is brought to a committee of the
Village.
Clerk-Treasurer Fisher told Council what is recorded in the permanent records
states minutes of the water advisory group were received.
Councilman Finger questioned if the Village’s sidewalk replacement was being
done as whole sections or patching.
Administrator Pauley told Council that the budget for sidewalks was limited and
property owners have stated that they do not want the sidewalk replaced in some
cases.
Mayor Bragga told Council that property owners can refuse to have the sidewalks
replaced in front of their house. The Village does not have an ordinance
requiring the resident to replace them. If a resident chooses to have the
sidewalk replaced, a payment plan can be set up.

Old Business/New Business
Councilman Thompson questioned the Clerk Treasurer as to why the Villages new
insurance plan had not been implemented August 1, 2001 as stated in a memo
dated June 15, 2001 from the Clerk Treasurer. The memo stated that the new
insurance coverage provided by Joslin Landis Ins. Co. which is through Medical
Mutual of Ohio (Super Med Plus), would be effective August 1, 2001 at the
latest. Councilman Thompson expressed concern that on June 18, 2001 Council had
passed an ordinance stating the new medical insurance was to go into effect
August 1, 2001. Thompson said as of today the Village is still with the old
plan. Thompson wanted to know what authority was given to the Clerk to stay
with the same medical coverage.
Clerk Treasurer Fisher told Council that on June 18, 2001coucnil passed a
motion to accept the medical insurance coverage by Medical Mutual of Ohio. Then
on August 3, 2001 a memo addressed to Council by Clerk Treasurer Fisher,
regarding the Medical Insurance asked Council to rescind the motion to change
the medical coverage. The reason being, the prior medical prescreens had
numerous changes in medical conditions and age that effected the medical rates.
The rates came back much higher. Clerk Treasurer Fisher told Council that with
the increase in cost it would be unfair to put the additional cost onto the
employee when we had told them they would be saving money.
Councilman Finger stated that at the Council Meeting August 6th Council went
into executive session over the medical insurance coverage and the public was
told that no action would be taken after the session.
Mayor Bragga expressed concern, stating he did not want the employees to suffer
the cost.
Clerk Treasurer Fisher told Council that she was not the contracting agent for
the Village and did not feel the responsibility was hers. In the past she had
presented figures for the Administrator and Mayor.
Mayor Bragga suggested that to prevent confusion in the future, a procedure
should be set up and the Village should talk to other municipalities as to how
they handle insurance bidding.
Motion by Finger to have the Village occur the difference in the medical
insurance costs through Medical Mutual of Ohio, not put the difference onto the
employees until rebids of the medical plan to be effective January 1, 2001.
2nd by Maloney
Roll: All yea, motion carried.
Council discussed and agreed that maybe the lowest bidder is not the best.
Along with bidding next time, the Village should include an agent spending time
each week at the Town Hall answering questions.

Visitor Comments
Citizen Cayce Baxley spoke to Council on her disenchantment on how Council was
handling Village situations. Baxley referred to the letter in the paper from
John Kusar regarding the Administrator’s residency. Discussed the long ordeal
with the sewer fund and increasing sewer rates. “The sewer rates increased and
then the Village hired another person for the Waste Water Plant. We have an
Administrator who is supposed to reside in the Village. Earlier this year we
went through a long ordeal of him moving into the Village, along with following
his contract. What transpired from that meeting? The residents thought the
residency issue had been resolved. The Village has Council rules, resolutions,
and ordinances that must be followed. Here we are not following them. Look what
the Village has gone through with the Recreation Center”.
Citizen John Kusar asked Council if the memorandum that Council received from
the Administrator on his residency was acceptable. Councilpeson Finger,
Herndon, and Maloney stated that they felt it was not acceptable. Kusar went on
to ask the President Pro Temp, as leader of the Village, sworn to uphold the
laws and ordinances of the Village how could this happen. The Administrator is
hired to enforce the ordinances of the Village. How can he show integrity to
the Village if he does not follow the ordinances and laws himself as
Administrator. Kusar expressed that the Village giving the Administraor 12
months was considerate, but felt he has made no attempt to move in. He then
told Council that he had called the telephone company and there was not a
listing for Robert Pauley in Jefferson.
Mayor Bragga told Council that a 576 number does not really have any meaning to
residency. But expressed to all that the Village requires the Administrator to
reside in the Village and to be on hand for the day to day operations of the
Village. The residency requirement is a part of his contract. Mayor Bragga
asked Council to please tell us what they were going to do.
Citizen Ken Fertig told Council that the residents of the Village thought the

   (L) Severance Pay
In the event Employee is terminated by the Village before the expiration of the
aforesaid initial or extended term of employment and during such time that
Employee is willing and able to perform his duties under this agreement, then
the Village agrees to pay Employee a lump sum payment equal to 3 months gross
salary, minus deductions, plus 1 month gross salary, minus deductions, for each
year of service with the Village: up to a maximum of 6 months of net salary. No
severance pay shall be paid to the Employee if the Village terminates this
Agreement during the first 6 months of employment probationary period, or if
this Agreement is terminated for cause. As used herein, cause means (1) any act
of omission by Employee which subjects the Village to civil or criminal
liability or tends to injure the Village’s business or repute, and (2) failure
to perform Employee’s duties specified above, except in the case of Employee’s
medically confirmed disability. In no event will the severance pay due
hereunder exceed 6 months of net salary.
Solicitor Lemire told Council under the agreement the Administrator can be
terminated without cause. With the Administrator being in Breach of his
contract there is no cause for the Village to pay out severance pay.

Visitors Comments:
Lou Kreider of the Water Advisory Committee spoke to Council concerning the
results of the Water Advisory Group meetings that have been held since May
2001.
Attached is the summary report and five year plan given to Council.
1.   Background
The Water Advisory Committee was authorized by the Village of Jefferson Council
in May 2001. The committee was formed to address recommendations in the
Insurance Services Office’s (ISO) letter of April 4, 2001 and to create a forum
whereby the Village and Consumers Ohio Water Company (COWC) could work
cooperatively to plan future water system improvements. The committee members
were as follows: Mayor Bragga, Administrator Pauley, Council Person Maloney,
Fire Chief Wayman and COWC representatives Fusco, Nutter, Brancaccio and
Kreider. The committee has met on five occasions beginning in May 2001.
2.    Committee Goals 
The committee established the following goals at its 5/24/01 meeting:
a.   Maintain ISO rating for the Village by addressing fire department and
water supply improvements.
b.   Identify low-cost improvements to benefit ISO rating – 2-way hydrants and
water mains.
c.   Identify and prioritize future water system improvements.
d.   Improve water flows and available supply within the Village.
e.   Insure water system prepared to address future growth and expansion
opportunities in the Village.
3.   Committee Meetings/Process
The committee reviewed the current status of the water system including fire
flows within the Village and the ISO report of April 2001. One of the first
recommendations of the committee was to request COWC replace certain 2-way
hydrants with hydrants containing pumper nozzles. The purpose of these
improvements was to provide more water supply to the fire department at these
specific locations. Chief Wayman identified the hydrants to be upgraded and
COWC replaced or repaired the hydrants as requested. The committee then
evaluated the potential benefits of various waterline improvements throughout
the Village. COWC prepared exhibits showing the benefits of various waterline
improvements to the ten ISO test locations. The COWC hydraulic model was
utilized to calculate the benefits of these improvements. The committee then
ranked in priority order the improvements which would provide the greatest
benefits to fire flows throughout the Village. (The committee’s recommendations
are attached as Exhibits for the years 2001 – 2006.) The committee, in
connection with fire department input, has recommended the use of reflective
tape to help fire fighters identify the flows available at different hydrant
locations. The committee also has requested for COWC to provide the fire
department with “route books” identifying the size of lines and hydrant
locations throughout the system.
The committee has also recommended COWC make modifications to its valve pit
serving the Roaming Shores system. This modification would allow for additional
fire flows to the Village of Jefferson in the event of a major fire. COWC has
contacted the Village of Roaming Shores to discuss this modification and
obtained the Village’s concurrence with this plan. COWC will order the
necessary materials and make this modification as soon as possible.
4.   Committee Recommendations
The following exhibits identify the proposed water supply improvements and
recent hydrant improvements for the years 2001 – 2006:
Exhibit A – Proposed Water System Improvements within Jefferson Village
Exhibit B – Fire Flow Improvements within the Jefferson Village
5.   Summary
   The committee intends to have follow-up meetings at approximately six-month
intervals. This process will allow the committee to review the progress of the
water supply improvement plan and to address any ISO reporting requirements.
These meetings will also be useful in addressing growth or Village expansion
opportunities.
Attachments:
Exhibit A – Proposed Water System Improvements within Jefferson Village
Exhibit B – Fire Flow Improvements within the Jefferson Village
cc:   WJP
   BTB
Council agreed that it would be beneficial to all if the group were to meet
every six months to review the progress of the water supply plan and improve
any ISO reporting requirements.
Councilperson Thompson questioned what effect the new water lines will have on
the old 4 – 6 inch lines and are those lines efficient for the areas in which
they are located.
Louis Kreider told Council that the 4- 6 inch lines are efficient in the areas
where they are currently located because they are in residential districts. The
ultimate plan is to eventually change all lines to 8 inch or above.
Councilperson Ward questioned if the Planning Commission should look at the
site for the new tank.
Council discussed the area where the water tank would be placed. Council was
informed that a 100’ x 100’ piece of property would need to be set aside. When
the section of property is picked out for the new water tank, all the
information will be given to the Planning Commission.
Mayor Bragga asked Lou Kreider if Consumers Ohio Water Company has increased
security since the terrorist attack on September 11, 2001.
Lou Kreider told Council that the security has been increased and the systems
are being monitored more.

Council discussed at length with the Mayor and Solicitor, the contract for the
Interim Director, Larry Carlson. Questioned if the person had a contract, could
he have control over the employees and could we tell him what hours to work
along with give him a job description.
Solicitor Lemire told Council the real issue is that he is a contractor and we
are asking him to perform the duties of an employee. Reason being, attached to
his contract is an employee job description. Independent contractors do not
have a job description, they have there own workers compensation and are
responsible for all tax withholdings, including Village income tax. Having the
interim director as a contractor with a job description attached to his
contract, the village is walking a fine line. It would be hard to prove him to
be a contractor.
Mayor Bragga told Council there was no intent to skirt any legal issues. He was
hired as a contractor to keep a piece of the Village functioning properly.
Councilperson Thompson stated we should look over our prior practice, done in
October 1999 when the last director resigned. We hired him as an employee under
the terms of an interim director.
Motion by Finger to hire an interim director.
2nd by Maloney

along with operating under the job description of director.

Safety
Fire Chief Wayman talked to Council on several solutions which would help the
ISO report.
1)   The Village would have to secure six more firefighters. On the roster
there are about 19 active firefighters.
2)   Each firefighter would have to have 36 hours of training. Line officers
would need an additional 12 hours of training. This is over and above regular
training.
3)   A 75 foot arial ladder truck would be needed to gain 5 points on the ISO
report. To purchase a used ladder truck it would cost the Village about 150-
175,000 dollars. After the truck is purchased the station would have to be
constructed so the ladder truck could fit into it.
Council discussed the options needed to increase the ISO report and help the
Village rates.
All agreed that dollars would need to be budgeted for training, possibly paying
the firefighters an hourly rate and a stipend, along with purchasing an arial
ladder truck.
Councilman Finger suggested Fire Chief Wayman give the Safety Committee some
recommendations for what is needed to run the department.
Fire Chief Wayman told Council that he would get with his staff and come back
to the committee with some recommendations for the department.
Mayor Bragga told Council that they have to look at future financial options
and possibly going to the voters to increase the Fire Levy.

Visitors Comments
Greg Odell of Consumers Ohio Water Co. presented Lloyd Gash with the
Neighborhood Hero Award. Gasho was honored for his 50 years as a Volunteer Fire
Fighter. He served as Fire Chief, a member of the Water Board, as well as years
of community service. Consumers Ohio Water Co. also donated $250.00 to a
charity of Lloyd Gasho’s choice. Gasho chose Dorset First Baptist.
Mayor Bragga thanked Lloyd Gasho for all the years of service to the community.
Mayor Bragga also noted that people like Lloyd are needed throughout the
country. It is all about strength of country, county, community and working
together.
Lloyd Gasho thanked all and humbly said he was unworthy of the award.
Trustee Martha Demshar discussed the Bicentennial Legacy Grant. Told Council
that the Village and Township would not meet all regulations and stipulations
regarding the grant so it would not be worthwhile to submit the application.
Expressed that the Township and Village could still work together to have a
nice Bicentennial for the community.

Visitors Comments
Jay Brook of 358 Hillyer Drive addressed Council with concerns of traffic
congestion in Elliott Allotment during the designated Halloween hours on
October 27, 2001. The neighborhood does not have sidewalks, which leave only
the road for the children to walk upon. Jay Brook asked Council to consider
closing the roads leading into the allotment to non resident traffic. The
Police Chief has been contacted and volunteers have stated they would help
direct traffic if Council approves the road closing. The superintendent has
been contacted and there are no events scheduled at the High School the night
of Halloween, so there is availability for parking at the High School.
Mayor Bragga told Council that the children walking on the streets in the
Elliott Allotment is a safety issue. Expressed that the residents of the
Allotment are well organized.
Jay Brook told Council that 83 concerned residents signed the petition. If this
plan works well this year, maybe the road closings can be extended to other
allotments in the Village that do not have sidewalks.
Motion by Finger to close the roads entering the Allotment at Jefferson
Eagleville Road and Poplar Street at Susan Drive during the hours of 3:30 pm to
6:30 pm on Halloween night, October 27th.
2nd by Maloney
Roll: All yea, motion carried.
Ken Fertig of 199 Franley Drive told Council that the residents in his
allotment have had the same concern for years.
Jan Scopel told Council that an employee with the Village of Rock Creek called
wanting to know the Village Trick or Treat hours. Stated they do not have an
ordinance regarding Halloween.
Cayce Baxley of the Jefferson Garden Club told Council October 27th at 10:00 am
is Make a Difference Day for the Garden Club. They are going to plant 1000 plus
Daffodil bulbs at the Cemetery and asked for help from the general public to
help with the planting.
John Kusar asked the Mayor how the search for the new administrator was coming
along.
Mayor Bragga stated the interview process was coming along and there would be a
recommendation to Council at the November 5th Council meeting.

Service
Councilperson Maloney reminded all that the leaf bags would be available
October 22nd at the Community Center and the Town Hall. The leaf bags are free
to Village residents. Pick up dates will be October 29th, and November 5th and
12th.
Administrator Pauley explained that Shell Energy and NOPEC have agreed to
modify the natural gas offer to residents who are signed up with NOPEC. Shell
Energy has offered to NOPEC customers the best of both worlds. The customers
can stay at the fixed price of $5.89 per mcf or they can opt for a variable
rate plan that will always remain five cents per mcf lower than the Dominion
price. One condition is if the NOPEC customer chooses to opt out of the
variable rate plan before August 2002, they will be charged a $20 exit fee.
Dominion East Ohio has sent out flyers to its customers with a lower fixed
rate.
Administrator Pauley explained that there was an application to participate in
the Ohio Public Works Commission Grant. The project will be a continuation of
the slip lining on Chestnut Street from Wall Street through the intersection on
Mulberry Street and State Route 307. Council will need to suspend Council rules
to have the application submitted on time.

2nd by Finger

Building/Lands
Councilperson Thompson asked the Solicitor for his opinion regarding the
potential vacating of Loomis Avenue.
Solicitor Lemire told Council that Tim Leehan investigated all the land
parcels. With the information obtained, if the Village chose to abandon the
street there would be no land locked parcels created. Under Ohio Revised Code
72304 to abandon the street, a petition must be filed by a resident owning a
lot in the Village.
Motion by Thompson to accept the Planning Commissions recommendation for the
zoning of the Bethel Bible Parcel.
2nd by Maloney.
Council discussed the Bethel Bible Parcel rezoning and was told by the
Solicitor that an ordinance should be drafted regarding the rezoning of the
land parcel. This Ordinance would cause a change in the zoning code. The
Ordinance would have to go to the Planning Commission for review and approval.
Upon approval it would then come back to Council. A public hearing would have
to be set before the first reading of the ordinance to rezone the land parcel.
Councilperson Thompson withdrew his motion.
Councilperson Maloney withdrew her second.

Planning Commissions recommendation for the zoning of the Bethel Bible Parcel.

Visitors Comments: 
Diana Sowry of 61 W. Satin St. addressed Council with concerns for temporary
shelters placed at the schools during the strike. Sowry told Council that she
looked through the Village’s codified ordinances and found nothing saying a
permit was needed for temporary shelters. Explained to Council that the Village
Chief of Police told her that they had to remove the porta-potty. Questioned
why they had to remove it, when the Health Department could have one for the
renovations. Asked for direction from Council because the Village statutes are
silent on this issue.
Mayor Bragga told Council that he has talked with the Police Chief concerning
the temporary shelters and the Porta-potty. Stated he directed the Police Chief
to request the Porta-potty be removed and if it was not it would be removed by
the Police Department.
Mayor Bragga did explain to all that the Village does have an ordinance in
place that deals with no signs permitted within the village right of way.
Tim Leehan of 139 North Spruce addressed Council with concerns to the
annexation of the 15.69 acres of land owned by Susan McIntyre. Explained to
Council that he had talked to McIntyre and the plan for the land is a fourteen-
lot subdivision. Told Council that to run sewer lines and water lines to this
property would not be cost prohibited. The alternative would be wells and
septic tanks. With the septic and wells, Leehan felt it would be detrimental to
the property value. The road also is a dirt road and adding fourteen houses
would increase traffic and cause problems. Residents concerned with annexation
should go to the Public Hearing December 18th at the Commissioners office and
voice their concern.
Jerald March of 376 East Beech St. told Council he also supports Tim Leehan
against the annexation of the McIntyre property. Said he felt it would hurt the
wells already in existence if fourteen more wells were put in the area. Also
told the Mayor he supported his decision on the removal of the Porta-potty.
Janice Smith of 280 North Spruce St. expressed her concern also about the
septic tanks and wells with the annexation of the McIntyre property.
Marilyn Leehan of 1200 East Beech St., a township resident, expressed her
concerns that the property is flat and there is no natural fall for drainage.
Putting fourteen wells and septic would hurt the other property owners in the
area for water because of wells. The ordinance for the annexation states what
services the Village will provide; which are fire protection, street lighting,
refuse removal, and sewer and street maintenance. Property owners now in the
area, which is part of the Village of Jefferson, do not have the availability
of all the sewers now. So how can the Village offer these services?
Bill Millard of 115 North Spruce St. told Council he was also concerned about
having fourteen septic tanks and wells on that property if annexed into the
Village.
Pat Nelson of 209 North Spruce St. told Council that the wells are already bad
with not enough water. The road is currently not being maintained. With
fourteen homes it would increase the traffic flow. The bridge is small and not
in the best of shape. Said in twenty-seven years living on that road there is
only one streetlight.
Jerry White of 1166 East Beech St. said he was worried about well and septic
also and felt later it would hurt the integrity of the neighborhood.
Martha Demshar a Jefferson Township Trustee stated her reasons against the
annexation. Asked if the Village Council has thought about what all annexations
in general would do. With the development of subdivisions it will have impact
on our schools which are already over populated. It would have an impact on the
village sewer plant, increase village streets which would cost more to service.
Told Council that the township residents do not want sewer. Asked Council to
consider all aspects of what the annexations would do for the village.
Motion by Maloney to move the Council meeting into Public Hearing.
2nd by Thompson
Roll: All yea, motion carried.
Public Hearing 8:11 pm
Administrator Pauley explained to Council that the proposed amended sidewalk
ordinance removes the conflict in the requirement for sidewalks for all new
construction, in subdivisions that were approved and platted prior to the
requirement for sidewalks as part of the subdivision review process. This does
not relieve the requirement for sidewalks as part of all new subdivisions that
are part of the subdivision review process.
Motion by Maloney to return to regular Council session.
2nd by Finger
Roll: All yea, motion carried.
Regular session 8:17 pm.
Councilperson Maloney explained to everyone that the Resolution the Village is
passing only states what services the Village of Jefferson will provide. This
Resolution is required by the Village to landowners who want to annex to the
Village.
Council discussed at great length, the issues involving annexation,
subdivisions, and requirements as to what the Village is required to do along
with what the property owner’s options are.

shanties and burn barrels.
Mayor Bragga told Council that the Administrator, Police Chief and himself have
been talking with the strikers to get through all this. Told Council that after
the strike is over Council should revisit the legislation with the current
codes and make changes so the Village will not have these problems next time.
Mayor Bragga discussed with Council, Ordinance 1924 pertaining to regulations
and use of the Public Greens. The ordinance was passed in October 1991 but was
never codified. The Village did not find the ordinance until about four weeks
into the strike. The Village is trying to stay neutral with the labor disputes.
Council discussed wind breakers on private property and owners making a mess on
the Village tree lawns. The Administrator was asked to look into and discuss
with the strikers for a gentlemens agreement.
Solicitor Lemire told Council they should adopt clear rules and regulations
which include penalties if the laws are broken.
Mayor Bragga told Council the issue between the unions needs to be resolved.
The biggest issue is that both parties need to communicate and compromise.
Mayor Bragga told Council that State Representative George Distel and himself
spoke at the rally on December 1st and agree that all parties should compromise
and resolve the issue as soon as possible.

Visitors Comments
Tim Leehan of 139 North Spruce Street spoke to Council about the annexation of
the McIntyre property to the Village. Leehan asked Council and the Mayor to
attend the annexation hearing Tuesday, December 18, 2001 at 2:00 pm regarding
the McIntyre annexation. Stated he was not opposed to the other annexations but
is opposed to the McIntyre annexation. Reason being upon annexation nothing
will change. Right now there is no water or sewer and the road is not paved.
Told Council if the McIntyre property is annexed some of the owners surrounding
the McIntyre property may annex to the Township.
Mayor Bragga explained to Leehan that if the property is annexed the property
owner would have to conform to the subdivision regulations passed in 1999. A
building or zoning permit would not be approved without conforming to the
regulations.
Solicitor Lemire explained to Council that it is very hard for the county
commissioners to reject the annexation. The county is limited for reasons to
reject an annexation. The decision then falls on the village to decide on the
annexation.

Village Administrator' Report for period ending December 14, 2001:
Service Dept.:
·   Culvert and drainage ditch enclosure was completed on East Beech Street at
East Beech Street Development Corp (Geriatric Center).
·   Tree removal continues at East Beech Street Development Corp (Geriatric
Center) for clear cutting of brush on unopened Pine Street. Allows temporary
horse shelter on geriatric center.
·   Contract included for removal of surplus trees on village right of way. Net
value to the village is $950.00. Requires no council action.
·   Brittany Lane was paved under private contract between the developer and
Velotta Paving. The Village will accept the total job after some adjustments to
sewer manholes.
·   Winter tree trim or removal list with quotes authorized by Village
Administrator.
(Note: This list represents all the notes, phone calls and lists that seem to
have accumulated for years.)
Recreation/Community Center:
·   Received nine responses to the first round of ads for the Recreation
Director position.
·   Ads placed for Senior van driver.
·   Major clean up, sorting out, under way in all storage and other behind the
scene areas.
·   Winter program offering finalized (Letter attached)
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Interior gas service line has been repaired. Gas service resumed to all
waste water buildings.
·   Safety railings being installed around open tanks.
·   Backhoe/loader being purchased to replace 1992 Case. New unit will be
swapped with Street Department.
·   Safety security lights to be installed around tank areas and buildings.
·   Mill Creek Pump Station rehabilitation delayed till January 2002.
Other:
·   Transfer from Landis to Keep Insurance Agency ran into a delay while
details are worked out. Will have no effect on our insurance coverage.
·   Attended City Managers meeting as the guest of Dan Weire. Meeting was held
at the Cleveland State University Maxine Goodman Levine College of Urban
Affairs. This was a good opportunity to meet peers and network with other
communities. Will seek membership. List of College Workshops included.
·   Three new computers were installed and are fully operational. Network
installation should occur before year end to connect the four main computers:
Sewer Billing, Income Tax, Clerk Treasurer, and Village Administrator. If 2002
budget allows, the financial software will be changed from the old Dos
programs.

Growth Partnership for review with the eye on help with development. (Copy
Attached)

Department Reports
The following is the Village Administrator's Report for period ending January
04, 2002:
Service Dept.:
·   Winter tree trim or removal work in progress.
·   Service Department will pick up Christmas trees at curbside through January
18, 2002.
(Note: Trees must be bare with no ornaments, tree bags or stands to allow for
chipping.)
·   Clean up from the first winter snow was completed without major problems.
Recreation/Community Center :
·   Received thirty- four résumé’s for the Recreation Director position. Have
interviewed six top quality applicants and expect to make a job offer by Friday
January 11.
·   Received twenty applicants for the senior van driver position. Expect to
interview six of the top candidates by Friday January 11.
·   Major clean up, sorting out, continues in all storage and other behind the
scene areas.
·   Winter program offerings are underway with the usual after Holiday fitness
rush.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Safety railings were installed around open tanks.
·   A set of steps with hand rails were installed on clarifier tank for
inspection purposes.
·   Backhoe/loader expected to arrive mid January.
·   Safety security lights yet to be installed around tank areas and buildings.
·   Sludge was pressed and disposed of for land application.
·   Mill Creek Pump Station rehabilitation delayed till January 2002.
Other:
·   Transfer from Landis to Keep Insurance Agency will be finalized.
·   Network installation scheduled for week of January 11 to connect the four
main computers: Sewer Billing, Income Tax, Clerk Treasurer, and Village
Administrator.
·   Zoning infractions are being aggressively addressed (attachment)
·   Voluntary Department wide Safety Inspections scheduled with Workers
Compensation Representative.

Utilities
Richard Hummel of 113 E. Cedar St. questioned the Opt –Out Natural Gas
Ordinance on the agenda.
Mayor Bragga explained that the procedures for the Natural Gas Opt Out
Aggregation program is the same as the Electric Aggregation program. This will
be placed on the ballot and Village residents will have the opportunity to vote
whether or not to go with NOPEC. NOPEC negotiates for the best gas rates. If
residents choose to stay with their current provider they have the option of
opting out of the NOPEC program just as they did with the electric.
Administrator Finger told Council that passing the resolution puts it on the
ballot and residents can then tell NOPEC what they want by their vote.
Motion by Stasny for the first reading of Resolution 02-R-2397
2nd by Thompson
Roll: All yea, motion carried.
Ordinance No. 02-R-2397   
An Ordinance Authorizing All Actions Necessary To Effect An Opt-Out Natural Gas
Aggregation Program Pursuant To Section 4929.26, Ohio Revised Code, Directing
The County Board Of Elections To Submit A Ballot Question To The Electors,
Authorizing The Execution Of An Agreement With NOPEC For Such Purposes And
Declaring An Emergency.

Officials
Diana Sowry of 61 W. Satin St. talked with Council regarding the parade that
the local 419 purposed to have on Saturday, January 26, 2002, “In Support of
Labor”.
Council discussed that the Village has no legislation addressing the request
for parades and the manpower to have a parade. The past practice has always
been Council approves the parade and the Village supplies the manpower and pays
the wages.
Councilperson Ward said that what is so disturbing is that no one can get any
information from both parties involved. He feels there should be a meeting with
both parties to get this issue resolved. Diana Sowry told Council that there is
a parents meeting being held January 10, 2002 from 6-8 pm at the Henderson
Library, everyone is invited.
Council discussed the parade issue. If Council does approve it, it may look as
if the Village Council is in support of the union. Agreed that the issue must
be resolved as soon as possible.
Councilperson Baxley told Council that the Village is not looking to take
sides. The village was presented with a memo requesting approval of a parade.
Regardless of who the person is representing the request, Council must approve
or deny the request.
Motion by Thompson to approve the Mayors recommendation for the request of a
parade. The parades purpose “In Support of Labor” to be held on January 26th at
1:00 pm
2nd by Maloney
Roll: All yea, motion carried.
Council agreed the refuse contract should stay on the agenda and the service
committee will discuss the contract at the committee meeting being held January
15th at 7:30 pm.

gives the Solicitor a salary rate of $1500.00 a month. When the solicitors

New Business/Old Business
Mayor Bragga gave the State of the Village Address
   The year 2001 proved to be a very fulfilling, insightful and fast-paced
year. I appreciate the communication and the support of many members of our
community. The administration has
continued to promote a more professional and business-like approach to the
operations of the village.
   I want to mention just a few of the many positives that have occurred in a
few short months.
   Through the partnership effort with our Jefferson Chamber of Commerce, the
village administrator, several citizens, and some cooperative council
committees, we are now on-line, with a web page and e-mail addresses. Our
citizens are able to view council and commission agendas, minutes and income
tax forms on-line .
   The efforts of our Water advisory group in 2001 have assisted in maintaining
our current ISO rating and have provided both short and long range plans for
water service to our community.
   Weekly department head meetings continue to occur to help insure a means of
communication and team-work among all village departments.
   We have developed a comprehensive sign ordinance to address the various
needs faced by our village in the future.
   We faced the interesting and challenging requests of annexations to the
village and will continue to learn and grow with the new legislation recently
approved by our state.
   We have stayed on course with respect to the planning for future use of the
Rush Creek property: including a motion (that needs to be an ordinance) to
preserve land as park and greenspace and we have established the appropriate
zoning for light industrial areas and have designated 9.37 acres of our Rush
Creek property for that purpose.
   We have recovered 10’s of thousands of dollars of delinquent sewer bills.
   We have developed a comprehensive and user friendly appropriation and budget
documents.
   We have recently employed Terry Finger as our administrator. He is excited
to be in our great village and is eager to manage with care and compassion,
always working to the letter of the laws and ordinances of our village.
   I could go on and on relating the many positive issues and changes that have
occurred in 2001; but, I must press forward and suggest and encourage this
village to address a variety of issues and challenges that face us in the next
few years beginning in 2002. The following are just a few of the many and
varied issues that we will face in the near future.
   As I mention a few issues and topics please remember that they are all
important with
no issue or topic having any specific priority over another ....... thus making
the plate very full of necessary and meaningful tasks and discussions.
   This council needs to review and revisit our refuse billing procedures and
be certain accurate bid specifications be developed immediately.
   Consideration needs to be given to all unimproved streets and their
development, let’s not continue to ignore this ongoing problem in hopes that it
will go away.
   Efficient village operations require the proper software and networking
system be approved starting with the town hall. A continued commitment to staff
development and training must continue.
   There are some safety issues we must address in 2002 and beyond:
We need to once again be pro-active in our discussion, study and approach to
fire service in the future. Like it or not, several factors (factors like
continuous growth and development and changes in society) dictate we attack
this important issue in 2002. The fire Chief and mayor
and village administrator will work on public awareness and recruitment this
year. And with the help of council, work toward long range plans for fire
service.
   We need to aggressively seek financial support for the needed truck route in
an effort to improve safety and efficient access to our industrial areas of the
Village.
   The village needs to be continually aware of its potential for growth and
development ...... planning and zoning regulations need to remain open and
improving documents that support and reflect what we want for our village and
what we believe this village should be and grow into.
   We must continue to learn and gain knowledge with respect to electric and
natural gas utilities and hope that our membership in NOPEC for electric and
gas deregulation will prove to be beneficial to the budgets of our citizens.
   We need to continue to explore our influence and communication with Consumer
Ohio Water Service as they provide water service to our village. (reminding
council that we will be discussing a new contract for water service ).
   Many administrative projects are on the table, projects that will enhance
and improve our total operation, to mention a few :
   1. develop an organizational flow chart for the village of Jefferson
   2. develop handouts that relate to all building, construction and zoning
regulations and
ordinances
   3. revisit and update our personnel manual   
   4. recognition of new businesses to the village
   5. create appropriate welcome signs at the four major entrances to the
village
   We need to update and improve the ordinances that relate to the use and
dignity of our rights of way, village greens and tree lawns.
   I observe that we are a community that enjoys and loves to walk so we must
increase our attention and financial commitment to a short and long range
sidewalk replacement and improvement program.
   We must continue to provide quality service to the village residents always
striving to be
the best we can be ... our street department, recreation department, police ,
wastewater and volunteer fire departments are made up of great people who need
our support and direction as we work together to be a wonderful community.
   The table is full but constantly changing .... and I have mentioned only
some of our many and varied issues and concerns ....... I would be remiss if I
failed to emphasize two most important pieces of our total community .... a
thanks to our churches, their leaders and church families ..... that create the
fundamental stable foundation for a quality community,,,,,.... as I relate a
basic premise to my simple philosophy , “ our community is no better than our
churches and our schools “ ...... We need to ask ‘BEG “ the board of education
and the local union members to get back to the business of negotiating so that
the task of educating the most important product of our country can resume to a
normal and effective and even superior level of performance ..... This strike
will not be settled by public opinion or influencing public opinion, it will be
settled by both parties meeting in a spirit of compromise and agreeing to a
fair and
workable contract. Please get together and give our school students and school
community a
chance to get back to improving and regaining its status a quality school
system.
   Finally , I thank this council for your patience , cooperation , knowledge,
communication and support .... my prayer continues to be that we work together
in a spirit of professionalism,
cooperation and honest hard work in a continuous effort to improve in making
our village a safe and beautiful place to live , work and raise a family.
Meeting adjourned at 9:10 pm.
Respectfully Submitted,
Patricia A. Fisher
Clerk of Council

Hall.

Administrator Report
The following is the Village Administrator' Report for period ending January
04, 2002:
   Service Dept.:
·   Winter tree trim or removal work nearing completion with stump removal
planned as practical.
·   Christmas trees pick up ended Friday January 18, 2002.
·   Christmas decorations were removed and put into storage.
·   American flags removed until spring.
Recreation/Community Center :
·   Larry Carlson was offered the full time Recreation Director position and
accepted.
·   Major clean up, sorting out, continues in all storage and other behind the
scene areas.
·   Purchased a new snow blower to handle heavy snow accumulations.
·   Obtaining quotes for a floor scrubber/polisher to improve floor finish.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Ongoing maintenance.
·   Sewer hook up inspections on Elliott, West Jefferson, and West Cedar
Street.
·   Sludge again being pressed and disposed of for land application.
Other:
·   Transfer from Landis to Keep Insurance Agency was finalized.
·   Network installation began week of January 11 to connect the four main
computers: Sewer Billing, Income Tax, Clerk Treasurer, and Village
Administrator.

Department Reports
Administrators Report
The following is the Village Administrator's Report for period ending February
15, 2002:
   Service Dept.:
·   Service Dept. completed safety training on the New Case Loader and the
loader has been put in service.
·   P.M. and repair to Trucks and Equipment as needed.
·   All Problems that were encountered during the safety inspection by The Ohio
Bureau of Workers Compensation are already corrected.
Recreation/Community Center :
·   Expansion of the weight lifting area (to the West) is nearing completion at
little or no cost to the village. (volunteer help)
·   Participation in programs continues to increase.
·   Staff is seeking and adding new programs.
·   Advertisements (thanks to the generosity of our papers) are improving.
·   Floor scrubber/polisher to improve floor finish is on order.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Ongoing maintenance.
·   Wastewater Dept. completed safety training on the New Case Loader
·   Sewer line cleaning continues as practical.
·   Receiving quotes to clean sludge that has accumulated in the holding tank.
Other:
·   Budget is Final and in your packet.
·   All minutes have been digitized and are available for electronic search,
view, and print.
·   All ordinances have been reviewed and digital version for search, view, and
print should be available in April.
·   All ordinances shall be kept up to date quarterly there after.
·   The next project has been identified as reviewing the Village Personnel
Practices Manual to eliminate it and codify the practices.
·   Have received quotes to bring the administration network to completion.
This will allow council to have access to all shared electronic records.
·   See Newspaper article regarding Workshop at Kent State Geauga Campus.
Administrator Finger told council that the pay out of vacation time to
Administrator Pauley was properly paid.

Certificate of the total amount from all sources available for expenditures and
balances.

Councilperson Baxley told council at the committee meeting they discussed the
following recommendations or action be taken.
   Administrator to check with COWC about shut off.
   Administrator to check with Auditor about bi annual and annual collection
time frames.
   Have Solicitor review and advise on ordinance 2258 and portions of Section
1030 need to rewrite for collection recommendation.
   Procedure for delinquent accounts: add 3% late charge per month reflected on
bills as late charge, letter notifying delinquent account holder that account
is delinquent and if unpaid in excess of 30 days it will be certified to the
Auditor with a 20% late charge fee to be added to assessment, and publishing of
delinquent account holders name.

council that he has not received a response for the February 15, 2002 deadline.

bills and WEK should pay the full amount. The Village has given them enough
options and time to pay the bill. Council agreed the Village should start
litigation on WEK for payment of their sewer bill.

really watch its revenue compared to expenses.
