Administrators Report
The following is the Village Administrator Report for period ending March 1,
2002:
   Service Dept.:
·   Safety training scheduled for chain saws and power trimmers at the County
Service Building.
·   OUPS Ohio Utility Protection Service meeting scheduled for April 30, 2002.
·   New signs were ordered for Frayer Drive and Buckeye Drive.
Recreation/Community Center :
·   Maintenance/Custodian A Dave Sawdey resigned. Replacement process has been
started.
·   Staff is seeking and adding new programs.
·   Floor scrubber/polisher to improve floor finish has been delivered.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Ongoing maintenance.
·   Sewer line cleaning continues as practical.
·   Receiving quotes to clean sludge that has accumulated in the holding tank.
Other:
·   Inventory is being brought up to date for our liability insurance renewal.
·   The next project has been identified as reviewing the Village Personnel
Practices Manual to eliminate it and codify the practices.
·   The administration network server is on order.

Visitors Comments :
Russ Santee the owner of Jefferson Pro Hardware spoke to Council regarding the
Village ordinance. Especially the “sandwich signs”. He told Council that people
come into his store stating that they have had trouble locating it. The signs
on the buildings are high and flat and not always visible. The sandwich sign is
an effective way to acquire better visibility for customers. The new ordinance
prohibits the sandwich sign. If business owners cannot attract customers by
using these signs we then risk losing business in the Village. Customers will
go somewhere else and as a whole we all lose. Santee asked if he could have the
opportunity to meet with the Building / Lands Committee to negotiate the
business signs.
Councilperson Baxley asked why do we have the ordinance? The Village needs to
enforce the ordinance or throw it out. The ordinance was created for safety
issues. The ordinance is now being violated and nothing is being done.
Administrator Finger explained to council that the new sign ordinance did not
become effective until mid February. He stated that he is not taking one
business on at a time. When the ordinance is in force he will notify every
business that is in violation. As of now, no business in town is being
disadvantaged by the passage of the sign ordinance.
Councilperson Ward told Council when the Building/Lands Committee meets he will
be glad to have the businesses come to the meeting and express their opinions.
The Village has been working on the passage of the sign ordinance for a long
time.

Administrators Report
The following is the Village Administrator's Report for period ending March 15,
2002:
   Service Dept.:
·   Completed safety training for chain saws and power trimmers at the County
Service Building for eight employees.
·   Six employees are scheduled to attend the free Ohio Safety Congress and
Expo. March 26, or March 27, or March 28 in Cleveland.
·   The concept of new signs for the entrances into the village was discussed
with Cicogna Signs of Ashtabula. Prices range from $700 to $1,500 each
depending on size and design. Monthly lease terms are available with $1.00 buy
out.
·   CT Consultants will re- submit Engineering study for West Cedar Street
completion to make sure the streets meet the Specifications of ordinance 02-O-
2412 passed last council meeting.
·   I have met three times with Benny Godleski regarding West Cedar Street. I
committed to him that once all the facts are known I would meet with all
interested parties.
·   CT Consultants will re-submit the Engineering Study for Sycamore/Pine/Rush
Creek area. Study will be re-evaluated in light of planned developments in that
area.
·   Maintenance of gravel roads (adding new stones) has begun.
Recreation/Community Center :
·   Thomas Fence is preparing a proposal for the fence around the skate park.
·   Skate board equipment to be moved back into area ASAP.
·   New Rental Rates put into effect.
·   New contract and Civic list are part of your packet.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Mill Creek Pump Station Rehab nearly complete.
·   CT Consultants will resubmit their proposal for the sludge storage shed.
·   Sewer connection procedure and guidelines to contractors is being up
graded.
·   Reviewing quotes to clean sludge that has accumulated in the holding tank.
Other:
·   Inventory is 95% complete for our liability insurance renewal.
·   Survey for Light Industrial and Park Land has been scheduled.
·   The administration network server was installed 3/15/02.
·   Sewer Billing and Refuse Billing changes are under development.

Committee and discuss the designing of new signs for the Village.

Administrator Report
The following is the Village Administrator's Report for period ending March 31,
2002:
   Service Dept.:
·   Four Street Dept. employees attended the free Ohio Safety Congress and
Expo. March 28 in Cleveland. Roland commented that this was the best Expo. they
had attended and had the most useful job related displays and information.
Report from Department will follow later.
·   Brush pick-up resumed today, the first Monday of April, and will continue
the first Monday of each month until fall.
·   Maintenance of gravel roads continues.
·   Cleaning of ditches and the installation of tile is in progress.
Recreation/Community Center :
·   Larry Carlson submitted his letter of resignation. Need a motion to accept
it.
·   Thomas Fence gave us a quote of about $1,200 to install temporary posts
until the fence issue is resolved. As an alternative we will borrow four
concrete highway lane dividers as barriers and area protection.
·   Reorganization of the Recreation department was discussed at the Rec.
Committee meeting. I would request as part of the Recreation Committee report
that we fully discuss the changes.
·   The new wage ordinance scheduled in the Finance Committee Report is a part
of the Recreation Department changes.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   On 3/26/02 at about 10:00 PM there was a total electrical failure at the
wastewater treatment plant. (See CT Consultant report.)
·   The failure was discovered at 5:30 AM on Wednesday 3/27/02 and the plant
was back in partial operation by 8:30 PM that evening.
·   During the evening of Wednesday 3/27/02 a fan coupling broke, again putting
the plant back down.
·   By 8:30 PM Thursday 3/28/02 the fan coupling was repaired and the plant
again back in operation.
·   During the night of Thursday 3/28/02 an anti-vibration coupling on the 16
inch air circulating pipes failed, again putting the plant down. This failure
was bypassed by noon Friday 3/29/02 and the plant was back on line.
·   Since noon Friday 3/29/02 the plant treating process has been back in full
operation and is continuing to function.
·   AT NO TIME DURING THIS PERIOD WAS UNTREATED WATER DISCHARGED FROM THE
PLANT.
·   ALL REQUIRED TESTING CONTINUED AND WAS RECORDED
·   TEST RESULTS SHOW THAT THERE WERE NO E.P.A. VIOLATIONS  
·   We can discuss more details during Wastewater Committee Report.
·   Mill Creek Pump Station Rehab nearly complete.
·   CT Consultants will resubmit their proposal for the sludge storage shed.
·   Sewer connection procedure and guidelines to contractors is being upgraded.
·   Reviewing quotes to clean sludge that has accumulated in the holding tank.
Other:
·   Request for a motion to accept Smolen Engineering Proposal
·   Inventory is complete for our liability insurance renewal.
·   Survey for Light Industrial and Park Land is in process.
·   Sewer Billing and Refuse Billing changes are under development.
·   FYI a copy of Ohio Bar Association discussion on Planned Unit Development.
Clerk Treasurer - no report
Police Chief – no report
Fire Chief – no report
Committee Reports
Utilities
Mayor Bragga reminded Council and the residents of the Village that NOPEC will
have the opt out provision for gas on the May ballot.
Waste Water Treatment
Councilperson Baxley told Council that the ordinance for fines regarding the
delinquent sewer and refuse bills still needs to be changed and asked if the
committee could work together on the ordinance.
Solicitor Lemire told Council that he received a response from Old WEK on March
20th regarding more time. Stated that he hoped to resolve the issue some time
next week. They are going to discuss and negotiate the complaint. Told Council
that if the issue cannot be resolved, a complaint will be filed against Old
WEK.
Administrator Finger thanked everyone who was involved and helped with the
emergency at the Waste Water Treatment Plant the week of March 25th. The event
occurred because of a mechanical failure of a valve. The basement filled up
with approximately 5 ½ feet of water. The wet floor warning electrical did not
go off to warn anyone of the water. The sump pumps could not keep up with the
amount of water and burnt out. The Village is taking measures to prevent this
in the future.
Administrator Finger assured Council that at no time during that period was
untreated water discharged from the plant. All required testing continued and
was recorded. The test results showed no EPA violations.
Building/Lands
Councilperson Ward announced a Building/Lands Committee meeting for Tuesday,
April 10th at 4:30 pm. The agenda will include the Sandwich signs, Planning
Development and Village Greens.
Council set a Public Hearing for Monday, May 6th at 8:30 pm during regular
Council session. The Public Hearing was set to cover Subdivision Regulations.
Council discussed the sign ordinance and felt something must be decided in the
business district for signs. Jefferson Village business district is a historic
district with old buildings that abut each other. If the business were in a new
business district there would be set backs and space for signs. Council agreed
that the Village should try to keep the main street historic.
Recreation
Motion by Ward to accept the resignation of Larry Carlson as Director of
Jefferson Community Recreation Center.
2nd by Maloney
Roll: All yea, motion carried.
Council discussed the Skateboard Park and possibly putting up a fence. The
fence would restrict the Fire Dept. access to electrical boxes if a fire were
to occur at the Recreation Center. Relocation of the electrical boxes would
cost the Village. If the fence post were to be put back into place the cost
would be around $1,200 to redrill the concrete barriers holding the posts. They
discussed putting in more lights and a video camera. Council agreed that was
the best option until a final decision is made for the Skateboard Park.
Ryan DiMarino of 20 East Ashtabula Street asked Council when all of the
Skateboard Equipment was going to be brought out of storage. Questioned if the
committee and Council were going to put a fence around the Skateboard Park.
Told Council he felt the fence could cause some safety issues, with kids
running into the fence by accident. Because the park is not that large in size
now, adding a fence will make it even smaller.
Ryan also told Council a video camera and more lights would help prevent kids
from damaging property.
Council discussed the Recreation Dept. reorganization. The decision to
reorganize has been ongoing from last year when the budget process began.
Administrator Finger told Council during the application process in December
the reorganization of the dept. was considered. The decision to change the pay
scale of the Director to $33,800.00 and a contract would not effect the budget.
With the reorganization the Assistant Director salary would change to $11.00 an
hour and title would become Youth/Adult Program Coordinator.
The full time Clerical/Program Advocate would become Clerical / Administrative
Support.
Custodian/Utility Maintenance A & B would be changed to
Custodian Part time in the Recreation Center and a new position Utility /
Maintenance part time under Administration, to be supervised by the
Administrator.
Councilperson Ward told Council what is in place now is not working. We should
reorganize and shift monies within the budget so that no additional funding
would be required for the new positions.
Councilperson Baxley told Council she was concerned with hiring a new director
as a contractor and the pay scale is a big jump from what we were paying. The
person must prove they are worth that amount of pay. Maybe they should start
lower and increase in six months.
Mayor Bragga told Council that the Village has invested a lot of money into the
building. We need a person in the building who will bring in the programs along
with revenue. There has been a person with recreation experience, business
experience and a retired athletic director, none of which has worked. To get a
qualified person the Village will have to pay more in salaries. Both applicants
interviewed have very good recommendations and work experience in the
Recreation field.
Motion by Ward to reorganize the Jefferson Recreation Dept. making the
directors job contractual and follow the new job descriptions on the new wage
ordinance. The new positions created would be Youth/Adult Program Coordinator,
Full time Clerical/Administrative Support, Custodian part time, and Utility/
Maintenance part time.
2nd by Maloney
Roll: All yea, motion carried.
Motion by Thompson to approve the Administrator recommendation to hire a new
Recreation Director by contract, capping the salary at $33,800 with a one year
contract. In the contract include two weeks vacation, two personal days and
sick time to accrue like all other full time employees. The one year contract
would be six months with a six month extension review, with the right to
cancel.
2nd by Maloney
Roll: Stasny yea, Thompson yea, Ward yea, Baxley nea, Maloney yea.
Councilperson Ward told Council that he spent time with both candidates and it
will be a hard decision.
Finance

Department Reports:
Administrator Report
The following is the Village Administrator's Report for period ending April 12
2002:
   Service Dept.:
·   Heritage Hills Homeowner Association has decided to stay a private street.
This action means they will not have to bring paving etc. up to Village
standards for acceptance.
·   I have asked for something in writing so we can introduce this information
into the minutes for future reference.
·   Brush pick-up resumed April 1, 2002 and will continue the first Monday of
each month until fall.
·   Cleaning of ditches and the installation of tile continues.
Recreation/Community Center :
·   Jenny DeCamillo submitted her letter of resignation. Need a motion to
accept it.
·   Skate park is back in operation with concrete barriers costing $160.00
instead of about $1,200 to install temporary posts.
·   Security Camera to be installed with return of warm weather.
·   The fence issue is on hold pending outcome of security camera monitoring.
·   Anita Perrotti (My choice for New Recreation Director) was put on a
Personal Services Contract, copy a should be in your packet.
·   Feedback from everyone who has met Anita has been overwhelmingly positive.
·   Recreation Committee to present Recreation Director Contract and New
Recreation Department Job Descriptions for Council’s approval.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Need a motion to accept the resignation of Judy Rockwell from the laborer
classification at the Wastewater Department.
·   Mill Creek Pump Station Rehab is complete.
·   Sludge storage shed project put on hold until restart costs are known.
·   Sludge clean out in EQ holding tank on hold until plant treatment
stabilizes.
Other:
·   Village liability insurance renewed with current carrier Todd Insurance
(Ohio Government Pool)
·   Village owned property records (deeds) are being reviewed for completeness
for our liability insurance.
·   Survey for Light Industrial and Park Land is in process.
·   Sewer Billing and Refuse Billing changes are under development.
Councilperson Ward asked the Administrator what was going on with Heritage Hill
Estates and the acceptance of the road.
Administrator Finger told Council that Heritage Hill Estates had decided to
keep the road private. The Village Safety forces will still protect the
Estates. But having the roads plowed, paved and maintained will be up to
Heritage Hill Estates. The Village will not accept the street and will not pay
for the street lights or plow the streets.
Clerk Treasurer - March Month-end submitted and First quarter vendors list.
Annexation paperwork filed with County Auditor and County Recorder forward to
Board of Elections Secretary of State.
Clerk Treasurer Fisher told Council that approximately 200 vendors were removed
from the vendors list to clean up the list.
Motion by Maloney to approve the first quarters vendor list for 2002.
2nd by Baxley
Roll: All yea, motion carried.
Police Chief – Mayor Bragga told Council that he has talked with Police Chief
Febel on enforcing traffic violations for speeding and rolling through stop
signs in the Village.
Fire Chief – Mayor Bragga told Council that he spoke with the Fire Chief and
Safety Comm. on paying the Fire Dept. employees through a deferred annuity for
retirement instead of receiving a paycheck.
Mayor Bragga asked the Solicitor to research the idea of paying Fire Dept.
employees with annuities.

Department Reports
Administrator Finger
The following is the Village Administrator's Report for period ending May 3,
2002:
   Service Dept.:
·   Cleaning of ditches and the installation of tile continues.
·   First of three Street Cleanings is complete.
·   2002 sidewalk replacements will be the entire length of East and West Erie
Streets, a section of South Market Street, the short public walk on the south
end of the South East Public Green, and a short section to complete Ashtabula
Street as budgeted.
·   Spring tree planting flags are placed to locate the trees. A list also is
provided.
·   I have had several residents, (3) three so far, object to having trees
planted in selected sites. My response has been to remove and relocate the
trees.
·   Roland Ferguson will contact all resident property owners to let them know
what the White Flags are for.
·   We need to replace Roland’s pick up as a Capital expenditure and delay
replacing the street department roof. Bid Specifications are being prepared.
·   Training request for 2002 Public Works Expo and Roadeo.
Recreation/Community Center :
·   Anita Perrotti (New Recreation Director) officially started April 22, 2002.
·   Anita completed and submitted the United Way Grant on time and filled out
correctly for the first time.
·   Summer Program plans are being developed.
·   We are interviewing for Program Coordinator, Part Time Custodian and Part
Time Maintenance/Utility.
·   Skate park is back in operation with few problems.
·   The Skate Park Security Camera has been installed.
·   The fence issue is still on hold pending outcome of security camera
monitoring.
·   We need to schedule a Recreation Committee meeting as soon as practical for
planning purposes.
·   Request to change Youth/Adult Coordinator from $11.00 per hour to $11.00 X
2080 hrs = $22,880 per year salary.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   All electric control circuits have been tested and re-marked to assure
recovery from our power outage.
·   Both Sump pumps have been replaced and are fully functional.
·   The Primary blower #1 must be replaced due to bearing failure unrelated to
the Power outage.
·   Plant is in summer operation mode, which requires double the lab testing.
·   Requests for training (attached) were approved as budgeted.
·   Sewer lines are being inspected to make sure flows are OK. Jetting to
resume on side streets as part of ongoing maintenance.
·   Woodside Pump Station Rehab is on hold.
·   Sludge storage shed project put on hold until restart costs are known.
·   Sludge clean out in EQ holding tank on hold until plant treatment
stabilizes.
Other:
·   New accounting software from (SSI) Software Solutions Inc. has been
selected from three venders. This package is $20,000 less than the one selected
last year.
·   Departmental charges and the project break down results in no purchase
order being over the $15,000 limit requiring council approval.
·   Village owned property records (deeds) are still being reviewed for
completeness for our records.
·   Survey for Light Industrial and Park Land is in process.
·   Sewer Billing and Refuse Billing changes will be implemented when the new
accounting software is operational.
·   The assessment process is being documented for discussion. This is needed
for paving: West Cedar Street, Elliott Drive, East Erie Street, Pine Street,
Sycamore Street and Mulberry Street.
·   Announcements/requests from VFW.
·   Prior notification of a church project at First Baptist Church.
Clerk Treasurer attended the Local Govt. Officials Conference on April 25 & 26.
In attending this conference the Clerk Treasurer will be in compliance with the
mandated training for the State Auditors for the year 2002.
Chief Febel extended to Council an invitation to ride with an officer during
their shift.

Council and the Township Trustees asked the Clerk Treasurer to look into when
the Trustees terms would expire. Reason being Councilperson Thompsons sheet had
two Trustees terms expiring in the same year.
Solicitor Lemire explained to Council and the Jefferson Township Trustees that
per the ORC the Joint Meeting must be held the first Council meeting in May.
The ORC states that there must be a Council and Township Trustee on the Board
but it does not designate who the third person must be. That person can be a
Village or Township resident.
Charlene Kusar of 1348 Rt. 307 West asked the Village Council and Township
Trustees why her owning a business was a conflict of interest and how it would
violate the Board rules. Questioned if her business violates the board rules
why would Scott Treens Insurance Co. not violate the Board rules.
Councilperson Thompson told Charlene Kusar that the Board passed a rule in 1946
that a person holding the position can not have a business that sells products
to the cemetery or deals directly with the public.
Township Trustee Shadle told Council and the Jefferson Township Trustees that
he interprets it different and an Insurance Co. is also a conflict of interest
and both should be treated the same.
Township Trustee Shadle also asked why the nominations were only accepted from
Council.

nominations and there could be a second nomination.

Public Hearing 8:40 pm
Solicitor Lemire swore in Jim McIntyre of 32 East Pine St. Jefferson, to speak
during the Public Hearing.
Jim McIntyre spoke to Council with concerns regarding the change in lot size
under the subdivision regulations. Told Council in changing the lot size it
will hinder people moving into the Village. Bigger lots will cost more.
Administrator Finger told Council what is changing is the current ordinance
which requires the subdivision regulations to have a minimum frontage of 75
feet. The new ordinance will require the subdivision regulations to have 110
feet and to specify a minimum lot acreage requirement of 0.5 acres which equals
21,780 square feet.
Councilperson Baxley told Council that with the new housing, they have 4
bedrooms, 2.5 baths and this size house is not fitting well on the current lot
size. Most new homes are about 2500 sq. ft.
Administrator Finger told Council that changing the lot size will prevent a lot
of people having to go to the Board of Zoning Appeals because houses or
additions will not fit on the existing lot size.
Motion by Maloney to close the Public Hearing at 8:45 pm

David Sawdey Commander of the American Legion Baylor Post 152, presented
Council with a check in the amount of $2154.80 to defray the cost of a security
camera and recording deck at the Recreation Center.
Norman David of Jefferson spoke to Council about the banner that the American
Legion is passing out to families of soldiers in active duty. The banner is to
be hung in the window to show that they have a family member serving in active
duty. To obtain a banner call Norman David at 576-2606.
Council was reminded of the Memorial Day parade on Monday, May 27th
Mary Beth Nassief, Ed Curie, and Jeff Coxen representing the Nassief property
spoke on the proposed rezoning of Nassief Inc. as Light Industrial.
Jeff Coxen, Nassief’s lawyer spoke of concerns with the ordinance that Council
has on the agenda and will be discussing at the Public Hearing on June 17th.
Asked what effects would the ordinance have on the Nassief property.
Mayor Bragga explained that with the new ordinance the single family
residential lot would have to meet the new requirements of 110 feet, a minimum
lot requirement of 0.5 acres (21,780 sq ft). because the lot is a whole parcel
which has not been broken down into separate parcels.
Jeff Coxen explained that Nassief Inc. has sketched three different plots which
would include a residential section, light industrial, and a B-1 section. He
also suggested that Council change the dealership from the proposed light
industrial to B1. If not it would limit future development.
Councilman Ward explained his main concern was to know the intentions for the
use of the property. Agreed that the Village should get it zoned Light
Industrial and make changes at a later date based on its usage. Council could
make changes in the language to support the car dealership in Light Industrial.
Mary Beth Nassief told Council the reason she wanted to annex into the Village
was because of sewers and her fathers dream. He always wanted to have a
development with houses on the property. She also explained that selling the
lots will defray the cost to extend a sewer line to the property.
Administrator Finger questioned the Nassief plan as to so much residential
compared to the light industrial. It lessens the impact of the availability of
funds by having less than a third Light Industrial.
Ed Curie explained to Council that selling residential lots is more cost
effective than selling Light Industrial.
Mayor Bragga told Council that part of the thinking on Light Industrial is that
the Village Council wants to keep our business on the main street in town. If
changing the zoning from Light Industrial to B1, there is opportunity there for
strip malls and stores closing in the main business section of town.
Richard Tamblyn of Jefferson also explained how the new subdivision ordinance
would effect his property and development plans.
Solicitor Lemire explained that if his development is already plotted out into
parcels the new ordinance would not effect his subdivision. But if the parcels
have not been broken down he will have to follow the new subdivision
regulations requiring a 0.5 acre minimum.
Administrator Finger explained if the three lots are left as the total PUD they
are still single family units. If the lots are parcelled off as lots, they will
require the 0.5 acres.
Solicitor Lemire told Council if they are already parceled off they would be
grandfathered in. But since they are not, they will have to meet the new
requirements.
Administrator Finger explained if the intent is to parcel off the lots, it is
best to do it before the new ordinance is passed and in place.

May 15, 2002
Lawrence Bragga, Mayor
Village of Jefferson   
27 East Jefferson Street
Jefferson, Ohio 44047
RE: May 14, 2002 Letter
Dear Mayor Bragga:
   Recently, questions have been raised with respect to the reasons why the
Ashtabula County Board of Elections failed to place on the May 7, 2002 primary
election ballot for the electors of the Village of Jefferson, the question of
whether the Village would participate in the Northeast Ohio Public Energy
Council Gas Aggregation Program. A review of the events surrounding the passage
of the Ordinance, which would have allowed the issue to be submitted to the
electors, will offer an explanation and a solution.
   Pursuant to Rule 20 of the Rules of Council, all ordinances shall be
prepared by the Solicitor prior to being submitted to Council. Additionally, if
the ordinance is submitted by someone who is not a member of Council, the
ordinance shall be referred to the committee concerned with the subject matter
of the ordinance. These rules exist so that there is an orderly adoption of
ordinances, and so that the tasks that are required to be performed to enable
the ordinances to become effective take place. The Rules of Council also exist
so that safeguards are constantly in place to make sure that the tasks are
performed. When the rules of Council are not followed, the safeguards are
removed and order is abandoned.    
   Pursuant to Rule 25 of the Rules of Council, all ordinances shall have three
readings, unless an actual emergency exists pursuant to Rule 26. On January 7,
2002, Ordinance 02-O-2397 was submitted to Council by the Mayor. The ordinance
was not prepared by the solicitor, and was never referred to any Council
Committee. Ordinance 02-O-2397 was passed as an emergency measure on January 7,
2002.
   In addition to the extra work normally placed upon me at the beginning of
each fiscal year, during the first four months of 2002 the Clerk/Treasurer of
the Village of Jefferson had the unprecedented task of supplying the Lake
County Prosecutor’s office and lawyers for Mark Glotzbecker with voluminous
financial records in anticipation of a very lengthy jury trial.
   In addition to the aforementioned demands that were place upon me by the
job, I was out of town for ten days during this time period, to be with my
eighty year old father who was hospitalized out of state. As a result of the
additional demands that were placed upon me professionally and personally
during the time period in question, Ordinance 02-O-2397 was not filed by
February 21, 2002.
   Had the three reading requirement, pursuant to Council Rule 25, been
followed, I am positive that Ordinance 02-O-2397 would have been filed with the
Ashtabula County Board of Elections by February 21, 2002 because I would have
had a reminder. Also, if the Village Solicitor had prepared the ordinance as
passed by Council on January 7, 2002, based upon my working relationship with
Mr. Lemire, I am sure he would have timely followed up on the matter and it
would have been filed by me on time.
   By dispensing with the Rules of Council with respect to the unnecessarily
rapid passage of Ordinance 02-O-2397, the safeguards provided by the rules were
eliminated. As a result of all of the aforementioned circumstances, the NOPEC
issue was not placed upon the May 7, 2002 primary election ballot.
   Fortunately, it is not too late to submit the NOPEC issue to the electors.
Village Council still has plenty of time to pass similar legislation and the
matter may be submitted to the electors on November 5, 2002, with absolutely no
harm or cost to the public.
   By working together, Council, the Mayor, the Solicitor and the Clerk/
Treasurer can easily resolve this matter and continue to serve the public.
Respectfully Submitted,
Patricia A. Fisher Clerk Treasurer    
Councilperson Thompson commented that in the past he has made it clear that he
expects things to flow through committee before coming to Council for a vote.
The process was not needed in this case because they all knew of the issue due
to the Mayor being on the NOPEC Board.

Visitor’s Comments:
Janet Switzer of Solid Waste Management District spoke to Council about the new
Solid Waste Management Plan. She told Council there are only three differences
in the new plan compared to the old plan. Which Are:
1)   The new plan is a 5-year plan
2)   Geneva Land Fill has filed a permit to extend the life of their land fill
for 10 years
3)   Solid Waste Management District has set new rules and plan to enforce them
for the best interest of Solid Waste Management District.
Janet Switzer of Solid Waste Management told Council the budget was eight
hundred thousand dollars ($800,000), eighty thousand ($80,000) in grants and
the rest is fees collected from the land fills. She explained that Geneva Land
fill does take out of state solid waste and they are looking at alternative
plans in case Geneva Land Fill hits its capacity. She explained to Council that
there are ten other land fills in Ohio along with one out of state that the
County could use.
Councilperson Ward questioned the meetings regarding the Ashtabula County Solid
Waste Management District. He asked if the meeting could be set for a different
time than during the day.
Janet Switzer told Council that any person can submit comments in writing and
the Board will consider the written comments
Councilperson Ward asked if a copy of the new rules could be sent to Council
and Administration. He was told that the rules are sent to the Village office.
Administrator Finger said he would make sure each member of Council gets a
copy.
Janet Switzer told Council that publicly controlled land fills are getting
fewer and fewer because of the financial burden.
Administrator Finger told Council that the new rules will have no impact on the
Village. The rules are directed to govern the landfills and limit out of state
input.
Council discussed the time line that they have on passing the new ordinance
approving the Ashtabula County Solid Waste Management Rules. All agreed the
Ordinance must be passed prior to July 22, 2002. A revised Ordinance will be in
the next Council packet.
Mary Jane Norris of 253 Westview Drive told Council her concern and experience
of renting the Recreation Center Hall over the past two years. She said she has
two major complaints with renting the hall. One was she was not adequately
informed about what cooking and storage equipment was available at the Hall for
her party. Secondly, she would have to wait a month to get her security deposit
back. Norris told Council she would not recommend renting the hall to anyone.
Mayor told Council that one of the problems at the Rec. Center has been the
turnover of directors in the past several years.
Anita Perrotti, the new director of the Jefferson Community Recreation Center,
told Council she has revised the contract and it specifies what exactly is
available. She told Council she has been contacting people who have rented the
rooms prior to the revised contract and asked what was specifically needed.
Clerk-Treasurer Fisher told Council she reimburses the security deposit when
she receives a voucher from the Recreation Center. Fisher told Council she just
received vouchers for March and April.
Recreation Director Perrotti told Council the Center will work on a system to
expedite the reimbursement of security deposits.

payers money and we should watch the money being spent on luxurious items.
Administrator Finger told Council the Ordinance was to authorize him to
purchase a ¾ ton 4x4 pick-up truck. When the truck is bid out he will look over
the specs and not purchase unnecessary items. The Village is looking at
spending between 25-35 thousand on this truck. We will buy what will suit the
streets departments needs.
Motion by Maloney for the first reading of Resolution 02-R-2423
2nd
Roll: All yea, motion carried.
Resolution no.02-R-2423
A resolution authorizing participation in the ODOT Cooperative Purchasing
Program for sodium chloride (rock salt) for purchase.
Administrator Finger asked Council if the Village could change the process of
how Ordinances such as the Rock Salt were being done. Suggested having them on
going instead of yearly.
Councilperson Thompson told Council he would like to keep the process the same.
If the Ordinance is locked in for more than one year, the Village may not see
all the changes that come automatically every year.
Councilperson Maloney questioned if the Flexible Benefits Resolution was in the
Codified Ordinance Book.
Clerk-Treasurer Fisher told Council it should be in the Code Book updates, but
would check it out.

$3.00.
WWTP
Councilperson Baxley told council we are waiting for the Solicitor to draw up
the ordinance for sewer and refuse.

2nd

2nd
Roll: All yea, motion carried.
Council discussed the PUD Ordinance that went to the Planning Commission.
Council looked over Section 1258.05 B2A which would allow a bonus if all
garages were placed so that the doors do not face the street that abuts the
front yard.
Councilman Ward told Council that the Planning Commission has approved the
Ordinance. The Ordinance went to Building and Lands Committee to be scheduled
for a public meeting.
Solicitor Lemire explained to Council after the Ordinance comes from the
Planning Commission a Public Hearing can be set.
Council set a Public Hearing for July 15, 2002 at 8:00 pm, during regular
Council meeting. Discussion will be over the PUD Ordinance.

12, 2002 at 4:30 pm to discuss the sandwich signs. The intent of the Committee
is to come back to Council with a recommendation.

year for the Strawberry Festival held in June.

advertise the Strawberry Festival.
2nd
Roll: All yea, motion carried.
Finance
Council discussed the Income Tax Ordinance. The new Ordinance will allow the
Village to continue to have a 1% Village income tax in Jefferson. The Committee
asked the Solicitor to prepare a new ordinance for next Council meeting. With
the first reading being done on June 17, 2002, it will be passed in a timely
manner to continue the 1% Income Tax for the Village of Jefferson.

2nd
Roll: All yea, Motion carried
Old Business/New Business
Councilperson Stasny told Council that she has been reviewing the list of new
businesses in the Village. The Committee will give Council a recommendation
sometime in June.
Councilperson Maloney told Council Jane Wilson was going to do some sketches
for the new welcome signs for the Village of Jefferson.
Council discussed the road upkeep on Jefferson Eagleville Road. The road is
only half owned by the Village.
Council also discussed the speed limit West bound is 40 mph and East bound is
25 mph. Suggested that someone contact the County to get it on the agenda to
set a safe speed
Township trustee Martha Demshar told Council that the County can not set a
speed limit for the back roads. The state sets the speed.
Council discussed the House Bill 245 which would allow Municipalities the
option of combining the offices of the clerk and treasurer into an appointed
office of the Village Fiscal Officer instead of elected. Council agreed the
Village should look at all options, the pluses and minuses in changing the
position. The bill does have provision to opt to change the position back to
elected. Council set up a special committee for the House Bill 245.
Councilpersons Baxley, Herndon and Maloney volunteered to be on the Committee.
Councilperson Thompson told Council to look at their calendars for August. A
meeting is needed to discuss the personnel rules and regulations.
Motion by Maloney to adjourn the council meeting a 9:25 pm.
2nd
Roll: All yea, motion carried.

Visitors Comments:
Julie Stainfield, Director of the Jefferson Emergency Rescue District,
demonstrated the new automatic external defibulator to Council. Stainfield
explained to Council that the two defibulators were bought out of the equipment
fund in their general fund. The defibulator cost the JERD about $2,200.00 each.
The JERD is in the process of training coaches and staff at the Jefferson
Junior-Senior High School. In the future, if funds or grants are available, the
JERD would like to purchase defibulators for the Community Center and one for
the police cruiser that is on duty during each shift. Stainfield told Council
the JERD became a full time department in 2000. The response time per call is
four minutes. The new building the JERD built will be paid off in 2003. To run
the building 75% is paid by service billings and 25% is by tax dollars. The
JERD has a membership drive that residents can join by giving the JERD a $20.00
donation. The donation covers every household in the Village that is not
covered by insurance. This will prevent the residents from having out of pocket
expense. The average paramedic call is $375.00 plus $12.00 loader miles. JERD
has a 3 ½ mil levy. The levy provides the JERD with 271 thousand dollars per
year. The payroll cost average about 275 thousand dollars per year. The JERD
averages about 800 calls per year.
Richard Hummel of 113 East Cedar Street asked Council if he could speak to
Council under Utilities.
John Gaul of 772 South Spruce Street spoke to Council with the request made to
the Village by John and Diana Gaul, which was rejected by Administrator Finger.
The proposal made to the Village is the Village of Jefferson provides pipe,
couplers, elbows and T's and covers for the required catch basins to pipe the
right-of-way from the Gaul's driveway entrance to Mr. Anchor's driveway
entrance (approx. 400 feet). John and Diana Gaul and Robert Anchor will install
the pipe system, backfill, grade and seed at no cost to the Village.
John Gaul presented benefits of the agreement to the Village of Jefferson:
1)   Cost savings for the Village of $1,200 to $2,200 for installation
2)   Ongoing cost avoidance payback for ditch maintenance of $500 per cleaning
forever
3)   Creation of a safe right-of-way, in light of the hazardous condition of
the street alignment
4)   Solution of a decade long drainage problem
5)   No burden on the work backlog of Village crews and equipment
6)   Retention of aesthetic value on the Village right-of-way
7)   Retention of trees - aesthetic value
John Gaul urged the Village Council to direct Administrator Finger to provide
necessary materials to complete the project.
Council discussed the issue at great length. The Village's past practice has
always been a resident would pay for the piping and the Village would install
the piping and cover it up and plant grass seed.
Council agreed that the Village should be consistent with what has been done in
the past.

Councilperson Thompson discussed with Council Adelphia and the filing of
Chapter 11 bankruptcy. Adelphia Cable pays the Village a franchise fee of 3%
from the cable rate charged to the Jefferson customers. Recent revelations have
brought questions as to the company's accounting practices. Has Adelphia paid
all it owes the Village? The Village has received $42,000 since 1999. The fact
that Adelphia locally has given different rates between cities, the Village
should do something. Thompson told Council the Village should look for
competitive services or an alternative supplier.
Solicitor Lemire told Council that Adelphia still owes Jefferson for franchise
fees from January 1 to June 25. Told Council the fees come to about $6,000
estimated on previous payments by Adelphia. Lemire told Council that the
Village could get an auditor to check Adelphia's books but that would be
costly.
Council agreed to look at the issue in a future meeting when it is known what
Adelphia Cable is considering in the future.
Mayor Bragga explained that NOPEC is looking at doing the same thing with cable
as they have done with electricity and gas, but it will take time.
Richard Hummel of 113 E. Cedar St. spoke to council stating that what Ed
Williams of Adelphia Cable stated, should be taken with a grain of salt.
Mayor Bragga told Council that electric rates will be dropping soon. At a
meeting with the Northeast Ohio Public Energy Council, he was told Green
Mountain will be dropping two percent with an additional one percent next year.
Local business will also receive a four percent discount with local government
groups receiving a six percent discount.
Bragga also explained that Interstate Gas Supply has guaranteed a five percent
savings off the gas rates if voters approve joining NOPEC for gas aggregation.
The gas aggregation issue was not on the ballot in May because of a clerical
error. But a Resolution will be brought to Council to approve it for the
November ballot. If the voters approve the gas aggregation, it will take weeks
to months for IGS to apply the five percent discount. The discount will not
apply until the winter months, most likely, if the NOPEC gas aggregation is
passed in November The Contract for IGS will be for two years. NOPEC has agreed
all future contracts will be guaranteed for two years so customers can plan
ahead.

Safety
Councilman Thompson discussed information regarding the K-9 contract with its
handler Patrolman Terry. The contract for the K-9 handler was for five years.
Patrolman Terry only completed two years of the contract. In the contract, the
K-9 handler will have to reimburse the Village of Jefferson $3,600. Solicitor
Lemire told Council the contract is with Patrolman Terry. Mr. Terry would be
the one paying the Village, where he gets the money is not the issue.
The Village received a donation of $10,000 from the Veterans group. The
Veterans group was disappointed in loosing the K-9 unit. Councilperson Maloney
suggested the money received from Patrolman Terry for the buy-out of his
contract be given back to the Veterans group.
Council agreed that the K-9 unit was expensive and spent about $14,547.15 for
cost of the dog, training, travel, veterinarian bills and modifications to
police cruiser.
Mayor Bragga told Council the Clerk-Treasurer brought it to his attention that
Patrolman Terry asked for his $550.00 for the care of the K-9 being housed at
the handler’s home. The compensation for the K-9 is paid on the anniversary
date of service for the next year. Patrolman Terry was not compensated. Council
agreed that if the opportunity arises again for a K-9, the Village would seek a
new dog for the Jefferson Police Department.
Councilperson Ward questioned if one of the new cruisers was being equipped for
a K-9.
Mayor Bragga told Council there was a new cruiser on order for K-9 use. When
Patrolman Terry resigned, the order was changed from a K-9 unit to a regular
unit.

PUD Public Hearing
Mayor Bragga explained to Council the public hearing has determined the Village
of Jefferson’s Zoning Code needs to be amended with rules and regulations for
the Planned Unit Development (PUD).
Council discussed at great length the PUD Ordinance, addressing questions and
concerns.
Councilperson Thompson questioned the 100-year flood plan.
Councilperson Baxley told Council that there is a flood every one hundred years
and you would have to have flood insurance. Councilperson Baxley told Council
she had concerns with the density and definitions of private space and open
space. With the density, you can have up to four units per acre unless you do
certain things that give you more. Not included in the gross density
calculations are flood plains, easements, and water excess of an acre, and 18%
for the streets right of ways. Also, open space is 25% of the gross acreage.
The main concern is if a potential PUD comes to the Village with five acres,
just of the hand, they could get twenty units. One unit on 2 ½ then you could
get 19 units plus on the remaining acres, you will be getting a high density on
one part of the land that is still a portion of the PUD, but is private open
space. How should this be included in the density definition?
Councilperson Ward told Council the consultant told the Committee why the
people have a PUD in their zoning is so a large piece of land which could be
used for various reasons, such as multi-family, schools or commercial The PUD
for Jefferson was set up to have the option for people to live creative in a
small community. The goal that the Village wants to achieve is written in the
Ordinance.
Councilperson Ward told Council he felt confident that the Village is going in
the right direction such as the Jefferson Geriatric Lot, one piece of land.
Administrator Finger explained that density is the entire parcel of land and
total number of units you can put in the parcel. Open space looks at leaving
out private land from the open space. You must have 25% of open space on the
areas that are private, common open space or public open space. It really
depends on how it is worded in the covenant whether they are private.
Councilperson Baxley questioned if the open spaces are considered private they
are included in the open density calculation but not included in the open space
calculation. Expressed concern, also, that a working document can be stretched
and twisted to interpret it different ways.
Administrator Finger stated to Council, a developer brings a plan to the Zoning
Inspector. The Zoning Inspector will make sure all items on the plan are in
place to be viewed by the Planning Commission. Planning Commission looks at the
plan, then makes a recommendation back to Council. Council still has the final
approval of everything that goes on with the developer’s plan. The Ordinance
sets up the guidelines.
Councilperson Baxley stated to Council she wanted private open space added to
open space in the definition.
Administrator Finger stated to Council whether you add it to Section A or
exclude it from Section B you still set the same end result. Private land can
not be considered open space.
Mayor Bragga told Council he understood that private open space is not
included. Reason being, private lots will be included in the language because
lot owner, so close to a PUD, need to sit in on the owners group. Private open
space is not included in the calculation in respect to density.
Councilperson Baxley said, “that in the discussion there are already two
different interpretations with this body. That is my main concern.”
Mayor Bragga stated that the Zoning Inspector’s interpretation is what counts.
Councilperson Baxley told Council that she feels any private open space should
be excluded from the density.
Mayor Bragga told Council that this is what the public hearing is for and the
Solicitor and Village Administrator (Zoning Inspector) will look over the
issues. Then it will come back to Council.
Solicitor Lemire told Council that if Council chooses to vote on something else
other than what was recommended by the Planning Commission you must have five
votes to adopt something else.
Motion by Maloney to close the Public Hearing and return to the regular Council
meeting
2nd
Roll:    All yea, motion carried.

protect the Village such as, site plans, inspections; and the Village Zoning
Administrator shall enforce the code throughout the construction of the PUD.
Solicitor Lemire reminded Council that what the Planning Commission has
recommended, you must have a majority vote to adopt which is four votes. To
change what the Planning Commission has recommended you must have five votes.

Visitors Comments
Tim Leehan of 139 North Spruce Street thanked Council for applying MC70 on his
road. Leehan also spoke to Council regarding the elected or appointed issue of
the Village Clerk-Treasurer’s position. Told Council if the position is
appointed down the road – he expressed that he liked his direct democracy and
the voter right to choose who is elected to the position. The village needs the
checks and balances and a system of internal control. An appointed employee
could be swayed or become a scapegoat when things go wrong. Told Council that
he strongly believes the Village should keep the Clerk-Treasurer’s position
elected.
John Kusar of 132 North Chestnut Street spoke to Council about the House Bill
245 changing the Clerk-Treasurer’s position from elected to appointed. Kusar
told Council that over the years he has written many letters to the editor and
never received much response. Told Council his letter regarding the Clerk-
Treasurer’s position has gotten the most response ever. Expressed to Council
that the residents have the right to vote and choose who they want in the
position. Stated that the Village should look to the future. Positions and the
people change but we still have a democracy. The check and balances need to
stay in place. Told Council that there is a mechanism in place. If the Clerk-
Treasurer, any member of Council or the Mayor is not performing the duties of
their office, then they can be voted out of the office. He said that if the
mater comes up later in the meeting, he would like to speak at that time.
Ed Flack of 384 North Spruce thanked Council for applying MC70 on their road.
Durward Newhart and Phil Curtis of the American Legion –
Phil Curtis told Council that he was quite upset with the dog leaving the
Village with his handler. The American Legion donated the money to the people
of the Village to obtain a K-9. Curtis stated to Council that, at meetings
prior to Patrolman Steve Terry obtaining the handler position, he told the
Legion he was going nowhere.
Durward Newhart expressed to Council the donation was given to the Village with
no strings attached, but they are very disappointed that Patrolman Terry left.
Mayor Bragga explained to Council that he couldn’t fault Terry for leaving for
a better job.
Patrolman Terry will have to repay the Village about $3,600; since he did not
complete the five-year contract he signed when he agreed to become Jefferson’s
K-9 handler. Council has the right to return the remaining money to the
American Legion if they desire to give it back.
Durward Newhart told Council that when Patrolman Terry pays the money to the
Village, if Council wished to give the money back, they should contact the
American Legion.
Richard Hummel of 113 E. Cedar Street asked Council if they had the power to
change the Clerk-Treasurer position from elected to appointed, without the vote
of the people. Mayor Bragga explained House Bill 245 was passed in February by
legislation. Village Councils in the State of Ohio have the right to take that
option. A committee was formed by the Jefferson Village Council. That committee
can bring back a recommendation to Council to change the position. The
Ordinance must pass by a 2/3 majority (4 of the 6 council members). The mayor
can not break a tie.
Councilperson Thompson told Council that if Council passes the Ordinance, the
citizens of the Village of Jefferson can take it to a referendum vote.
Richard Hummel asked Council to think deeply and keep the vote in the hands of
the people.

Finance
Councilperson Baxley told Council that she was notified that she should go to
the bank and sign a form so she would be able to sign checks for the Village in
the absence of the Clerk. Told Council that she felt, before any paperwork is
signed, an Ordinance or Resolution should be passed by Council authorizing
Councilperson Baxley to sign checks in the absence of the Clerk Treasurer.
Baxley explained to Council a motion has been passed, but she would feel more
comfortable with an Ordinance or Resolution authorizing her to delegate someone

Recreation
Administrator Finger told Council that the Recreation Center roof leaked during
the last severe rainstorm. The roof has been repaired many times. The last time
we repaired it, the Village thought it was fixed. The expenses that have
accrued fixing it and replacing the tiles have been costly. A meeting is being
set-up with the contractor that installed the rubber roof. The Village is going
to have to do repairs or replace the roof to prevent water from leaking in on
our building.
Anita Perrotti the director of the Jefferson Recreation Center told Council the
SOCC Board purchased a new piece of equipment for the Center. The Elliptical
Trainer is non-electrical. It is powered by the person. It is designed to help
people who have had hip replacements and knee surgery. With this machine, there
is less stress on the joints when working out. The Recreation Center can also
track the number of hours it has been used. At this time, the machine is being
used all hours of the day.

system since 1997. They say it is full cost accounting and has shown a net
operating profit. Told the Village that this is saving its residents dollars.

Visitors Comments:
Richard Hummel of 113 E. Cedar St. told Council he appreciated the hard work
the Village was doing with the sidewalks. Asked Council what effect would it
have on the Village with the County Commissioners moving forward with
purchasing the water.
Mayor Bragga told Council that the Village of Jefferson spent money in
litigation on purchasing it back from COWC. There did not seem to be a savings
for the Village to move forward with the litigation. Council at that time chose
to be pro active with COWC. A Water Advisory committee was set up. COWC has
been doing repairs and upgrades to water lines in the Village. The door is not
shut and only time will tell who will be the water supplier for the Village.
The County Commissioners have spent about 680,000 dollars in the battle over
the water company with legal and consulting fees. The Villages franchise
agreement is up in 2007.
Department Reports
Administrators Report
The following is the Village Administrator's Report for the period ending
August 16, 2002:
   Service Dept.:
·   Work on the final sidewalk replacement sections for 2002 commenced Monday
August 19th. These are North side of E. Erie from S. Market 600 feet East and
the North side of the intersection of West Jefferson and Elm Street.
·   My recommendation for acceptance of paving bids for 2002 is in the packet.
·   Bid summary for Rolland’s truck replacement is included and low enough to
not require Council approval.
·   The budget calls for an expenditure of $10,000 for street crack sealing.
After reviewing the streets with Earl Koontz VP of Russell Standard Corp he has
agreed with me that we would be wasting money. His recommendation is to chip
and seal thereby extending the pavement life a minimum of three years.
Therefore I am recommending we chip and seal the following streets: South Elm,
North Elm, West Ashtabula and Maplewood for less than $10,000.
 
   Recreation/Community Center :
·   The rubber roof was inspected and several repairs were completed.
·   A major source of water leaking into the building proved to be from the air
conditioning units on the roof. The drainpipes in the units were totally rusted
shut, which allowed water to leak on the ductwork and drip to the ceiling in
numerous places.
·   The roof will be further evaluated to assure there are no more leaks.
·   I ask Council to approve Anita’s training request for McCormick Place in
Chicago.
 
   Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Initial Engineering work commenced Monday August 19 to clean and videotape
North Chestnut Street as part of the slip-lining project.
·   EQ holding tank cleaning was completed.
·   The Master Sewer Plan is in progress with Burgess and Niple. We had to
switch the survey work from Westfall to the Burgess & Niple crew.
·   EPA will do an inspection in September.
·   Various repairs continue as needed.
   Other:
·   New Utility Billing, Tax, Payroll, Financial and Cash handling software
installation were completed. All computers and the network are fully
functional. The training and implementation plan is included for your
information.
·   The staff made a collective decision to manually enter their data rather
than risk a mechanical conversion. This has a potential savings of $16,000 for
Village of Jefferson.
·   Meeting conducted with Pam Hanover of Squire, Sanders, and Dempsey Law
Firm, July 17 at 9:00 AM, left Jerry and I questioning the value for current
projects. More to follow. 
·   Spent all day August 8, 2002 with Allen Siewert State Urban Forester. We
were able to evaluate only the trees on East Jefferson Street: Chestnut Street
to the RR tracks. This evolved into a pick his brain sort of meeting that will
require a complete write up to the forestry committee and subsequent submission
to Council.
·   Clerk/Treasurer and I plan to meet Tuesday, August 20, at 3:00 PM to review
the village Financial results Year – To – Date against the budget plan. We will
submit a new appropriation ordinance to cover recent grants and required new
fund accounts.
·   THESE CHANGES WILL NOT CHANGE THE VILLAGE BOTTOM LINE YEAR END DOLLAR
BUDGET:
·   Add revenue from a grant to a fund and then add expenditure to equal the
grant in a fund sub account.
·   Add new fund sub accounts with money moved from another sub account within
the same fund.
·   Increase dollars in sub accounts with dollars taken from another sub
account within the same fund.
·   These changes will be presented to Council at the next meeting with only a
few changes requiring Council action.
·   Make sure you sign the “welcome to Jefferson” certificates for new
businesses.

Building/Lands
Motion by Ward for the third reading of Ordinance 02-O-2433
2nd 
Discussion
Councilperson Baxley explained to Council that she still has come concerns with
the density definitions of private space and open space in the PUD ordinance.
She spoke with Julie Lindner about her concerns. Lindner stated that this PUD
Ordinance is an unusual PUD, but felt how it was written would be alright.
Baxley feels like the PUD Ordinance has a flaw in it. Section 1260.05 should
have a number 6 which should say (After the above calculation for 1-5 have been
determined, for lots larger in size than the majority of the units within the
development, density shall be calculated at two (2) units per acre. Baxley
referred back to her memo, the density issue was allowing 6 maximum units per
acre. Without the correct verbiage the document can be exploited to allow for
density in some acres in excess of 12 units per acre. At the Building/Lands
committee meeting on March 1, 2002 under number 4, it states definition of
density. Four (4) units per acre is unacceptable for the Village. The Village
needs to maintain green space on the front, back and both sides of these
dwellings. Break between a certain number of dwellings, possibly 3 dwellings
then green space (example). She thanked Council for the consideration along
with expressing the importance for the community.
Administrator Finger stated that Julie Lindner sent an e-mail saying “Just so
there is no confusion, I felt I was very clear in that this type of limitation
wouldn’t work and should not be included in the PUD language.”
Councilperson Thompson stated that worked into the Ordinance is a plan review.
It must go to the Planning Commission and Council and at any time Planning
Commission and Council can object to the plans.
Administrator Finger told Council that the developer must go through Planning
Commission. There are checks and balances in place for the PUD Ordinance. The
ordinance provides rules for the best use of the land.
Mayor Bragga told Council that he felt that the PUD Ordinance was a workable
document.
Roll: Stasny yea, Thompson yea, Ward yea, Baxley nea, Herndon yea, Maloney yea.
Motion carried.

Councilperson Thompson requested the IRS penalty be removed from the Finance
for discussion because a reimbursement has been received by the Village.
Councilperson Thompson discussed the LEADERship Ashtabula class that the Clerk
Treasurer took without approval by Council. Stated that contrary to practice by
Council, Fisher never requested permission to attend the training nor did the
payment for the class appear on the list of bills. Thompson stated he had no
knowledge of any discussion nor any vote to approve the training.
Motion by Thompson to have Clerk Treasurer Fisher repay the Village $1,275.00
2nd 
Discussion
Councilperson Baxley told Council that Fisher did not have to obtain approval
from Council because she is an elected official. An employee is required to
come before Council and go through this process because they may have to take
time off from work. The Clerk Treasurer is not an employee. It is in her budget
for education. Baxley said in several past minutes, it notes that a
Councilperson mentioned attending a meeting but no vote was taken by Council.
Councilperson Ward told Council that he and Councilperson Thompson followed
proper procedure, the meeting minutes were reminders. They had already been
approved by Council. Ward stated the training never went through Council. How
do we know any of the bills we vote on are accurate.
Mayor Bragga told Council that prior to Terry Finger becoming Village
Administrator it was common practice for Council and Village officials to go
straight to Fisher for payment of bills without a purchase order or approval.
Bragga told Council that he felt the LEADERship class was beneficial to attend.
In the class you work with representatives from all over the county. Which
could be of help to the Village. Stated that the Village has participated in
the class. On Government Day a group came to the Village Office and were told
the type of Village Government the Village of Jefferson is and our growth and
economic development in the Village. Bragga stated that the Clerk – Treasurer
had discussed LEADERship Ashtabula County with him. He also stated that he goes
to a lot of meetings in Cleveland for NOPEC and he does not get approval from
Council. If Council does desire they can pass an ordinance or resolution
requiring approval to attend any meeting.
Clerk Treasurer Fisher told Council that she followed the precedence that was
used by Council and village officials in the past. Stated that the LEADERship
class cost $1,750.00 with $250,00 in a scholarship, $1,275.00 paid by the
Village and $225.00 plus travel and meals paid by the Clerk. Fisher told
Council that last year she received $720.00 in scholarships and whenever
training is attended by the clerk she tries to save the taxpayers as much money
as possible by sharing hotel rooms, rides and not turning in meals expenses.

Visitors Comments:
Citizen John Kusar of 132 North Chestnut Street spoke to Council about concerns
with the Clerk-Treasurer and training dealing with Leadership Ashtabula County,
and the old Administrator Pauley’s training. Kusar stated that Councilman
Thompson expressed he felt the clerk’s training was for personal gain and not
professional. Kusar brought up the issue – why would the Village not approve
the Clerk’s training, but still sent the old administrator to two trainings
(GASBE 34 and NOLA Internet) after the Village fired him.? He questioned the
spending of tax payers dollars when the Village would not gain anything from
the training received by the old administrator. The cost of the training also
included hotel, meals and mileage.
Councilman Thompson stated that in his contract those seminars were listed.
John Kusar questioned the double standard at the will of Council. He addressed
Councilperson Ward regarding Ward’s comment from last meeting stating he was
appalled at his not knowing about the training of the Clerk. Kusar wondered how
that could be, when the budget was approved in the amount $3,500 in 2000;
$2,500 in 2001and $3,500 in 2002. Also there was a carry over, all of the
budgeted money was not spent.
Councilperson Ward stated that this was the first expenditure that came out of
her budget that was not voted on before the Clerk-Treasured did the training.
John Kusar asked Councilperson Ward if he got approval to all the Seminars he
attended.
Councilperson Ward stated, absolutely.
John Kusar said that at last Council meeting it was stated that approval had
been given for a training session held in Brecksville. Kusar stated, he asked
for copies of the minutes prior and after the meeting in Brecksville and there
was no approval from Council to attend the meeting. Councilperson Ward told
John Kusar he did not look hard enough or it was not put in the minutes.
Councilperson Ward said everything Council has attended has been brought to the
Council floor.
John Kusar stated, it may have been brought to the Council floor, but was never
voted on. Kusar asked if there was a policy for going to seminars or training.
He asked if going on passed procedures was wrong, the Clerk-Treasurer did the
same as Council.
Mayor Bragga told Council since he has been Mayor he has tried to get everyone
– employee, Council seat or anyone- to bring the information to the Council
floor before the training is done. Is that necessary-“no.” Mayor Bragga told
Council there is no Ordinance regarding the request.
According to Statute, the Mayor has the authority to approve the request as
long as it is in the budget, and it does not have to go to Council. Once the
budget is approved, the person can go to the Mayor and the Mayor can say yes or
no to the request to attend a seminar or training session. The issue here is
that Council did not have knowledge nor did they approve the training. Bragga
did state that he felt the program was a good program.
John Kusar asked the solicitor, as an elected official, if it is in the Clerk-
Treasurer’s budget, does she need approval from Council for training.
Solicitor Lemire told Council that there is no Code Section for attendance or
training. There is a Section in the Ohio Revised Code Section 733.39 that
provides for conferences and conventions with the Mayor’s approval. You can
argue that this is not a conference. There is no Code provision for the
attendance of training.
John Kusar questioned the Solicitor, under the Ohio Revised Code did the Clerk-
Treasurer do anything wrong since she had the money approved in her budget.
Solicitor Lemire told Council that there was no clear statutory violation.
Mayor Bragga told Council it does not make any difference. This Council and
Mayor has chosen now for it to go to Council. Any elected board or body has the
right to determine their local policy. This body has chosen that the approval
must go to the Mayor and then to Council, if at all possible. If something
comes up and they come to the Mayor, the Mayor would then decide if the person
could attend the conference, then at a later time tell Council.
John Kusar quoted to Council the Ohio Revised Code Section 733.79, regarding
attendance to any conference or convention, a request shall be made in writing
to the Mayor. Did Council have their request in writing to the Mayor when they
attended their conferences?
Mayor Bragga stated, “no”, that he has tried to bring it to the Council for
approval. There have been no requests in writing for attendance to conferences.
Conferences will now be brought to this Council, and a vote will be in the
minutes.
John Kusar told Council that only once has there been any approval for a
Councilperson to attend a conference and that was July 16, 2001 with a motion
coming from Councilperson Finger.
John Kusar stated that he went farther back in the minutes and there has been
no approval from Council for a Councilperson to attend a conference.
Mayor Bragga stated that there has been no approval, probably, because Council
has chosen not to attend any conferences.
John Kusar questioned that Council does not seem to follow any policy, but they
want to hold the Clerk-Treasurer responsible.
Mayor Bragga stated that since he became Mayor, Council has followed the
policy. This elected body has the right to chose.
Councilperson Maloney told Council that the last time any Councilperson
attended a conference it was voted on by Council. The motion was last July 16,
2001, which Councilperson Finger made a motion to allow anyone on Council
interested to attend the seminar.
Councilperson Baxley told Council that Councilperson Thompson just attended a
conference and there was no motion from Council. He just brought it to
Council’s attention. In the Statute, the request can be written or oral. I
think you would have to be brain dead for the whole year to not know that the
Clerk-Treasurer was attending the Ashtabula County Leadership classes. There
was pre-knowledge of the class. Therefore, to let her get into the class and
graduate and not bringing it up before this, seems ignorant. Reading articles
in the paper about other public officials and entities payng for the classes
for their people is embarrassing to the Village.
Councilperson Maloney told Council what was upsetting to Council was that a
bill was paid without Council’s knowledge. Bills are suppose to go though
Council.
John Kusar asked if the Village only writes checks every two weeks.
Clerk-Treasurer Fisher told Council that prior to every Council meeting she
gives Council a list of bills for that period; but stated that she writes
checks everyday, depending when a check is needed. Fisher asked the Solicitor
if there was a section in the Ohio Revised Code that requires Council’s
approval before payment.
Solicitor Lemire stated to Council that municipal law has a lot of gray areas.
There is no statute that clearly states that Council must approve the bills
prior to payment. There is a statute that says the Treasurer must pay the bills
and it states that Council can pass a resolution requiring Council approve the
payment of the bills. The Council does not have a resolution stating Council
must approve. In the Ohio Revised Code, the resolution does not state that it
is required; but it does state the Treasurer must pay the bill.
Clerk-Treasurer Fisher told Council that in past precedence, she has always
written checks in between meetings. Council can chose if they want to pass a
resolution stating all checks must go to Council prior to payment. We do not
have a policy or resolution and have just followed what was done in the past.
Councilperson Baxley stated these are all things after the fact. The Village is
now requiring purchase orders for everything. We are constantly putting things
in place that were not in place before. (NOTE: This was the auditor’s
recommendation following the 2000-2001 audit.)
Clerk-Treasurer Fisher told Council she is now listing the bills that are paid
between Council meetings.
Administrator Finger told Council that the whole purchasing process needs to go
to the Finance Committee and a policies and procedures recommendation presented
to Council.
Councilperson Ward told Council “the knowledge of these things going on is what
I appreciate. I did not know anything about the training. I am not in the
Village Hall everyday to know what is going on, I live in the Village”.
In the past when an employee wanted to attend a conference between Council
meetings, the Mayor gave approval and told Council at the next meeting.
Clerk-Treasurer Fisher told Council that she researched all the way back to
1997 and found the following:
·   In 1997 Councilperson Thompson attended the Ohio Municipal League
Conference. There was no approval in the minutes to attend the conference, no
purchase order or approval in the list of bills for a reimbursement.
·   In 1998, Councilperson Aho attended the Ohio Municipal League Conference.
There was no approval in the minutes to attend the conference, no purchase
order, but there was approval in the list of bills April 6, 1998 for the
reimbursement.
·   In 1999, Councilperson Thompson attended the Ohio Municipal League
Conference. There was no approval in the minutes to attend the conference, no
purchase order or approval of the reimbursement.
·   There was a mention in the minutes of the Growth Partnership Dinner in the
Council meeting minutes of August 16, 1999, but no approval or purchase order.
·   In 2000, Councilperson Thompson attended the Ohio Municipal League
Conference. There was no approval in the minutes to attend the conference. The
conference was mentioned March 6, 2000 in the minutes. There were no purchase
orders or approval for the reimbursement.
·   In 2001, Councilpersons Thompson and Ward attended the Ohio Municipal
League Conference. There was a motion in the Council minutes on July 16, 2001
to attend the conference. A purchase order was made out and approval on the
list of bills on August 20, 2001 for payment to the conference, but no approval
for the reimbursement.
·   In 2002, Councilperson Thompson attended two Ohio Municipal League
Conferences. In the Council meeting minutes he mentioned attending the
conferences.
·   The conference in February 2002, there was no approval in the minutes to
attend the conference, no purchase order was issued or approval of the
reimbursement.
·   The August 2002 conference, there was a purchase order issued, no approval
in the minutes for payment, but the reimbursement was on the list of bills for
August 19, 2002.
The purchase order was issued by the Clerk-Treasurer for Councilperson
Thompson’s conference in August, because after the post audit in May, one of
the issues with our audit was the Village was not writing purchase orders for
everything. The Administrator and Clerk-Treasure have set-up policies for
purchase orders now. Fisher stated to Council that she did nothing wrong. Told
Council she has just followed past practice. She let people know that she was
attending the Leadership class. Even the old administrator knew she was
attending the class.
John Kusar said, if the Ohio Revised Section 733.79 cames up again during the
meeting, he would like to speak again,
Mayor Bragga told Council that the financial operation and financial managing
has been evolving since he came on board in 2000, and it has continued to be a
learning process. Something opens up everyday, and we learn from that to move
forward to better the Village in setting up procedures and policies.
Richard Hummel of 113 E. Cedar Street asked to speak during the Finance
Committee. Told Council that North Kingsville is also moving forward with the
appointment of the Clerk. Expressed that he was totally against the appointment
of the Clerk and will express his feelings until the Ordinance is passed.
