Visitors’ Comments
John Kusar of 132 North Chestnut Street Jefferson spoke to council regarding
that councilperson Thompson stated that the reason the old Administrator Pauley
was permitted to go to training sessions was because it was in his contract.
Kusar told council that he requested a copy of the contract and those seminar
requests were not in his contract.
Councilperson Thompson stated all I’m going to say on the matter is that the
training was approved before Mr. Pauley was terminated, and he had a right to
go to them.
John Kusar stated he did not understand why council couldn’t stop him from
going. It seems to me it’s a double standard. I pulled a copy of the minutes
off the internet. On page 7 talking with the issue with the Clerk-Treasurer –
Every person on Council voted these minutes were correct. In the minutes it
says “Solicitor Lemire told Council there was no clear statutory violation
regarding Leadership Ashtabula County training and the repayment of the
$1275.00. Kusar questioned Council and Administration. If the Solicitor has
stated there was no clear statutory violation, how can the Clerk-Treasurer be
expected to pay back the money for the training. If Council decides to proceed
forward legally and make the Clerk-Treasurer pay back the money, because the
Solicitor determined there was no violation, is the Village not legally
responsible to pay for her defense, if it goes to court?
Mayor Bragga stated he defers that question to the Solicitor.
Solicitor Lemire told council there is no movement to take the Clerk- Treasurer
to court. It’s up to the Council to decide what it wants to do if the Clerk-
Treasurer does not pay back the money. If Council chooses to take some kind of
action, when the issue comes up then it will be addressed. Also told council
that he was unsure of the personnel rules for the Village of Jefferson in
respect to paying legal fees for the Clerk-Treasurer.
John Kusar stated it seems a lot of things get put on the table then gets
forgotten.
It just doesn’t seem right to me.
Mayor Bragga questioned Kusar asking him to name one. You say a lot of things,
let’s name some, give me your list and we’ll work on it. I want it now. Give me
a list now.
John Kusar told Mayor he did not want to.
Councilperson Baxley asked if she could answer Some of John Kusar’s questions.
I don’t think this Council is prepared to take it further. There may be those
on Council that are wanting to take it further, and there are those on Council
who will fight them tooth and nail. So it’s kind of a moot point at this point;
and for the Clerk- Treasurer to think that she should pay anything back would
be an admission of guilt and calling herself a liar, which I truly believe her
words, her action have shown that it is not the case at all.
Councilperson Ward asked the Solicitor’s opinion, and requested it in writing
regarding the Ohio Revised Code section 733.79. I would like your written
comments on that. I want also to make sure that when this is in the minutes
next meeting, that it’s exactly clear that the solicitor said he is unsure
about the personnel rules and regulations, if the Village Council will have to
pay for the clerk’s defense.
Solicitor Lemire told Council that’s true. I’ll give you that memorandum.

Administrator’s Report
The following is the Village Administrator's Report for the period ending
September 15, 2002:
   Service Dept.:
·   Chip and Seal for: South Elm, North Elm, West Ashtabula and Maplewood and
several intersections was completed Thursday, September 12, 2002 without
incident.
·   Ditching work will resume this week September 16, 2002.
·   Pre–Construction meeting for paving Village of Jefferson streets was held
Friday Sept. 13. Date of paving not known as I type this report.
·   Elliott Avenue Paving at property owners request to be addressed at Council
Meeting and with a resolution of necessity from Finance Committee.
·   Drainage issues in Elliott Allotment are under review.
·   Crosswalk lines were painted on Willis and Uselma.
·   The issue of Caution Signs for Children in streets is still under
investigation to make sure we do not expose the Village to unexpected
additional liability.
 
   Recreation/Community Center :
·   New expanded hours for Rec. begin September 30 with the new Fall schedule
of classes.
·   Soccer program ended for the year. Follow up meeting with parents scheduled
Sept. 18.
·   Recreation Department seems to be developing a nice smooth running sound
these days.
 
   Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Repairs continue on valves and process equipment as needed.
·   The Burgess and Niple Master Sewer Plan work continues with a need for
additional survey work to verify accuracy of information.
   Other:
·   The revised 2002 Expense VS Budget Report is in your packet. This has all
fund sub account changes in place and all expenditures thru 9/12/02.
·   Your packet contains (For Your Information) the outline of our new
purchasing policy that is being implemented.
·   Request a motion to offer the Planning and Zoning Workshop to the Planning
Commission, Zoning Board of Appeals, Council, and Administration.

Councilperson Ward questioned if there could be a special number or line set up
at the Village Office that could ring during Council meetings. Reason being is
that if anyone needed to get in touch with Council if there was an emergency.
Councilperson Ward questioned if the Village could look into the cost of having
a court recorder do the minutes for the Village of Jefferson. Ward expressed
that he felt the minutes were unjust and one sided. The first nine pages of the
minutes dealt with the visitor’s comments and only a few pages dealt with the
regular Council meeting.
Mayor Bragga told Council that he would have the Administrator get prices for a
court recorder to come to a Council meeting. Told Council that there is a
democratic process. The Clerk can record the minutes and Council can choose to
amend them if they want, when they are approved at the next Council meeting.
Solicitor Lemire told Council that the Clerk-Treasurer is the record keeper for
the Village of Jefferson’s minutes. The Clerk may record what she feels is an
important issue and Council may not look at that issue as important. The
approval of the Council’s meeting minutes is the process when Council can voice
their opinion. Lemire also explained to Council at times do to issues that
minutes of the Council meeting may need to be more detailed. Solicitor Lemire
explained that a court recorder is too pricey and did not feel it to be
advantageous to pursue the issue.

Visitors’ Comments
John Wynn of 30 W. Walnut Street told Council he spoke with Attorney Lemire
today and told him that he had filed an application for rezoning his property.
The application went to The Planning Commission, which was approved for the
rezoning the property. Attorney Lemire told Council several years ago there was
another case that was challenged because it was not presented to the commission
with a resolution. Mr. Wynn asked Council if he had followed the correct
procedure. Councilperson Ward stated that Mr. Wynn had followed the correct
procedures to change the zoning status of the property. Councilperson Ward
stated an ordinance must be forwarded to the Planning Commission for approval.
The Planning Commission will then forward a recommendation to Council approving
the zoning change. Council submits the new Ordinance to The Planning Commission
with the zoning changes then waits for approval. Councilperson Ward stated that
he was the only Planning Commission member that voted no previously because he
wanted more time to think about it before he gave a yes answer. He understands
Mr. Wynn’s situation and that it is an isolated one since he does have
commercial use all around him. The Planning Commission does support it right
now, but in the past, have voted not to re-zone additional property into
residential areas.
John Kusar asked Council if he could reserve the right to talk under “The Legal
Requirement” memo requested by Councilperson Ward and was so noted by Mayor
Bragga.

Administrator’s Report
   The following is the Village Administrator's Report for the period ending
October 4, 2002:
   Service Dept.:
·   Leaf pickup starts this week and we will make one last pick up of brush
piles.
·   We will be sweeping loose stone from South Elm, North Elm, West Ashtabula,
Maplewood and several intersections this week as part of the original plan.
These roads will continue to be monitored for acceptability.
·   Ditching work is continuing with a requested workload taking us out into
2004.
·   Part I paving of Village of Jefferson streets is scheduled to commence week
of October 7th. This includes Washington Blvd. and parts of East Erie, South
Sycamore, North Market and Hillyer.
·   I request approval of the Part II paving bid submitted by Velotta Paving
Company $67,146.68.
·   I request approval of the resolution to proceed with Elliott Avenue Paving.
·   Drainage issues in Elliott Allotment were observed by Roland and me during
a heavy rainstorm. The problems are in the nuisance category and on private
property. They will be addressed as time permits.
·   Consumer Ohio Water Company will be adding two new 12 inch waterlines in
the village as part of our ongoing waterline improvement plan. One line will be
added to Popular Street between the North Fairgrounds entrance and West
Jefferson Street. The second will be on Sycamore Street between East Jefferson
Street and East Erie Street. Construction could begin within a week. (drawings
are available for viewing.)
Fire Dept.:
·   Safety Committee has the request authorizing me to accept the quote from
Findley Fire and issue a Purchase order for $18,585.00 part of what was
budgeted for equipment upgrades to meet ISO rate certification requirements.
  Recreation/Community Center :
·   Rec. committee has our request to approve the two new part time employees.
·   New expanded hours for Rec. are being utilized.
·   I attended the first Family night as a baby sitter for my grand kids. We
all enjoyed ourselves. I encourage anyone with access to kids to join in.
·   Gymnastics returns to Rec. with Anita instructing three classes the largest
one having 18 participants.
·   There are 32 kids in flag football, 25 people in line dancing (Come join
us, we need some more men.)
·   Overall usage of the Recreation Center continues to increase.
  Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   The Burgess and Niple Master Sewer Plan Phase One draft is included for
your review and if needed referral to committee.
·   Slip lining Bid packet was received, I will need a resolution authorizing
me to advertise for bids. Resolution should be ready for Council Monday.
·   
Other:
·   Request the names of anyone from council that will be attending the
Planning and Zoning Workshop approved by council last meeting. There are
Currently four of us planning on attending.
·   Planning Commission approved the request to rezone 30 West Walnut Street
from RS Residential to B1 Commercial. That request is being forwarded to
Council for request for ordinance.
·   I Request approval to attend two conferences: State and Federal Personnel
Laws in Ohio, November 6 & 7, (Cost $405.00) and Ohio Purchasing and Record

Committee Reports
Utilities
Administrator Finger told Council with his visit to The Conneaut Telephone Co.,
he learned that The Conneaut Telephone Co. is able to provide cable, data, and
phone service all on one line. Explained The Village Of Jefferson could have
Conneaut Cable TV which would come from one fiber optic line for all services
from Conneaut to Jefferson. The Village Of Jefferson would have to set up a
main building in Jefferson to handle the distribution, programming, etc.
Administrator Finger told Council that he and the Mayor are planning to set up
a meeting with the City Of Wadsworth to look at how they run a government
operated cable site.
Mayor Bragga told Council the opt-out legislation for the Village of Jefferson
would be on the November ballot. NOPEC has contracted a deal with IGS and are
guaranteeing 5% below the going rate. The rate is variable and will vary
depending on the quarter. If you vote for Jefferson to have opt-out gas you can
still opt into another program if you choose. For more information regarding
opt-out gas you may visit websites or call the NOPEC number for more
information.
Councilperson Maloney asked Mayor Bragga when Jefferson’s contract with
Adelphia Cable is up. Mayor Bragga told council he would look at the contract
and see how many more years the Village has with Adelphia Cable. Administrator
Finger told Council it was a 5-year contract and there were a few more years
left on it, but there was an escape clause in it. So if Jefferson did find a
cheaper cable provider they could possibly make a change.
WWTP
Administrator Finger updated Council with the Burgess & Niple Master Sewer Plan
Updated Draft told Council that the burden of all improvements for the Sanitary
Sewer does not fall upon the Village Of Jefferson. A developer can install a
line to suit their needs, which could be just an 8 in. line. We, the Village,
have to see what size is actually needed to service the area for future plans.
For example, if all that’s required is an 8 in. line and the Village feels a
12-in. line would be better to service the area, the Village pays the
difference in the cost between the 8-in. line and the 12-in. line. We want to
have a plan in place and to look at the areas we are developing. We’ll want to
meet and go over a new map and plan future developments.
Administrator Finger told Council the total cost is approximately $255,000 for
the North Chestnut Sanitary Street slip lining, Jefferson’s portion is $102,000
and the Village will receive $153,000 from a grant. This is just an estimate.
When we receive the bids back, we will know the actual cost.

Mayor Bragga told Council included in their Council packet was a letter
regarding Violence Awareness Month. There will be a walk in support of it. Red
Ribbon week is October 23-31 and is sponsored by Ashtabula County Coalition and
Ohio Parents for a Drug Free Youth.
Right now we are working with Green Mountain Energy for production of energy
through NOPEC.

scheduled.
Councilperson Maloney stated that the Safety Center didn’t seem to be listed on
the Village property list. Clerk-Treasurer Fisher told council she would look
over the property deeds
Councilperson Baxley asked if something could be done for Veteran’s Day. Asked
if the Village could observe a moment of silence and have the Veteran’s
ceremony at the gazebo. Mayor Bragga told Councilperson Baxley to coordinate
the Veteran’s Day ceremony with the Jefferson Community Recreation Center
Director and make sure the police know the time so they can shut down the
intersection for a brief period.
In the packet was a letter from Solicitor Lemire to Councilperson Ward
regarding legal requirements pertaining to convention, conference, and seminar
attendance.
Councilperson Ward questioned page 3-third paragraph, where the Clerk-Treasurer
has taken the position that the Leadership Course is not a conference,
convention, or meeting and therefore the statue of rules does not apply.
Solicitor Lemire said there is some ambiguity there. Clerk-Treasurer Fisher’s
position is that Code 733.79 does not apply to her. We may disagree with that,
but that is her position. Most of us didn’t know that statue existed until a
couple of months ago. Councilperson Thompson asked what future protocol would
be for training? Solicitor Lemire said any request for future training would
need to be submitted in writing, the Mayor approves it, and Clerk-Treasurer
certifies funds are appropriate and available. This requirement applies to
municipal officers and to employees of The Village.
Councilperson Baxley stated after reading the last statement of the Auditor’s
opinion, it doesn’t clearly require the Clerk-Treasurer to make written
application or seek The Mayor’s approval.
Mayor Bragga told Council that his position is that all education, training,
clinics, workshops, etc. all have to be approved by everyone, The Clerk, Mayor,
Administration and Council.
John Kusar of 132 North Chestnut Street stated that the Solicitor says it
doesn’t clearly state in 733.79 that Clerk-Treasurer owes this money so how can
Village Council make
a motion for the Clerk Treasurer to pay back the money if there’s no legal
standing? John Kusar suggested that Council rescind the motion and from now on
have everything done with a purchase order so there can be a “checks &
balances”. That is what the taxpayers want to see, checks and balances. If this
goes to court, Solicitor Lemire said The Village would have to cover Clerk-
Treasures legal fees. John Kusar pointed out that this would cost taxpayers
more money.
Mayor Bragga stated he was not going to pursue the issue and if Council wanted
to rescind the motion it was up to them.
Motion by Baxley to rescind the motion that the Clerk Treasurer repays the
Leadership Ashtabula County money that the Village paid.
2nd
Discussion:
Councilperson Ward said he had no problem at all with rescinding that motion.
The problem is solved and he is very happy it took place in the public arena.
Roll:   Baxley Yea, Herndon Yea, Maloney Nea, Stasny Yea, Thompson Nea, Ward
Yea.
4 Yeas - 2 Neas, motion carried.

Administrator’s Report
The following is the Village Administrator's Report for the period ending
November 1, 2002:
   Service Dept.:
·   Brush pick up is completed for the year while leaf pickup will continue.
·   Elliott Avenue asphalt base coat (3 inches) is complete.
·   Elliott Avenue asphalt finish coats (2 coats @ 1.5 inches each) plus
Washington Blvd. and parts of East Erie, South Sycamore, North Market and
Hillyer will be completed next year as soon as reliable temperatures return.
·   Popular and South Sycamore new waterline installation is in progress with
little disruption to traffic.
·   Service trucks are ready for snow.
Fire Dept.:
·   ISO equipment is arriving and will be in service by November 15 prior to
the ISO re-inspect.
 
Recreation/Community Center :
·   The Halloween party October 26 was a great success with 207 children plus
adults attending.
·   Skate Park will be dismantled this week for winter storage and
rehabilitation of ramps.
·   Requests for quote to repair the North West corner of the building are in
process.
 
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   The Burgess and Niple Master Sewer Plan was reviewed and several changes
were requested before presentation to Council.
·    Bid opening for North Chestnut Street Sanitary sewer slip lining will be
November 8, 2002.
·   I would like a motion tonight to accept the low bid if terms are OK. If I
am going to recommend other than low bid I, will present the justification at
the November 18 Council meeting. In either case, at the 18th meeting I’ll
present the bid results summary.
 
Other:
·   Fall tree planting is in progress with 30 in the ground, 14 more planned
for the tree lawn, and eight new shrubs due at the Gazebo any day.
·   Large tree removal will commence and continue in Jan. & Feb. once the final
tree list is developed and approved.
·   Request a motion to approve temporary part time secretary expressly for
data entry to new financial software package.
Discussion:
Mayor Bragga asked Administrator Finger to comment on the tree situation in
Jefferson.
Administrator Finger told Council the State Forester visited Jefferson and told
him many of our mature trees are in bad shape. There are a lot that need to be
cut down. First priority will be given to those that are near areas of concern,
such as the Library, School, etc., where a pedestrian or building could be
harmed.
Councilperson Maloney told Council she felt the trees were not in as bad of
shape as the State Forester had said and the trees could come down gradually
over the next few years.
Mayor Bragg asked Council if some of the trees could be of value instead of a
cost for removal, maybe for purposes of lumber?
Administrator Finger explained coming down are trees with a high level of decay
in the trunk. They could be hollowed out, but typically trees from Villages
aren’t taken for lumber because they have had nails driven into them.
Councilperson Ward asked Council if the request for the motion to accept the
low bid “Under Wastewater Treatment Plant” followed the Ohio Revised Code and
the Village rules.
Solicitor Lemire told Council they would be authorizing the acceptance of the
lowest bid and saw no reason why that would be illegal or improper.
Police Chief ‘s Report
Mayor Bragga asked Police Chief Febel to give Council an update on Amber Alert
and Overtime.
Chief Febel told Council that the Village Of Jefferson joined a group of nine
separate Counties that set up the Amber Alert Program which stands for
“Americans Missing: Broadcast Emergency Response”. Explained to Council that
there is now a plan in effect that makes three phone calls when a child is
missing. The first phone call activates the Amber Alert and the next two-phone
calls fax information. The crime Committee will be training area Police
Departments next Thursday on The Amber Alert program. Secom is the emergency
communications system for Cuyahoga County. The counties participating in this
program are Ashtabula, Erie, Cuyahoga, Geauga, Huron, Lake, Lorain, Medina, and
Summit. Chief Febel told Council a copy of the Amendment to the Missing
Juvenile Report was also in their Council packets. Told Council the Federal
Government is putting monies together to get billboards on the side of freeways
to be used in the event of an Amber Alert.
Mayor Bragga expressed thanks to Police Chief Febel, Councilpersons Ward, and
Maloney for all their hard work in getting The Amber Alert started in our
Community. Councilperson Maloney told Council that she had the opportunity to
see an Amber Alert broadcast on television when there was a child reported
missing from Maple Heights. The child was found thanks to The Amber Alert being
broadcast every 15 minutes for an hour and a half.
Police Chief Febel and Mayor Bragga discussed overtime in the police
department. Included in the Council packets was a month-end report of all
overtime for the Police Department to review.
Police Chief Febel told Council Trick or Treat went well with the exception of
traffic on Susan Drive.
Clerk-Treasurer’s Report
Clerk-Treasurer Fisher told council September’s month-end report is in their
packet.
Clerk-Treasurer Fisher stated that the conversion is coming along despite a few
glitches that are being worked out. The target to go live is set for December
9, 2002.

located South of the football field behind the stadium. This agreement is a
five-year contract with the understanding that either party may cancel provided
one-year notice is given in writing.
Councilperson Ward questioned where parking would be for these fields?
Community Center Director, Anita Perrotti told Council there would be a fence
installed next to the cage and parking will be permitted along the fence along
with the regular parking available when school is not in session.
Councilperson Ward suggested listing the name of the School Board President on
the agreement. Mayor Bragga asked Council if they still wanted to pass the
motion to accept the agreement pending Solicitor Lemire’s review of the
document.
Councilperson Maloney questioned the impact on the Recreation Center’s use of
the field and their soccer programs if the school decided to start their own?
Mayor Bragga told Council if the school started their own soccer program it
would probably be a different age group and time when the Community Center is
running their program.
Community Center Director, Anita Perrotti told Council the Centers programs run
in the summer and the school program runs in the fall. The School program only
consists of Junior High and Senior High School students. The Community Center
would only lose about 10-15 students based on the numbers from last year, but
would be getting new 3-5 year olds. Overall affects would be minimal.
Councilperson Herndon withdrew her motion
Councilperson Maloney withdrew her second
Councilperson Herndon suggests keeping the agreement for the Gym and Tennis
Court use on the agenda until Solicitor Lemire reviews it as well.
Councilperson Ward said he would like to see the tennis court section removed
from the agreement because he thought there was an Ordinance in place for the
tennis courts.
Administrator Finger told Council that there was never an agreement between the
School and Village for the tennis courts.
Mayor Bragga suggested doing separate agreements for the tennis courts and gym.
Bragga told Council that Council had approved funds to have the tennis courts
resurfaced 4-5 years ago and it was not done properly. Suggested to Council if
they decide to invest future funds into the tennis courts it needs to be
overseen and assured that it is done properly.
Community Center Director, Anita Perrotti, questioned having separate
agreements for the tennis courts and gym because it states that The Community
Center would be able to use them both without cost.
Councilperson Ward is in favor of keeping the tennis courts in the agreement
and if it is The Village’s responsibility to keep those grounds up then we
should.
Administrator Finger told Council the Community Center Director and he will
draft three different agreements, one for the soccer fields, tennis courts, and
the gyms. They will be forwardered to the Solicitor for review then they will
be submitted to Council again for approval.
Councilperson Ward suggested having a consultant survey the tennis courts if
Council ever decided to resurface them at a later date.
Safety
Councilperson Maloney informed Council that there would be a Safety meeting as
soon as the ISO inspection is finisher.
Motion by Maloney to stop traffic at 10:49am in the center of town for
Veteran’s Day by closing the intersections at Satin, Chestnut, and Walnut.
2nd
Roll: All yea, motion carried
Service – No Report
Utilities
Mayor Bragga told Council that the polls casted on November 5th showed support
of the Opt-Out Gas Legislation listed on the ballot.
Waste Water Treatment
Councilperson Baxley suggested to Council the motion for Council to accept the
lowest bid for North Chestnut Street Sanitary slip lining before the bids have
been opened goes against the Purchase Order procedures the Village has in
place. Baxley expressed that the motion to approve the North Chestnut Street
Sanitary bid should be delayed until next Council meeting. Council agreed and
the motion to approve the North Chestnut Street Sanitary slip-lining bid should
wait until next Council meeting.

Visitors’ Comments  
On behalf of the American Legion and The VFW Post, Dave Sawdey thanked the
following residents for making Veteran’s Day, November 11th a complete success:
Mayor Bragga, Village Administrator Terry Finger, The Jefferson Village Council
for approving the use of the Community Center for St. Thomas Aquinas School to
host a spaghetti dinner for the Veterans, Anita Perrotti for working on her day
off at the center, Police Chief Steve Febel and his officers for traffic
control which made the ceremony run smoothly.
Mayor Bragga thanked Council for closing the streets of Jefferson for a period
of time during the ceremony. It made it very dignified and peaceful.
Deward Newhart asked Mayor Bragga if he could move the reading of the letter
from St. Thomas Aquinas School up on the agenda because some of the visitors
would not be able to attend the entire Council Meeting, Mayor Bragga agreed.
Mayor Bragga read the letter from St. Thomas Aquinas School thanking the
Village of Jefferson for supporting the Veteran’s Day Celebration.
Councilperson Baxley told Council the Garden Club purchased the wreath for the
Veterans Day Celebration and was glad to see it was up.
Mr. Hummel commented on the enjoyable time he had at the book sale last Friday.
He met some of the finest people and is proud to live in this town.

Administrator’s Report
The following is the Village Administrator's Report for the period ending
November 15, 2002:
Service Department:
·   Leaf pick will continue as needed
·   Popular and South Sycamore new waterline installation are complete except
for cover restoration.
·   Service trucks are scheduled for winterization in prep for snow.
Fire Department :
·   ISO equipment is arriving and will be in service prior to the ISO re-
inspect
Recreation/ Community Center:
·   Skate Park has been dismantled for winter storage and rehabilitation of
ramps.
·   Programs and rentals continue to increase.
·   Anita has successfully completed her probationary period and I recommend
her to permanent status.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   The Burgess and Niple Master Sewer Plan was presented to Wastewater
Committee Chairman for planned review.
·   Bid results for North Chestnut Street Sanitary sewer slip lining are in the
packets and I request approval to proceed.
·   Maintenance and repairs continue at high level.
Other:
·   Fall Tree planting will be completed this week.
·   Large tree removal will commence and continue in Jan. & Feb. once the final
tree list is developed and approved.
·   Jerry’s review of the Village solicitation Ordinance is included for your
information.
·   Medical insurance rate increases and a recommendation to change provider
network to Emerald Health network is included in finance.

snow plowing starts.

House regarding the Ohio Municipal League Task Force Senate Bill 261. Mayor

opposition on Senate Bill 261, he would have the letter faxed to the Committee
so Council would be placed on the list as a Community that is in opposition of
Senate Bill 261.
Motion by Baxley for Administrator Finger to draft a letter of opposition to
Senate Bill 261 to be faxed on November 19, 2002.
2nd

Mayor Bragga told Council they should have a new OML update regarding Bill 261
and House Bill 258 in their box tonight or tomorrow. House Bill 258 takes away
local government home rule with respect to resident’s requirements for people
such as Village Administrator, City Manager, Chief of Police, Fire, etc. A copy
of Bill 258 was included in Council’s packet. There was Legislation in attempt
to pass Bill 258 a few years ago but it failed. Mayor Bragga urged Council to
watch how local Representatives vote on this bill.
Councilperson Maloney feels it would be a shame to have all of the Villages
taxes taken over because of this bill after having taken almost five years to
get things straightened out. It would be difficult for Columbus to keep track
of it from there.
Clerk-Treasurer Fisher told Council at one time non-filers were about 700 and
right now they are down to 150 to 175. Income tax subpoenas are being done on
non-filer’s requiring all tax information be brought in for review.

Visitors’ Comments  
Erik Westfall of Westfall Surveying discussed with Council the Rush Creek Area
Project. Mr. Westfall told Council there would be some existing areas of the
Village Greens and dedicated roadways that will be affected. All of Ashtabula
Street will be affected. There may be some legal issues that need addressed on
whether it should be vacated or set aside. The 100 foot high bank by the creek
may be too much. Westfall told Council he will do the map of the 80 acres at
100 feet then submit it to Council for review. There may be some areas that
need dropped down to 50 feet. Told Council it would be best to do the project
in phases. Westfall told Council there are some legal issues on Pine Street
regarding the right of way, as well as Ashtabula Street coming in from Market
heading East to the railroad that need to be looked over as the project is
worked on.
Councilperson Baxley asked if the 100 feet was from the 500-year flood plain or
the 100-year? Westfall told council the mapping would be produced off the 1992
aero photography. Westfall told Council the mapping is sufficient for what they
will be doing and he has done extensive checking on the contours along with the
railroad right of ways. It is based on the vertical dam by the cemetery.
Westfall told Council that he was using the high bank of 920 and going 100 feet
above that.
Mayor Bragga told Council he thought the hundred feet might not be needed in
the light industrial area. Bragga told Council he also thought it would be
beneficial to have maps of the entire Rush Creek property in order to complete
the process.

Utilities  
Mayor Bragga told Council that he and the Administrator spent two full days
learning about the communications industry such as cable T.V., Internet, and
electronics services. A meeting that was held with Ashtabula and Geneva City
regarding the internet/cable industry and technology went well. They also spent
a day in Wadsworth touring the entire running of a Government run facility.
Bragga told Council the Administrator will prepare a report on their findings
and will give the Village a cost proposal. There are two ways Jefferson could
have cable locally.
1)   The Village could add the head end, which means The Village puts up
satellite dishes, towers, receives and processes the signals, and sends them
out on Village owned cable.
2)   The Village could buy the signal, which would alleviate the dishes,
towers, etc. but a distribution plan would still need to be in place.
Administrator Finger said all the pros and cons will need to be weighed and his
report will cover all of that for Council.
Mayor Bragga informed Council that Wadsworth has approximately 3,000 customers.
Time Warner was their primary provider for cable services. Bragga also told
Council Wadsworth has its own utility company, which helped the City alleviate
the costs when setting up their own cable service

County Auditors Office.

December 13, 2002:

holiday.
Fire Dept.:
·   Equipment is in for ISO re-certification. No date set for re-inspection.

vendors, most have already committed for another show in the spring. Santa
Clause had over 60 children visit with him; free program trials were well
attended. The Chinese auction appeared to be standing room only.
·   New carpet due December 16.
 
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   The changes and additions to the Master Sewer Plan as discussed in WW
Committee amount to $3,400.00. I am asking for a motion to modify the original
purchase order to increase it by this amount.
·   Maintenance and repairs for this year are complete. The repair and
maintenance to the diffusers has already created an improved efficiency (lower
blower motor speed = lower electricity consumption.)

facilities for Thursday December 19 beginning 9:00 AM.

Jefferson much more money than his wages have cost.

Mayor Bragga told Council that he and Chief Febel interviewed seven candidates
for the Village auxiliary of the seven he recommended that four be chosen to

Chris Villers, and Martin Hayes.

training and asked if he should be removed from the list until training was
complete.
Chief Febel told Council that Martin Hayes will be attending school under the
departments’ colors and once he is certified he will be able to be a road
qualified officer. Hayes will be able to assist and ride with full-time
officers or road qualified auxiliary. He could work special details at the high
school if needed. Chief Febel said there are three different sections of part-
time auxiliary Officer
1)   Auxiliary Officer with no arrest power
2)   Auxiliary Officer with arrest power and weapon possession
3)   Civilian Member of the Department.

Councilperson Baxley told Council she attended the Safety Committee meeting and
had since been online looking up information and reading how other
municipalities with small police departments have dealt with a non-aggressive
canine. Councilperson Baxley told Council she found six items that should be
considered:
1)   A need within the community and department
2)   Research and document the effectiveness of the canine unit
3)   Liability
4)   Expense, start up costs, and yearly budgets
5)   Training
6)   Public Relations
Councilperson Baxley told Council other informative points were city vs.
sleeping community vs. industrial community, and retirement provisions for a
dog. Councilperson Baxley noted that the police budget in 2002 is slightly less
than 2003 and realizes that was before the increased costs of health insurance,
Medicare, etc. Councilperson Baxley feels the financial aspect of hiring a
resource officer and getting a police dog have not been weighed completely.
Councilperson Baxley told Council that, after reading this article, she
realized the amount of time that was involved in being a police officer with a
canine. Baxley also stated there had been 47.5 hours of overtime in the last 2
weeks into the police department. Questioned how The Village could afford to
lose their main police officer for training and calls dealing with the canine.
Councilperson Baxley also pointed out that getting a police dog would be a very
physical process with training, etc. and suggested finding out if the
department would be up to the challenge before getting a dog. Councilperson
Baxley told Council that her son had asked her, “Why should The Village pay all
the costs pertaining to the resource officer for the whole school district?” He
felt the decision should be shared among all the schools. Councilperson Baxley
said if The Village gets a resource officer, it will put the tax burden on The
Village and not the school district. Baxley requested Council wait until
Councilperson Herndon returns to give her an opportunity to share her opinion
as well.
Mayor Bragga told Council that Councilperson Baxley had valid points and felt
that Council should research the program to see if it was a good idea for the
Community before asking The Chief to devote his time to it. Mayor Bragga said
that in his conversations with Kevin Turner, the school superintendent there
might be some Board of Education money available through grants to help defray
the costs of a resource officer. Mayor Bragga also pointed out that The Village
of Jefferson is the law enforcement agency of the two schools that would be
served by this resource officer both school are in the Village limits and the
school system would share expenses. Mayor Bragga reiterated that the idea was
proposed to Council for the purpose of research. Council would need to decide
if it were beneficial and if the issue should be pursued.
Councilperson Ward told Council the three items of discussion on the agenda
were at the request of the Committee and the Committee felt it would be
worthwhile for the Chief to investigate it further so a decision can be made.
Councilperson Ward suggested putting any questions in writing to Chief Febel so
he could respond to them.
Councilperson Ward told Council that the Village had received some money from a
civic group for the last police dog that was on board. The Safety Committee
worked very hard to cover all the bases with a contract and no one could
foresee the officer leaving and feels a good job was done.
Councilperson Wards thinks it is important to have a resource officer because
Jefferson’s schools are important to the community. With all the potential for
growth that Jefferson has, Ward told Councils he feels that Council should make
sure the community and school systems are taken care of. Stated he felt that
Chief Febel should look further into getting information regarding a resource
officer and a non-aggressive dog.
Councilperson Ward told Council that the Auxiliary Officers are paid part-time
wages and all their expenses are not covered. The Fire Department’s gear and
expenses are covered and they volunteer Fire Fighters. But the Village
auxiliary officers have to supply their own uniforms. There are eight Auxiliary
Officers now and with the new appointed four the Village should be able to
afford to pay for some of the uniform expense.
Motion by Maloney to authorize Chief Febel to investigate obtaining a non-
aggressive dog
2nd
Roll:   Baxley Nea, Maloney Yea, Stasny Yea, Thompson Yea, Ward Yea
4 Yeas – 1 Nea, motion carried.
Motion by Maloney to authorize Chief Febel to investigate grant monies for a
resource officer
2nd
Discussion:
Councilperson Stasney questioned if the school was interested in the resource
officer.
Mayor Bragga told Council in his conversations with the superintendent; it
seemed like a favorable thing and he thought the Village should look into it
further.
Councilperson Maloney told Council every school in Ashtabula County has a
resource officer. Jefferson is the only one that does not.
Roll:    Ward Yea, Baxley Nea, Maloney Yea, Stasny Yea, Thompson Yea
4 Yeas – 1 Nea, motion carried
Councilperson Ward thanked Council on behalf of the Safety Committee for
allowing Chief Febel to do his work.
Chief Febel told Council some information regarding the non-aggressive canine
and uniform allowance for the auxiliary officers. Febel told Council regarding
the dog issue; the Village had received $3,600.00 back from Appollo. Stated the
costs regarding the canine are. The cage will cost $1,400.00, door opener
$529.00, miscellaneous equipment $500.00, the vet has agreed to donating
services with the Village being responsible for medication, the maintenance
contract $550.00 a year, marking for the cruiser $100.00, window tint $250.00,
canine badge $45.00, the dog and training is $2500.00. The training period is a
three-week period for 200 hours the dog would be pre-trained before it came.
The dog would work on the following narcotics: Marijuana, Cocaine, Heroine,
Methamphetamines, and Ecstasy. They will also cover canine behavior, drug
safety, identification, search patterns, first-aide, public demonstrations,
legal seizure laws, and preparation for courtroom.
Chief Febel told Council regarding the auxiliary uniforms, a memo was sent to
Mayor Bragga. Febel told Council the he checked other agencies in the county
and found they were either issuing uniforms or giving a $200-$300 uniform
allowance to auxiliary officers. Chief Febel recommended that the Village issue
a pair of navy blue uniform pants, one long sleeve shirt, one short sleeve
shirt, and one tie. The officer be issued equipment and he be responsible for
maintaining it during his service to the department and is returned to the
department upon end of service. The cost would be $133.99 per officer. Items
the officer will be required to purchase are shoes, gun belt, jacket, hat, etc.
Chief Febel stated that the resource officer information for the grant had to
be entered in by both the Village and the school system. Both entities are
required to send information into the state for a grant. The Village is on a
waiting list to receive this information for the grant.
Councilperson Maloney said a letter was received from The Attorney General
thanking the Safety Committee for being a participant in the Northern Ohio
Amber Alert program as well as a letter from The Council Of Dynamic Ministries
Of The United Methodist Church. For Child Safety Days.

Jefferson Village Council
27 East Jefferson Street
Jefferson, Ohio 44047
Dear Members of Council
   I was unable to attend the Village Council Meeting this evening do to my
commitment as advisor to the Ski Club. But I would like to address a couple of
items on your agenda.
   First Issue that I would like to address is the of exploring a Village owned
cable and Internet service. I cannot phantom this Council wanting to spend
$15,000 just to explore an idea. Not to mention the cost involved if decided to
go forward with the idea. How long would it take to save the taxpayers money or
would we ever recoup the indivual investment? Then to think how much the
Village would run these services. Step back and take a look at the sewer
billing problems over the last few years. A better use of the money would be to
improve current services, or add a traffic light at Beech & Chestnut.

Department to have a K-9 officer. It was just 8 months ago when Steve Terry

Officials 
Mayor Bragga gave a State of The Village Address.
The year 2002 continued to be a year of attending to, adjusting and managing
the total operations and planned growth of the village. The year passed by very
rapidly with considerable support from many members of our community. There
were, of course, a few interesting challenges. The administration has continued
to promote a professional and business-like approach to the operations of the
village.
Terry Finger our village administrator has now completed over one year of
service with the village. He has managed to create a business approach to the
operations and management of our town and still maintain a proper measure of
caring and personal concern for our residents.
Our effort to give the public an opportunity to know what is happening in
village government continues to grow and more information becomes more
accessible. The village website, accessible through the Jefferson Chamber of
Commerce site, provides you the ability to view agendas, minutes, income tax
forms and information, recreation center information and various ordinances. We
are setting the pace for local governments in an attempt to provide information
and schedules to our constituents.
Our 2003 appropriations are close to being adopted; the good news is that we
will be continuing to operate in the black with a continuation of quality
service by all departments. I am sure you are all aware that our only long-term
debt continues to be the payment of the loan for necessary improvements and
upgrades to our wastewater treatment facility and the yearly bond payment for
the purchase and renovation of the recreation center.
The recent installation of new financial software for all accounting procedures
is complete and functioning. We are confident that all operations and
procedures will be more efficient and effective in the accounting and managing
of all the villages’ financial accounts.
2002 was a very busy year for the planning commission and council: the
completion of zoning text for planned unit developments (PUD) and the
annexations of several outstanding parcels were challenging and exciting. The
cooperative effort and annexation approval of the Nassief property will provide
an opportunity for light industrial development in central Ashtabula County.
The village is committed to assisting with extension of infrastructure to the
light industrial park. The East Beech Street development project will also
challenge the council to learn and be creative in the future improvements
needed to enhance the northeast portion of the village. That northeast portion
includes decisions regarding village owned property for deeded green-space
( park), residential space, light industrial area and the entire infrastructure
associated with those areas.
I have talked about the development of a truck route connecting route 307 with
route 167 for several years and we have pursued that idea, but with no
immediate conclusion, due primarily to the lack of federal, state and local
funds available for such a project. I am placing that idea in the file and
making improvements to the state route 46 through the village a priority,
especially emphasizing safety and engineering improvements to the route 46 and
route 307-north intersection. The goal is not a quick fix, but with the support
of council it could be resolved within a few years.
Maintenance and needed repairs to our wastewater treatment plant have been
occurring with regularity under administrator Finger. A complete engineering
study of our total waste water system is near completion, then, a plan will be
developed to address the projected future needs of the village.
Our approach to water will continue to be, watch and learn from the decisions
other entities are making in the area and proceed cautiously with proper
education and planning.
We plan to maintain our Water Advisory Committee in an effort communicate our
concerns to Consumers Ohio Water Service and to have them make improvements to
the many old and under-sized lines in the system.
Mr. Finger and I have invested many hours learning and investigating the
alternatives to our existing cable and high-speed Internet service. Our council
will be asked to make some decisions regarding the possible approaches to this
concern. We know the cost of service is expensive, but without existing
competition, the consumer has no real choice.
I plan to continue as the counties representative to the Northeast Ohio Public
Energy Council’s board of directors. This is currently the nation’s largest
aggregation for public utilities. The work and efforts of NOPEC have worked to
the financial advantage of the consumer. Future efforts of NOPEC look effective
as a public body working to keep a more level playing field in the utility area
and other related services.
I will encourage the safety committee and Fire Chief Wayman and his staff to
fact find and investigate possible solutions to future fire service needs to
our community. I commend the chief and department on their improvements and
approach to adjusting to ISO standards and making it possible to maintain great
ratings. 2003 needs to be a year of planning, identifying and meeting short and
long-range fire protection needs.
The safety committee and police chief Febel and his staff will be addressing
short and long-range department needs. They will be considering the possibility
of a K-9 for the department. They will also be communicating with school
officials regarding the feasibility of a school resource officer.
The recreation committee will continue to investigate the future recreational
needs of the community. I expect significant dialog to occur regarding
programs, parkland development and the future facility wants and needs.
I am asking that the buildings and lands committee review current ordinances
relating to cleanliness, up-keep and beautification of public and private
property and consider possible changes that will enhance the value and
condition of all property in our village.
We need to remember to celebrate the Bicentennial of the great state of OHIO
this year, 1803 to 2003.
Once again, I thank this council for your cooperation, communication, diligence
and support … my prayer continues to be that we work together in a spirit of
cooperation and honest “hard work” in a constant effort to make our village
safe and an even more wonderful place to live, work and raise a family. May God
richly bless this community and the people who are the community!

Administrator’s Report
The following is the Village Administrator's Report for the period ending
January 17, 2003:
   Service Dept.:
   Christmas trees will continue to be picked up each Monday in January as
weather permits.
   Again we must stress that the trees need to have stands, ornaments and bags
removed.
   Winter snow removal is in full swing and I would like to publicly
acknowledge the super job the street department does in keeping our streets,
sidewalks and the downtown business area clear.
   We received a complaint about not plowing sidewalks in a given area. We
investigated and found that the person was complaining about not plowing a
private sidewalk. Our Street Department does a great job clearing sidewalks but
as a reminder I have included our Code Section #660.05 that outlines that
property owners have a statutory duty regarding repair and cleanliness of
sidewalks, curbs, and gutters.
   Fire Dept.:
   ISO re-certification inspection took place January 13th and 14th but will
remain an open issue until fire hydrant flow rates can be rechecked in the
spring.
 Recreation/Community Center:
   There is a lot on the agenda to be covered by the committee.
   Recreation Long Range Planning Meeting notifications were sent Monday 1/13/
03 to 54 Community Leaders inviting them to join our brainstorming session.
 Wastewater Treatment Plant:
   Repairs to safety railings have been completed.
   I have approved Gary Licate‘s request to take his Class Three Waste Water
Operators exam and ask council to approve the motion coming from the Committee.
   North Sycamore Street Sewer Slip Lining will take place the week of January
27th. There will be two, one - day disruptions to businesses and residences on
North Chestnut Street. One day for those who have service between Wall Street
and Ashtabula Street, then another one day disruption between Ashtabula and RT
307/RT 167 intersection. One lane of traffic will be maintained with flaggers
but alternate routes are recommended when possible. Complete details will be
presented to effected property owners.
Other:
   Drawings for The PUD on East Beech Street have been reviewed. A
recommendation will be made to the Planning Commission as soon as all the
issues are resolved with the plans.
   Mayor and I met with COW management and were reassured that all the
commitments made to the Water Advisory Committee will continue to be given high
priority.

The following is the Village Administrator's Report for the period ending
January 31, 2003:
   Service Dept.:
   Winter work requirements continue as scheduled.
   Fire Dept.:
   Safety Committee met to work on long-range plans. 
 
Recreation/Community Center:
   Recreation Long Range Planning Meeting met February 27. Twenty-four active
participants had an excellent meeting.
   Tammy Spangler has completed her six-month probation period and we recommend
her for regular part time employment status.
   I recommend that Council approve Anita’s request to attend the Brownfield
training class. This is intended to aid in grant preparation for future
parkland development.
   Request to hold Jefferson days was forwarded to the Recreation Committee.
 Wastewater Treatment Plant:
   North Sycamore Street Sewer Slip Lining scheduled to take place the week of
January 27th was cancelled due to bad weather.
   Work is being scheduled to minimize disruptions to businesses and residences
on North Chestnut Street.
   Final written instructions will be presented to effected property owners as
soon as firm plans are set.
   Wastewater/Service/Utility Committee worked with me to recommend changes to
Sewer Service Fees and Rates. I ask for your support in passing this change.
   The Wastewater master plan is complete and available for review to all
interested parties. This report brings together in one place the data the
Village of Jefferson needs to be proactive to future growth.

   I will prepare copies and a written update for the safety committee for
review.

Administrator Finger explained to Council the Ordinance seemed to be
interpreted as the Village would have a license to raise the fees 3 ½ % a year
and it can not. The Administrator must review the finances of The Wastewater
Department and make a recommendation to the Wastewater Committee and bring
forth a recommendation in February on what the Administrator recommends the
fees should be for the next year this Ordinance represents that procedure.

Administrator’s Report
 
The following is the Village Administrator's Report for the period ending
February 14, 2003:
   Service Dept.:
   Winter work requirements continue as scheduled.
   I ask council to approve paying $15.00 each for four of us to attend the
Urban Forestry Conference.
   This is a necessity for the village to keep up with the newest trouble
areas, grants and opportunities in maintaining/improving our considerable
investment in our young Urban Forest.
   Fire Dept.:
   Nothing To Report. 
 
Recreation/Community Center:
   Recreation Long Range Planning Meeting will meet February 24th at the
Village Hall.
   Recreation Department has included monthly income report as requested by
Council.
   Little League contract needs a motion to approve.
   I have approved Anita’s request to attend the second grant writing training
session and ask council to also approve this request.
 Wastewater Treatment Plant:
   North Chestnut Street Sewer Slip Lining from Wall Street to Ashtabula Street
was completed February 8th and 9th with little disruption to businesses. I have
received no complaints only compliments that we were able to do the work during
the evening hours.
   North Chestnut Street Sewer Slip Lining from Ashtabula Street to RT #307 and
Beech Street is scheduled for Friday, February 14 commencing at 8:00 AM and
continuing until completed. The contractors assure me that no businesses will
have to shut down and private residents can run water and flush but should
restrict washing dishes and laundry Friday afternoon. All property owners have
been notified.
   Monday, Feb. 7, emergency repairs were needed to replace a valve on #2
aeration tank. The treatment plant had to be shut down for 24 hours and flow
diverted to holding tanks.
   The wastewater employees worked together and suggested a change in design to
add two additional valves. The addition of these valves allows the diversion
and redirection of flow to enable the plant to run at half treatment capacity.
   Due to excellent communications and cooperation among employees the repair
was well planned and executed. There were three tired employees after working
20 hours straight.
   We have already had to utilize the new valve configuration, as another valve
failed on Wednesday, February 12. We will replace this one on Tuesday, February
17, 2003.

Ordinance No 03-O-2467
An Ordinance amending sections 1030.15 distribution of collection fees, 1030.17
connection fees, and 1030.18 sewer rated of the codified Ordinances of the
Village of Jefferson to increase the proportion of sewer collection fees to be
allocated to the Sewer Improvement Fund and decrease the allocation to the
Waste Treatment Fund; to increase the Sewer connection fees; and increase sewer
rates.
Vernon Kirkenburg of 414 Washington Blvd. Asked Council if the Sewer Increase
was a one time increase or would it be done automatically at three 3% every
year. Questioned why the increase was taking place since the Village just had a
large sewer increase less than two years ago. Kirkenburg asked how the sewer
bills were calculated and asked if there was going to be also a increase in the
garbage rates. Expressed to Council that at this time it is not good to do a
lot of increases.
Vernon Kirkenburg of 414 Washington Blvd. Asked if Washington Blvd. was going
to be paved this summer. Asked if the road was going too ground and sloped
before being paved. Last time the road was paved it was not done correctly and
there was a 4-inch drop off from the Road.
Administrator Finger explained that the sewer increase was for the cost to keep
the plant running and operating. The sewer bills are calculated on the water
consumption. Any rate increases that are done at the Wastewater Treatment Plant
are done through Council, they must vote to do increases.
Administrator Finger told Kirkenburg that when the road is paved there would be
a slope of asphalt down to the driveway. The Village will butt up to the road
asphalt-to-asphalt or stone-to- stone. The engineers have looked over the road
and the road will be paved to their specs. There is a good base and it will be
used for the paving.
Buildings/Lands

on as well as The Village Greens Ordinance.
Councilperson Ward told Council that The Rush Creek Plat project was ready to
move forward. The Committee will meet then come back to Council with any
changes to the Plat. One major issue the Village must decide on is if they want
a 100 feet or 30 feet set back from the 920 Foot Contour Line of the High Bank.

Council discussed at great length the issues regarding the Tax Abatement for
Pickens’ s Plastic.
Councilperson Baxley brought some concerns to Council in regards that Pickens
Plastic has already started building the new addition before they requested the
Tax Abatement. Baxley shared with Council some issues what Tax Abatement has
done in Ohio what it is costing schools and revenue dollars to the Entities
involved.
Mayor Bragga discussed with Council the issue that the Village should look at
the big picture in regards to Tax Incentives for the future. Nassief has put in
their newly annexed property to the Village a Light Industrial Area. To have
business come to Jefferson Tax Abatement will be a piece of the picture.
Abatement does cost the school money but it will only last as long as the
Abatement is approved for. Council has the right to negotiate the percentage
and amount of years the Tax Abatement will be for.
Other concerns Council had with the application for the Enterprise Zone Tax
Incentive, the paperwork from the County Commissioner did not give the Village
14 days to look over the application. A response must be sent back to the
Commissioner by February 26, 2003.
Council agreed a letter must be sent to the County Commissioners stating that
no action shall be taken until the Jefferson Village Council has had time to
discuss the Abatement with the County Commissioners, Growth Partnership and all
other parties involved in the Tax Abatement.

Visitors’ Comments
Citizen - John Kusar of 132 North Chestnut Street Jefferson spoke to Council
with questions regarding the Pickens Plastic Tax Abatement. Asked Council how
they could vote for the Tax Abatement when the School Board is against the
Abatement. He also questioned Council how they could even consider the Tax
Abatement when the building was started before Pickens’s Plastic applied for
the Abatement. Kusar told Council that he found some information regarding
Pickens’s Plastic as being one of the biggest pollutants in Ohio.
Citizen – John Kusar question Council with a conflict of interest with the
Village Mayor and President Pro Temp Councilperson Thompson regarding any
involvement with the Pickens’s Plastic Tax Abatement because they are employed
with the Schools and the Abatement involves the School system. Kusar told
Council of an advisory opinion made on October 11, 1991which states any person
employed by the school system cannot be involved with Tax Abatement within the
School District.
Mayor Bragga told Council that, today, the Solicitor told him of the same
opinion. That he and Councilperson Thompson can not be involved with the
Special Council meeting concerning Tax Abatement or any other discussion
regarding the Abatement.
Solicitor Lemire told Council his opinion is any person employed by the Schools
should not vote, discuss or participate in any deliberations with the
Abatement.
Citizen – John Kusar told Council in the opinion there was a section stating
any person employed by the schools could not participate for up to a year after
they have resigned form the School position in anything regarding Abatement.
Mayor Bragga told Council that the Solicitor is going to look into the opinion
and come back to him with a decision. Bragga told Council that Council would
have to appoint a Councilperson tonight to run the Special Council Meeting on
March 13, 2003.

Discussion:
In Council packets was a letter from the NEC regarding their upcoming banquet
rental. The NEC requested the banquet rental be no charge with respect to the
agreement The Recreation Center has with the Jefferson Board of Education. The
agreement between the Village and the Board of Education has not yet been
signed. It states that the Board of Education can use the facilities for
“meetings” at no cost but does not address banquets.
Administrator Finger told Council that he and the Recreation Director discussed
the rental for the NEC and because there is an agreement in the process of
being signed. The NEC Banquet is an official sanctioned function by the School
District; the question is: What is defined as being a meeting? The agreement
states that the Recreation Center could use the School’s facilities provided
nothing was scheduled and vise versa. Administrator Finger told Council he made
the determination to allow the NEC to use the facility at no cost for their
banquet.
Councilperson Thompson explained to Council that during the NEC banquet, there
is a dinner and awards. However, there is a meeting, as well. They conduct
business and sometimes have the elections of officers and such. It was
suggested that the Administrator and Recreation Director speak with Mr. Locy,
the Athletic Director, regarding this issue.
Administrator Finger told Council he instructed the Recreation Director to
grant the rental request.
Councilperson Baxley told Council if the Village grants the request for the
NEC, at no cost, then others organizations with the School will request the
same.
Mayor Bragga suggested Council look over the contract with the Jefferson School
Board again to prevent any incidents happening like this again. Bragga also
asked Council to make a decision tonight regarding the issue so the Recreation
Director can give the School an answer.
Council discussed the issue and agreed, the wording of the contract needed to
be looked over more. Council asked the Administrator, Solicitor and Recreation
Director to get together and go over the contract again.
 
Councilperson Baxley expressed to Council that the contract has not yet been
signed.
NEC has paid for their banquet rentals at the Recreation Center, in the past,
and should pay for this one as well.
Administrator Finger told Council that the Village is working on cooperating
with the Board of Education and the School system.
Motion by Ward to support The Administrator’s decision to waive the fee for The
NEC banquet at The Recreation Center

Mayor Bragga welcomed visitors to Council and explained there was a new agenda
addition. Visitor’s comments have been added to the end of Council meeting as
well. You must step up to the microphone, give your name, and place of
residence in the Village. Mayor Bragga acknowledged that Gladys Bannister,
Florence Newcomb, Loma Shmurtz, and Larry Browning requested to speak regarding
the condition of Maplewood Drive.
Visitors Comments
Gladys Bannister of Maplewood Drive told Council the condition of Maplewood
Drive is now in worse condition than a year ago. There is loose dirt and stone
that’s been thrown back 3-4 feet from the snowplows. Now that the snow is
melted it is more noticeable. Bannister told Council she feels it was a mistake
to lay tar and stone and requested something be done to fix the road.
Larry Browning of 162 Maplewood Drive told Council there is a lot of loose
gravel and feels it is dangerous for the children bike riding on the street.
Browning requested that something be done about the condition of the road.
Mayor Bragga explained that in an attempt to extend the life of paved streets
in the Village it was recommended to the Administrator to chip and seal. This
was done to Maplewood Drive and Elm Street last summer. It was evident to
Council that after the road was chipped and sealed the residents of the Village
were not satisfied with that process.
Administrator Finger told Council that he lives on Elm and has the same problem
with a 3-foot wide strip of loose stone. Administrator Finger told Council that
the supplier from Pennsylvania was to come back and take a look at the
condition of the roads.
Mayor Bragga explained that the Village was trying to conserve tax dollars by
not having a consultant look at the street prior to the repairs. The Village
had retired County Engineer Smolen look at the roads.
Administrator Finger told Council that is was Smolen who made recommendation
because other areas in the County were using it.
Dan Gaul of Elm Street brought pictures of his driveway in for Council. He
asked Council if it was going to be cleaned up or was it the resident’s
responsibility to rake up the loose gravel.
Mayor Bragga told Council that he, Administrator Finger and Roland Ferguson,
the Streets foreman, would get together and discuss what could be done.
Councilperson Baxley said there was money set aside for paving. Asked Council
since the paving process of Maplewood and Elm was not correct would that put
these two streets back at the top of the list for repairs. Administrator Finger
said he would like Council to do a drive through on the streets and they could
get together to discuss a plan. Councilperson Baxley requested residents of
these streets be contacted when a plan is developed. Administrator Finger
stated it would be listed in the newspaper.

Mayor Bragga introduced Kerry McCarthy who represents NOPEC through SVA
Communication and Joel Heiser and opened the floor for questions.
Mr. McCarthy said the topics for discussion are the goals of operation,
funding, consumer participation, natural gas process, and the opt out option.
Councilperson Thompson asked if the residents will be notified by mail from
NOPEC. Mr. McCarthy stated that all eligible customers in the Village and
Ashtabula who are not currently with a natural gas supplier will be notified by
mail with a pre-notice and then the actual opt-out notice itself. This will
include the rates, the arrangements NOPEC has with its suppliers, and give the
customer the opportunity to opt-out free of charge in a postage paid card
within 21 days. The customers who do not opt out will be automatically enrolled
and start to receive their gas supply.
Councilperson Thompson asked for some examples of what the savings might be for
an average household. Kerry McCarthy said everyone’s usage level differs and
that is what determines your bill. He explained that the NOPEC IGS offers
residents to save 5% below what their charges would be if they were with
Dominio East Ohio or Columbia Gas. The savings offer is for 5 % below and is
called GTR which stands for gas to cost recovery. That is the price that the
utility will charge for gas supply and that price fluctuates every quarter. The
savings formula guarantees that no matter what happens in the gas market,
customers will always save 5% below what the utility is charging.
Councilperson Baxley asked if it were comparable to the other NOPEC options the
Village has because when you pay the transportation fee it ends up being more.
Mr. McCarthy said 1/3 of your bill is deregulated (open to competition) also
known as the generation charge, and 2/3 of your bill is all regulated charges
(not open to competition). Natural gas is similar, the difference is that the
gas supply portion of your bill is comprised of two thirds and the distribution
charge is one third. The transmission/distribution charges are fixed. The
excise tax is the only thing that changes and it is equivalent to a sales tax,
around 4 or 5 percent and varies by county. There will still be a 5% savings on
the GCR portion of the bill.
Kerry McCarthy thanked Mayor Bragga for helping all of Ohio in expanding their
options for utility choices for both gas and electricity. Kerry said it was a
privilege to be on the NOPEC Board of Directors with Mayor Bragga.
Mayor Bragga stated he had sent a letter of resignation to NOPEC. Mayor Bragga
said he had been on the board for two years and appreciates the work of NOPEC.

Visitors Comments
Citizen Ronald Cramer of 2557 South Denmark Road said he appreciates the
Recreation Center and the fact that it is also accessible to non-residents of
the Village. His concern is over the increase in membership fees and the
discrepancy in the percentage of savings for paying annually versus monthly
between residents and non-residence. (Residents have a 50% savings and non-
residents have a 33% savings.) He asked if a study had been made and if the
public had been advised of the increase.
Administrator Finger said there had been a study, which was broken down by
resident and non-resident. Administrator Finger said several letters were
received and the issues had been taken back to the committee and discussed
again. Where it is is where it stands. He said taking it back to committee
again might be a possibility. Councilperson Baxley said she sat in on that
committee meeting, and they distinctly saw the difference in the percentage of
savings. Justification is that residents of the Village pay property taxes as
well as income tax
Mayor Bragga said over $300,000 per year is spent to operate the Community
Center. The challenge given to the Recreation Director to re-coop more dollars
was to either cut programs/staff or to increase revenue. Mayor Bragga stated
that what is being done at the Recreation center is an attempt to balance and
increase the amount of dollars, while maintaining and/or increasing the amount
of services the Community Center provides.
Recreation Director Anita Perrotti, noted that a public meeting was held and
the issues were discussed on three separate occasion; and the topics of the
meetings were published in the paper.
Mayor Bragga stated that the Recreation Committee reviews all fees once a year
and that Mr. Cramer’s feedback will be taken into consideration
Mr. Cramer said he checked with Clerk-Treasurer Fisher and she stated The
Community Center receives $167,000 from The Village income tax, a one percent
income tax for operation, which is 50% of its budget according to the $300,000
figure that was given.
Mayor Bragga said he thought that was a total amount. Clerk-Treasurer Fisher
said they made transfers this year and will continue to throughout the year:
from the general fund $167, 000 total, and from the capital improvements fund
for the bond payment of $93,000.
Administrator Finger noted that’s almost $300,000 being transferred in, but
that money is not just income tax. Clerk Treasurer said 50% of income tax goes
into the general fund and 50% goes into the capital improvements fund.

   Discussion of enclosed EPA Public Notice and council’s direction to respond.
Mayor Bragga said the 10% payable by the Village for the Route 307 and 46 North
improvements may seem like a lot of money. However, that amount encompasses
more than just a traffic light. It encompasses widening lane changes,
decreasing the grade from 5% to 3% for visibility purposes, new sidewalks,
curbs, etc. Mayor Bragga expressed his appreciation for Administrator Finger's
work on the issue.
Administrator Finger and Mayor Bragga’s recommendation for the paving on
Ashtabula Street (in green on map), North Elm, South Elm, (in green on map),
Cedar Street, Maplewood would be, if Council approves, to pull the 2005 paving
forward with the 2003. Meaning, to do 2003 and 2005 at the same time even if it
means borrowing some money to accomplish that.
Mayor Bragga said waiting until 2005 to re-do those roads is not a good idea,
and to look at the financial situation to enable us to do those now. The amount
is $75,000 and was not calculated into the budget, so funds would have to be
generated for that expense or borrowing for it. This would put the resurfacing
schedule ahead. One possibility is to not budget any dollars for those expenses
in 2005, carry the debt, and pay it off then, in 2005. Mayor Bragga asked
Council to consider those ideas. Administrator Finger requested immediate
feedback, because specs are being written now and he would like to get bids in.
Councilperson Baxley asked how the Village was time-wise with receiving the
Block Grant, because it was senseless to pave it without the grant.
Administrator Finger said not according to the engineer, the paving could be
done and the ditching later.
Councilperson Thompson asked what the total dollar figure was. Administrator
Finger said $75,000 was budgeted for "2002" and $75,000 more is what's needed.
Motion by Maloney for Administrator Finger to prepare specs for street
improvements for the years 2003 and 2005 on the Village of Jefferson 2003-2008
resurfacing plan.
2nd
Councilperson Thompson asked if an ordinance was needed for the additional
$75,000 loan. Administrator Finger said yes.
All yea, motion carried.
Administrator Finger said the skate park is not up because no one has
registered. Mayor Bragga said they are skating, just in other places.
Administrator Finger said The Recreation committee would like them do be safe
and wear helmets, etc., but cannot force them to do it. Recreation Director
Perrotti stated there were 68 kids who skated last year and 68 letters were
sent out to let them know about it as well as in The Gazette Paper twice. Out
of 68 children, 7 liability waivers have been received.
Mayor Bragga said the logic in putting a skate park here was to keep the kids
in an area where they can skate. Councilperson Baxley said seven children have
paid to use and should be using it. If there are kids back there without a
waiver and fee's paid they are trespassing and there are laws for that. Council
thinks that if the equipment were out the kids would see it and come into
register. Councilperson Thompson suggested purchasing helmets for use. Clerk-
Treasurer Fisher suggested they rent them for $1.00. Council discussed
liability with regards to helmets. Recreation Director Perrotti said the waiver
states all must have helmets. Councilperson Ward said if we don't fence it in,
these will be on going issues. Mayor Bragga said he would like to see the
equipment up and the kids using it.
Administrator Finger told council that a TIF training/work session is scheduled
for May 7 at 6:00 pm.. Administrator Finger explained to Council that the TIF
diverts the additional property tax. The tax pays the infrastructure
improvement in lieu of going to the county commissioner. Finger told Council
that this session will be very informative in helping the village move forward
with improvement needed in Light Industrial zoned property.

Memo
To:      Mayor Bragga         Members of Council
From:      Terry Finger, Village Administrator
Subject:   Revenue needed for future paving demand
Date:      May 19, 2003
________________________________________________________________
   I asked Patricia to give you a memo to show what the replacement Road Levy
would generate:    $83,105.71 current, increasing to $116,000.00 if passed
   Along with this information I wanted to make sure you have the expense side
for justification.
   In 2002 the village set aside money ($104,000) to pave 7,450 linear feet
(1.4 miles) of asphalt.
   The recent survey of all roads in the village shows total mileage of
accepted roads at 24.95 or 25 miles.
   Average life of paving in Jefferson is seven years.
   To pave all our dedicated streets every seven years we need to pave 25
miles/7 years or 3.57 miles per year.
   In 2002 dollars we need to spend about $265,200 per year to keep paving
current.
Also to be noted, we applied MC70 in 2002 for $8,000.00 and chip and seal for
$8,570.00 dollars.
We can apply MC70 one more time then the recommendation is to chip and seal or
pave.
With the overwhelming negative feedback from chip and seal in the village our
only viable option is to pave with asphalt.
I hope these numbers help all of us understand the need for this replacement
levy and can help us explain the need to the voters.

2nd
