Council discussed the memo regarding pay increases for elected officials.
Solicitor Lemire explained to Council that in a previous memo, he stated that
elected officials could not get an interim raise. But based on the Ohio
Attorney General’s opinion, an interim raise is permitted as long as it is set
by ordinance and enacted no later than five days prior to the last day for
filing as a candidate for such office.
Councilperson Baxley asked about the status of a raise for the Clerk-Treasurer.
She said she felt that a cost of living raise would be appropriate, and asked
the Finance Committee to address the issue.
Councilperson Thompson stated, he felt that a raise was not needed, and that
based on the time frame for an ordinance, it is not feasible.
Councilperson Baxley said that the Clerk-Treasurer is the chief fiscal officer
and as such should not be the lowest salaried employee. She asked if an
ordinance can be submitted by other than the Finance Committee.
Solicitor Lemire stated that as per Rule 20 of the Rules of Council, any
councilperson can bring forth an ordinance.
Councilperson Maloney said that the Clerk-Treasurer’s position is only part-
time.
Councilperson Baxley said she had asked the Clerk-Treasurer to keep a log of
her hours. Based on the hours she works, the job of Clerk-Treasurer is not a
part-time position.
Clerk-Treasurer Fisher stated that she averages between 60-70 hours a week.
Councilperson Herndon said she feels that the Clerk-Treasurer should get a
raise just based on the length of time since the last ordinance. She asked,
would anyone go that long without a raise?
Mayor Bragga asked the Solicitor to look into elected officials receiving
benefits.
Mayor Bragga told Council to contact Solicitor Lemire regarding further
questions or concerns on the issue.
Councilperson Ward stated that he was still concerned about the appropriateness
of the Clerk-Treasurer purchasing the gifts for Secretary’s Day.

Recommendation # 1 –
The committee recommends that this Council pass an Ordinance to reserve the
following area as Permanent Parkland:
   All Village property on the north side of ravine at the 920 elevation marker
+ 100’
   All the ravine area below the 920 elevation marker
   All Village property on the south side of the ravine between Sycamore Street
over to Cucumber Street including the current Village Park
Motion by Maloney to have the Solicitor draft an Ordinance for Recommendation
#1
2nd
Roll: All yea, motion carried
Recommendation # 2 –
Ashtabula Street is a paper street through the heart of the ravine area. There
is no foreseeable reason to maintain this paper street. This committee
recommends that Council, by ordinance, abandon this paper street starting at
the Conrail Tracks on the West over to the eastern most 920-elevation marker.
Motion by Maloney to have the Solicitor draft an Ordinance for Recommendation
#2 for the vacating of Ashtabula Street.
2nd
Roll: All yea, motion carried
Recommendation # 3 –
In the bottom of the ravine at the intersection of the Ashtabula Street and
Sycamore Street there are 4 Village Greens. Most importantly with
Recommendation # 1, these greens are included in the permanent Parkland. And
along with Recommendation # 2 Ashtabula Street will not exist. It is the
recommendation of this committee that this Council, by ordinance, eliminates
the designated Village Greens presently at the intersection of Ashtabula and
Sycamore Streets.
Motion by Maloney to have the Solicitor draft an Ordinance for Recommendation
#3 to abandon the four greens.
2nd
Roll: All yea, motion carried
Recommendation # 4 –
This recommendation will have 3 specific items – there might need to be a vote
on each item if there is significant concern on any one item - Council can
decide if this is one complete recommendation or 3 separate.
The gas well at the bottom of the ravine must be removed in hopes of obtaining
recreation or park grants. There must be a title search to see if anyone other
then the Village has ownership to this well.
1.   This committee recommends that Council approve the Village Administrator
to hire a firm to do the title search on the gas well.
The gas well removal can be completely paid for by a state grant. This grant
can be received as repayment also. If the Village would wait for the grant to
come in prior to doing the work, the Village would not come up on the list
until about 2007 or 2008. But if the Village went ahead with the removal of the
gas well and was repaid in 2007 or 2008, the Village can still proceed with
other grants for parkland or recreational uses. In order to qualify for these
two types of grants the land must have a clean record and with the gas well
currently on the property, the Village would not qualify for either the
parkland or recreational improvement grants.
2.   This committee recommends that Council approve the Village Administrator
to place this project on a list to be budgeted for and completed during fiscal
year 2004.
A path will be needed cleared for heavy equipment to reach the gas well. There
will be some tree removed. These trees can be sold since the quality of these
trees is in excellent condition and the majority of these trees are of a
marketable quality. The hope of this committee that the funds received for
these trees will be repayment for the title search and allow for any additional
improvements to the path after the well has been removed and all the work is
complete. The idea is to bring the heavy equipment down on the north side off
of Sycamore Street. This is the straightest and easiest path.
   
3.   This committee recommends that Council approve the clearing of needed
trees to gain access for heavy equipment to the gas well. Council needs to also
make a motion for the Village Administrator to advertise or seek the highest
and best bidder for the clearing of the timber and sale of the wood.
Motion by Maloney for Recommendation #4 to approve the Administrator hiring a
firm to do a title search on the gas well for the Orphan Well Grant.
2nd
Roll: All yea, motion carried
Motion by Maloney for Recommendation #4 to have the Administrator place on the
2004 budget the project for the Orphan Well grant, with the Village paying the
expenditure up front. If the Grant is approved, the Village will receive a
reimbursement from the State. The project will be completed in 5 to 7 years
2nd
Roll: All yea, motion carried
Motion by Baxley for Recommendation #4 to approve the Administrator to have the

2nd

This is one large long lot. The committee believes that the property should
split into two lots and considered surplus. This will allow the land to be
sold. This committee recommends that Council make a motion on to have the
Village Administrator have the legal description changed to show two parcels.

Motion by Baxley for Recommendation #6 to have the legal descriptions changed

as surplus to sell.

prior to the elected term.

the 6-½ percent pick-up of PERS.

Mayor Bragga read the Ashtabula County Flag Narrative
ASHTABULA COUNTY FLAG NARRATIVE
The flag is a combination of two designs and symbolizes much of Ashtabula
County’s diverse historical, agricultural and recreational character. The blue
background symbolizes the waters that border and run through Ashtabula County.
The Conneaut Lighthouse recognizes the commercial shipping industry as well as
commercial and recreational fishing. The beam from the lighthouse stands for
the light of freedom for the slaves who traveled through Ashtabula County on
the Underground Railroad and a beacon welcoming people to visit Ashtabula
County. The tilled soil represents the agribusiness that is so vital to our
county. The grapes reflect the many wine producing ventures in our county.
Lastly, the State Road Covered Bridge represents the rich heritage of the
preservation of covered bridges.

Motion by Baxley for the first reading of Ordinance No. 03-0-2487
2nd
Council discussed at great length the issue of a pay raise for the Clerk-
Treasurer. Council discussed the position as being an elected position and not
as an employee. Councilperson Ward stated – I want to make sure all
personalities are thrown out and we look at the position. Councilperson Maloney
told Council that the Ohio Law poorly defines the Clerk-Treasurer’s position.
The job has duties but no qualifications. To run for the position, you must be
a registered voter and reside in the Village a year. To do the job, you must
have intelligence, but the Ohio Revised Code doesn’t think so.
Councilperson Baxley and Maloney provided Council with a list of salary
increases by Council, Mayor, Clerk-Treasurer and department from 1986 thru
2003. Councilperson Baxley told Council everyone in the Village the last few
years has gotten a cost of living raise. The Village should at least give the
Clerk-Treasurer a cost of living raise. Mayor Bragga told Council the Village
couldn’t tell the Clerk-Treasurer when to work. As long as the work is done,
that is all that matters, no matter many hours it takes.
Roll: Thompson, nea; Ward, nea; Baxley, yea; Herndon, yea; Maloney, nea;
Stasny, yea. Vote 3-3, Mayor, nea. Motion Failed

Of Jefferson, To Increase The Salary For The Position Of Clerk-Treasurer Of The
Village Of Jefferson, Ohio, From $33,000 Per Year To $36,960 Per Year

Public Hearing
Clerk Treasurer Fisher explained to Council that the tax budget shows estimated
revenues for the fiscal year 2004. A 3-½ % increase is showed in some of the
anticipated revenue lines. The Local Government fund line do not show the same
increase as the Local Government funds are being cut at the State level. The
estimated revenues are not the final figures. The County has a formula that is
followed to what monies the Village will receive. The County Auditor must
accept the Tax Budget. If there are any changes in anticipated the Village will
submit the changes to the County Auditor.

Chief Febel
Mayor Bragga spoke briefly about the 100-year re-run of the 1903
transcontinental trip by Jefferson native Tom Fetch in a Model F Packard call
“Old Pacific”. The re-run of the original Tom Fetch transcontinental run
started from both coasts and will meet here in Jefferson, an original stop and
home of Tom Fetch, on July 24, 2003. Mayor Bragga will issue a Proclamation to
be presented at a ceremony at the BiLo location in honor of the event.

Service Dept.:
   2003 paving has been scheduled for the week after Labor Day. It will take
two weeks to complete.
   With councils blessing I would like to hold up paving East Cedar Street
until next year to allow the Street Department time to replace the storm drain
culvert on the South East end of East Cedar. Recent inspection showed that this
pipe is rusted and or broken and needs to be replaced. We would have to cancel
the sidewalk replacements that are scheduled to enable the Street Department
time to make this replacement before Labor Day.
   Contractors continue to start and sometimes finish jobs before getting
proper permits. It is important to note that there is no statute of limitations
on work completed without the proper permits. We have stopped jobs. Made people
tear down partially completed structures and move foundations. It is helpful if
you see a job start without a Zoning Permit and Building Permit displayed to
call me with the information. We have one investigation in process now that was
completed on the weekend with no permit issued.
   If construction is started without a permit it is stopped until permits are
issued. If construction violates zoning code it must be corrected or appealed
to the zoning board of appeals.
   Parking issues continue to be a problem. I have been reviewing all codes
related to parking and will report the problem code language to building and
lands committee with suggested changes.
   Current Code Language allows NO Front Yard Parking. Front yards are allowed
to have a driveway leading to Parking Spaces in the Side Yard or Rear Yard.
Therefore 40% to 50% of the parking is in violation of Village Ordinances.
   In 1976, residents with non-conforming parking could apply for a permit for
the fee of $1.00 to register their non-conforming parking.
   I will search the permanent records for information on all such permits
issued.
Fire Dept.:
   ISO meeting is scheduled for August (5) fifth at 9:00 AM at the fire
department.
   Meeting with Todd Insurance scheduled for August 7, 8:00 PM at the fire
station. Question and answer session for a better understanding of coverage and
costs.

   Nothing significant

   Gary Licate will have to retake his Class Three Wastewater Exam in November.
I recommend that we allow him the opportunity, as I believe he would make an
excellent long-term supervisor.
   With Council’s motion I will seek a temporary EPA permit to allow us to
operate with Gary as supervisor with Burgess and Niple as backup if needed.
Other Items:

the Villages’ representative to the Ashtabula County Ohio Public Works
Commission integrating Committee. (Local Group that determines which OPWC

   Terry Finger was elected by the four counties in District Seven of the State
of Ohio to be one of three village representatives in the District Seven OPWC
integrating Committee.
   I would like to request an executive session to address the attached letter
from the Clerk Treasurer under the privilege of personnel issues. While in

Administrator Finger asked for an Executive session at the end of Council to
address personnel issues.
Councilperson Ward asked Administrator Finger if there could be a training
session for police so they would know what kind of offenses to be on the alert
for, such as construction without zoning permits, yard sale signs, front yard
parking, etc. That would help capture some of the problems so we aren’t running
around fixing problems a lot.
Mayor Bragga said it was a good idea, and Administrator Finger said he would
put it on the Wednesday docket for the staff meeting.
Councilperson Baxley asked Administrator Finger to bring Council up to speed on
a problem on E. Jefferson St. that is, again, a result of a zoning permit
violation.
Administrator Finger informed Council that over the weekend there was a gravel
parking area that was improved to concrete. There were two parking spots across
from the mill. A contractor came in Saturday excavated out two parking spaces
and poured the concrete. Monday on the way to work Roland noticed it. In the
Village storm drain which is 50’ away from where that concrete work was done,
he could see fresh concrete splashed on top of the grate in the roadway. He
stopped and discovered that when the truck dumped its load of concrete our
storm sewer was half filled with concrete. After the truck driver said that he
washed the truck out, the cement company owner spent about three days digging
that concrete out of the storm sewer. That’s the kind of eyes we need out
there. It’s a burden on all the taxpayers when someone does a dumb thing like
dump a load of concrete in our storm sewers.
Administrator Finger told Council, there is concrete where there use to be
gravel in the Village tree lawn in a commercial area – no permits. Worst case
is we make them break it up, dig it out and put back the gravel.

Public Hearing, 8:00 p.m.
Mayor Bragga asked if anyone wanted to address Public Hearing on the proposed
PUD, the East Beech St. development.
Councilperson Maloney had a question regarding the issue of no outdoor close
line permitted. Her thinking is that it’s too technical. Administrator Finger
mentioned that this is in the covenant, and homebuyers are aware of it. The
Village is not responsible for enforcing the rules of the covenant. Supposedly,
that is the way they want the neighborhood to be.
Councilperson Baxley said her concerns were with Section 1260.02. Four main
issues here:
   Front yard and side yard set back. While they may be to fire code, they are
not to our building code.
   No lighting or landscape plan.
   No plans to develop Cucumber St.
   The Village is getting nothing back for our concessions.
Main concern is that setback is not in compliance with Village zoning.
Mayor Bragga said the purpose of the Public Hearing is not to debate the
actions of the Planning Commission, but to give the public the opportunity to
speak to those issues. Mayor Bragga said he believed Administrator Finger is
saying that the Planning Commission did take those things into consideration.
The issue will come back to Council, after this hearing, to deliberate on
whether they want to accept or deny the Planning Commission’s recommendation.
Councilperson Baxley said that if it is accepted tonight, Council is accepting
the concessions they have made.
Mayor Bragga said this is a Public Hearing to give individuals the opportunity
to speak to this issue. At a later time, it will appear on the Agenda to decide
whether or not Council agrees with the Planning Commissions’ recommendation.

Councilperson Thompson asked Clerk-Treasurer and Solicitor for an overview of
the new tax laws for Council.
Solicitor Lemire and Clerk-Treasurer Fisher explained to Council that the State
of Ohio passed new house bills 95 and 718 that have an impact on the Village’s
Income Tax Ordinance. A main concern with the new laws passed was the Municipal
Taxation of S corporation share holders. The bill expands the scope of the
municipal income tax exemption for income flowing from an S corporation to a
share holder. The new law will only be able to tax shareholders that have a S
Corporation in Ohio.
Fisher and Lemire explained to Council that municipalities are questioning the
continuation of the taxation of the next profits of an S corporation. Some
communities are passing an ordinance to put a referendum on the ballot in
November objecting the new legislation for S corporations. The Village, at this
time, does not have strong figures and enough information to ask the residents
to vote on the issue. The system through SSI will help the Village in the
future to track revenues coming from S corporations. Solicitor Lemire told
Council he would write a memo on what changes need to be done to update the
Village Income Tax Ordinance.
Clerk-Treasurer Fisher told Council she would keep them informed on the new
laws.

Mayor Bragga told Council that the Joint Fire District Committee with the
Township of Lenox and the Township of Jefferson is a working committee that is
moving in an effort to develop some long range planning for our safety and fire
services. Questions in respect to some ISO will continue to be looked at to see
what can be done to address that situation.
 
Mayor Bragga thanked the efforts of our Safety services –fire, emergency
rescue, police – in terms of the black out that occurred on Thursday, August
14, 2003. Mayor Bragga told Council of concerns regarding fuel for emergency
vehicles should the problem happen again. Within our own fire department there
is generation power enough to supply power to get some pumps running. Mayor
Bragga suggested that Jefferson be a hub to develop some sort of a plan so
emergency vehicles could get fuel should we have an extended period of a safety
issue. Mayor Bragga asked everyone in the community to look at our residential
plan so that every homeowner has a plan with respect to their own house. For
instance, a few days supply of drinking water, batteries, maybe a radio that
works off of batteries, those sorts of things. Another consideration would be
the elderly, people who may have oxygen needs; where would they go? There are
some things in place between Emergency Rescue and 911, but it would be a good
idea to take a look at what we would do as a Village; what are we as residents
going to do to meet this kind of crisis? Mayor Bragga welcomes any ideas on the
matter of keeping us safe and better prepared for emergencies.

Motion by Ward for the first reading of Ordinance No. 03-O-2494
2nd
Discussion
Don Locy of the East Beech Street Development explained to Council that at the
last meeting he felt that not everyone understood what the Beech Street
Development’s plans were. Locy explained the vision of the developers was to
have a planned campus styled community that would be associated with the
Jefferson Geriatrics Center and the assisted living component. This community
was the start of a PUD called the Woodlands of Jefferson.
The community would consist of single-family houses that would have concrete
roads, sidewalks, clubhouse, walking trail, Gazebo and a lake with swans. The
development consists of 40 units with 10’ between the units. Some houses may
have a side entry garage; some a front entry garage. There will be a Home
Owners Association that will make sure the grass is mowed, snow plowed and
areas planted. An association dues will pay for all this maintenance.
Councilperson Thompson told Council that he felt the PUD ordinance allow the
Village to address any concerns dealing with new developments.
Chad Brenner of the East Beech Street Development told Council that this
development is a wonderful expansion for the Village of Jefferson. The
development reaches all the needs of the people that want to live in a planned
campus community. The residents of the community will be able to live in a
development as they would be able to live in any community, but the maintenance
is taken care of by the association. The development has talked with growth
partnership on working a TIF for the Cucumber Street extension. If this is
completed it will also benefit the Village. These are questions that have
answers, but it is a working process.
Councilperson Ward told Council that Planning Commission’s vision was to have a
Housing Development in the Village. This is what the residents need and what
the Village wants.
Afterward, Don Locy told Council, regarding the question of the 10’ between
units, the allotted distance between the units had been scrutinized by the
Planning Commission and determined to be adequate and also within the fire
code. In actuality the distance between units vary depending on the size of the
unit. The smaller units will have more distance between them. The rationale of
having a 10’ minimum is that this would allow for more property to be available
for the common areas, such as lake, sidewalks, landscaping, clubhouse, etc. The
East Beech Street Development did consider eliminating lots to allow for the
20’distance between each lot. But the cost would have been too high and things
would have to be eliminated, such as the clubhouse.
Roll: Ward, yea; Baxley, nay; Herndon, yes; Maloney, yes; Stasny, nay;
Thompson,
yea. Roll: 4 yea-2 nay, motion carried.
Ordinance No. 03-O-2494
An ordinance establishing a Planned Unit Development (PUD) to be known as “The
Woodlands of Jefferson”

Visitors Comments  
Durward Newhard addressed Council regarding the issue of the helicopter that
has been offered to the Village as a Vietnam Memorial. Mr. Newhard feels the
Village should accept the helicopter and find an appropriate site to display
it. The only cost to the Village regarding the helicopter would be the site and
the pad upon which it will be displayed.
Mayor Bragga told Council that he was informed that the only equipment
available at this time is a Cobra helicopter, and he was quoted that the size
of the base is 13’ x 13’. He said placing the helicopter would be an expense
and Council wants to make sure it’s don right, taking into consideration
maintenance, etc.
Councilperson Baxley said she talked to the donor, and was told the actual
space needed would be a 20’ x 40’. Perhaps, once it gets into committee, there
might be somebody who would donate a beautiful public site on a corner for the
display. We might get together with the County Commissioners. In front of their
building would be a nice spot where a wreath could be place on Memorial Day.
Councilperson Baxley also stated that the helicopter issue should be put in
committee
Mr. Fertig, addressing Mayor Bragga, stated that the Village should decide if
the helicopter is wanted before searching out a sites. Mr. Fertig said the
Village parks are dwindling. He feels we have a lot of memorials now, and one
of this magnitude may not be as appealing as it is going to be an eye sore. Mr.
Fertig said there are other branches of the service that may want to be
honored, if we accept one we had better accept them all.
Mayor Bragga stated that Mr. Fertig has brought up many good points and many
good questions. Mr. Bragga said it is his position that the matter has to be
brought to committee for review and recommendations brought back to the Council
floor. All committee meetings are posted and are open to the public.
Mayor Bragga asked if there were any more visitor comments.
Mr. Polucci has expressed a desire to have Village sewer extended in the
Township. He is interested in buying property to put up apartments west on 307,
next to the apartments there. Mayor Bragga stated that the current ordinance
says that there are to be no sewer tape-ins in the Township.
Mr. Fertig said that in looking over the bills, he saw that a 1986 Mustang was
sold, and that in August, $50.00 in repairs and $250.00 in repairs were spent.
Mr. Fertig asked why money was spent to repair a vehicle that was going to be
sold? Mayor Bragga said it was decided to do minor repairs to make the vehicle
safe. It was being put up for public sale and we did what we had to do to make
it somewhat safe.

Visitors Comments  
Patricia Inman and Mark Helmer, representing the Jefferson Pride School Levy
Committee, requested a letter of support from Council to publicly let the
community know the value of Issue 22. Issue 22 is a five-year, 4.5 mill renewal
General Operating levy that generates approximately $584.000 for the district.
Motion by Thompson approving Council’s support of the School Levy
2nd 
Discussion:
Mrs. Baxley said, “I have supported the schools for 15 years. However, to ask
this legislative body to support the levy, you’re asking me to support it. I
cannot say how the voters of this community feel about the levy, some voters
express great support, some various, serious doubts about our current
superintendent and school board and actions, fiscal responsibilities and
decisions in the past. It’s not my responsibility to use this office to
influence the voters. Therefore, I cannot support the motion for these
reasons.”
Roll: Stasny, yea; Thompson, yea; Ward, yea; Baxley, nay; Herndon, yea;
Maloney, yea Roll vote: 5 yea; 1-nay, motion carried.
Sollicitor Lemire brought up the issue regarding a possible conflict of
interest because Mr. Thompson works for the school district, perhaps he should
abstain.
Mr. Thompson said that’s fine, but he stated publicly that when he goes to the
ballot he will vote yes. It’s his constitutional right.
Mayor Bragga asked if there was anyone else who wanted to address Council.
Mr. Fertig stated that at the last meeting he raised some questions regarding
the accepting of the helicopter that has been donated to the Village. He said
that he has heard that someone on Council said he was grandstanding because
he’s asking these questions. He said that if you can’t come to a Council and
ask a question and get a civil answer without being ridiculed, there’s
something wrong. He said, at the time, Mayor Bragga said that he had brought up
some good points. Mr. Fertig said that he intends to be at a lot of meetings,
and will be asking a lot of questions.
Mayor Bragga acknowledged that that is what he had said. Mayor Bragga said he
doesn’t know where the comments were coming from, but he hasn’t said anything
bad about Mr. Fertig or anyone else. There has been a committee meeting since
the last Council meeting to discuss the helicopter issue. No action has been
taken, because there are still some concerns that need to be discussed.
Diane Sowry voiced a concern regarding a few plants in the Village and one
outside the village that make plastic fiberglass products. Her concern is the
health and safety issue.
She said, in researching the problem, she has been told that Styrene which is
used in making plastic is a cancer causing agent. Administrator finger said the
amount that escape the buildings is most likely not hazardous, but we need to
find out for sure if that is true. He said the smell is probably more of a
nuisance than anything else. Administrator Finger said there are ways the
Village can monitor the plants more closely, and he is going to look into the
issue, so it can be discussed during future meetings.
Councilperson Thompson rescinded his previous motion to approve Council’s
support of the School Levy
Motion by Maloney approving Council’s support of the School Levy
2nd 
Roll: Thompson, abstain; Ward, yea; Baxley, nay; Herndon, yea; Maloney, yea;
Stasny, yea Roll vote: 4 yea; 1-nay, one abstention motion carried.

site to fabricate the stand. That’s part of the proposition also.

Township. Parking at the old Township garage.

Service Dept.:
·   Street Department welcomes Roland and John back to work. Larry’s broken
continues to mend.
·   Street Department is at full strength with Bob Reitz filling in for Larry.
·   Storm Sewer replacement of lines on East Cedar Street is on hold.

paved.
·   Christmas decorating is in progress.
·   Leaf pickup continues as warranted.
·   Brush pickup must be discontinued until spring.
·   Trucks are ready for snow removal if needed.
Fire Dept.:
·   Heat Tape will be installed on the roofline to prevent the ice formation
experienced in prior years.
·   Fire Department received complaints of a strong oil/gas odor on Thursday
November 20 and again on Friday November 21, 2003. The odor was determined to
be coming from a well being drilled in the township just east of Spruce Street.
Chief Wayman checked and determined there was no fire hazard from the odor.
·   Due to numerous complaints from Village residents the State Division of Oil
and Gas was notified. The company drilling the well (C-Gas) was notified and
drilling was halted. The driller changed from dry drilling to wet drilling and
eliminated the problem odor.
Recreation/Community Center :
·   The Recreation Committee and Director have met several times to again
revisit the fee structure. A recommendation will come from committee.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   I would like to introduce our newest employee, Mr. Mark Reighard recently
hired at the wastewater treatment plant.
·   Repairs continue to be a priority with the following additional items
completed: the two new blower motors are installed, and the Kohler motor tune
up on the stand-by power unit at the main pump station.
·   The following are scheduled and staged for completion: Emergency power for
lighting the site and service building, three swing arms, and replacement of
the commutator which grinds solids.
Finance/Appropriations/Budget:
·   Finance committee meeting scheduled for Wednesday December 3rd was
postponed and must be rescheduled.
Other Items:
·   42 new trees were planted and look great. We will be straightening them as
needed until they take root.
·   After walking the Ashtabula Street right of way that we are considering
abandoning, I think we need to retain the section west of North Sycamore to the
RR Tracks. The strip of parkland needs the right of way to maintain access and
the sewer trunk line is in this right of way. I would suggest we table the
ordinance until next meeting to enable adaquate review time.

Officials
Mayor
Mayor Bragga told Council that it has been an honor serving as the Mayor of the
Village of Jefferson, and the four years have gone by quickly. He said Council
is losing a very good Councilperson in Ed Ward. Councilperson Ward has served
the Village diligently; he has worked hard in his committees, devoted a lot of
time, and has been forthright with the Mayor.. Ed Ward will be missed! On the
other side, looking at the glass as being half full, the Mayor is looking
forward to working with Ken Fertig who is going to be joining Council in a
couple of weeks. Times change, people change but the Village will go on.
Old Business/New Business
Councilperson Baxley told Council that under the tax administration code
section 890.09 duties of tax administrator and ordinance 2283 passed 11/15/99
states under section 80 the administrator of this chapter shall be the Clerk-
Treasurer of the Village. She said, with talks with Mr. Lemire, this is not a
thing that Council can request of the Clerk-Treasurer.
Mr. Lemire told Council that we are doing a rewrite of the tax code, because of
a lot of changes that have taken place in Columbus. One issue that has come up
during this review is the issue of the Tax Administrator. In those discussions,
it is basically his view that Council cannot order the Village Clerk-Treasurer
to be the Tax Administrator. The Clerk-Treasurer is an elective official, and
her job specifications are designed by statute. Council can ask and the clerk-
treasurer can volunteer to be the Tax Administrator, but it is probably
inappropriate to specify in the code that the Clerk-Treasure will be the Tax
Administrator. In the tax code rewrite there will be a lot of changes tied with
legislature. One suggestion will be to strike that provision.
Mayor Bragga said the issue of Tax Administrator will be explored, and a
Committee will be formed to come up with recommendations.
Visitors’ Comments -

2nd
Roll: All yea, motion carried

Patricia A. Fisher

Mayor Bragga referred to last Council meeting’s discussion regarding the Tax
Administrator and the Tax administrator duties that relates to Ohio Revised
Code 733.85. To clear up misinformation or confusion, Mayor Bragga talked to

is the Tax Administrator.
Mayor’s address to the Village of Jefferson 2004
The 2003-year was highlighted with several significant improvements and plans:
The paving plan progressed with the completion of paving of streets scheduled
for 2003. The challenge will be generating finances to keep pace with the
paving plan. The current paving plan will need to be adjusted in 2004 to
reflect the available dollars.
The waste water plan is in place and will serve as a guide and resource to us
as we continue to manage and improve the waste water facility and system. Many
significant safety and operational improvements were made during 2003. The
operation is back to 3 fulltime operators tending to a facility that requires a
24/7 treatment capability.
This administration has been active and successful in obtaining grants for the
Village.
·   The Orphan gas well grant to plug the gas well on the parkland of the Rush
Creek property has been approved for 100% funding (35 to 50 thousand dollars)
with work to begin in 2004.
·   A grant has been approved to renovate the Woodside lift station (83
thousand dollars). This project is to be started in 2004 and completed in 2005.
·   A block grant for the improvement of drainage in the Jeffersonian Estate
area has been approved for 80 thousand dollars with work to begin in 2004.
·   The ODOT safety grant for the intersection of routes 46/167/307 north of
the village has been approved at a 10% local match. The estimated cost of this
major project is expected to be in the million-dollar range. Construction on
this major project will not begin until 2005 or 2006. This important safety
project will only cost our local village 10% of the total project cost.
·   The Ohio public works grant for the culvert replacement on South Market
street will be completed in 2004. The grant is for 106 thousand dollars.
The financial situation of the village will reduce the capability of securing
future grants because of the lack of available local dollars. Most grants
require 40% to 60% local match for potential projects. Projects such as: Cedar
street improvement (Chestnut to Elm), Sycamore street project, Cucumber street
project and North Trunk sewer line project will be delayed due to a current
lack of local resources.
The primary challenge to village council will be balancing the revenue with the
current and expected services offered at the levels we are now receiving.
Generally, the amount of revenue available to operate all departments of the
village has remained fairly constant or decreased. Most of the fixed cost areas
(all utilities, fuel, gas, health care and contracted services) have increased
with no real option to control those increases without affecting the normal and
current services we expect. The decision of the community several years ago to
create a complete recreation department and to borrow money in order to
purchase and renovate a recreation center that serves the whole area, without
adding enough revenue, is certainly demanding the attention of village council.
The decision to offer a comprehensive recreation department (the 2003
expenditures, including the yearly Recreation Building Bond payment of $94,840,
will be in the 350 thousand dollar range) has been a significant factor in
reducing the dollars available in the general fund and capital improvement
fund. The major challenge in the first six months of 2004 will be facing the
reality of balancing the future financial picture of our village. Increasing
revenue or reducing services are possible answers to correcting the financial
status of Jefferson.
Jefferson is a community that we choose because it provides the services and
agencies we believe are important. Quality safety services (police and fire),
attractive and well maintained streets, sidewalks and greens, essential waste
water services, efficient trash collection, brush pick-up, leaf pick-up,
Christmas tree pick-up, snow removal of sidewalks, safety force leadership and
safety force involvement at no cost to the organizers of many parades and
recognition events, recreational programs for citizens, clean and attractive
community recreation center and many other services are all examples of why we
are a safe and desirable Jefferson. I believe we need to continue to provide
existing services and increase services when feasible. I recommend that council
examine revenue options and add revenue to maintain services and improve the
quality of life through proper planning and directing desired growth. Revenue
increases can come in the form of specific or general levies to property tax or
an increase in village income tax.
The fire department, along with village and township officials, has used 2003
to discuss our needs and define needs for the future. There is a need to
replace a fire truck at a cost of around 400 thousand dollars. We have a need
to significantly increase our fire safety inspections on a regular schedule
within our fire district. Fire prevention is a primary goal of our department,
making inspections a necessity.
It may be time for this community to review and consider combining the
resources and people of the existing safety services. I will spend some time in
2004 becoming more familiar and knowledgeable with the operation of the
Jefferson Emergency Rescue District.
2004 will be a year of watching the planned unit development progress on East
Beech street. This project is a positive and exciting development for Jefferson
and all of Ashtabula County.
Another challenge for the 2004 council will be developing requests for proposal
for village owned parcels of light industrial and residential property. It is
time we become pro-active and turn these assets into revenue generating
properties.
I plan to maintain the Water Advisory committee in an effort to communicate our
concerns, needs and priorities to Consumers Ohio Water Service. The committee
has been instrumental in creating short and long range plans for water
improvements and services. I will continue to watch and learn from decisions
other entities are making in our county and area and proceed with proper
education and planning.
I am asking that the buildings and lands committee review current ordinances
relating to cleanliness, up-keep and improvement of private property Changes,
additions or creating language to enhance the value and condition of all
property are needed.
Progress continues to be made as the new financial software is in operation in
several departments of the village. Using this software will fulfill new state
requirements for financial management and reporting.
The collective work and efforts of the administrator, clerk, central office
personnel, council and all departments of the village is evident and essential
to the total operation of the village. The administrative ability of Terry
Finger provides the guidance, knowledge and attention to detail that is
necessary in the management and operation of our business.
I thank council for you cooperation and diligence in approving the legislation
for the business of Jefferson. As future challenges occur I am confident we can
work together in a spirit of cooperation in a constant effort to make our town
the best place to live.
May God richly bless this community and all of the people who are the
community!

Motion by Maloney to go into Executive Session for the purpose of personnel
regarding resignation and compensation
2nd
Solicitor Lemire told Council that according to statute the motion has to be
more specific, basically what subject. Statute requires that we name the issue.
You go into executive session to go into personnel matters to discuss
appointment, employment, dismissal, discipline, promotion, demotion or
compensation for a public employee.
 
Council indicated that discussion will be in regard to all of those issues.
Lemire told Council they have to tell what they are talking about.
Councilperson Maloney said they are talking about resignation and compensation.
Lemire asked if it was the same person. Maloney answered that no it was two
different persons.
Lemire asked if one of the persons was the Senior Coordinator’s compensation.
When it was confirmed, Lemire told Council, the statute says if you are going
to talk about a personnel matter regarding a public employee, the public
employee can request it be a public discussion.
When asked, Chris Litwiler said she would very much like the discussion to be
public.
Since Chris Litwiler requested the discussion be public, the Mayor asked if
Council would like to remove the motion to go into Executive Session from the
table.
The motion and second were withdrawn.
Mayor Bragga stated that Council is back in regular session
Mayor Bragga told Council he has always supported the Community Center, he was
on the first Rec. Board formed in the village around 1969. Mayor Bragga said he
is not opposed to Rec. It is not an issue of Rec. or no Rec. It has been
determined that $80,000 has to be shaved from Recreation Center budget. The
challenge to that Department is what has to be done to make the necessary cuts
to make the budget balance.
Councilperson Thompson agrees that Council needs to find additional revenue.
Even if Council decides how to get additional revenue, it would be a year
before it would come in. As Finance Chairman at this point, Thompson said he
doesn’t see a way to change the work that has been done. If anyone knows of a
source of revenue somewhere bring it to his attention. Thompson told Council,
to address your statements tonight and your hard work, cuts were made
everywhere, in every department; but there were no vital positions eliminated -
even though there was discussion of eliminating some positions completely.
Councilperson Maloney said she got information from Clerk-Treasurer Fisher
regarding the new insurance rates coverage
·   Cost for the Village for coverage for family, husband and wife = $636.38
per month
·   Cost for the Village for a Single person = $327.28
If a person were to go from the family coverage down to the single coverage
that would be a savings of almost $4,000 a year.
Janitors and night desk help were cut out of the budget for a savings of
$28,000 a year.
Councilperson Maloney said, if you cut the time from 40 hours a week to 25
hours a week you are saving $6,800. Maloney said if Council is making all those
other cuts, perhaps, if this person might want to be satisfied with a different
health insurance plan, then maybe it wouldn’t be necessary to cut the hours
from 40 to 25 hours. Councilperson Maloney said maybe Council should look a
little bit deeper into the figures first to see whether or not the senior
program is bringing in money. If it is not bringing in money, then maybe the
senior hours need to be cut. If the senior program is bringing money and is
profitable, maybe it should have a second glance.
Mayor Bragga stated that with respect to prudent and intelligent thought about
what Council is doing, we’re still going to have final numbers. In reality, we
still have not closed out 2003; and that, in and of itself, could change some
of the picture. Mayor Bragga cautioned Council that it isn’t easy, it’s tough,
when you love and care about people who are in the village, but you have to be
able and willing to make tough decisions. If you aren’t willing to do that,
then you’re sitting in the wrong chair.
Councilperson Herndon told Council she would like to see the Senior Director on
full time. Herndon thinks that thoughts were that insurance is an issue.
Councilperson Baxley said, perhaps, Council needs to look at medical payments
across the board. Perhaps the Village can no longer pay 2/3 of a family’s
insurance bills, perhaps the Village should only be paying ½.. That is
something that should be dealt with equally. Baxley said she sees Chris
Litwiler at the Senior Center and is aware of what is happening in the Senior
Center. Baxley said that last meeting she praised Janet Butler and her
performance as an employee at the Community Center, but perhaps if hours have
to be cut, Janet is the one who should go to part-time. Baxley said she doesn’t
think Council can make any sort of discussion on this until there are final
figures.
Councilperson Herndon said she agreed with Councilperson Baxley.
Thompson said the people here have to be advised that for the past six years
the Community Center has been an asset in our Community - it’s a jewel in the
County. But the Center has required monies from the General Funds to finish out
the year for the past six years. The Mayor mentioned $80,000, again, on the
operational side to finish out this year. That’s why Council had to look at
ways to cut. It is not as if you sit there in a dark room with a magic wand and
you find places to cut. It’s departmentally you have to find those and you have
to make the cuts you can - the equipment side, the program side, the employee
side, the hours it’s open, the operational costs, heating, everything.
Mayor Bragga said final numbers aren’t yet available. Certainly, Council has
the power to approve the cuts of the current part-time people, table the
decision on this particular position until final numbers are in so there is a
better grasp of exactly where Council is; then come back again to try to solve
the issue here.

Administrator’s Report
Grant information will be added later in the year for 2005 projects.
 
We have been awarded a $9,500.40 grant from Ashtabula County Department of Job
and Family Services through the Senior Service Levy Fund to help defray the
cost of the Senior Van
Service Dept.:
·   Snow Ban No Parking is in effect from Midnight to 6:00 AM until April.
·   There are also restrictions that prevent parking on or across sidewalks. In
winter it is especially critical to adhere to these restrictions. We can not
plow walks that are blocked and walkers can not easily bypass these blocked
areas because of the snow.
·   Wall Street is NO PARKING any time snow is greater than 2 inches deep to
allow the snowplows to be able to pass.
·   Christmas Tree pickup will continue as practical.
·   Remember to remove lights, ornaments, tree stands and tree bags. Bare trees
only can be recycled.
·   Salt trucks, plows and the sidewalk tractor have been busy keeping up with
snowfall.
Fire Dept.:
·   Heat Tape quotes are in and work will go to Larry Fink who also did the
police Department roof in 2001. Weather will dictate completion schedule.
·   Insurance coverage information for the cadet program was forwarded to
Safety Chair and The Fire Department.
Recreation/Community Center :
·   All new programs are running at the Rec. Center with about 20 kids per day
in Basketball.
·   There are 15 kids signed up for the alpine ski trip on Monday.
·   Feedback from the recreation survey was presented January 12th 2004 with
good newspaper coverage on the initial information. Final report will be
delivered and available around the end of January.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Thanks to the utilities committee for being willing to get a live update at
wastewater in a snowstorm.
·   Repairs continue to be a priority with the following additional items
completed: The third swing arm was replaced.
·   The following repairs are scheduled and staged for completion: The laser
alignment of two replacement motors on the digester blowers, and replacement of
the commutator, which grinds solids.
·   Two employees are in the process of completing their CDL’s with the final
driving test having been scheduled.
·   All three employees are getting their Sewer Collections Certification
(Wastewater Collection 1) that covers all the requirements and specifications
for the gravity main lines, forced main lines, sewer jetting, smoke testing,
die testing, televising, and inspecting sewer laterals. This certification is
in addition to the wastewater treatment licensing process.
Finance/Appropriations/Budget:
·   Finance committee has received 2003 year end figures and continues to meet
to deal with 2004 appropriations.
Other Items:
·   I am asking for a motion authorizing me to enter into a renewal contract

further study.

28, 2003 meeting. Councilperson Fertig had been brought up to date by
Administrator finger and some of the other council people. Municipal parking is
also on hold because there has been a possible change in ownership of the
concerned properties; and presently there are just no finances available to
purchase property.
 
The Mayor was asked to remind the Police Department about enforcing parking
ordinances.

ordinance 19224 to regulate use of public greens, parks, and right of ways with
input from Administrator Finger.
 
Building and Lands also discussed the Methodist Church request for property for
Habitat for Humanity All the committee members present agreed that Council can
not give away Village land. It would have to be sold at a fair, appraised
price. Cayce Baxley will do an appraisal of a 1-acre parcel on Mercer Street
and Lynden (Parcel B).

surveyed. Administrator Finger will contact Eric Westfall to do the survey.
Westfall will be given 120 days total time-line to finish the survey after the
contract is awarded.

buildings in the Village. After 4 or 5 years of input from business owners,

Administrator Finger is to send out notices to violators.

Old Business/New Business
 
Councilperson Baxley told Council that an e-mail message from Solicitor Lemire
was received regarding in-term pay increases to elected officials. Solicitor
Lemire stated his opinion that he did not think it was right in the case of
Creed vs City of Hubbard. Councilperson Baxley said she did some digging and
talked to the State Auditor’s office and the Attorney General’s Office. Creed
vs the City of Hubbard is a case of a Mayor getting an increase not a Clerk-
Treasurer. Councilperson Baxley gave the Solicitor three documents from the
Ohio Ethics Commission stating the Clerk, or Clerk-Treasurer is not prohibited
by the section 102.03 of the Revised Code from accepting an increase in
compensation enacted by the Village Council during his current term of office.
 
Motion by Baxley that the ordinance be resubmitted to Council granting the
Clerk-Treasurer a pay increase, which would bring her pay to $36,960.00
 
Councilperson Baxley that in the past 17 years the Administrative position has
received $27,000.00 in additional compensation; the Recreation Director has
received $21,000 in additional compensation, the Clerk-Treasurer has received
$16,500 in additional compensation, the Mayor’s position has received 40%
increase in compensation and council has received 35% increase in compensation.
Councilperson Baxley said it is discriminatory to not raise the salary of the
Clerk-Treasurer’s position.
2nd
Councilperson Fertig asked when the Clerk-Treasurer last got a raise. The
Clerk-Treasurer answered. April 1, 2000.
 
Councilperson Fertig asked if a raise was granted, what fund would it come
from. Answer - Clerk-Treasurer’s wages comes out of the General Fund.
 
Motion by Maloney to table the motion until there is more information for the
rest of the Council.
2nd
Councilperson Baxley will give Council copies of the documents she received.

Visitors Comments:
Bruce Becker spoke to Council promoting the 5 Mil School Replacement Levy. It
is an operating levy-goes for supplies, textbooks, transportation etc. There
are presently two levies that the District is working with, a 2-mil levy and a
5-mil levy, making a total of 7-mils. The 5-mil replacement levy that is on the
ballot in March will replace the previous 5-mil levy.
The Board of Education has already voted to drop collection on the 2-mil levy,
when the 5-mil replacement levy passes. A 5-mil replacement levy will actually
generate more income than from the existing 2 levies. As it stands now, the
District will have to ask the voters for a renewal levy every year for the next
5 years. With the passage of a 5 Mil replacement levy, it won’t have to be
voted on for another 5 years.
Councilperson Baxley stated that a 5-mil replacement levy would mean a 23%
increase in taxes.
Bruce Becker told Council that costs have increased to run the school system,
on the same dollar revenue. Chamber of Commerce is supporting the levy, and
will help with the promotion costs of a flyer sent to voters. Mr. Becker
encouraged everyone to get out to vote – no matter how they vote.
Durward Newhard told Council that Aaron Stehura, a Jefferson Area High School
student won the area’s Voice of Democracy award. Although Aaron did not win at
the State level, his speech was very impressive.
Mr. Newhard told Council that after some research and an e-mail message, it is
determined that the helicopter project is approved. Hopefully, the red tape
will soon be cleared away. Mr. Hayslettt is anxious to get things moving.
Buzz Furman, Golden Dawn representative brought up points of concern regarding
the sign ordinance:
·   The sign directly in front of Golden Dawn generates revenue for Golden
Dawn.
·   Larry Sonoski, owner, feels that the ordinance encroaches on his ability to
display signs on his property as he sees fit.
·   The store and parking lot is always well maintained, and the owner and
employees have always supported the community.
·   The ordinance also dictates how long and where signs can be hung in the
windows.
Mr. Furman said he would like assurance that the ordinance is enforced across
the board and not just some of it.
Mayor Bragga said that input was invited from community businesses before the
ordinance was passed. This is the beginning of sign ordinance enforcement.
Letters have been sent to businesses in violation of the ordinance. The village
needs time to enforce the ordinance; it will be consistent and fairly
delivered.
Regarding the village banners on the utility poles, the village received
permission from the utility company to hang banners from their poles and the
municipal statute governs it.
The Mayor said the Village needs time to consistently and fairly enforce the
ordinance. It may have to be revisited again in the future.
Vince Crawford of Chardon Hauling Division of Waste Management told Council
that they have acquired Country Disposal and wants to reassure Council that the
Village will receive the same service as previously supplied by Country
Disposal. Waste Management serves several neighboring communities and are
committed to serving the Jefferson community. Waste Management practices safety
and have good employees. Five out of seven Country Disposal employees have
agreed to continue on with Waste Management.
Council was assured that any changes or ideas will be presented to Council
before proceeding with changes. If the Village provides a database of
residents, Waste Management will send flyers out.
Mayor Bragga explained that the “student mayor” who is to receive the
Proclamation has
Not been able to make the meetings, because she does not drive. Perhaps when
the
weather improves she will be able to make it to a meeting.

Old Business/New Business   
Concerning whether a request for an opinion from the solicitor could be asked
verbally or must it be in writing - Council Rule 20 is in conflict with Chapter
234. In the last paragraph of Rule 20 the phrase should read “by way of written
form”.
Councilperson Thompson told Council that at a seminar he attended, it was
stated that all inquiries to the solicitor should be in writing, since it could
be a matter of public record.
Mayor Bragga is sending the matter to a special committee - Thompson and
Baxley- for review and updating of the duties and responsibilities of the
solicitor.
A discussion of the in-term raise for clerk-treasurer ensued.
Councilperson Thompson told Council the Oath of Office should be followed. ORC
was followed in June 2003 when the same subject was addressed. He asked –
should not the same law be in place now?
Councilperson Maloney stated that this is the second time the solicitor has
given Council his opinion. Council did not follow his opinion the first time.
Maloney said the solicitor is doing a good job and his opinion should be
followed. She asked, why have a solicitor if we are not going to follow his
opinions?
Mayor Bragga told Council 731.13 ORC indicates very clearly the procedure for
in term raise.
Mayor Bragga told Council that at the last meeting Councilperson Baxley made
reference to % of raises given to personnel over the years, but he didn’t have
paperwork from Baxley documenting resources named in the minutes of the last
discussion of the matter.
Councilperson Fertig interjected that there are 3 people on Council who does
not want the clerk to get a raise.
Councilperson Baxley told Council that she was told by the State Auditor’s
office in Youngstown to call the Attorney General’s office rather than the
State Auditor’s office. Baxley said she had spoken with someone in the Attorney
General’s office last August regarding another matter.
Mayor Bragga told Council he had different figures than Councilperson Baxley
regarding raises, but he didn’t have her notes for an actual comparison. Mayor
Bragga told Council that Council is in charge of enforcing ordinances. Sign
ordinances and other ordinances are enforced; this law should be enforced as
well. Mayor Bragga questioned home rule over statute.
Solicitor Lemire stated that he spoke to John Gotterman from OML regarding in
term raises. A statutory village like Jefferson must follow procedure by
legislature, as to time frame for raises; but legislature cannot dictate the
amount given. Charter municipalities have more power. Home rule is over
substance (amount given) and not procedure (time when allowed for raise). There
has been not exact case decision yet on 731.13
Councilperson Thompson said that home rule has strength when legislature is
weak.
Mayor Bragga asked that if 731.13 is not enforced how can other rules be
enforced? The Mayor stated, it should be noted that the Clerk-Treasures has not
been receiving family healthcare benefits of which she is entitled. This needs
to be corrected.
Motion by Baxley to return the tabled Clerk-Treasure Raise motion back to the
table
2nd 
Roll: Thompson, nay; Baxley, yea; Fertig, yea, Herndon, yea; Maloney, nay;
Stasny, yea.
Roll vote – 4-yea; 2-nay; motion carried.
Motion by Baxley for the first reading of Ordinance No. 04-O- 2537
2nd
Roll: Baxley, yea; Fertig, yea, Herndon, yea; Maloney, nay; Stasny,
yea;Thompson, nay
Roll vote – 4 yea, 2 nay; motion carried.
Ordinance No. 04-O- 2537
An ordinance amending section 236.05 of the codified ordinances of the Village
of Jefferson, to increase the salary of the position of Clerk-Treasurer of the
Village of Jefferson, Ohio, from $33,000 per year to $36,960 per year.

Visitors Comments:
Durward Newhard told Council that over the course of the events of the year,
the transportationof the helicopter has become our responsibility. Durward is
soliciting for donations for transportation. Durward is still in touch with the
anonymous donor regarding the question of the painting of the helicopter. It
will be the community’s responsibility to maintain the helicopter received. It
is understood that any lease for the location of the memorial is between
Durward and Lewis Hayslett. VFW 3334 has set up a separate account for the
donations for transportation of the helicopter Donations can be sent to Durward
Newhard at 341 S. Elm St., Jefferson, Ohio.
Durward Newhard also told Council that May 3, 2004 is Loyalty Day and May 31,
2004 is Memorial Day.
Mayor Bragga told Council that he spoke with the junior mayor and although she
is unable to be here tonight, she does want to attend a Council meeting in the
future.
Department Reports
Administrator’s Report
Grant information will be added later in the year for 2005 projects.
Service Dept.:
·   We have started spring-cleaning at all facilities. The main emphasis is on
cleaning up the out side of our buildings and trimming brush and plant life for
appearance sake.
·   If any of you spot an eyesore on village property please let me know so we
can get it taken care of.
·   The next step in clean- up will be to identify the private rubbish and
trash and go after the owners to clean it up.
·   To coincide with this effort I have requested a price from Waste Management
for dumpsters and an available time period.
·   Cleanup of parkland frontage at East Jefferson is underway.
Fire Dept.:
·   Nothing new to report
Recreation/Community Center :
·   Draft of the spring offerings was provided for your review.
·   Senior Van was involved in a car accident. Van was empty and there were no
injuries reported. All proper procedures were followed and since it is to be
replaced we may not repair the dented fender.
·   There is a request from Anita to attend the Ohio Association of Senior
Centers 2004 Spring Conference. The local District XI Area on Aging is paying
the registration fee. The cost to
the Rec. Department Budget will be two nights lodging and three meals. Council
needs to approve the request.
 
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Repairs and maintenance continue.
·   Preparations are underway for the OPWC grant.
Finance/Appropriations/Budget:
·   Cayce, Wilma and I attended our first Tax abatement meeting for Pickens
Plastic. They are still in a hiring mode and working to achieve the objectives
stated in their application. There will be a meeting each year to review the
progress. Council needs to determine what your level of involvement should be.
·   Quotes to remove the timber for the gas well clean up site show no cost or
no gain for the Village. A revenue neutral event.
·   Allowing the gas well clean up company to cut their own path would also be
a revenue neutral event.
·   When the buyers looked at this timber they also gave me a dollar value to
remove all usable timber from the Light Industrial parcel, the recently
surveyed Part #2 of the Rush Creek Property (approximately 17 acres total) and
the well sight.
·   The value of this timber is in excess of $35,000.00 dollars.
·   I would recommend we (Council Committees) consider this option because
harvesting the timber does not lower the value of the land to a potential
developer.
·   I request that Council approve Roni, Jan and I attending the SSI Software
user meeting for up to date information and networking reasons. This will help
with cross training.
Other Items:
·   Copies of the Request for Proposal on two village properties have been
mailed to potential interested parties and the public notice will run one more
time.
·   Survey work is complete for parcel #2 of the Rush Creek property. The plat
is available for review.
·   The request for the purchase order to survey the third parcel (Part #6) was
written 3/9/04.
·   The Zoning map has been updated to reflect all the latest changes. I am
still reviewing old maps and ordinances to make sure I have a correct and
accurate map. I will have large copies made when it is complete.
Councilperson Maloney asked if it were possible to ask the county commissioners
to give Council more notice of future abatement hearings. Mayor Bragga said he
would write to the Commissioners and ask for three or four weeks notice of
future abatement hearings, so Council will have time to discuss it at Council
meeting.

Clerk-Treasurer Fisher told Council that Council has Payroll Reports from the
last two pay periods. There is also January month-end report. February is
closed out, but it was not completed by the time Council packets were
distributed. February’s month-end report will be
included in the next Council packet. There is a memo to Council on the Audit.
Although figures matched, SSI reports did not match up appropriately, so the
Auditors asked that the reports be resubmitted. Clerk-Treasurer is working with

earlier than usual. We received it last week, usually the Village receives it
in April.

Motion by Maloney to approve Chief Febel’s attendance at classes:

Mayor Bragga told Council that Chief Febel will be heading up a group which
will include the Safety Committee, Fire Chief, Emergency Rescue District, etc,
The Village will borrow from some other municipalities and come up with
protocols and SOP’s for various emergency situations. The Village is lacking in
that area for some reason, so this will be an opportunity to bring this group
together. If an emergency arises and the Chief is not available, for whatever
reason, the protocol will be in place to know who will do what has to be done.
The Village has done nothing wrong, it’s just good to be prepared. The Mayor
recounted the power outage in the Village last fall. It was handled okay, but
if procedure had been in place we would have known what to do.

Mayor
Mayor Bragga told Council that seven Ashtabula County Mayors met twice for the
purpose of forming an Ashtabula County Mayor’s organization to discuss issues
and help all communities.

Motion by Baxley for the second reading of Ordinance No. 04-O-2537
2nd
Roll: 3 yea; 2 nay; 1 abstained = 3 yea, 2 nay motion failed.
Council discussed the General Operating Levy of 1.75 mils and the .50 percent
Income Tax increase.
The General Operating Levy will end December 31, 2004. Council agreed that if
the Village wants to put it on the ballot in November, it must be to the Board
of Elections by the August filing date.
Mayor Bragga discussed with Council the options of not renewing the 1.75 mil
General Operating Levy, but adding a .50 percent Income Tax Increase to the
Village’s 1 percent Income Tax. Council agreed the .50 percent income tax
increase would not affect senior citizens on their property taxes. The income
tax increase would bring in more revenue than an operating levy.
Mayor Bragga suggested to Council that the Finance Committee, the Administrator
and Clerk-Treasurer get some facts and figures and report back to Council.

Service Dept.:
·   We were able to recover 80 Tons of grits (Snow traction material) from the
first street cleaning of the year. This will realize about an $800.00 saving on
material purchases in 2004.
·   I am recommending that we use this $800 savings and another $10,200 dollars
from the Material fund (Salt or MC70) to pay for the asphalt to pave South
Sycamore Street per attached letter of expected cost. The property owners would
petition for pavement and we will assess the property owners following the same
process that we used for Elliott Ave. I am asking for a motion to precede with
the process .
·   Leaf pickup will be included with the April and May brush pick up as long
as the leaves are properly bagged.
·   Brush pickup resumes on the first Monday of each month from April to
September.
·   Tree trimming of the new trees planted during the last six years is nearing
completion. This trimming is designed to promote the growth of a central leader
and future removal of all low branches (up to 10 feet from the ground).

·   No report
Recreation/Community Center :
·   Staff is actively working on grant applications.
·   Community park trails are being groomed to remove dead limbs, trees, and
add wood chips to keep hikers out of the mud.
·   Skate Park is back in operation.
·   Park benches have been bolted down to keep them in their intended location.
·   The play school had a surprise inspection from the State Board of Children
Services. It has been determined that the center will need to be licensed and
the process has started. This is a change in the state’s original requirements.
The center was told before we started the program they didn’t need to be
licensed.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Bid documents for the first half of the 2004 District Seven OPWC Round 18
(Woodside Pump Station Rehabilitation Project and Market Street Main Sewer
Lines Study) are complete. Clerk/Treasurer will advertise and I will make a
recommendation to Council after bids are opened.
·   Preliminary project scope for 2005 OPWC Round 19 has been completed. This
project will make improvements to the Main Pump Station, and increase emergency
power to enable the plant to run in the advent of a total power outage . I am
requesting a motion to proceed with preliminary work. Committee will meet to
review the scope of work and if acceptable ask for enabling legislation to be
prepared.
·   There are two repairs remaining from the list developed last year and one
new one.
·    In replacing one of the main blower motors it was noted that the fan
bearing was beginning to fail. We are replacing the bearings in the blower
along with the new motor.
·   The Comminutor (Trash Grinder) replacement is still in progress.

Service Dept.:
·   I am recommending that we use this $800 savings and another $10,200 dollars
from the Material fund (Salt or MC70) to pay for the asphalt to pave South
Sycamore Street per attached letter of expected cost. The property owners would
petition for pavement and we will assess the property owners following the same
process that we used for Elliott Ave. I am asking for a motion to proceed with
the process .
·   Leaf pickup will be included with the April and May brush pick up as long
as the leaves are bagged in village supplied biodegradable paper bags.
·   Brush pickup resumes on the first Monday of each month from April to
September.
·   For the sake of cleanliness and order we continue to stress that the brush
and leaves should only be put curbside the weekend before pickup.
·   Tree trimming of the new trees planted during the last six years is done
for the year.
·   The next scheduled tree work will be the removal of several dead trees
along Village Streets.
·   The stump removal, cleanup, and re-seeding will be done later this summer
when the ground has dried up.

current areas of emphasis. East Cedar, North Popular, South Sycamore, East
Erie, North Chestnut, and Hillyer.

for the play school.
·   Community park trails are being groomed to remove dead limbs, trees, and
add wood chips to keep hikers out of the mud.
·   Programs continue to grow.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Wastewater discovered an airline that had been leaking air underground
(undetected) for years. With an excellent spirit of urgency and cooperation
between the street department, wastewater, and vendor: Krzic Enterprises Inc.
we were able to have the pipe excavated, rusty section removed, pipe cleaned
and repaired, and the air circulation head rebuilt in a total of six hours. The
crew worked through lunch and when I bought coffee it got cold before being
consumed.
·   I was proud of their effort and want to publicly acknowledge a job well
done.
·   As a result of this repair, a valve that had to be fully open to deliver a
minimum amount of air to the raw sewer tank now only needs to be ¼ open.
·   This air leak was also affecting the air flow to the two digester tanks and
now we have much better air flow to them also.
·   The main blower motor and fan rebuild is complete.
·   Friday, the Ferric Chloride tank was cleaned and reworked to remove the
sludge that had accumulated over the years. This chemical treats the phosphates
to meet EPA standards. A loss of ability to inject this chemical could lead to
a waste stream out of standard and a potential EPA violation.
·   The following are active repairs known to remain.
·   The Comminutor (Trash Grinder) replacement is still in progress.
·   The EQ Tank pumps are going to be replaced/repaired as needed.
·   The emergency back up generator failed to start automatically when we shut
down power for the airline repair.
·   Final repairs at Thousand Trails are scheduled for May 4th.
·   April 23rd Control Associates will be doing an annual recalibrating of our
Chlorine treatment system before the May 1 required start up.
Finance/Appropriations/Budget:
·   Clerk/Treasurer has provided the tax revenue projections requested by
council.
Other Items:
·   Helicopter donation is moving forward.
·   Survey of parcel six of the Rush Creek property is complete.
·   Property owners with non conforming signs that are not grand fathered will
be notified week of April 19th and be given until the end of the month to
comply before formal citations are issued.

Finance  
There was discussion of the .50% increase in income tax as opposed to an
increase in property tax.
Council has two options to choose from: Pass an Ordinance to keep the 1.75 mils
on the ballot or pass an ordinance to increase the income tax by .50 S%.
Mayor Bragga said in order to maintain the services the Village provides, it is
imperative that whichever ordinance Council chooses it must be on the November
2, 2004 ballot.
Councilperson Baxley said that from what she has been hearing the people are
more in favor of an increase in income tax rather then an increase in property
tax.
Councilpersons Maloney and Fertig both said that the people they talked to seem
to lean toward an increase in income tax instead of an increase in property
tax.
It was noted that .50% taken out of a monthly paycheck is not that much and
might be preferable to a big amount on the property tax. People who work in the
Village also enjoy the many services provided by the Village.
The first reading of an ordinance must be no later then the first meeting in
June to allow for the three readings and the 30 days needed to have it put on
the November Ballot.
 
Motion by Thompson to direct the solicitor to draft legislation for language
for .50 % increase in income tax
2nd 
Roll: All yea, motion carried.

   Service Dept.:
·   Sidewalk snowplow ruts and scrapes have been dressed up for lawn mowing.
·   Leaf pickup will be included with the April and May brush pick up as long
as the leaves are bagged in village supplied biodegradable paper bags.
·   Brush pickup resumes on the first Monday of each month from April to
September.
·   For the sake of cleanliness and order we continue to stress that the brush
and leaves should only be put curbside the weekend before pickup.
·   Ditch work for storm water control is back in full operation with six
current areas of emphasis. East Cedar (Done), North Poplar, South Sycamore
(Done), East Erie (in progress), North Chestnut, and Hillyer.
Fire Dept.:
·   No report
Recreation/Community Center:
·   The new Village Community Center Van is in service and available for
council to look over.
·   Staff is actively working on licensing requirements for the play school.
·   Community park trails are being groomed to remove dead limbs, trees, and
add wood chips to keep hikers out of the mud.
·   Programs continue to grow with over 100 kids signed up for T Ball and over
50 kids the first day of registration for soccer.
·   We are looking at the other grant opportunities available for parks,
recreation, and seniors.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Ferric chloride tank cleaning is complete and in service
·   Chlorine treatment system has been checked and calibrated ready for the May
1 required start up.
·   EPA’s Erm Gomes visited our plant so we could update him on the
improvements that have been made and are planned.
·   I would like the Wastewater Committee to again visit the plant for another
update and status report in the near future.
·   Gary Lacate retook his Operator Class III test April 27th. He believes that
he did very well on this exam.
·   EPA has pointed out that time is running out for us operating with a class
two operator and if Gary is not successful on this test, we are going to have
to get a class three operator to monitor operations.
·   The following are active repairs known to remain.
·   The Comminutor (Trash Grinder) replacement is still in progress.
·   The EQ Tank pumps are going to be replaced/repaired as needed.
·   The emergency back up generator failed to start automatically when we shut
down power for the airline repair.
·   Final repairs at Thousand Trails are scheduled for May 4th.
Finance/Appropriations/Budget:
·   No Exceptions known
·   I request approval to attend The Fundamentals of Successful Construction
Projects in Ohio. (Flier included)
Other Items:
·   I took photos of a Helicopter in Bath, N. Y. and supplied them to Durward
and Lew Hayslett with a copy also in my office.
·   Property owners with non conforming signs that are not grand fathered have
been notified and most have already removed them and the rest are willing to
comply.

   Service Dept.:
·   The first village clean up day planning is complete. Seniors have been sent
letters offering help if needed (Copy included).
·   Select property owners with either junk vehicles or filthy accumulations
have been notified that they must correct the offense or the village will start
civil or criminal action (copy included).
·   Leaf pickup will be included with the April and May brush pick up as long
as the leaves are bagged in biodegradable paper bags purchased from the
village.
·   Brush pickup resumes on the first Monday of each month from April to
September.
·   For the sake of cleanliness and order we continue to stress that the brush
and leaves should only be put curbside the weekend before pickup.
·   Ditch work for storm water control is back in full operation with six
current areas of emphasis. East Cedar (Done), South Sycamore (Done), East Erie
(Done), North Poplar, North Chestnut, and Hillyer.
·   The first batch of tall grass notices will go out week of 5/17/04.

·   Committee to report
