·   The retired Village Community Center Van has been advertised as surplus
with a bid opening scheduled for June 2nd.
·   The enlargement of the playschool room is nearing completion.
·   Staff is actively working on licensing requirements for the playschool and
will schedule an inspection as soon as the State Department of Children’s
Services responds.
·   The new soccer fields are being groomed for the beginning of Soccer on June
8th.
·   Programs continue to grow with over 100 kids signed up for T Ball and over
120 kids for soccer.
·   The exchange club has released any interest in the pool table they donated
to the community center.
·   We have a request from the AA halfway house affiliated with Glenbay
Hospital for the Village to donate the pool table to them.
·   I would ask for a motion to allow this donation.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Chlorine treatment system has been activated for the summer months.
·   Final repairs at Thousand Trails are scheduled for May 4th.
·   The following are active repairs known to remain.
·   The Comminutor (Trash Grinder) replacement is still in progress.
·   The EQ Tank pumps are going to be replaced/repaired as needed.
·   The emergency back up generator fails to start automatically and must be
started manually when needed. The long term solution is to replace it as the
current engine can no longer be reasonably serviced

·   I was unable to attend The Fundamentals of Successful Construction Projects
in Ohio that council approved and did not complete the registration process or
make payment.

Village of Jefferson report in Excel based on the State supplied sample.
·   The financial data has been input and the State Auditor’s Office will
review it on Tuesday 5/18/04 for comment and acceptance.
·   Roni went above and beyond her normal job requirements spending upwards of
50 hours to complete this task. The future implications are that the Village
will not have to pay an outside agent up to $2,500 per year to do this report.

Service Dept.:
·   The first village clean up is complete.
·   Numerous seniors were assisted with pick up of heavy objects.
·   Twenty-seven property owners with either junk vehicles or filthy
accumulations were notified that they must correct the offense.
·   Dumpsters were provided at four resident locations due to the amount of
clean - up needed.
·   In access of 224 cubic yards of compacted waste/junk was collected and
hauled.
·   Over 166 tires were removed from the village.
·   Village crews at my direction and with the knowledge of the mayor and
solicitor forced clean – up at five residences.
·   On 5/27/04 nine junk vehicle owners were issued official notice that they
had three days to correct their junk vehicle complaint.
·   By 6/1/04 all but three were in full compliance and these three were moving
to compliance.
·   On 6/2/04 eleven additional junk vehicle offenders were served official
notice.
·   To date there have been over 15 junk vehicles removed from the village with
15 more in the process.
·   Tall grass notices were delivered to 16 property owners that must have
their grass cut by Friday June 4th. Note: (By June 2nd all but six were cut.)
·   Brush pickup continues to be a problem with brush set out far to early and
exposed far to long on the tree lawns.
·   For the sake of cleanliness and order we continue to stress that the brush
and leaves should only be put curbside the weekend before pickup.
·   Ditch work for storm water control is back in full operation with three
remaining areas of emphasis: North Poplar, North Chestnut, and Hillyer.
Fire Dept.:
·   Committee to report
Recreation/Community Center :
·   I recommend we accept the only bid of $501.50 for the surplus Village
Community Center Van.
·   The enlargement of the playschool room is complete.
·   Anita received an electrical shock while unplugging a treadmill that was
smoking. Anita is OK but still has a headache and aching teeth.
·   Staff is actively working on licensing requirements for the playschool and
will schedule an inspection as soon as the State Department of Children’s
Services responds.
·   The new soccer fields are groomed and ready for the beginning of Soccer on
June 8th with 160 kids signed up to participate.
·   All the play equipment is installed at the Jeffersonian Estates playground.
The Billy Cole donations were used to purchase this equipment and the family
will gather Sunday, June 13th for a dedication and remembrance at the park.

Mayor Bragga told Council that a total cost of the clean-up has not yet been
determined. There are still some outstanding charges. The dumpsters that were
provided at the Village expense, this year, were placed at the worst locations,
with the understanding that if the property is junky it has to be cleaned up.
In the future, the cost of the dumpsters will be passed on to the resident.
Mayor Bragga said the Village will continue to work on issues of unsightly
property. Money for clean up was budgeted in the Refuse Fund, and the cost was
less than that budgeted. Councilperson Fertig said most people he talked to
thought the clean-up project was a huge success and liked the idea of having an
annual “clean-up day”

   Service Dept.:

o    Material i.e. dumping and dumpsters.   $2,495.74

o   Tires excess cost:   $90.00
o   Labor      $1,248.00

·   First round of tall grass complaints have all been mowed.
·   Repainting of the village street markings (except centerlines) is complete.
·   On Friday the 25th of June the Jefferson Football players with Jason Root
will be assisting the street crew with some community service work.
·   June 29th we will be applying SRC02 (next step up from MC70) dust control
to Spruce Street, Mulberry Street, East Erie Street, East Pine Street, and
North Sycamore Street.
·   Ditch work for storm water control is stalled due to weather and other
priorities. We will restart in two weeks with three remaining areas of
emphasis: North Poplar, North Chestnut, and Hillyer.
·   Tree removal, trimming and stump removal is expected by mid July.

Mayor
Mayor Bragga thanked Council for reserving a little bit of time to discuss Ohio
Schools facility and he wants Council to be thinking in a pro-active fashion
with respect to facilities for the school district. One of the places that
Council can help and potentially be impacted is on location. Mayor Bragga said
he is obviously in favor of having the Jefferson Elementary Building in the
Village of Jefferson. The only way the Board can have it in the Village of
Jefferson is if they have the land. It’s been said, they are going to need 16
acres. Mayor Bragga said he will be meeting with the Board president to ride
around the Village to look at possible sites. It’s important for Council to
have a game plan to be able to contribute and assist in the planning and
construction of a much needed school facility to meet the needs of the
community. Council’s concern is, obviously, also income tax. There are a large
number of school employees who live in the Village and we would loose
significantly in terms of income tax if they leave the Village. The Mayor
encouraged Council to get involved, if possible. Try to attend meetings; it is
our community, it’s our schools and we do need them.

Planning Commission to serve out Lowell Masirovits’ term; which expires on 12/
31/04.

Clerk/Treasurer Report
Clerk-Treasurer Fisher told Council that Council Packet includes:
·   Payroll Report
·   June Month-End Report
Clerk-Treasurer Fisher said that the General Fund balance is only $92,000.
Anticipated revenue of 36,500 will go into the general fund with the sale of
property. We will be getting our income tax money and some local government
funds from the Auditor, but no big amount until October. Under the sewer/
revenue comparison, we’ve collected $275,000 this year compared to $304,000
last year. We have $33,000 in delinquent sewer bills. Roni Guerini, Utilities
Clerk, is sending out delinquent letters. They have until the end of August to
pay the delinquent amount. At the end of August, the delinquent balance will be
sent to the Auditor to be assessed to their property tax. The assessed amount
will not be collected from the Auditor for another year. Income Tax is about
right on line. We are collecting more money this year then we will collect the
beginning of next year because we are enforcing and collecting declaration
payments (estimated payment). Solicitor Lemire and Clerk-Treasurer Fisher are
going to court against those people who have defaulted on their payment plan.
When all avenues of collections have been exhausted, we can garnish wages,
which we intend to do.

new tile set on East Beech Street.

schedule. North Chestnut street is yet unscheduled.

progress.
·   The application of SRC02 (next step up from MC70) dust control to Spruce
Street, Mulberry Street, East Erie Street, East Pine, and North Sycamore Street
with excellent results and no complaints. In fact I have received five positive
comments on the street from residents I did not know.
·   Tree removal and trimming is complete except for future additions.
·   Brobst delayed stump removal until late August due to weather delays.
·   I have delayed scheduling Holden Arboretum for tree trimming and tree care
training until fall due to the lower priority of this project.
·   2004 paving bids will open today 7/30/04 and be included in the packet if
timely or at the 8/2/04 council meeting.

complete.

the estimated cost figures available to the property owners.

priority.
Recreation/Community Center :
·   The recreation department with the aid of the Chamber of Commerce sponsored
the return of the Circus to the Ashtabula County Fairgrounds. Early results
show this to be a profitable event. I will share final profits to the
recreation center when they are available.
·   The Recreation Center play school has received State of Ohio certification
as a day care center.
·   The staff is to be commended since the certification passed with flying
colors and no delays and took a lot of preparation time to complete and
present.
·   Repainting and fix up of the facility is nearing completion thanks to Walt
Burgwin’s perseverance.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Gary Licate will have to retake his Wastewater III exam again in November
having missed the cut off by one point.
·   Gary was advised that the State of Ohio is revising how they calculate the
scores due to the high (80%) failure rate. This change will be effective for
the November exam. He was also told that had this new scoring been in place he
would have passed the last two exams.
·   The following are active repairs known to remain.
·   The Comminutor (Trash Grinder) replacement is still in progress.
·   The fresh coat of paint is being quoted for select areas at the plant to
complete the face-lift before major OPWC Project begins.
·   Part one (east side collection system cleaning and televising) 0f 2004 OPWC
project can finally begin having received a verbal notice to proceed.
·   Part two (Woodside pump station repairs, upgrades, and stand-by power) is
advertised for bid with bid opening scheduled for August 17, 2004.
·   Our 2005 OPWC project (Main pump station repairs, upgrades, and stand-by
power to operate the entire plant) has been recommended for funding at the
local level. It has also been determined that the village will be able to
borrow our local share match at 0% interest.

Visitors Comments  
Dan Claypool, Lenox Township Trustee, addressed Council regarding the Lenox
Township fire contract. He said the Township supports the fire department’s
replacing the fire truck but is against hiring a full time fire inspector. Mr.
Claypool said that the new contract starts January 1, 2005. He said that even
if a levy passed in November, they would not collect until 2006. Mr. Claypool
said he didn’t understand the reasoning regarding the 4 equal payments. Lenox
Township usually pays 75% in April. Mr. Claypool said he would like Council to
reconsider the date of the contract and the method of payments – 4 equal
payments. He said it is better for the Township to pay the Village when the
money is received from the auditor.
Martha Demshar from Jefferson Township stated that Jefferson Township supports
the fire department, and also expressed the concerns registered by Dan Claypool
She stated that the April and October payment plan better suites the Jefferson
Township situation.
Demshar and Claypool again said both their governments are in favor of
supporting the volunteer fire department, but would like to have a joint
meeting with the safety committee to hammer out some of the details of the
contract.
Councilperson Maloney said she would set a date soon for the safety committee
meeting.
Durward Newhard gave and update on the helicopter memorial. Terms are being
drawn up for a 25-year lease between the Veterans and Lew Hayslett to be
recorded at the courthouse. Mr. Newhard is still working on transportation for
delivery of the helicopter.

Councilperson Fertig opened discussion on Thorne’s sign request. He said the
issue was forwarded to the Planning Commission. Administrator Finger said the
Planning Commission approved the request 4-1. The next step is to bring it
before Council.
Councilperson Baxley said she would open discussion since hers was the one
descending vote. She said, in reviewing Mr. Finger’s memo, he said the sign
code is a maximum of 50 sq. ft. She said that on a building of this size, she
agrees, that’s somewhat unreasonable. The CVS sign was 415 sq. ft, which was
828 % more than our code allowed. Now Thorne’s asking to go up 699, which is
1398 sq. ft % more than the code allowed. . Councilperson Baxley’s
recommendation to Council was not to accept the recommendation of the Planning
Commission. Perhaps BiLo could negotiate their request down. She asked if there
could be a compromise. After working with figures, she estimated a sign 469 sq.
ft., which is still more than they’ve got now and is more than the 800% of what
the code allows, is a good point to go from.
Councilperson Fertig stated a concern regarding a trailer parked on the south
side of the building and debris in the back of the building BiLo purchased.
Rod Confer, Director of Operations, said the area around the building will be
cleaned up and the storage trailers will be removed.
Paul Sekula, President of Sekula Sign Corporation, does work for Thorne Corp.
had color pictures of the building, and showed pictures of signs that they are
requesting.
Administrator Finger said any changes in signage for new businesses or
redeveloped businesses beyond the 50 sq. ft.goes through the Planning
Commission. This is the first time where an existing building is under new
development
Motion by Maloney that this discussion goes back to the Building and Lands and
Building and Lands discuss a compromise with Thorne’s
2nd

Service Dept.:
·   The Village finally received $447.86 from the sale of scrap metal collected
during this springs village clean up. This amount nearly covers the $600.00 we
paid for the dumpsters used on various sites in the village.
·   West Cedar Street open ditching scheduled for the week of 12/6 is delayed
due to weather.
·   Leaf and brush pick up has been suspended as the crews focus on snow
removal.
·   Snow parking ban is in effect as described in the attached Police letter
dated December 28th.
·   Christmas tree pickup dates are January 10, 18, 24 as described below.
·   § 660.19   CHRISTMAS TREE PICKUP SERVICE.
·      (a)   In the month of January of each year, the village will pick up
Christmas trees belonging to residents of the village which are placed at the
curb side. Said trees must be free of stands, trim and other objects. Trees
must not be covered by or contained within plastic bags or other material. The
date on which Christmas trees will be picked up will be selected by the Village
Administrator and will be announced in advance and published in a local
newspaper of general circulation within the village. The scheduled date for
Christmas tree pickup shall also be maintained on file at the office of the
Clerk.
·      (b)   Any Christmas tree placed at the curb for pickup by the village
that is rejected for any reason, or any tree placed at the curb for pickup
after the scheduled date for pickup, must be removed from the tree lawn within
48 hours after having been placed at the curb.
·      (c)   Whoever violates this section is guilty of a minor misdemeanor.
Punishment shall be provided in § 698.02.
·   (`80 Code, § 660.19) (Ord. 2189, passed 11-17-97)
·   A word of caution to vehicle drivers: Please slow down and be cautious of
our street crews while they are maintaining traffic safety. There were numerous
dangerous situations during this last snowfall, rain, and freeze. People
driving too fast for conditions, disregarding detour instructions, and
disregarding the safety of workers in the street. There will be zero tolerance
when drivers put others in danger!!

·   Snow Parking Ban is in effect.
·   Residents should take a few moments and shovel the snow from around fire
hydrants for ease of access in case of a fire.

Official
Mayor – State of the Village of Jefferson 2005
The 2004 year was a year of financial scrutiny and planning with the goal of
maintaining and improving village services, enhancing village infrastructure
and demonstrating the necessity of additional revenue. Council asked our
constituents to vote yes for an additional ½% income tax and reduced property
taxes by not replacing a 1.75 mill general operating levy. The failure of that
referendum in November of 2004 will cause a reduction in services, repairs,
maintenance, and equipment replacement needs in 2005 and beyond.
   The need for additional revenue has caused council to request our support of
a referendum to increase local income tax by ½ %. The funds generated by this
tax will be set aside to fund only the fire department, the police department
and other safety related issues. The passage of this referendum will reduce
general fund contributions to those departments.
I intend to continue to work and continue planning to improve all departments
of our village.
·   We have a street repair and paving plan, it is now behind schedule, we need
new dollars to maintain and improve our streets.
·   We must replace fire truck #411. This is a 1975 pumper –tanker. A new unit
will cost around $350,000.00 and will be a year in the making. The 1978 reserve
ladder truck #401is currently out of service.
·   Additional funds are needed to increase fire inspections in our fire
district.
·   We must continue to address the need to upgrade our waste water treatment
facility and all of the lines and pump stations in our system.
·   We need to develop a map of our storm sewer and storm drainage system.
There are currently no records or maps for this portion of our infrastructure.
·   Plans need to be developed for our existing park land. The survey of the
property is complete.
·   The Jefferson Community Center and recreation department must generate more
revenue from programs, rentals, memberships and usage. Earning more revenue
will reduce general fund contributions to the operation of the recreation
department.
    2004 saw the approval of several grants and the completion of some grant
programs.
·   The culvert replacement project on South Market St. was completed.
·   The televising and cleaning of all sewer lines on the east side of town
were completed. Three emergency repairs were completed to the lines. The
results of the televising will assist in the improvement of the system and help
in obtaining future funds for the waste water system.
·   The orphan well grant received in 2004 will be completed in 2005. This will
close the well that exists in our park land.
·   The OPWC grant to renovate the Woodside pump station is finalized.
Construction will begin in 2005.
·   The Ashtabula county block grant to improve storm drains in Jeffersonian
Estates on Jackson Street, Linden Street and the north end of Adams will be
completed in 2005.
·   The major safety grant for the intersection of route 46 North and state
route 307 has been approved by ODOT. Engineers will be selected and
construction plans will be developed in 2005. Project construction is expected
to occur in 2006 and 2007.
·   The Water Advisory Committee continues to develop plans and establish
priorities to improve service and fire flows. Aqua Ohio continues to be
diligent in making improvements to water lines. 2004 saw the replacement of the
water line on East Jefferson Street from Market to Sycamore.
    2004 saw the sale of 13 acres of residential land on the south side of
undeveloped East Pine Street. The majority of the money generated from the sale
is earmarked for the village share of the route 46 / route 307 safety grant.
The 4 .6 acre parcel of light industrial land on North Sycamore street and the
1 acre parcel of residential land in Jeffersonian Estates remains for sale as
surplus land.
   2005 will be a year of planning and completion of various grant based
projects. We will be considering applying for EPA grants and loans to continue
to improve waste water plant renovation and collection system repairs.
    Our current and challenging financial situation is caused by a variety of
reasons, including:
·   Reduction in local government funding
·   Increased fixed costs to normal and essential operations; electric costs,
fuel, gasoline, communications, increase in county dispatch services, employee
health care, Public Employee Retirement System increases, insurance premiums,
and natural gas costs.
·   The added costs of maintaining our current ISO rating for fire services.
·   The added costs of increasing duty pay and training pay for our volunteer
fire department members.
·   Increased costs in materials such as: paving, salt, road materials, pipe
and other consumable supplies
·   Decrease in income tax revenue do to fewer jobs and fewer businesses in the
village.
·   The continued effort to operate a recreation department and pay the annual
bond payment of $95,400.00 on the recreation building.
    Our efforts to just maintain essential services will require additional
funding. Failure to secure additional revenue will cause personnel cuts, limit
our ability to replace old equipment, limit our ability to purchase repair
materials and cause additional cuts throughout all departments.
    It will be necessary to enlist the leadership and assistance of some
residents to work on a campaign to pass a necessary income tax referendum or
property tax levies to address the financial shortfall.
   It is my desire to keep our community a safe and most desirable place to
live in northeastern Ohio. Our village is the best! We need to be informed and
support efforts to keep it that way!
Old Business/New Business
   Council will have a resolution drawn up to be presented at the next meeting
approving participation in forming the Northeast Ohio League for Leadership and
Advocacy (NOLLA), a voluntary organization comprised of elected officials from
township, municipal and county governments that prioritize issues, devise
strategic action and methods for meaningful impact and influence on elected
officials of the state and federal government.

Bill Hale with Community and Economic Corp addressed the Council regarding
property purchased on Jefferson St. He shared the projected plans for the
property, and said they plan to meet with the Mayor and Village Administrator
to discuss the options available then take it back to the Planning commission.
Their goal is to make a positive contribution to the community.
The first phase of their plan is to rehabilitate 32 rental units on the
property, and they are asking Council for a resolution as an endorsement for
the renovation of those units as a part of an application to get funding
assistance.
Mayor Bragga told them to draw up the proposed resolution to be presented to
the Building and Lands Committee for approval. Then Building and Lands will
bring the recommendation to Council. The rules of council can be suspended to
enable the resolution to be passed to meet a timeline if necessary.

Service Dept.:
·   The Village Street Department trucks are all back in operation after
repairs to two truck ABS systems (wetness related) and one trucks on board
computer.
·   West Cedar Street open ditching is scheduled as weather permits.for the
week of 12/6 is delayed due to weather.
·   Christmas tree pickup continues on the announced dates of January 10, 18,
24.
·   The streetlights order for West Mulberry St. has been confirmed by First
Energy. Due to the fact that they are going to have to run new wires,
installation could take four to six weeks.
·   The Light at the Helicopter site is also confirmed and should be completed
within a week.
Fire Dept./Police Department
·   Activity reports are in your packets for police and fire.
·   The police department has implemented the new on line reporting routine
required by First Energy for streetlight problems. There were six complaints
entered with almost immediate feedback from First Energy on confirmation of
receipt. Within one day they had received work order numbers and are tracking
response time to those work orders. We have agreed to meet with First Energy
again if response is too slow.
Recreation/Community Center :
·   I have asked the recreation department for a motion to approve the new part
time program staff person.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   The plant along with many others in Ohio bypassed due to the heavy rains.
·   The waterline to the Elm Street pump station is broken and was shut off
until repaired. Low impact.
·   The EQ basin pump failure has been repaired and is back in operation.
·   Electrical repairs were completed to the main breaker to the press
building. The breaker was replaced.
Finance/Appropriations/Budget:
·   Year-end closings are going well according to Patty.

None to report

Service Dept.
·   The Street crew is working with minimal overtime. They have worked a flexed
schedule and only worked overtime as a result of call outs for safety reasons.
·   For instance, Saturday, January 29, there was a water line leaking
downtown. Steve Fable and I with the help of one street department employee
handled everything until the water company could get mobilized.
·   A Village Street Department truck is down waiting for a new oil pan. All
trucks are showing heavy rust damage.
·   West Cedar Street open ditching will be scheduled as weather permits.
·   Christmas tree pickup finished Feb 2, 2005.
·   First Energy has scheduled the three streetlights for West Mulberry Street.
Due to the fact that they are going to have to run new wires; installation
could take four to six weeks.
·   The Light at the Helicopter site has been installed and is operational.
·   The spotlights at the Veterans Memorial have received temporary repairs.
They will be replaced as soon as good weather comes due to excessive corrosion.
·   John Buzzard Submitted a letter of intention to retire effective as soon
after April 1, 2005 as the paperwork process allows.
Fire Dept./Police Department
·   The police department has implemented the new on line reporting routine
required by First Energy for streetlight problems. There were six complaints
entered with almost immediate feedback from First Energy on confirmation of
receipt. Within one day they had received work order numbers and are tracking
response time to those work orders. We have agreed to meet with First Energy
again if response is too slow.
·   First Energy is actively involved in our complaint about slow service.
Recreation/Community Center:
·   The Village has submitted a letter of intent to ODOT. We have asked for
$145,000 to improve our trails in the park. If this request receives any hope
of funding there will be a formal application and always the right of refusal.
·   New Treadmill donated by SOCC is due to be delivered Monday the 7th.
·   The Planning commission is working on establishing a park district.
·   The Park as discussed and moved by council is in the process of being
platted and then recorded.
·   I am making the recommendation to renew Anita’s employment contract under
its present terms for another year. I ask that a motion come from the
Recreation Committee and need that added to the agenda.
 Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   There have been a high number of maintenance type repairs needed recently.
All are being scheduled with minimal overtime.
·   Repairs are in process on a valve, grinder, and pump to enable proper flow
to the press building.
·   The waterline to the Elm Street pump station is broken and was shut off
until repaired. Low impact.
·   A natural gas leak was detected and repaired.
·   An electrical panel needs to be serviced due to moisture damage from
condensation.
Finance/Appropriations/Budget:
·   I ask council for a motion to authorize me to enter a contract with Love
Insurance agency for liability insurance coverage through the Arrowhead Public
Risk Municipal Package Plan.
·   The Arrowhead Package will give us comparable coverage for about $4,000.00
less a year.
·   I need to ask finance committee to suspend the three reading rule and move
to adopt the wage ordinance to enable us to pay our part time program
instructor his proper rate.
Other Items:
I am referring a rezoning matter to council for their consideration
Mr. Mark Holden asked that since the Planning Commission turned down his
request what was his next step could be. His next step is to present his
argument to the Village Council.
If Council wishes to rezone his property and modify the Planning Commission
decision to deny it will take a super majority or a vote of five in favor of
rezoning.
I am asking Council how they want to proceed. (Refer to building and lands)
(Discuss tonight) (Vote to overturn Planning Commission) (Vote to support the
Planning Commission recommendation).

Visitors Comments 
Mike Bogo representing Neighborhood Development said he was present at the
meeting to clarify any issues with the request for a resolution regarding the
rehabilitation of the property known as Jefferson Courtyard Apartments. A
letter was faxed to Council on February 18 with points for consideration. After
reviewing the letter, with minor adjustments agreed to by both parties, Council
approved the document.
Dee Ringer, President of the Jefferson Garden Club, asked about the status of
the Village flowers being watered this summer, since John Buzzard is retiring.
Mayor Bragga said that because of the Village’s financial situation, the
recommendation to the Council would be to not fill the position at this time.
The Mayor told Mrs. Ringer that the Village is appreciative of all the Garden
Club does for the Village, and it is with regret that the Village can’t commit
to the watering of the flowers this summer. There’s a possibility that the
Chamber of Commerce would be able to help out.
Administrator Finger read a report from Durward Newhard on the status of the
helicopter project. The lights are in and the flagpoles will be installed as
soon the weather permits. Mr. Newhard said thank you letters have been sent
out, and he wanted to especially thank Martha for all of her hard work There
will be a meeting on March 3, 2005 at 3.p.m. which is critical to the
completion of the project.

Service Dept.:
·   The Street crew is continuing to work with minimal overtime.
·   West Cedar Street open ditching was started 2/8/05 but discontinued due to
snow. We will resume work as weather permits.
·   First Energy has installed the three streetlights for West Mulberry Street.
Jackie Heath called me at home to deliver a heartfelt thank you from her and
the neighbors.
·   If you are out and about take a drive and look for yourself.
·   There are no plans at this time to replace John Buzzard upon his
retirement.
Fire Dept./Police Department
·   The police department has implemented the new on line reporting routine
required by First Energy for streetlight problems. There were six complaints
entered with almost immediate feedback from First Energy on confirmation of
receipt. Within one day they had received work order numbers and are tracking
response time to those work orders. We have agreed to meet with First Energy
again if response is too slow.
·   Still no response from First Energy regarding these repairs.
Recreation/Community Center:
·   New Treadmill donated by SOCC was delivered and is in service. I have heard
a lot of positive feedback about it.
·   The Park, as discussed and moved by council, is in the process of being
platted and then recorded
·   A drawing was prepared for the park showing some previously recommended
improvements.
·   Anita was given written notice that the Village was not renewing her
contract.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   The plant is getting back to more normal operation as repairs are
completed.
·   There have been a high number of maintenance type repairs needed recently.
All are being scheduled with minimal overtime.
·   I shot several photos of repairs I reported last meeting that are in
process or have been complete. I am not sure everyone understands the high
level of skill, and demanding physical labor involved.
·   The waterline to the Elm Street pump station is broken and was shut off
until repaired. Low impact.
·   The electrical panel was repaired.
Finance/Appropriations/Budget:
·   I ask council for a motion to authorize me to start the process to find a
design firm to prepare the drawings and specifications for the safety grant.
·   Included in your packet is the selection process that has been approved by
the State for selecting the Professional Design Firm. Jerry has recommended
codifying it so that it will be a part of our ordinance book.
Other Items:
Mr. Marty Holden submitted his zoning interpretation question in writing and
Jerry is preparing a reply.

Resolution No. 05-R- 2574
A Resolution in support of the Housing Credit Program Proposed by the Community
and Economic Development Corporation to Acquire and Rehabilitate the Property
known as Jefferson Courtyard Apartments.
Councilperson Baxley asked that the February 18, 2005 letter from Community &
Economic Development Corporation be entered into the minutes for official
record:
Dear Council,
I want to thank all of your for meeting with me regarding the renovation at
Jefferson Courtyard.
I think we agreed to the following:
1.    Our temporary relocation plan will include:
   A.   We will pay all moving expenses, rent and utilities (including phone
and cable) for each tenant for each move required.
   B.   We will give the tenants at least 3 options as to where to relocate
off-site if that becomes necessary.
   C.   We will develop the plan such that the tenants who wish can move back
into the unit from which they had to temporarily relocate.
   D.   Prior to any movement we will meet with each tenant privately so we can
address any special needs or circumstances.
2.   We will work with you to explore the possibility of placing mobile units
or some type of acceptable temporary housing on the site or the adjacent land
to enable temporary relocation to occur on-site.
3.   We will work with the architect to develop a second means of egress from
the back of the unit. (The development staff has already had discussions about
doing such and adding a small concrete pad at the rear of the unit for another
project, so they did not see this as a major issue).
   The estimated cost for the acquisition and rehab is approximately
$3,000,000.
The calendar for adoption of the resolution of support for the tax credit
application (rehab only) is:
1.   First reading 2/22/05
2.   Second Reading and passage on 3/07/05
   Again, I want to stress that our interests are the same in that we are both
concerned with the residents and their quality of life. Providing quality
affordable housing and quality customer based management is the mission of our
non-profit.
   Please feel free to mark this up or suggest changes.
   Throughout this entire sequence of events I welcome your input and feedback
both regarding construction issues and, especially, the residents.
Again, my thanks for the time you have invested in assuring a quality project.
Sincerely,
(Signed) Dave Vaughan
cc: Mayor Larry Bragga

Visitors Comments –
Mayor Bragga recognized Boy Scout Troup #41. John Patterson said that the boys
are working on their badges, and part of the requirement if to attend a public
meeting.
Mayor Bragga told the boys that at the end of the meeting there are visitor’s
comments – and if they have any questions – at the end of the meeting they can
be recognized.
John Patterson said they have to be back at the church by 8:30- so they won’t
be able to stay until the end.
Mick Prochko told Council that he and his wife, Kathy, have been involved with
farmer’s markets for over five years. They have been asked if a farm market
could be started in Jefferson. His request is to set-up a farmer’s market at
the Jefferson Community Center parking lot on Fridays from 1;00 p.m. until 5:00
p.m. Fresh locally grown produce would be offered. Vendors sign an agreement
that they grow the items sold. Councilperson Baxley said the Gazebo a good
location. The Jefferson Garden Club has its annual plant and flower sale at the
Gazebo with great success.
Motion by Baxley to have Administrator Finger and Mayor Bragga draw up a
contract for use of the Gazebo for a Farmer’s Market, and the agreement therein
2nd
Mich Prochko said there would be signed agreements from the vendors, also.
Roll: All yea, motion carried.
Mayor Bragga recognized visitor Jacqueline Heath, representing Brittany Lane
residents. She thanked Council for responding to their request for lighting on
Mulberry Street. The residents believe the newly installed street lights will
help prevent dangerous situations for drivers, bikers, and walkers in that
area.
Mayor Bragga explained for the benefit of the Boy Scout Troup – that the
request from the citizen was that there was a street that needed some street
lights. It was dark and there were safety concerns. The proper protocol was
that the citizen came to Council and made the request known. It took Council a
few months to work the wrinkles out, and finally got the lights installed. Now
the citizen is back and very happy. That just a small example of how positive
citizen involvement can help to make local government work. – Pretty neat!

Service Dept.:
·   The Street crew is continuing to work with minimal overtime.
·   Aqua Ohio has had to repair two broken water mains, Jefferson Street by the
Elementary School and downtown in front of The Deli.
·   West Cedar Street open ditching was started 2/8/05 but discontinued due to
snow. We will resume work as weather permits.
·   John Buzzard gave me a proposal to water the hanging flower baskets
provided by the Garden Club. It looks like the Chamber of Commerce will
contract John independent of the village to continue to water the baskets. John
will use his own tractor, gas, water and Garden Club provided fertilizer. The
Village will retain ownership of the sprayer and allow the Chamber to use it.
·   If residents question why John is still watering the flowers make sure to
tell them to thank the Garden Club and Chamber of Commerce for keeping downtown
beautiful.
Fire Dept./Police Department
·   First Energy has looked at out streetlights, repaired some and determined
that they will have to straighten poles and replace underground wiring on many
in the spring.
Recreation/Community Center:
·   Income revenue and expenses have been on target for January and February.
·   The Park, as discussed and moved by council, is in the process of being
platted and then recorded
·   The Park Development Committee met March 2 to discuss grants and civic
group involvement on the park.
·   The Village has received an invitation to apply for the ODOT trails grant I
made reference to last meeting. The grant estimate is $145,000.
·   There is a resolution in your packet authorizing me to prepare the grant.
Cost estimate is $500.00 for document preparation. If you vote to proceed, the
grant will cover 80% of the construction costs but none of the yet undetermined
costs for engineering work, environmental studies or future upkeep. There are
at least two civic groups (SOCC and Rotary) who have expressed interest in
working with the village to make this park a reality.
·   There is a high degree of probability that the State of Ohio could fund
100% of Construction and the Village engineering costs and studies would be
counted as our contribution.
·   We always have the right to refuse this grant before committing the real
dollars, if money is not available.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   The plant repairs continue as planned.
·   Wastewater Committee is scheduled to meet March 14, 11:00 AM in the
committee room of town hall. We will provide an update on repairs, review the
treatment fees, give an update on projects, and review the EPA inspection
letter and approval of our license to operate the Plant.
Finance/Appropriations/Budget:
·   Nothing unusual to report.
Other Items:
·   Nothing to report

Visitors Comments
Shawn Osbourne asked if being on the SOCC board influences Council members
opinion regarding the Recreation Director. Cayce Baxley said the SOCC board is
mainly a fund raising organization, which is removed from the running of the
Recreation Center. Mr. Osbourne asked how the Director is expected to account
for her time? What benefit is hourly as opposed to salary? Councilperson Baxley
said that where a contract is concerned, there is no record of time worked;
hourly workers use a time clock. Councilperson Baxley said that there have been
Recreation Committee meetings that are open to the public, and any decisions to
be made are voted on by Council..
Anita Perrotti reserved the right to speak under the Recreation portion of the
meeting.

Service Dept.:
·   The Street crew is continuing to work with minimal overtime.
·   We are in the process of preparing a master drawing of the Village Storm
Drain System.
·   This work MUST BE DONE !!! EPA mandates that we SHALL find and cure our
storm water infiltration into our sanitary sewer system. This amounts to
600,000 gallons a day during a heavy rain.
·   High infiltration areas have been identified as South Chestnut (Erie to
Jefferson), East Satin Street (South Chestnut to South Market) and East Walnut
Street (North Chestnut to North Market).
·   The village has no drawings to show pipe location, size, or type; nothing
showing direction of flow; and nothing showing catch basin and grate type,
location, and size. You will see street department employees, wastewater
employees and me measuring, sketching, and digging holes to get the
documentation we need for a master plan.
·   West Cedar Street open ditching was started 2/8/05 but discontinued due to
snow. We will resume work as weather permits.
·   The Street Department has more projects than we have manpower, or money to
complete.
Fire Dept./Police Department
·   First Energy continues to work with us to correct streetlight problems.
They repair those that they can and have determined that they will have to
delay many until good weather in the spring.
Recreation/Community Center:
·   Breakfast with the Easter Bunny will be Saturday March 19. Thorns BiLo
donated food and free photos with the bunny and Subway donated money for gifts
to each child.
·   As a token of appreciation Mayor Bragga has approved a free Corporate
Membership to each. The recreation staff is preparing a flyer for distribution
to employees of Corporate Sponsors to explain the benefits.
·   Jefferson School Board approved purchase of a Corporate Membership.
·   Saturday the 19th evening there will be another teen dance sponsored by
Police Athletic League.
·   Saturday April 2nd there will be a craft show during the day and then
beginning at 6:00 PM another Texas Holdum Tournament sponsored by the Chamber
of Commerce. Profits from this tournament have been earmarked to pay for
watering and care of the hanging flower baskets in the business district.
·   Sign up for activities during spring break are very low.
·   Sign up for JAGS and Little League are also running 1/3 less than prior
years.
·   The Billy Joel Cole family is having a benefit Barbecue Dinner at the
Eagles April 2nd with proceeds earmarked for purchase of more playground
equipment for village parks.
·   The application for the ODOT trails grant I made reference to last meeting
will be submitted by April 1, 2005. The grant estimate is $145,000.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   The plant repairs continue as planned.
·   Wastewater Committee is asked to reschedule a meeting date and time. We
will provide an update on repairs, review the treatment fees, give an update on
projects, and review the EPA inspection letter and approval of our license to
operate the Plant.
Finance/Appropriations/Budget:
·   Nothing unusual to report.
Other Items: 
·   The drawing used by the census bureau was updated and submitted to
Washington. The update added our new annexations, street name changes, and new
streets.
·   The Village’s answer to Marty Holden’s questions on the interpretation of
zoning code is included in your packet and was sent to Mr. Holden.
Clerk/Treasurer Report
Clerk-Treasurer told Council their packets include:
·   Payroll reports with overtime on the last page – overtime has been limited
·   January and February month-end
We have not received property tax revenue from the Auditor due to the county’s
financial situation.
Also, the county’s layoffs will affect our income tax

Recreation  
Motion by Herndon that the Village of Jefferson offer Anita Perrotti a position
as an hourly working supervisor for the Recreation/Parks Department at $15.00
per hour, with no written contract
2nd
Discussion followed: Clerk-Treasurer told Council the $15 per hour figure was
arrived at by averaging the wages of salaried and hourly department heads
within the village She said that if Anita Perrotti worked 5 hours a week
overtime, she would make the same as she makes at the $17.14 an hour as a
salaried employee.
Mayor Bragga pointed out that he has directed village leadership to avoid all
overtime, except for emergencies, so Council could not count on Perrotti
getting the extra money cut from her salary.
Councilperson Maloney said she did not understand the reasoning behind changing
from a director to a supervisor.
Councilperson Herndon, who chairs the village’s recreation committee and made
the motion to change the director’s title and salary, said she believed her
actions are to the betterment of the village.
Roll: Herndon, yea; Maloney, nay; Stasny, yea; Thompson, nay; Baxley, yea;
Fertig, yea
Roll: 4-yea; 2-nay, motion carried.
Motion by Herndon to suspend Councils Rules
2nd
Roll: Herndon, yea; Maloney, nay; Stasny, yea; Thompson, nay; Baxley, yea;
Fertig, yea
Roll: 4-yea; 2-nay, motion failed

Service Dept.:
·   The Street crew is fully occupied with brush pick-up which will take almost
two full weeks for four people.
·   We are in the process of preparing a master drawing of the Village Storm
Drain System as time permits.
·   West Cedar Street open ditching was started 2/8/05 but discontinued due to
snow. We will resume work as time priorities and weather permit.
·   Parks and Village owned properties need to be cleaned up after the last
snowstorm, as there was considerable evergreen damage.
·   The Street Department has more projects than we have manpower, or money to
complete.
Fire Dept./Police Department
·   First Energy continues to promise but not deliver on correcting streetlight
problems. Any light pole with Green Tape has been reported to First Energy.
·   Out of twenty reported problems one has been repaired and others are
scheduled for follow up repairs. Dianne Tressler is coordinating activities
with First Energy.
Recreation/Community Center:
·   Anita will start as an hourly supervisor for all time worked after April
22.
·   The Center was successful in obtaining an $11,000.00 grant to supply
emergency flashing light adapters for Senior Citizens.
·   If an emergency call is made to Police, Fire, or EMT the occupant can
activate the flashing light as a beacon for ease in finding the address. The
coverage area includes the Township and Village.
·   Our Challenge is to find the money to purchase the adapters so we can then
be reimbursed by the Senior Grant Money.
·   This project can be treated like the circus was last year. We need to amend
the budget and expenses to cover the project. Clerk/Treasurer would have to
transfer money early to allow the purchase order to be written.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   The plant repairs continue as planned.
·   Wastewater Committee met on April 11, 2005 at 10:30. We provided an update
on repairs, reviewed the treatment fees, gave an update on projects, and
reviewed the EPA inspection letter and approval of our license to operate the
Plant.
·   The Village received a request to extend Sewer lines to Harassments Tavern
north of town. Village ordinances do not allow extension outside the village
limits without approval of council. I recommend that we do not extend the sewer
service and will so notify them in writing unless council directs me otherwise.
Finance/Appropriations/Budget:
·   Nothing unusual to report.
Other Items: 
·   I am supplying information to Department of Natural Resources to enable
them to update the Floodplain information for the village. The Department will
be using Digital drawing information for greater accuracy.
·   I am asking Council to suspend the three reading rule on two ordinances in
Building and Lands committee:
o   Acceptance of the plat for The PUD which is unchanged from the final
drawings which were discussed and approved by both the planning Commission and
Council. This plat has been completely checked by Smolen Engineering for
correctness and accuracy.
o   The second one modifies the provision that prevents new construction on
unopened and accepted streets as long as there is a financial instrument (Bond,
Escrow Account, or other acceptable set aside of funds) to complete the street.
Clerk/Treasurer Report
Clerk-Treasurer included the Payroll report in the Council packets.

Councilperson Thompson said he contacted the Ohio Ethics Commission to ask for
a ruling regarding a conflict of interest status, since he is employed by the
Jefferson Area Local Schools. Their ruling was that he should abstain. The
Jefferson Area Local School also employs Ken Fertig so the ruling would also
apply to him.

until the following month.
·   We are in the process of preparing a master drawing of the Village Storm
Drain System as time permits.
·   West Cedar Street open ditching was started 2/8/05 but discontinued due to

trees and brush.

streetlight problems.
·   I told them that if our problems are not corrected by the end of May we

council meeting.

Service Dept.:
·   The Street crew completed May brush pick up. Next brush pick up will begin
the week of June 6, 2005.
·   Parks and Village owned properties are being cleaned up to remove damaged
trees and brush.
·   Villagewide clean up is scheduled for Saturday June 18, 2005. Anyone
needing help with trash/rubbish outside the dwelling should contact Terry
Finger at 576 – 3941 so we can plan assistance.
·   We are in the process of preparing a master drawing of the Village Storm
Drain System as time permits.
·   West Cedar Street open ditching was started 2/8/05 but discontinued due to
snow. We will resume work as time priorities and weather permit.
·   Street Department has been actively involved with the Storm Drain
improvements on Jackson and Linden Street, which is Block Grant funded.
·   Students from Rick Hoyson’s class will be cleaning up downtown Sunday May
22.
Fire Dept./Police Department
·   We have planned an emergency siren test for June 8, 2005 at 11:00 AM. After
this test we will publish a schedule for the rest of the year.
·   The Police Department and I met again with First Energy concerning
streetlight problems.
·   I told them that if our problems were not corrected by the end of May we
would put the money for the street light bill in an escrow account
·   I am asking that the Clerk Treasurer set up that escrow account to receive
payment of the street lighting bills into that account until authorized to
release the money to First Energy.
Recreation/Community Center:
·   The Recreation Committee has recommended a new draft job description for
the supervisor of Recreation, Parks and Community Affairs.
·   Jason Tobie has turned in his resignation letter from the part time program
instructor job effective May 18, 2005.
·   Janet Butler has agreed to fill in at Jason’s rate of pay until we can
replace Jason. She will be working T- Ball and Soccer and as otherwise
scheduled.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   The waterline repair has been completed.
·   Lab test results for the Digester’s contents show no hazardous material in
our waste stream. Cleaning is scheduled for 05/16/05 with disposal at a normal
landfill.
·   Once the digester cleaning is complete we can proceed with grinder, pump
and valve replacements that I presented earlier this year.
·   Woodside pump station rehab should begin first of June.
Finance/Appropriations/Budget:
·   The Income tax levy passed! Thanks to all who helped in any way:
·   I included a copy of the placemat, which represents the commitment outlined
in the Mayors notes to residents.
·   The Mayor and I are focusing on our commitment to the voters and moving
forward with:
o   Fire Truck specifications for replacement of the 1975 truck
o   Fire Hall roof replacement estimate
o   Estimate to replace the Heating System for the fire hall.
o   Estimate to replace certain doors and windows for the fire hall.
o   Review of all roads and a revised paving schedule for 2006 to 2010.
o   Evaluating manpower for the Street Department to replace John Buzzard this
year and plan for Roland’s replacement in 2006
o   Capitol equipment replacement plan update
o   Facility maintenance improvement plan for the future
·   Other items that must be put back on the table for priority considerations
are:
o   Parking agreement with downtown merchants
o   Paving West Cedar Street by assessment of the property owners
o   Paving South Sycamore Street by assessment of property owners
o   Infrastructure improvements in support of the new schools.
Other Items: 
·   A security review of all Village facilities has commenced with lock changes
ordered and more dead bolt systems installed on some doors.
·   Tire replacement purchase complaint.
Farmer’s Market will begin in July and be held on Friday afternoons. With the
proper approval, banners will be displayed across the road. To participate in
Market Day the vendor must have grown the produce. Hopefully, it will be a big
success. Most of the people are Jefferson Area residents. It will be held at
the Community Center because there is more room then at the Gazebo.

Mayor Bragga informed Council that he and Administrator Finger are pursuing a
possible source of a revenue stream - a potential gas well on the Rush Creek
Property. There’s an excellent well in another nearby area. Basically,
Solicitor Lemire has been in contact with some folks and he’s going to be
reviewing that information. It could be a revenue stream that could possibly be
used to offset the cost of heating or in terms of park improvement. It’s just
another thing that is being explored.

Councilperson Baxley said Adelphia would be discussed under correspondence. She
said her only other concern was that there were 27 ½ hours of overtime in WWTP.
Administrator Finger said waterline repair shut the power off at Wastewater
facility. They had to work the hours because the plant couldn’t be down any
longer than absolutely necessary..
Building/Lands
Councilperson Fertig asked why it was necessary to table Ordinance 05-O-2595.
Administrator Finger said that ordinance is an ordinance vacating a portion of
East Pine Street where it intersects the eastern boundary of the right of way
for North Sycamore. He said that they had forgotten there is a sewer trunk line
that extends about 100 feet there to the east in the Pine Street right of way.
It has to be surveyed, with the easement described and registered, before it’s
abandoned. Mayor Bragga said the ordinance would be tabled until we get the
needed documentation, at which time the ordinance will be brought back for the
final reading.

Service Dept.:
·   June brush pick up began today June 6, 2005.
·   Parks and Village owned properties are being cleaned up to remove damaged
trees and brush.
·   Village wide clean up is scheduled for Saturday June 18, 2005. Anyone
needing help with trash/rubbish outside the dwelling should contact Terry
Finger at 576 – 3941 so we can plan assistance.
·   We are in the process of preparing a master drawing of the Village Storm
Drain System as time permits.
·   West Cedar Street open ditching will resume after brush pick up this week.
·   Street Department has been actively involved with the Storm Drain
improvements on Jackson and Linden Street, which is Block Grant funded. All the
pipe is in the ground. Top work is being completed this week.
·   The orphan well is removed with little or no damage to the surrounding
area. They did a nice job.
Fire Dept./Police Department
·   We have planned an emergency siren test for June 8, 2005 at 11:00 AM. After
this test we will publish a schedule for the rest of the year.
·   I have had a follow up phone conversation with First Energy concerning
streetlight problems and they were under the impression that everything was
fixed.
·   I told them that the crooked light poles on our complaint list also needed
to be straightened.
Recreation/Community Center:
·   A new draft job description for the supervisor of Recreation, Parks and
Community Affairs was placed in Council mailboxes for your review.
·   Sample Copies of some of the monthly reports from the recreation department
are in your packet. Anita, Patti and I continue to work to streamline the
process so council will get useful ones.
·   The first completed set will be in the June 20 council packet and at the
second meeting of each month thereafter.
·   Janet Butler has agreed to volunteer to coach T- Ball and Soccer but will
be unable to work other hours.
·   I have given Anita the go ahead to re-employ Patrick Bartone as the part
time Program Coordinator until we can hire a replacement for Jason.
·   A classified ad will run for two weeks
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   The waterline repair has been completed.
·   Cleaning of the digester is complete and the tank is back in operation.
·   EQ tank pump replacement is complete and EQ is at 100% condition.
·   The cement work to fill the unused settling tank and provide additional
parking is scheduled.
·   With the digester clean we can precede with the grinder, pump and valve
replacements that I presented earlier this year.
·   Woodside pump station rehab is scheduled for June 6th or 7th.
Finance/Appropriations/Budget:
·   The Recreation department revenue is behind the projection and is being
monitored.
·   Expenses and revenue must balance at year end and adjustments made as
needed.
Other Items: 
·   A security review of all Village facilities was completed and new keys
provided as needed. These were the only changes made at this time.
Clerk/Treasurer Report
Clerk-Treasurer told Council that the Payroll and Month-end reports are in
their agenda packets.
Clerk-Treasurer explained to Council the cover sheet for the month-ed reports
details that collections in the Income Tax Department, Wastewater Treatment
Department and Recreation Department are up-to-date per month.

Resolution No. 05-R-2598
A resolution for the submission to the electors of the Jefferson Village-
Jefferson Township Joint Union Cemetery District. Ashtabula County, Ohio, on
the 8th day of November 2005, of the question of the replacement levy on .75
mill per year for five years for each dollar of the taxable property within the
Village of Jefferson and the Township of Jefferson, Ashtabula County, Ohio, for
the purpose of paying the current operating and maintenance expenses of the
Jefferson Village –Jefferson Township Joint Union Cemetery District, in
accordance with the provisions of sections 759.34, 5705.19 and 5705.25 of the
Ohio Revised Code. Said levy to appear upon the tax duplicate of said Village
of Jefferson and Township of Jefferson, Ashtabula County, Ohio, for the tax
years 2005 to 2009 inclusive.

basins.

Personnel Issue:
Section 254.20F of our village ordinances says:
Upon delivery of an oral or written reprimand the appropriate department head
shall forward to the Mayor and/or Village Administrator a copy of such
discipline, including explanatory documents or memorandums. If a department
head, the Mayor and/or the Village Administrator are considering suspension,
discharge, or another form of discipline; he or she shall first consult with
Council. The purpose of this section is to ensure uniform administration of
discipline throughout the village.
On 7/14/2005 I presented Anita with a performance review that contained a
written warning. Anita read and signed the review stating that she had areas of
disagreement. Anita has been offered the opportunity to reply in writing and
when this takes place we will meet to discuss her reply.
I redirected Anita to section 254.20 to review several sections with her to
make sure she understood proper procedures.
Once the proper procedures are followed and the performance evaluation is filed
it can be reviewed by the appointing authority.
At this time there are no pending additional disciplinary actions. Council will
be kept informed as required.

Motion by Maloney to go in the public hearing for the Tax Budget at 8:00 p.m.
2nd
Roll: All yea, motion carried.
Clerk-Treasurer Fisher told Council the annual tax budget has to be at the
County Auditor’s office by the 20th of July. The budget has all the anticipated
figures for next year, which includes the new 219 Safety Fund, ½ % income tax
changes, plus the percentage break down split among the General, Capital
Improvement Fund and 219 Fund ($43,000 was taken from income tax to accommodate
the split). In the General fund, we’ve reduced the revenue by $237,000. Council
is reminded that we dropped the 1.75 general operating levy. Included in the
General Fund for 2005 is the sale of part of the property in the amount of
$48,000. $44,000 was received from a one-time inheritance tax, Over the past
three years we’ve been aggressively collecting past due taxes. Therefore, we
won’t be collecting as much revenue, since more accounts are current. In
addition, we are now requiring declarations be submitted, so the revenue for
the first quarter will be down a little bit. Because companies are buying as
needed and not holding as much inventory, there is some reduction in real
property taxes.
Councilperson Baxley reminded Council they still have to be cautious in
spending. The fact that the Village has lost Glastics and that under the terms
of the abatement, Pickens does not have all the employees promised, the income
tax increase isn’t as significant as it might appear.
Clerk-Treasurer Fisher said the income tax increase would start to be collected
July 1, but the quarterly withholdings for the businesses will not be coming in
until the end of September or the first of October. The amended budget reflects
only about $75,000 of the percent of the income tax for this year for the new
219 Safety Fund.

Personnel Issue:
Internal Job Opening posting for Roland’s replacement was posted July 18, 2005.
Requests for consideration are due to me tomorrow August 2, 2005.
Service Dept.:
·   Application of MC 70 and/or CRS04 for dust control was completed Saturday
July 23 for Mulberry Street, Part of East Erie Street, Part of South Sycamore
Street, part of South Spruce Street, and Woodside and part of Frayer Ave.
·   I reviewed the job area with Roland today and we determined to add more
stone in areas where the emulsion is showing through.
·   Bid opening for 2005 paving will be Wednesday August 3, 2005 at 12:00 noon.
Results will be presented at the next Council meeting August 15, 2005 for
Council’s approval.
·   The announcement of the safety improvement grant for 307 and N. Chestnut
was posted on the ODOT web site beginning today. As a result of the posting we
will receive letters of intent from interested Engineering firms and will
select one to begin the design work. I will publish a proposed timeline for
next Council meeting.
·   Street parking lines, crosswalks, and School Zones have been repainted
during the evening hours.
Fire Dept./Police Department
·   Clerk/treasurer is continuing to place the first First Energy street light
bill payment in the escrow account. As of 7/13/05 First Energy was in town
working to correct our complaints.
Recreation/Community Center:
·   Alison Shuman who was reported to be Mrs. Price’s replacement for the pre
school program has been unresponsive to our offer. Alternative plans are in
progress.
·   With the Jeffersonian storm water project completed we will now be able to
install the new swing set and spring mounted duck that were donated by the
Billy Cole Family. (Waiting for utilities to mark their lines.)
·   Four skate park boxes are 100% finished and will be placed in the park this
week.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Woodside pump station rehab is in process and about 75% complete. The
contractor is waiting for the replacement motors to be delivered for
installation (Promised August 28, 2005.)
·   Plant operation has been normal.
Finance/Appropriations/Budget:      
·   Nothing to report.
Other Items: 
·   There will be THREE new waterline projects in the Village of Jefferson this
summer:
o   West Cedar Street Extension of 8” line to South Chestnut
o   Replace 4” waterline with an 8” line on the Southside of East Erie Street
between South Market and South Chestnut.
o   New 8” line from 307 north to Linden Street on the West side of N. Chestnut
St. (In progress)

Recreation 
Councilperson Herndon said she was disappointed in the updated recreation
report. There’s nothing that can be done on Council floor. A Recreation
Committee meeting will be scheduled soon and maybe there can be a better
understanding.
Councilperson Baxley said she went through the report and its nice to see
there’s 6 or 7 new senior program, because the seniors really support the
recreation center. Non-instructor, adult programs, offered during this session,
only four of them happened. Of the field trips, there were 4 offered – 2 of
them happened – one of them had only less then 50% of the projected people.
Councilperson Baxley said she feels there’s a real deficit as to what types of
activities are planned. She said that when she went to the finance committee
meeting she was shocked that the Village may be $63,000 in the hole at the Rec.
Center at the end of the year. According to today’s figures, there is a balance
in the Rec. fund of 27,090. Payroll until the end of the year for the Rec.
Center is $46,794. The Center deposits have been averaging between $5 -7,000
per month. Based on these figures, it looks like a negative $70,000 +.
Mayor Bragga said his position is, the Rec. Center has to work within its
budget. If that means cuts – he said he realized that when people are cut there
has to be workers’ comp paid, but he doesn’t see any other choice. A budget has
been established; we’re not getting the revenue through the department. That
being the case, “we have to knock off what has to be knocked off”. Mayor Bragga
told Councilperson Baxley he appreciates her keeping “an eyeball” on it.
Administrator Finger said he and Anita have talked, and she is to come up with
a plan as to how the Rec. Center will survive.
When asked about a personnel concern, Administrator Finger said that on advise
of Counsel, written responses to evaluations are to be placed in the personnel
file. The personnel files are opened to Council for review only, no copies can
be made. Personnel records are not open to the public.
Mayor Bragga asked Councilperson Herndon if she would put transportation on the
agenda for the next Recreation Committee meeting. Some things came up while
Administrator Finger was out, and it looks like the issue of transportation
needs to be addressed to see that we’re consistent on how it’s being done.

Personnel Issues:
·   Bob Lachey, part time firefighter, responded to the Internal Job Opening
posting for Roland’s job.
·   Based on Bob’s background and interview, I am recommending his hire with a
starting date of September 6, 2005.
·   At the last Council meeting there was a question about employees working
without taking a lunch. I rechecked the Fair Labor Laws and again confirmed
that there is no requirement to grant a lunch period, but there is a
requirement to grant two breaks.
·   The village of Jefferson is complying with the Fair Labor Laws.
Service Dept.:
·   Bid opening for 2005 paving took place Wednesday August 3, 2005 at 11:00
AM. My recommendation to contract with Vellotta Paving at $10,000.00 less than
the Engineers estimate is on the Agenda.
·   The timeline for the 307 and N. Chestnut Safety Improvement Grant is in the
packet as a follow up memo from last Council meeting. I will update this
timeline as needed to keep the project on track.
·   The new street, Woodlands Way, which will service the PUD is currently
under construction. The road bed passed the roll test, base material is being
placed and rolled, with concrete soon to follow.
Fire Dept./Police Department
·   Clerk/treasurer is continuing to place the First Energy street light bill
payment in the escrow account. As of 8/12/05 the amount in escrow is
$12,320.73. Patty said as of 8/11/05 she has had no complaints from First
Energy for non-payment.
Recreation/Community Center:
·   Mrs. Price will return from retirement for the fall pre school program.
·   The new swing set and spring mounted duck that were donated by the Billy
Cole Family have been installed at the Jeffersonian Estates Park
·   Safety Town will operate the week of August 15 to19 with 60 new students.
·   I will be making changes to the Recreation Department to make sure that we
do not overspend their funding level.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Woodside pump station stand by power is in operation. With a power outage
the generator automatically starts and we should never overflow to the creek.
The contractor is still waiting for the replacement pumps to be delivered for
installation (Promised August 28, 2005.) When they arrive we can finish the
project and sign off on the grant.
·   Plant operation has been normal.
·   I refused Stan Nizen’s request to cancel all his late payments assessed
against his sewer bill since 2002. These late payment fees were caused when the
tenant at the Village Restaurant failed to pay any of his sewer bills. The
amount asked for is $398.56. (Refer to my memo.) Stan is asking Council to
overrule me in his favor.
Finance/Appropriations/Budget:
·   Recreation Department numbers have been reviewed with the Recreation
Committee and I will have to make staffing changes to operate within the
budget.
Other Items:
·   Waterline projects in the Village of Jefferson:
o   West Cedar Street Extension of 8” line to South Chestnut. Scheduled to
begin August 15, 2005.
o   Replace 4” waterline with an 8” line on the Southside of East Erie Street
between South Market and South Chestnut. Scheduled to begin August 15, 2005.
o   New 8” line from 307 north to Linden Street on the West side of N. Chestnut
St. (In progress)

chair the committee…Judy Maloney volunteered to chair the committee.

Motion by Baxley to approve Administrator Finger’s recommendation to hire
Robert Lachey for the Working Foreman Job at the Street Department @the $15.00/
hr. probationary rate, starting date: September 6, 2006
2nd
Roll: All yea, motion carried.
Motion by Baxley to approve Administrator Finger’s recommendation to accept low
bid from Vellotta Paving Company for $50,543.00 and to authorize Administrator
Finger to execute the required contracts to complete the project.
2nd
Roll: All yea, motion carried.
Councilperson Baxley asked if Administrator Finger wanted discussion on Stan
Nizen’s request that Council waive late fees on the delinquent sewer bills
incurred by a tenant. Administrator Finger stated his direction on how to deal
with late fees, incurred because tenant didn’t pay sewer charges, is based on
Village statute. If a tenant is delinquent, our ordinances allow for those
charges to be certified to the property tax. In this particular case, it was a
bankruptcy call. As soon as the bankruptcy is filed, our ordinance is real
clear--with the final bill it goes as a proceeding against the property tax.
Stan Nizen’s argument was that we didn’t notify him every time the tenant’s
payment was late . It was certified in 2003, Nizen received notification by
certified letter- he paid that property tax. Stan Nizen not only knew the sewer
bill wasn’t being paid, he entered into an agreement with the tenant involved
in the restaurant. The tenant didn’t pay Mr. Nizen…he didn’t pay him rent – so
regarding Mr. Nizen’s argument that he didn’t know the tenant wasn’t paying us
– why would the tenant be paying us and nobody else? He wasn’t paying anything.
Not only does Mr. Nizen want us to waive the fees on the current bill, he wants
us to refund the late fees that he already paid in 2003. Administrator Finger
said Mr. Nizen asked him to take his request to Council to see if Council would
over-rule him. Administrator Finger’s response, “Folks if you over-rule me, you
have to change the ordinance”.
Members of Council agree that the ordinances are in place and they need to be
enforced.
Motion by Maloney that Council not approve the Stan Nizen’s request to dismiss
the late fees on delinquent sewer bills
2nd
Roll: All yea, motion carried.
Mayor Bragga stated that Clerk-Treasurer Fisher should send Mr. Nizen a
certified letter informing him of Council’s action.

Personnel Issues:
·   Bob Lachey, new Street Department Supervisor started work today September
06, 2005.
Service Dept.:
·   The 2005 paving contract with Vellotta Paving is signed and I am waiting on
a confirmed start date.
·   $6,000.00 of the money earmarked for paving but not needed due to a lower
than expected bid will be used for crack sealing.
·   The quote for crack sealing West Ashtabula Street, North and South Elm,
West Jefferson Street, and Maplewood Street is $12,800.00. Moving the $6,000.00
from paving to crack sealing will enable us to do all the Streets.
·   The nine letters of intent from Engineering firms to do the design work for
the 307 and N. Chestnut Safety Improvement Grant are in the process of being
evaluated according to the Professional Design Firm Selection Process. This
process is in Compliance with Ohio Revised Code Sections 153.65 through 153.71.
A contract will be in place by October 8, 2005.
·   The new street, Woodlands Way, which will service the PUD is currently
under construction. The concrete curbs should be finished today and they will
start pouring the roadbed September 7, 2005.
Fire Dept./Police Department
·   Clerk/treasurer is continuing to place the First Energy street light bill
payment in the escrow account. As of 9/02/05 the amount in escrow is

Personnel Issues:
·   Effective Monday September 19th 2005, the three full time employees at the
Community Center: Anita, Barb, and Chris have had their hours reduced to 20
hours per week.
·   This action was necessary due to the Community Center’s inability to earn
the revenue needed to pay the expenses as budgeted.
·   We have a legal obligation to live within the budget and therefore must cut
expenses.
·   This action was one of the options discussed with council in July and
August and is projected to balance the year- end budget.
·   Patty and I have had two meetings with the employees to make sure they have
all the information they need.
·   Each employee received the cobra forms to continue their medical coverage
if they desire, and Robin Blon answered any questions that they had.
Service Dept.:
·   Bob Lachey is adjusting to his new job just fine.
·   I am waiting on a confirmed start date for paving.
·   Purchase order for crack sealing has been written.
·   The eight letters of intent from Engineering firms to do the design work
for the 307 and N. Chestnut Safety Improvement Grant are in the final stage of
being evaluated according to the Professional Design Firm Selection Process. A
contract will be in place by October 8, 2005.
·   The new street, Woodlands Way, which will service the PUD is nearing
completion. The concrete curbs are finished and a large part of the roadbed is
complete.
Fire Dept./Police Department
·   Clerk/treasurer is continuing to place the First Energy street light bill
payment in the escrow account. As of 9/16/05 the amount in escrow is
$18,348.68. We received our first complaint 9/2/05 regarding non- payment. I
have called First energy collections to explain the problem. William was going
to take our complaint to operations but I have not heard from them yet.
Recreation/Community Center:
·   We are continuing to add any program that will help raise revenue
·   Roni Guerini moved to the Community Center Friday afternoon and will

location.

running them.

booth seeking “Friends of the Community Center”. This booth was suggested by
seniors and is being manned by Senior Volunteers.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:

as early as this week. Completion of this work will finish the project and we
can sign off on the grant.

Virginia Wilson met with the Mayor, Me, Gary Licate, and representatives of
Smolen Engineering to work out a plan to reduce storm water infiltration into

Starting October 18, contributions will be accepted. Tutoring is by volunteers
and transportation is the responsibility of the student/family.
The Health Fair went well. Sixty-five Crime Watch Lamp Adapters
were   distributed to the senior citizens attending. The Crime Watch Lamp
Adapters will be available at the Community Center, the Administration Office,
Fire Department, Police Department and the EMS.
The purpose of the adapters is to alert emergency vehicles of the residence of
an emergency. The adapter is screwed into the porch light socket, then the bulb
is screwed into the socket. The bulb will work as usual, but if an emergency
vehicle, such as an ambulance, has been summoned to the residence, by hitting
the light switch twice, the bulb will blink off and on indicating that the
residence is the one in need of assistance.
