Personnel Issues:
·   Jan Scopel, Income Tax Clerk will be moving to Kansas City as soon as her
house closes. We are advertising for her replacement and will hire Jan’s
replacement as soon as possible.
·   Barb Heath has announced her intention to retire effective October 23rd.
Service Dept.:
·   Paving has been scheduled for week of October 3rd to 7th.
·   Purchase order for crack sealing has been written.
·   The eight letters of intent from Engineering firms to do the design work
for the 307 and N. Chestnut Safety Improvement Grant have been fully evaluated
according to the Professional Design Firm Selection Process. Negotiations are
underway with Smolen Engineering, the top candidate. A contract will be in
place by October 8, 2005.
·   The Street Department has been working on repairs to our storm water
drainage system repairing and replacing broken pipes and damaged catch basins.
The primary aim is to make sure there is no standing water on roadways that
could freeze in cold weather.
Fire Dept./Police Department
·   Clerk/treasurer is continuing to place the First Energy street light bill
payment in the escrow account. As of 9/30/05 the amount in escrow is
$17,614.52. We received our first complaint 9/2/05 regarding non- payment. I
have called First energy collections to explain the problem. William was going
to take our complaint to operations but as of 9/30/05 I have not heard from
them yet.
Recreation/Community Center:
·   We continue to seek new programs and add back any former programs that we
can.
·   All classes with enough enrollment are running as scheduled.
·   We have extended the Centers’ Friday closing time from 2:00 PM until 5:00
PM.
·   Roni Guerini’s and my move to the Community Center in my opinion went
flawlessly. All our computer systems and records are available to us so we can
continue our work from this new location.
·   The Senior Health Fair scheduled for Saturday September 17th was a huge
success with well over 400 people attending.
·   The Senior Health Fair booth seeking “Friends of the Community Center” was
suggested by and was manned by Senior Volunteers. As a result of this effort,
and with follow-up calls by me, we now have nine new volunteers and about ten
rededicated former helpers.
·   A special thanks to Ken and Bev Fertig, Wilma, Mary, Judy and Cayce for
their continuing volunteer efforts on behalf of the Community Center.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Woodside pump station replacement pumps (OPWC Round 18 project) are
installed and operational. As soon as the new valve vault is waterproofed and
the safety lifting device is installed we can sign off on the grant.
·   Elm Street Pump Station and Auxiliary Power (OPWC Round 19 project) bid
documents are nearing completion and we will advertise this project late
October.
·   The resolution authorizing me to complete the application for the Main
Plant Upgrade, (OPWC Round 20 project) is in your packet. If you would suspend
rules and adopt the resolution it will be timely for filing in November.
Finance/Appropriations/Budget:

2nd
Roll: All yea, motion carried.
Mayor Bragga opened the Public Hearing. The purpose of the Public Hearing is to
give the public an opportunity to ask question or make comments with respect to
the proposed changes in zoning in the Old Town Business/Commercial District and
to the Public Parks District.
The Old Town Business/Commercial District zoning change = first floor of a
building could be a business, upstairs an apartment. Administrator Finger said
this seems to be a win-win situation (will improve business and liven up the
down town area.).
The park development – Rush Creek property and Linden St. & Jackson Street -
the park in Jeffersonian Estates are included in the Park District. Not only
will the parks provide the obvious benefits to the community, the designation
of the property as Park Land exempts the Village from paying property tax on
the property.

Visitors Comments
Mike Prochko and Tom Milligan thanked council for the opportunity of running
the Farmers’ Market this year and gave a slide show of the festivities on
Market days.
Council was told that depending on the weather, the Market opening date will be
earlier next year. An anticipated grant from the Visitor’s Bureau will help
with advertising and other expenses. This year’s Market was a success, and the
group will try to expand on the things that keep people shopping longer, such
as having activities to keep children entertained.
Charlene Kusar made a plea for the Animal Protective League, asking for any
kind of donations from money to old or new rugs, blankets, towels, as well as,
litter, canned food—things that are not ordinarily thought of such as bleach,
paper towels, collars, leashes, etc. The APL has money for bare necessities and
to pay for their staff, any help would be appreciated. She asked if the
community center could be a drop off point. (Judy Maloney said she would help.)
The Mayor said that it would not be a problem to have the Community Center used
as a drop-off point.

Personnel Issues:
·   I am seeking approval on two new job descriptions:
o   Administrative Assistant in the Administration Department, this will
upgrade Roni’s job to reflect what she does now and adds more financial
reporting and oversight for grant reporting.
o   Maintenance/Utility person in the Street Department will be the snow
plowing, grass trimming, and maintenance of grounds, parks, and buildings
position. John Buzzards replacement.
Service Dept.:
·   Snow removal services began 11/17/05.
Fire Dept./Police Department
·   Nothing to report.
Recreation/Community Center:
·   While revenue is strong at the Community Center, the Community Center
budget incurred unexpected costs with retirements and resignations.
·   I am asking your support on the resolution to add $10,000.00 to the
recreation fund to replace the money spent on these unexpected costs. This
action will make sure all programs can continue and the fund will remain in a
positive balance.
·   We have new instructors for Biddy Bowling, Biddy Basketball, Stompin
Soccer, Pre-School Sportsarama, Drum Lessons, and Cheerleading.
·   We are still seeking instructors for: Exercise Class and Gymnastics.
·   Lakeshore Art Club has original artwork created by local members on display
and for sale on the walls of the Community Center Halls. These will be
displayed until after Christmas. Plans are for future displays also.
·   Posters, placemats and an updated brochure are being displayed at local
businesses, and restaurants to make sure the programs receive more
advertisement.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   OPWC Round 19, Elm Street pump station rehab. specifications were revised
for clarity and are out for bid.
·   The OPWC Round 20, Main Plant repairs and rehab. project was moved forward
from Round 20 to Round 19. This action was taken because there was money left
in the loan fund and the Jefferson Project was ready to proceed.
·   Plant operations have been normal.
Finance/Appropriations/Budget:
·   Appropriation meetings with the finance committee are in progress.
·   There is an ordinance in your packet to make several changes to the wages
and or job titles to add the new position descriptions or modify old ones. I
ask for your support on this ordinance.
Other Items:
The Harju property repair is moving forward. The walls and roof are up.
Clerk/Treasurer Report
The payroll report, overtime report, check register, and month-end
reconciliation for September are in Council packet.
Clerk-Treasurer introduced Kevin Steed, the new Income Tax Clerk. Kevin started
working on November 1, 2005 and is doing an outstanding job of becoming
acquainted with the position and personnel.
Regarding the necessity to transfer $10,000.00 from the general fund to the
recreation fund, it was noted that with the recent retirement of Barb Heath and
resignation of Anita Perrotti at the recreation center expenses were increased
by $10,000 to fulfill our financial obligation to these employees. With the
anticipated increase in revenue and a decrease in expenditures, along with the
$10,000 transfer, the recreation fund should balance at the end of the year
without further help from the general fund.

Recreation
Administrator Finger said that the tutoring program is still going on. The
original flyer stated that it was to go through the 18th of November. There is
still interest so the tutoring program will go on through the school year.
There are more high school students who are willing to tutor the junior high
students. The retired teachers who initially volunteered have gone to Florida
for the winter. The program has been well received. Donations are accepted, but
not solicited.

Official
Mayor
Mayor’s address to Village of Jefferson 2006 / January 3, 2006
 The year 2005 was a year that tested our ability to manage our Village
finances while campaigning for additional tax dollars. We made tough decisions
as we managed the budgets of all departments:
·   No wage increases were granted in 2005
·   Reduction in staff at the community center occurred in 2005
·   Reduction in staff in the streets department, due to retirements
·   A temporary move of the Village Administrator and Administrative Secretary
to the community center occurred to give them a day to day view of the
operation, enabling evaluations and management decisions to be made
The operation and bond payment for the center and recreation department will
continue to be a challenge for present and future councils. We are obligated to
make the bond payment for the purchase and renovation of the building. The
bonds will be callable in 2008, so the council needs a plan for the future of
the center and the operation of the department.
The important passage of the ½% income tax for safety services was a critical
and positive decision made by the community in 2005. That revenue will replace
the 1.75 mil reduction in property taxes for village residents.
Zoning, delineating and creating the Old Town Business district and village
parkland were completed in 2005. Defining the boundaries and creating layered
zoning in the OTB, brings diversity and more options to the property in the
OTB.
2005 saw the completion of several projects:
·   Renovation to the Woodside lift station, Ohio Public Works Commission grant
$40K, provided emergency power and upgrades to prevent raw sewage discharge to
the stream. It also allowed us to clean and videotape the entire Eastside
collection system for future repairs.
·   Major improvement to the drainage in Jeffersonian Estates were completed,
$80K
·   Professional Engineering Firm Selection and contract signed for Safety
improvements and traffic light at the SR307N, SR46, SR167 intersection
·   The Senior Crime watch and Safety grant was initiated, $15K
·   The static helicopter display Memorial for our Veterans
·   Mapping of the village storm sewer project began in 2005
·   The Orphan gas well in the park was eliminated, grant up to $50K
·   Improvements to the Fire hall were approved, $28K ( new over head doors,
windows, and siding )
In 2005 we have been approved for additional grants for emergency power,
ultraviolet treatment, new pumps/motors, electrical upgrades and other
improvements at the WWTP; OPWC round 19, $90K; and OPWC round 20, $412K.
   The United Way grant for seniors was awarded, $14K.
Senior Transportation Grant awarded, $24K.
   Field-testing for gas drilling in the park may be completed by the end of
2005.
   The Jefferson Police department managed to maintain all shifts during the
absence of Chief Febel. Chief has recovered from surgery on his knee and back
and has been cleared to return to service in January of 2006.
   Street foreman, Roland Ferguson retired after 28 years of service to the
village. We thank him for his dedication and service to the Village of
Jefferson.
   Many important issues and goals are on the horizon in 2006:
·   Rejuvenate the Community Center and Recreation Department, staff,
restructure and organize the operation. Recruit and use many more volunteers.
·   Maintain our active involvement in the Jefferson Area Schools facility
project.
·   Approve wage increases for village employees.
·   Approve and purchase a new fire truck and other fire apparatus.
·   Replace the heating system at the Safety Center ( fire and police ).
·   Approve the street development plan for West Cedar from Chestnut to Elm.
·   Maintain the progress of the Water Advisory Committee.
·   Rejuvenate and prioritize the street paving and maintenance plan.
·   Develop a sidewalk improvement plan.
·   Complete the storm sewer maps.
·   Increase tree replacement in our tree plan.
·   Review Zoning Codes for potential changes.
·   Research and develop a safety plan to increase fire inspections.
·   Study and discuss the need for a more effective solid waste-recycling
program.
·   Revisit the plan and future use of village owned property. ( two
residential lots and 4.6 acres of light industrial property )
·   Improve and develop the use of electronic communication for council
business.
Council will be addressing the need for replacing or renewing a 1.0 mill fire
levy and 1.55 mill street light levy in 2006.
2006 will see the administration develop a plan and strategy for promoting
planned growth and marketing the many desirable aspects of the Village of
Jefferson. The plan involves recruiting and earning the support of community
stakeholders.
I am inviting council to stay for a few minutes after tonight’s meeting to
preview the presentation. A meeting with several community stakeholders will
occur on Wednesday, January 4, 2006. The plan will be shared with the Jefferson
Chamber Economic task force on Saturday, January 7, 2006.
 It is my desire to keep our community safe, clean, and well maintained and
continue to be the most desirable place to live in northeastern Ohio. Our
village is the best! Let us work together to preserve our past and embrace our
future! Thank you and Happy 2006!

Recreation Department and the new Administrative Assistant position.
·   Anita Perrotti’s unemployment claim has been denied by the state due to her
resignation. We are no longer obligated to pay out any money for unemployment.
·   Anita also has a workman compensation claim that is in dispute and being
moved through the appeals process.
Service Dept.:
·   The Street department has been cold patching any damaged areas to our
roadways.
·   Brobst Tree Service has removed all dead trees on our cut list. Stump
removal will be scheduled at a later date.
·   A purchase order was also issued for three more days of deadwood removal.
This will be completed by the end of March 2006.
·   Christmas tree removal is being performed as needed. A reminder that only
bare trees (no plastic bags, ornaments or tree stands) can be recycled.
·   The department has scheduled open ditch cleaning on several streets.
Fire Dept./Police Department
·   Chief Fable has returned to work full time with no physical restrictions.
Recreation/Community Center :
·   I ask Council to confirm Tara Dean’s hiring as a part time clerical/
administrative support person for the recreation department.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   One bid for OPWC Round 19, Elm Street pump station rehab. was opened
December 22, 2006. The bid exceeded the allowed 10% overage so was rejected.
Bid specifications are being reviewed and the job will be re-advertised.
·   Plant operations are normal.
Finance/Appropriations/Budget:
·   Nothing to report
  Other Items:
·   On Wednesday January 11, 2006 at 7:30 PM the mayor received notification
that CEI was going to have to cut electric service beginning at 9:00 PM to make
a repair on a 45,000 Volt line. 4,500 customers would lose power as the power
grid containing all of Jefferson Village and parts of Jefferson Township was
turned off.
·   At 7:32 the mayor activated Village services to respond to this
notification.
·   By 8:45 the following occurred in the Village.
o   The Police had extra officers on duty.
o   The Fire Department was manned and emergency power made available to the
Safety Center.
o   The Wastewater Department was manned and emergency power made ready.
o   The Street Department emergency power was ready and the supervisor had
employees on standby if needed.
o   All Village Computers were powered down.
o   The Emergency Rescue District was advised and prepared in case of a home
medical emergency.
o   Most operating factories, grocery stores, gas stations, restaurants and
other businesses were notified in person that power was scheduled to be turned
off at 9:00 PM.
o   The emergency phone notification (commonly called reverse 911) to
individuals and business was activated at the emergency management control
center at the county offices.
·    This Village should be proud of the instant unquestioning action that was
set in motion, I know I am proud to have been witness to the events.

Personnel Issues:
·   I request that council approve the new position description for the Street
Department, Maintenance/Utility position, that is intended to be a full time
position for John Buzzard’s replacement. This position was discussed last year
but was inadvertently missed in the last batch of job descriptions. This
position will take care of mowing, weed control, sidewalk plowing, hanging
flower baskets, painting, fixing and the like for all village buildings as
needed and directed. The wage for this position is in the wage ordinance at
$11.95/hr.
·   Anita Perrotti’s unemployment claim was originally denied by the state due
to her resignation. Anita appealed; we supplied additional information and are
waiting for another determination.
·   Anita also has a workman compensation claim that is in a medical dispute
and being moved through the appeals process.
Service Dept.:
·   The Street department has completely reworked the private parking area
behind Mugs restaurant and the photo studio to enable use for public parking.
·   Brobst Tree Service has completed all dead tree removal and dead branch
removal scheduled for this winter. Stump removal will be scheduled as weather
allows avoiding tearing up tree lawns.
·   The department has been doing a lot of open ditch cleaning during the mild
weather.
·   Street crews are also doing street repairs and grooming normally done in
April or May.
·   We need to schedule an Utility/Service Committee meeting to make final
plans for street paving and sidewalk repairs.
Fire Dept./Police Department
·   Safety Committee met with the fire department and we are prepared for the
final finance meeting.
Recreation/Community Center :
·   Ads for the Community Center supervisor position are ready to run as soon
as possible.
·   I intend to have Roni back at the Administration Office by the end of
February and I intend to be back at the Administration Office by the end of
March.
·   Programs and revenue continue to grow. PAL sponsored teen dance attendance
is at 80+ kids. We will be scheduling two dances a month instead of one
beginning this month (February).
·   The body blast exercise class is so successful that the participants
requested we add a second session. This class now runs Tuesday night and
Saturday morning. The class is full and has the potential of grossing income of
$1,600.00 per month.
·   To further compliment these sessions we have added companion classes for
the children of the participants.
·   THE COMMUNITY CENTER WILL TRY ANY PROGRAM THAT MAY FIT THIS COMMUNITY’S
NEEDS.
·   We could still use two more volunteers willing to man the Center one night
a week.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   A Meeting with Mel Gravely, Ohio Public Works Commission Regional Director
here in Jefferson has been rescheduled three times to accommodate his schedule.
Clerk/Treasurer Fisher has asked for some training on handling the financial
reporting and payment recovery required by our various OPWC projects.
·   Plant operations are normal.
Finance/Appropriations/Budget:
·   The wage ordinance before council is the same as last meeting with the
addition of the Street Department Maintenance/Utility position. I need your
support to be able to move ahead with filling many new job descriptions that
result in an overall cost savings to this Village.
·   We can be ready for a final finance Committee meeting after Wednesday the
8th.
  Other Items:
·   On Monday morning Mayor Bragga will be meeting with First Energy Officials
to further resolve our service problems.
·   I expect to release the money in escrow by February 10th if all goes well.

Personnel Issues:
·   On appeal, the Ohio Industrial Commission ruled to add Trigeminal Neuralgia
to Anita Perrotti’s workman’s compensation claim.
·   The Village of Jefferson has again appealed this decision until the medical
dispute between the State of Ohio’s and Anita’s doctors is resolved.
·   I ask Council to confirm Lisa’s and my recommendation to hire the two desk
help part time employees needed to meet our budget commitment.
Service Dept.:
·   The Street department has a few more trees to cull out of the south end of
the Village Park. The trees will be put on the ground before leafing out even
if we have to remove them later in the year when the ground firms up.
·   The area for a pavilion to be constructed by Rotary Club has been cleared
and is ready for construction.
·   All work on trees scheduled for removal or dead wood trimming have been
completed.
·   Stump removal will be scheduled as weather and ground conditions permit.
·   The department continues to do open ditch cleaning during the mild weather.
·   Progress on each of the major projects we have discussed for 2006 is as
Follows:
·   2006 Village Street Paving:
n   Ads for bids are running. Bid opening is Scheduled for April 13th with a
recommendation to Council for approval on the 17th of April.
·   2006 ODOT Paving of Chestnut Street:
n   No Change
·   Downtown Sidewalk repairs:
n   Estimate for concrete work without underground utilities is done
n   First Energy and I have discussed the project and I am to meet their
planner this week.
n   King Luminaire and Village met, King Luminaire will give us a quote for
lamps.
·   Completion of West Cedar Street between S. Chestnut and S. Elm:
n   Updated estimates are done
n   Resolution of necessity will be introduced at Council March 6th. & the
second reading is scheduled for March 20th.
n   The Documents will be on file with the Clerk Treasurer for public view.
·   Improvements to Mulberry Street for the new schools:
n   Grant information has been requested
n   Estimates are done
n   Engineering proposal is due for the grant request
Fire Dept./Police Department
·   There has been a lot of interest in the Vehicles being declared surplus.
o   First Reading: February 21, 2006
Second Reading: March 6, 2006
Third Reading: March 20, 2006

30 days from passage to be effective: April 19, 2006.

Start Advertisement for sealed bids two weeks prior to effective date: April
5, 2006

Bid opening Friday April 21, 2006 at 1:00 PM in Village Hall.
·   The ads for bids on the new fire truck are running. We have been proactive
in sending overnight packets to the major manufacturers. Bid opening is
scheduled for April 13th with a recommendation to Council on April 17. The
order must be placed by the end of April to avoid a scheduled price increase.
·   The Clerk/Treasurer will make sure there are no money issues to delay
placing the order.
Recreation/Community Center :
·   Lisa Hamper has entered the Recreation Supervisor’s job at full speed. Her
introduction to the routines and systems has been without a problem.
·   The activity level at the center continues to grow as we add new programs
and members..
·   Roni moved back to the Administration Office on February 28 and I intend to
be back at the Administration Office by the end of March.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Quotes are being gathered for the new sewer jet, and storage building.
·   Repairs continue as we seek to improve the plants overall condition.
·   Plant treatment operations are normal.
Finance/Appropriations/Budget:
·   Special emphasis must be placed on financial issues and reporting to enable
the Village to accomplish our ambitious projects list.
  Other Items:
·   I need an executive session to brief Council on two possible legal actions.
·   There are still only rumors to report on a new Auto Zone Store.
·   The Gas Exploration Company did find a good drilling target in the Village
parkland and expects to drill in the June or July time frame. They owe us a map
showing the exact location.

redeemed at the community center. Max of $300.00 per year. 100% on rentals,
100% on weight room, 50% on classes; non-transferable, 18-years or older.

rates stay the same for building rental weight room.
3.   Instructor rates 50/50 unless approved by Mayor or Admin. (Need a motion
for this)

5.   There should be a 10% discount for more than one child from the same
family in the same class.

sign-up in th emiddle of the month.
7.   Garden Club and VFW get one meeting a month at no charge.

an Auto Zone is going to be built, which she feels does not fit into the Old

speak-up and voice their concern to Council, Council stated that all of Council
is willing to listen to residents and that Auto Zone is not a done deal.

Conversation” on May 4, 2006 from 7-9 p.m. at the Lenox Community Center.

pavilion project the last week-end of April. The recommended size of the
pavilion is 24’ x 48’

Personnel Issues:
·   Hamid Danesh has accepted the Income Tax Clerk position and passed his
required physical and background check. I ask council to confirm his
appointment.
·   Kevin Steed will continue to work evenings and weekends as needed for a
smooth transition.
Service Dept.:
·   The Street Department has started brush pick-up, moving and normal spring
activities.
·   The department continues to do open ditch cleaning.
·   20 stumps were removed over a two-day period and the rest will be removed,
as it is practical.
·   Village wide cleanup is scheduled for May 6, 2006. Pick up will be curbside
at each resident’s home. Informational Flyers are included in your packet.
·   Material must be out Friday night to make sure it gets picked up. Waste
Management will start with six trucks on the East side of the Village at 7:00
A.M. Pick-up will move to the West quickly with no provisions to return to an
area a second time.
·   Village employees will also be working to remove appliances and tires that
have been pre arranged and pre paid.
·   Progress on each of the major projects we have discussed for 2006 is as
Follows:
·   2006 Village Street Paving:
n   Five paving bids were opened April 13, 2006. Koski Construction Company
submitted the low bid of $133,770.
n   I am asking for a motion to accept that bid, and authorization to sign the
contract with Koski Construction.
·   2006 ODOT Paving of Chestnut Street:
n   The published list of 2006 ODOT paving did not include this project.
n   ODOT has told me that SRT 45 and RT 46 Jefferson Village will be advertised
in August, Awarded in November and scheduled for paving next Summer. Statewide
a lot of projects have been rescheduled.
n   This change actually helps in allowing additional time to work on Street
Lighting and sidewalk improvements.
·   Downtown Sidewalk repairs:
n   Estimate for concrete work without underground utilities is done.
n   Smolen Engineering will prepare plans for First Energy.
n   First Energy will do nothing until Smolen Engineering is finished with the
plans.
n   King Luminaire and Village met, King Luminaire will give us a quote for
lamps.
n   A Community Development Block Grant will be modified and resubmitted.
·   Completion of West Cedar Street between S. Chestnut and S. Elm:
n   Updated estimates are done
n   Resolution of necessity has been completed.
n   Drawings and plans are scheduled to be complete April 17, 2006.
n   The Documents will be on file with the Clerk Treasurer for public view.
·   Improvements to Mulberry Street for the new schools:
n   Grant information has been requested
n   Estimates are done
n   Engineering proposal will be prepared.
Fire Dept./Police Department
·   The Village received one fire truck bid from Pierce Manufacturing for a
total of $417,103.00. There are available discounts that we take amounting to
$25,919. We will finance $391,184.00.
·   The Clerk/Treasurer has made sure there are no money issues to delay
placing the order.
·   I need a motion confirming acceptance of this bid and authorizing me to
enter a contract to secure this truck with the discounts.
·   There has been a lot of interest in the Vehicles being declared surplus.

Recreation/Community Center:
·   The activity level at the center continues to grow as we add new programs
and members.
·   We had over 100 people attend the breakfast with the Easter Bunny.
·   There are about 55 kids signed up for Tee Ball this year, about triple the

Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   A purchase order was issued for the new sewer jet, and the storage
building.
·   Since the Sewer Jet is a State Contract purchase we did not need to bid
this unit.

utility/maintenance person for the Street Departments.

maintenance person pending satisfactory completion of his physical and
background check.
·   I also ask that Council accept the resignation of Hamid Danish our newly
hired Income Tax Clerk.
·   We will be interviewing from the last batch of applicants for his
replacement.
·   I need to call for an executive session to bring Council up to date on a
possible litigation issue.
Service Dept.:
·   The department continues to do open ditch cleaning.
·   The Village wide cleanup on May 6, 2006 went smoothly. Pick up was
completed by 9:00 A.M.
·   I recommend that curbside pick up be scheduled the first Saturday of May
each Year in the future.
·   Cost was below the budgeted amount of $5,500.00.

Follows:

n   Hillyer Drive and East Satin Street are complete. East Jefferson should be
completed in about two weeks, weather permitting.

n   ODOT has told me that SRT 45 and RT 46 Jefferson Village will be advertised
in August, Awarded in November and scheduled for paving next Summer. Statewide
a lot of projects have been rescheduled.
n   This change actually helps in allowing additional time to work on Street
Lighting and sidewalk improvements.

lighting downtown.
n   Smolen Engineering is preparing plans for First Energy.
n   First Energy will do nothing until Smolen Engineering is finished with the
plans.
n   A Community Development Block Grant will be modified and resubmitted.
·   Completion of West Cedar Street between S. Chestnut and S. Elm:
n   Drawings and plans are complete and on file with the Clerk Treasurer for
public view.

in August, Awarded in November and scheduled for paving next Summer. Statewide
a lot of projects have been rescheduled.

Personnel Issues:
·   Anita Licate and the equipment manufacturer settled her injury lawsuit and
Workers Compensation also recovered the money paid in medical expenses.
Service Dept.:
·   The department continues spring/summer projects as needed.
·   Concrete repairs to sidewalks and other Village areas are being scheduled
and work is expected to commence in early July through end of August.
·   Progress on each of the major projects we have discussed for 2006 is as
Follows:
·   2006 Village Street Paving:
n   Hillyer Drive and East Satin Street are complete. East Jefferson was
delayed until school was finished for the summer.
n   The railroad crossing on East Jefferson will be closed for four days to
rebuild the tracks and allow repaving.
n   Tentative date set for June 26 to June 29.
·   2006 ODOT Paving of Chestnut Street:
n   No Change
·   Downtown Sidewalk repairs:
n   Smolen Engineering is preparing plans for First Energy.
n   First Energy will give us a cost to relocate utilities when Smolen
Engineering is finished with the plans.
n   The Community Development Block Grant to help pay for replacement of the
sidewalks was declined due to projects of higher priority.
·   Completion of West Cedar Street between S. Chestnut and S. Elm:
n   Drawings and plans are complete and on file with the Clerk Treasurer for
public view.
n   Bid documents are complete.
n   Property owner notifications were mailed by certified letter 6/15/2006.
·   Improvements to Mulberry Street for the new schools:
n   Engineering proposal is in process.
n   OPWC Round 21 grant request has been submitted.
Fire Dept./Police Department
·   Fire Department is willing to except a surplus generator set from the
wastewater plant. This generator is large enough to supply police and fire
power needs during an electric outage.
·   Police Cruiser bid information is forthcoming.
Recreation/Community Center :
·   The Recreation Center continues to operate on the revenue being generated
each month.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Design work for the OPWC issue 20 grant to refurbish the main plant control
system and replace chlorine from the treatment process by using ultraviolet
light will commence 6/20/2006.
·   Mark Reighard missed his class II certification by one question. He will
retake the exam in November 2006.
·   Plant treatment operations are normal.
Finance/Appropriations/Budget:
·   I intend to cancel the capital expenditure at the community center for an
upgrade to the security camera. The money will be used for improvements at the
park. Items like, picnic tables, grills, stump removal, sewer tap, and pavilion
related expenses.
·   I intend to delay the Street Department building roof repair another year
and instead use the money for more critical road repair (MC 70 and crack
sealing)
·   These changes do not require appropriating more money it just shifts the
money from one project to a more urgent one.
Other Items:      None.

department maintenance job as soon as I return from vacation.
Service Dept.:
·   Concrete repairs to sidewalks on North Chestnut, East Side; South Chestnut,
West Side; South Market, East Side and other Village areas are progressing as
scheduled.
·   Progress on each of the major projects we have discussed for 2006 is as
Follows:
·   2006 ODOT Paving of Chestnut Street:
n   To Bid in August. Construction to be 2007.
·   Downtown Sidewalk repairs:
n   Smolen Engineering is preparing plans for First Energy.
n   First Energy will give us a cost to relocate utilities when Smolen
Engineering is finished with the plans.
·   Completion of West Cedar Street between S. Chestnut and S. Elm:
n   We have served all notices and need to wait another week to close all the
objection periods.
n   An assessment review board needs to be appointed to deal with several
objections.
n   Job is ready to go for bids as soon as property owner objections are
resolved.
·   Improvements to Mulberry Street for the new schools:
n   OPWC Round 21 grant request was submitted to the State being given our
districts top priority
n   We are approved to receive $150,000.00 grant and $150,000.00 0% interest
loan but will need to borrow the remaining $396,000.00 at $3.4% interest.
Fire Dept./Police Department
·   Nothing new to report.
Recreation/Community Center :
·   The Recreation Center continues to operate on the revenue being generated
each month.
·   The gas well drilled on parkland has the potential of being productive. My
recommendation is to use any revenue generated to pay the Community Center
building payment first, then if any is left to fund other park and recreation
improvements/programs.
·   By using any revenue in this manner, money currently transferred from other
funds can remain in those funds and be budgeted as appropriated by Council.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Elm Street pump station repairs should begin after Labor Day.
·   The new sewer jet is scheduled for delivery week of August 21st.
·   Plant treatment operations are normal.
Finance/Appropriations/Budget:
·   Nothing new to report.

·   Julie Lindner met with planning commission Council members and interested
residents August 14th to discuss zoning language changes in the business
district.
·   Julie will prepare draft zoning language and meet with us after Labor Day.
·   Kirby Date from the Cleveland State School of Public Affairs will tour the
village with me on September 11th and meet Planning Commission and interested
Council members at 7:30 to discuss their proposal to the Village.

Old Business/New Business
The police cruisers are on order. In addition to the cruisers, 2 street trucks
and a
backhoe has also been ordered which are on a 5-year lease purchase agreement
Council member Ken Fertig said hopefully some of the empty housing units will
be filled, given the new schools that are being built in the school district.
He said he just couldn’t see how the minimal increase is going to make up for
lost revenues. Fertig said he has had time to go over the figures and the
village always seemed to do well with sewer revenues. He said the village has a
$180,000 grant coming, as well as some other funds, which should be able to
assist with the sewer revenue shortfalls. He said he doesn’t feel at this time
the increase is needed---maybe down the road.

Motion by Brabender for the third reading of Ordinance 06-O-2657

Councilman Ward asked who made the recommendation for the sewer rate increase,
since the committee had a mixed vote.
The major factor in the decision to raise the sewer rates is based on the
decrease in revenue due to so many vacant houses in the Village
Administrator Finger said another reason for asking for a rate increase at this
time is based on an increased costs in items such as fuel and sewer
improvements.. The last increase was in January 2004.
Councilman Thompson suggested that the committee look at the ordinance, discuss
the increase, then come back to council.

Correspondence
Visitors’ Comments 
Beverly Cowles said she felt Council did not inform the public properly on the
matter (of the 5 ordinances) right before and during the public hearing. Cowles
disagreed with the changes to zoning and accused council of “spot zoning” and
said the properties should be left as “non-conforming’.
Council member Ed Ward defended council’s decision to move forward on the
ordinances’ amendments, and said the zoning changes have been in the works more
than a year and a half.
The ordinances were discussed at several council meetings and the public
hearing was advertised. Gary Pascarella said he feels that the public had been
adequately advised.

Mr. Richard Hummel referred Council to an article in the Star Beacon which
details the steps Geneva is taking toward a cable franchise agreement that will
give the city a piece of Time-Warner Cable company’s financial pie. Mr.Hummel
feels Jefferson should follow suite when it comes time to renew our contract
with Time-Warner Cable Co. Geneva is forming a task force committee
representing the citizens, the schools, the library and other entities that are
affected by the telecommunications contract. This task force will make
recommendations regarding the contract based on the needs of the citizens and
local organizations.

candy to the Community Center after trick or treat was concluded on the
streets.
·   Even with the huge crowd everyone had a good time.
·   Fall programs were well attended and more programs are in the works.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Elm Street pump station repairs (OPWC round 19) are nearing completion. The
first new pump and controller functioned perfectly. This variable drive pump
running at half speed with a 50% duty cycle (five minutes on, five minutes off)
moves as much water as one of the old pumps running continuously at full speed.
·   The controls that we replaced were vintage 1960’s from the same company as
the new ones. The service technicians don’t think there is anyone left at the
manufacturing plant that has ever worked on our old control unit. We donated it
to them.
·   This project adds auxiliary power to operate the main plant, and replaces
the two pumps and motors that lift the raw sewage from the entire east side of
the village to the treatment plant.
·   The broken valve on the East digester tank is scheduled for repair.
Finance/Appropriations/Budget: 
·   Recreation Department and Wastewater department submitted a first
appropriation draft to the Finance Committee.
Other Items:   
·   Julie Lindner has submitted a second draft of the zoning language changes
for B2 business district that was discussed at planning Commission meeting
Monday, October 30 th at 7:30 PM.

Mayor
Mayor Maloney read her State of the Village Address:
Last year when I listened to Mayor Bragga’s State of the Village Address, I had
no idea that I would be taking the Oath of Office in August.
Having been on Council for six years, I had a good working relationship with
the employees and had been involved with the planning and setting of goals for
the Village.
·   In 2006 the Mayor started a program to promote the Village and bring
business into the Village. The DVD and the material are ready to send. There
will be a Media Blitz on January 6TH at 9 am at the Town Hall.
·   After a year and a half of planning a new fire truck was ordered and will
be here sometime this spring.
·   We have purchased two police cruisers to replace the older cruisers.
·   The Waste Water Plant purchased a sewer jet that will help the department
keep the lines clean.
·   We purchased two trucks for the Streets Department. One truck has been
delivered and the other truck will be delivered in January.
·   The Community Center has increased income so that the amount needed to
support the Center was decreased from $81,500 to $10,000.
The Village has 3 FEMA Projects that are under construction: 2 culvert repairs,
at the Mill on East Jefferson Street and East Erie Street, and a bridge repair
on Spruce Street. The projects were funded 87½% by the federal and state
governments with the Village funding 12½%.
We would like to thank the voters for passing two replacement levies in
November; 1 mil for the Fire Department and 1 ½ mil for street lighting.
For 2007 the major projects will be:
·   The improvement of Mulberry Street for the new school complex. This project
will cost approximately $695,000.00.
·   We will be paving streets and improving sidewalks.
·   The State is planning on paving Route 46 from Mulberry to Beech Street and
at that time the Village hopes to put in new sidewalks.
·   We have plans to increase the tree planting and then to apply to be a part
of Tree City USA.
·   Along with the Chamber, the Village plans to distribute the DVD to possible
new businesses.
·   There are lone range plans to improve the park with the help of volunteer
groups. The playground equipment will be moved closer to the pavilion. Again,
we want to thank the Rotary for their hard work in making that pavilion
possible.
·   Barbeque grills for the pavilion and a horseshoe pitching area are to
added.
·   We are still working on the pavement project for Cedar Street between
Chestnut and Elm Streets, as this is a safety issue. This project has been on
our plate for a number of years and we hope to resolve it this year.
·   The Planning Commission along with the Building and Lands Committee, has
been meeting with Julie Linder to establish a B-2 District to allow better use
of our business district on Chestnut and Jefferson Streets. The B-1 District
should be our “core” business district from Satin to Walnut Streets. This has
not been approved yet.
The school complex at the end of Mulberry Street should begin construction,
weather permitting, the end of March or the beginning of April. The project to
improve Mulberry Street will be at the same time and will present construction
challenges that might conflict with each other. The end result will be a new
school complex with high tech equipment and a newly paved street.

Council discussed the new Ordinance to create a B-2 Business/Commercial
District. Questions on page 7; the yard requirement changes in B1 front from
40-0 side from 5-0 and OTP the same.
Administrator Finger told council the Ordinance has been in place since 1976.

before a public hearing can be set.

Ordinance No. 07-O-2683
An Ordinance setting forth the pay for salaried, hourly and part-time employees
of the Village of Jefferson, Ohio
Discussion: Solicitor Lemire told Council that his opinion of the pay increase
changes to the Clerk/Treasurer, Councilperson and Mayor are considered an in-
term pay increase; even though it is just the PERS pick-up. Through Ethics and
the Home Rule Authority, Council can pass. In the past there have been issues
that have been questioned in the Village’s jurisdiction where the court system
ruled it illegal. Solicitor Lemire’s opinion is that Council should not pass
the Ordinances.

Personnel Issues:
·   Curt, John Buzzard Jr., Bruce Thompson, Mayor Maloney and I are attending
the Forestry Conference at Lakeland Community College this Friday, March 9th.
Service Dept.: 
·   The Street Crew is patching potholes and making sure drains are clear for
water flow.
·   The second new dump truck is in service after a warranty replacement to the
computer.
·   We are ready to dispose of the one dump truck as soon as the resolution to
surplus is effective.
·   Progress on each of the major projects we have been discussing are as
follows:
·   Route 46, (Chestnut Street) paving will be scheduled early in the paving
season of 2007.
·   SR307 and SR46 intersection improvement:
§   Right-of-Way accusations are complete with final drawing due to ODOT March
19th.
·   Drawings for SR307 and SR46 Sewer Line extension taking place concurrently
with the road improvement are 90% complete, I will review final drawings March
8th with Burgess and Niple.
·   Spruce Street Culvert repair design work is complete. The FEMA project of
bringing the culvert back to pre-flood condition will go forward.
·   Completion of West Cedar Street between South Chestnut and South Elm:
§   The West Cedar Street Appraisal Equalization Board met February 27th at 7:
30 PM. Minutes are included in your Council Packet.
§   The Board has delivered their written opinion that the assessments have
been applied equitably according to Resolution of Necessity 06-R-2656 adopted
under RC 727.12.
§   IF COUNCIL WILL PASS A MOTION TO ACCEPT THE BOARDS RECOMMENDATION, I WILL
PROCEED TO SEEK BIDS TO COMPLETE THIS JOB AT THE EARLIEST TIME POSSIBLE.
·   Mulberry Street Improvements for the new schools:
§   Design work is underway
§   Bid documents and bid opening to be completed by end of April with a 90-day
signing clause and bid price guarantee.
§   Construction Contract signing and construction can not begin before OPWC
contracts are signed (first week of July) or we lose $300,000.00 in assistance.
Fire Dept. /Police Department
·   Nothing new to report.
Recreation/Community Center :
·   Nothing unusual to report.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   OPWC Round 19 (rehab of the Elm Street pump station and main plant stand by
power) will be complete as soon as Natural Gas flow to the new generator is
complete.
·   We started the generator but it is starved for natural gas.
·   Dominion failed to remember that years ago the main gas line to the plant
had been repaired with a plastic liner restricting flow through a 3/8 orifice.
·   We may have to replace the gas line from the end of Elm Street to the Plant
to get the required flow to run the generator under full load.
·   OPWC Round 20 (rehab of the Main Plant Electrical Controls) will go to bid
in March, 2007

Motion by Councilman Thompson to go into Public Hearing at 8:00 pm regarding
the new Zoning Ordinance to create a B-2 Business/Commercial District
2nd
Roll: All yea; motion carried
Administrator Finger explained to Council and to the public that the new B-
2 Business/Commercial District Zoning would redefine the B-1 Business District
and create a B-2 Business/Commercial District and Old Town Business District.
The New B-2 District and Old Town Business District would change the set backs,
front yards and driveway access. The B-1 permissive use limits would change the
non-residential uses with drive-in or drive-through services.
Solicitor Lemire explained to the Council and public the zoning issues came up
last summer when Auto Zone was looking at property to purchase in the Village.
Some residents were upset due to the possibility of tearing down old historical
houses, and came to Council with their concerns.
Council hired Consultant Julie Linder to put together a combination of other
Business Districts and came to the Planning Commission with a recommendation.
The Planning Commission voted on the new recommendation with a 5-0 vote passing
the legislation then sent the legislation to Council to take action.
The Village also hired Cleveland State University to work on a two-year plan
with the Village Zoning Code.
Solicitor Lemire explained to everyone that anyone who wishes to speak during
the Public Hearing will be giving a public testimony and must be sworn in.
Solicitor Lemire administered the Oath of Truthfulness to Administrator Finger,
Franklin Snyder of 116 West Jefferson Street, Jefferson, OH and Barney Harrell
of Wyoming.
Franklin Snyder, of 116 West Jefferson Street, Jefferson, OH., addressed
Council in regards to his suggested changes to Amend the Village of Jefferson’s
Zoning Code Ordinance; which include the following:
{'{'}not available{'}'}
Barney Harrell of Wyoming told Council that Mr. Snyder did a very good job with
his suggestions. He suggested to Council under 1256.03 page 8…strike and have
site improvements-architectural features. Page 9 item number 2 conflicts with
requirements, it should be 20 feet. Questioned map; B-1 District established
one property that faces Chestnut Street as B-2, why?
Administrator Finger told Mr. Harrell that the property was non-conforming.

Memo: Out-of-Office
   Councilman Thompson questioned who would be covering for the Clerk/Treasurer
when she will be out-of-the-office.
Clerk/Treasurer Fisher reported to Council that prior to her leaving the office
on Friday, March 23rd, payroll will be completed. All checks and purchase
orders will be written by Friday also. If a purchase order is required during
this time, Administrator Finger will have the book to give out numbers. Vickie
Rodgers will be taking minutes in the absence of the Clerk/Treasurer Fisher at
the April 2nd, 2007 Council Meeting.
Clerk/Treasurer Fisher explained to Council that the Billy Joe Cole Fund was a
Trust Fund and to close a Trust Fund a written request must be made by those in
charge of the fund. The family of Billy Joe Cole sent a written request stating
they wished the Trust Fund to be closed and monies be used in a Scholarship
Fund for Kid’s Activities at the Jefferson Community Recreation Center.

·   A complete review and rewrite of all Village job descriptions is under way
and will be presented to council for approval by the end of Summer.
·   Curt and I attended the Storm Water management class march 28th as planned.
·   The Village of Jefferson is exempt from all the permit requirements and
expensive run off prevention.
·   I will provide Council with a summary of the conference and report how we
have already implemented some of the best practices that EPA recommends.
Service Dept.: 
·   The Street Department started brush pick up today April 2, 2007 and will
continue the first Monday of the month through October 7th. 2007.
·   Progress on each of the major projects we have been discussing are as
follows:
·   Route 46, (Chestnut Street) paving will be scheduled early in the paving
season of 2007.
·   SR307 and SR46 intersection improvement:
§   Right-of-way acquisitions are Complete
§   Final Drawings were delivered to ODOT. We are waiting for final approval.
§   Drawings for SR307 and SR46 Sewer line extension taking place concurrently
with the road improvement are complete and have been included in the
Intersection bid set.
·   Spruce Street Culvert repair design work is complete. The FEMA project,
bringing the culvert back to pre-flood condition, will go forward.
·   Completion of West Cedar Street between S. Chestnut and S. Elm:
§   Legal ads are running in the papers.
§   Pre Bid meeting is scheduled for April 6th.
§   Bid opening is scheduled for April 13th.
·   Mulberry Street Improvements for the new schools:
§   Design work is underway
§   Bid documents and bid opening to be completed by end of April with a 90-day
signing clause and bid price guarantee.
§   Construction Contract signing and construction can not begin before OPWC
contracts are signed (first week of July) or we lose $300,000.00 in assistance

items.

Solicitor Lemire informed Council that he had a conversation with Mr. Todd
Rodgers. Mr Rodgers is an attorney with Chester, Willcox, & Saxbe, LLP, of 65
East State Street, Suite 1000, Columbus, OH. Mr. Rodgers drafted the article
Effectively Regulating Cable and Video Programming Services as Technologies and
Regulatory Environments Evolve.
Mr. Rodgers advised Solicitor Lemire that his hourly rate is $190.00. He
suggested that the Council pass a Comprehensive Right-of-Way Ordinance usage by
way of fees and permits for electric, water, cable, telephone, and gas
companies.
Many cities have adopted and Ordinance and then implemented it.
Right-of-Way Revised Code State Legislation regulates how much we can charge.
The State says we can not override. Ordinance will need to go to PUCO. All
utilities that are already in place will be required to follow the
Comprehensive Right-of-Way Ordinance.
It will cost approximately $5,000 to pass Ordinance and to go through PUCO.
There will be a low annual fee of 1,200-1,300 per year after Ordinance is
adopted.
Columbus is pushing legislation to do away with franchise fees that are
currently in place. In passing this Comprehensive Right-of-Way Ordinance, we
will recoup some of the fees and keep our monies set-up in the Ordinance.
Councilman Hoyson asked if this would include satellite services. No they are
not on the Right-of-Way as per Solicitor Lemire.
Councilman Thompson asked that the following information is taken from the
above mentioned article by Mr. Todd Rodgers.
Traditional telephone companies (Telcos), long regulated by the Federal
Communications Commission (FCC) and state public utility commissions in the
provision of traditional land line telephone service, are not more aggressively
entering the cable television.
In Ohio, AT&T is beginning to roll out Project Lightspeed and offer a
competitive video service called U-Verse. Verizon is beginning to roll out its
Project VIOS, offering similar services as AT&T’s Project Lightspeed.
In exchange for granting a cable franchise for use of the local public right-
of-way, municipalities can require cable companies to pay a local franchising
fee. This fee cannot exceed to five percent (5%) of gross revenues received for
cable services sold in the local municipality.
Telcos seeking to provide competitive video service are trying to avoid cable
franchise requirements. Telcos argue that their competitive video service is
not a cable service because of the different technology used to provide video
programming. Telcos argue that their video programming service is an
information service under the 1996 Telecommunication Act and thereby exempt
from traditional cable regulatory framework found in 47 U.S.C. §521 et.seq. A
federal district court in the northern district of California held that a
municipality had the right to require AT&T to obtain a franchise from the
municipality prior to providing a competitive video service in the community
despite the technological differences.
Even through the current versions of the bills retain the franchise fee payment
to municipalities, there is always the possibility that these bills could be
amended prior to passage to remove the local franchise fee payment requirement.
The best action that a municipality can take, is if has not already done so, is
to enact a Comprehensive Right-of-Way Ordinance that sets forth regulations for
use of municipal right-of-ways and permits the municipality to recoup the costs
of regulating the rights of way through the imposition of cost based annual
right-of-way fees.
Why is a Comprehensive Right-of-Way Ordinance the answer to adapting to changes
in the telecommunications services market and potential changes to federal law
regarding cable television franchising? The answer is simple-a Comprehensive
Right-of-Way Ordinance serves a similar purpose as a cable franchise. Yet, a
Comprehensive Right-of-Way Ordinance is not affected by the nature or type of
technology developed by a company using the public right-of-way to construct
their networks. Additionally, a Comprehensive Right-of-Way is unlikely to be
impacted by any amendments to the Telecommunications Act of 1996.
A Comprehensive Right-of-Way Ordinance regulates the location and placement of
facilities in a municipal right-of-way and generally requires cooperation among
service providers to work together to conserve valuable and limited right-of-
way space. Additionally, most Comprehensive Right-of-Way Ordinances also impose
an annual fee for the use of the right-of-ways.
Those municipalities with a Comprehensive Right-of-Way Ordinance will be able
to continue to regulate such items as the location and placement of facilities
in municipal rights-of-ways by cable and competitive video providers. Will be
able to require cable and video programming services providers to restore
right-of-way that has been damaged by their respective operations.
The competitive video services agreement should require that Telcos pay the
same fees to the municipality as cable companies do. Telcos should also be
subject to all of the same requirements to which cable companies who provide
cable services in your community are subject. In the meantime, those
municipalities that have yet to enact a Comprehensive Right-of-Way Ordinance
need to seriously consider enacting a Comprehensive Right-of-Way Ordinance. A
Comprehensive Right-of-Way Ordinance will allow the municipality to protect its
rights to regulate its public rights-of-ways and to recoup a fee to offset
those costs incurred in regulating the right-of-way regardless of any changes
in technology that may occur in the future and how such technologies may be
currently regulated under the 1996 Telecommunications Act.
Motion by Councilman Fertig to have Solicitor Lemire to draft the Ordinance,
then sending the Ordinance to Mr. Todd Rodgers to look over.

Ordinance No. 07-O-2706
An Ordinance authorizing the issuance of special assessment notes to the amount
of, not to exceed, two hundred seventy thousand dollars (270,000) in
anticipation of the issuance of bonds for the purpose of improving and paving
West Cedar Street between the points where it intersects with South Chestnut
and South Elm Street and declaring an emergency
Buildings/Lands
Richard Crowe of the Chestnut Street Associates spoke to Council about
opposition of the zoning change. These issues go back as far as last summer.
This has prohibited the sale of the property for Auto-Zone.
Gary Pascalone, attorney for Chestnut Street Associates, told Council that the
Village did not comply in accordance to the Ohio Revised Code. Stated Public
Hearing notices are not adequate. Further stated that the Village was in
violation because not a second hearing was not set in advance. Notices were not
sent to the surrounding property owners. Do to these violations the sale of the
property was prohibited.
The houses have been modified and do not meet criteria for the historical
district.
Councilman Ward told Council that Solicitor Lemire gave his opinion and the
revised ordinance did not change the context of the ordinance, it cleared up
wording and spelling. Solicitor Lemire said that we did not have to have
another public hearing.
Solicitor Lemire explained to Council that in his opinion the Village was in
compliance with everything regarding the original public hearing and stated a
second hearing was not needed because the context of the ordinance was not
changed.
Fran Blanchard of Triple C Development addressed Council stating that Auto Zone
was and is trying to do everything in context to the ordinance in place. Told
Council that Administrator Finger has been very supportive with their efforts
to do everything correctly so that Auto Zone would be in compliance to the
ordinance. Also stated that it will take a great deal of money to get the
property ready to build.
Motion by Councilman Ward for the third reading of Ordinance No. 07-O-2698
2nd
Roll: All yea; motion carried
Motion by Councilman Ward to adopt Ordinance No. 07-O-2698
2nd
Roll: All yea; motion carried

Personnel Issues:
·   Christine Harting, part time desk help at rec., has given two weeks notice
for resignation. The open position will be posted internally before advertising
to the general public.
·   I need Council to accept her resignation.
Service Dept.: 
·   Quotes on the new cold storage building have been reviewed with Jackson
Construction submitting the lowest and best Quote. Jackson Construction also
built the building at the wastewater plant.
·   This project is being done in three phases to accommodate the cash flow in
224 fund.
·   Phase one will be the building
·   Phase two the concrete floor
·   Phase three will be finishing the inside.
·   Each phase is below the $25,000.00 bid limit.
·   The Village park work is moving forward,
·   Topsoil and seed to be finished by June 25th..
·   Boy Scout horseshoe pits are delayed pending project approval from the Boy
Scout review board.
·   Site plan for the restrooms with utilities is complete.
·   Restroom plans have been approved by the building department.
·   Concrete grill pads will be poured June 14th for the cooking grills.
·   Repaving the parking area will take place after the underground utilities
are run past the area to be paved.
·   Normal paving bid was accepted by council and is awaiting a scheduled time
slot.
·   Progress on each of the major projects we have been discussing are as
follows:
·   Route 46, (Chestnut Street) paving project:
§   Intermediate paving complete
§   Finish Surface paving June 29th . June 19 downtown area starting at 5:00
AM, June 20 north and south ends.
§   Final paint for lanes and parking as soon as practical after paving.
§   Concrete sidewalks and ramps Complete.
·   SR307 and SR46 intersection improvement:
§   Utility relocation is well under way. Electric, Gas and water is scheduled.
§   All paperwork submitted to the State June 1st.
§   Award of the Construction Contract scheduled for:   6/5/2007
§   Waiting for Notice to Proceed from ODOT
·   Spruce Street Culvert repair is out for bid. With opening scheduled for
June 15th.
·   Spruce Street site distance improvements will be the Village 2008 OPWC
round 22 grant request.
·   Paving West Cedar Street between S. Chestnut and S. Elm:
§   Contract with Hysong Paving is completed.
§   Start Construction June 25th 
§   Complete Construction by July 27th.
·   Mulberry Street Improvements for the new schools:
§   Design work is underway
§   Bid documents and bid opening to be completed by end of ?.
§   Construction Contract signing and construction can not begin before OPWC
contracts are signed (first week of July) or we lose $300,000.00 in assistance.
§   The street is already beginning to show breakup as we expected from the
heavy equipment.
§   We will monitor conditions daily and repair as necessairy.
·   New School Construction:
§   Well under way and ahead of schedule.
§   Village will inspect storm drain lines and relocation of drainage ditch.
§   Village will also inspect the Sanitary Sewer installation out side the
buildings.
§   We are receiving over 52,000 cubic yards of good clay fill dirt on Sycamore
truck route.
§   This fill dirt would be valued at over $200,000.00 if we had to purchase
it.
Fire Dept./Police Department
Nothing to report
Recreation/Community Center :
·   Soccer session one is under way.

·   Day Camps are under way as well.

A motion at 8:00 pm. by Councilman Thompson to go into the published Public
Hearing for review of the 2008 Tax Budget,
2nd
Roll: All yea, motion carried
Clerk-Treasurer Fisher told Council that this is the estimated Tax Budget for
2008. These figures are estimated based on the revenues that come in and year
end figures
Councilman Ward asked if there had been a drop in the General Fund revenue
since 2005. He questioned where all the income tax monies were – what funds
they are placed in; and asked about the personal property tax along with the
Homestead Roll backs
Clerk-Treasurer Fisher explained that when the Village increased the .50%
Income Tax, the Village dropped a 1.75 general operating levy, which reduced
the General Fund revenue. The Village divided the income tax into three funds-
General, Capital, and a new Safety Services fund.
Regarding Personal Property Taxes – they were reduced because they will be
phased out by 2010; and the Homestead Tax is a reduced rate to assist Senior
Citizens.
A motion at 8:15 pm. by Councilman Thompson to return to regular session
2nd
Roll: All yea, motion carried.
Regular Session – 8:15 pm.
A motion by Councilman Thompson to approve the Tax Budget for 2008
2nd
Roll: All yea, motion carried.
After the tax budget was approved, Councilman Thompson remarked that the
Recreation Department would need financial help from Council, if the present
trend continues.
In regard to the sewer increase, Administrator Finger told Council that the
increase had been discussed as far back as the end of 2006, and when the budget
process was taking place at the beginning of 2007, as noted in the memo dated
1/22/07.
Councilman Ward expressed concern that the sewer rate increase will affect the
senior citizens in the Village. Most live on a fixed income. He said that
according to a Cleveland State study from 1990-2000, the Village now has about
53% of the residents on a fixed income. Councilman Ward did say that the sewer
rates have been idle for a few years until 2007.
Councilman Ward asked if the Village could pick up the refuse cost and take the
expense from the General Fund, stating this would help some of the cost to the
residents.
Councilman Thompson said he favors the increase and stated that maybe we as
Council should have been implementing the 3.5 percent increase yearly over the
last few years. Mr. Thompson also stated that the Sewer Improvement Fund is an
Enterprise Fund and should support itself not transfer monies from the General
Fund
Administrator Finger told Council that the Plant had an EPA inspection with no
problems. The Village has been spending the money for these projects to keep us
in compliance with the EPA.
Councilman Hoyson stated he understands that all the projects and costs are
dealing with safety issues and the Village must be up to date with everything.
Councilman Fertig told Council the Village has borrowed a lot of money for
projects and maybe we should not do as many projects.
Administrator Finger told Council the money we borrowed for these projects are
at zero or a minimal interest rate at the 2007 interest rate.

Personnel Issues:
·   Engineering summer intern Leo Debevic finished summer employment and will
return to Case. He was a real asset and became part of the team.
Service Dept.: 
·   Cold Storage Building construction is underway.
·   The Village park work is moving forward,
·   Boy Scout horseshoe pit project is complete .
·   SOCC approved $5,000.00 to help pay to extend utilities past the parking
area.
·   Receiving quotes on Utility extension at the park
·   Normal paving bid was accepted by council and is scheduled for late August.
·   Progress on each of the major projects we have been discussing are as
follows:
·   SR307 and SR46 intersection improvement:
§   Utility relocation is complete.
§   Received Notice to Proceed from ODOT
§   All contracts to be signed 8/20/2002
§   Pre construction meeting is scheduled for 10:00 AM 8/20/2007.
§   I should have a construction timeline soon after that meeting
·   Spruce Street Culvert repair bid was successful.
§   Start date not scheduled yet.
·   Paving West Cedar Street between S. Chestnut and S. Elm:
§   Construction started on July 5th and is progressing.
§   Construction completion by the end of August.
·   Mulberry Street Improvements for the new schools:
§   Bid opening at 12:00 noon August 17th produced a low bid of $684,487.00
from Tri Mor Corporation., Twinsburg, Ohio. I recommend that Council accept
this low bid and suspend Council three reading rule to adopt the resolution for
this project.
§   There were three bidders: Tri Mor Construction, Koski, and Mr. Excavator
Inc. The Tri Mor bid was some $43,000.00 higher than the estimate but still
below the 115% maximum allowed.
§   I held a meeting with the school staff and school construction management
firm to make some preliminary plans for traffic flow.
§   The consensus was to continue to restrict through traffic and send buses
and students out Popular Street. There will be manual operation of the street
light on Jefferson Street to speed the flow.
§   We are continuing to monitor the street conditions and maintaining as
needed.
·   New School Construction:
§   Village has been inspecting the storm and sanitary sewer line
installations.
§   We will still receive fill from the school construction.
§   Due to the huge volume of dirt we received, we had to file a notice of
intent and storm water management plan with OEPA. The Street Department has
delayed other work to make sure we are in compliance with OEPA.
·   Sidewalk replacement.
§   Work is scheduled to begin week of 8/20/07.
Fire Dept./Police Department
Nothing to report
Recreation/Community Center :
·   Morning pre school classes are full and there are ten kids signed up for an
afternoon class.
·   We have a growing number of students attending the safety town program.
This year there were 85 young ones with seven high school helpers.
·   Rec. is planning a Halloween scary forest event in the park this year
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Work on the FEMA Safety Grant to stabilize the stream bank is scheduled to
start week of 8/20/07.
·   The Thursday night, August 9th, rain event was the first real test of the
Elm Street pump station improved pumping capacity with out overflow capability
to the creek. We did not overflow anywhere!
·   There are a couple problems that surfaced with control floats and controls
that need to be addressed.
Finance/Appropriations/Budget:
§   Finance committee met to go over the sewer improvement fund shortfall under
discussion.
§   Finance committee has asked for further information and discussion will
continue.
Other Items:   
·   None to report

Austinburg on route 45. He talked with Mark Jones, the area manager of First
Energy, and the power outage was caused by a grid that went down in Austinburg
on route 45. All of the south county was down as far as Orwell.
Administrator Finger said that a Public Notice will be sent out stating that
the intersection at route 46 and 307 will be closed from September 4, 2007 to
November 12, 2007.

2nd
Roll: All yea, motion carried.
Resolution No. 07-R-2718
A resolution re-authorizing the pickup of 95% of the Mandatory 10% employee
contribution to the Ohio Police & Fire Pension Fund and declaring an emergency.
Clerk/Treasurer Fisher explained to Council that the reason this resolution is
before Council is because Ohio Police & Fire Pension Fund would not accept the
Village’s pickup Resolution previously adopted by Council.
During discussion that followed, Councilman Ward questioned the wording “95% of
10%”; and he also asked if there would be penalties if the ordinance was not in
compliance with Ohio Police & Fire Pension Fund.
Clerk/Treasurer Fisher said that according to the letter from Ohio Police &
Fire Pension Fund dated July 25th which Councilman Ward requested, there could
be penalties up to $1,000 a day if the issues are not corrected and the
resolution adopted by August 22, 2007.
Clerk/Treasurer Fisher told Council that the resolution, which is before
Council, was a draft recommended by Ohio Police & Fire Pension Fund which was
attached to the July 25th letter.
Motion by Councilman Ward to suspend Council rules for Resolution No. 07-R-2718
2nd
Roll: All yea, motion carried.
Motion by Councilman Ward to adopt Resolution No. 07-R-2718
2nd
Roll: All yea, motion carried.
Motion by Councilman Ward for the first reading of Resolution No. 07-R-2719
2nd
Roll: All yea, motion carried.

Jim Reuschling, a local contractor, commented on a publicized proposal to
increase tape-in fees into the village sewer system. Mr. Reuschling asked
Council to reconsider increasing the tap-in fees. He said an increase would be
bad for the local housing industry. The poor economy is taking a toll on the
contracting businesses in the area.
Councilman Ward told Reuschling that Council has yet to make a final decision
regarding the tap-in fees. Councilman Ward said Council is studying everything
from sewer rates to tap-in fees in an effort to resolve the sewer fund deficit
issue.

Councilman Ward questioned the unclaimed funds on the list of bills.
Clerk/Treasurer Fisher told Council that when a check has not been cashed after
a sixty day period, it becomes invalid. A letter is sent to the person the
check was issued to advising them if the check is still in their position to
bring it in, since it is now invalid, and a new one will be issued to them. If
for some reason the check did not reach them at all, they are asked to come in
and a check will be issued to them for the amount owed them.

Chris Wright from Tennessee spoke to Council regarding to the new Auto Zone
sign. Wright told Council that he had spoken to the Planning Commission asking
for permission to use 110 square feet sign. The code requirement is not to
exceed 50 square feet. The Planning Commission did not approve the signage
variance. Wright presented to Council new signage figures totaling 65 square
feet of signage for the Auto Zone Building He asked the Council to consider the
new change. He explained that Auto Zone would bring in more tax dollars.
Councilman Ward told Council Auto Zone was requesting the signage variance
because of a hardship of the building being set back so far. Ward expressed
that the hardship was induced and they should have no problem marketing Auto
Zone.

help the Village keep its pristine look.

Visitor Comments: (five (5) minute limit, as per council rule #13)
Carolyn Angelotti went over Embarq’s concerns detailed in the following
handout:
October 24, 2007
Jefferson Right of Way Policy (draft ) 07-02714
Concerns of Embarq
1.   Embarq still has a concern with the fee of $1500.00, how did the village
arrive or come up with the permit fee amount? What was the cost basis? This
question still has not been answered
2.   1019.03 F – page 8 – Newly created ROW committee will approve or deny
applications, hear and determine applications for hardship variances. There are
no specific times listed here.
3.   1019.04 B – page 8 & 9 – The term of each such General Right-of Way Permit
shall be for ten (10) years from issuance, or such lesser term as the Applicant
requests. This should not apply to Embarq since we are required by state law
(Carrier of Last Resort obligations) to provide telecommunications service to
all in the community? We would like it to be open ended. Possibly you could
keep the 10 years with an exception for all ‘required’ public utilities like
Embarq? We still have concerns with timing on approvals. Would “A” apply to
Embarq verses “B”? Would this be a blanket franchise where once I have paid the
$1500 we can go wherever we need to go? Which means approval times wouldn’t
apply to us. Or, do I need to apply every time work needs to be completed? If
it’s a blanket franchise, the term “BLANKET” needs to be put into the policy
(29 days for approval)
4.   1019.06 #9 – Page 13 – We’re not sure what is intended in the paragraph?
Could you further explain? Clarify language – does this mean joint use/someone
else leasing lines from us/or both?
5.   1019.09 A – Page 15 – This was one of our main concerns when we met with
the Village Council. We agree with number iv, but disagree with number 1, 11,
111, and v. Embarq believes that having a valid agreement with Embarq is
critical for safety concerns and a clear understanding for the joint use of
facilities. We still do not agree with this language. We do agree with number
4, but disagree with number 1, ii, iii, and v.
6.   1019.12 A – Page 17 – This is a change in procedure. Who do we notify and
what information will be needed? Still not clear on who needs to be notified.
Will an operations manual be created on what to do and what is required to be
filled out”?
Jennifer Godleski of West Cedar Street asked Council what the Solicitor found
out aout accepting the road.
Solicitor Lemire told everyone that the Village will not have to do paperwork
to accept the road because we built the road. Building permits can be issued.
Administrator Finger told Council Hyson is scheduled to do the repairs, but the
repairs will not be completed until Spring Everything is completed but three
repairs.
Jennifer Godleski requested a copy of Hyson’s contract, the ODOT inspection
approving the road, and asked what engineering company did the inspection.
Administrator Finger told Godleski that Smolen engineering did the inspection
and he would get her the paperwork. Administrator Finger also told Council that
First Energy has a request to turn the lights n at Route 46 and it will be done
this week.
DEPARTMENT REPORTS
Administrator’s Report
The following is the Village Administrator's update on active projects.
Service Dept.: 
·   Repairs for West Cedar Street were attempted on Friday 11/29/07 but cold
temperatures prevented paving. A final attempt will be scheduled for first week
of December. If this attempt fails then we will wait until spring of 2008.
·   SR307, SR 167 and SR46 intersection improvement project and sewer extension
is close to completion.
·   Traffic signals should be completed by Tuesday, December 4th.
·   The road can legally be reopened as soon as the traffic signals are
functional.
·   Final site restoration and new sidewalks will be scheduled in the spring of
2008.
·   North Spruce Street at East Jefferson Street is reopened as planned
·   Mulberry Street was reopened Friday November 30.
·   24 inches of berm material was applied Monday December 3rd.
·   Final grading will continue as practical with some work needing to be
finished next year.
·   Finish surface coat will not be applied until 2009 after the school
construction traffic has finished.
·   Leaf and brush pick up continues.
·   OPWC round 22 Spruce Street grant is the top ranked project from our
region. Notice to proceed is expected in July 2008 after Council approves the
final award.
Fire Dept./Police Department
·   Nothing to report.
Recreation Department
·   Nothing unusual to report.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   The digester blower was received Friday November 30 and it will be
installed as soon as possible.
·   The last major project to upgrade the wastewater plant began Monday
November 26 and will continue through the winter.
Other Items:
·   Departmental appropriation meetings are going well. Fire and Administration
are scheduled with the Finance Committee on December 10th at 5:30 PM.
·   I request that council approve me and the four supervisors attending a new
supervisors training class in Hudson, Ohio on December 13th.

The following is the Village Administrator's update on active projects.
Service Dept.:
