·   The following notice was attached to each residents door.
PUBLIC SERVICE ANNOUNCEMENT
Village of Jefferson
Construction will cease on W. Mulberry Street until spring of 2008.
At a meeting today, 12/03/2007, Tri More Construction, the general contractor
for this project, and the Village of Jefferson have decided to cease
construction due to the deteriorating weather.
Items expected to be completed before total cession include:
·   Restoration of mail boxes and road berms next to each mail box.
·   Addition of berming material next to parking aprons.
·   Storm water drainage sufficient enough to prevent ponding.
·   Traffic control signage to maintain safe traffic flow.
·   Edge of pavement markers to warn of soft shoulders.
Spring of 2008 Tri More Construction will finish the following:
·   Right of way clean up, final grading, topsoil, and seeding
·   Provide berm material for the entire street as needed
·   Pavement edge sealing
·   Edge line, center line marking and other similar items.
·   Repairs to problem areas that may show up through the winter. (Mutually
agreed upon)
W. Mulberry Street was built to a condition of strength to handle the truck
traffic that will be generated by the construction of the new Jr. Sr. High
School in 2008.
Any road problems that may show up during this time can be addressed while the
surface is still in an unfinished state.
The final finished asphalt surface will be applied after the heavy construction
traffic at the schools has ceased. At this time the final road profile will be
set, driveways will be matched to finish grade, edge material will again be
added and rolled to give us a smooth, well constructed road.
If you have any problems call me at 440-576-3946
Thank you for your cooperation and understanding.
Terry Finger
Village Administrator

The names of the candidates for the vacant council seat were presented:
Kathleen C. Baxley, Kay Ann Brabender, Gary L. Godleski, John G. Kish, and John
G. Kish.
A secret ballot was taken and counted.:
Kay Ann Brabender: three votes
Kathleen Baxley: one vote
Frank Snyder: one vote
A Village ordinance states that a candidate must have a total of three votes to
win the vacated council seat, so Kay Ann Brabender was declared the winner.

meeting

Service Dept.: 
·   Christmas tree pick up is under way and will continue until January 14th.
·   Trees need to be stripped of plastic bags, ornaments, lights, and stands in
other words just natural trees.
·   Yearly village wide trash pick up is scheduled for Saturday, May 3rd. Items
to be disposed of need to be at curb side by 7:00 AM. Curbside pick up will be
completed for the entire village by 9:30 AM. More information will be provided
before May 3rd.
·   Leaf and brush pick up will be discontinued until spring.
·   A replacement sidewalk plow was put in service just in time before this
last heavy snow. The old plow transmission overheated in heavy snow and the
differential was worn out.
·   Natural Gas and Electricity is installed in the Community Park. This
electricity will also power the oil pump at the Gas well enabling production to
begin as soon as the gauges are calibrated by Dominion East Ohio Gas Company.
Time estimate is seven to ten days.
Fire Dept./Police Department
·   No bids were received for the surplus fire truck.
Recreation Department
·   The Natural Gas well revenue will be used to pay the bond payment on the
Recreation Center as approved by Council.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Nothing unusual to report.
·   During 2008 we will start eliminating storm water infiltration into our
wastewater collection system as mandated by OEPA.
Other Items:
·   The Jefferson membership in the Flood Plan Insurance Program was renewed
effective December 18, 2007. As noted before, there are no structures existing
in the flood plane, this includes our wastewater plant buildings.

Mayor Maloney read her State of the Village Address::
   At the end 2006, I had been Mayor for 4 months. 2007 was my first full year
in office. After a year, I can tell you that being Mayor has been a pleasure –
yes, a challenge at times, but always a pleasure.
   Everyone who lives here takes pride in the community making our job easier.
The list of major projects that were projected at the beginning of the year,
has dwindled. Most are completed and others are well on their way to
completion.
2007 Completed projects include:
·   FEMA N. Spruce Culvert   at a cost of $43,000.00
·   FEMA             E. Erie Street       Culvert at a cost of $20,400.00
·   FEMA             E. Jefferson Street       Culvert at a cost of $123,505.00
·   OPWC Emergency Repair Stream Edge at a cost of $213,575.00
·   OWDA Sewer Extension N. Chestnut at a cost of $274.000.00
·   W. Cedar Street       at a cost of $276,000.00
·   2007 Street Repaving at a cost of $155,000,00
·   2007 Sidewalks repaired at a cost of $40,000.00
·   New Cold Storage at Streets at a cost of $47,000.00
·   Web Site development at a cost of a$7,200.00
·   Village Tree Maintenance/Replacement at a cost of $13,000.00
These completed projects totaled $1,233,180.00
2007/2008 Projects in progress include:
·   OPWC #20 Main Plant (Loan) $410,000.00
·   OPWC #            21 Mulberry Street       at an estimated cost of
$695,000.00
·   Safety Grant 307, 46 N. Intersection at an estimated cost of $1,100,900.00
·   Park Drawings/Pond/Restrooms/Utilities at an estimated cost of $12,000.00
·   Park Trails/School Sidewalks Grant cost unknown
·   Cleveland          State       Downtown Study at an estimated cost of
$34,000.00
At this time, the cost of projects in progress total $2,251,900.00
2008 Projects in Progress include:
·   OPWC North and South Spruce Grade change at an estimated cost of
$188,235.00
·   Zoning/All Map Updates at an estimated cost of $3,000.00
·   Street Lights at Intersection at an estimated cost of $30,000.00
Projects that are planned for 2008/2009
·   Streetscape Downtown cost unknown
·   N. Sycamore Truck Route       cost unknown
·   Increase Sidewalk Repairs at an estimated cost of $60,000.00
·   Mulberry Sidewalks at an estimated cost of $20,000.00
·   Final Paving for             Mulberry Street       at an estimated cost of
$55,000.00
   There are several projects that were major, but the one that stands out as
not only a benefit to the Village but also to the County is the Rt. 46 & 307/
167 intersection. The work was completed the first part of December and is a
welcome convenience.
   Another that benefits the whole community is the park on             East
Jefferson Street      . There were groups of volunteers and individual
volunteers who helped pull this project together. From the pavilion, to the
playground, lights and parking lot, we could not have asked for a more
dedicated and devoted group.
   Programs at the ever popular             Jefferson          Community
Center       have been very well received with excellent participation
   The Planning Commission and Building and Lands Committee are still designing
and working through the arduous task of establishing Business districts to
allow for better use of our commercial area.
   The promotional effort between the Village and Chamber which produced a
documentary type DVD that is narrated by former Mayor Larry Bragga, does the
Village and the County proud. The DVD is still available. Just stop by if you
want one.
There have been streets paved, sidewalks replaced, and the trees that we
planted qualifies us to be a part of Tree City, USA.
   Reconstruction of             Mulberry Street       to accommodate heavy
construction traffic to the new school site is complete. The school complex,
which we are looking forward to, is coming along nicely.
   In conclusion, I’d like to wish you all a happy, healthy and prosperous New
Year!

Service Dept.: 
·   The gas well was activated on January 17, 2008. By next council meeting
(Feb 4th.) we should have some idea how productive it will be.
·   Yearly village wide trash pick up is scheduled for Saturday, May 3rd. Items
to be disposed of need to be at curb side by 7:00 AM. Curbside pick up will be
completed for the entire village by 9:30 AM. More information will be provided
before May 3rd.
·   Leaf and brush pick up will be discontinued until spring.
·   Village crews are actively working on ditch cleaning/repair with the break
in Winter Weather.
·   Water and sewer lines will be installed by the Village crew at the park.
·   West Cedar water retention ditch will be tiled and closed in by the Village
crew as required by Council.
Fire Dept./Police Department
·   Solicitor Lemire has advised me that we can accept the bid from Dorset Fire
Department for the surplus fire truck. No new bids were received for the
surplus fire ruck at the last opening. We have already spent about $1,500 in
advertising three different times.
·   My recommendation to the Council is to accept the $8,000.00 bid from Dorset
and disregard the expectation of receiving more money for it.
Recreation Department
·   Nothing unusual to report.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Main plant electrical upgrade is continuing.
·   During 2008 we will start eliminating storm water infiltration into our
wastewater collection system as mandated by OEPA.
Other Items:
·   The Village of Jefferson facilities received an inspection from the Bureau
of Workers’ Compensation Safety and Health Compliance Office. His overall
impression was so favorable that he is telling everyone what a great
environment and concern for safety we have. A written report will address the
few minor issues he found. Another very good job by all our employees.
·   I have assigned Curt Stone and Bill Hitchcock to attend the Professional
Young Tree Pruning Workshop in Vermilion, Ohio Wednesday January 23rd. They
will drive a Village Vehicle in case you get a call.
·   In your packet there is a training flyer for the annual North Coast Urban
Forestry Conference held at Lakeland Community College. I would like a motion
for Curt, Bill, and me to attend along with members of the Forestry Committee
if possible. This is a needed session to keep up with the latest topics in
managing the Village street trees.
Administrator Finger included a brochure on the North Coast Urban Forestry
Conference for Council’s review.

Finance
There was discussion concerning the 1975 Fire Truck put out for bid. After it
was published twice with only two responses, the highest being $8,000, the Fire
Chief reported that there seems to be additional interest in the truck. Since
it is so expensive to advertise, it was thought that perhaps, it would be more
advantageous to accept the $8,000.00 bid. Councilman Fertig said we should
approach other fire departments in anticipation of getting a higher bid.
Councilman Hoyson said we should get as much as we can. Administrator Finger
said it is a 30-year old truck, and there doesn’t seem to be that much
interest. Councilman Thompson said we should “put the fire truck to bed” and
not seek more bids.
Motion by Councilman Thompson to accept the $8,000.00 bid by the Dorset
Volunteer Fire Department for the 1975 Fire Truck
2nd 
      Roll: Fertig, nay; Hoyson, nay; Thompson, yea; Ward, yea; Brabender, yea
Roll: 3-yea; 2-nay, motion carried.
A finance committee meeting was scheduled for January 28 at 7:00 pm to wrap up
the 2008 budget and discuss possibility of raises.

Service Dept.: 
·   The gas well was activated on January 17, 2008. On February 1st the well
was still pumping water with little gas pressure. We still have no idea how
productive it will be.
·   Leaf and brush pick up will be discontinued until spring except for wind
damage limbs.
·   Village crews are actively working on ditch cleaning/repair as weather
permits.
·   Water line was installed by the Village crew at the park. Sewer lines are
still planned.
·   Material to tile the West Cedar water retention ditch has been received and
will be tiled and closed in by the Village crew as required by Council.
Fire Dept./Police Department
·   Nothing unusual to report
Recreation Department
·   Nothing unusual to report.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Main plant electrical upgrade is progressing nicely.
·   During 2008 we will start eliminating storm water infiltration into our
wastewater collection system as mandated by OEPA.
Other Items:
·   Curt Stone and Bill Hitchcock attended the Professional Young Tree Pruning
Workshop in Vermilion, Ohio Wednesday January 23rd. They were both impressed
with the school. They got to work on the city of Vermilion trees and learned
that Vermilion had poor practices in the past. Namely planting trees too deep
and not pruning after planting..
·   There will be five of us going to the annual North Coast Urban Forestry
Conference held at Lakeland Community College. Curt, Bill, John, Kay Anne, and
I will attend.
·   I need a motion to also send Curt and Bill and the Vocational School
Instructor (if possible) to the Tree Survival School in Perry Ohio.
·   Your packet contains job descriptions for all active employees except fire
department. Fire Departments are finished but not reviewed by the chief. As
soon as these have been reviewed and a couple unmanned part time position
descriptions are written, I will ask for Council’s approval on these as well.
·   I will be reviewing all personnel folders for completeness and conformance
to village and privacy requirements.

Service Dept.: 
·   The gas well pressures have improved to indicate we may have a very
productive well. To date five sections of distribution pipe (Made in China)
have split seams and had to be replaced. More information to be provided as it
becomes available.
·   The street crews have been very busy with the return of winter weather.
·   Water line was installed by the Village crew at the park. Sewer lines are
still planned.
·   The West Cedar water retention ditch access road was started to enable tile
installation as required by Council.
·   The New Schools rain water retention pond and pumps are not working to
prevent excess water flow to Elliot Ave., West Cedar and Hillyer. We will
continue to monitor this situation until it is resolved.
Fire Dept./Police Department
·   Nothing unusual to report
Recreation Department
·   Nothing unusual to report.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Main plant electrical upgrade is progressing nicely.
·   The new generator at Elm Street Pump station is being repaired under
warrantee. It would not supply the output needed to run both pumps at full
power.
·   I am working with Thousand Trails Campground to eliminate rain water
infiltration (as much as 100,000 in two days). The campground is closed and we
should be seeing no flow.
·   The new school sites also appear to have rain water infiltration into the
sewer system. I am working with Gavin Smith to make sure this infiltration is
resolved before the schools open.
·   During 2008 we have to start eliminating storm water infiltration into our
wastewater collection system as mandated by OEPA.
Other Items:
·   Five of us attended the “Building Effective Supervisors” seminar on Monday
Feb. 11 as approved by Council. This excellent seminar should help all of us
improve our supervision skills and work together as a well integrated team.
·   You received job descriptions for all active employees except fire
department. I am asking Council to approve them so I can begin distribution.
·   I will be reviewing all personnel folders for completeness and conformance
to village and privacy requirements.

·   The gas well so far has produced little gas and 160 barrels of oil.
·   The street crews continue with snow removal duties.
·   The West Cedar water retention ditch access road is about 20% complete and
work will continue as weather permits.
Fire Dept./Police Department
·   Fire Department year end report submitted to Council.
·   Police are continuing to run radar enforcement at select locations in the
Village. The latest patrol resulted in 25 citations
Recreation Department
·   Recreation Committee Report in packet
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Main plant electrical upgrade is progressing nicely.
·   The new generator at Elm Street Pump station is being repaired under
warrantee. It would not supply the output needed to run both pumps at full
power.
·   I am working with Thousand Trails Campground to eliminate rain water
infiltration (as much as 100,000 in two days). The campground is closed and we
should be seeing no flow.
·   The new school sites also appear to have rain water infiltration into the
sewer system. I am working with Gavin Smith to make sure this infiltration is
resolved before the schools open.
·   During 2008 we have to start eliminating storm water infiltration into our
wastewater collection system as mandated by OEPA.

Service Dept.: 
·   The Village Street Trees held up well under the weight from ice last week.
Portions of three streets were effected and about eight additional home
services.
·   At about noon Friday the power was restored at the main lines and secondary
repairs continued into Saturday.
·   The street department backhoe consumed over 220 gallons of diesel fuel in a
day and a half removing snow from the downtown area. Diesel fuel prices exceed
$4.00 a gallon at the moment.
·   We used no salt over the weekend until the snow stopped.
Fire Dept./Police Department
·   I made my first call to 911 to report the fire at Pizza Joe’s on Wednesday.
We cleared the buildings and moved the cars to make room for the fire trucks.
·   Emergency rescue and the police arrived to check for injuries and block
traffic. EMT’s assisted the fire department early on until more volunteers
arrived.
·   The fire happened and the response occurred with such speed and precession
that is seems surreal.
Recreation Department
·   The Community Center provided day shelter to several residents until other
accommodations were made.
·   We were in contact with the Red Cross and Sheriff’s Department and on
standby to accommodate people with overnight shelter but were not asked to
remain open.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Main plant electrical upgrade is progressing nicely.
·   I met with the Service Committee (See Committee Minutes).
·   The new generator at Elm Street Pump station is undersized and will not
supply the output needed to run both new pumps at full power.
·   Since our power outages seem to occur while we are at peak flow and we can
not discharge to the creek, we have to be able to pump at capacity.
·   We are able to run Elm Street Pump Station on the generator at the main
plant.
·   We will be taking actual current readings for all loads needed to run both
the Main Plant and Elm Street Pump Station and make a recommendation on how to
proceed with emergency power needs in the near future.
·   Contractor had to cut our new pavement in front of the galley to repair the
sewer lateral to the businesses in the strip plaza.
·   Final repair to pavement will be delayed until the asphalt plants open up.
Other Items:
·   Nothing significant to report
Following the Administrator’s Report, Administrator Finger reported that the
crack sealing on Jefferson Street did not hold, it was decided that it would be
advantageous to pave the street instead of resealing it.
Mr. Stanisa acquainted council of the services and charges of Lake Shore
Energy. Council was convinced that Lake Shore Energy was the supplier they
would use to supply natural gas to the Village municipal buildings.
Motion by Councilman Fertig to accept Lake Shore Energy as the supplier of
natural gas for Village municipal buildings at a variable monthly rate
2md
Roll: All yea, motion carried.

Star Ohio Report
Councilman Ward questioned why the recreation revenue report did not match up
to the expenditures for Senior Trip and Recreation Department trips.
Clerk-Treasurer Fisher told Council that sometimes the monies expended out are
for trips in the future and a purchase order is written for the expense. The
revenue will come in up to the event. The revenue is recorded in Recreation
Department through central cash.
Clerk-Treasurer Fisher told Council that a cost analysis would be nice to
receive from the Recreation Department to see if revenues verses expenditures
match. In the past we did receive cost analysis. Also when the money is
deposited at the Recreation Center, if it is not put under the right revenue
code, it will not show the correct revenue.
Administrator Finger told Council he would talk with the director regarding the
cost analysis sheets and making sure the revenues are put under the right
revenue code.

Service Dept.: 
·   We applied for $37,000.00 in disaster funds related to the cleanup costs
from the ice storm.
·   Quotes for concrete work at fire department, police department and
sidewalks have been received and work will commence as soon as weather
cooperates. Labor @$2.10 per square foot and concrete at $104.00 per cubic
yard.
·   Street paving bid documents are being prepared and we will bid as soon as
possible.
·   The MC 70 dust control quote is due any day for our unpaved streets
·   Construction to finish SRT 46 and SRT 307 Intersection and Mulberry will
start as soon as the weather permits.
·   The new backhoe is scheduled for delivery in mid April.
·   The waterline at Recreation Park is in the ground and scheduled for
connection to the main waterline by Aqua Ohio Water Company.
Fire Dept./Police Department
·   Our back up fire truck was struck on the right front corner while on route
to a fire. A driver tried to pass the truck on the right in spite of the
flashing lights and siren. The truck is drivable and scheduled for repair.
Recreation Department
·   The Community Center spring craft show is scheduled for this weekend,
Saturday, April 5th. All table space for vendors is sold out.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Gary Licate is back to work having recovered from pneumonia.
·   Main plant electrical upgrade is progressing nicely.
·   The Elm Street Pump Station is equipped with stand by power sufficient to
run both pumps at full speed.
·   The new generator at Elm Street Pump station that was undersized will be
used in another location.
·   We are taking actual current readings for all loads needed to run both the
Main Plant and Elm Street Pump Station and will have a plan in place soon for
one generator large enough to run the entire plant on stand by power.
·   Thousand trails pump station was without power for two days while repairs
were made to the utility power connection at the camp meter.
Other Items:
·   The citizen advisory group unanimously accepted the final Phase II report
from Cleveland State Consultants for the downtown business area. Final bound
copies will be provided to the Planning Commission and Council as soon as we
receive them.
·   Phase III of the project was included in the budget appropriation for 2008
and will begin as soon as Phase III requirements are refined to match the
citizens committee report.

Service Dept.: 
·   We received notification of eligibility of up to $ 57,000.00 in disaster
funds related to the cleanup costs from the ice storm.
·   Concrete work at fire department, police department and sidewalks will
begin next week.
·   Street paving bid documents are complete. The estimated cost ($ 190,000)
exceeds what we budgeted ($ 150,000.00). One street (East Cedar) will be
offered as an alternative.
·   Bid plans call for paving:
·   East Jefferson; Railroad to Chestnut
·   West Jefferson   ; Business District
·   West Ashtabula   ; Market to Chestnut.
·   East Cedar; Market to Spruce
·   The MC 70 dust control quote is past due for our unpaved streets
·   Construction to finish SRT 46 and SRT 307 Intersection and Mulberry will
start as soon as the weather permits.
·   The new backhoe was delivered and is in service.
·   The waterline at Recreation Park is tied into the main waterline
complements of Aqua Ohio Water Company.
Fire Dept./Police Department
·   Drug dogs are active.
Recreation Department
·   The Community Center spring craft show was considered a success by the
vendors. Attendance was somewhat lower than the Fall Show.
·   Skate board equipment will be inspected and put back in service beginning
this week.
·   Weight room members are very thankful for the new treadmill and think it is
the best model we have purchased.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Main plant electrical upgrade is progressing nicely.
·   We are taking actual current readings for all loads needed to run both the
Main Plant and Elm Street Pump Station and will have a plan in place soon for
one generator large enough to run the entire plant on stand by power.
·   We will be smoke testing the collection lines at Thousand Trails this week
to identify the sources of water infiltration so they can be repaired.
Other Items:
·   Leo Debevc, Civil Engineering Student from Case, will return to the summer

nominated for a 1-year term. It should have been a three year term, which would
make his term expire in 2009. Therefore, there should not have been a motion to
elect Gary Helfer to a 3-year term in 2007. The trustees’ terms would then be
staggered according to the rules:
·   Ken Fertig – December 31, 2008
·   Gary Helfer – December 31, 2009
·   Martha Demshar – December 31, 2010
Trustee Demshar asked if the information reflected what was in their minutes.
Mayor Maloney told everyone that per the Ohio Revised Code the terms are to be
staggered and are three year terms. Mayor Maloney also explained that she is
having the Village Solicitor look into it more thoroughly.

the Village. Through the Ohio Revised Code, the Municipality can take the lead

enforce the actions through the court system.

Street.

Lachey’s house will resume after brush pick up is completed.

week.

nicely in the restoration areas.

installed this year.

Recreation Department
·   Summer program attendance is much lower than anticipated.
·   Participants have pre-registered and then not showed for the activity.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Our OPWC Grant request to replace the 35 year old forced main from Elm St.
pump station to the main plant will be funded in December of this year.
·   Our other OPWC requests for paving Mulberry and replacing two culverts are
below the funding line for now. We will have final notice by July 2009.
·   Main plant electrical upgrade is progressing nicely without disruption of
treatment activities.
·   We have completed the load calculations for the backup power generator at
the main plant and were approved for funding at the local OPWC meeting. As soon
as final approval is received we can order the other generator.
Other Items:
·   Administration traded in the 1999 Ford Ranger for a 2005 Ford F150 four
passenger with four wheel drive at Tom David Motors.

blighted homes. The property owners have 30 days to comply.

three additional properties.
·   Several Junk cars have been removed several more remain to be cited into

Visitor’s Comments:
Pat Inman addressed Council regarding citizen concerns about not having
sidewalks completed along Mulberry Street in time for the Elementary School
opening. She also touched on concerns regarding the installation of a traffic
light at Chestnut and Mulberry, the problem with only one entrance to the new
complex, and having a police officer present at the beginning and ending of the
school day.
Mrs. Inman also stated that the school and the Village need to communicate to
the residents of the Village and be prepared to have suggestions to concerned
residents and parents. Mrs. Inman also suggested to Council to have a Community
Communication meeting before school starts to inform everyone.
Mayor Maloney said that sidewalk grant money will be available until 2010, and
the traffic light will be installed when the high school is complete, which
will increase traffic flow.
Mayor Maloney also told everyone that the Village Police will be on site at the
new school to help with all issues.
Jerry Westfall, Operations Manager of Presrite Corporation at 322 S. Cucumber
Street, addressed Council requesting a zoning change to accommodate the
expansion of the company.
Mr. Westfall’s major concern is the time it will take to do the rezoning.
Solicitor Lemire explained that the zoning code is going to have to be amended
for the commercial properly. The Planning Commission will set a meeting, if
approved by the Planning Commission. The recommendation then goes to Council.
If Council approves the Planning Commission’s recommendation, a Public Hearing
is set up for thirty days. After the Public Hearing, Council then brings forth
an Ordinance to approve the amendment to the zoning code. The Ordinance takes
three readings and after the third reading, it will not take effect until
thirty days after that. These are the steps that are put in place by the State.

Mulberry Street
 
Service Dept  
·   Street Paving for 2008 is on schedule for August and includes E. Cedar St.,
E. Jefferson St., The Business District of W. Jefferson St, and E. Ashtabula
Street.
·   Sidewalk repairs and concrete work are continuing on East Jefferson Street,
SR 307 West, then North Chestnut from Pine Street linking to the new sidewalk
at the intersection.
·   Mulberry Street right of way has been finish graded and seeded. Resident
complaints regarding standing water were addressed by taking the fabric out of
the storm grates as a result of weather reports showing a period of no rain in
the forecast.
·   The new grass already growing will minimize the risk of straw flowing into
the pipe.
·   Some final adjustments are planned after the ground is stabilized and the
grass is growing.
·   Repairs are planned to replace broken pavement on Mulberry Street before
school starts. These surface repairs will be completed without additional cost
to the village. As part of the repair process the Village will add additional
finger drains to assure water drains properly in these repaired areas of the
street.
·   Street Lighting bids for the intersection were opened Friday 7/18/08.
Clerk/Treasurer will need to report the results.
Fire Dept./Police Department
·   Nothing to report
Recreation Department
·   Department is working on a plan to keep revenue and expenses in line to
prevent an end of year shortfall.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Operations continue on a normal level.
·   Construction projects continue
·   Additional grant up dates will be available in the future.
Other Items:
·   I would request a motion from Council agreeing to close Popular Street
during Fair Week.
·   We have received replies from three of the four property owners who
received letters to repair or demolish blighted homes. Permits have been issued
for the Popular Street House. Attorneys are working on the two on E. Jefferson
Street. We have not received notification of delivery on the fourth house on S.
Elm Street.
·   I received a complaint from Chuck Cornell and the residents on Center
Street that Lantern Beverage Car Wash had added drier fans that were
excessively noisy. Mr. Dave Blashinski understood the complaint and
discontinued the fan blowers operation until he can get the proper permits and
provide sound suppression that enables him to meet our code.
·   Presrite Corporation at 322 S. Cucumber Street is expanding again. Jerry
Westfall, Operations Manager, will address Council asking for a zoning change
for the front yard requirement at 322 S. Chestnut Street. (Additional
information in Council packet and sent to the Planning Commission.)
·   An additional Zoning Change request received from James and Terri Toukonen
requests that their property on the corner of E. Jefferson and S. Sycamore
Street be rezoned from Industrial to Single Family Residential as currently
occupied. The properties to the East along E. Jefferson Street are currently
zoned Single Family Residential. This request also has been forwarded to
Planning Commission.
·   A recommendation letter from the building and lands committee concerning
the current elementary school playground has been completed and should be
reviewed by Council in executive session.
·   Pat Inman will address Council regarding citizen concerns for not having
sidewalks completed along Mulberry Street in time for the new Elementary School
opening.

Safety
– No Report
Arlene Rice of 120 Center Street came to Council with concerns about the
Lantern Beverage Car Wash and the noise that the new blowers to dry off the
cars are making. Mrs. Rice told Council that she presented a petition with
fifty-three residents with concerns of the noise.
Mayor Maloney told Council that the owner of Lantern Beverage was in and talked
with Administrator Finger for permits to build a structure to reduce the noise.
The owner of the Lantern Beverage has turned off the blowers until the issue
can be resolved.
Bob Lister of 18 E. Satin Street presented Council with pictures of the
sidewalk in front of his house and wants to know when they will get fixed. Mr.
Lister told Council that he has filled out paperwork and has been trying ever
since he has owned the house to get new sidewalks. He stated that his sidewalks
are dangerous and would like to get them fixed.
Solicitor Lemire told Council per the Ohio Revised Code that the owner is
responsible for the sidewalks in front of the house they own-no matter how
minor the damage is. The Village does have an ordinance in place to repair
sidewalks and it is the owners responsibility to pay for the cement.

Book Stores and Adult Motion picture Theaters and Nudity of the Codified
Ordinances of the Village of Jefferson to Reduce the Gross Income and Retail

Solicitor Lemire reported back to Council regarding discussion on height
regulations at the last Council meeting. According to 1248.01 Minimum and
Maximum Limits:
(a)   Thirty-five feet maximum RS and RD Districts
(b)   Two stories minimum and at least 26 feet and fifty feet maximum in the B-
1 and OTB district
(c)   Two and one-half stories maximum and not the exceeding 40 feet in the B-
2 District
(d)   Fifty feet maximum the LI and I districts.
Heights above the established limits may be approved by Council in cases
involving unoccupied structures.

Service Dept  
·   Survey and legal description is complete for the Elementary School
Playground. Jerry and I will follow up on the contract and lot split, and
recording of deed.
·   Mulberry Street Core samples from four sets of tests show the sub base to
be deficient.
·   Mulberry Street repair plans are being developed and the contractor states
he will fix the problems.
·   Village has retained Bricker and Eckler Law Firm to advise us as we work
out a final comprehensive repair plan for Mulberry Street.
·   Street Lighting for the SR46, SR307, and SR166 intersection project is
still waiting for additional quotes from electrical contractors. Cost of the
copper wires is excessively high. We budgeted $30,000 and wire quote alone is
$26,000
·   No action yet on roof repairs at Town Hall, Community Center, or Street
Department.

Police and Fire Department before the end of 2008.

·   Classes are well attended.

·   Nothing unusual to report.

·   Repairs are in progress at both the Popular Street and S. Elm Street
blighted Houses.
·   Demolition permit was issued for 295 East Jefferson Street blighted house.
·   There has been action to repair 315 E. Jefferson Street blighted house. Due
to misinformation that was supplied to get a zoning permit, a stop work order
was issued and the zoning permit was revoked.
·   Correspondence attached.
·   Lantern Beverage Car Wash has no activity.
·   Village has started to clean the storm water ditch that runs between W.
Satin and South Popular.

Service Dept  
·   Curt Stone and I reviewed all applications for the Street Department
utility /maintenance job at least three times. We narrowed to seven finalists
and interviewed four. Curt and I both agreed on two candidates. I ask Council
to accept Curt Stone’s recommendation to hire John Powers, pending physical
results, for the open Maintenance/Utility position. We will add John to the
payroll as soon as possible.
·   Contract for purchase of the Elementary School Playground with 1.88 Acres
was delivered to Superintendent Hladek and is awaiting Board of Education
action.
·   Mulberry Street repair planning meeting was held Monday, November 3 with
Tri Mor. Their repair proposal to fix the road follows:
·   Tri More expects the Village of Jefferson to pay full remaining contract
pricing for the work performed (about $130,000), even though the work does not
meet the contract specifications.
·   Tri Mor has recommended re-grinding the entire road to sixteen inches deep,
Mixing in 6% Portland Cement at an additional cost of $85,000.00 to fix this
failed sub base. They recommend repaving with 2” of intermediate asphalt
instead of the current specified 4 “ of asphalt for an additional cost of
$74,901.
·   The Village tax payers, according to Tri Mor’s repair plan, would be
responsible to pay: $130,000 + $85,000 + $74,901) or an additional $289,901
dollars. (We have already paid $560,871.00)
·   Jerry and I will be attending a Constructions Claims Seminar in Dublin,
Ohio on Monday, November 17, 2008. This seminar is sponsored by Bricker &
Eckler and several of the sessions are being taught by the Attorney we have
engaged for advice on Mulberry Street.
·   It is highly unlikely Jerry and I will be able to be back in Jefferson for
Council meeting.
·   I will be delivering the final three test results to Bricker and Eckler law
firm at this meeting which will enable them to finalize their recommendation to
the Village regarding the Mulberry Street project.
·   Street Lighting for the SR46, SR307, and SR167 intersection project is
scheduled to be completed this year, 2008.
·   35 new trees have been planted in various tree lawn areas of the Village.
·   Curt has received four bids to replace the flat roof on the streets
building and put metal siding on the outside of the building. Low bid
($48,000.00) is only $2,000.00 more than the bid to repair the flat roof. We
recommend going forward with the pitched roof replacement.
Fire Dept./Police Department
·   Nothing new to report.
Recreation Department
·   Nothing new to report
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Nothing unusual to report.
Other Items:
·   On Thursday 11/14/08 Jerry represented the Village before Judge Mackey. The
295 E. Jefferson Street House will be demolished by December 17, 2008.
·   The 315 E. Jefferson Street House discussion will be taken to mediation
before going to trial.
·   Lantern Beverage Car Wash has no activity.
·   Two new welcome to Jefferson signs were installed on State Route #46 North
and South. These have been in the works for about seven years and were timed
for installation upon completion of the intersection improvements.
Clerk-Treasurer told Council that the Village received the Real Estate
agreement from the Board of Education.

Service Dept  
·   In an effort to offset some of the increased cost of salt (from $34 to $68
a ton) we are mixing sand ($16/ton) with the salt. This will reduce cost and
put traction medium and thaw medium on the streets.
·   John Powers passed all requirements to be hired for the Village and started
work on 11/19/2008.
·   Final paperwork for the Elementary School Playground deed with 1.88 Acres
is being prepared and will be filed ASAP.
·   Jerry and I attended a Constructions Claims Seminar in Dublin, Ohio on
Monday, November 17, 2008. This seminar sponsored by Bricker & Eckler proved to
be very beneficial. Jerry and I are much more confidant in the Village position
and can be more pro active in getting an acceptable solution.
·   Bricker & Eckler has reviewed all documentation and in their opinion “ the
Village is in a very strong position ”. A written summary and recommendation
will be delivered around Thanksgiving.
·   With the Village position being that the proposed repair to Mulberry Street
from Tri Mor is “Totally Ridiculous”; I have asked Urban Engineers from Erie
PA. to give us a counter proposal for the repair plan on Mulberry Street.
Fire Dept./Police Department
·   Nothing new to report.
Recreation Department
·   Nothing new to report
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Nothing unusual to report.
Other Items:
·   Christmas decorations are being installed up town. These include new
lighted wreaths, snow flakes and a train.
·   Lantern Beverage Car Wash has no activity.
·   The new sign on the south end of town will be relocated to allow increased
visibility to the North.

Ordinance No. 08-0-2763
An Ordinance Amending Subsection 1240.07 Definitions, subsection (5) Adult Book
Store & subsection (6) Adult Motion Picture Theater; and section 1246.13 Adult
Book Stores and Adult Motion picture Theaters and Nudity of the Codified
Ordinances of the Village of Jefferson to Reduce the Gross Income and Retail
Percentage in the Definition of Adult Book Store, to Add Regulations of Adult
Only Entertainment Establishments, and to Increase the Set Back Requirements
for Such Establishments from RD and RD Residential Districts to 1000 feet.
Solicitor Lemire told Council that the new ordinance explains what areas and
subsections allow adult book stores

Treasurer to Execute a Quit Claim Deed Conveying Property from the Village of
Jefferson to the Jefferson United Methodist Church for the Purpose of
Fulfilling the Obligation of the village to Utilize Lot 65 in the Gideon
Granger Town Plat of Jefferson for Ministry Purposes

Methodist church is okay as it is written and is consistent with how the
Village has done church parcels in the past

OFFICIALS
Mayor
State of the Village 2009:
On January 7, 2008, I took the oath of office as the officially elected mayor
of the Village of Jefferson. Seventeen months earlier I had been appointed
Mayor by Council following Mayor Bragga’s retirement. Just as I had hoped, 2008
has been a wonderful and challenging year for the Village of Jefferson with
much activity and many major accomplishments
The Police Department acquired 2 K-9 officers to help with drug enforcement.
The K-9 officers have been utilized at the Jefferson Area Local schools and
surrounding area; and have aided officers in drug searches at traffic stops.
New auxiliary officers and a part time officer have been hired to aid in
traffic control, special events and to fill in for vacations.
The Fire Department’s new fire truck is an asset to the village. It has been
used frequently in ’’Jefferson’ and the surrounding areas as mutual aid. The
Fire department is continuing with the cadet program and finds the program very
successful
Both departments participated in a safety forces day along with Jefferson
Rescue. All the buildings were open for the public and the personnel were
available for demonstrations and questions. All three departments pronounced
the event successful and plan to make this an annual event.
The JeffersonCommunity Center, along with the Senior Center, has continued to
offer new programs and events for participants. The “long night of games” for
children has been very successful. Halloween, Christmas, and Easter events have
also been well attended. The Christmas craft show was the largest so far with
85 crafters and 1200-1300 shoppers.
The Senior Center continues to offer lunch, exercise, an assortment of programs
beneficial and entertaining, as well as a variety of trips to locations far
(but not too far) and near geared to provide our senior population a more
social, active and healthier life style.
Village Park has been equipped with electricity and village drinking water to
make sporting events, family picnics and parties more enjoyable. The gas well
generates $12,000 per year in revenue toward the community center bond payment
and, as a bonus, supplies all the natural gas we can use in the park.
The new elementary school opened this past fall and the old building was
vacated. The village worked with the school board to purchase the play ground
area to keep it in the village for use by the children. This is a treasure and
an asset for the community. The skate park will be relocated to the playground
area, and a ball field will be made available for use by village residents and
friends.
With the sale of the rest of the property at that site the village will see the
return of 14-15 feet of village green, with the plan to add picnic tables and
park benches.
2008 Infrastructure projects were completed totaling $2,565,105 dollars funded
with grants and 0% loans. These projects included:
Cedar St. after 30+ years of discussion; Route 46 North Intersection Safety
improvements (which averaged 13 accidents per year);
Mulberry Street paving (pavement failure is being protested), Sewer plant
electrical upgrades, and others. In addition to these outside funded projects
the village funded $280,000 dollars in street repair, side walk repair, and
tree removal and planting.
We formed a water advisory board with the Aqua Ohio Water Company and have been
systematically replacing water lines to reduce breakages and to generally
improve water quality and flow. The next major improvement will be a second
water tower to stabilize water flow and pressure during times of high usage.
Jefferson Village now has the lowest water rates in the County. We are
continually working to reduce costs to our residents as opportunities present
themselves. The most recent being Natural Gas Aggregation to bring village
residents gas prices in the $8.00 to $9.00 per mcf range rather than the
current $10.00 to $12.00 per mcf.
The administrator and department heads’ weekly meetings have been highly
successful in pulling all the departments closer together and allowing them to
participate in budgeting, planning, and prioritizing.
Looking ahead, infrastructure projects are planned for 2009 and beyond totaling
$6,072,261.00 dollars in 100% grants from the economic stimulus package. These
include improvements to the business district to remove overhead wires, improve
sidewalk and lighting conditions, truck bypass, sewer extensions, culvert
repairs, paving and retaining walls.
The village is partnered with the chamber of Commerce to purchase lighted and
animated Christmas decorations at a 50% sale price during February and March.
With the completion of the intersection at 46, 307, and 167 we will be adding
new street lighting that will also have the lighted wreaths and snowflakes next
year.
On behalf of Council and the Village, I would also like to thank the employees
of the village for working together to make this village a safe and beautiful
place to live, work and raise a family.
In conclusion, I would like to thank council for their phenomenal support,
cooperation, communication, and willingness to pitch in on projects when there
is a need.

Service Dept  
·   Streets Department is Working Saturday and Sunday mornings to move snow in
anticipation of the next storm.
·   Sidewalk plowing is slower than usual due to the need to switch to the snow
blower.
·   Mulberry Street project has had no additional action.
·   Design work is nearing completion on Spruce Street/E. Jefferson St.
intersection sight distance and stream/culvert headwalls.
·   Jefferson Village Park has been chosen to receive the first Rain Garden in
Ashtabula County. A grant was awarded to install a rain water filtering bed
next to the parking lot at the park. The filtering bed will be planted with
flowering plants and catch the water coming off the pavement. The filtering bed
prevents oil, gas, antifreeze and such from getting into mill creek.
Fire Dept./Police Department
·   Fire Department has received their Pick Up Truck
·   Marcs radios remain on order.
·   Police cruisers have been ordered.
Recreation Department
·   The trip to Washington DC for inauguration was completed with no incidents.
Temperatures hovered around 12 degrees F.
·   Lisa and her group found an inside venue that allowed them to step outside
and experience the crowd or stay inside the warm auditorium to sit and watch
the inauguration on several large projection screens.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Nothing unusual to report.
Other Items:
·   Lantern Beverage Car Wash has removed the blowers from the outside of the
building.
·   Love insurance received quotes on the Village liability insurance from Two
Insurance Companies and one Governmental Pool. A fourth Company declined to
quote saying they could not be competitive.
·   Our current insurance carrier Fireman’s fund (Houston Common Carriers) will
be renewed.
2009 premium will be $1,000 less than 2008’s even with increases in coverage
limits
Councilman Damon commented that on Wednesday, January 28th it was hard to
travel because of the snow on the roads. Administrator Finger responded by
saying that anyone can call him if there is a problem of snow removal within
the Village.

Visitor’s Comments (five minute limit per council rule # 13)
Eleanor Pengle of 128 Center Street questioned the sewer increase stating that
there was a large rates increase last year. Administrator Finger explained that
the Village of Jefferson’s rates are lower or comparable to other
municipalities in the area. Jefferson’s monthly minimum charge is only $7.26,
which is the lowest in the area: Orwell- $70.00; Geneva-$10.02; Conneaut-
$15.02; Middlefield-$35.00; Kingsville-$18.00. The low monthly minimum charge
helps senior citizens in our area. The Capital Improvements that are done at
the Wastewater Treatment Plant are mandated by EPA.
 Frank Snyder or 116 West Jefferson Street expressed his opposition to the
proposed changes to Section 1246.07 of the codified ordinances of the Village
of Jefferson to the proposed wind turbine addition to the zoning ordinance.
Mr. Snyder also commended Council for being fiscally responsible in regard to
the sewer increase.

Service Dept  
·   The wind storm took down several street trees that have been cleaned up. A
street light blew over on North Chestnut Street taking out electric service to
seven customers and blocking traffic until 8:00 AM. The Village employees
(Fire, Police, and Street Dept.) cleared the hazard and restored traffic flow.
·   A civil lawsuit has been filed against Tri Mor Corporation concerning the
Mulberry Street project.
·   Tri Mor has in turn filed a civil suit against the Villageof Jefferson.
Fire Dept. /Police Department
·   Nothing unusual to report.
Recreation Department
·   Enrollment in programs remains higher than 2008.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Plant operation remains normal.
·   I have recommended to the Service Committee that we implement the 3.5% rate
increase as planned in the 2007 rate study.
Other Items:
·   Our current liability insurance carrier Fireman’s fund (Houston Common
Carriers) was renewed for greater coverage at a lower premium.
·   I have recommended a 2% wage increase for village employees to show
appreciation for their cost saving ideas and safe work habits.
o   $62,000.00 reduction in workers compensation premium based on our safe work
record and training efforts.
o   $30,000.00 savings per year by village employees finishing the sidewalk
concrete.
o   Over $50,000.00 savings by village employees renting equipment and
performing excavation work normally contracted out. (W. Cedar drain pipes,
Spruce Street elevation change, Elementary school playground reclamation,
Village park improvements, N. Sycamore future truck route, and Spruce Street
Culvert replacement).
o   $35,000.00 savings by village employees drilling and setting street light
poles at State Route #46 N. and State Route #307 west.
o   $15,000.00 savings by using Jobs and Family Service clients and residents
who need to do community service.
$10,000.00 per year savings by wastewater employees and street dept employees
using village camera equipment and cleaning equipment

Service Dept  
·   Village wide curb side clean up is scheduled for Saturday, May 9th. As
usual all material must be in place for pick up by Friday Night. If residents
need Village crews to assist they should call 576 – 3941. I will evaluate all
requests.  
·   I will be doing a windshield inspection and inviting select locations to
participate in the clean up. Failure to voluntarily participate will lead to
citations.
·   Tree trimming is underway by the Street Department to remove lower branches
up to the required 13 foot clearance as required in Local Code #1026.06 -- - -
- - - - ,Trimming Required - - - - -.
·   Brobst Tree Service has finished tree removal and stump removal for the
time being. There will be more scheduled as is practical.
·   A motion was filed in court to combine the two civil lawsuits filed
regarding Mulberry Street into one case with Jefferson Village as the
plaintiff.
Fire Dept. /Police Department
·   Electrical upgrades and generator hook up are in progress.
Recreation Department
·   Enrollment in programs remains higher than 2008.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Plant operation remains normal.
·   Generator Instillation to finish the main plant upgrade will be scheduled
as weather permits.
Other Items:
·   Cleveland State met with the group of residents working on establishing a
local downtown historic district.
·   Julie Lindner was retained by Cleveland State to write Zoning Code that
meets the group’s objectives and the State of Ohio requirements for becoming a
certified local government.
·   All the text will be submitted to the Planning Commission and follow the
normal route to becoming code.
·   Planning Commission will hold public meetings to agree, modify, or reject
the text. New text would be presented to council who will schedule another
public meeting and finally pass, modify, or reject the new code.
·   If new code is accepted that also meets the State of Ohio’s requirements
and the Village of Jefferson becomes a certified local government, we can seek
grants to further develop the downtown area.
Administrator Finger said that May 9th is clean-up day, and mentioned that
Waste Management won’t pick up hazardous materials.

Frank Snyder of 116 West Jefferson Street said that he supported the wind
turbine if the proper zoning is followed. There were questions regarding set
back distance. Most people oppose Fall Zone Height Section Z
Administrator Finger said any structure over 35 feet must have a Council
approval.
John Kish of 222 Elliott Avenue has a health concern. The 24/7 noise can cause
sleep problems, headaches, etc.
Diane Kish of 131 Woodside is concerned with the 24/7 noise.
Doug Holadek introduced Mike Spacek of Engineer Processing of Hudson, Ohio, who
is the school district’s consultant.
Mike Spacek said setback in rural area is a couple of acres. Different turbines
make different amounts of noise. Turbine noise is minimal when blades stay
below 80 RPMS. The proposed site is south of the new building – between the
Elementary and High School. The purposed turbine would generate 500 kilowatts
per year. It would pay for itself in 15 years, max. Maintenance and service is
essential to the proper operation of all such equipment.

Visitor’s Comments (five minute limit per council rule # 13)
Larry Meckly of South Spruce Street is concerned with the west side South
Spruce Street; the catch basin is higher then the ground. Administrator Finger
said they will be paving from the intersection of Jefferson Street south 150
feet, which should alleviate the problem.
Mr. Meckley asked who determines when the siren is turned on? Answer: Duty
officer, it is a take cover siren used if a tornado is in sight.
When Jim Donathon of Susan Drive addressed Council, he urged members to study
the wind turbine issue more thoroughly before taking steps to modify the zoning
code. He assured Council that he has nothing against wind turbines or wind
energy per se. But he is concerned that too many turbines could become an
“eyesore”; that the potential for fire should be addressed, as well as what
would happen if a turbine was no longer used. He suggested Council visit
turbine sites and research more before passing the ordinance, and his final
concern was that amending the zoning code was practically the same as ‘spot
zoning’.
Administrator Finger said the village does not spot zone property in town. The
proposed change simply lists wind turbines and wind mills as an accepted use
within an already established zoning classification. Each proposed wind turbine
will need to have its plans reviewed by his office before construction can
proceed.

Councilman Hoyson explained the Resource Officer Grant which would place a
police officer at the local schools. The Grant has been applied for and the
parties would have to reach an agreement before it would be implemented. When
school is not in session the officer would be used by the Village A policy and
job description would have to be drafted and approved. .The position would be
paid 100% through the grant for the first three years of the program. The
Village and School would fund the fourth year.
At the Ashtabula County Safety Council Annual Awards Banquet on Thursday, April
9, 2009, the Village of Jefferson received an award for “Outstanding Safety
Performance”
Councilman Thompson extended congratulations to the Village employees for the
“Outstanding Safety Performance” award acknowledging their excellent safety
record!
As a matter of safety, the Village will have a Siren Test on April 22, 2009 at
10:30 a.m.
Councilman Thompson alerted the Council and community of a very authentic
looking scam letter that is being circulated via the USPS. He received a letter
from a seemingly reputable organization that said he had won a cash prize. In
order to claim the money, however, he was required to send a smaller amount
from his own bank account to the sender. Initially receptive to the offer, he
thought better of it and took the letter to Police Chief Steve Febel. Chief
Febel said the letter had all the earmarks of a professionally-run scam. The
letter originated from one address, while the money was to be sent to a second
address in Canada. The message Chief Febel and Councilman Thompson want to
convey is “Don’t be scammed…if it seems too good to be true—it probably is!

Service Dept  
·   Village crew continues to prep and clean up the school playground area and
Park.
·   The rain garden site was completed as scheduled on April 23rd.
·   Brush pick up resumed on April 6th and will continue the first Monday of
each month.
·   Jefferson Village employees are continuing with street sweeping and should
have all streets completed by the mid May.
·   We are continuing cold patching the sidewalks to remove high or low spots
until the sidewalks can be replaced.
·   Spruce Street headwall construction project bid was below the engineers
estimate of $34,000.00.
·   I need a motion to accept the low bid of $26,484.00 from Phil Miller
Construction for the Spruce Street culvert headwall et al.
Fire Dept. /Police Department
·   Police Department has received two new white police cruisers. These will be
in service as soon as the equipment set up and decals are complete.
·   Two other cars will be retired from police service.
Recreation Department
·   Summer free lunch program will begin after the school year is completed.
·   T ball has about 75 kids signed up.
·   Summer Day Care class is expected to be full with a waiting list.
·   The first ever Recreation Department presentation to the United Way Funding
Committee without support from the Clerk/Treasurer or Administrative office was
successfully completed.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Forced main replacement drawings have been submitted to OEPA for approval.
Once approved the job can be advertised for bid.
·   There was a fuse that blew on the first energy utility pole at the
wastewater treatment plant with enough noise that the fire Department and
Police Department were called. No damage to the plant or responsibility of the
plant occurred. First Energy will have to replace an underground line between
the pole and main transformer.
·   Village was awarded a stimulus package grant that would have required us to
borrow 50% of the project cost. I recommend that we decline this award due to
the need to add another payment to the already stretched wastewater capitol
fund.
Other Items:
·   I will be attending the wind power expo in Chicago on May 6th and 7th as
approved by Council .
·   I received a 60 page reply from Brickler and Eckler to a request for
information from Tri Mor’s attorney. As soon as Jerry and I have digested its
content we will inform Council as needed.

Downtown
 
Service Dept  
·   Village crews are setting the Street Light Poles at the intersection of SRT
#46 and 307 North. Harmon Electric is doing the electrical work.
·   Village clean up day was completed with no problems.
·   Brush pick up will continue the first Monday of each month.
·   Jefferson Village employees will commence work on Spruce Street
improvements as soon as they finish the street lights.
·   Phil Miller Construction is set to begin work on the Spruce Street headwall
construction project as soon as school is out.
·   Village employees are setting new trees in the Village Park on E. Jefferson
St.
Fire Dept. /Police Department
·   Police Department has received the third of three new white police
cruisers. These will be in service as soon as the equipment set up and decals
are complete.
·   Three other cars will be retired from police service.
Recreation Department
·   There are more people reserving Village Park this year for private parties
than ever in the past (A good thing).
·   Summer free lunch program will begin after the school year is completed.
·   T ball is in progress with about 75 kids signed up.
·   Summer Day Care class has seven students signed up to start when school
ends.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   First Energy and the Village are scheduled to begin the replacement of the
high Voltage lines that were found to be defective.
·   The utility pole to the north of the bridge will be eliminated and two new
poles will be set south of the entrance road and bridge. The plant will end up
with completely new service lines to the main transformer that will be encased
in conduit.
·   The only cost to the Village will be to have T&K Engineering document the
changes and up date the plant drawings.
·   Because the plant has so many underground pipes and lines the excavation
needs to avoid collateral damage so will be slow and precise.
·   Forced main replacement drawings have been submitted to OEPA for approval.
Once approved the job can be advertised for bid.
·   Instillation of the large backup generator as the final part of main plant
improvement project is scheduled to begin May 18th. This same contractor will
install the back up power generator at Village Hall during this same time
period.
Other Items:
·   I will have a trip report regarding the wind power expo in Chicago for
Council meeting Monday May 18th.
·   I need an executive session to discuss details of our action against Tri
Mor regarding Mulberry Street.

Mulberry Street, Clerk Treasurer Fisher pointed out that Phase II work was not
in the 2009 budget but was anticipated for 2010 budget. Since in either case we
expected to have to borrow the Village’s $70,000.00 share. We filled out a
second application for the 0% loan money.
·   I was advised that if we expected to get both the $150,000 and $70,000 as a
0% loan in 2009 we had to file one application for $220,000.00.
·   Council needs to be aware of this change and grant approval for the
additional amount.

Downtown
 
Service Dept  
·   Three street lights at the intersection of St Rt 46 and 307 will have the
reflectors modified to shield residents from bright light.
·   A cracked light pole next to the recreation center was replaced.
·   Brush pick up will continue the first Monday of each month.
·   Jefferson Village employees are replacing sidewalks as planned.
·   Spruce Street headwall construction, relocation of the stream bed, and the
deflection stone placement are complete. Work continues on the road elevation
change.
·   The Village playground ball field grass is growing nicely.
Fire Dept. /Police Department
·   Letter from Sherriff Johnson canceling the Village contract for dispatch
service is attached. Villages are seeking alternative solutions to dispatch
service to avoid paying the Sheriff’s proposed increase.
·   All Village taxpayers are paying property taxes to the County general fund
already.
·   Chief Febel had his return to work physical and was released for work
effective 8/3/09.
Recreation Department
·   Jefferson Boosters owners of Memorial Field called to see if the Village
was interested in taking ownership. I advised them that the village certainly
was open to starting the discussion.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Work on the main power lines being replaced at the Wastewater Plant Is
complete.
·   Forced main replacement drawings have been approved by OEPA. We are
currently seeking a second grant to fund the Village’s portion of this cost.
·   Installation of the large backup generator as the final part of main plant
improvement project is complete. The operational tests are scheduled for August
12th, 2009.
·   Once the generator is on line we will operate the plant on the generator
frequently to assure switch over procedures are well documented, employees are
comfortable with its’ operation, and to wear in the equipment.
Other Items:
·   Our application for a 0% loan submitted to the local OPWC coordinators is
the number three ranked project. Final approval meeting is scheduled for August
11, 2009 at the Geauga County Engineer’s Office.
·   Tri Mor settlement letter is supposed to be in the mail. The final wording
was exactly the same as the draft wording shared with Council in executive
session.
·   We will issue a press release as soon as documents are signed by both
parties and we are allowed by Legal Council.

JOINT UNION CEMETERY MEETING

Mayor Judy Maloney called the meeting to order.
Resolution No.09-R-2775 was sent to the Board of Elections with language to be
placed on the ballot in November which met all of their criteria. The auditor
is requiring a resolution asking him to certify resolution No. 09-R-2775.
This requirement has been policy for many years, but previous auditors never
enforced it. The present auditor is doing everything by the book, thus we will
continue to follow this procedure!
It was determined that this meeting was called with the intention of approving
a resolution asking the auditor to certify Resolution No. 09-R-2775 to the
Board of Election which will put a .75 mill renewal levy on the ballot.

It’s a village with warm loving people who care,
When someone is hurting their burdens we share.
We reach out our hand with a warm loving touch
To show those in sorrow we love them so much.
It’s a village with people when happy they smile,
Their joy and their victory will last for a while.
So don’t be discouraged and feel down or sad,
There’s a friend waiting near you to make your heart glad.
It’s a village with leaders having morals and faith,
And friendly policemen to keep our town safe
We trust our town council right decisions to make,
They try to do good things for every ones sake.
It’s a village with veterans who kept our land free,
They preserved our freedom and our liberty
We say to each veteran we love you and care
May your life be all happy no heartaches to bear.
It’s a village all white when it’s covered with snow,
The roads may be blocked and there’s no place to go,
So we sit by our window and breathe out a sigh,
And watch as a snowflake floats gently by.
It’s a village with doctors and nurses we trust,
To have their kind healing is really a must.
Their warm friendly manners erases our fear
And gives us the courage to cope with each tear.
It’s a village with teachers who cause kids to learn,
They show love and caring though sometimes are stern.
Because of their guidance through calm and through strife
Our graduates are ready for success out in life.
It’s a village with churches our God to be true,
With Pastors who love us in all that we do.
With Sunday school teachers our children do love,
Who point them to Jesus and God up above.
It’s a village we care for in health or in pain.
We’re happy we live here in sunshine or rain
Someday we will leave here and tell friends goodbye
And join those we love in God’s village on high.
Lloyd Behr

Service Dept
"   Mulberry repair is four days ahead of schedule. Base repair was completed
today 9/04/2009.
"   Mulberry Street will always be open to emergency traffic, and Mulberry
Street residents. All truck and school transportation traffic must be routed to
the Popular Street entrance until final paving is complete.
"   Paving can start September 14th ahead of schedule.
"   Sidewalk construction on Mulberry Street will begin after the paving is
completed.
"   Jefferson Village employees are replacing sidewalks as planned.
"   Work on Spruce Street road elevation change is progressing on schedule.
Fire Dept. /Police Department
"   Aqua Ohio Water Company will begin construction on the new water storage
tank this fall with the intent to have it operational by fall of 2010. This
tank will provide an additional 500,000 gallons of reserve water in the village
to enhance fire fighting and to preserve water pressure.
"   Two surplus police patrol cars were sold one for $1,000.00 and the other
for $811.00.
"   Police department has increased patrol coverage in response to citizen
complaints.
"   Criminal citations have increased in response to citizen complaints.

Forestry
Administrator Finger and Mayor Maloney attended the September Jefferson Garden
Club meeting. Administrator Finger told the Garden Club that tree planting is
pretty much on schedule, although there is always work to be done. The Garden
Club has always been generous, but in light of the economic climate, it would
not be a hardship for the Village if the Garden Club is unable to donate to the
project next year.
The Garden Club plans to continue to beautify and maintain projects in the
Village, were possible; but will be unable to make their customary $2,000
donation for trees, at this time.

Safety
FYI: Mutual aid between Jefferson Fire Department and the Jefferson Rescue
District is now on file in the Clerk-Treasurer's office.
Fire Chief Wayman commented that the ambulance and fire department started out
together in the 70's and now we are back working together. The new Jefferson
Emergency Rescue Department administrator and board have made this possible.
The previous administrator would have never agreed to this. Chief Wayman said
his department is looking forward to working together with the Rescue District.
The Rescue District will be provided with turnout gear. If there is no medical
situation at a fire, the paramedics will help fight the fire. There are at
least 18 certified firefighters at the Rescue District, and they are all
willing to work with Jefferson Fire Department.

Councilman Thompson asked about the status of 911.

calls are recorded so they can be tracked to insure that the Sheriff's
Department follows through.

a savings to the Village of Jefferson
Councilman Hoyson commented that the transfer of dispatch to Middlefield was

benefit financially by this agreement, as well.

before the actual paving is complete.. Weather permitting; paving is scheduled
for October 12th.

Utilities/Wastewater Treatment/Service
Update on the Wastewater generator: The original generator was too small to run
the plant at full capacity, so to correct the situation, a larger generator was
purchased to accommodate the wastewater plants' need. The smaller generator was
installed at the Town Hall.
Clerk-treasurer Fisher told Council that because of the closing of several
plants recently, revenue is down approximately $62,000. Because the larger
generator was more expensive, a $46,473.00 loan was necessary.
On another matter, Councilman Fertig took issue with the Village employees
providing the labor for a private residence.

the Mayor.

Wastewater Treatment Plant:
"   Everything is operating normally.
"   Elm Street Forced main replacement remains on hold as we seek a grant from
CDBG for the Village matching portion.
"   Monday November 2nd the plant switched to the Generator produced
electricity and did not use First Energy supplied power as a test.
"   Initial estimates indicated if we could run eight days (4 gallons per hour)
on a tank of Diesel Fuel we could save about $48,000 per year in electric cost.
* Electric cost/year = $96,000 - $48,000 fuel = $48,000 savings.
"   Actual test results show we can run the plant at full operation for only 60
hours on a tank of fuel.
"   With a 600 gallon fuel tank, consumption was 10 gallons of fuel per hour.
Our break even point on fuel cost vs line power cost needed to be 8 gallons per
hour.
"   Our testing showed the capability of the back up generator to produce what
is needed and showed us that the fuel gauge drops at an increasingly faster
rate as fuel is consumed.
"   The Generator will perform as planned and Line supplied electricity is
still the most cost effective (yet costly) option.
Other Items:
"   Demo of 315 E Jefferson Street is complete.
"   Demo and grass seeding is complete at the old elementary school.
"   Village is having the Village Green area formerly occupied by the north end
of the School surveyed to reclaim the area of encroachment.
"   Mr. Mel Brown, Risk Control Field Representative performed a risk
assessment of the Village departments on Tuesday the 10th for Alliance™, the
municipal insurance alliance that underwrites the Village liability insurance.
"   We should receive a very favorable report!
The Administration, Employees and Elected Officials should be proud of the
repeated glowing reports we continue to receive from OSHA, Workers
Compensation, EPA and now our Liability Insurance Carrier. They all comment on
our orderliness, attention to details, compliance with the law, compliance to
standard practices and written procedures. We are always verbally one of the
best they have inspected.
They always find something that can be improved!
Thank you for your commitments and support in constantly seeking improvements.

OFFICIALS   
MAYOR  
State of the Village of Jefferson 2009
If you look at the Village through the eyes of a visitor, it’s obvious that we
have much to be proud of.
Some of the major accomplishments handled during 2009:
·   Completed the installation of 26 decorative street lights at the improved
intersection of STR #46 N and STR #307.
·   Completed all funded paving, sidewalk repair, tree maintenance and
planting, correspondence, reports, contract administration, utility rate
reductions for residents, contract negotiations, budgeting, and other
Administrator’s duties.
·   Continued safety awareness by having Mel Brown; Risk Control Manager for
The Alliance, our Municipal Insurance Carrier, inspect all Village Departments
and Village Facilities.
·   Renegotiated our Work Uniform cleaning contract saving $12,000.00 per year.
·   Continued to use Village Employees allowing us to save $30,000 by doing
sidewalk repairs and over $16,000.00 on the Spruce Street Project.
·   Continued Purchases of lighted Christmas decorations at 50% off retail
price.
·   Installed a cut sand stone sign at Jefferson Village Park on E. Jefferson
Street.
·   Assisted in installing the first Rain Garden in Ashtabula County. Joint
project with the Soil and conservation District and Ashtabula Joint vocational
horticulture Class.
·   Lisa and a group of Jefferson students attended the inauguration of the
newly elected president in Washington D. C.
·   Completed the revised Main Plant (W. W.) Rehabilitation for a total project
cost of $ 452,800
·   Completed 100% of Mulberry Street paving with sidewalks to everyone
satisfaction.
·   Completed 85% of Spruce Street grade change project with the final paving
held off until spring of 2010.
·   Installed new welcome to Jefferson signs at two main entrances to the
Village.
·   Reactivated the Safe Routes to Schools $6,000 grant. This grant will fund
the larger proposal and study needed to identify and secure a 100% Construction
grant.
·   Worked with the New High School Contractor to modify the storm drains to
prevent flooding in Elliott Allotment during heavy rains.
·   Jefferson Village employees are sweeping the streets with the Geneva- on-
the-Lake street sweeper which was stored indoors at wastewater as per our in-
kind agreement. Savings of $4,500.00/year
·   295 and 315 E. Jefferson Street distressed homes were demolished by the
property owner
·   Electrical upgrades and generator hook were completed at the police and
fire station.
·   New generator installed at Village Hall
·   First Energy, at the Village’s request, replaced the entire High voltage
electric service to the wastewater plant.
A lot of pride and effort goes into the planning and maintenance of our
Village. With all we’ve accomplished over the past year, the Village is in
stable financial standing.
The Community Center continues to offer a variety of programs and activities
for all age groups. The pre-school program is operating at maximum. The summer
lunch program which started last summer had between 70-80 participants daily.
The exercise rooms and exercise classers keep the staff busy handling
enrollment and all the paperwork involved with keeping things running smoothly.
Our senior program –from the daily bingo game and lunches – to the trips and
excursions continue to serve our seniors well.
The annual Halloween Boo in the Park and party, as well as the annual Christmas
Craft Show continues to grow in popularity.
The three new police cruisers we purchased to replace older cruisers represent
some of the changes, improvements and accomplishments we’ve make over the past
year.
When the Sheriff’s Department notified us that due to the economy there would
be a substantial increase in our dispatching fees, we found it necessary to
seek services elsewhere. Through much negotiation we contracted with Middletown
for our dispatching needs. The Police Department has expressed that the
transition has gone smoothly and satisfactorily.
As for the Fire Department, an agreement has been signed with the Jefferson
Rescue for mutual aid. The Department continues with their cadet program, and
training is on going. The department is always looking for new members and will
interview anyone interested in joining the team.
The playground purchased from the Board of Education when the elementary school
moved to its new site, will continue to be enjoyed by our young people for
many, many years, and allowed us to retain a valuable and historic asset.
Under the supervising eye of the Rotary Club, the Masonry Department at the Vo-
Ed and the expertise of Herb Housel and his crew, the playground will have a
new restroom facility ready for summer vacation. The project was funded by the
Support Our Community Center through an endowment from the estate of Kay
Roberts.
In another joint effort, the Village of Jefferson and the Jefferson Chamber of
Commerce partnered during the holiday season by sharing the cost of Christmas
decorations and flags for the street light poles.
The Village and the entire community are appreciative and grateful to these
organizations for the help, support and pride they contribute in making and
keeping Jefferson a warm and welcoming place to live and work.
