fee, and lunch. I will drive the Village truck to avoid having to pay mileage
for the use of my personal vehicle. I would ask for a motion of approval.
·   Our three year Contract with Waste Management expires on April 31, 2010.
The contract has a provision for two one year extensions. After initial
discussions with Waste Management regarding these extensions, I have determined
that it is in the best interests of our residents to re-bid this contract.
·   Rather than having an increase for refuse collections I would expect to see
about a $10,000/year reduction to our residents. (Included in your packet is
the request for bid to be published.)

the bid process is complete.
·   I received notification today that NOPEC will have $50,000 grant available
to each of its member communities. Grants money awarded to Villages will be
distributed directly to the municipality while grants awarded to townships will
be distributed to the County.
·   There is legislation in place allowing me to apply for this so I will keep
you informed as more details are available.

Culverts
 
Service Dept  
·   I have received several complaints from individuals relating to the amount
of dirt accumulating on their garage floors as the snow melts from beneath
their cars.
·   I keep telling the individuals that I also see the dirt on my garage floor.
·   It is a byproduct of our mixing grit and salt together to reduce the cost
of snow and ice control.
·   I have scheduled all Street Department and Wastewater Department employees
to attend a free three hour “Work Zone Traffic Control and Safety” course
offered at the Saybrook Township Administrative Center on February 23 rd at 1:
00 PM. This is a class normally taught in Columbus, Ohio but is now part of a
“Circuit Rider” program which offers these ODOT programs at regional sights
statewide.
·   Any council members planning to go to Lakeland Urban Forestry Conference
must let me know.
Fire Dept. /Police Department
·   Help support the fire department auxiliary by attending their great pancake
breakfasts.
·   As reported the Police have been more active at the Jefferson area schools.
Recreation Department
·   The Community Center is busier than prior years with increasing levels of
activity in most programs.
·   Carpet in the reading room (library) has been completed.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Plant operations are normal with nothing exceptional to report.
·   The year end operation report has been filed with Ohio EPA.
·   Our Wastewater Plant Operations renewal Permits, due every five years, have
been completed and filed.
Other Items:
·   The Village Codified personnel rules are still being reviewed to correct
areas of inconsistency and/or areas where wording is being misinterpreted.
·   Our three year refuse contract is out for re-bid as discussed.
·   I signed a contract agreement for cell phones with Verizon wireless
Government Sales.
o   This is a federally bid government contract which is also available to
State and Local governments.
o   It saves the Village about $ 87.00 per month below our local Verizon
wireless “family share” contracts.
o   A seasoned Account Executive is our contact person rather than the ever
changing local Rep.
o   Free Equipment upgrades are available every 10 months.
o   Phones can be added or removed as warranted with no fees or contract terms
hindering us.
o   There is reduced pricing also available to other employees and family
members.
o   Police and Fire personnel will receive “rough service phones” waterproof
and drop resistant.
o   The contract also provides the wireless service required by the police
department to contact State and Federal records data bases by mobile cruiser
mounted laptops.
·   Village offices have the new carpet installed in the hall and Council
chambers to eliminate several trip hazards.
·   All areas of the Village Office have been rearranged and cleaned to remove
clutter and untidiness, including the basement.

Service Dept  
·   All Street Department and Wastewater Department employees attended the free
three hour “Work Zone Traffic Control and Safety” course offered at the
Saybrook Township Administrative Center on February 23rd at 1:00 PM. The
supervisors felt it was well worth the time and is a critical topic for our
employees working on the streets in traffic.
·   We have received written quotes for labor and for material to replace the
roof and add metal siding to the Street Department building. As soon after
April first as the new appropriations kick in we will be issuing a P.O. to
purchase the material and another P.O. for the labor. Total project will be
significantly below the budget amount and each purchase order is well below the
$25,000 limit that would require a sealed bid process.
Fire Dept. /Police Department
·   We have received two sealed bids for surplus police cruisers. Bid opening
will be Monday March 1 and I will report on the results at Council meeting.
Recreation Department
·   The Community Center remains busier than prior years with increasing levels
of activity in most programs.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Plant operations are normal with nothing exceptional to report.
Other Items:
·   The Village Codified personnel rules are still being reviewed to correct
areas of inconsistency and/or areas where wording is being misinterpreted.
·   I have included a summary of the three year refuse contract bids and need a
motion to accept the bid and have Jerry prepare the accepting resolution.
·   Planning Commission met Thursday February 25 to discuss the Historic
Preservation District Ordinance. There were seven local residents (six of the 7
were participants in the study group that met over a two year period) with
lively discussion within the audience and within the Planning Commission.
·   Planning Commission voted to approve an amended ( minor wording changes to
clarify the staggered terms appointment language) Historic Preservation
District Ordinance by a 3-2 vote and recommends its adoption to Village
Council.
·   I have asked for an executive session at the end of the meeting with no
action to be taken, to discuss personnel issues.

Culverts
 
Service Dept  
·   Brush pick up will begin April 5 th , 2010 and continue the first Monday of
each month thru the fall.
·   Village wide cleanup day has been scheduled for Saturday, May 8 th , 2010.
All County Disposal will have collections completed before 8:00 AM so all
refuse must be out Friday night May 7 th .
·   Items and procedures are the same as prior years. Village employees will
pick up appliances and metal items. There is a Freon removal fee for air
conditioners, refrigerators and freezers. Incidental tires will be picked up
for a fee with advance notice.
·   Village will evaluate requests for help in moving refuse to the curb but
will not be able to enter private residences.
·   A flyer is included with this report, information will be posted to the
Village web site and distributed to residents. .
·   Street Department employees are trimming and pruning street shade trees
according to 1026.06(c) which requires that lower branches be trimmed to 13
feet from the ground.
Fire Dept. /Police Department
·   We have received payment for one of the surplus police cruisers with the
second one still being stripped of its Jefferson identification markings.
Recreation Department
·   Spring Craft Show is scheduled at the Community Center on Saturday March 13
th  stop and check it out.
·   Carpet in the reading room was replaced by the supplier to get rid of the
miss matched seam.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Ohio EPA inspected our plant operations as part of our permit renewal
process. Jefferson plant is considered as an “Exemplary Plant” by EPA.
·   Our EPA violation records show only one minor violation as reported to
Council. That was the release of black sludge from Stone Container that caused
one daily sample report to show oil content that exceeded the plant limit. The
problem was corrected within two hours of discovery.
·   The EPA inspector noted that most plants have pages and pages of
violations.
·   In his words, our violation was so insignificant that EPA would not even
raise an eyebrow.
·   There was a second violation on record that Gary had challenged as being in
error (entire report in the EPA data base did not match the report submitted.
This error will be corrected.
·   EPA advised us of changes coming in our new permit that will add cost to
our treatment process. We will have to start monitoring mercury and switch from
monitoring fecal bacteria to E. coli bacteria. These changes will be phased in
over 18 months and are subject to further discussion.
·   EPA will issue a written inspection report as a result of the inspection.
Other Items:
·   The Village Codified personnel rules are still being reviewed to correct

Service Dept  
·   Two part time Police Officers, Mike Riffle and Erin McCracken have
expressed an interest in doing part time summer work for the Village Street
Department. Curt will schedule them as required in lieu of replacing Danny
Hubbard at this time.
·   Brush pick will continue the first Monday of each month thru the fall.
·   At our Wednesday staff meeting Curt Stone and I reviewed all the work that
needs to be completed this year and it is a bit overwhelming. We are pushing
hard to make this Village a better place in which to live. If Someone on
council has a pet project that concerns them please contact me and I can tell
you where it is in my priority listing.
·   Street Department employees continue sweeping streets, cleaning catch
basins, picking up stone and grit at intersections, cold patching and soon will
be repainting line striping.
·   County has been contracted to paint center lines as in past years.
·   The Service Committee (Fertig and March) and I reviewed the idea of
partnering with the County and Cemetery Board to seek OPWC grant funding to
replace the N. Market Street culvert, Pine Street Culvert and the bridge across
Cemetery Creek. I will proceed with the Grant request which will be submitted
in July. Awards will be announced by July 2011 and the work, if funded, would
need to be complete by 2013. Because this is a multi-jurisdictional project
there is a high probability it will be funded. Local cost can be covered with
in kind work in lieu of cash and local cost will be split among beneficiaries
of the improvements.
Fire Dept. /Police Department
·   May 6 th Prom promise at the High School
·   May 15 th Part Time Officer firearm certification
·   June 10 and 12 All Officers night time firearms certification
Recreation Department
·   Construction has resumed on the restroom at the playground park.
·   Playground Park is being upgraded with new basketball backboards, mulch,
equipment repairs, and baseball bases. The baseball backstop may be available
from a private property owner wishing to decommission his private playing
field. Price or terms have not been discussed yet so I will keep everyone
posted.
·   The reclaimed green area vacated by the demolition of the elementary school
has sidewalks completed, and new trees planted.
·   The fence and shrubs are still in the works.
·   I have also attached a recommended park bench to be made available to those
wishing to donate a memorial or offer an advertisement. The bench is 100%
recycled plastic, maintenance free, and has a guaranteed 50 year life. Cost
through Government purchasing is $254.88 each plus $2.00/per letter for
engraving.
·   Police are seeking prices to install monitoring cameras at the park and the
electrical and mounting requirements have been factored into the electrical
requirements.
·   SOCC and Rotary will wire the new restroom building but the Village will be
responsible to get power to the building, light pole, pavilion, and sign.
·   80 youth will start T Ball on May 3 rd . Play will be at the Little league
Complex.
·   Children Services through State of Ohio funding will be serving free lunch
at the playground park again this summer. This service is a magnet that drew
many youth to our summer programs at the park last year. We expect this second
year participation to be even greater.
·   Children Services will also offer free lunches at Safety Day on July 17 th
and Safety Town in August.
·   The senior centers’ funding meeting on April 23 rd with United Way went
very well. Senior Center expects to be funded at the same level as 2009. United
Way staff were very impressed at what they say when they visited the Senior
Center.
·   Allison (Senior Program Coordinator was recognized for being one of only
three people in Ashtabula County certified to advise Senior Citizens on the
many complexities of the new Medicaid Part II supplemental options that are
available.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   While First energy was replacing a utility pole on East Jefferson Street
they drilled a hole through our sewer trunk line. The line was immediately
repaired and we will seek reimbursement from First Energy.
·   Wastewater has been experiencing unexpected inflow that is causing unusual
treatment problems. Gary was advised to call EPA and have an inspector help us
in finding the source of the unexpected inflow. While we have had no violations
someone is dumping unacceptable contaminants into our system.
Other Items:
·   First Energy will be trimming trees in Jefferson beginning about the middle
of May. I would like the Forestry Committee to schedule a meeting time so
Mayor, Forestry Committee, First Energy and Nelson Tree Service can come to a
better understanding of what the Village concerns are before Nelson Tree
Service starts trimming and we receive resident’s complaints.
·   I am seeking a price to paint Jefferson something (welcome to Jefferson),
(Jefferson Falcons), (Ashtabula County Seat) (?????????) on the new water tank.
Will keep you posted!
Administrator Finger was asked if the agreement with First energy reduced the
cost at the Wastewater Treatment plant. Administrator Finger said the cost per
Kilowatt Hr. went down, but the distribution cost went up. Councilman Diehl and
Administrator Finger will do an electrical study at the WWTP to assess the
situation.

Motion at 8:00 by Councilman Damon to go into the Public Hearing in regard to
the proposed Historic District Ordinance.
2nd
Roll: All yea, motion Carried.
Guy Hansford of 26 E. Satin Street was recognized. Before his testimony he was
sworn in by Solicitor Lemire.
Mr. Hansford expressed his concern that the Architectural Review Board would be
taking authority away from Village Council. He also concerned that the entire
Village is part of the historical district not just the Business District. He
is concerned that there is no Grandfather Clause and he feels the fines were
excessive. He then compared the fines with DUI and feels the District fines are
too much.
Councilman Fertig said that zoning fines are $100 per day, and to his knowledge
the Village has yet to fine anyone for a zoning violation.
Councilman Damon stated that zoning and DUI are separate issues and aren’t
comparable .
Solicitor Lemire stated that the ordinance only sets the mechanism in place to
establish the Historical District Review Board. All rules will have to be
approved by Council.
Mayor Maloney stated that a local review board will be trained by the State
Review Board. The establishment of an Historical District will allow businesses
to apply for grants to improve or repair their property.

2nd’
Roll: All yea, motion carried.

Service Dept  
·   Work on the new roof and siding at the Street Department is progressing
without any problems.
·   Curt has recommended and I have approved the reclassifications of John
Buzzard Jr. from Driver/Laborer to Equipment Operator and John Powers from
Utility/Maintenance to Driver/Laborer.
·   We will not be filling the opening in the Utility Maintenance position
until fall of 2010. I intend to do mowing and such with temporary summer help.
·   Brush pick up is completed for April, 2010 and will continue the first
Monday of each month thru the fall.
·   Street Department employees continue sweeping streets, cleaning catch
basins, picking up stone and grit at intersections and cold patching.
·   Parks have been rolled and grass mowing began April 2 nd .
·   We are preparing a dead tree removal list for spring cutting.
Fire Dept. /Police Department
·   We received notification that Jefferson is still being considered for a
resource officer grant.
Recreation Department
·   Construction has resumed on the restroom at the playground park.
·   Playground Park will be upgraded with new basketball backboards, mulch,
equipment repairs, and baseball bases and backstop.
·   The reclaimed green area vacated by the demolition of the elementary school
is being fenced in, will have a new sidewalk section and will have some bushes
and trees planted soon.
·   Police are increasing surveillance and we are seeking prices to install a
monitoring camera at the park..
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Wastewater now has an updated and OSHA approved “Respirator Protection
Program”. Attached is a copy for your information.
·   After a very lively Utility/Wastewater meeting on April 5, 2010 to discuss
the revenue shortfall there seemed to be a split opinion on a solution. Some
members of Council want to transfer as much money as needed to cover the fund
while others favor the 3.5% rate increase to minimize the amount of money that
will need to be transferred..
·   I am again asking for a motion to allow the 3.5% rate increase that was
planned and agreed to by Council during the 2007 budget meetings on wastewater.
Approval by motion will allow the increase to be effective immediately and
appear on the next bi - monthly bill.
Other Items:
·   First Energy is replacing 27 utility poles in the Village over the next
couple of weeks.

Utilities/Wastewater Treatment/Service  
- No Report
Motion by Councilman March to approve Administrator Finger’s recommendation for
a 3.5% raise in sewer rates
2nd
Roll: March, yea; Brabender, yea; Damon, nay; Diehl, yea; Fertig, nay; Hoyson,
yea
Roll: 4, yea 2, nay motion carried
Council discussed at great length the pros and cons of a 3.5 % increase in
sewer rates. Administrator Finger told Council with the revenue decrease, the
WWTP fund would fall short of monies by July 1. Overtime has been decreased to
cut expenditures. The plant has to be operational. With the transfer of
$10,000.00 and the 3.5 increase in the sewer rates, it is just a short term
fix. The issue will have to be watched monthly.
A service Committee meeting was set-up for Wednesday, April 21 at 10:30 p.m. to
discuss culvert replacement under Market Street.

Visitor’s Comments (five minute limit per council rule # 13)
John Boczar of 433 Brittany Lane asked council to consider front yard parking
at 34 East Walnut Street. The parking is for his tenants to park if he does not
have the front yard zoning change he will have problems of parking. The
Planning Commission on May 10, 2010 voted to deny the approval the ordinance to
change the front yard parking. Boczar told council when he bought the house he
did not know about the zoning for front yard parking because this house has
always had the tenants parking in the front yard or side yard before the house
was built next to his property. Boczar told council he wanted the parking for
his tenants to be 15 by 15 in from of the house.
Ken Boczar of Jefferson Township told council that to help the tenants he made
the parking bigger by 10’ by 15’.
Administrator Finger told Council that this property is a single family
property that is non conforming to the Villages Zoning code. Ariel photos do
not show any front yard parking until after 2003. Parking for three cars will
require an area 20’ by 30’

Service Dept  
∙   Brush pick up will begin April 5th, 2010 and continue the first Monday of
each month thru the fall.
∙   Village wide cleanup day has been scheduled for Saturday, May 8th, 2010.
All County Disposal will have collections completed before 8:00 AM so all
refuse must be out Friday night May 7th.
∙   Items and procedures are the same as prior years. Village employees will
pick up appliances and metal items. There is a Freon removal fee for air
conditioners, refrigerators and freezers. Incidental tires will be picked up
for a fee with advance notice.
∙   Village will evaluate requests for help in moving refuse to the curb but
will not be able to enter private residences.
∙   A flyer is included with this report, information will be posted to the
Village web site and distributed to residents. .
∙   Street Department employees are trimming and pruning street shade trees
according to 1026.06(c) which requires that lower branches be trimmed to 13
feet from the ground.
Fire Dept. /Police Department
∙   We have received payment for one of the surplus police cruisers with the
second one still being stripped of its Jefferson identification markings.
Recreation Department
∙   Spring Craft Show is scheduled at the Community Center on Saturday March
13th stop and check it out.
∙   Carpet in the reading room was replaced by the supplier to get rid of the
miss matched seam.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
∙   Ohio EPA inspected our plant operations as part of our permit renewal
process. Jefferson plant is considered as an “Exemplary Plant” by EPA.
∙   Our EPA violation records show only one minor violation as reported to
Council. That was the release of black sludge from Stone Container that caused
one daily sample report to show oil content that exceeded the plant limit. The
problem was corrected within two hours of discovery.
∙   The EPA inspector noted that most plants have pages and pages of
violations.
∙   In his words, our violation was so insignificant that EPA would not even
raise an eyebrow.
∙   There was a second violation on record that Gary had challenged as being in
error (entire report in the EPA data base did not match the report submitted.
This error will be corrected.
∙   EPA advised us of changes coming in our new permit that will add cost to
our treatment process. We will have to start monitoring mercury and switch from
monitoring fecal bacteria to E. coli bacteria. These changes will be phased in
over 18 months and are subject to further discussion.
∙   EPA will issue a written inspection report as a result of the inspection.
Other Items:
∙   The Village Codified personnel rules are still being reviewed to correct
areas of inconsistency and/or areas where wording is being misinterpreted.
∙   A planning Commission meeting to continue the front yard parking issue at
34 E. Walnut Street is scheduled for March 18th at 7:30 PM.

Service Dept  
∙   All the work currently scheduled for this summer (copy attached) has been
updated.
∙   Street Department has removed seven smaller dead trees. The balance of the
tree trimming/removal will be contracted to Brobst for a flat rate of $1,800
per day.
∙   Nelson tree Service began trimming Village trees for line clearance on
Monday June 14th. Their aggressive trimming exceeded the verbal agreement rules
that were discussed between the Village, First Energy, and Nelson Tree Service.
∙   Nelson Tree Service was compelled to stop their work until such time as
First Energy and the Village worked out the differences between a “trim” and a
“short summer buzz”.
∙   First Energy Certified Forester, Roy Klingamen met with Mayor and I Tuesday
the 15th to work on the problem. He agreed with us that the trimming was more
aggressive than we expected.
∙   Roy    will accompany Nelson Tree Service when they resume work to make
sure all issues are immediately mediated.
Fire Dept. /Police Department
∙   Police cruiser was vandalized (mirror broken, scratches) while parked at
the police station.
∙   Marcs Radio Grant has been completed
∙   COPS Grant reapplication has been submitted.
Recreation Department
∙   The restroom at the playground park officially opened on June 14th as
planned. Occupancy permit has been issued and opening (unlock) and closing
(lock) duties have been assigned.
∙   The new sign face at Central Park has been installed to replace the
Jefferson School sign.
∙   I have included a second copy of the costs associated with Central Park and
playground refurbishment.
∙   Electric installation at the bathroom, security lamp, and pavilion has been
completed and the electrical inspection passed.
∙   Summer free lunch program began June 14th with 58 lunches served and 88
lunches on the second day.
∙   There are 11 active soccer teams for the summer consisting of over 100
kids.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
∙   Concrete repair is under way. The deteriorating concrete was becoming a
safety concern in addition to a maintenance need. These repairs will help
prevent trips and falls.
∙   Wastewater Plant operation has been modified to reduce the amount of time
the large air blowers operate in an effort to reduce electric usage (cost).
∙   It costs $0.06/hour/horse power to blow air in the digester tanks and
aeration tanks.
∙   We will reduce the digester air input provided by motors totaling 90 HP by
seven hours/day.
∙   Savings of $.06 X 7 hrs X 20 days X 90 hp = $756.00 per month
∙   We will reduce the aeration air input provided by a 75 hp motor by 8 hours/
day.
∙   Savings of $0.06 X 8 hrs X 30 days X 75 hp = $1,080.00 per month
∙   Estimated yearly savings            = $22,032 per year
∙   If this manual test does not adversely effect the treatment specifications
we can automate the process and possibly increase the off time of these blowers
to potentially realize a greater electric bill savings.

Front Yard Ordinance –
Solicitor Jerry Lemire swore in Roger Mericka, John Boczar and Richard
Reuschiling in regard to their testimony concerning zoning ordinances before
Council
Administrator Finger explained to Council that the Village of Jefferson Council
passed a zoning ordinance sometime between 1996-1998 regarding front yard
parking. 34 East Walnut Street was bought in 2004 after the front yard parking
ordinance was passed. The property is a three family apartment in a residential
and is non-conforming to the zoning code with no deed restrictions preserving
parking on the lot.
There was two planning commission meeting regarding the parking issue.
∙   The first meeting, the votes were 3-2 to allow the front yard parking, put
legally the commission needs an ordinance present to pass.
∙   The second meeting, with the written ordinance, the planning commission
voted the zoning change down.
Council can choose to overturn Planning Commission’s decision with five votes/
Councilman Damon asked to have the pictures given to Council put in record:
∙   First picture was in 1992 prior to the zoning ordinance with front yard
parking.
∙   Second picture was in 2006 after zoning ordinance passed.
Councilman Fertig noted that there was no disclose issue on the property when
it was bought. He also stated that the Village should not change zoning to fit
any particular situation.
Richard Reuschling testified that he was opposed to front parking in the rental
property that is next door to his residence. It would be only two feet from his
property. There would be no room to put up a fence. He stated that there would
be a problem keeping snow and water away from his property.
Roger Merika objects to parking in the front yard – it would be an eye sore. He
suggesting tearing down the garage to put parking in the rear. It is illegal to
park in the yard, and it should be enforced.
John Boczar said the garage is used for storage. The area had previously been
used for parking. In the winter the street cannot be used for parking due to
snow removal. He said that there are 12 houses that have parking in front of
the house.
West Cedar Street Subdivision Regulations Ordinance
Administrator Finger explained the lot split on West Cedar Street – The
Planning Commission approved the 9116 frontage for the two lots with a 5-
0 vote. At this time, the Planning Commission is asking for Council approval.

Wastewater Treatment Plant:
Our first measurable results from intermittently running the blowers show that
our electric bill decreased from $7,941.38 to $6,578.46 in the first month of
operation. This savings ($1,362.92) is recorded at a time when the fans need to
run most frequently (hot weather). It is entirely possible that the savings may
be greater than ($1,362.99 X 12 = $16,355.04) per year when cooler weather
returns.

Recreation Department
∙   Construction has resumed on the restroom at the playground park.
∙   Playground Park will be upgraded with new basketball backboards, mulch,
equipment repairs, and baseball bases and backstop.

and trees planted soon.

Wastewater Treatment Plant:
∙   Wastewater now has an updated and OSHA approved “Respirator Protection
Program”. Attached is a copy for your information.
∙   After a very lively Utility/Wastewater meeting on April 5, 2010 to discuss
the revenue shortfall there seemed to be a split opinion on a solution. Some
members of Council want to transfer as much money as needed to cover the fund
while others favor the 3.5% rate increase to minimize the amount of money that
will need to be transferred..
∙   I am again asking for a motion to allow the 3.5% rate increase that was
planned and agreed to by Council during the 2007 budget meetings on wastewater.
Approval by motion will allow the increase to be effective immediately and
appear on the next bi - monthly bill.

her neighborhood, Solicitor Lemire sent a letter requesting that the owner of
the dogs comply to the Village ordinance limiting the number of dogs to three

the date be extended to February 1, 2011 in order to find suitable homes for
the dogs that have to be relocated. Council has agreed to honor the request.

Culverts
 
Service Dept:
∙   Leaf pickup begins the first Monday of November with a reminder that leaves
must be placed in biodegradable paper bags to be recycled as mulch.
∙   Street sweeping and cleaning storm water catch basins had to be suspended
due to a breakdown of Geneva on the lake’s vacuum truck. We provide inside
Winter storage in exchange for being able to use the Machine at no cost.
∙   The Village is looking into additional options for sweeping and vacuum
service.
∙   We are continuing to use the pot hole repair machine that belongs to
Ashtabula City to evaluate and see if it is practical to purchase the machine.
∙   Street edges continue to have the stone material replaced/refreshed.
∙   We will be planting 20 new trees
∙   Nelson tree Service utility line tree trimming resumed October 26. Work has
been progressing with no problems.
∙   Spruce Street intersection improvements project has been completed. Thanks
to the County Road Department and County Engineer for their excellent
cooperation and job.
∙   Presrite’s plant expansion is progressing nicely.
∙   Presrite’s additional expansion plans may require opening Mulberry Street
to Spruce Street to accommodate additional truck traffic flow. Rough draft
plans are being developed to enable more complete planning and discussions.
Fire Dept. /Police Department:
∙   Police Cruiser #396 has been taken out of service and will be declared
scrap. The frame is rusted through and the vehicle is no longer road worthy.
∙   We are working on replacement plans which will be implemented ASAP.
∙   Hot Dogs and Hamburgers will be on sale by the Fire Department Auxiliary
Saturday Night Oct. 30. Stop by to support the sales event.
Recreation Department:
∙   Health Fair attendance fell short of last years attendance levels.
∙   Boo in the Park will take place Again on Oct. 29 and Oct. 30.
∙   There will also be a Halloween Party at the Community Center after trick or
treating on Saturday Oct. 30.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
∙   Plant operation has been normal.
∙   We had to discontinue running air circulating blowers intermittently and
resume continuous operation. This attempt to reduce electric costs worked but
caused other problems. The odor became unacceptable, our fly population
increased 1,000 fold, sediment fall out blocked the diffusers which caused air
flow deficiency upon restarting the blowers.
∙   We are now monitoring oxygen content and running the pumps at a variable
speed without shutting them off.
Other Items:
∙   Mayor, Jerry and I have reviewed the economic development incentive program
discussed at the finance committee meeting and have engaged Vorys, Sater,
Seymour and Pease LLP in Columbus to finalize our ordinance, application and
details to assure we meet the letter of the laws involved.
∙   Mayor Maloney led the quarterly administrative review of Village finances
involving The Clerk/Treasurer, Administrative Assistant, and me. As a result of
this review the Mayor, with our concurrence, has chosen about $62,000 in lease/
loan amounts to pay off in 2010.
∙   Paying these early will free that amount of money from having to be paid in
2011.
∙   Additionally the revised appropriations ordinance on Council’s agenda
reflects changes in spending to enable us to make this payment, accomplish the
remaining goals for 2010, and reduce 2010’s total spending by $183,283.40.
∙   The reduction results from moving two projects originally scheduled for
2010 into 2011.
   o   Sanitary forced main. $175,500
   o   Safe Routes to Schools $6,000, and
   o   $1,783.40 of the reduction is miscellaneous fine tuning.

Visitor’s Comments (five minute limit per council rule # 13)
The Jefferson Curves franchise plans to close. .Shelly Knight the present owner
of Curves addressed Council asking Council to consider ways that Curves and the
Village can form a relationship/partnership. Several of the members present
state the benefits of the Curves program and are hopeful that the franchise can
be continued. Councilwoman told the group that the a Recreation Committee
meeting is scheduled for Thursday, November 18 th at 1:00 p.m. at the Village
Hall, and the Curves issue will be put on the agenda.

Culverts
 
Service Dept:
∙   Leaf pickup will continue as needed. A reminder to residents that leaves
must be placed in biodegradable paper bags to be recycled as mulch.
∙   We have planted 20 new trees.
∙   Nelson tree Service utility line tree trimming continues to until all lines
are cleared.
∙   Curt and I looked at sample of a refurbished dump/plow truck that looks
promising as a future replacement for one of ours in 2011. These are box
delivery trucks that have high miles with zero plowing miles. The box is
removed and the chassis is totally refitted as a plow/dump truck. Included as
new are the plow and attachment, salt spreader, dump box and hydraulics. Prices
run around $52,000 compared to $120,000 for a totally new one.
Fire Dept. /Police Department:
∙   A replacement for Police Cruiser #396 has been ordered at State purchase
pricing.
∙   Lease pricing is below $25,000 so no ordinance is required.
Recreation Department:
∙   The Halloween Party at the Community Center after trick or treating was
attended by 75 kids.
∙   Skate park equipment that was beyond repair has been destroyed.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
∙   Plant operation has been normal.
Other Items:
∙   Village Department heads are ready for budget meetings with the Finance
Committee.
∙   The economic development incentive program discussed at the finance
committee meeting is still being drafted by Vorys, Sater, Seymour and Pease LLP
in Columbus.

Recreation Department:
∙   I need Council’s confirmation of Allison Brown as new Recreation/Park
Supervisor
∙   With Lisa’s departure from the Supervisors job at the Community the staff
has been doing an excellent job to make sure the facility is maintained,
staffed, and professional.
∙   By the first of the year there should be a new senior program coordinator,
and the van driver should be back from sick leave.
∙   Allison has new instructors scheduled to begin programs beginning in
January also.
∙   After much discussion Curves has decided not to relocate to the Community
Center and closed on November 30th.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
∙   Plant operation has been normal until the Thanksgiving Day rain.
∙   Gary informed me that the alarms had gone off at Woodside pump station and
the pumps could not keep up with the incoming muddy water.
∙   His investigation led to a broken sewer lateral at an empty lot just east
of Hillier Street intersection.
∙   Muddy rain water was running through the woods and disappearing into a hole
in the ground.
∙   Street department excavated the area and found the broken lateral and it
was capped.
∙   Gary has been searching for rain water infiltration into this system for
three years.
∙   It finally got bad enough that a hole opened large enough to easily spot.
∙   System is now again sealed from rain water at least in this spot.

Finance Committee.

hands awaiting further discussion.

Service Dept:
∙   Village crews have been actively engaged in snow cleanup.
∙   Snow plows remained active to keep the village streets open and passable.
∙   Again this year we are using a sand (grit) salt mixture on the streets.
This combination takes a little longer to melt the snow so drivers need to
reduce speeds when the streets are snow covered.
∙   The sidewalk snow plow had to be converted from the V plow to the snow
blower to be able to move the deep and heavy accumulation.
∙   Sidewalks in the business district were given extra priority since the
Schools were closed.
∙   I can personally attest to the fact that snow plow operators clearing
driveways are piling snow on the sidewalks. These piles of snow are difficult
and sometimes impossible to remove with our sidewalk plow/blower.
∙   We will begin identifying the offenders, re-educating them, and issuing
citations to the continuing offenders.
∙   Trying to remove piles of hard packed snow from these plow operators delays
the clean up and causes shear pin failure on the snow blower attachment.
Fire Dept. /Police Department:
∙   New Cruiser delivery is expected between Christmas and New Years.
Recreation Department:
∙   Village of Jefferson Senior Department lost an $18,000 Senior
Transportation Grant. This grant was used to provide transportation money to
offset some of: the Van Drivers wages, the Senior Director’s wages, and senior
trips shopping or to entertainment events.
∙   There is a consolidation of services taking place in the Senior
Transportation Services area.
∙   Country Neighbor located in Orwell was chosen to coordinate the Senior
Transportation for Ashtabula County. Monday, December 20 Allison will meet with
Country Neighbor to better understand the new organization.
∙   We have reviewed numerous applications to fill the senior program
coordinator and are conducting interviews with select applicants.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
∙   Plant operation is again normal.
Other Items:
∙   As reported by the news papers, The Village (Mayor and I) received a phone
call from Aqua Ohio on Saturday at 1:29 PM telling us that Ohio American had an
EPA recordable event (Turbidity - cloudy water) which is an indicator of
drinking water quality problems.
∙   The EPA advised Ohio American to notify all their customers that there was
a boil drinking water advisory in effect until water quality testing was
completed.
∙   Since Aqua purchases some of Jefferson’s water supply from Ohio American,
Aqua notified Village of Jefferson officials.
∙   Judy and I agreed that it was an event worthy of issuing a Code Red alert
to all Jefferson’s residents.
∙   EMA Director George Sabo’s was notified and within one hour he had mapped
the call area, down loaded phone numbers from the 911 data base, and the system
had called 1,052 Village resident phone numbers.
∙   With the call area and phone numbers permanently saved, each of the second
and third notifications took only eight (8) minutes to complete.
∙   Each call notification cost about $86.00 to complete.
∙   Residents who did not receive a Code Red call should visit Ashtabula County
Web site and register with Code Red to make sure they receive future
notifications.

OFFICIALS
MAYOR  
STATE OF THE VILLAGE 2010
As we approach the second decade of the 21 st century, we are grateful the
Village of Jefferson remains happy, healthy and hopeful. With due diligence,
the department supervisors, the administrative staff and the clerk-treasurer
are constantly working to be watchful stewards of the Village finances. Budget
issues were accomplished. In addition, several loans were repaid early. We
reduced spending by $183.283.40 with a $700,000+ carryover.
The Village Council, administration and staff have strived to assure that
Jefferson continues to be the epitome of the “All-American” Village and the
welcoming environment of the County Seat.
We are proud of our Village workers, who are personable, courteous and willing
to help whenever and wherever there is a need.
One of this year’s greatest accomplishments is the development and completion
of the area that once was the site of the Jefferson Elementary School. The park
and playground will be a welcoming gathering place for our residents, young and
old, for many years. The restrooms have been completed and dedicated! The
restrooms will reopen in the Spring.
In addition to maintaining, painting and adding to our buildings and grounds,
some of the projects that were accomplished by each Village department are:
Street Department
·   Finished Spruce Street (OPWC Project) improve sight distance and pave
·   Repaired and paved south end of Spruce Street and fixed a flooding problem
at the railroad overpass site
·   Service garage project (Grant Approved)
   §   Insulate the sides
   §   Install metal siding
   §   Install new windows
   §   Install new lights
   §   Change from flat roof to peaked roof
   §   Install new overhead doors
   §   Install new man doors
   §   Install new sign
·   Repair $20,000.00 worth of sidewalks
·   Park improvements
   §   Finish engraving the stone at the east park (Village of Jefferson East
Park)
   §   Put drain tile in at North Cucumber gas well site and reopen the walking
trail
   §   New restrooms and storage building completed at Central Park (Rotary and
SOCC project)
   §   Finished mulch at park
   §   Equipment repairs at the park
   §   Install new Basketball backstop (surplus from High School)
   §   Salvage shrubs from home on 307 west, install at park
   §   Installed new shrubs and mulch at public greens area
   §   Planted several new Oak Trees
   §   Change the sign face at the public greens area
   §   Installed Park Benches as they are sold.
Recreation Department
·   Replaced five of six employees:
   §   Supervisor
   §   Senior Coordinator
   §   Senior van Driver
   §   Two front desk staff
Wastewater
·   Continued to seek ways to reduce cost
   §   Negotiated a reduced rate for Electricity cost.
   §   Tried various changes in run times for motors seeking reduced
consumption
   §   Reduced rain water infiltration at several points
Administration
·   Personnel rules change
·   Installed back up power at the Village Administration Building
·   Paved     East Walnut Street between Market and Chestnut Streets
·   Worked with First Energy and Nelson Tree Service to maximize the esthetics
of their required tree trimming
·   Mayor appointed the Historical district members
Our continued goal is to keep our Village attractive and appealing. We have
created a “Design Review Board” intended to protect historic buildings and
areas within the Village.
We look forward to the challenges and rewards of 2011, and hope you, your
family and friends have a Happy, Healthy and Prosperous New Year.

Service Dept  
·   Dump truck and backhoe ordinances are in Council’s packet for approval.
·   The Dump Truck financing is in order and the truck is on hold for us.
Approval will enable me to advertise and dispose of the two dump trucks we have
declared surplus.
·   The backhoe ordinance will enable us to get in on the State 2010 Purchase
Price. Delay will cost us an estimated additional $8,000.00. Delivery is not
expected until April, 2011.
·   Christmas tree pick up at will from here on. As the street crews observe
them and are not plowing they will be picked up.
·   During last weeks mild weather the Street Department employees cleaned and
repainted about ½ the inside of the main building. Stop in to see the
remarkable transformation from grimy to freshly painted.
Fire Dept. /Police Department
·   Tim Blon has returned to work with no limitations.
·   The new Cruiser is in service and the old one has been sold as scrap.
Recreation Department
·   The Community Center is once again at full staffing levels. New hires are
in place, vacations completed, and those on sick leave have returned.
·   We can expect improvements in all aspects of the center’s operation.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Everything is operating normally.

maintenance code. Sending the information to Committee Building & Lands 715.621

Service Dept  
·   The Dump Truck should be shipping any day and may be here by Monday’s
Council meeting.
·   The backhoe has been ordered with delivery expected in April, 2011.
·   Snow management has been the priority as everyone knows.
·   Sand/grit mix has caused accumulations on the streets as expected. We will
utilize the Geneva-on-the-lake’s sweeper to clean up in the spring.
·   It is worth mentioning again that grit costs $7.50 dollars per ton while
salt costs $56.41 dollars a ton.
Fire Dept. /Police Department
·   Plans for an addition on the Police Department are under consideration.
·   The furnace at the Police Department is being replaced.
Recreation Department
·   Carpet for the Community Center multi – purpose room should be installed
week of February 7 thru 11th.
·   The Community Center is looking for grant money to replace the Senior Van.
Repairs on the Van amounted to over $4,000 in 2010. See attached Current Van
Statistics.
·   No action on purchasing a Van can take place without an approved resolution
from Council.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Everything is operating normally.
·   Service Committee needs to meet soon to discuss treatment plant finances
and financial options prior to finalizing the 2011 appropriations.
Other Items:
·   Two ordinances are included in Council packet:
   o   The Noise ordinance is still in Committee
   o   The Personnel rules change is for language clarification and does not
change the intended content of the rules passed in January.
·   I would like approval to send three employees plus, Mayor, me, and any
Councilperson to the annual Forestry meeting.

Service Dept  
·   The Street Department crew quickly cleared storm drains of snow and leaves
and cut channels for the standing water on roadways to get into the drains.
Flooded spots were almost completely cleared before the 8:00 AM traffic rush..
·   The New Dump Truck is in service.
·   Surplus trucks are being advertised for sale by highest bid.
·   Pothole repair continues to be a priority during the current thaw cycle.
·   The remaining Christmas decorations have been removed and put back in
storage.
·   Easements have been prepared along Eagleville Road to enable us to proceed
with the Culvert replacement.
·   Ken Fertig, our representative on the Cemetery Board, has indicated there
is a reluctance to commit the $20,000 that was discussed with the Cemetery
Board when we planned the Market Street Culvert replacement. The plans as
submitted would have added an additional box culvert section which will enable
the Cemetery to eliminate the defective bridge and cross over the stream at the
box culvert.
·   Mayor Maloney and I will attend the next Cemetery Board meeting to get a
definite commitment for the $20,000 or the plans will be completed without the
extra box section.
Fire Dept. /Police Department
·   Plans for an addition on the Police Department are progressing nicely.
·   The furnace at the Police Department has not yet been installed.
Recreation Department
·   Painting has been completed in the aerobics, multi-purpose, free weight,
exercise machine rooms and Director’s and Senior staff offices.
·   Several new classes are being well attended while some could use some more
participants
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Everything is operating normally.
·   Wastewater handled the Sunday night rain and thaw event with no overflows.
Pumps ran at maximum to handle the rain water inflow from several manholes that
were underwater.
Other Items:
·   The refuse contract calls for a rate increase effective May 1st, 2011. We
are not going to pass this increase on to the residents until we reduce the
fund carry over amount by $20,000.
Administrator Finger mentioned that the W. Erie Street water line break is
being investigated by the water company to see if it needs replaced. We will
meet with Aqua Ohio to assess the situation.

Service Dept  
·   The Street Department will resume brush pickup Monday April 4th, 2011. It
may take more than one day to complete the Village.
·   The 1998 surplus truck received a bid that exceeded the minimum and will be
sold.
·   The 1995 truck received one bid lower than the minimum price of $15,000.
·   Pothole repair continues to be a priority during the current thaw cycle.
·   Painting the inside of the Street Department building has been completed.
·   Mayor Maloney and I meet with the Cemetery board to clear up an
misunderstandings regarding the Market Street Culvert replacement project. At
the next Cemetery Board meeting they will discuss the project again and
consider if they want to participate.
Fire Dept. /Police Department
·   Plans for an addition on the Police Department are progressing nicely.
·   The furnace at the Police Department has been installed and will be
operational soon.
Recreation Department
·   All painting has been completed in the inside of the Community Center. This
summer painting will focus on the East and North sides of the building.
·   All events are being well attended with more to come. The downward slide
has been reversed and everything is up beat at Rec.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   EPA inspected our plant last week and we were again given acceptable marks
on all phases of the operation.
·   The sewer ordinance on Council floor adds a capitol improvement charge of
$4.52 per month to each user connected to the Village Sewer System. Minimum
monthly billing will remain the same for around 284 low volume users. The
treatment fee per consumption of water remains unchanged from 2010. The fee
will be removed in 2016 and rates may be able to be lowered further when the
$151,000 annual payment for plant improvements is finished.
·   See attached sewer billing comparisons with the new ordinance in place.
·   For two years we have transferred a total of $55,000 from the General Fund
to cover the Sewer Plant expenses. This money must be paid back and this year
there is not enough money to further subsidize the plant funds.
Other Items:
·   The refuse contract calls for a rate increase of $0.40/month effective May
1st, 2011. We are not going to pass this increase on to the residents until we
reduce the fund carry over amount by $20,000.
Administrator Finger told Council that the County has agreed to buy the 1995
surplus Dump Truck for $15,000 worth of in kind work.
Administrator Finger stated that the Ohio Environmental Protection Agency’s
wastewater evaluation, included in Council’s packet, was very good.

Service Dept  
∙   Village wide Cleanup on Saturday, May 7th was another successful event.
Pickers were active all day Friday and Waste Management completed the entire
village between 7:00 AM and 9:00 AM. Street department employees picked up
several tires and metal from the entire Village.
∙   The Jefferson Historic Society will be receiving a check for about $940.00
from the scrap metal that was collected and sold.
∙   We are receiving free fill (value if purchased > $10,000) dirt from the
Dollar General Store construction site. It is being stockpiled behind the salt
storage bin for the Market Street Culvert replacement project.
∙   Presrite Corporation’s culvert replacements and additional concrete culvert
pipe to allow for truck turn out has been completed on the Village right of
way.
∙   MC70 dust control will be scheduled as early as weather permits.
Fire Dept. /Police Department
∙   The production of drawings for the Police Department addition has been
reassigned to Smolen Engineering due to non performance of the last company.
Recreation Department
∙   Peggy Otto has decided to retire with a firm date of May 27 as publicized
in the Gazette Newspaper.
∙   We will be moving Jennifer Housel, the current Van Driver, to fill the
position vacated by the retirement of Peggy Otto.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
∙   Operations have returned to normal in spite of the high amount of rain.
∙   We had to make another repair to our main sewer line on West Ashtabula
Street. This will be the second break this year and these are usually a rare
occurrence.
Other Items:
∙   Historic District Board is active with implementing the Local Historic
District ordinance.
∙   Andover Bank not Lakeview Federal Credit Union has donated two flowering
crab trees for village beautification. A planting event will be scheduled.

Service Dept  
∙   SCR 2 dust control was completed on June 2nd for the following Streets:
North Spruce, South Spruce, East Erie, South Sycamore, Pine Street, Woodside,
Frayer, and Elliott. The Contractor and street department did an excellent job.
∙   Presrite Corporation has requested that the Village vacate the remaining
portion of unopened East Mulberry Street from the edge of Worthington’s
property to Spruce Street. I agree with this request since this portion
includes Railroad right- of- way, a wide stream basin and is useless to develop
as a street.
∙   We are continuing to receiving free fill (value if purchased > $15,000)
dirt from the Dollar General Store construction site.
∙   Storm water drainage has been exceptional. We are investigating three minor
complaints where there may be a blocked/damaged line.
∙   Sidewalk construction will commence June 8th and continue through the
summer.
∙   Easements on the South side of Eagleville/West Jefferson Street have been
completed. The OPWC culvert project will commence as soon as Dominion can
relocate their gas lines.
 Fire Dept. /Police Department
∙   The Police Department air conditioning unit has been activated just in time
for warm weather.
∙   Addition drawings are still to be completed.
Recreation Department
∙   Programs continue to be added and staffing evaluated.
∙   We will be advertising for a part time desk person according to our budget.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
∙   Sewer lines at the new High School did not have any storm water
infiltration in spite of the high amount of rain.
∙   Plant is operating under normal conditions with no exceptions to report.
Other Items:
∙   Historic District Board continues to meet and is actively implementing the
Local Historic District ordinance.
∙   The property maintenance code is being released for full Council’s
consideration.
∙   Village has contracted mowing tall grass for nine (9) properties. Monday I
will review properties again and contact owners who did not get caught up this
weekend.
Administrator Finger discussed the letter from Presrite which was presented to
the Planning Commission.
Administrator Finger informed Council that the Planning Commission voted to
prepare the ordinances to: Rezone the Senior Apartments on E. Jefferson Street,
abandon Mulberry Street per Presrite’s request, and add Historic District to
zoning map

∙   Presrite Corporation’s zoning permit was issued for a 64,000 sq. ft.
addition as planned.
∙   Presrite has also requested a five year property tax abatement on this
investment.
∙   Sidewalk replacement commenced June 8th as planned and has been recessed
until after the two street construction projects are complete.
∙   Eagleville culvert replacement will start on Monday as planned.
∙   The next sidewalk priority area will shift from West Jefferson to West
Walnut Street.
 Fire Dept. /Police Department
∙   The Police Department addition’s drawings are complete and financing is
being arranged by Clerk/Treasurer.
∙   Middlefield dispatching contract and ordinance is in council packet. The
yearly fee is the same as 2010 but the change to fifteen months makes it look
like there is an increase.
∙   Middlefield is doing a onetime 15 month contract to correspond to their
January to December budget cycle.
Recreation Department
∙   Youth Soccer relocation to the grassy area east of the Playground equipment
at Central Park has been favorable to parents and players.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
∙   Plant is operating under normal conditions with no exceptions to report.
∙   I need to schedule a service committee meeting to discuss new EPA
requirements at the plant.
Other Items:
∙   A Civil complaint was filed against John Boczar for failure to correct his
long standing Zoning Violations.
∙   Eleven complaint letters were sent to property owners regarding property
maintenance issues. Six have either taken action or promised action. Additional
follow up is planned ASAP.

the Recreation Center Bond to save about $8,000 a year. He also expressed
concern that the Village should utilize the Recreation Center Building that we
have now and try to make some revenue
Jim Donathan told Council he opposes the purchase of the old elementary school.
The main reason being double taxes. The residents are paying twice on the
building. He told Council that he does agree that the Police Department needs a
new building, but the Village should utilize the space we have. He asked
Council to look at the land values to make sure the Village is not paying too
much.

Visitor’s Comments (five minute limit per council rule # 13)
Jim Donathon of 337 Susan Drive Jefferson, Ohio expressed to Council that he
opposes the purchase of the old elementary school. Donathon stated that he felt
300,000.00 dollars is too much to spend on the school and feels that the
residents are be taxed twice for the building if the Village buys it. Donathon
also explained that he is not against the Police Department getting a new
building. Donathon also asked the village to look at the ownership of the Land
that the old Jefferson Elementary school is on. Donathon stated if the village
goes forward with the third reading a referendum will be filed against the
ordinance.
Solicitor Lemire explained that the referendum must be filed with the clerk-
treasurer within thirty days after the third reading of the Ordinance. The
Clerk- Treasurer will then file the referendum paperwork with the board of
elections and the decision to buy the building will be on the ballot next
November.
Tina Fuller of 145 South Elm Street Jefferson, Ohio told Council that they
should reconsider purchasing the property of the Jefferson old Elementary
School. With the loss of businesses in the Village and the economy. Fuller
stated this purchase would put another burden on the village residents. The
Village already has so many empty houses and houses in foreclosure.
Casey Baxley of 245 East Jefferson Street Jefferson, Ohio read a lengthy
statement explaining why she is against the purchase of the old Jefferson
Elementary School. Included in the statement was potential issue with the
building found thru the appraisal done for the Village. Baxley also stated the
Old Rock Creek School building was sold by the school board one dollar and ten
thousand dollars an acre. Baxley asked why is the school charging the village
so much for this building and why is the village in such a rush to purchase a
building that has been vacant for years. The question was also brought up will
the Village have to hire more people to do the in-kind work.
Robert Lister OF 18 East Satin Street Jefferson, Ohio told council he opposes
the Village buying the old Jefferson Elementary School building. Lister asked
if it was legal to have the Village employees work for the school. Also told
council that the jobs listed would be taken away from employees at the school.
Solicitor Lemire told council and the residents the Village employees working
at the school would be paid thru the Village Of Jefferson.
Administrator Finger express to everyone that what was proposed in the contract
was what the School Board suggested. If there are any issues with the work the
school wants, the concerned residents should go to the school board.
Diana Dickson Sowry of 61 West satin Street Jefferson, Ohio told council she
was also against the purchase of the Old Elementary school building. Asked why
both governing boards did not post a public hearing to inform the residents of
the Village. Dickson Sowry also expressed concern with the change in the
Ordinance to eliminate the prohibition against hiring immediate family members
of the Village Council and Clerk Treasurer.
Solicitor Lemire told everyone that our village ordinance was more strict that
the state law. With this change that is proposed it will not break any State
statues and the Village will be in line more with the State.
Frank Snyder of 116 West Jefferson Street expressed to council the he feels
$300.000.00 is a bit much for the old school building. He does agree that the
Police Department need more space. Suggested to Council to hold the third
reading and negotiate the offer more. If not there will be a referendum the
Ordinance and the building will be held up for a year.

December 5, 2011
COUNCIL OF THE WHOLE
December 5, 2011
7:00
President Pro-Tem Rick Hoyson called the meeting to order.
Those present: Rick Hoyson, Brian Diehl, Ken Fertig, Jerry March, Kay Ann
Brabender, Lon Damon, Clerk/Treasurer Patricia Fisher, Administrator Terry
Finger, Mayor Judy Maloney , Rev. Fred Grimm, Frank Snyder, Pat Bradek;
Stefanie Wessell, Gazette; Tina Fuller, Cayce Baxley, E. Pengel, Bob Lister.
The confidentiality issue in regard to Executive Session was the topic
discussed.
Discussion determined that confidentiality would be addressed as Rule #40 in
Council Rules.
I t was determined that if someone other than Council is included in the
Executive Session, that person is to be advised of the confidentiality status
of Executive Session. If that person violates the confidentially mandate that
person would be in violation of the confidentiality mandate Council Rule #40 –
violation of Rule #40 will be covered in Rule #16.
Motion by Councilman Diehl seconded by Councilman Damon to designate Rule #40
as an item in Council rules that would state that items discussed in Executive
Session be confidential until it is presented in an open public meeting.
Roll: Rick Hoyson, yea; Brian Diehl, yea; Ken Fertig, nay; Jerry March, yea;
Kay Ann Brabender, yea; Lon Damon, yea. 5-yea; 1-nay, motion carried.
Councilman by Councilman Damon seconded by Councilman March to adjourn.
Roll: All yea, motion carried.
Meeting adjourned at 7:18
Submitted by
Patricia A. Fisher, Clerk of Council

00 p.m. this evening.

Councilman Fertig question an e-mail sent to council regarding the
administrative secretary wages.
Administrator Finger told council that it was just information the he receives
about job openings that other municipalities have.
Visitor’s Comment
Tina Fuller of 145 South Elm Street questioned the Village Administrator as to
why the tree was cut down on her property and she was not notified. Fuller told
council the tree was decorated with Christmas lights and the company that took
the tree down and placed them on the porch. Fuller said at the last council
meeting the administrator told council that the Village was not going to cut
any more trees down this year. Fuller also questioned why the Administrator did
not follow the Village Ordinance, which states that the property owner be
contacted with a written notice. Fuller also wanted to know where the wood was.
Stating that if a tree is cut down the property owner can have it.
Administrator Finger told Fuller that Brobst tree service contacted him that
day and said they were coming to cut trees down in the Village, because they
had nothing scheduled that day. Finger told fuller that the tree was a danger
because it was leaning over the road. Finger told Fuller the wood was on
Cucumber Street and she could have it if she wanted. The wood was removed from
the front yard as per process started about four years ago. To protect a mess
in the Village right of way.
Casey Baxley of 245 East Jefferson Street asked council what happened to the
wooden toy solder and train decorations that were always in the Center of town.
Baxley also asked how much the Village was spending in Christmas decorations.

- Administrator Finger read the Village of Jefferson Codified Ordinance section
1026.06 and 129.09 to Council pertaining to trees. Administrator Finger told
council this section provides the questions Tina Fuller had at the last meeting
about a tree being cut down on her property.
 (b)     The Village Arborist shall, and he is hereby directed to, keep all
trees standing upon any public place in the village trimmed so that the
branches of such trees projecting over any public sidewalk or private drive way
or into any public street beyond the curb line shall not conflict with the
public welfare.
When the Village Arborist finds it necessary to order the trimming,
preservation or removal of trees or plants upon private property, as authorized
in §§ 1026.03(c) and 1026.06(c), he shall serve a written order to correct the
dangerous condition upon the owner, lessee, agent, operator, occupant or other
person responsible for its existence.

OFFICIALS
MAYOR
2011 STATE OF THE VILLAGE
2011 has been a year of many challenges for the Nation, State and Village. The
Village of Jefferson is fortunate, in that we have managed to stay ahead of the
game. Due to an exceptional staff, constant vigilance to our budget and
prioritizing, we have accomplished much over the past 12-months.
Here are some of the major accomplishments handled during 2011:
·   Purchased a new backhoe at Street Department.
·   Stockpiled additional clay fill dirt from Dollar General construction site
for the Market Street Project in 2012.
·   Completed:
   o   MC70 paving, and Tree Maintenance.
   o   Community Center roof repair
   o   Village Hall roof and floor repairs
   o   Property Maintenance ordinance and commenced enforcement
   o   Noise ordinance
   o   Culvert replacement on Eagleville Road just past Popular Street using
Village employees
   o   Carpet replacement at the Community Center main meeting room
   o   Wastewater changes required by the EPA renewal of our treatment permit.
·   Completed about 1/3 of the South Sycamore Truck Route project (Phase I)
using Village employees.
·   The Village has entered a three year dispatching contract for $24,500/year
with Middlefield Village effective 10/01/2011.
·   Village Employees continued doing sidewalk repairs which saves us from
hiring outside contractors.
·   Street Department employees working on grant projects have saved the
Village over $41,000.00 on Eagleville Culvert and S. Sycamore grant projects.
Major projects scheduled for 2012 are:
·   Finish the S. Spruce truck route phase I including paving
·   Commence the Pine Street and N. Market Street OPWC culvert replacement
project
·   Continuing Sidewalk replacements, Tree trimming and removal, and resuming
new tree planting.
·   Complete the OPWC project to replace the forced main piping from Elm Street
pump station to the main plant.
Our aim is to keep Jefferson as quaint and appealing as in days of old while
keeping up with the 21st century.
We want to thank our residents for their patience and support at times when
there may have been delays and inconveniences.
We look forward to 2012 with great expectations and enthusiasm.

Ordinance No. 12-o-2891
An Ordinance Adopting Council Rule #40, to limit the disclosure of information
presented in an executive session of council by a council member
Councilman Snyder told council he had concerns if council presented public
records information in executive session would that force a conflict.
Solicitor Lemire told council these are rules for council to follow and public
information is public. Council cannot state public information to be
confidential. Lemire also explained that this rule is already in affect from
last meeting when council did a motion to enact it. This is just to put
paperwork in place to codify the new rule.

Visitor’s Comment
Citizen Ken Fertig of 373 West Cedar Street Jefferson, Ohio asked council if
the Village was going to pay cash for the Old Elementary School Building.
Administrator Finger- stated the Village could pay cash for the 150 thousand
dollars instead of a loan. The Village still has a contract for the 150
thousand dollar in-kind work.
Citizen Robert Lister of 18 East satin Street asked council if an appraisal was
done before the Village went into a contract with the School Board and asked if
so what it appraised for.
Administrator Finger- stated an appraisal was not done. The figures that were
reflected upon were from the appraisal the school board had done.
Citizen Robert Lister of 18 East satin Street questioned council stating that
real-estate is down 32% for houses in the Village since 2008. How could the
Value of the Old Elementary School Building stay the same.
Councilman March- told Lister when the Methodist Church was looking at the
building it appraised for1.1 million.
Cayce Baxley of 245 East Jefferson Street Jefferson asked Council why there was
no action taken regarding the litigation under the Clerk-Treasurer and if the
Village was going to go forward with the purchase of the Old Elementary School
building since the Clerk–Treasurer is not going to certify the referendum
paperwork to the Board Of Elections.
Solicitor Lemire- Explained he received a call from Kyle Smith stating the
Referendum Committee was going to go forward with a law suit. Since a law suite
has been filed against the village there will be no action to any paperwork
regarding the Old Elementary School building. Everything will be put on hold
until a decision is made from the Judge. Lemire did tell council that the
Village does have a contract with the school. The school or the Village at
anytime can back out of the deal if the party chooses.

Visitor’s Comments
Citizen Ken Fertig of 373 West Cedar Street asked Council about the letter that
was send out on December 29, 2011. Fertig asked if the letter was sent out to
all the residents of the Village or just the residents who signed the
referendum paperwork. Fertig also asked why he was not informed when he was
still a member of Council at that time. Also questioned who sent out the
letter, it was not signed by anyone.
Administrator Finger told Fertig that he was asked by the Mayor and Council to
prepare a letter of response to the “Letters to the Editor” that had appeared
in the Papers. Since the response was too long for the papers Mayor and I
decided to mail it to those who had signed the petitions.
Citizen Robert Lister of 18 East Satin Street asked the Administrator about the
appraisals that were done at the Old Elementary School property. Told the
Administrator he keeps getting different answers on the appraisals. Lister also
asked how much the Village Of Jefferson paid for appraisals. Who did the
appraisals, when they were done and what the cost was. Lister also told council
that per the Ohio Revised Code section 501.04. three appraisals must be done
and they must be disinterested appraisers. Lister also questioned if the
Village had been planning on buying the school since 2008. Reason being an
appraisal was done in April of 2008.
Administrator Finger explained that the appraisals were done for the purpose of
purchasing the Old Elementary playground.
Councilman March explained to Lister that in 2008 the appraisal was done for
one parcel. Later the parcel was split off.
Citizen Jim Donathan of 337 Susan Drive asked council who was the engineer that
designed the plans for the addition for the new section of the Police
Department and what was the cost.
Administrator Finger told Donathan at first we had an engineer from Rock Creek
and found out he was not a certified engineer. The draftsman was reprimanded by
the State Of Ohio Architectural Review Board so the Village switched to Smolen
Engineering.
Administrator Finger told Donathan that it was suggested by Council and the
Mayor to look at buying the Old Elementary School as an alternative to building
the addition. This was after we received the plans back and found out the cost
for a 960 square foot addition. With the addition we would lose parking space
also.
Citizen Jim Donathan of 337 Susan Drive told council that the Village and the
School need to protect all the tax payers of Jefferson Village. The taxpayers
have already paid out their tax money for the Old School Building once and
should not have to pay for it again. Donathan also questioned how the Village
Street Department employees are going to keep up with their work if we are
going to contract $150,000 worth of work with the School. Donathan also
questioned why we asked residents to help clean out Catch Basins and if the
Post Office was still interested in buying the Old Elementary School.
Administrator Finger explained that we were asking the residents to help keep
the grass and leaves clear of the drains.
Mayor Maloney told Donathan that she did talk with the post office and they are
tied into a lease. Also explained when the research was done for the addition
for the Police Department, the cost of $150,000 and $150,000 worth of in-kind
work was a better option for the space that is going to be gained.
Citizen Tina Fuller told Council the letter that was written to the citizens
that signed the referendum paperwork, was unprofessional and how could council
condone such action. The letter had bullying actions and name calling. Fuller
also asked why not every Councilperson knew about the letter. Fuller suggested
that the Council and village should look at everything involved with the
Building. Cost analysis and studies should have been done.
Jefferson Township resident Steve Magda told Council that they are supposed to
honor the residents Constitutional rights and the State of Ohio Constitution.
The Citizens of the Village Of Jefferson should be allowed to vote on the Old
School Building and other items that involve taxpayer’s money. The Old School
Building should be put on the ballot November 8, 2012 and let them choose.
These issues could go all the way to the Supreme Court if not. Council is to
protect the citizens of the Village not deny them there rights.
Solicitor Lemire stated that the Village Council has no role in certifying the
referendum petitions. The Clerk Treasurer is mandated by the Ohio Revised Code.
The petitions are in the hands of the Clerk Treasurer. In consulting with the
Clerk Treasurer on the referendum process, it was found that one step was not
followed by the referendum committee and this question is now going thru the
legal process.
Citizen Juanita Adkins of 165 West Satin Street #18 told Council that the
resident who signed the referendum petition were called ignorant. The
information put in the letter was judgmental and incorrect, and the resident
that signed the petition were not forced or given the wrong information.
Citizen Cayce Baxley of 245 East Jefferson Street asked why the letter was not
signed by the Village council. Stated the information in the letter was wrong.
Why residents that signed the letter were contacted and asked why they signed
it. That it is a persons’ constitutional right to sign a petition if they want
to.

Public Hearing
Administrator Fing    Administrator Finger explained to council that there will
be two steps to the new Planned Unit Development. We will have three readings
of the new Ordinance and thirty days for the Ordinance to become official. The
Administrator cannot issue a permit without each plan being approved by both
the Planning Commission and Council. The Developers will then have to bring new
development plans to the Planning Commission. The Planning Commission will have
to approve the new development plans for the site plan and layout of the
development. A specific Ordinance will come from the Planning Commission to
Council for approval. The Village will then have to follow the same process as
they did with the readings of the first Ordinance.
Councilwoman Brabender asked Administrator Finger if there was any age
preference to who could move into the new duplexes.
Administrator Finger explained to council the duplexes will be three bedrooms
and triplexes two bedrooms. Any restrictions and rules will be part of the
second step for approval of a specific plan.
Randy Dearing explained to Council that the development will be set up like a
condo community with duplexes that have garages instead of apartment complexes
that do not have garages.
Administrator Finger explained that in the existing Planned Unit Development
there is not cluster housing.
Councilman Diehl questioned if all the electrical, sewer and gas services will
have to be inspected by the Village. Who will be responsible for the permits
and will there be separate services.
Administrator Finger explained that the developers will be responsible in
having to apply for all Zoning, building and other required permits. They will
have to meet all codes involved with the development.
Motion by Councilman Diehl to go out of the Public Hearing at 7:45 p.m. and
return back to regular session.
2nd
Roll: All yea, motion carried.
