Ordinance No. 12-O-2891
An Ordinance Adopting Council Rule #40, to limit the disclosure of information
presented in an executive session of council by a council member
Motion by Councilperson Hoyson adopt Ordinance No. 12-0-2891
2nd Roll: All yea, motion carried.
Councilperson Diehl gave his take as a councilperson, on the purchase of the
school property.
Comments on the School Property Purchase
During the budget process in December 2009, a discussion was held regarding the
expansion of the police department. The finance committee and the police
department agreed that it was not fiscally prudent to pursue an expansion at
that time due to the state of the economy.
This request was made for the following reasons:
·   The current facilities do not provide adequate facilities to meet ORC
2901.13 requirements for the collection and retention of evidence.
·   The current facilities require that suspect be interviewed at the kitchen
table, also used by the employees for breaks and meals.
·   The current facilities do not meet the requirements of SB77, 128th
legislature regarding interviewing and detaining suspects
During the budget process in December 2010, the request was again made to the
finance committee to pursue an expansion on the police station. The finance
committee agreed with the need to pursue the expansion and felt the financial
position of the Village was such that the cost could be supported. The
committee advised the department to procure an estimate for the expansion.
After consulting with Smolen engineering, the expansion was estimated at
$150,000, and would provide an additional 960 square feet. This would provide
the necessary space to the police department, but is also a significant cost to
pay for limited space. Due to the location of the existing station, no further
expansion would be possible in the future.
Given the cost and the limited space gained, council and the administration
felt that this was not an ideal solution.
The concept of pursuing the available school property was presented as an
alternative and council agreed to allow the administrator to pursue
negotiations with the school.
After negotiations with the school, the best possible bid accepted was $150,000
cash and $150,000 in kind services. Lower offers were presented and denied by
the school. Concern was expressed in executive session that no annual cap was
placed on the in kind services, therefore a $25,000 cap was placed on the bid,
essentially providing a no interest loan from the school to the village for a
minimum of 6 years.
After the inspection report was received, a bid was obtained from a reputable
local contractor to determine costs of repairing all deficiencies noted in the
inspection report. This not to exceed bid was $25,000.
Given the total cost of $325,000, $150,000 of which was not in cash and could
be spread over a minimum of 6 years as, the majority of council felt that this
was the preferred alternative to meet the needs of the police station
expansion. Additionally, the building and property offered a full commercial
kitchen and would complete the park space on Market St. It was also recognized
that the $25,000 /year would not be entirely in cash or labor, and therefore
not burden the village with excessive cost or labor requirements.
For me, the facts that led me to support the decision are as follows:
·   $325,000 for a 12,000 square foot commercial building on 4 acres of village
property is more than reasonable. It was also the minimum that would be
accepted by the school.
·   Council and the administration had agreed to pursue the expansion of the
police station and therefore, money will be spent to meet the state
requirements. Given the option of spending $150,000 on the 960 sqft expansion
or $175,000 with the additional $150,000 spread over time, I feel the school
building purchase was a better alternative.
·   Given that the building was purchased by taxpayers in Jefferson Village,
Jefferson Township, Lenox, Rock Creek, Sheffield, and Dorset, we are “buying
out” their portion of the property. The money remains in the public domain and
I hold the highest expectation of the school that they will use our money
responsibility.
·   Although no negotiations can be held until the village owns the building,
interested parties have approached the village regarding leasing the other half
of the building. This provides a potential income stream that would help cover
the cost of the building.
·   The building provides the needed space for the police, and additionally
provides a full commercial kitchen and additional space for other use.
·   The land expands and connects two existing parks, adding to a highly used
park space and one of the nice features of the village.
Visitor’s Comments (five minute limit per council rule # 13)
Citizen E. Pengel of 128 Center Street asks Council why the Recreation Center
and Senior Center were down so much for the year 2011 and why are we buying a
new Senior Van if the Village has lost the Senior Transportation Grant.
Administrator Finger told the residents the Recreation Center took a strong hit
when the economy started to go bad, Residents had to choose to pay bills
instead of taking a program at the Recreation Center. The Village lost the
County Senior Levy Transportation Grant and programs are down. The Village is
buying a new Senior Van because we still have the District X1 Grant which
provides transportation within the limits of the Village of Jefferson. The New
Senior Van will not be wheel chair assessable but we will keep the old Van for
residents who are in wheel chairs.
Jefferson Township resident Steve Magda asked Council if all the commercial
equipment was included with the purchase of the Old elementary School.
Councilman Diehl told the residents that all the commercial equipment in the
cafeteria section was included but the old cabinets and lunch tables were not
included. The school still has equipment to take out.
Jefferson Township resident Steve Magda asked Council how could the Police
Department and the children that would be in our park co-exist with criminals
being interrogated at the Police Department.
Mayor Maloney told the residents that the Police Department is right across
from the playground now and we interrogate criminals now. Maloney also told the
residents if we added on to the Police Department we have now we would lose
half dozen parking spaces. That is one of the reasons why Council in the
discussion of buying the Old Elementary School Building thought it was more
suitable along with the space that would be gained instead of building on to
the existing Building.
Citizen Richard Hummel of 13 East Cedar Street Apt # 8 asked Council if the
Court Case with the referendum was resolved. And if there was still a
restraining order preventing the Clerk treasurer and Administrator to go
forward with the contract with the school. Hummel also asked what cost will
accrue to move over to the Old School Building.
Administrator Finger told the residents we have an estimate from a local
contractor for $25, 000.00 dollars to repair all deficiencies. A lot of the
revisions will be done by the Police Department and we found out that the phone
system will be no cost to the Village.
Solicitor Lemire told the residents that the court case with the referendum was
still in process. As the Solicitor for the Village I presented all information
that the judge asked the defendants to provide. We are still waiting on the
referendums Committees lawyer to respond back with what Judge Mackey asked of
both parties. The main issue is the Clerks interpretation and the Referendum
Committees interpretation of the law. The judge will make a decision of the
interpretation for us.
Citizen Richard Hummel of 13 East Cedar Street Apt # 8 told Council that he is
resigning for the Income Tax Board of Review. He presented his letter to the
Clerk Treasurer.

Executive Session.

Service Dept  
·   Street Department is working on cold patching pot holes, berm
reconditioning, and other street repairs.
·   Brobst removed 20 dead or damaged trees this week. Stump removal is not
planned yet. This will complete major tree removal until we have either frozen
ground or dry hard ground.
·   Our Street Department employees will continue to trim young/new trees as
weather permits.
·   We have received the tractor mounted broom and rake that were approved for
purchase. We were able to purchase a brand new rake on E Bay for $4,000 less
than the one through the dealer network. Another good money saving purchase!
·   The ordinance to purchase the Durapatcher street repair machine is in
Council packet. It will be ordered as soon as the approval is in place.
Fire Dept. /Police Department
·   Village had not received a bid to purchase the surplus #402 fire truck by
the time I wrote this report. If there are no bids meeting the minimum the
truck will be re-advertised and sold to the highest bidder without a reserve.
RecreationDepartment
·   The ordinance to approve the purchase of a new shuttle bus for the Seniors
and Community Center that is available through State purchasing for $47,000 is
in council packet. By purchasing through the State program, we will not have to
seek our own bids.
·   Christina Blair’s broken ankle is mending nicely. She is in a walking boot
and much more mobile.
·   Repairs to ceiling tiles and floor tiles are in progress as part of general
maintenance at the center.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Plant is operating under normal conditions with no exceptions to report.
·   The Village has reapplied to EPA for permits for the forced main
replacement project at the wastewater plant. We can bid this project as soon as
permits are issued.
Other Items:
   None
Administrator Finger told Council that Brobst is in town removing dead wood out
of trees and will continue with the tree trimming when the weather brakes.

Visitor’s Comments (five minute limit per council rule #13)   
Jefferson Township resident Steve Magda asked Solicitor Lemire if the Ordinance
that Council passed regarding executive session is in compliance with the
Sunshine Laws.
Solicitor Lemire told Mr. Magda the Council passed the Ordinance for Council
Rules to be stricter on what information is given out in executive session and
to make sure it is not given out to the public for disclosure. Council has not
violated any Sunshine Laws. They are being stricter.
Jefferson Township resident Steve Magda asked Solicitor Lemire if council is
following the open meetings act when they go into executive session.
Solicitor Lemire told Mr. Magda the Council is in compliance with the open
meeting act regarding going into executive session and in his opinion they are
not abusing the law. To go into executitive session there must be certain
topics. Purchase of property, pending or imminent litigation, personnel issues
or real estate contracts.
Jefferson Township resident Steve Magda also told Council that he is opening an
information center in the Village of Jefferson to help out residents when they
need it.

Service Dept
·   Street Department is cleaning streets with the Geneva on the Lake street
sweeper. We provide winter inside storage in exchange for being able to use it
before the strip opens and after it closes.
·   Crews are installing drain tiles to close in several open ditches. Dorset @
S. Market, E. Erie @ S. Sycamore, Westview @ W. Satin.
·   Brobst removed dead wood from Village shade trees on Chestnut, Jefferson,
and Elm streets.
·   There are a lot more trees that need trimming to prevent dead wood from
falling and causing damage.
·   I have recommended adding an additional $4,000 to the next appropriation
change to make sure we can deal with problem trees. This change will increase
the line item back to $12,000 which is what we spent last year.
·   Our Street Department employees have stopped trimming young/new trees until
they go dormant at the end of the year.
·   We are working to get loose ends wrapped up before we resume S. Sycamore
truck route phase 1 and the Market Street Culvert replacement.
Fire Dept. /Police Department
·   Village will re-advertise the 1988 fire truck and sell to the highest
bidder without a reserve.

·   The revised ordinance to purchase a new shuttle bus for the seniors and
Community Center reflects the addition of the wheel chair lift as requested by
Council. Price changes from $47,420.00 to $50,165.00. By purchasing through the
State program, we will not have to seek our own bids.
·   Street Department constructed a new storage area in the back of the
Community Center to enable the police department to move items currently in
storage in another area of the Community Center.
·   By the Police moving within the building the current storage area can be
opened up to allow the free weight area to expand.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Plant is operating under normal conditions with no exceptions to report.
·   The Village has reapplied to EPA for permits for the forced main
replacement project at the wastewater plant. We can bid this project as soon as
permits are issued. Note: Still waiting for the new permit!

Visitor’s Comments (five minute limit per council rule #13)   
Citizen Cayce Baxley of 245 East Jefferson Street said she read in the paper
last week that the Village is going to use the lottery money to purchase a new
Duropatch Machine and new Senior Van. Has the Village collected the all the
money yet? There is only one lottery winner that is a resident of the Village.
The other winners are non residents. What about the other Villages and Cities
the winners live in, they are going to want their money also.
Solicitor Lemire told Council and the residents that in the Village Ordinance
we can collect the money. The issue is a lack of clarity at the state law and
the legal law is not clear who has the precedence in the collection of the
lottery money. The Village is not spending the lottery money until we have
looked into the legalities further.
Citizen Jim Donathan of 337 Susan Drive asked Administrator Finger if the
Village was going to do any of the sidewalks on Satin Street from Chestnut
Street to Popular Street. Donathan told Council that he has seen allot of kids
walking on the roads when they walk to school. The sidewalks are not used that
much in the Winter thru Spring, the sidewalks do need replaced. Donathan asked
the Administrator if the Village was looking at grant to replace them and also
asked if we were going to have them four feet wide.
Mayor Maloney told Donathan that the Village has looked into the Safe Routes to
School. But there will be still a cost to the Village if we did receive the
grant, reason being the grant is only a fifty percent Village and fifty percent
grant.
Administrator Finger told Donathan that it is the responsibility of the home
owner to keep up the sidewalks. The only cost to the home owner if sidewalk is
replaced in front of their house is the cement. The Village absorbs the rest.
Citizen Phil Pawlowski of 22 East Walnut Street asked Council if the purchase
of the Old Elementary School property is going forward and how is the Village
going to pay for the purchase of the building.
Mayor Maloney told Pawlowski that there is still litigation going on with the
purchase of the Old Elementary School property so the purchase is on hold. The
Village was in the process of financing the building until the litigation on
the purchase came up.

Service Dept.  
·   Street Department will resume S. Sycamore truck route phase 1 road
rebuilding Monday, March 19. We will be able to maintain traffic initially.
·   S. Sycamore Street will have to be closed for several weeks after all the
drainage work is complete to enable us to rebuild the roadbed.
·   We will not pave the surface of S. Sycamore Street until fall. This will
allow truck traffic to further compact the roadbed before paving in the fall.
·   Crews are redressing road intersections where trucks have missed the road
and tracked up the tree lawns.
·   We have resumed brush pick up at curbside and will continue on the first of
each month.
·   Residents should mark Saturday, May 5th, on their calendars as the
scheduled day for village wide curbside rubbish removal. More reminders to
come!
Fire Dept. /Police Department
·   The new Peirce fire truck has been ordered.
·   The Fire Department looked at the truck on state bid and determined that
with the additional equipment specified originally, the state Bid price with
options would raise up comparable to the Peirce pricing.
RecreationDepartment
·   The Community Center has been doing spring house cleaning to rid the
building of unused items. The items will be for sale at the Spring rummage sale
scheduled for Saturday, April 21, between 9:00 AM and 2:00 PM.
·   Spring Craft Show will take place on Saturday, March 24, between 9:00 AM
and 3:00 PM.
·   The Police department relocated stored material within the building and the
free weight area has been expanded to accommodate a relocation of equipment.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Plant is operating under normal conditions with no exceptions to report.
·   The Village has reapplied to EPA for permits for the forced main
replacement project at the wastewater plant. We can bid this project as soon as
permits are issued. Note: Still waiting for the new permit!

Service Dept.
·   S. Sycamore Street was closed March 26 and will remain closed for several
weeks.
·   Street Department continues with S. Sycamore truck route phase 1 road
rebuilding without delays and according to the design plans.
·   We will not pave the surface of S. Sycamore Street until fall. This will
allow truck traffic to further compact the roadbed before paving in the fall.
·   We have resumed brush pick up at curbside and will continue on the first of
each month.
·   Residents should mark Saturday, May 5th, on their calendars as the
scheduled day for village wide curbside rubbish removal. More reminders to
come!
   ·   Smolen Engineering, Curt Stone and I met with the Buffalo District Army
Corp. of Engineers to resolve permit issues regarding the Market Street Culvert
replacement. Since we have to disturb the stream flowing in the valley there
are several open issues:
   ·   Mitigation of wetlands
   ·   Stream bank improvements including planting trees and shrubs to shade
the stream, adding more deep holes, and adding rapids.
   ·   As soon as I receive the published report we can discuss it in committee
or full Council.
   ·   The absolute earliest we can begin any work will be the beginning of
June almost six weeks later than we had hoped.
Fire Dept. /Police Department
·   The new fire truck is on order with delivery expected in 2013.
Recreation Department:  
None
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Plant is operating under normal conditions with no exceptions to report.
·   The Village has received the EPA permit for the forced main replacement
project at the wastewater plant.
·   We are preparing bid documents for this project and will begin as soon as
practical.

Service Dept.  
·   S. Sycamore Street was reopened to through traffic on May 4, 2012.
·   The road bed is excellent and packed solid enough to allow paving ASAP.
Legal notices are posted and advertised to enable bid opening on May 23rd at
noon.
·   Also included in the paving bid package are two optional street sections
(W. Walnut; Chestnut to Elm and Elm to Popular) Engineers estimate shows we
should be able to do all streets in the bid within our budgeted amount. If bids
are too high we can pick and choose options without having to re-advertise or
rebid the job.
·   I will comment at the council meeting on the success of the village wide
curbside rubbish removal.  
·   We have not received the published report from Army Corp of Engineers on
the Market Street Project.
·   As the EPA and Army Corp of Engineers permits delay construction we will
have to reset a timeline to be sure we can complete construction in the 2012
season.
Fire Dept. /Police Department
·   We have revised the budget to remove any money allocated for the School
purchase until the voter referendum is completed.
RecreationDepartment
·   During the budget work sessions we had discussed purchasing a new Senior
Van and financing the purchase price. The second scenario was to buy the Van
and pay cash. The revised appropriations ordinance to be discussed at the
finance meeting May 7th contains the dollars to purchase the new Van and
finance the amount. We are asking Council (if they agree with the new
appropriation ordinance) to bring the ordinance to purchase the Van off the
table and pass it.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Plant is operating under normal conditions with no exceptions to report.
·   We are still waiting for new bid documents for this project and will begin
as soon as practical.

   None

Service Dept.  
·   S. Sycamore Street was reopened to through traffic on May 4, 2012.
·   The road bed has no deflection and has proved to be packed solid enough to
allow paving ASAP.
·   Paving bid opening will be on May 23rd at noon.
·   We have not received the published report from Army Corp of Engineers on
the Market Street Project.
·   As the EPA and Army Corp of Engineers permits delay construction we will
have to reset a timeline to be sure we can complete construction in the 2012
season.
·   Street Department has been replacing storm water culverts, cold patching
streets, and doing final restoration to various Village Tree Lawn areas.
Fire Dept. /Police Department
·   We will allow the Memorial Day parade to travel on the same route as past
years Jefferson to North Market Street and to the Cemetery.
·   The delay in the Market Street Project allows us to maintain the former
route.
RecreationDepartment
·   The new van financing interest rate will be 3.5% from Andover Bank.
·   The van can be ordered as soon as the State of Ohio reissues the new State
Purchasing contracts.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   Plant is operating under normal conditions with no exceptions to report.
·   We have received all the permits and bid documents for the forced main
replacement project.
·   Bid opening is scheduled for May 31, at Noon.

Building and Lands
Councilman Snyder asked the solicitor questions concerning the Woodlands Of
Jefferson Ordinance. Snyder questioned under exhibit A the Deed restrictions
which states the deed could not be further subdivided. Snyder also questioned
the road was accepted in 2005 will there be any problems with the Village
accepting it with a new name.
Solicitor Lemire told Snyder that the Deed restrictions are for the person that
buys into the condominium. The Ordinance is set up this way to preserve the
original Pud Ordinance.
Solicitor Lemire told Snyder that the Village can accept a road more than once.
What is worded on the Platt is what the Village is going to go with. The Platt
for the property the Woodlands Of Jefferson is correct.

Service Dept.  
∙   S. Sycamore Street Phase I paving and West Walnut Street paving has been
completed.
∙   S. Sycamore Street Phase II grant for $199,900 and 0% loan for $115,900 was
approved by OPWC and contracts signed. Design work will take place in 2013.
∙   The County and Village will delay the construction work for the Market
Street Project until 2013.
∙   EPA and Army Corp of Engineers fees and final documents are paid and
complete. The Construction delay will allow time for the permits to be issued
or problems resolved.
∙   I have requested a motion to authorize me to advertise for bids to pave W.
Satin Street between S. Chestnut and S. Popular utilizing the money that was
appropriated for the Market Street Project.
∙   Street Department has started base repairs to West Satin Street in
anticipation of future paving. A quote from Koski Construction was $38,388. A
quote from Pro Paving was $14,400. A purchase order has been issued to Pro
Paving for the repairs.
∙   Stump grinding was completed with a few missed ones to be picked up in the
future.
∙   Another batch of dead trees will have to be removed before the end of
Summer.
∙   Residents are asked to help water the new trees under 3 inched in diameter
to make sure we do not have high mortality from drought.
Fire Dept. /Police Department
∙   A recommendation to hire for the Police Secretary position is before
Council.
Recreation Department
∙   The new van approved for purchase has been ordered. Bond paperwork required
by the bank is in your packet and on the agenda.
∙   AA meetings have relocated from the Community Center to a local church.
∙   We have received several applications for the Van driver position and will
interview the top three applicants.
∙   New Security Cameras have been installed and are operational at the Center.
There is some fine tuning yet to be completed before we declare the project
complete.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
∙   Easton Leasing Inc. contract is in place for the forced main replacement.
Project will start as soon as the ordered material arrives.
∙   Mark Reighard slipped on the dump truck step and fell. He dislocated his
shoulder and sustained a fracture. Medical tests are scheduled to determine the
extent of his injuries and appropriate future treatment. He has continued
working under a light duty restriction until his doctors determine what needs
to be done.

Visitor’s Comments (five minute limit per council rule # 13 )
Citizen Ken Fertig of 373 West Cedar Street talked to Council about the June
22, 2012 incident at the old Elementary School. Has Asked Council who
authorized the Village Employees to do the clean-up was it the Administrator.
Fertig also questioned did the Village have a contract prior to the clean-up
with the School Board. Fertig asked the Solicitor if he was asked by the Mayor
or Administrator for his opinion. Fertig told Council the $162.80 does not
cover all the cost for the two Street Department employees. What about workers
compensation, medical, and PERS
Mayor Maloney told Fertig Administration authorized the employees to clean-up
the Old Elementary School for Safety Services Day to show residents of the
Village what the plan for the building are if the voters approve the
referendum.
Solicitor Lemire told Fertig that he did not give the Village any opinion on
whether the Village employees should clean-up the building.
Administrator Finger told Fertig that the Village did not have a contract with
the School to clean-up the building.
Citizen Diana Dickson Sowry of 61 West Satin Street asked Council who
authorized at the School Board authorized the Village employees to clean the
Old Elementary School Building. There is nothing in the minutes or a contract
for the Village to be in the School Building. Sowry also asked when the
donation was made to the Village of 162.80 did the Village write a receipt with
the person’s name on it Did the person who made the donation put a request in
to pay the services.
Mayor Maloney told Sowry that the Assistant Chief of Police talked with the
School and made arrangement for the Village to go into the Building to clean-up
and have it open for the Safety Services Days.
Clerk Treasurer Fisher told Sowry that the name of the person was not put on
the receipt because it was a cashier’s check from a bank. If the person had
written a check with their name on it. Then their name would be in the computer
system.
Citizen E Pengel of 128 Center Street asked Council why does the Village not
promote or publish the free produce being given out at the Recreation Center.
Is it a formal program set up the help the citizens.
Administrator Finger told Pengel that he did not know anything of a program for
free produce being given out at the Recreation Center. He told her that he
would tomorrow ask at the Recreation Department and let her know.
Citizen Fuller of 145 South Elm Street asked Council who is covering the Police
when they are volunteering for activities. Fuller also asked the Council that
home owners and residents of the Village are struggling to make ends with now.
Maybe Council should think about it and take it off the ballot in November.
Solicitor Lemire told Fuller that as a rule a policeman is never off duty. They
are on call twenty four seven. They are covered thru the Village at all times
even if they are not in the State of Ohio and act as a patrolman. Lemire also
told Fuller that misuse of public funds in general the courts talks of an
expenditure of public funds not services provided.
Citizen Juanita Adkins why did the council talk with the School Board not to
tear down all of the Old Elementary School Building.
Administrator Finger told Adkins that the Council did not discuss any part of
saving the Building with the School board.

is complete.

∙   Dead tree removal (about 16 trees) is scheduled September 7 th . Trees are
marked with a yellow or orange ribbon. Stump grinding will occur at the same
time.
∙   The Village and Ashtabula County line painting crews have been repainting
all lines within the village. The final phase will be to add thermal tape lines
and arrows to the 46 & 307 intersection.
∙   Sidewalk replacement is continuing with the focus being on W. Jefferson and
W. Walnut streets.
∙   ( No pricing information yet.) Curt’s pickup truck has been having
reliability problems and high repair costs. We are seeking pricing to purchase
a new truck under State Purchase pricing prior to snowfall. Payment can be
delayed until 2013 budget appropriations occur according to Patty.
∙   Electric service has been installed at central park. The community bulletin
sign will now be lighted and power outlets are available in the park area along
E. Jefferson Street.

Middlefield’s contract termination.
∙   We advertised the surplus fire truck and received three bids. I recommend
that the Village accept John Wayman’s high bid.

∙   The new van approved for purchase has arrived and is in service. Lettering
will be scheduled ASAP.

∙   Our Senior Coordinator Christina Blair has resigned to seek full time
employment.
∙   Ashley Febel has given two weeks’ notice that she will be resigning. She
has been offered a position with more hours of work.

∙   The forced main replacement is expected to be complete by September 7 th .

Richard Hummel of 113 East Cedar Street talked to Council about the finding a
new Senior Coordinator for the Recreation Department. He suggested that the
Village should search for someone that will be devoted to the Seniors and has
an interest in the Seniors that come to the Recreation Department.
Richard Hummel of 113 East Cedar Street also asked Council about a letter he
received from NOPEC regarding the electric rates.
Administrator Finger told Hummel that NOPEC rates are about 7.02 and is a fixed
rate. Finger also told everyone that the best rate out there right now is a
company called American Electric and Power from Columbus the rate is 5.90.
Jim Donathon of 337 Susan Drive representing the covered Bridge Committee told
Council that the Covered Bridge Festival is October 13 th and 14 2012 Saturday
and Sunday. Donathon requested to Council for the closing of Poplar Street.
Donathon also told Council that this would be the 29 annual festival. This year
some the hours for the Festival will be extended till seven p.m. There will be
more kid’s rides. The festival Committee this year brought back the queen for
the Festival. The queen from 1987 will be crowning the new queen.

September 27, 2012
VILLAGE OF JEFFERSON
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING
Meeting called to order by Mayor Maloney
Pledge of Allegiance
Moment of Silence
Motion by Councilman Damon to appoint Councilman Hoyson as acting Clerk
Treasurer in the Absence of Clerk Treasurer Fisher.
2 nd        
Roll: All yea, motion carried
Roll Call of Council:
March Brabender Damon Diehl-Absent Snyder Hoyson
Also present:  Chief Febel, Assistant Chief Wassie and Stephanie Wessell
Gazette.
Mayor Maloney explained to Council that the Special Council Meeting was to
discuss the Dispatching contract for the Village of Jefferson.
Maloney explained to Council that the Village of Jefferson was looking at
contracts with the City Of Ashtabula and the Ashtabula County Commissioners.
Three years ago the Commissioner sent a letter stating they were going to
increase the Dispatch fees to for the Village the increase would have been
double what the Village was paying at that time. The action of the Commissioner
let to Communities scrambling to find a dispatch service for their
municipality. The Communities worked together and found Middlefield to do the
Dispatch for Village of Roaming Shores, Village Of Andover, Village of Orwell
and the Village Of Jefferson.
Maloney Told Council that the Village Of Middlefield contacted the Villages
that they have been doing the dispatching for the past few years stating that
they were going to stop the dispatching for the Communities in the contract
reason being that the Geauga County Commissioner were going to do there
dispatching for free.
Chief Febel and Assistant Chief Wassie talked with the City of Ashtabula and
Frank Snyder talked with the Sheriff. Wassie explained the pros and cons to why
the Villages should go with the City Of Ashtabula.
The County Commissioner’s did send a contract to the Villages offering their
dispatching fees. All the Municipalities had the same concern to what had
happened in the past. If the County cuts their budget . the Count would double
the fees as they did in the past.
Council was concerned that they fee was higher than the Commissioners presented
to the Villages.
Wassie told Council his concerns that he had with the sheriffs and what had
happened in the past . Wassie one of the biggest concerns the Village of
Jefferson had with the Sheriff’s department was the 911 calls the Sheriff’s
Department monitored them and only told the Village Police Department the ones
they felt necessary. Also budget cut were done in the County and they put the
expenses for their services back onto small municipalities.
Wassie also explained that he felt the services would be much better . The cost
for the Village of Jefferson would be five thousand dollars total for
dispatching fees for November and December. January 1 thru December 31 2013 the
fees would be thirty thousand dollars.
Motion by Councilman Hoyson for the First Reading of Ordinance No 12-O- 2914
2nd
Roll Call: Damon yea, Snyder no, Hoyson yea, March yea, Brabender yea, motion
passed.
First Reading Of Ordinance 12-O-2914
An Ordinance Authorizing the Jefferson Village Administrator and Clerk/
Treasurer to sign a contract with the City of Ashtabula, Ashtabula, Ohio, and
Declaring an Emergency.
Motion by Councilperson Diehl to Suspend Council Rules on Ordinance No. 12-O-
2918
2nd
Roll Call: Damon yea, Snyder no, Hoyson yea, March no, Brabender yea, motion
did not pass.

Culvert
 
Service Dept.  
∙   Grant for the Durapatch Machine was denied! We have been advised to revise
our request and reapply.
∙   Our Bureau of Workman’s Comp. Reps. are following up with the Commission to
see where we should improve our request and they will advise me.
∙   No EPA permit issued yet for Market Street .
∙   Army Corp of Engineers has not issued our provisional permit for Market
Street culvert replacement.
∙   The Village had one tree blow down that took out power to E. Satin Street.
This tree was next to one that had been marked for removal. The tree that was
marked for removal is still standing. It’s hard to tell what is going on
underground.
∙   Brobst Tree Service will reschedule Village tree removal after they have
finished storm clean up.
∙   The new waterline project for Willis Ave has increased in scope.
∙   Aqua Ohio has scheduled to replace the 4 inch lines on Willis, Uselma, N.
Elm and W. Walnut streets with 8 inch lines.
∙   They will also be changing waterlines on W. Ashtabula Street from a 4 inch
to an 8 inch line.
∙   The 8 inch lines will help water flow in this entire area. The Fire
Department will also have a greater firefighting water source.
Fire Dept. /Police Department
∙   The change over from Middlefield dispatching to Ash. City took place on
October 31 st as planned.
∙   I have heard of no problems with the switch over, and will keep listening
for feedback.
∙   The election tomorrow November 6 th will determine how the Village proceeds
with securing more office space for the Police Department.
Recreation Department
∙   We are asking Council to accept the donation of a professional Octane
elliptical fitness machine from John Mantell.
∙   Mr. Mantell paid $3,600.00 a few years ago but it was gathering dust
lately.
∙   The machine type is one that receives high usage and is a welcomed addition
to the Community Center.
∙   After acceptance of this donation it will be added to the inventory list
and a thank you note will be sent to Mr. Mantell.
∙   Halloween party was well attended.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
∙   Plant operations are stressed due to the high rainfall. We had one out flow
of partially treated water that was reported to Ohio EPA.
∙   Monday night and Tuesday we operated the plant on the backup generator to
prevent damage to pump motors from the brown outs (low voltage periods) we were
experiencing. There were no problems with everything operating as planned.
Other Items:
Administrator Finger told Council that Aqua Ohio has schedules to replace 4
inch lines on Willis, Uselma. N. Elm and W. Walnut Streets with 8 inch lines.
This project will take all winter. There will be two road cuts on West Walnut
Street.
Administrator Finger told Council that the Grant for the Dura Patch machine was
denied. The Village is reapplying. The usage for the machine is more than what
was put on the ordinal application. The Village will know within the next three
weeks if we have been approved for the Grant with the changes.

     Star Ohio Report
Total Cash available to the Village of Jefferson with the Lotto money is.
$1,774,161.09
In the Clerk/Treasurer’s Report Fisher informed Council that the Income Tax
Department is up 5.1% compared to last year, we have in the Village Escrow
Account $818,231.70 for the Income Tax Department in Lottery money.
Wastewater Sewer Collections are up 3.1% compared to last year, Recreation 204
is up .01% compared to last year and Senior 205 is down 23.5% compared to last
year.
Clerk Treasurer Fisher told Council that the Ordinance to move forward in the
process of refinancing the Village Recreation Bond is in the Council packet.
This Ordinance has emergency wording so the refinancing can be done by December
1, 2012. With the refinancing of the Recreation Bond the savings will be about
10% a year, which is about ten thousand dollars a year thru the life of the
Bond. The ending date for the new Bond will be the same as the Original Bond.

Culvert
 
Service Dept.  
∙   I have revised our grant request for the Durapatch Machine. We should have
an answer on our revised request by the middle of December.
∙   Our E. Jefferson Street culvert replacement project is the number one rated
job to be funded in District 4 for OPWC funding.
∙   I was recommended to serve a three year term as a Small Government
Representative at the State of Ohio’s Small Government Board. This appointment
gives us a voice in the rules making body of OPWC at the State Level. Final
approval will occur in March of 2013 and require me to attend three or four
meetings each year in Columbus.
∙   We received correspondence from Ohio EPA regarding the Market Street
Project. They have determined that this is a low impact project and only
requires the Village to post notice in local papers for one day. Monday,
November 19 th, the legal notice will be published in the Star Beacon. Once we
send a copy of the published notice OEPA can proceed with issuing the permit.
∙   WE ARE GETTING CLOSE!
∙   Once OEPA finishes their permit Army Corp of Engineers will be able to
issue their permit.
∙   The waterline replacement project for Willis, Uselma, N. Elm, and W. Walnut
streets is progressing nicely. I have received no complaints.
∙   Christmas Decorations are nearly all in place.
∙   Curt Informed the Mayor and I that his new truck has been delivered to the
Dealer and he should have it in service the week after Thanksgiving.
Fire Dept. /Police Department:
∙   The change over from Middlefield dispatching to Ash. City has been working
with no major problems.
∙   911 Calls to Jefferson have been improved greatly. Jefferson officers now
have access to the call on their patrol car computer and do not have to rely on
just phone contact.
∙   As reported by the news agencies, the Village residents have approved the
purchase of the former Elementary School Property. The Village is taking no
action until after the final vote is certified by the Board of Elections on
November 27 th , 2012.
Recreation Department:
∙   Staffing levels are at full strength again.
∙   Jefferson certified preschool is seeking additional State certification
which will allow us to receive a $1,500 yearly grant for program expenses and
allow us to receive additional funding money to purchase program supplies.
∙   Reverse Raffle is a sellout. (More to report after the event.)
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
∙   Plant operations have returned to normal.
∙   Plant is working on additional OEPA requirements for a storm water plan.
∙   The Class one operators, Keith and Mark, are both working to get their
Class two certification. If neither can pass the certification, one will have
to be laid off and a new class two operator hired for the plant to meet the
operational permit requirements.
Other Items:

Mayor
State of The Village 2012
I am pleased to report that the village is in good financial standing. The
departments, administration and council have been diligent in their spending.
The clerk/treasurer, tax clerk and solicitor revised our tax code several years
ago to include lottery winnings when the ticket was purchased in the village.
As a result we received approx. $850,000.00 from a winning lottery ticket that
was sold in Jefferson. $46,000 was paid as a down payment for the new fire
truck while the remainder is being held in reserve.
Here are some of the major projects that were completed during 2012:
∙   Finished the $321,200 S. Spruce truck route Phase I, including paving.
(This was the largest project the Street Department has undertaken and they did
a great job!) This effort saved the Village $73,000 cash by us doing the work
rather than contracting it.
∙   The Pine Street and N. Market Street OPWC culvert replacement project has
been delayed while we satisfy the Army Corps of Engineers and EPA permit
requirements.
∙   Continued sidewalk replacements, tree trimming and removal, and planted 16
new trees. $16,000 in labor cost saved in sidewalks and tree planting by
Village employees performing the work.
∙   Succeeded in receiving a $40,000 BWC safety intervention grant to purchase
a $62,000 Duraco Durapatcher Model 125 DJT. Machine will enable the Street
Department to perform crack sealing and pot hole   repairs saving over $18,000
per year.
∙   Continued using the Geneva-on-the-Lake street sweeper saving $4,500.00 for
sweeping and $3,500.00 for catch basin cleaning per year .
∙   Completed the $186,500 OPWC project to replace the forced main piping from
Elm Street pump station to the main plant.
∙   Refinanced the community center building loan saving $130,000.00
∙   Continuing negotiations with Aqua Ohio led to waterline replacements on:
West Satin St, Uselma Ave, Willis Ave, West Walnut St, N. Elm St, and West
Ashtabula St.
∙   Purchased and put a new $465,000.00 fire truck into service.
∙   The new community center van was purchased through the Minnesota State
Purchasing plan saving $5,000.00 off the $52,000.00 quoted price.
∙   Street department purchased a new rake through E Bay saving $4,000.00 off
the local price.
∙   Won the referendum vote to purchase the former elementary school property.
∙   Negotiated and put into place a contract for police dispatching service to
be provided by Ashtabula City Police Department.
∙   Completed MC70 dust control; paving of West Satin St and West Walnut St
($165,700.00); community center roof repair; Village Hall roof, floor and
ceiling repairs; new carpet in Village Hall; expansion of free weight room at
Rec; and the installation of electric service at Central Park.
∙   Implemented Property Maintenance Code and the Noise Ordinance.
Thanks to our employees, administration and council Jefferson is a great place
to live.
We hope that the year 2013 will be another great year for Jefferson.
Old Business/New Business

Ferric Chloride.

W.W.T.P. Finger explained even though there was a quick reaction to the spill.

plan for the plant.

Culvert
 
Service Dept.  
∙   Smolen Engineering and I met with OEPA on 2/14/13 to discuss the Market
Street issues.
∙   They had two areas of concern: The culvert was too narrow. We proposed
replacing the 14 foot culvert with a 14 foot culvert.
∙   EPA has requested a 19 foot 11 inch culvert to improve stream water
quality.
∙   They also did not favor the Army Corp. of Engineers proposed stream channel
location and said they would work to come to an agreement with the Army Corp.
on an approved channel.
∙   Smolen Engineering is doing an impact study to determine the feasibility
and cost of the EPA requests.
∙   EPA has assured us that they can finish approvals so we are not delayed for
2013 construction.
∙   The old 4 inch line and leaky valves were cut and capped or repaired this
weekend 2/15 to 1/16.
∙   The grant award for the Durapatcher was not sent in check form but as an
automatic transfer to the Village account.
∙   Clerk/Treasurer said we received the money mid - January. The Durapatcher
was ordered February 8 th , 2013. Delivery of the machine should be three weeks
after the order was placed.
Fire Dept. /Police Department:
∙   The Village finalized the transfer of the old Elementary School Property on
February 7 th , 2013.
∙   Renovations are already in progress and Police occupancy should occur by
early April.
Recreation Department:
∙   The Ashtabula County Sherriff may transfer all their exercise equipment to
the Community Center since he needs the floor space for a renovation project.
∙   We will keep you posted.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
∙   Our two employees Keith and Mark are finding the wastewater treatment class
and instructor to be very helpful and are enthusiastic.
∙   During our meeting with the EPA we also discussed a pending wastewater
plant change being required by EPA. We will need to eliminate the Chlorine
treatment at the plant and switch to ultraviolet treatment.

John Boczar a Jefferson Township trustee asked the Solicitor about the
annexation status for the property located in Jefferson Township by Bill
Cunningham. Can the Village Of Jefferson and the Township draw up an agreement
to share the revenues of tax dollars from the property.
Solicitor Lemire told Boczar that he would look into the annexation rules
governed by the Ohio Revised Code. This annexation will be different than other
annexations and he feels. The Village and the Township can draw up a contract
stating that they will share revenues. The Village of Jefferson has never done
an annexation like this before and he will have to look into the laws governed
by the Ohio Revised Code.

Councilperson Snyder discussed with Council the residency requirement for the
Chief of Police. If Wassie is appointed to the Village of Jefferson as Chief,
the Village is not in compliance with the Village Codified Ordinances which
states he should be a resident. Snyder asked the Mayor what the Village was
going to do. Snyder also told Council that he has heard concerns about the
Police Chief not residing in the Village.

other candidate showed interest. The Committee Chairman, I and the
Administrator interviewed Deputy Chief Wassie. Mayor Maloney told Council an
Ordinance will have to come to Council and passed by Council to lift the
residency requirement.
Council discussed at length the residency requirement for the Chief of Police
for the Village Of Jefferson.
Councilperson Hoyson told Council that the Committee has not heard of any
complaints or concerns about the residency requirement for the Chief of Police
for the Village of Jefferson. Hoyson told Council he is confident with the
Committees recommendation to put Deputy Chief Wassie’s in the Chiefs position.

State representative Dr. John Patterson of 78 East Beech Street Jefferson,
Ohio. Told Council it is an honor to represent the Village of Jefferson as the
State representative.
Patterson updated Council with some of the issues that are going on in Columbus
and some issues that will have effect of residents of the County. Patterson
spoke on House Bill 59 that wants more centralization to the Health Departments
in the State of Ohio. Patterson also spoke on House Bill 5 the standardizing of
the Income Tax in the State of Ohio. Patterson stated he did receive the
Village of Jefferson’s Resolution opposing the change.
Patterson spoke on the changes that are going on in the County. He is so proud
that the Giddings Law office is being moved. Told Council and the people
representing the Ashtabula County Historical Society that if helped is needed
contact him or the Ohio Historical Society. Patterson told Council that the
State is working on the Local Government Funds bring the amount back up to what
they were in 2009 along with the travel Center trying to get funding for a part
time person to run the building. Patterson spoke on many other things that are
going on in Columbus such as, Port Dredging, Fracking, School Funding and many
more issues in the County. Patterson said that Ashtabula County has allotted to
offer people in the State and he is trying to open the eyes of representative
in Columbus Ohio.
Mary Hedberg of the Ashtabula County Historical Society thanked the Village of
Jefferson with everything they have been involved with in the moving of the
Giddings Law Office.

Administrator Finger told Council that the Village of Jefferson and surrounding
residents of Jefferson have a Natural Gas problem. East Ohio determined that
work being done on the Jefferson Eagleville Road has caused a problem by
putting air into the main gas line to the Village of Jefferson. All residents
will have the gas shut of at their house from the main line going into the
house. Dominion East Ohio Gas Company is purging the air in the gas line. The
residents will not have gas for some time. There are supervisors and crews out
resolving this problem. The longest the gas will be out is five days but
Dominion is trying to resolve the issue fast. Dominion East Ohio will be coming
into each residents house turning on the meters, heat and water tanks. The
Village is working in whatever way they can to help resolve this issue.
Administrator Finger did tell Council that the Ashtabula county historical
society did vote to move the Law Office to the Village
Councilperson Brabender asked Administrator Finger if it all possible next time
could he please inform her or issues that come up at the Recreation Center. Her
concern was that she did not know that the Senior Coordinator resigned until
she read it in the Administrator report.
Administrator Finger told Councilperson Brabender he would keep her informed in
the future with changes that is going on at the recreation center.

Visitor’s Comments (five minute limit per council rule # 13 )         
Bob Harley and Rosemary Dziak representing Dominion East Ohio spoke to Council.
Bob Harley of Dominion East Ohio thanked the Village of Jefferson for helping
and supporting the Dominion Gas Company during the gas issue that started on
April 15, 2013. Harley explained to Council that the Village of Jefferson lost
gas pressure due to compressed air getting into the main gas line coming into
the Village. The Gas Company had to shut off service to all customers. The Gas
Company and its employees did their best to get all the customers serviced and
running as fast as they could. Harley told Council that in his thirty five
years at the gas company this is a first. Harley assured Council that the gas
company is taking all steps that these issues will not happen again.
Council thanked the Company for all their hard work and support for the Village
of Jefferson.
Bob Harley of Dominion East Ohio told Council that the Gas Company is sending a
check to the Village for support that the village gave the Gas Company and its
employees.

Old Business/New Business     
Councilman Damon brought up some question and concerns on the passage of the
new Income Tax Ordinance. He said that he has had some resident bring up
concerns.
Solicitor Lemire explained to Council that the new Income Tax Ordinance
clarifies the 25% of gross wages from employees that work only part time in the
Village. Lemire explained that he did have a call from the County Prosecutors
Office representing the County with some concerns on the Ordinance being
effective the beginning of the year 2013 and the employees that only come in to
drop of paperwork. Lemire told Council that the Clerk- Treasurer, County
Auditor and the County Prosecutor are setting up a meeting to resolve the
issues.

as part of the Village’s 50% cost contribution toward this project.

restructure vendors and reach a new contract.

reinstallation.

cleanup to enable the police department to move in to the new building.

July 12th. We will have it for most of August and move it according to reported
complaints of speeding vehicles.

on their streets. We will retain it as long as possible.

two old batteries and he replaced them.

resignation” as per Village Code #254-(d) Absence without leave.

Visitor’s Comments      
Joe Niemi of the Sheriff’s Department asked Council to table Ordinance 13-O-
2953 pertaining to the Income Tax of the Village of Jefferson. Niemi told
Council that the Income Tax Ordinance goes against the 311 Ohio Revised Code
for a Deputy Sheriff. The road Deputy’s will fight the new proposed Income Tax
Ordinance. This opens door to other municipalities to do the same. Niemi also
stated instead of the 25% the logging is too time consuming on the deputies. He
also told Council that the Road Deputies would fight it in a law suit.
Sean Ward of the Sheriff’s Department also asked Council to table Ordinance 13-
O-2953 pertaining to the Income Tax of the Village of Jefferson. Ward told
Council that he has the same concerns that Joe Niemi has. Ward also felt this
would open up to many doors to other municipalities the Sheriff’s Department
goes to.
Clerk Treasurer Fisher told Council that she has been trying to resolve the
issues since she started in 1996. Council has asked her to resolve the issues
with the County. Fisher told Council about four years ago she subpoenaed the
County Auditor and it has been between the Lawyers since.
Solicitor Lemire told Council that he did get a call from the Sheriff, the
County Prosecutor and the County Auditor with the concerns. The County Auditor
myself and the Clerk Treasurer had a meeting that helps resolve some of the
issues with the 25%. We came up with if a employee does not feel they work 25%
of the time they can do a log and present it to the Village Income Tax
Department for a refund.

Service Dept.  
∙   With continued good weather, Housel Construction should complete with the
Market Street Culvert and wing walls by mid-October.
∙   The County Engineer employees and Village Employees will then take over the
site to finish the new stream channel, removal of the two old culverts, site
grading, and road reconstruction.
∙   Sycamore Street Culvert project was completed September Sept 27 th and the
road was opened for traffic. Contractor will return to correct two problems,
bank erosion and guard rail alignment.
∙   Street Department continues site work on Market Street culvert project
where practical.
∙   I am still not aware of a schedule to complete the sidewalk and other
finish work for a reopening of the Giddings Law Office.
∙   ADA approved hand rails were installed on the newly repaired front entrance
to Village Hall.
∙   Street Department will continue work on sidewalk replacements on East
Walnut Street.
∙   We continue to use the Durapatcher to repair damaged asphalt.
∙   The transfer of the School Drive (South Popular Street) to the Village as a
highway easement is nearing completion. Survey has been completed and as soon
as the description text is complete the package will go to Jerry Lemire to file
on behalf of the village.
∙   This transfer will remove $35,000 from the $125,000 in kind work as part of
the sales agreement between the school and the village for the purchase of the
old elementary school property.
Fire Dept. /Police Department:
∙   Fire department will have roof repairs completed before bad weather starts.
∙   Police department office space is complete. All functions are operating
from the new office space.
∙   It needs to be noted that no new furniture or office equipment was
purchased to complete this move!  No new desks, chairs, tables, file cabinets,
book cases, shelving units, storage lockers and such were purchased. Surplus
equipment from the school closing added anything that has been needed.
∙   The Vocational School Students are completing the brick work and will pour
the sidewalks as needed.
∙   Fire Department now has full control of their building and will use it
according to their needs.
Recreation Department:
∙   All operations are normal.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
∙   All operations have been normal.
∙   The Martuccio sewer extension was approved by EPA and construction should
start next week
Other Items:
∙   Property owner Ed Utterback has been issued demolition permits for the
three buildings remaining on the property.

Administrator Finger told Council that the Market Street Culvert project will
not be done until August of next year. Administrator gave Council a memo
regarding the project. Council asked to have the Administrator make the memo a
public service announcement. Inserted below is the announcement.
PUBLIC SERVICE ANNOUNCEMENT
Village of Jefferson
NORTH MARKET STREET TO REMAIN CLOSED UNTIL AUGUST 2014
There seems to be some grumbling starting to surface about having Market Street
closed this winter. To enable an informed discussion and eliminate rumors here
are some facts that will help explain why it must be closed.
∙    The project criterion was to construct a new culvert to carry cemetery
creek under Market St. It eliminates a narrow and failing sand stone culvert
built in the 1890’s, eliminates a failed bridge across cemetery creek in the
valley, and eliminates a crumbling culvert under Pine Street.
∙    This 2011 project was delayed for a year and a half while we worked to
satisfy the EPA’s stream improvement criteria and also satisfy the Army Corp.’s
stream flow criteria.
∙    These delays assured that the design would handle the 100 year “worst
case” water flow, prevent stream degradation and preserve/improve water
quality.
∙    The stream mitigation plans also call for replanting about two acres of
the Valley with native variety trees and shrubs to restore shade and habitat.
∙    While we hoped to be started with construction as soon as warm weather
arrived, the culvert bid process could not be completed until June 3 rd , 2013
when Housel Construction was awarded the contract.
∙    The lead time for precast pipes was 10 to 12 weeks or we could choose to
pour it in place in about half the time.
∙    With the weather delays, and unreported main gas line in the construction
zone delay, Housel did not start construction until 8/19/2013.
∙    The poured in place culvert was finished and cured by 11/6/2013.
BEFORE THE ROAD CAN BE OPENED THE FOLLOWING ADDITIONAL MAJOR WORK MUST BE
COMPLETED.
∙    The new creek channel must be dug and improved so water flow is redirected
through the new culvert.
∙    The old sand stone culvert must be removed and filled in.
∙    The bridge across cemetery creek will be removed and the concrete removed.
∙    The culvert under Pine St. must be removed and filled in.
∙    The west side of market must be filled and storm drains installed
∙    The east side of Market must be widened with fill dirt for a sidewalk and
the cemetery service road.
∙    The road surface can be reconditioned and paved after all work requiring
heavy tracked construction machinery is complete.
∙    After paving and shoulder work is complete the new guard rails will be
installed and the road can be opened.
AFTER THE ROAD IS PAVED AND OPENED TO TRAFFIC, THE FOLLOWING MUST BE COMPLETED
TO FINISH THE PROJECT.
∙    The valley must be re-graded to remove the current service road and
provide a gradual slope to the stream bed.
∙    The conservation easement must be planted with the type and quantity of
trees and shrubs required by the EPA mitigation permit.
∙    There will be an inspection by both agencies with follow up for ten years.
Administrator Finger told Council that McDonalds is moving forward. After the
three parcels are combined into one McDonalds will have to bring the plans to
Historical Review Board for a stamped of approval before they can move forward.
Councilperson Snyder asked who would be paying the costs for the transfer of
the road by the High School.
Administrator Finger told Council the cost for the title transfers would come
out of the in-kind agreement the Village has with the School.

Service Dept.  
∙   The Street Department is again using a grit/salt mixture for ice control on
the Village Streets. Some residents complain because the roads are not bare
like when we used only salt. Other residents complain because the grit (sand)
gets tracked into their garages and houses.
∙   The documents needed to place a road easement on the new school property’s
drive (South Popular Street) for the Village to maintain the roadway have been
completed. Jerry Lemire to file on behalf of the Village.
∙   As soon as Jerry Lemire files the easement we can remove $35,000 from the
$125,000 in kind work due the Jefferson School Board. This transaction was part
of the sales agreement between the school and the Village for the purchase of
the old elementary school property.
∙   Refuse bids with recycling were mailed to four suppliers on 12/13/13. Bid
opening is scheduled for January 9 th 2014.
Fire Dept. /Police Department:
∙   Fire Department is doing renovations to the former Police section of their
building to freshen it up for their use.
∙   The Police Department received a complaint that their temporary sign was
blocking the view to the Giddings Law Office. Norma Waters looked at the
placement and feels it is someone’s petty view. Once the permanent signs,
sidewalk and landscaping are complete it will be fine.
Recreation Department:
∙   Another great craft show and sale.
∙   Santa’s visit was well attended.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
∙   All operations have been normal.
Other Items:
∙   The McDonalds site work has been completed. Three parcels have been
combined into one as required. Application for the Zoning permit is under
consideration (I need to resolve a road cut issue across N. Chestnut Street)
Historic Review Board is set to approve and issue a certificate of
acceptability.
∙   McDonalds plans to advertise for construction bids in February 2014 with a
construction start after receiving a successful bid.
∙   Electric bills are consolidated into one bill. We are in the process of
changing all bills to Direct Energy at a low rate of .05165.
∙   Once this has been finalized we will request a study of all accounts to
verify that all service codes are correct for each of our 19 accounts.
∙   Christmas parade was again the largest ever. Attendance is growing along
with the length of the parade. Great job by everyone involved.

week.

tried to find a replacement to rent to no avail.
∙   Street department is using a walk behind snow blower which is terribly
slow.
∙   All plow trucks are operational. With these cold temperatures we may have
to drive on snow covered roads until temperatures rise to enable the salt to
melt it off the roads.

Mayor
STATE OF THE VILLAGE 2014
MAYORS 2013 “END OF YEAR REPORT”
The Village has ended the year with a $989,000.00 carry over plus the
$840,000.00 in lottery tax. Thanks to the Dept. Supervisors, all the Admin
Staff and of course Council.
We are all conservative when spending tax payer money.
Following is a list of projects started/completed in 2013:
∙   The Pine Street and N. Market Street OPWC culvert replacement project
started after one and a half years of delays while we satisfied the Army Corps
of Engineers and EPA permit requirements. Total Project cost $449,000.
∙   The Village in kind contribution of $39,587 in 2013 will save us $39,587 of
additional cash outlay for the Market Street project in 2014.
∙   This joint project (50%/50% split between the County and Village) has had
an added benefit of building great cooperation between the Village workers and
County workers.
∙   Purchased a $62,000 Duraco Durapatcher Model 125 DJT Pot Hole repair
Machine with a $40,000 BWC safety intervention grant . This machine enables the
Street Department to perform crack sealing and Pot Hole repairs  saving over
$18,000 per year.
∙   Streets repaired with the Durapatcher included: Susan, Wall St., West
Jefferson, and new Police parking lot, Market, E. Walnut, E. Ashtabula,
Brittney Lane, Wastewater Plant, E. Cedar, S. Elm, Netcher Rd., Pine and N. &
S. Spruce.
∙   Continued using the Geneva-on-the-Lake street sweeper saving $4,500.00 for
sweeping and $3,500.00 for catch basin cleaning per year .
∙   The Phase II $399,800 Sycamore Street Culvert replacement project was
completed below cost and on schedule. The final total cost for this project was
$375,448.53 which included $17,484 of in kind work. Project cost savings of
$41,836 with in kind.
∙   Design work for the East Jefferson St. Culvert replacement, estimated to
cost $128,800, began in December 2013. This project will be completed by
Village Employees after Market St is reopened. This job is nearly identical to
the culvert we replaced on West Jefferson St. (Eagleville Rd.) just past
Popular St.
∙   Continued Sidewalk replacements, Tree trimming and removal, and planted 1
new tree. $15,000 in labor cost saved in sidewalks and tree planting by Village
employees performing the work.
∙   Renewed the Police Dispatching contract to be provided by Ashtabula City
Police Department at the current price of $30,000.
∙   Completed the purchase of the new Police building and all its renovations.
Repaired the paving at the new school drive to be transferred to the Village
and fixed the flooding problem in Elliott from water coming from the School
property.
∙   Demolished three properties under the property maintenance code enacted by
Village Council.
∙   Completed all budget items except Market Street Culvert Project.
On a sad note we lost our fire chief of 42 years Chief John Wayman. His passing
leaves a void in the lives of his family, the fire dept. and the community. He
will be missed.
I want to thank all the employees for their dedication to the village and the
pride they take in making this village a great place to live.
In 2014 the village will continue to be cost conscious while accomplishing as
many Capital Improvements as possible and maintaining services.
I wish everyone a Happy and prosperous New Year.
Judy Maloney
Jefferson Village Mayor

Service Dept.  
·   All Street Department snow servicing equipment is operational.
·   Christmas trees as well as other curbside brush have been removed. Monthly
brush pick up will resume in April 2014.
·   Refuse bids and recycling is scheduled to be discussed at a service
committee meeting Monday, February 3, at 6:30 PM.
Fire Dept. /Police Department:
·   Fire Department is having a pancake Breakfast Sunday February 2, and Feb.
16. This would be a good time to view the makeover of the former Police
section.
·   The Police Department received their new cruiser Friday, January 3, 2014
and it is in service.
·   Police electric bill has been reduced to $267 this last month. This is
comparable to the charges they were paying for the former location.
Recreation Department:
·   We need to approve the rental contract terms for Central Park Community
Center so we can be prepared to schedule events.
·   Rec. is adding two part time desk help employees to bring them back up to
their budgeted level of employees which is: 1 full time director, 1 part time
Clerical, 2 part time desk help, 1 part time Senior director and 1 part time
van driver.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
·   All operations have been normal.
Other Items:
·   Patty and I have signed a purchase order with Blue Technologies to change
our phone service from Century Link to voice over internet.
·   The cost for the first three years (includes new equipment) would be
$754.88 per month verses our $993.00/month for Century Link. Savings of about
$238.00 per month or $2,856.00 per year.
·   After the equipment is paid off the monthly charge drops to $468/month. A
savings of ($993 – $468 =) $525/month or $6,300 per year.
·   I will let you know when we are up and running.
Administrator Finger told council that the recreation department hired two part
time desk help. This does not change the budget at all. The Recreation center
has lost some of the help they had from Jobs and Family Services.
Administrator Finger told council that our sidewalk driver was in a wreck and
is injured and will be taking some time off to heal. Bill Hitchcock will be
plowing the sidewalks until Mike Riffle returns to work.

Visitor’s Comments 
Grant Brighman of 2378 Eagleville Road Jefferson spoke to Council on a recent
incident with Administrator Finger. Brighman told Council that he felt he had
his constitutional rights taken away from him when he was protesting in front
of Huntington National Bank with signs on his parked car stating Huntington
Steals. Brighman said Administrator Finger told him to remove the signs from
his vehicle and remove his truck from the right away. Brighman told Council
also that he had already talked with the Police chief and he gave him
permission to be there.
Administrator Finger told Council that he asked Grant Brighman to remove his
car from where he was parking. Reason being, he was parked in a Village Right
Of Way in a No Parking Zone. There were two violations per the Village’s zoning
code: Parking in a No Parking Zone and posting signs in the Village Right Of
Way. With the Car parked where it was, He would have to take the signs down.
Administrator Finger checked with Police Chief Wassie who said that he had NOT
given Mr. Brigman permission to park in a No Parking Zone. Chief Wassie quickly
resolved the issue.

∙   Solicitor Lemire and Nate drafted a final contract for Journey Church. It
is with the church for final review and signature.
∙   Operations are normal and there are no roof leaks.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
∙   Wastewater had a comprehensive EPA inspection at the plant. They looked at
the entire plant operation, reviewed our procedures, checked all the records
(including an incident report from three years ago), photo copied time cards,
and took lots of notes.
∙   Gary Licate was pleased with the process and able to answer any questions
to their satisfaction. He felt that it went very well.
∙   We “of course” will receive a full written report from the EPA.
∙   As part of the final design process for the OPWC project to get rid of
Chlorine and replace it with Ultra Violet light may have taken a new twist. EPA
may require us to send all plant over flow water through Ultra Violet
treatment. The light system would be resized from handling 1.3 million gallons
of flow up to handling 8 million gallons.
∙   The cost increase is estimated to be an additional $150,000.00. I will keep
you posted as it develops.
∙   In preparing this year’s OPWC application we had to do some testing on E.
Ashtabula St. Tests show that the Village owned laterals, under the road, are
broken and subject to causing sewer back up into homes if not repaired.
∙   The grant application will be prepared to replace all the broken clay tile
laterals with new PVC pipe. Funding required will be in the year 2016 when the
main plant improvement loan is paid off. This will free up $150,000 in payments
thereafter.
Other Items:
∙   McDonalds construction continues as planned.
o   The Sanitary Sewer tap has been completed.
o   As soon as Aqua finishes on Market Street they will move to North Chestnut
Street to lower their water line to allow the storm sewer line to pass over the
top and to provide the water tap needed for McDonalds.
Administrator Finger told council that the work being done at the Central Park
lot by the play ground the Village is claiming back the green space.

Oakwood Estates, Elliott Allotment and the school resources for kids, adults
and bike riders.

purchase bid price for 2014 (for purchases after Jan 1, 2015) increased to
$102.00 per ton. This is nearly triple what we expected.
∙   The Village has withdrawn its request to purchase salt from the State Bid.
Our guarantee to purchase 500 tons would cost over $53,000.
∙   We will again reduce the amount of salt we apply and rely on traction
control using grit.

∙   The Church rental of the cafeteria area in the police building has been
trouble free and a welcomed source of revenue.

for food prep. for Ashtabula County Senior meals on wheels and other events.
∙   The Police department was provided an office desk at the high school. Now
when an officer on patrol, stops at the school or is called to the school, they
will have a place to write reports and a police computer for resource work.
Despite rumors to the contrary there has not been a police officer assigned
full time to the school. Police involvement is the same as in past years.
Police are assigned as needed anywhere in the Village.
Recreation Department:

Visitor’s Comments
None
Tim Leehan – Here to speak to the proposed lot split that has been submitted to
the Village on Dorset Road. Not super familiar with everything but understand
that 110’ frontage and ½ acre are required and assisting the owner and realtor
on this. Survey and aerial photo of the duplex and single family buildings on a
single lot have been submitted. There is more than sufficient frontage to split
the 8/10 th acre parcel into separate lots. There are several reasons for this,
#1 is that most people today don’t have the necessary 25% down payment and
would need to finance the purchase. In order to do this the single family
residence needs to be on its own and the duplex on a separate parcel. What is
the process that needs to happen to accomplish?
Administrator Finger explained that the code is very specific, a variance was
submitted but the issues preventing him from approving aren’t variance related
items. Nor can the planning commission re-write the code, only Council can make
those changes if they desire.
Councilor Snyder questioned that since these are changes to the zoning code,
don’t they first have to go through the Planning Commission for approval or
recommendation, such as in 2010 for the frontage reductions on West Cedar
Street, et al.? Solicitor Lemire confirmed that the changes should first go
through the Planning Commission.
Councilor Snyder pointed out that in addition to the change required for less
than the required area, the lot split as presented also would not meet code
for; not having a 90° angle with the road on the new property line, following
the split the duplex would front on SR 307 (Mulberry Street) and the existing
parking is there but would then be located in the “front” yard between the
building and street, which is prohibited. The encroachment on the adjoining
property could be an issue with “marketability” and should be corrected or
remedied at this time. Utility services which would be located on differenct
new parcels should be identified and easements granted along with the split.
Administrator Finger added that the survey doesn’t demonstrate that the
required side yard setbacks between the single and duplex structures will be
achieved relative to the new property line. The planning commission can meet
anytime upon notice, first the additional information should be added to the
survey, perhaps have the survey overlaid on the aerial.
Mr. Leehan said that they will contact the surveyor to get the additional
information added to the survey and send in to have a planning commission
meeting scheduled.
Roland Quickle – First of all, he is concerned with the house on Elm Street,
what is being done, will this take years?
Administrator Finger advised Mr. Quickle that notices were sent on 9/5, they
have 60 days to respond so nothing can happen until after 11/5/2014. We can’t
just tear it down, the process takes time, but it is better than it used to be.
Mr. Quickle’s next item is related to the tree at 115 South Elm that he has
been asking to have removed for years now, what is being done on that?
Administrator Finger let Mr. Quickle know that if he has looked at it and it’s
still there then it’s OK. Typically any issues with trees and the need to
remove, we consult with, and rely on the tree cutters for their opinions, they
are the experts.
Mr. Quickle asked Councilor Snyder what he has done since he showed pictures of
the tree to him a couple of meetings ago?
Councilor Snyder let Mr. Quickle know that he and Councilor Brabender went and
looked at that and another tree on South Elm Street that night. One is large
and appears to be dead in the top, the one on the east side is smaller and also
seemed dead but not as much of a safety concern. We shared the locations with
Administrator Finger.
Mr. Quickle wanted to know what happened to the Administrators village issued
truck, the passenger door has been damaged twice?
Administrator Finger responded that his wife has backed into it, he will be
parking it out of the way.
