Visitor’s Comments
Vince Crawford of Waste Management told the Jefferson village Council that the
Community is doing very well with the new recycling program. He told Council
that Jefferson is one of the best Communities that they do recycling with. The
program had been in effect for about six months. Waste Management has seen a
drop in the amount of regular trash since the program has started. Crawford
told Council that this is good. Because it is proof that the residents are
using the recycling program.
Crawford told Council some of the acceptable items Waste Management is picking
up for recycling are. Metal cans, plastic bottles, containers #1-5 & 7, paper,
paper cardboard, dairy and juice containers, flattened cardboard and
paperboard, glass bottles and jars. Items that Waste Management will not pick
up are food waste, plastic bags, polystyrene foam, cups and containers.
Roland Quickle of 130 South Elm Street asked Administrator Finger why he has
not repaired his pickup truck that has been dented into. There are two spots
that need fixed. For Safety it is the Villages reasonability to fix the truck.
Quickle also questioned the Administrator if he had looked at the tree he asked
him to. He told Council that he has been asking for it to be cut down for seven
years.
Quickle also questioned the Administrator on September 21, 2014 why he was
hauling limbs and brush in his truck from him home.
Administrator Finger responded to Roland Quickle to the questions he asked.
Finger told Quickle he is in the process of getting his truck fixed and the
limbs in his truck were from his home. He put them in his truck and took them
to the brush site to save the Village Streets Department men some time. The
Village picks up brush for everyone in the Village of Jefferson. Finger also
told Quickle that the tree he is talking about he will have Brobst Tree Service
look at it to see if the tree needs to be cut down.
Roland Quickle also told Mayor Maloney that he has three hundred signatures for
his petition to get her removed from office.
Rodney Butcher of 355 Susan drive spoke to Council in regards to Susan drive
and why it is not been paved. Butcher told Council that he has thirty seven
signatures stating that the road needs to done and the Village has put it of to
long. Butcher told Council that the residents of Susan Drive have waited too
long to have the road paved. The Village has chipped and sealed the road but
that made more of a mess. The road is ruff and now has stone for the chip and
seal. The residents of the Susan Drive have asked to have the road swept, this
has not been done.
Butcher asked the Administrator what he was going to do because the Village has
waited to long now the road is to far gone is must be ground up and started all
over. The chip and seal is already breaking up and if the road is pave with the
condition of the road. The village will be just throwing their money away.
Administrator Finger told Butcher that Susan Drive is scheduled to be paved
next year. Finger also told Butcher he would have our engineering firm look at
the road and give the Village an opinion what needs to be done.
Brad Marinchak of 350 Susan Drive told Council that this has been over seven
years the residents of Susan Drive have been trying to get this road paved.
Marinchak also told Council if it is not done properly the Village will be
wasting tax payer’s money and not spending it wisely.

Recreation
Council at this time moved the Council Meeting over to the Recreation
Department to discuss the situation with Fitness Brokers in regards to the new
matting that was put down at the Recreation Center.
Village of Jefferson purchased rubber matting to replace the tile in the
aerobics room. Fitness Brokers supplied the rubber matting and installed it.
After becoming aware of the problems with instillation: miss match in color
between rolls, installed using double backed tape not glue, material left
underneath the matt in several places, poor fit at all wall edges, poor door
transition and unfinished edges Council and the contractor agreed to the
following.
∙   Contractor will remove the material left under the matt
∙   Contractor will find a transition piece for all wall edges that meets
Village approval and covers the edge gaps and all the small pieces around the
edge.
∙   Village will reluctantly accept the miss match in color between the rolls
which makes the floor look striped.
∙   Contractor will provide and install a transition Strip between both locker
rooms and the main floor edge.
∙   Contractor will finish the edges to the storage rooms and along the
walkway.
Motion by Council Brabender to implement the stipulations written above as
discussed by Council and Fitness Brokers

Mayor
STATE OF THE VILLAGE 2015
MAYORS 2014 “END OF YEAR REPORT”
State of the Village 2014
Again the Village has ended the year within the self-imposed 15% carryover.
The Department heads, Administration and Council are very watchful in the
spending of taxpayers dollars.
Here are some of the major projects that were completed during 2014:
∙   The Pine Street and N. Market Street OPWC culvert replacement project
costing about $590,000 was completed.
∙   The Village in kind contribution of $86,000 of labor in the project saved
us $86,000 in cash outlay for the Market Street project.
∙   Durapatcher repairs increased this year saving over $20,000 in street
repair costs. Streets repaired with the Durapatcher included: Susan, Wall St.,
West Jefferson, Police parking lot, Market, Walnut, Ashtabula, Brittney Lane,
Wastewater Plant, E. Cedar, Elm, Pine, Spruce, School access road, Municipal
parking lots plus many others.
∙   Continued using the Geneva-on-the-Lake street sweeper until May. A broken
shaft sidelined the sweeper for the remainder of the year.
∙   The East Jefferson St. Culvert replacement, estimated to cost $128,800, was
delayed until 2015. This project will be completed by Village Employees as a
cash saving measure.
∙   Completed $18,607 of in kind work for the School District as part of our
purchase agreement. Total in kind has been $60,734 of $150,000. Balance
remaining is $89,266. The majority of the in kind in 2014 was for the new
sidewalk from Elliott Dr. to the High School
∙   Continued all normal services: sidewalk snow plowing, repair, replacement,
tree trimming, removal, leaves/grass, brush, Christmas tree pick up, ditch
cleaning, road repair, and others
∙   Renewed the Police Dispatching contract to be provided by Ashtabula City
Police Department at the current price of $30,000.
∙   Completed the occupancy of the former elementary school building:
o   Police Department takes about one third
o   Community Action of Ashtabula “Meals on Wheels” rents the kitchen area 40
hours per week for food prep.
o   Journey Church rents the main room for 24 hours per month.
o   The Community center holds classes in the main room and the main room is
available to rent for large parties.
o   New street lights were installed to increase visibility in the parking area
and drive.
∙   Police enforcement remains at a high level to make sure residents and
visitors are safe in Jefferson.
∙   The Fire Department was awarded a grant to purchase a new jaws of life.
They have also received various donations that were used to purchase other
needed equipment.
∙   Wastewater Plant continues its exemplary operation with praise from EPA.
∙   Property Maintenance enforcement continues with one demolition to commence
Jan 5, 2015. There may be two more needed in 2015.
∙   Implemented curb side recycling and received an $18,720 dollar award from
the Solid Waste District. The award will be used to prevent cost increases as
long as the money lasts.
∙   Our efforts working with Aqua Ohio (our water supplier) continue to yield
new improvements including replacing old water lines at S. Elm St. and E. Erie
St. which yield better flow rates for fire protection and morning showers.
∙   Our jobs base continues to improve with two new additions at Presrite
Corporation, doubling the size of the ACMC medical center, new tenants
interested in the Pickens Plastic Plant, a new McDonalds, and other new tenants
in the Business District. a bakery, a medical Insurance broker, The White Whale
Restaurant, and new owners for the Deli In The Rye.
I want to thank all of our employees for their dedication and hard work that
makes this village a safe and welcoming place to live and visit.
We are all looking forward to another great year in Jefferson.
I wish all a safe and prosperous New Year.
FYI: 2014 Village Officials, Members of Committees and Boards
FYI: Letter from State Rep. John Patterson
FYI: Ohio EPA

Service Dept.  
∙   Urban Engineers from Erie PA is still evaluating Susan Drive paving
project.
∙   Still waiting for Army Core of Engineers written report regarding Market
Street.
∙   Street crews have busy removing snow and maintaining equipment.
∙   Nearly all Christmas decorations have been removed.
∙   We will have to close two streets and rebuild two RR crossings before June
of this year. The RR is removing tracks that serve Western Reserve and cross E.
Walnut Street. They are also pulling tracks on S. Cucumber St. in a land swap
deal with Presrite Corp.
Fire Dept. /Police Department:
∙   Food prep at the Central Park building is operating smoothly.
∙   Mayor, Allison, Chief Wassie, Curt Stone, Kay Ann, Bev and I have all eaten
at the Senior nutrition site and are pleased with the quality and tastiness of
the food we have been served.
∙   The Community Center will work to increase the number of people that eat
there now that everything is running smoothly.
Recreation Department:
∙   The Community Center rubber matting was finished to our liking.
∙   Once the new tile strip has been completed to the weight room they will
return to install the transition strip between the matt and tile.
∙   Senior center has undergone changes to make more room available for
activities now that the tables and chairs are no longer needed for daily
lunches.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
∙   The Village and Smolen Engineering had a phone conference with OEPA to
discuss the need to continue using chlorine after the Ultra Violet treatment
project had been completed. OEPA agreed with us and will allow us to
discontinue the chlorine process. OEPA had expressed a desire that we continue
chlorination of overflow rain event water. We will monitor the out flow of rain
events for a year to gather data to support the need or lack thereof for storm
water treatment.
∙   The main blower in the basement below the lab and office is failing. To
replace that blower we will have to cut an opening through the basement wall to
replace the blower. The original access door was covered over when the lab was
built.
Other Items:
∙   Demolition of 112 S. Elm St. house is complete. Sewer lateral was capped as
well as the storm water drain.
∙   Final site grading and grass seeding will take place in the spring.
∙   All costs are being tabulated to allow us to notify the property owners and
file a lien on the property.

Service Dept. 
∙   Street crews have busy removing snow piles to make room for more snow.    
∙   A replacement dump truck and a replacement Case backhoe have been ordered
at State bid purchase prices.    
Fire Dept. /Police Department:
∙   Food prep at the Central Park building is fully functional.   
∙   In addition to the home delivered meals they are serving from 20 to 30
persons per day in the cafeteria area.    
∙    The Community Center staff+ is working with Community Action to increase
the number of people that eat in the building.    
∙    Mayor, Rec. Supervisor (Allison), Senior Center coordinator (Tony), and I
are inviting select individuals to join us for lunch to promote the excellent
food and service to the community. It will be nice to serve 50 to 60 persons
per day.   
∙   Police department has ordered two new replacement vehicles to be delivered
this year.     
Recreation Department:
∙   Senior center has undergone changes to make more room available for
activities now that the tables and chairs are no longer needed for daily
lunches.   
∙   The kitchen area is being cleaned and rearranged now that the Community
Action food service has been relocated to the former Elementary School
Cafeteria area.   
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
∙   The Village and Smolen Engineering have submitted the design for replacing
Chlorine with ultraviolet light for final treatment of the waste water during
the summer months to EPA for final approval.    
∙   The main blower noise problem in the basement below the lab and office is
being studied. The problem of unusual noise may be caused by a leak in the air
line that carries blown air to the digesters.   
∙   We will keep you up to date as facts are discovered.   
  Other Items:
Curt ordered 100 tons of salt to carry us through the year.
Pot holes have not been a problem as of yet.
I was in Mentor and Cleveland this last week and their roads are terrible with
plenty of pot holes needing repairs. Our Durapatcher repair machine has worked
out well at preventing the spread of failed road surfaces. The patches hold up
and are not knocked out by the snow plows blade.
Curt and I think that we can flatten the patches some to make the repair
smoother and not so bumpy.

Visitor’s Comments 
James Janson owner of Chicago Title 60 East Jefferson Street asked Village
Council if there were any plans for the sidewalks being repaired in the
downtown district.
Administrator Finger told Mr. Janson that the Village has the sidewalk for the
downtown area planned for this year. The sidewalks will be replaced from Satin
Street to Walnut Street of the down town district.
Mayor Maloney Read a Proclamation for the Historic Preservation of the Village
of Jefferson
Pat Bradek Chairman of the Historic District did the Recognition of Historical
and Architectural Significance properties being honored.
Administrator Finger told the visitors that the Village and the Historic
Preservation Committee worked to address concerns raised by Village residents
to preserve the downtown area along Chestnut Street and Jefferson Street. The
Committee worked with Cleveland State University and the State of Ohio Historic
Preservation Department for about three years to come up with a way to preserve
the areas and/or prevent the destruction of the Historic character of
Jefferson. A Local Historic District was formed with controls to monitor
changes to structures that have been registered with the State Of Ohio as
significantly valuable to Jefferson. These properties receive a certificate of
recognition. Before a Zoning Permit can be issued for changes to any of the
registered properties the Historic Review Board has to issue a letter of
approval. Approval is based on comparison to the design standards recommended
by the Board and approved by Council.

Visitor’s Comments 
Resident Howard Weisman of 384 Beverly drive spoke to Council regarding the
Storm Water Culvert at Kathleen and Beverly Drive. Weisman told Council that
the area has been plagued with water and flooding since the installation of the
single pipe in the area. Weisman told Council that he believes a dual 30 inch
or 36 inch pipe should have been installed instead of what was installed.
Weisman quoted what Smolen Engineering stated in their report. He told Council
that the additional piping should have been installed. Weisman asked Council on
behalf of the residents of the area to please fix the issues before more damage
is done to their homes. Weisman told Council that the resident have never had
any problems until the Village erroneously put in the single pipe.
Resident Dan Rice of 350 Kathleen drive told Council that his backyard has a
catch basin and his yard services seven parcels of property, which has led to
him being the most affected. Rice told Council since the installation of the 30
inch pipe he has experienced significant flooding in his back yard and
basement, damaging carpeting and more belonging that must be replaced. Rice
gave Council pictures of his property flooded with water and damage to his
basement. Rice told Council the he cleaned up the mess and is not asking to be
reimbursed for the mess. He wants to move forward and he is not pointing
fingers he just wants to fix the problem before the issues gets worse.
Administrator Finger told the resident that the Village is not taking this
lightly. The Village is discussing the issue with Smolen engineering and a
report is expected back to the Village by the end of Tuesday July 21, 2015.
Finger told the resident that he will make sure they will be told of the
resolution to the problem.
Mayor Maloney asked the residents in attendance to make sure they signed in
with their names and address, so they could be invited to the future meeting
with Smolen Engineering about possible solutions.
Dr Greg Ray of Ray Chiropractic Office came to Council to see if he could get
approved a sign on the corner of Pine Street and St. Rt. 46 to help customers
find his office. Dr. Ray told Council that he owns the property and wanted to
comply with the Village sign Ordinance. He said that he wants to put up a 2” by
2” sign.
Administrator Finger told Council that he cannot do anything to grant the sign
because there is no prevision in the code to comply with what he wants to do.
The options are to rewrite the code or change the zoning on his residential
house to business.
Council set up a Committee Meeting Wednesday July 29, 2015 at 7:00 p. m.
Jim Donathan of 337 Susan drive asked Administrator Finger if the Village was
going to fix the burming on Susan Drive he told Council that there is a 10 inch
to 12 inch drop now that the Street has been paved. Donathan also asked if
something was going to be done with the manholes also.
Administrator Finger told Donathan that he would go to Susan Drive and look at
the burming. He also said the Streets Department is going to finish the

Market
Service Dept. 
∙   The culvert work in the open ditch between Beverly and Kathleen is on hold
pending a review of the entire project. A rain event in the 100 year category
caused an accumulation of water that got into one basement (has happened
several times in the past) and was high enough to worry two other property
owners. Smolen Engineering is reviewing the potential flow calculations, and
Jerry is reviewing storm water responsibilities under EPA and Army Corp. in
light of recent Supreme Court rulings.   
∙   Rough grading is complete and temporary grass is growing.   
∙   It needs to be noted that the piping system that was installed when Elliott
was developed was not a Village of Jefferson project. The 24” tile between
Beverly and Hillyer will not carry all the surface water when rain approaches
the ten year high average rain event. It never has and it will not in the
future. Storm water accumulates in back yards bordering the west side of the
school property, surface storm water follows the low points through properties
east of Elliot Drive and enters the Village right of way at two distinct points
and then enters the storm water piping. When the piping reaches capacity flow,
the storm water overflows the piping and flows on the surface to accumulate in
low points until the rain event subsides and the water can go back underground
into the piping. W. Cedar and Hillyer streets flood in high rain events and as
rain fall subsides the water recedes back into the piping.    
∙   I was asked if the Village could clean an open ditch which we did. Then I
was asked if there was anything to keep the vegetation from growing back, and
also asked if there was anything we could do to make the area more safe to
small kids when the ditch is full of water and flowing so fast.   
∙   To make a long story short, we put tile pipe in the open ditch and covered
the pipe and planted grass. This application is like many others in the
Village. There is a pipe in the ground with drain openings to the surface into
a swale (shallow ditch) area. The swale will carry the excess surface water
until the flow slows down and storm water can recede into the pipe.   
∙   Arguments and discussions continue challenging if the Village installed the
pipe correctly, or caused more flooding. I will report more information as soon
as it all gets sorted out.    
∙   Downtown sidewalk replacement bids were opened on July 8th at 12:00 Noon
(bids included in Council Packet) Easton Construction was low bidder. I have
requested a motion to accept the bid authorize me to sign the contract.   
∙   The E. Jefferson St. tile replacement project will start July 20 and take
about 10 days of decent weather to complete. E. Jefferson Street between
Cucumber and Spruce will be closed to through traffic.   
∙   Street Dept. has completed the demolition of the storage shed behind the
School bus garage. This work totaled $3,550.40 and was charged against the in
kind agreement with the Jefferson Local School District.    
∙   Aqua Water Company will start the 4” waterline replacement on S. Elm St.
around the first week of August. All effected property owners will be notified.
   
Fire Dept. /Police Department:
∙   Personnel changes have been included in Council Packet   
Recreation Department:
∙   The Exercise room floor replacement project has been completed.   
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
∙   Operations are normal.   
∙   I received the EPA 37 page plant inspection report today (7/17/15). I will
provide the report to anyone that wants a copy. It is a favorable report. Out
of ten groupings of items: 4 were totally acceptable, six needed some
modifications, and no areas were unacceptable. Of the six needing modification:
   
∙   Four require more frequent thermometer calibration    
∙   Two need revised or new procedures.   
Other Items:
∙   St Joe’s barn move to the police Station: We are receiving cost estimated
from the Utilities to disconnect and then reconnect their services. As soon as
I have a complete picture of all costs we will meet to discuss the plan of
action.   
∙   Painters would be complete with the repainting of the Village
Administration building except for the rain delays. We have received a ton of
positive comments.

in by the residents of the Street 20 to 30 years ago. This is not Village
property and there is not an Easement so the Village would not be responsible
to repair the drain.

South Market
Service Dept. 
∙   Aqua Ohio has finished surface restoration at both S. Elm and E. Erie
streets.   
∙   Aqua Ohio has also donated a baseball backstop fence for the south end of
Giddings Park. This will be used for recreation type baseball. Installation
will be completed by 12/04/2015.   
∙   Over 800 trees and shrubs have been planted in the valley between the two
Cemetery sections. This was required by EPA and Army Corp. in exchange for
relocating the stream under Market Street.    
∙   If the resident deer herd damages the trees and shrubs we will seek a
nuisance deer permit from ODNR to cull the deer population until the plants are
no longer in danger of being damaged. Any damaged plants that do not recover
must be replaced during a five year period.   
∙   We are still removing unwanted growth on and trimming newer trees to
maintain the required head clearance of 12 feet.   
∙   Leaf pick has been completed for the year!    
Fire Dept. /Police Department:
∙   Nothing new to report    
Recreation Department:
∙   Nothing unusual to report    
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
∙   Operations are normal.   
∙   EPA has issued our new operating permit. The plant personnel are adjusting
some of the test procedures as needed in this new permit.   
∙   We will have to consider extending the Sewer Capital Improvement charge for
several years to cover the EPA mandated improvements listed in our new
permit.   
∙   We have four capital improvement projects that must be done:   
   o   Install UV Treatment/eliminate
Chlorine.                   $119,900.00   
   o   Repair E. Ashtabula St. lateral connections at the main line that are
failing.       $181,620.00   
   o   Replace sludge pumps and valves                  $ 49,935.00   
   o   Eliminate surface water leaks into the sanitary to prevent overflows to
the stream.    $ Unknown cost

Market
Service Dept. 
∙   Aqua Ohio has also donated a baseball backstop fence for the south end of
Giddings Park. Installation has been completed.   
∙   The resident deer herd has damaged trees and shrubs in our mitigation area
between cemetery sections.    
∙   I had ODNR from Akron visit and observe the damage. By mutual agreement we
will seek a nuisance deer permit from ODNR to cull the deer population until
the plants are no longer in danger of being damaged.    
∙   The permit will be issued effective Jan 1, 2016. We will take up to five
deer and then reevaluate for continued damage. If needed the culling process
will be continued.   
∙   Only pre-qualified rifle marksmen will participate, I will pick the time
and shooters, Chief Wassie will issue the shooting permit to conform to ODNR
specifications.   
∙   Street Department is all set up to handle snow.   
∙   With a lack of snow they are cleaning up our storage areas and enlarging
the brush pile area.    
Fire Dept. /Police Department:
∙   Nothing new to report

Mayor 
2015 State of the Village
Again the Village has ended the year within the self-imposed 15% cash
carryover.
The Department heads, Administration and Council are very watchful in the
spending of tax payers’ dollars.
Here are some of the major projects that were completed during 2015:
   The Pine Street and N. Market Street OPWC culvert replacement project
costing about $590,000 was completed with the planting of 400 trees and 400
shrubs costing $20,000.   
   The East Jefferson St. Culvert replacement, estimated to cost $128,800, was
completed during 2015 by Village Employees. Total finished costs were $75,120.
Village Employees saved us $53,679 on the project.   
   Paving of Susan, Beverly, Uselma, S. Market and chip and seal amounted to
$183,000.00.    
   Durapatcher repairs increased this year saving over $30,000 in street repair
costs. The Durapatcher allowed us to make spot full depth repairs before
repaving or chip and seal on: Susan, Uselma, S. Market, Spruce, Woodside,
Frayer, and E. Erie.    
   Additional Durapatcher repairs were completed on, Police, Admin. Rec.
Wastewater, Street and public parking lots, West Jefferson, Willis, Center,
Walnut, Ashtabula, Brittney Lane, E. Cedar, Elm, Pine, School access road, plus
many others.    
   Completed $13,935.21 of in kind work for the School District as part of our
purchase agreement. This total in kind includes $7,849.12 for the School
Resource Officer and $6,086.09 for additional work requested by the School.   
   Original In Kind amount was $150,000. End of 2015 balance remaining is
$76,599.67.    
   Completed flooding improvements in Elliott allotment between Beverly and
Susan amounting to $48,819. Residents’ charges were $7,486.   
   Continued all normal services: sidewalk snow plowing, repair, replacement,
tree trimming, removal, leaves/grass, brush, Christmas tree pick up, ditch
cleaning, road repair, and others   
   Renewed the Police Dispatching contract to be provided by Ashtabula City
Police Department at the current price of $30,000.   
   Completed the first full year of occupancy of the former elementary school
building:    
      o   Police Department takes about one third   
      o   Police Department also utilizes the open floor space for In House
Training and State mandated training provided by outside paid instructors.    
      o   Community Action of Ashtabula “Meals on Wheels” continues to rent the
kitchen area 40 hours per week for food prep on a new five year contract.   
      o   Journey Church rents the main room for 24 hours per week.   
      o   The Community center holds classes in the main room and the main room
is available to rent for large parties.   
   Police enforcement remains at a high level to make sure residents and
visitors are safe in Jefferson.   
   The Fire Department maintains a well-trained staff of volunteer
firefighters.    
   Wastewater Plant continues its exemplary operation with praise from EPA,
while the newly issued operations permit requires two improvements:    
      o   Eliminate chlorine treatment    
      o   Eliminate storm water infiltration to prevent overflow into the
stream   
   Paid off:   
      o   The Police Building loan $93,091   
      o   Paid $156,060 off the Mulberry St. construction loan. Final payment
of $33,100 will be paid in 2016.   
   Purchased:   
      o   2 new police cruisers and computers/radios $72,122   
      o   New dump truck, backhoe and mower $162,000.   
      o   Fire turn out gear $10,800.    
   Our efforts working with Aqua Ohio (our water supplier) continue to yield
new improvements including replacing old water lines at S. Elm St. and E. Erie
St. which yield better flow rates for fire protection and morning showers.   
   Aqua also donated a baseball backstop for Giddings Park for t ball and pick
up baseball games.   
   Our jobs base continues to improve with new additions at Next Dimensions at
223 S. Spruce and Zehrco-Giancola Company Inc. at 382 E Erie St. ADA Solutions
Inc. purchased the former Pickens building for expansion purposes. King
Luminaire purchased 70 acres behind their current plant which abuts Nassief’s
property for future expansion and possibly annexation. All the downtown
business locations are occupied except the theater and Tom David’s car lot.    
I want to thank all of our employees for their dedication and hard work that
makes this village a safe and welcoming place to live and visit.
We are all looking forward to another great year (2016) in Jefferson.
I wish all a safe and prosperous New Year.
Mayor Maloney

Visitor’s Comments 
Tim Martin County Engineer spoke to Council regarding the new Income Tax
Ordinance that has been put in effect January 1, 2016. Martin told Council that
the Village had an agreement in place since 2013 and is asking the Council to
reconsider the agreement again with the County. Martin told Council the
agreement that the Village had in place worked for his County employees. His
employees only punch in and out at the Engineers office. They are not even in
the Village two hours a day. Martin told Council he gave the Tax Administrator
the job titles for all his employees. Martin told Council if his employees had
to take out 100 % of the Village Income Tax and do a log to show how much they
are really in the Village it would be a heavy burden on the employees. Martin
also told of his concern if the Village did not do a new contract and charged
the County Employees the 100% and retried it back to the first of the year it
would be financial burned on the employees.
Sheriff Billy Johnson spoke to Council regarding the new Income Tax Ordinance
that has been put in effect January 1, 2016. Johnson also told Council that he
has the same feelings as the County Engineer. Johnson told Council if it was
the money the Village needed he could save the Village money by the Sheriff’s
Department contracting with Jefferson Village and have the Village patrolled by
the Sheriff’s Department. He said he would hire the patrolmen that the Village
has now and take some of the financial burden away from the Village. He also
told Council that he had called other Departments with the same circumstances
as his Department and the Municipalities only charge there Sheriff’s Department
25%. Johnson also told Council he could have his employees do there briefing
outside the Village and not have his patrolman even come into the Village. In
doing this patrolman would not have to pay Village Income Tax.
Councilperson Diehl told Council that the Villages Finances are in good shape.
The Village did not put the Ordinance in place to gain more money. The Village
had to put the new Ordinance in place because of House Bill 5 that was passed
by the State last year. House Bill 5 does allow the Income Tax Administrator to
go into special agreements based on special circumstances.
Tim Leehan spoke to Council regarding the proposed lot split that the Public
Hear is in place for tonight at 7:45 p.m. The propose lot split is the Buckeye
Title building and the First Merit building. The Villages Subdivision that is
in place requires all lots subject to the Density regulations to have a minimum
frontage of 110 feet and a lot size of an half of an acre. The lost that are in
the business district are the old town business district that was put in place
years ago and does not confirm to the new subdivision regulations. Leehan also
told Council he has a buyer for the Buckeye Title building, but cannot sell it
because of the subdivision regulations.
Leehan asked Council for future references that the Council look into the
possibly to change the Subdivision Regulations to confirm to the old town
business district or every time a business wants to sell the property. The
Village will have the same issue. Leehan also asked Council if they could waive
the three reading rule to move the process forward.
Council agreed to set up a Finance Committee Meeting for Monday March 7th at 7:
00 p.m. to discuss the Income Tax Ordinance and possible agreement with the
County.
Public Hearing March 7, 2016 at 7:45 p.m.
Motion by Councilperson Hoyson to go into the Public Hearing at 7:45 p.m.
2nd       
Roll: All yea, motion carried
Administrator Finger asked Council if they had any questions regarding the lot
split between Buckeye Title and First Merit Bank.
Councilperson Snyder told Council that the Village should look into drafting an
Ordinance for the Old Town business district since is does not fit into the
Subdivision Regulations the Village has in place now.

Service Dept.  
∙    The Durapatcher Crew is busy with road repairs.
∙    Chestnut Street paving is scheduled to begin on May 17, 2016.
∙    We received four quotes for paving Village Streets: Willis, Kathleen, and
S. Franley Blvd. Koski Construction gave us the lowest quote at $47,270.00.
Paving plants open mid-May and we will be the second job in their schedule
∙    CT Consultants has completed the re-calculation of property owners cost
for replacing the sidewalks with curbs between 66 N. Chestnut St. and 46 S.
Chestnut St. as per resolution. The plans, profiles and specifications along
with the estimated assessment for each property owner have been placed with the
Clerk Treasurer for public viewing.
Fire Dept. /Police Department:
∙    Police Auxiliary is sponsoring a fund raising spaghetti dinner for retired
Chief Febel. Steve has had no feeling in his legs since his back operations.
The money from the fund raiser will go to the police auxiliary who will build a
bathroom on the first floor of his home on S. Market St.
Recreation Department:
∙    I believe all the changes that needed to be made at the Community Center
have been put in place. Mistakes that occur from now on cannot be attributed to
incorrect rates or missing procedures.
∙   We will start re-staffing by adding another part time desk help person.
This person will eliminate the need for Roni or me to fill in open times in the
schedule.
∙    Journey Church has requested a one year rental agreement for the 11 E.
Jefferson St. Community Center. The lease and Church use should not impact the
proposed Bingo use later on Sunday.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
∙    UV project received five bids with the low bidder being Jack Gibson
Construction at $138,000.00.
∙    We have been approved for an OWDA loan to cover the Villages part of this
project. This action will enable us to complete the sludge pumps and valves
project (OPWC Round #30) this year also. This project cannot wait until next
year.
Other Items:
∙    Design work to build a covered bridge style pavilion at Giddings Park has
started. The goal is to have this project completed by the 2016 Covered Bridge
Festival.
∙    Arbor Day tree planting took place 4/29/2016. A Jefferson Elm was planted
by the helicopter in honor to Durward Newhard. An additional planting will be
scheduled for a tree donated by Andover Bank.

Service Dept.
∙    Downtown sidewalk replacement put on hold until council passes required
legislation.
∙    Curt and I are interviewing about six applicants out of the submittals and
expect to have chosen a full time and part time new hire by mid-September.
∙    Village crew will be doing two more sidewalk repair sections before the
end of fall.
∙    Tree removal will be scheduled as soon as Brobst can fit us into his
cutting schedule. Will advise!
∙    Village has submitted 12 blighted properties to the Ashtabula County Land
Reutilization Corporation seeking grant money to demo these blighted
properties.
Fire Dept. /Police Department:
∙    Tim Blon has returned to the school as resource officer and Joe Erickson
is back on active duty.
∙    The north drive entrance to the police department has been rebuilt and
repaved. Additional parking spaces were added beside the west side of the
drive. Now there are two dedicated spaces for the Giddings law office staff.
Recreation Department:
∙    Two new Security cameras and a new recorder have been installed and are
operational. All security cameras are operating on the same recording system.
The recording system at Rec. is the same make as the one at the Police
Department. Video quality, archiving and storage will be much easier.
∙    The new air conditioning unit was installed on Wed. & Thurs. and was fully
operational by Friday Sept 2.
∙    Pat Bradek has agreed to continue as a contract employee until further
notice. She is recovering nicely from her fall and is becoming more mobile as
time passes.
∙    The parking lot and the Village Hall parking area have been seal coated
and restriped. This work was in kind trade for the Street Dept. dump truck we
had trouble selling for cash.
∙    Pat is receiving quotes to redo the carpeting in the multipurpose room and
hall. She will be looking at two options: Vinyl flooring or new carpet. I will
report the results to the Recreation Committee as soon as they are finalized.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
∙    UV project is close to completion.
∙    The Giddings Park restroom sewer line was repaired at the end of the
soccer field next to East Satin street. This repair should help prevent some of
the blockages that have been happening.
Other Items:
∙    The five Village stand-by emergency Generators have been put on a time
schedule for general maintenance and load testing. General maintenance will be
every two years and load testing will be every three years.
Administrator Finger told Council that the tree removal for the fall will be
the second week of October. Stumps and tree will be removed for the year 2016
Administrator Finger told Council that the State Salt price this year is $39.14
a ton compares to last year $70.00 a ton.
Administrator Finger told Council that he has not heard of anymore complaints
from the noise at the car wash.

Service Dept.
•   The state purchase price for road salt was bid at $39.14 per ton compared
to over $70 per ton last year.
•   Curt and I reviewed all applicant applications for the full Time Utility
Maintenance position. We had several very qualified applicants. After
interviewing three we chose Joseph Albergo with fourteen years of experience
almost identical to the Village’s requirements. References listed rated him as
an excellent employee.
•   I am asking for Council to approve his hiring pending completion of his
physical and background check.
•   Curt and I also interviewed for the part time utility maintenance position
and offered the job to Mr. Roger Kubat pending confirmation of Council and
conditional on his passing a physical and background check.
•   I am asking for Council to approve his hiring pending completion of his
physical and background check
•   Tree removal will be scheduled for the second week of October. Trees
scheduled for removal will have an orange ribbon tied around them.
•   Communications between the Ashtabula County Land Reutilization Corporation
and the Village Solicitor continues regarding the 12 blighted properties we
submitted for demolition. The bottom line is not all 12 qualify but we should
expect to have at least 3 qualified.
Fire Dept. /Police Department:
•   Nothing exceptional to report
Recreation Department:
•   Several members of the Community Center are taking the lead in promoting
the November levy earmarked for the Community Center.
•   Pat Bradek’s recovery from her broken ankle is taking longer than Pat
hoped. We want her to take good care of the ankle and follow her medical
advice.
•   Pat is receiving quotes to redo the carpeting in the multipurpose room and
hall. She will be looking at two options: Vinyl flooring or new carpet. I will
report the results to the Recreation Committee as soon as they are finalized.
•   We have received a resignation notice from Jami Loach, part time desk
position. She is taking a similar job in Conneaut. We have advertised for her
replacement.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
• UV project was completed and is now in operation. The Chlorine tanks and
treatment equipment will be held in reserve until EPA approves their removal.
• After our UV project results are tested and our confidence level is high the
plant will start the Sludge Pump and valve replacement project that has been
approved with grant funding.

Motion for the Second Reading Amended Resolution No. 16-R- 3046_
A Resolution Declaring the necessity of repairing the sidewalks, curbs, and/or
gutters abutting the properties on the East side of Chestnut Street from 20
North Chestnut Street to 66 North Chestnut Street and from 14 South Chestnut
Street to 48 South Chestnut Street
2nd
Roll call: Yea – Hoyson, March, Brabender, Diehl; Nay, Snyder. Motion carried.
Councilperson Snyder appreciated the corrected address but questioned the why
the 30 day time for owner performed repairs was not extended to 180 days or
similar since the project won’t be started by the Village until sometime in the
spring of 2017 giving owners the full timing to complete the work rather than
the minimum 30 days. Administrator Finger reported that the notifications to
the owners wouldn’t be sent until next spring allowing the owners from now
until 30 days after they receive notice next year. If council wants he could
prepare and bring for Council approval a letter explaining the anticipated
schedule and then mail with the notification this fall. Councilperson Diehl
expressed hope that we wouldn’t pass the resolution now, then later tell the
owners “gotcha” and not allow them opportunity to do the repairs if they
desired before the Village performs.

scheduled for removal will have an orange ribbon tied around them.
•   We have also scheduled two days of Stump grinding for trees removed in past
years.
•   Communications between the Ashtabula County Land Reutilization Corporation
and the Village Solicitor continues regarding the 12 blighted properties we
submitted for demolition. There are four properties that are in foreclosure and
will be the first properties selected for demolition. There are four additional
properties that are in the paperwork process.
•   We received delivery on the new Kubota tractor and it has been put into
service.
•   Both new employees will be on the payroll on Monday 10/3/16.

•   Nothing exceptional to report
Recreation Department:
•   The recreation levy committee is taking the lead in promoting the November
levy. Signs will be placed and fliers prepared promoting the passage of the 1
mill levy.
•   Pat has received quotes to redo the carpeting in the multipurpose room and
hall. They are included in your packet as information prior to 2017 budget
meetings.
•   We are reviewing about fourteen applications for the desk help position
created by the resignation of Jami Loach.
•   We still need to schedule a Rec. Committee meeting. Lets’ set a time
tonight for a day that works for the committee.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
•   UV project was completed and test results show it is performing the
treatment as intended. The Chlorine tanks and treatment equipment will be held
in reserve until EPA approves their removal.
•   The design work for the Sludge Pump and valve replacement project is
underway. Our intention is to complete this work ASAP.

•   Village workers are assisting the Covered Bridge Festival organizers to
assure there are enough picnic tables, garbage cans and such to help make sure
the festival has no logistics problems.

recreation Department are for next year’s budget preparation. Finger told
Council that he wanted Council to have the information ahead of time.

Service Dept.
∙    Tree removal is scheduled on October 26 & 27. Trees scheduled for removal
will have orange ribbon/orange paint to identify them for removal.
∙    The first day of stump grinding will be October 31 then a second day to be
scheduled thereafter.
∙    I have started gathering the documentation needed for the Ashtabula County
Land Reutilization Corporation to enable the Village to clean up several
blighted properties.
∙    This time of year the street department clears brush and limbs overhanging
village sidewalks that will interfere with sidewalk snow removal. The new
Kubota tractor is taller than the one it replaced. This will mean removal of
more branches than usual.
∙    Both new employees are working at their assigned jobs.
∙    I have a traffic signal study in progress to determine the cost to bring
them up to current standards. Will report results to Council as soon as it is
completed.
Fire Dept. /Police Department:
∙    Nothing exceptional to report
Recreation Department:
∙    Senior Center activities are 750 service units below last years’
activities. This may have an impact on our transportation grants. Pat and Toni
are working with Roni on the new grant application.
∙    Pat has reviewed all the applications for the front desk position and has
interviewed three candidates. Pat offered Monica Greer the part time front desk
opening pending the outcome of her physical and background check.
∙    We had a Recreation Committee meeting. See minutes.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
∙    UV treatment has been in operation without any problems. The Chlorine
tanks and treatment equipment will continue to be held in reserve until EPA
approves their removal.
∙    Sludge pump project design documents are being worked on.
Other Items:
∙    The Covered Bridge Festival had good weather and nice crowds this year.
Village is cleaned up and restored to normal activities.
∙    We need to have a Finance Committee meeting to review several items
discussed at the Rec. Committee meeting and several procedural changes for WW,
Streets, and Police discussed at Staff meetings.
Administrator Finger showed Council an example of the sign the Village is
looking at for in front of the Gazebo. Finger told Council he has been getting
prices from various companies. A decision has to be made if the Village wants
to go with the Chamber in purchasing the sign or the Village purchasing the
sign by them.

Service Dept.
∙    Village crew is setting up the Christmas displays in good weather ahead of
the actual lighting times.
∙   Tree removal took place on October 26 & 27. Not all trees scheduled for
removal were removed. Those missed will be removed at the next scheduled
cutting.
∙    The first day of stump grinding was rescheduled to November 14 then a
second day to be scheduled thereafter.
∙    Mike and I have reduced our properties list for the Ashtabula County Land
Reutilization Corporation of blighted properties to three that I need to
notify.
∙    The brush and limbs overhanging village sidewalks that will interfere with
sidewalk snow removal have been cut. We should be ready for snow removal.
∙    I have a traffic signal study in progress to determine the cost to bring
them up to current standards. Will report results to Utility Committee as we
prepare for next year’s budget.
Fire Dept. /Police Department:
∙    Need to pass the ordinance with a couple minor changes for the Police
Department. See attached summary from the Finance Committee meeting.
Recreation Department:
∙    Senior Center transportation grants have been submitted for 2017.
∙    Monica Greer the new part time front desk employee has passed all
background checks and her physical. She will be starting work Monday November
7, 2016.
∙    Lunch will be served to Veterans on 11/11/2016 at 11:00 Thanks to the
generosity of the Knights of Columbus.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
∙    UV treatment has been in operation without any problems. The Chlorine
tanks and treatment equipment will continue to be held in reserve until EPA
approves their removal.
∙    Sludge pump project design documents are complete. The notice to proceed
with the project has been submitted to OPWC for approval.
Other Items:
∙    Page two of this report is a summary of rules changes that have been
discussed at both the Recreation Committee and Finance Committee. Both
Committees accepted the changes and ordinances have been forwarded to the full
Council for implementation approval.

now.

Mayor
 
2016 State Of The Village
 
Again the Village has ended the year within the self-imposed 15% cash
carryover.
 
The Department heads, Administration and Council are very watchful in the
spending of tax payers’ dollars.
 
Here are some of the major accomplishments that were completed during 2016:
∙    Installed Ultraviolet lights into the sewer treatment routine to eliminate
chlorine treatment. Project cost was $199,900
∙    Replaced defective sludge pumps and valves at the WW plant. Cost of
99,870.
∙    Made the last annual payments of $150,000 for improvements to the main
wastewater plant and the Elm Street lift station which originally cost over
$2,000,000.
∙    The Pine Street and N. Market Street OPWC culvert replacement project
requires monitoring to assure that the reforesting required by EPA reaches
maturity. There was only minor deer damage to the vegetation in 2016. All
damaged trees and shrubs must be monitored for growth with a report to EPA and
Army Corp. for a ten year period until 2025. All damaged and dead trees must be
replaced to maintain 400 trees and 400 shrubs.
∙    Forestry services consisting of brush grinding, dead tree removal and
stump grinding totaled $21,650
∙    Street paving (Kathleen, Willis and S. Franley); street repairs
(durapatch, cold patch, and chip sealing); snow removal and sidewalk repairs
amounted to $575,849 in 2016.
∙    When we purchased the current Police building one half of the purchase
price payment to the schools was an in- kind Credit amounting to $150,000. Now
at the end of 2016 our balance is $76,275.85.
∙    We have now completed the second full year of occupancy of the former
elementary school building:
   o   Police Department takes about one third of the space.
   o   Police Department also utilizes the open floor space for In House
Training and State mandated training provided by outside paid instructors.
   o   Community Action of Ashtabula “Meals on Wheels” continues to rent the
kitchen area 40 hours per week for food prep on a new five year contract. They
prepare seven meals per week for 400 senior residents County wide.
   o   The Community center holds classes in the main room and the main room is
available to rent for large parties.
∙    Continued all normal services: sidewalk snow plowing, repair, replacement,
tree trimming, removal, leaves/grass, brush, Christmas tree pick up, ditch
cleaning, road repair, and others
∙    Renewed the Police Dispatching contract to be provided by Ashtabula City
Police Department at the current price of $30,000.
∙    Police enforcement remains at a high level to make sure residents and
visitors are safe in Jefferson.
∙    The Fire Department replaced their mobile air tank (SCUBA) refilling
trailer with a permanently installed air fill station at the fire hall cost of
$45,000.
∙    They also have a group of well- trained new firefighters
∙    Wastewater Plant continues its exemplary operation even with emergency
breakdowns.
∙    Recreation Department has had many changes in personnel. Pat Bradek is in
charge of operations and has made many changes.
∙    Thanks to the voters for approving a five year levy to bring more money
into the department beginning in 2018.
 
In addition to the nuts and bolts results of operations in the Village we are
constantly improving the Village’s image to the outside world.
The Covered Bridge Festival continues to grow in size, activities,
participation and attendance.
We have received a State grant of $100,000 thanks to our State Rep Dr.
Patterson to build an entertainment pavilion for the use of the Covered Bridge
Festival. It will also be available to any other group that chooses to schedule
it.
Our Christmas Parade continues with a degree of excellence that draws bigger
and bigger crowds every year.
Decorations, property maintenance, spring curbside clean up, and the condition
of our roads and sidewalks with our continuing efforts to eliminate blighted
properties helps make the Village a desirable place to live, work, visit and
enjoy.
I want to thank all of our employees for their dedication and hard work that
makes this village a safe and welcoming place to live and visit.
We are all looking forward to another great year (2017) in Jefferson.
I wish all a safe and prosperous New Year.
Mayor Maloney

∙    Tuesday night 1/10/17 Village Hall had a power outage. The backup
generator activated as planned and we operated all day Wednesday 1/12/17 on the
generator. Thursday after First Energy made a repair we switched back to line
power. There was no loss of continuity and nothing had to be reset. Good test
of operations.

Vince Crawford of Waste Management updated Council with the recycle program for
Jefferson. Vince told Council that the Village of Jefferson recycled about 160
tons in the year 2016. This is up from the year 2015. Crawford gave Council a
flier on some of the items that can be recycled. Some of the items that have
been added in the plastic bottle and containers section along with the glass
bottles and containers. Crawford also told Council that the Jefferson village
Day clean up will be May 13, 2017. Last year the Village Clean up day has over
two more truck filled than the year before.

back again this year staying in the park. She said she was promised by the
administrator last year they would not be back again. She stated they are using

Zwaduk also stated she wanted a promise they would not be back next year. She
stated she is disappointed in the Mayor and the Village Administrator for
letting this happen.

concerns as Betsy Zwaduk. Why the carnies were back this year. They were camped
out for a week and did not leave until almost three today. How did the Chamber
let this happen also.

next year . She promised.

on Cucumber St.

park land as requested by the adjacent property owners.

repair and Truck route rehab Phase III.
We need to submit authorizing legislation which is in Council Packet.
Fire Dept. /Police Department:
Nothing unusual to report.

The alternative homecoming dance event took place without any incidents.
We are not budgeting to replace the folding wall now that everything works
properly.
Items on the Rec Budget for 2018 include: Crossover weight training machine, a
second rehab machine for knees and hips, a new treadmill (will total four), a
replacement elliptical machine and new transportation van without wheelchair
lift.

progress as we move forward.
The part time temporary worker is on the Wastewater payroll having successfully
completed the physical and background check.

Department heads are working on 2018 budget requirements to enable early
discussions with Council.

they are only 1000 watts each and still in working condition. So they could be
used if the Village so desires.

Visitor’s Comments 
Bill Painter of 889 East Beech Street Jefferson Ohio and Corey Jones of
Pierpont Ohio from the Covered Bridge Festival. Presented a Grand Sponsor
Plaque of recognition to the Village of Jefferson for their support to the
Covered Bridge Festival.
Joe Wesley of 1250 Gates Mills Ohio the developer of Oakwood Estates talked
with Council in regard to the Oakwood Estates. He told Council that he is
building nice new homes in the development that will be affordable. He also
told Council that his intentions are to follow the specs according to plan. If
there is a variance needed on some of the homes he will come back to Council
and have the proper paperwork.
Council person Diehl told Wesley that finishing the development is a good
investment for the Village. It will bring new houses and help the property
values.
Administrator Finger told Council that there are three homes under construction
and they all will look different.
Councilperson Hoyson stated that he looked at the houses and they are all
different in external style.
Janet Discher of 366 Fryer Drive told Council that she was concerned with the
type of new house being built. She stated that she did not want the houses to
be cookie cutter houses (all look alike). Discher also asked Council if the
Village could enforce the deed restrictions. Discher also questioned the
variance for the front yard setback.
Solicitor Hamper told Council that the Village cannot enforce or tell the
builder how to build the house. The deed restrictions were set up in the

precede. The project replaces all the traffic signs on State Rt. 46 north and
south through the Village limits and all the traffic signs from SR 46 east on
SR 167 to the Village limits.
There is no cost to the Village for these repairs.

Service Dept.  
Curt’s work force is at full strength with the hiring of Daniel Crumrine as the
replacement dump truck Driver/Utility man.
Pothole repairs with the durapatcher have been completed. The Durapatcher will
be cleaned up and go into storage at the WW Plant.
The property line between East Park and Casey Baxley’s pond has been cleared of
dead shrubs and now has a three rail fence installed on the property line. This
split rail fence was salvaged from a property owner who was replacing it. The
fence looks great and is a much better barrier between the pond and the park.
The fence access gate on N. Cucumber to our road repair material/brush grinding
area will be relocated the second week in November, north to the edge of the
Village owned park land as requested by the adjacent property owners.
All of the Village owned generators have been serviced as agreed between the
Village and our repairs supplier.
We have received the new digital sign to be installed by the Gazebo. Street
Dept. is working with the electrical supplier to install and make ready. This
new sign will make changing messages much easier and faster.
Fire Dept. /Police Department:
No action yet on the Police Department garage.
Recreation Department:
The Rec Dept. staffing has stabilized and everyone is working as a team.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
E. Ashtabula St. sewer line rehab project is progressing faster than I
expected. The repair to the risers and laterals could be done by 11/15/17 at
the current rate of repair.
Communications between the contractor and property owners has been outstanding.
I know of no resident complaints. The Contractor cannot believe how easy it has
been to work with the homeowners and how cooperative they have been.
Curt, Gary and Smolen Engineering all report very positive and professional
work by the contractor.
During the reconstruction we have found sewer lines tied into out Storm lines
and storm lines tied into the sewer lines. We have found broken lines as
expected and lines that we are not sure where they flowed.
This project will cure a lot of problems and prevent many impending future
problems.
Other Items:
We will start putting up Christmas decorations on November 8 th or 9 th .

E. Ashtabula
 
Service Dept.  
The fence access gate on N. Cucumber to our road repair material/brush grinding
area will be relocated rescheduled to week of December 4th , north to the edge
of the Village owned park land as requested by the adjacent property owners.
We have installed the new digital sign by the Gazebo. The Street Dept. crew is
working with the electrical supplier to power up the sign and make ready for
December 2 Christmas parade. Contractors are so busy it is hard to get them for
small jobs.
Patty/SOCC has been seeking funds from philanthropic persons and organizations
to meet our $50,000 match to secure the $100,000 grant for a covered bridge
pavilion. There have been no offers to help.
Our budget presentation will show the Village funding the $50,000 thru cash and
in-kind work. If we do not fund the Village portion we lose the $100,000 grant.
Brobst is scheduled for one more day of dead tree removal (about eight trees).
No time frame is set.
Fire Dept. /Police Department:
We need to discuss the Police Department garage.
Prefab metal 2,500 square ft. with electric is estimated at $20,000
A pole barn 2,500 square ft. with electric is estimated at $68,000.
A Commercial stick and block 2,500 square foot with electric is estimated at
$100,000.
Mayor and Chief Wassie were looking for the prefab metal building but council
wanted to see some other options before budget time.
What is Council’s pleasure to move forward for the budget meeting,
Recreation Department:
Pat has determined that a new van will cost $30,000 at State Purchasing price.
Trade in value for the 2004 van with 119.008 miles is $2,500.
A buyer is willing to give us $3,000 for the van.
We need to declare the 2004 van as surplus and advertise it for sale with a
minimum of $3,000.
Pat is seeking grants to cover one half of the cost for the new van.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
E. Ashtabula St. Sewer repair is progressing as planned. Slip lining and
grouting of laterals is scheduled for week of 12/04/17.
It should take four days to complete the slip lining and grouting. When this is
done the project will go dormant until spring for paving.
The temporary employee will finish at the end of December. We will add back a
temporary employee in April or May.
Other Items:
Tree harvesting is planned on the 13.364 acres we sold to East Beech
Development Corp. on the north edge of the Rush creek property.
Administrator Finger told Council that the new sign at the center of town he is
working on getting is up and running .

Mayor
State of the Village 2017
Once again the Village has ended the year with a sound financial carryover of
$838,397.59. Our self-imposed carryover of 15% reserve would be $688,309.50.
This means we will carryover $150,088.09 more than our minimum of $688309.50
The Department heads, Administration and Council are very watchful in the
spending of tax payers’ dollars.
Here are some of the major accomplishments that were completed during 2017:
Wastewater Department:
Replaced defective sludge pumps and valves at the WW plant.
Replaced leaking air lines and water lines.
Completed a total reconditioning of E. Ashtabula sewer collection system.
EPA surprise inspection resulted in a very positive report of plant operations.
Emergency repair on the sludge press required us to haul liquid until the
repair was completed.
Street Department:
Forestry services of brush pick up and grinding; dead tree removal (38), stump
grinding, and new tree planting (72).
Street paving (Center, W. Cedar, Hillyer, Woodside, N. Franley, Maple, and Wall
Street.
Street repairs (with durapatch, cold patch, and chip sealing); snow removal.
Replaced N. Spruce Street Culvert.
Sidewalk repairs, east side of Business District and Center Street.
Doubled the number of lighted Christmas Displays.
Recreation Department:
Community Action of Ashtabula “Meals on Wheels” continues to rent the kitchen
area at Giddings Hall 40 hours per week for food prep on a new five year
contract. They prepare seven meals per week for 400 senior residents County
wide. They also serve 35 to 50 people at the Giddings Hall
Revenue from the recently passed levy will be budgeted for use in 2018. New
equipment and new carpeting will be added from that revenue.
Recreation Department has added programs and increased soccer, flag football, t
ball and summer youth events and improved Safety Town.
Police:
Replaced two cruisers
Increased local enforcement to keep visitors and residents safe to walk the
streets and have no fear.
Fire:
Increased the number of volunteers and continue to provide constant training.
Completed ISO inspection for insurance certification.
In addition to the nuts and bolts results of operations in the Village we are
constantly improving the Village’s image to the outside world.
The new sidewalks on the east side business district help improve the
professional look in the Business District.
Continued replacement and upgrades of our drinking water and firefighting water
flows in cooperation with Aqua Ohio Water Company enhances the quality of life
and safety of our residents.
The Covered Bridge Festival continues to grow in size, activities,
participation and attendance.
Our Christmas Parade continues with a degree of excellence that draws bigger
and bigger crowds every year.
Village Christmas Decorations almost doubled in number with the purchase of
many of Kennisee Campground’s surplus lighted displays.
Spring curbside clean up, brush pick up, leaf pick up, property maintenance
efforts, the condition of our roads and sidewalks helps make the Village a
desirable place to live, work, visit and enjoy.
I want to thank all of our employees for their dedication and hard work that
makes this village a safe and welcoming place to live and visit.
We are all looking forward to another great year (2018) in Jefferson.
I wish all a safe and prosperous New Year.
Mayor Maloney
FYI: 2018 Village Officials, Members of Committees and Boards

ditch.

is going to be a third step recovery so the people can get comfortable living
in a normal life.

to the Village to change the zoning for the property and it take a process.

Janet Discher of 366 Fryer Drive questioned the deed restriction at the Oakwood
Estates. She said that the first floor is 2000 foot and the second is also does
that match the deed restrictions in the Ordinance.
Solicitor Hamper told Council that the Ordinance did not match the deed
restriction exactly and there should be a motion to amend the Ordinance during
Building and Lands if Council desired to make them match.
Cheryl McCourt owner of the Opal House talked to Council in regard to the men’s
transnational housing recovery service for men that will be located at 228
North Chestnut Street Jefferson Ohio. The residents that will live in the house
are resident’s recovering from addiction and are trying to live a productive
life in society and get back on their feet. The men that live in the house will
have the same rules as the women that live in the Opal House across the Street.
The residents will be drug tested. The will be responsible to stay clean and
sober or the will be kicked out of the program. They volunteer in the community
and love and respect where they live. This is on the high-end spectrum of
mental heath programs.
Teresa Taylor of Jefferson told Council that she worked at the Opal House as a
step-down support person. She has helped residents become productive members of
society; she also stated that there is no crime aloud or permitted out of the
Opal House.
Geraldine Richardson of Ashtabula told Council that she lived in the Opal House
for two years. She told Council that Opal House being there helped build her
life back where she could later move back into a place and live a normal life.
She said she is now sober and working a job doing taxes.
Brittany Gatterello told Council that the Opal House taught her how to be a
grounded woman that could go back in society and live a normal life. She told
Council she had no place to go or live and Opal house took her in and taught
her to be a resident of society.
Jeff Bolander told everyone that being a resident of a structured environment
helps people go out into society and build their life back up and give them the
confidence to live a normal life.
Sherri Bolander told Council she has been sober for eleven years. She
Volunteers at the Opal House and help the residents however she can. She had
helped residents get to the doctor and has helped residents there get driver
licenses so they can go find a job.
Nichole Booth told Council she has been sober for four and half years she moved
into the Opal House when she got out of prison. She said she was taught life
skills and the people running the Opal House saw something in her that she did
not see in herself. She said she has since become a CDCA Chemical Dependent
Counselor. The success story is that the resident can live clean and sober.
They have gotten jobs in town at Hardee’s, McDonald’s, and Golden Dawn.

Visitor’s Comments 
Cheryl McCourt owner of the Opal House talked to Council in regard to the men’s
transactional housing recovery service for men that will be located at 228
North Chestnut Street Jefferson Ohio. Mc Court told Council that she wished to
address some of the objections she has been made aware of. Mc Court told that
she was told by Administrator Terry Finger the house was zoned correctly. Mc
Court told Council that she has received a state grant that will reimburse her
in the amount of $290,000.00 for the purchase of the property. But the grant is
contingent on the zoning. Mc Court talked to Council about the three women that
spoke against the plan stating they saw a man urinating from the balcony of the
house located at 228 North chestnut Street. She stated no men have stayed in
the house. She has had work done on the floor and there were a few men that
came to do the work. She said if the workers did do this they would have had to
walk by bathrooms to get to the balcony and the balcony is roped of. Plus if
they saw this why did they not call the police.
Daniel Wagner of 241 North Chestnut Street spoke against the zoning change.
Wagner stated that the housing would be great for some individuals but he is
concerned about people who use it as a way to get out of jail. Wagner said he
has concerns about a transitional home opening up on his Street. He said his
children play outside and believes that would have to change. Wagner said he
does not love the idea of having to take the freedom away from my children to
ride their bikes in front of my house.
Cayce Baxley ,Tamila Wise, Cheryl Mc Court, Laura Rowan, Kendra Morris,
Christen Sonoski, Nikki Booth, Jason Weesc, Joann Douglas, John Diaz, Jason
Carril, Bernard Grossla, Stephanie Vishak, Lee Parney Heather Diaz and Evan
Howe.
The various people got up and spoke for the zoning to open the transitional
home for men. Most of the stated that they or someone such as family neighbor
or friends have been addicts and place such as the opal house has helped people
live a productive life in society and get back on their feet.

Public Hearing for Section 1246.06 of the Codified Ordinance of the Village of
Jefferson on November 5, 2018 at 7:48 p.m.
Councilperson Damon requested that Joe Burgoon give testimony for the zoning
change being considered to have something on the record. Joe Burgoon, who was
present on behalf of his mother who owns 148 South Sycamore Street, Jefferson,
Ohio 44047, stated that the change contemplated by the proposed ordinance would
affect approximately 20 properties in the Village and would be a positive move
for the Village.
Councilperson Diehl asked Solicitor Hamper whether the proposed ordinance was
limited in scope given the prior discussions about the R3 uses in the planning
commission and some confusion between two provisions of the proposed ordinance.
Solicitor Hamper explained that Paragraph 12 was for existing R3 uses to be
repaired, not rebuilt, and that Paragraph 13 would allow for a person who owns
any plot with a residential use in the industrial area as of the time of the
ordinance to rebuild a R1 use on that plot, which acts to prohibit additional
R3 uses from being built in the industrial area.
Motion by Councilperson Damon to go out of the Public Hearing and back into
regular session at 7:52p.m.

Roll: All yea, motion carried

Review of Council Rules
Ohio Division of Liquor Control
New Liquor License for 22 North Chestnut Street
Mayor Maloney informed everyone about an application for a liquor permit that
was filed and informed Council that they have the opportunity to request a
hearing and requested Solicitor Hamper to explain how the hearing worked.
Solicitor Hamper explained the proper steps to Council on what needs to be done
for the hearing for the new liquor license.
Solicitor Hamper informed Council that the liquor permit was for the building
next to the Diner which used to be a newsstand and that the permit requested
was a D1, D2, and D3 permit, which are for a restaurant to serve spirits,
liquor, beer, and wine. Solicitor Hamper continued that the reason Council was
entitled to request a hearing was because of the Village’s status as a dry
municipality based on a vote in 1933 when Prohibition was repealed. Clerk-
Treasurer Fisher informed Council that they had until November 13, 2018 to
decide whether they wished to request a hearing. Councilperson Damon asked why
the Village would hold a hearing.
Solicitor Hamper answered that it would be to gain information about the
project, understand what sort of occupancy and other plans were made for the
building, and to hear more about the person’s plans to operate a restaurant.
Motion by Councilperson Brabender to have the Clerk Treasurer request a hearing
for the new
Liquor License for 22 North Chestnut Street in Ashtabula County.

Roll: All yea, motion carried

Robert Leach the attorney for Russ Nank talked to Council about the liquor
permit for 22 North Chestnut Street Jefferson Ohio 44047. Robert Leach told
Council that Russ Nank has been a resident of the county for twenty years.
Water and sewer are in place in the building.
Robert Leach told Council that Russ Nank has hope and plans to create a place
that will have a social meeting spot for people to have their shoes shined
along with leather product to buy. While getting your shoes shined you will be
able to have a spirit and relax.
Robert Leach explained the this place will be a old time store that will have
breakfast food a light lunch and snacks to eat while it is open. The permit is
a D1, D2, D3, with no Sunday sales. The business will hold about 20 people
Russ Nank owner of 22 North chestnut Street spoke to Council saying that his
place is not going to be a bar. It is a spirit place where customers can have a
spirit while they are getting their shoes shined. The business will be open
from six a.m. to 7 p.m. at night. Opening date will be sometime in 2019.
Russ Nank also asked if there was still going be a hearing since they were in
public with Council discussing everything.
Mayor Maloney stated to everyone as long as Council was happy with what they
were told a hearing probably would not be needed as long as the State agreed.
Joe Burgoon spoke to Council on behalf of his mother about the residence of 148
South Sycamore Street. Burgoon stated that the industrial zoning has not been
modified since 1995. With this new zoning there will be about twenty homes that
will effect for the good. This also will allow about a half dozen new home that
could be built in the Village.
