Mayor
State of the Village 2018
Once again the Village has ended the year 2018 with a sound financial carryover
of $1,142,303. Our 2017 carryover was $977,519.
The Department heads, Administration and Council are very watchful in the
spending of tax payers’ dollars.
Here are some of the major accomplishments that were completed during 2018:
Wastewater Department:
∙    Completed sludge application update.
∙    Implemented the low level mercury elimination program required in our
operation permit.
∙    Completed smoke testing on the west side of the Village looking for
improper connection and/or broken sewer lines to correct and reduce storm water
infiltration required by our EPA Permit.
∙    Budgeted money for the EPA mandated storm water pollution prevention
permit (SWPPP) project to correct the infiltration of storm water that was
identified in the smoke testing.
∙    Continued upgrades/repairs to current equipment at the plant which enables
better plant efficiency:
   o   Cleaned 360,000 gallon EQ Basin
   o   Repaired EQ Basin diffuser header
   o   Replaced, underground airline to the grit chamber, aeration tank
diffusers, #2 & #3 aeration blower starters, 100 h.p. blower motor, 60 h.p.
blower motor, and the roots digester motor.
Street Department:
∙    Forestry services of brush pick up and grinding; dead tree removal (125),
stump grinding, and new tree planting (123).
∙    Paving (W. Jefferson Street, Rec parking lot, Village Hall, Police
Department/ Giddings Hall parking lot, Muni parking lot ( Chinese Restaurant ).
∙    Street repairs (with durapatch machine, cold patching, and chip sealing);
snow removal.
∙    Replaced storm drains on Popular Street by fairgrounds.
Recreation Department:
∙    Community Action of Ashtabula “Meals on Wheels” continues to rent the
kitchen area at Giddings Hall 40 hours per week for food prep on a five year
contract. They prepare and distribute over 2,800 meals per week for senior
residents, County wide. They also serve 35 to 50 people daily five days per
week at the Giddings Hall.
∙    Revenue from the 2018 Rec levy was used to purchase/repair weight room
equipment, a new transportation van, new carpeting and repairs to roof leaks.
∙    Recreation Department has a new senior coordinator with lots of new
programs.
∙    The center has added programs and increased soccer, flag football, t ball
and summer youth events and improved Safety Town.
Police:
∙    Added a police resource officer at the Elementary School to join one
already in place at the Jr./ Senior High Schools. The wages for these positions
are being paid from the school system funds not the Village funds.
∙    Increased Training for officers to meet new State Requirements.
∙    Purchased new body armor, body cameras, and high resolution property
surveillance cameras.
∙    Maintained our high level of local enforcement to keep visitors and
residents safe to walk the streets and have no fear.
Fire:
∙    Increased the number of volunteers and continue to provide constant
training.
∙    Upgraded equipment such as Scott air packs, thermal imaging sensor, and
turn out gear.
∙    Completed ISO inspection for insurance certification.
 
In addition to the nuts and bolts results of operations in the Village we are
constantly improving the Village’s image to the outside world.
Continued replacement and upgrades of our drinking water flows and firefighting
water flows in cooperation with Aqua Ohio Water Company, these improvements
enhance the quality of life and safety of our residents.
The Covered Bridge Festival continues to grow in size, activities,
participation and attendance.
Our Christmas Parade continues with a degree of excellence that draws bigger
and bigger crowds every year.
Village lighted Christmas Decorations and displays continue to draw visitors
into town to ride around and view them.
Spring curbside clean up, brush pick up, leaf pick up, property maintenance
efforts, the condition of our roads and sidewalks helps make the Village a
desirable place to live, work, visit and enjoy.
There are 10 specific actions for junk vehicles and 4 specific actions for
debris/filthy accumulations under way that will continue into 2019. Failure of
property owners to correct these violations voluntarily will lead to legal
prosecution after January 31.
 
I want to thank all of our employees for their dedication and hard work that
makes this village a safe and welcoming place to live and visit.
I would also like to thank our residents and property owners for working co-
operatively with us to make our village a shining star among
We are all looking forward to another great year (2019) in Jefferson.
I wish all a safe and prosperous New Year.
Mayor Maloney

Corrections or Additions to the Agenda
Changed “Ordinance” to “Resolution” and “O” to “R” for the Resolution to be
read at the meeting.
Added a Motion to Suspend Council Rules and a Motion to Adopt to the Motion for
the Resolution to be read at the meeting.
Visitor’s Comments
None
Finance
Motion by Councilperson Diehl for the First Reading of Resolution Number 19-R-
3138, Seconded by Councilperson Hoyson
Discussion:
Councilperson Damon asked if the replacement was a full replacement.
Administrator Finger said no, it was just to take off and replace the rubber
part of the roof, but the work was guaranteed for twenty years.
Councilperson Diehl asked how much the work was going to cost. Administrator
Finger answered that he had an estimate of $88,000 to replace the roof, but
that the Village was going to bid the work and the first bid advertisement
would be in the paper on Friday, February 1 st .
Councilperson Brabender asked for clarification that there would be no peaking
of the roof. Mayor Maloney said that was correct.
Councilperson Snyder asked if it was okay to perform the work when the weather
is cold. Administrator Finger said it was okay because the work is cold-
applied.
Councilperson Snyder asked if the twenty-year guarantee still applies when it
is cold. Administrator Finger said yes, the cold-applied application sections
off the roof pieces at a time and the whole roof will not be exposed at a
single time.
Councilperson Damon asked if the $88,000 estimate included just material or if
it also included labor. Administrator Finger said it included both.
Councilperson Diehl asked if the $88,000 was in the last budget. Administrator
Finger said yes, it was.
Councilperson Diehl asked what in the budget had to be removed to accommodate
the roof replacement at this time. Administrator Fingers aid nothing because it
was budgeted the entire time. Administrator Finger continued by saying that the
Village had spent about $8,000 per year in temporary repairs for the last four
years and this replacement is better than trying to do another temporary
repair.
 
Roll:    All yea, motion carried
 
Motion by Councilperson Diehl to Suspend Council Rules for Resolution Number
19-R-3138, Seconded by Councilperson Hoyson
Roll:   All yea, motion carried
 
Motion by Councilperson Diehl to Adopt Resolution Number 19-R-3138, Seconded by
Councilperson Hoyson
Roll:   All yea, motion carried

commented that it was “raining” in the conference room during the leaks last
week.

∙    Our tree management efforts have paid off. There were a few isolated power
outages in the village. One pine tree blew over and two large limbs broke off.
∙    We continue to have repair issues (parts failures) with our snow plow
tractor. If you receive complaints please let the person know that we keep
repairing and resuming snow removal ASAP.
Fire Dept. /Police Department:
∙    Nothing new to report.
Recreation Department:
∙    Swipe card access has been activated. There were several start- up
computer related issues that have been addressed. All activity has been in the
morning with zero activity in the evening.
∙    Bids were opened for the roof replacement. Since the bid opening there has
been a lot of questions, discussions, and additional information gathered.
Solicitor Hamper has been actively involved to assure that the Village follows
accepted procedures.
∙    I have recommended that we reject all bids and start this project over.
∙    Solicitor Hamper will provide Administration and Council his best advice
to assure that the proper procedures and actions are in the best interest of
everyone involved.
∙    Pat Bradek has started working on the Village web page re-development.
Progress has been slow.

∙    Plant operations are running at fully acceptable levels.

2/14/19 – paving ASAP after asphalt plants open,
   o   Giddings Park Covered Bridge Pavilion – Design is 95% complete. Must be

   o   Engineers estimate for the pavilion is below the $150,000.00 money we

   o   Popular Street Culvert repair - a fall project.

exiting contract out to look over all the options. They also asked how much the
rates would go up if they dropped the recycling program.

probably more than what they are offering now.

the Committee to look over. The committee would them pick a few candidates for
Council to interview.

∙    We had one minor roof leak during a heavy rainstorm which was repaired.

∙    The emergency repairs do not eliminate the need to replace the roof.
Council and Administration will need to formulate a plan to replace the roof.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
∙    Plant operations are running at fully acceptable levels.
∙    The Wastewater plant is under pressure to eliminate all I and I from the
west side of the village. Gary is interviewing for two part time helpers to
clean and televise as much of the collection system as possible.
∙    There are two OPWC grant requests being prepared for wastewater dealing
with requirements of our operating permit.

the subdivision requirements to discuss smaller square foot requirements for
the first floor. Mike Hamper will map out the legal process involved to make
sure we meet the letter of the law. This will be a hot topic once we begin.

and as of right now we should have no leaks. The emergency repairs do not
eliminate the need to replace the roof. Council and Administration will need to
formulate a plan to replace the roof.
∙    AC/heating unit #3 is scheduled to be replaced 6/18/19 by Ogram heating &
Cooling. Current unit is 32 years old and repairs wouldn’t be cost effective.
New unit is a 7.5 Ton Carrier and it comes with a 10 Yr. warranty on heat
exchanger, 5 yrs. on the compressor and 1 yr. parts and labor.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
∙    Plant operations are running at fully acceptable levels.
∙    The Wastewater plant is under pressure to eliminate all I and I from the
west side of the village. Gary has interviewed for two part time helpers to
clean and televise as much of the collection system as possible. Tyler Maylish
has been hired for summer help and Frankie Fioritto is being recommended for
hire. Frankie has passed his background check
∙    There are two OPWC grant requests being prepared for wastewater dealing
with requirements of our operating permit.
∙    I have requested for our sewer guys to inspect and camera the whole line
on Elm St. If any repairs are needed, I would recommend that we do them before
the whole street gets newly paved. Our records from previous smoke tests look
ok though.
Other Items:
∙    Centerra permit approved.
∙    Paving plans have been completed for Oakwood Estates to pave all streets
to meet the Village specifications.
∙    New owners of Oakwood Estates are the majority of stake holders by virtue
of holding title to all the undeveloped lots. They are requesting to re- open
the subdivision requirements to discuss smaller square foot requirements for
the first floor. Mike Hamper will map out the legal process involved to make
sure we meet the letter of the law. This will be a hot topic once we begin.
∙    We finally received an estimate for the damage caused by our mower to the
marker at the Historical Society. Total damage was $2,325 and a liability claim
was initiated at Glazier insurance. No deductible for liability claims
∙    Administrator Martuccio told Council the demo agreement for the Spang
house has been approved.

Recreation Department:
I have contacted Mr. Polta and Mr. Brockett at A-Tech and they are excited to
help with the building of the cupola for the covered bridge pavilion. No answer
yet.
Building Technicians Corporation did some more preventative repairs on the Rec
CTR roof and, even after this heavy rain, we have no leaks. The emergency
repairs do not eliminate the need to replace the roof. Council and
Administration will need to formulate a plan to replace the roof.
AC/heating unit #3 was replaced 6/18/19 by Ogram heating & Cooling. Working
well.
Our custodian Robin Cottrell has given her resignations. Connie Bayt is already
working for us at Rec. CTR and is being recommended by Pat Bradek for the
position.
Summer sports programs are being well attended.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
Plant operations are running at fully acceptable levels.
The Wastewater plant is under pressure to eliminate all I and I from the west
side of the village. We have hired two part time helpers to clean and televise
as much of the collection system as possible. They have started by smoke
testing W Satin and W Jefferson. It looks like the streets that have curb
drains are the ones that are responsible for majority of infiltration. Smoke
was observed coming out of the drains therefore, storm sewers are connected to
sanitary. More investigation is needed to come up with a solution. We need to
determine if lining the sanitary lines is sufficient and where would the excess
storm water go to once lining is complete.
The two OPWC grant requests prepared for wastewater were submitted. The first
one pertains to cleaning, televising and lining our sanitary lines and we have
reason to believe that it will be funded based on the scoring received.
The second one pertaining replacement of wastewater bridge and stairs might
also get funded but received a lower score. We have a meeting 7/18/19 at the
County Engineers office to discuss our scoring.
We have inspected and televised the whole line on Elm St. and according to Gary
no repairs are needed before paving.

Visitor’s Comments
Lucy Rowe of 121 West Satin Street spoke to Council about a incident that
happened on her property and she feels concerned with the Past and Present
Administrator. There has been incidents from the past and present Administrator
requesting the Village workers to go onto her private property. The Village
Street Department came onto her property and removed longs that have been on
her property for ten months. The Administrator did not communicate with her
about removing them or ask her permission to come on to her property. She also
told Council that her ninety-two-year-old mother rents from the new
Administrator and he about the issue.
Solicitor Hamper to everyone that the Administrator did not legally have to
communicate to Lucy Rowe. The property that the Village Street Department
employees in in the Village right of way.
Administrator Martuccio explained to everyone that he had tried to contact Lucy
Rowe but did not get ahold of her. He told Council that the Streets Department
crew was just around the corner and he asked them to take the logs that were in
the font yard down to our dump site and put them separate from the other brush
if she still wanted them.
Administrator Martuccio explained to everyone that he had no intention to up
anyone.

We are actively looking for funding to replace the roof. 
We had a meeting with Jennifer Brown from CT Consultants and Michael Antonille
from USDA. USDA might be able to finance the roof with a loan. At this point it
doesn’t look like we can find any grants, just loans. Nopec also has a loan
program that we are looking into.
On 10/15/19 our van driver turned a corner a little to tight and ended up
scraping the metal post protecting the corner of the DDM building. Damage is
confined to the rear panel on the driver side of the senior van. Our insurance
was notified and we have an estimate for $5,346.41 from Custom Quality for the
repairs. Repair time is estimated to be 2 weeks.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
Plant operations are running at fully acceptable levels.
The Wastewater plant is under pressure to eliminate all I and I from the west
side of the village.
We now have 3 OPWC grant requests prepared and submitted.
The first one pertains to cleaning, televising and lining our sanitary lines
and we have reason to believe that it will be funded based on the scoring
received.
The second one has to do with emergency repairs namely the replacement of
wastewater bridge. OPWC has verbally committed to a 90% Grant ($99,100) pending
application submittal.
The third one had originally been submitted to OPWC for the Bridge and the
Stairs.
However, since we are now funding part of bridge with emergency funds, we have
to submit a final app to Small Gov. and deduct the amount of emergency funding
that we should be receiving.
On 10/11/19 our sewer line backed up on E. Satin St in proximity of the
Lutheran church. The basement at 68 E Satin was flooded with sewage. I had to
call Servpro for cleanup. Total cost $4,539.34
Police:
Fire:
We had a meeting with Jennifer Brown from CT Consultants and Michael Antonille
from USDA. USDA might be able to offer $50,000 grant towards the purchase of
our new Fire Truck and finance the balance at 3% for 10 years reducing our
annual payment from about $90,000 to about $60,000. We are working to submit an
application to them ASAP.

Operating normal tasks.
Will be planting trees weather permitting.
Recreation Department:
We are actively looking for funding to replace the roof. 
We are in the process of gathering all information needed to submit a loan
application with USDA. At this point it doesn’t look like we can find any
grants, just loans.
Connie Bayt has resigned as custodian/desk clerk as of January 3rd ,2020. Pat
Bradek has been looking for a replacement. In the interim, our previous
custodian Robin Cottrell is going to help until we find a replacement.
Tammy Strasser currently employed at the Rec Center is being recommended for
the position of van driver.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
Plant operations are running at fully acceptable levels.
The Wastewater plant is under pressure to eliminate all I and I from the west
side of the village.
We now have 3 OPWC grant requests prepared and submitted.
The first one pertains to cleaning, televising and lining our sanitary lines
and we have reason to believe that it will be funded based on the scoring
received.
The second one has to do with emergency repairs namely the replacement of
wastewater bridge. OPWC has approved our application. The total cost for this
project is $110,000, of that, $99,000 is Grant money.
The third one had originally been submitted to OPWC for the Bridge and the
Stairs. However, since we are now funding part of bridge with emergency funds,
we have submitted a final app to Small Gov. for the balance.
Police:
Fire:
We had a meeting with Jennifer Brown from CT Consultants and Michael Antonille
from USDA. USDA might be able to offer $100,000 grant towards the purchase of
our new Fire Truck and finance the balance at 3% for 10 years reducing our
annual payment from about $90,000 to about $55,000. We have completed and
submitted the application. Waiting for USDA in Columbus to review it.
Other Items:
Solicitor Hamper is working on finalizing dispatch contracts for police and
fire.

Mayor
State of the Village 2019
Once again, the Village has ended the year 2019 with a sound financial
carryover of $1,300,000.
The Department heads, Administration and Council are very watchful in the
spending of taxpayers’ dollars.
Here are some of the major accomplishments that were completed during 2019:
Wastewater Department:
Completed emergency repairs to a manhole at the WWTP that suffered severe
damage after the 2 major storms we had this summer.
Implemented the low-level mercury elimination program required in our operation
permit.
Completed smoke testing on the west side of the Village looking for improper
connection and/or broken sewer lines to correct and reduce storm water
infiltration required by our EPA Permit. We have identified 4 sections of our
sewer system that are going to be slip-lined in 2020 with OPWC’s funding.
Cleaned and televised all sewer lines in the Elliott allotment.
Continued upgrades/repairs to current equipment at the plant which enables
better plant efficiency.
Replaced Gary’s pick up with a new utility truck.
Street Department:
Forestry services of brush pick up and grinding; we removed numerous dead
trees, stump grinding, and new tree planting.
Paving: Elm Street, Sycamore Street (Phase 3 truck route) and Frayer Drive
(paving was paid by the developer and the Village crew did the burming).
Street repairs (with durapatch machine, cold patching, and chip sealing); snow
removal.
Replaced storm drains on East Erie Street by Kids Only.
This summer we received our new backhoe, dump truck and Kubota utility vehicle.
Recreation Department:
Community Action of Ashtabula “Meals on Wheels” continues to rent the kitchen
area at Giddings Hall 40 hours per week for food prep on a five-year contract.
The number of meals they provide for senior residents in the County has been
steadily increasing. They also serve 40 to 60 people daily five days per week
at the Giddings Hall.
Revenue from the 2019 Rec levy was used to purchase/repair weight room
equipment, new carpeting in the hallway and most of all for repairs to roof
leaks.
Recreation Department has a new senior coordinator Michelle Adkins. She has
been well received by our seniors and is doing a great job in growing the
program.
All youth events such as soccer, flag football, t ball was very successful this
summer. In addition, all summer programs for elementary age children sold out!
More classes for all age groups were added.
The new van is being used to provide transportation for seniors in town as well
as many scheduled senior trips.
Last, but not least, our Covered Bridge Pavilion has been completed. We have
received many praises for this majestic structure. We hope that this one of a
kind structures would serve our residents for years to come and be a point of
attraction for people visiting our beautiful town.
Police:
Increased Training for officers to meet new State Requirements.
Purchased new police cruiser.
Maintained our high level of local enforcement to keep visitors and residents
safe to walk the streets and have no fear.
Fire:
We continue to provide constant training for our Volunteer Firefighters.
Upgraded equipment such as Scott air packs, thermal imaging sensor, and turn
out gear.
Completed application with USDA for a Grant/Loan to finance the new fire truck.
Admin:
After 18 years as Village Administrator, Terry Finger has retired, passing the
baton down to Pasquale Martuccio. We welcome him to his new job. I would like
to thank Terry for his work and dedication to the Village and for making
Jefferson a better place to work and live. He will be missed.
Purchased a new admin vehicle to replace the old pickup truck.
 
In addition to the nuts and bolts results of operations in the Village we are
constantly improving the Village’s image to the outside world.
Continued replacement and upgrades of our drinking water flows and firefighting
water flows in cooperation with Aqua Ohio Water Company, these improvements
enhance the quality of life and safety of our residents.
The Covered Bridge Festival continues to grow in size, activities,
participation and attendance. The new Covered Bridge Pavilion has definitely
given the event a boost.
Our Christmas Parade continues with a degree of excellence that draws bigger
and bigger crowds every year.
Village lighted Christmas Decorations and displays continue to draw visitors
into town to ride around and view them.
Spring curbside clean up, brush pick up, leaf pick up, property maintenance
efforts, the condition of our roads and sidewalks helps make the Village a
desirable place to live, work, visit and enjoy.
We constantly monitor properties in the Village that are not in compliance with
our maintenance code. This year we demolished the house at 123 N. Chestnut.
I want to thank all of our employees for their dedication and hard work that
makes this village a safe and welcoming place to live and visit.
I would also like to thank our residents and property owners for working co-
operatively with us to make our village a shining star among
We are all looking forward to another great year (2020) in Jefferson.
I wish all a safe and prosperous New Year.
Mayor Maloney

Street Dept. 
Brobst finished cutting down most of the trees on our dangerous/dead tree list.
Stumps will be ground in the spring-summer of 2020.
Operating normal tasks.
We planted over 100 trees. We have about 75 more to plant weather permitting.
Phase IV truck route has been funded and CT Consultants has started preliminary
surveying for final engineering.
Twin culvert repair project is on hold until we hear about the outcome of our
application submitted to ODOT. I hope to have an answer soon.
Recreation Department:
We are actively looking for different options and funding to replace the roof. 
Connie Bayt has resigned as custodian/desk clerk as of January 3rd ,2020. Pat
Bradek has interviewed and selected Karla Zavada for the part-time custodian
position. Need a motion to hire Karla pending background check and passing the
physical.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
Plant operations are running at fully acceptable levels.
The Wastewater plant is under pressure to eliminate all I and I from the west
side of the village.
We now have 3 OPWC grant requests prepared and submitted.
The first one pertains to cleaning, televising and lining our sanitary lines.
We are working with CT Consultants to finalize the details for this project.
The second one has to do with emergency repairs namely the replacement of
wastewater bridge. OPWC has approved our application. The total cost for this
project is $110,000, of that, $99,000 is Grant money. Working with Smolen on
different options to minimize bridge downtime and access to the WWTP.
The third one had originally been submitted to OPWC for the Bridge and the
Stairs. However, since we are now funding part of bridge with emergency funds,
we have submitted a final app to Small Gov. for the balance.
Police:
Fire:
FIRETRUCK UPDATE: I have been in contact with Mike at USDA and he indicated
that our application is still being processed. He doesn’t foresee any problems
at this point, and we can order the firetruck and not jeopardize USDA funding.
He also said that USDA has not done their appropriations for 2020 just yet. We
have until the end of this month to order the new firetruck and still receive
2019 pricing. If we order the truck and we don’t get funding from USDA, we
still have about 6 months to arrange for a loan from any local bank.
Other Items:
Solicitor Hamper is working on finalizing dispatch contracts for police and
fire.

Alex Sarna and myself to a NE Ohio Trenching and Confined Space Safety
Conference on February 12 sponsored by the OHIO Bureau of Workers Compensation.
Need a motion to amend section 254.03 of our Code regarding (HSA)
contributions.

wastewater bridge. OPWC has approved our application. The total cost for this
project is $110,000, of that, $99,000 is Grant money. Working with Smolen on
different options to minimize bridge downtime and access to the WWTP.

on our fire truck loan. We are working with bond council and USDA to close on
this transaction by June 1 st , 2020. Our yearly payment starting in 2021 is
estimated to be $53,250.
 
Other Items:
 
Need an EMERGENCY bond ordinance for the fire truck.
Need council to adopt Planning Commission’s recommendation in regard to signage
for Sanders Market/True Value. If council is in favor, we need to instruct our
solicitor to prepare legislation for next council meeting.
Need Council to approve the purchase (see agreement) of a small tract of land
by Poplar St. and Falcon Way. The idea is to use such land in the future when
Falcon Way gets improved and to correct the sharp curve we currently have when
transitioning from Poplar St. to Falcon Way.
Covid-19: We continue to monitor the situation and make necessary changes to
comply with Gov. DeWine’s orders. My hope is that next month we might start
seeing a substantial drop in infections and that our Gov. might reopen some of
the businesses that have been ordered to close.

VILLAGE OF JEFFERSON
COUNCIL MEETING

Meeting Minutes of May 20, 2020

Visitor’s Comments (five-minute limit per council rule #13)
Visitor’s Comments
 
Steven Sekenina of 322 Elliot spoke to Council about the Board of Zoning
appeals decision of changing the requirement for the R2 2000 square feet
requirement. He asked how they could approve the variance when the footage for
the first floor is 1325. The property owners knew before they even purchased
the lot on May 26 that it needed to be 2000 square feet on the first floor.
 
Dave Chah of 425 Woodside spoke to Council about the Board of Zoning Appeals
decision to approve the variance of the square footage of the house. He stated
in the development of the allotment the 2000 square footage was in the
paperwork and nothing lower.
 
Mark Lyerly spoke to Council regarding his disappointment in the Board of
Zoning Appeals decision to approve the variance of the lot 346 Oakwood Estates.
He asked if the board of Zoning appeals gave the reasons as to why they chose
to approve the variance. The 2000 square footage in the R2 District is clearly
explained in the Ordinance.
 
Administrator Martuccio explained that the seven points the Solicitor drew up
for the Zoning Board of Appeals was to help them with their decision on the
variance. It did not steer the board on any decision, and he had no explanation
as to why the board chose to give the variance.
 
Linda Keifer of 353 Frayer told the Council that the Bissell’s should have to
build a home the size that is required in the Oakwood Estate zoning
requirements. They knew when they bought the property what the requirements
were.
 
Steven Sekenina of 322 Elliot told Council that they should follow the rules
just as everyone else that bought in the Oakwood Estate followed the rules that
are in place.
 
Diane Miller told Council that they bought the property because of the
surrounding and the beautiful area. They were told when they bought it about
the requirements, and they followed the lot size that was put in place in 1982.
If the Board of Zoning Appeals changes the current rules in the R2 it would
affect the property values in the area. The Board of Zoning Appeals decision
was unethical and unfair to the property owners in the development.
 
Mary Talcott of 398 Frayer told Council she was upset with the Board of Zoning
Appeals decision. The Oakwood Estate development was set up in 1980 along with
the set back and size of the house. They went against what has been in place
for years.
 
Janet Discher of 366 Frayer asked Council if this can be stopped before the
house is built. They are cutting trees down and marking the utilities to build
the house. The Board of Zoning Appeals decision must be stopped and can the
Village of Jefferson appeal the decision and stop the building of the house
thru the Common Pleas Court.
 
Administrator Martuccio told everyone at the meeting that the next step is to
appeal the decision with the Common Pleas Court and the court system will
decide on the ruling. The Courts can consider a injunction to have the property
owners not move forward on building the house.
 
David Chah of 425 Woodside told Council that his agreement was in place with
Wesley which required that all the houses to be built would be 2000 square on
the first floor.
 
Mayor Maloney told everyone that the Village has never been in favor of spot
zoning.

Street Dept.  
Stumps will be ground in the spring-summer of 2020.
Operating normal tasks.
We are moving ahead with Phase IV truck route. Opening bid set for June 17. We
then have 60 days to award the job.
We are working with BWC to obtain a grant for the purchase of a Vermeer Vac-
Tron vacuum trailer (75% grant).
Recreation Department:
We are thinking about reopening the Rec center for select activities and
reduced hours. Target reopening date is June 29. Most of the center and
activities will be running with the big exception being the fitness room. At
this point, due to the covid restrictions, we don’t feel like we could open the
fitness room. We are working to provide more details on how and what we will be
offering in the coming weeks.
Roof project is postponed.
We are tacking pre-school applications. Because of the new rules we will only
be allowed 9 kids instead of 12.
 
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
Plant operations are running at fully acceptable levels.
The Wastewater plant is under pressure to eliminate all I and I from the west
side of the village. We are working with CT consultants and the EPA to renew
our permit.
All projects at Wastewater and sewer related are on hold until OPWC has a
better idea of how their funding is going to be affected.
Police:
Tim Blon will be retiring August 1st, 2020. He will be taking vacation and
personal time up to such date. JALHS intends to hire Tim as a part time school
resource officer. His pay and benefits will be handled by the school. However,
Jefferson PD will be holding his commission. The Village will provide the Crown
Vic police car, pay for car insurance, car maintenance, bond & liability
insurance. We are going to need a MOU with the school that also spells out how
we use our in-kind for the expenses we will incur because of this arrangement.
Solicitor Hamper has prepared a draft for review.
Meghann Stell has submitted a resignation letter effective 6/21/2020. She has
found employment elsewhere. Her duties are being reassigned to other staff
members.
 
Fire:
 
Other Items:
On June 4th,2020 I received a petition signed by 20 residents of the Oakwood
Estates questioning the decision adopted by the BZA on June 1st ,2020. The
petitioners srongly disagree with the BZA’s decision to grant a variance for
the Bissell’s for their new home to be built on sublot 346 of the Oakwood
Estates.
The proposed home does not meet the minimum 2,000 SqFt requirement for the R-
2 district. We need a Council motion to authorize Solicitor Hamper to appeal
the BZA decision.
We had to replace the AC coil and complessor (over 27 years old) for the back
section of town hall. Total cost was $4,300 for a 4 Ton Seer 16 unit. We have
NOPEC grant money to pay for this expense.
Tall grass letters have been sent to property owners in violation.
Waste Management has agreed to a Village cleanup day set for August 8th,2020.
Covid-19: We continue to monitor the situation and make necessary changes to
comply with Gov. DeWine’s orders. We are starting to see significant reductions
in some companies’ payroll taxes. We are asking all departments to be mindful
of all non-essential expenses. Overtime is to be reduced to a minimum and
granted only when absolutely necessary.

Visitor’s Comments (five-minute limit per council rule #13)
Nathan Bissell of 82 W. Ashtabula Street spoke to council about his concern
with
how quickly the 36 hour notice of the meeting was. He stated that he has many
Jefferson Village constituents that partake in the local syrup business that he
is
involved in and he considers the council a “mini-democracy.” He asked what
constitutes an emergency. He believes that the BZA weighed all the criteria,
that they
are smart and voted their conscience. He said that is why the members of the
BZA
were appointed in the first place. He said that increasing the square footage
would
cause financial hardship and that those who are in office have a financial
responsibility
to create a foundation for those moving into Jefferson. He also stated that
believes that
the general fund was used to benefit or produce gain of individuals on Council.
Steven Sekenina of 322 Elliot spoke to Council about his opinions of financial
ruin. He
described how he and his wife had upheld the Deed Restrictions without
requesting a
change from Council. They were in the same position and chose to increase the
square
footage to meet the zoning requirements. He suggested that the community wants
to
maintain its zoning integrity. He said that is what zoning is for, to protect
these
situations from happening.
Victoria Miller of 252 Susan Drive asked what qualifies as reason to declare
emergencies. Solicitor Hamper replied that the meeting was set up within the
statutory
time limit. She described that she was confused because zoning had been changed
for a
halfway house in a zoned district. She reminded Council that in April of 2018
there
was an incidence of a deed restriction that involved a second floor 2000k
square foot
situation.

Street Dept.  
We have added a Part-Time Equipment Operator to the wage ordinance pending
Council approval.
Brobst was in town to cut down dead and dangerous trees.
Operating normal tasks.
Started sidewalk work on Dorset Rd.
Will be doing concrete work for the Jr. High & High school as part of the in-
kind we owe the schools.
Work on phase IV truck route (E. Erie street) will start this week. All
businesses in the area are excited about the improvements and have been alerted
to changes in traffic patterns. Construction is expected to last anywhere from
4 to 6 weeks depending on weather.
We are working with BWC to obtain a grant for the purchase of a Vermeer Vac-
Tron vacuum trailer (75% grant).
 
Recreation Department:
We have reopened the Rec Center on reduced hours and only for those activities
that present a lower risk for Covid spread. Kids classes and sports are having
no issues and people are excited to be back. The fitness room remains closed
and we had to cancel all senior activities due to health department directives.
We are waiting to see when and what activities can be added in the coming
weeks.
Roof project was postponed right at the start of Covid-19 due to budget
uncertainties. However, the last couple of torrential rains have caused some
damage. I feel that we should try to find funds to do the part of the roof with
the biggest issues. We should have a finance committee meeting before next
council meeting to see if this might be a possibility.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
Plant operations are running at fully acceptable levels.
The Wastewater plant is under pressure to eliminate all I and I from the west
side of the village. We are working with CT consultants and the EPA to renew
our permit.
The sewer lining project has been released and approved for financing by OPWC.
Working with Gary and CT Consultants to finalize details. The plan is to reline
5,500 LF of our sewers on the west side of town.
The bridge and stairs project has also been approved and we are working with
Smolen to finalize the plans. Both above projects are expected to start
sometime in the fall.
 
Police:
We are working on finalizing the MOU with Mr. Montanaro. I hope to have it
signed this week.
We currently have a 2009 and a 2011 cruiser that are reaching the end of their
service life. I will be working with USDA to see if they can help with grant/
loan funding.
We have added a “Part Time Police Secretary” to our wage ordinance to be
approved by council tonight. Maria Sharp (currently a Part Time Class B
occasional) has been doing the secretarial work since Covid started. Mayor and
I spoke with Maria and she indicated that she would be happy to take on
secretarial responsibilities and she feels knowledgeable about her duties.
 
Fire:
 
Need a motion to accept Mayors’ and Chief Lacheys’ recommendation to hire Aaron
Painter as Fire Training/Fire Runs.
Other Items:
I would like to ask for a motion to schedule a Finance Committee meeting before
our next Council meeting on August 17, 2020 at 6:30 PM to discuss budget.
On July 27th Larry Carlson submitted a resignation letter from the Board of
Zoning Appeals
112 S. Elm St. has been sold.
Village cleanup day set for August 8th,2020.
Covid-19: We continue to monitor the situation and make necessary changes to
comply with Gov. DeWine’s orders. We are starting to see significant reductions
in some companies’ payroll taxes. We are asking all departments to be mindful
of all non-essential expenses. Overtime is to be reduced to a minimum and
granted only when necessary.

Street Dept.  
Operating normal tasks.
Concrete work for the Jr. High & High school is almost complete. Street crew
will continue with sidewalk replacement in areas of need.
Work on phase IV truck route (E. Erie street) is underway. All businesses in
the area are excited about the improvements and have been alerted to changes in
traffic patterns. Construction is expected to last for another 4 weeks
depending on weather.
We are working with BWC to obtain a grant for the purchase of a Vermeer Vac-
Tron vacuum trailer (75% grant).
 
Recreation Department:
   
We have reopened the Rec Center on reduced hours and only for those activities
that present a lower risk for Covid spread. Kids classes and sports are having
no issues and people are excited to be back. The fitness room remains closed
and we had to cancel all senior activities due to health department directives.
We are waiting to see when and what activities can be added in the coming
weeks.
Roof project: We have an agreement with Damschroder to replace the east side
roof. The total cost for this section is $ 49.929.30 and work is expected to
start by the end of this month.
 
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
Plant operations are running at fully acceptable levels.
The Wastewater plant is under pressure to eliminate all I and I from the west
side of the village. We are working with CT consultants and the EPA to renew
our permit.
The sewer lining project will be advertised for bids in the weeks to come. Our
WWTP personnel have been busy cleaning and televising the sewers ahead of
lining. However, our jet mounted sewer camera is not meant for this kind of
work and is not capable of producing the required reports ahead of lining. For
this reason, we had MTech come and demo a self-propelled sewer camera. We were
all impressed with the camera and after a week of negotiations we decided to
purchase it for the cost of $38,255.28. Camera is scheduled for delivery
tomorrow 08/18/2020. The plan is to reline 5,500 LF of our sewers on the west
side of town.
The bridge and stairs project has also been approved and we are working with
Smolen to finalize the plans. Both above projects are expected to start
sometime in the fall.
 
Police:
We are working on finalizing the MOU with Mr. Montanaro. I sent it over for
signature. Waiting to get it back.
We currently have a 2009 and a 2011 cruiser that are reaching the end of their
service life. I will be working with USDA to see if they can help with grant/
loan funding.
 
Fire:
Other Items:
 
Village cleanup was a success. Next year we need to make sure that our
residents understand that big fabric items such as mattresses, box springs,
couches and similar items need to be wrapped in plastic and sealed with duck
taped. Waste Management will not pick up those items any longer unless those
requirements are met. This year we had to send our street dept to collect all
items left behind by WM. WM did provide a big dumpster at no charge.
Covid-19: We continue to monitor the situation and make necessary changes to
comply with Gov. DeWine’s orders. We are starting to see significant reductions
in some companies’ payroll taxes. We are asking all departments to be mindful
of all non-essential expenses. Overtime is to be reduced to a minimum and
granted only when necessary.

IV of truck
route
 
 
Street Dept.  
Operating normal tasks.
Concrete work for the Jr. High & High school is complete. Street crew will
continue with sidewalk replacement in areas of need.
Work on phase IV truck route (E. Erie street) is underway. All businesses in
the area are excited about the improvements and have been alerted to changes in
traffic patterns. Construction is expected to last for another 4 weeks
depending on weather.
 
Recreation Department:
We are reopening the Rec center starting today. Most of the classes are going
to be back with a few exceptions. We are going to use some of the CARES Act
moneys we received to pay for an independent contractor that would be doing the
extra cleaning required for Covid-19 compliance. The exercise room will be open
to a restricted number of participants at one time. The weight room remains
closed and we had to cancel all senior activities due to health department
directives. We are waiting to see when and what activities can be added in the
coming weeks.
Roof project: The south-east section of the roof designated as Phase 2 is now
done and I am very pleased with Damschroder for the quality of their work.
However, after the heavy storm we had last week we experienced a very large
leak coming from the south-west part of the roof designated as Phase 1. The
leak was extensive enough to cause some drywall damage as water was literally
pouring in. The floor also got soaked but we were able to dry it up. I was able
to locate and temporarily fix the tear in the membrane to stop more water from
coming in. I also scheduled Damschroder to come back on September 15 to replace
this section as well. The cost for this section is going to be $49,367.56.
 
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
Plant operations are running at fully acceptable levels.
The Wastewater plant is under pressure to eliminate all I and I from the west
side of the village. We are working with CT consultants and the EPA to renew
our permit.
The sewer lining project was advertised for bids. Bid opening is 9/9/2020 at
noon. Our WWTP personnel have been busy cleaning and televising the sewers
ahead of lining. Our new camera has arrived and is being used daily. The plan
is to reline 5,500 LF of our sewers on the west side of town.
The bridge and stairs projects have also been approved and we are working with
Smolen to finalize the plans. Both projects might slide into next year due to
engineering not being complete, unavailability of precast beams and undesirable
overlap with the sewer lining project.
 
Police:
We currently have a 2009 and a 2011 cruiser that are reaching the end of their
service life. I have submitted a preliminary application to USDA and I received
a response confirming that all paperwork looks to be in good order. I now need
an ordinance that would allow me to officially submit the app.
 
Fire:
Other Items:
 
Covid-19: We continue to monitor the situation and make necessary changes to
comply with Gov. DeWine’s orders.
Covid-19 has impacted our finances. However, we have a strong balance sheet for
the foreseeable future thanks to the early cuts we adopted. For this reason, I
would like to ask council to approve a resolution lifting the hiring freeze. We
continue to ask all departments to be mindful of all non-essential expenses and
we are trying to keep overtime to a minimum.
I would like for council to approve a resolution allowing for the village to
complete the land purchase/swop where Poplar turns into Falcon Way.

our permit.

Recreation Department:
The Rec center is now open for all activities. The weight room is open as well.
 
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
Plant operations are running at fully acceptable levels.
The Wastewater plant is under pressure to eliminate all I and I from the west
side of the village. We are working with CT consultants and the EPA to renew
our permit.
The sewer lining project: Having precon meeting on 10/22/2020.
The bridge and stairs projects have also been approved and we are working with
Smolen to finalize the plans. Both projects are going to slide into next year
due to engineering not being complete, unavailability of precast beams and
undesirable overlap with the sewer lining project.
 
Police:
Police Cruisers: Final application to USDA has been submitted. Waiting to hear
back from USDA.
Last week I discovered that many communities in Ohio are using CARES Act funds
to purchase Covid-19 cruisers. Perry, Madison Township, Willoughby and many
more have already ordered and received their Covid cruisers. Currently we have
2 cruisers that are not safe to use for Covid infected individuals or officers.
I had our legal council prepare an ordinance with emergency language to allow
me to place an order for one new cruiser that meets safety standards for Covid.
(See letter from Chief Wassie)

Covid-19: We continue to monitor the situation and make necessary changes to
comply with Gov. DeWine’s orders.

and we are trying to keep overtime to a minimum.

Street Dept.  
Operating normal tasks.
Street crew is wrapping up sidewalk replacement in areas of need. West Walnut
St is complete.
Work on phase IV truck route is almost complete. Punch list given to
contractor. It is looking like Easton might have to complete the grass seeding
part in the spring.
 
Recreation Department:
   
The Rec center is now open for all activities. The weight room is open as well.
 
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
Plant operations are running at fully acceptable levels.
The Wastewater plant is under pressure to eliminate all I and I from the west
side of the village. We are working with CT consultants and the EPA to renew
our permit.
The sewer lining project: Starting ASAP.
The bridge and stairs projects have also been approved and we are working with
Smolen to finalize the plans. Both projects are going to slide into next year
due to engineering not being complete, unavailability of precast beams and
undesirable overlap with the sewer lining project.
 
Police:
Police Cruisers: Final application to USDA has been submitted. Waiting to hear
back from USDA.
We received the Covid-19 cruiser. Waiting on papers for title. New cruiser is
scheduled to get striped and outfitted to our specs. We hope to have it done
and ready to be put into service in December.
 
Fire:
 
Fire truck should be delivered before the end of the year.
 
Other Items:
 
In the next few days, we should be closing on the Cunningham purchase. There is
a resolution for Council to approve the dedication of said land as public road
and part of Poplar Street.
Cares Act funds: We are working with all our departments to identify Covid-19
expenditures. Mostly, we are looking to upgrade fixtures and other items to
touchless technology to prevent the spread of Covid. I also have a resolution
for the Village to commit up to $15,000 of our Cares Act funds to JERD to
assist with the purchase of needed equipment. Jefferson Township has committed
the same amount.
 
Covid-19: We continue to monitor the situation and make necessary changes to
comply with Gov. DeWine’s orders.
We continue to ask all departments to be mindful of all non-essential expenses
and we are trying to keep overtime to a minimum.

going to hold some retainage funds to be paid in the spring after we are able
to verify that all grass seeding survived the winter.
 
Recreation Department:
   
The Rec center is now open for all activities. The weight room is open as well.
There is a very strong chance that we might have to close the Rec Center due to
the latest increase in Covid-19 positive cases. We are going to keep vigilant
and act accordingly.
 
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
Plant operations are running at fully acceptable levels.
The Wastewater plant is under pressure to eliminate all I and I from the west
side of the village. We are working with CT consultants and the EPA to renew
our permit.
The sewer lining project: Started on 11/13/2020 (cleaning ahead of lining).
The bridge and stairs projects have also been approved and we are working with
Smolen to finalize the plans. Both projects are going to slide into next year
due to engineering not being complete, unavailability of precast beams and
undesirable overlap with the sewer lining project.
 
Police:
Police Cruisers: Final application to USDA has been submitted. USDA has not
received funding for projects as of 11/09/2020.
We received the Covid-19 cruiser. New cruiser is scheduled to get striped and
outfitted to our specs. We hope to have it done and ready to be put into
service in December.
 
Fire:
 
Fire truck should be delivered before the end of the year.
Jefferson Township has committed up to $15,000 of their Cares Act funds to the
Village of Jefferson for the benefit of the Jefferson Fire Department. Said
funds are going to be used for the purchase of gear and equipment necessary to
prevent the spread of Covid-19.
 
Other Items:
 
In the next few days, we should be closing on the Cunningham purchase. We had
to postpone closing due to unexpected issues.
Cares Act funds: We are working with all our departments to identify Covid-19
expenditures. Mostly, we are looking to upgrade fixtures and other items to
touchless technology to prevent the spread of Covid-19.
Covid-19: We continue to monitor the situation and make necessary changes to
comply with Gov. DeWine’s orders.
We continue to ask all departments to be mindful of all non-essential expenses
and we are trying to keep overtime to a minimum.

Mayor
2020 State of the Village
 
   2020 has been a year like we have never seen before. Despite all negatives,
the Village has ended the year with a sound financial carryover of
approximately $1,350,000. About $105,000 of the total carryover was a direct
result of refunds we received for workers compensation premiums paid. The
Village also received CARES ACT funds that were used for wages and to upgrade
our facilities with touchless technologies. We also purchased a new police
cruiser better equipped for the mitigation of Covid-19.
The Department heads, Administration and Council are very watchful in the
spending of taxpayer’s dollars.
We have been very busy this year, here are some of the major accomplishments
for 2020:
Wastewater- Streets Departments:
Secured funding for a major sewer relining project on W. Jefferson St and
surrounding areas.
Purchased top of the line Sewer-Storm Camera and a used ambulance from
Ashtabula Township for the purpose of televising our utility lines. We no
longer need to depend on third party contractors to identify sewer and storm
problems.
Cleaned and televised all sewer lines on the west side of town in preparation
of the sewer lining project.
Continued upgrades/repairs to current equipment at the plant which enables
better plant efficiency.
Forestry services of brush pick up and grinding; we removed numerous dead trees
and stumps. We also planted over 175 new trees throughout the Village.
We finally completed paving of our truck route on E. Erie St and S. Spruce.
Obtained 100% funding for the twin culvert repair on Poplar St.
Completed concrete work for the High School and replaced sidewalks on Dorset
Rd, Chestnut St. and W. Walnut St.
Street repairs (with durapatch machine, cold patching, chip and crack sealing);
snow removal.
Completed a land purchase to create a more gentle bend between Poplar Street
and Falcon Way.
Hired Don Goodenow as our new equipment operator to replace Mark Sowry that
retired after many years of service to the Village. Congratulation Mark, enjoy
your retirement.
 
 Recreation Department:
Community Action of Ashtabula "Meals on Wheels" continues to rent the kitchen
area at Giddings Hall 40 hours per week for food prep on a five-year contract.
The number of meals they provide for senior residents in the County has been
steadily increasing. Because of Covid-19 they had to stop serving meals at
Giddings Hall and had to increase meal deliveries.
Replaced 2/3 of the roof on the Recreation Center, we hope to finish the rest
in 2021.
Completed installation of 2 new lights and finished landscaping around the new
Covered Bridge Pavilion. A big thanks to Joe Cole from United Excavating for
volunteering dozer grading work.
All youth events such as soccer, flag football, T-ball were very successful
this summer despite all Covid restrictions.
 
 Police:
Submitted application to USDA for the replacement of 2 older police cruisers.
Maintained our high level of local enforcement to keep visitors and residents
safe to walk the streets and have no fear.
Tim Blon retired from our police department after many years of service. Tim
will stay on with the fire department and was rehired by the High School as
their resource officer. Congrats to Tim for his retirement and rehire.
Fire:
We continue to provide constant training for our Firefighters.
Upgraded equipment such as Scott air packs, thermal imaging sensor, and turn
out gear.
Completed the purchase of a new fire tuck. We received $100,000 GRANT from
USDA, the remainder $469,000 was financed by USDA for 10 years at 2.35%.
The Fire Station was remodeled and it turned out beautifully. A big thanks to
Chief Tom Lachey and all the firefighters that volunteered their time and skill
for this.
 
In addition, this year we were able to provide all the employees with a year-
end bonus since we had to suspend the raises when Covid-19 first started.
Spring curb side clean up, brush pick up, leaf pick up, property maintenance
efforts, the condition of our roads and sidewalks helps make the Village a
desirable place to live, work, visit and enjoy.
We constantly monitor properties in the Village that are not in compliance with
our maintenance code. This year we sold the lot at 112 S. Elm St. A few years
ago we had to demolish the house at that address.
 
I want to thank all our employees for their dedication and hard work that makes
this village a safe and welcoming place to live and visit.
I would also like to thank our residents and property owners for working co-
operatively with us to make our village a shining star.
We are all looking forward to another great year (2021) in Jefferson. I wish
all a safe and prosperous New Year.
Mayor Maloney

Street Dept.  
Operating normal tasks.
We have scheduled Lake County Sewers to perform a 2-day cleaning of sections of
storm lines on W. Jefferson and W. Satin St. Some of these storm lines have
severe blockages. This cleaning should serve a dual purpose; a) improve storm
water flows and b) allow for our camera to inspect the lines while looking for
storm-to-sewer cross connections.
 
Recreation Department:
We continue to monitor the covid-19 regulations and act accordingly.
 
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
Plant operations are running at fully acceptable levels.
The Wastewater plant is under pressure to eliminate all I and I from the west
side of the village. We are working with CT consultants and the EPA to renew
our permit.
The sewer lining project: Started on 11/13/2020. Cleaning ahead of lining is
done. It has been determined that we need to perform 5 point repairs as part of
this project. Point repairs are performed by digging up and replacing broken
laterals that cannot be grouted or lined. Unfortunately, 3 of those digs are
going to be on recently paved roads. 2 on W. Jefferson and 1 on S. Elm.
The bridge and stairs projects have also been approved and we are working with
Smolen to finalize the plans. Both projects are going to slide into next year
due to engineering not being complete, unavailability of precast beams and
undesirable overlap with the sewer lining project.
 
Police:
Police Cruisers: Final application to USDA has been submitted. USDA has not
received funding for projects as of 12/30/2020.
Covid-19 cruiser has been striped and is scheduled to get outfitted to our
specs. We hope to have it done and ready to be put into service any day now.
 
Fire:
New Fire Truck was delivered.
 
Other Items:
We closed on the Cunningham purchase. The school board signed off on final
paperwork. Mike Hamper is going to complete all required recordings.
Covid-19: We continue to monitor the situation and make necessary changes to
comply with Gov. DeWine’s orders.
We continue to ask all departments to be mindful of all non-essential expenses
and we are trying to keep overtime to a minimum.

Street Dept.  
Operating normal tasks.
Last month we installed 2 new “Welcome to Jefferson” signs, one on our Right-
of-Way on East Beech Street and one on Sander’s Market property on South
Chestnut Street. I have attached a consent paperwork signed by Sander’s
representative to be submitted for the record.
Bill Painter from Get Your Graphics custom built the signs at the cost of
$2,207 each. Since the signs are one-sided, Chief Lachey suggested we contact
the High School to see if the art department would like to tackle decorating
the back side.
I contacted Mr. Huber and he had Mrs. Archuleta (HS art teacher) reach out to
me for details. The HS graphic design class is currently working on a couple of
designs to be submitted to council for approval. My understanding is that the
class is excited to be working on this project. The students will get to see
their work on display right here in town for years to come.
 
Recreation Department:
We continue to monitor the covid-19 regulations and act accordingly.
 
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
Need a motion to accept the new sewer rates for 2021 according to the rate
schedule attached to ordinance 2020-O-3170.
Plant operations are running at fully acceptable levels.
The Wastewater plant is under pressure to eliminate all I and I from the west
side of the village. We are working with CT consultants and the EPA to renew
our permit.
The sewer lining project: Started on 11/13/2020. Cleaning ahead of lining is
done. It has been determined that we need to perform 5 point repairs as part of
this project. Point repairs are performed by digging up and replacing broken
laterals that cannot be grouted or lined. Unfortunately, 3 of those digs are
going to be on recently paved roads. 2 on W. Jefferson and 1 on S. Elm.
The bridge and stairs projects have also been approved and we are working with
Smolen to finalize the plans. Both projects are going to slide into next year
due to engineering not being complete, unavailability of precast beams and
undesirable overlap with the sewer lining project.
 
Police:
Police Cruisers: Final application to USDA has been submitted. USDA has not
received funding for projects as of 12/30/2020.
Covid-19 cruiser has been striped and is scheduled to get outfitted to our
specs. We hope to have it done and ready to be put into service any day now.
 
Fire:
New Fire Truck was delivered.
 
Other Items:
We closed on the Cunningham purchase. The school board signed off on final
paperwork. Mike Hamper is going to complete all required recordings.
Covid-19: We continue to monitor the situation and make necessary changes to
comply with Gov. DeWine’s orders.
We continue to ask all departments to be mindful of all non-essential expenses
and we are trying to keep overtime to a minimum.

Street Dept.  
Operating normal tasks.
The recent snow falls accompanied by cold temperatures are forcing our crews to
be out there spreading a little more salt than usual for this time of the year.
We are starting to look at purchasing new trees to replace the ones that we had
to remove last year. We figured we are going to need between 35 and 40 new
trees that will be planted in the fall.
After removing snow in the mornings, some members of our street crew have been
painting the hallway here at Village Hall. They are doing a very nice job! They
have also started to repaint our Rec Center.
 
Recreation Department:
We continue to monitor the covid-19 regulations and act accordingly.
On 2/23/21 I was informed that one of our staff members at the Rec Center had
tested positive for Covid. Said employee had not been to work since Friday 2/
19/21 and at that time exhibited no Covid symptoms. As a precaution we decided
to close the Rec Center until March 8th, 2021. We are going to use this down
time to perform extra cleaning and painting. The objective is to freshen up the
current look with new colors. I would like to thank Mrs. Archuleta for
volunteering her time in helping with the paint color selection.  
 
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
Plant operations are running at fully acceptable levels.
The Wastewater plant is under pressure to eliminate all I and I from the west
side of the village. We are working with CT consultants and the EPA to renew
our permit.
The sewer lining project: Started on 11/13/2020. Cleaning ahead of lining is
done. It has been determined that we need to perform 5 point repairs as part of
this project. Point repairs are performed by digging up and replacing broken
laterals that cannot be grouted or lined. Unfortunately, 3 of those digs are
going to be on recently paved roads. 2 on W. Jefferson and 1 on S. Elm. We now
have a schedule for the lining that should be completed by the end of this
month.
The bridge and stairs projects have also been approved and we are working with
Smolen to finalize the plans. Both projects are close to being complete as far
as the engineering goes. I would like to go to bidding in May and possibly
start work in June.
 
Police:
Police Cruisers: Final application to USDA has been submitted. USDA has
received funding and is now in the process of allocating them. I hope to hear
something from them in the next couple of weeks
Covid-19 cruiser has been delivered and is now in service with Sergeant
Dumperth at the wheel. Congratz!
 
Fire:
I would like to recognize Chief Tom Lachey for applying and receiving a 2020
Fire Department Training Grant ($2,741) and a 2021 MARKS Grant ($22,978).
Great job Tom, well done! (See attached Grant Award Letters)
 
Other Items:
Covid-19: We continue to monitor the situation and make necessary changes to
comply with Gov. DeWine’s orders.
We continue to ask all departments to be mindful of all non-essential expenses
and we are trying to keep overtime to a minimum.

Street Dept.  
Operating normal tasks.
We purchased 40 trees that should get planted next week.
Street crew has been installing drain pipes on North Spruce Street.
 
Recreation Department:
We continue to monitor the covid-19 regulations and act accordingly.
Most activities are running at full capacity according to the Governor’s rules.
 
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
Plant operations are running at fully acceptable levels.
The Wastewater plant is under pressure to eliminate all I and I from the west
side of the village. We are working with CT consultants and the EPA to renew
our permit.
The sewer lining project: The lining part of the project is done. All there is
left to do is the 5 point repairs. Point repairs are performed by digging up
and replacing broken laterals that cannot be grouted or lined. Unfortunately, 3
of those digs are going to be on recently paved roads. 2 on W. Jefferson and 1
on S. Elm. We expect the point repairs to be done within the next month or so.
The bridge and stairs projects have also been approved and we are working with
Smolen to finalize the plans. Both projects are close to being complete as far
as the engineering goes. I would like to go to bidding in May and possibly
start work in June.
Police:
Police Cruisers: Waiting on USDA for funding.
 
Fire:
Other Items:
Covid-19: We continue to monitor the situation and make necessary changes to
comply with Gov. DeWine’s orders.
We continue to ask all departments to be mindful of all non-essential expenses
and we are trying to keep overtime to a minimum.
I have been receiving few complaints about some properties that have been on
our radar for some time. I have tried numerous times to talk with some of these
property owners but it’s not working. At this point I have no choice but to
start cracking down on properties with junk cars, trash, tall grass and in
major disrepair. The other issue that we have been dealing with is that some
residents will set out their bulk garbage (furniture, couches, mattresses) on
the tree lawn and expect WM to pick it up. It doesn’t work that way! For
starters, if a resident has a bulk item that needs disposed of, they need to
call the Village to schedule a special pick up. If the item is made out of
cloth fabric, it needs to be wrapped with plastic and sealed off with duct
tape.

Street Dept.  
Operating normal tasks.
This week we will be interviewing for our Street Department job openings.
Our Street crew planted the new trees we purchased.
We worked with the County to dispose of all tires we collected in the Village
in the past 2 years. We provided a backhoe to help load the tires and they are
not charging us for the disposal. We had over 70 tires.
The Village cleanup day was a success thanks to the efforts of Village
Residents, WM personnel and Village Street Crew. Great job everyone! I would
also like thank The Gazette and the Star Beacon for covering the event and
helping inform our residents.
We have identified 4 small road sections that need overlayed/repaired.
W. Ashtabula, Maplewood, Dorset and Brittany. Working on getting estimates.
 
Recreation Department:
We continue to monitor the covid-19 regulations and act accordingly.
Most activities are expected to return at full capacity once that the health
orders are removed on June 2nd.
The Rec. Ctr. is advertising a part-time position for Front Desk Support.
T-Ball and other summer sports activities are getting scheduled.
Starting in June we are going to have music in the park – summer concerts. The
event will be funded with NOPEC grant money for this purpose that we submitted
for. Mr. Burazer and the HS Stage Band are going to kick off the season with a
concert on June 3rd starting at 6 PM. The other dates being considered are June
24th, July 22nd and August 5th. More details coming soon!
We are planning a September 11 Blue Grass Festival at the Covered Bridge
Pavilion for this year’s 20th anniversary of the tragic events that occurred 9/
11/2001. We hope to turn this into a yearly event scheduled for the second
Saturday in September for years to come. We are working on finalizing details
and I will share more about this project as more info becomes available.    
 
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
Plant operations are running at fully acceptable levels.
The Wastewater plant is under pressure to eliminate all I and I from the west
side of the village. We are working with CT consultants and the EPA to renew
our permit.
The sewer lining project: This project is almost complete! We had to perform a
total of 6 point repairs. Asphalt repairs will be done as soon as possible.
The bridge and stairs projects have also been approved and we are working with
Smolen to finalize the plans. Both projects are close to being complete as far
as the engineering goes.
 
Police:
Police Cruisers: Waiting on USDA for funding.
 
Fire:
Other Items:
We continue to ask all departments to be mindful of all non-essential expenses
and we are trying to keep overtime to a minimum.

Jack Boyd of 172 Garfield Lane spoke to Council in support of Sergeant Dumperth
as being the next Chief of Police. He also complimented the Jefferson Police
Department for protecting Jefferson.
 
John Nemith of 2059 Jefferson Street asked if the Police Department is short of
officers. Also complimented the Police Department at the work they do with the
Drug Task Force.
 
Pat Parson of 138 West Walnut Street compared Sargent Dumperth to Dave Wassie.
Also Asked Council felt his residence not a problem.
 
Steve Luz of 416 Brittney Lane told to Council he felt he was passionate for
his work. And is confident in his abilities, people skills along with his
police knowledge.
 
Dave Blessing told Council that he has worked with Sergeant Dumperth the last
tow years. He fits the mold of a good officer and Chief.
  
Ryan White of 533 Heritage Square told Council Sergeant Dumperth he leads with
knowledge and gets the job done and takes pride in his job.
White also told Council to put personal feeling aside and stop playing
politics. All Council is doing is hurting the department making them short
staffed. Also told Council that they work for them. White also told Council
that he might leave the Department if Sergeant Dumperth does not get to be
Police Chief.
He is qualified for the job. He works when he is off duty, that is how
dedicated he is.
Branden Nelling of 6825 Jefferson Road Ashtabula told Council he has worked
with Sergeant Dumperth eight years. He has made me a better officer working
along with him. He is a great friend, great boss. Community oriented works with
the kids at the school. He told Council he may look for another job if Sergeant
Dumperth does not get the Chiefs position.
 
David Wassie 247 High Street Conneaut, retied Chief as of May 31, 2021. My job
was to train Sergeant Dumperth for the Chiefs position when I retired. Wassie
told his he trained his to be the next Chief and feel that Sergeant Dumperth
can do the job. He knows other officers from other Law enforcements along with

trained and ready to be the next Chief.

Visitor’s Comments (five-minute limit per council rule #13)
Visitor’s Comments
Sgt. Aaron Dumperth of 2207 Lenox New Lyme Road spoke to the Council regards to
being appointed Police Chief for the Village of Jefferson and his residency.
Dumperth spoke to Council stating he is not a resident of the Village of
Jefferson, but he has deep roots and is devoted to the Village of Jefferson. He
stated that he lives five minutes out of town. He has been involved the
Community his whole life and he has devoted the last ten years of his life
protecting and serving the Community.
 
Terry Finger of 104 West Jefferson Street spoke to Council in regards of the
Police chief’s residency. He spoke to Council on three important things.
First thing is the Oath of Office.
Second one is Barring Cities from requiring employees to live within the city
limits. The Supreme Court passed legislation on 2009 stating the employee did
not have to live in the Village. Finger told council his opinion in requiring
residency was settled in 2009 when the Supreme Court passed the legislation.
Third thing is Executive Sessions. Finger stated from the News Paper that
executive sessions may have started to be taken lightly. The executive session
that Councilperson Diehl called tonight is valid. The Council must remember to
have a valid reason when an executive session is called. Council also must
remember you cannot call up three people and discuss what is going on either.
That is considered a meeting if more than two people are involved in a
discussion.
 
Mary Jackson of 333South Market Street apt .3, spoke to Council stating that
Sgt. Dumperth has been helpful for her as a black member or the community
during the last 18 months. She stated that he is helpful with the challenging
topic relating the law enforcement.
 
Jefferson Village Solicitor Jason Fairchild countered Fingers review of the
Supreme Court decision. Stating that the decision related to lower -level
employees of a City or Village, not the Police Chief. The appellate decisions
affirmed the right of a Village to maintain residency requirements for a Police
Chief or to waive the residency requirement.
Also present:  
Jack and Donna Boyd, Nicholes Belder, Pat Bradek, John Perrotti, Jacob Morgan,
Terry Finger, Aaron Dumperth, Tina Dumperth, Rachel Peer, Megan Lynch, Steven
Sekanina, Mary Jackson, Stephanie Wessell of the Gazette, Karen Roderick, Ken

Street Dept.  
Curt Stone has retired from the street dept. Thank you Curt for the years of
service to the Village, we will miss you.
Operating normal tasks.
We have received quotes for resurfacing 4 small road sections: Ashtabula,
Maplewood, Dorset and Brittany. The plan is to mill 1-1/2” along the edges of
all roads to 0” at the centerline. This will allow for greater crowning of the
road and will also help with meeting driveway elevations as the new 1-1/2”
layer is applied evenly across the entire surface. Ashtabula St. is also
getting fabric installed under the new layer to help control road cracks. We
selected Koski Paving for the job for pricing and because they offer full width
paving that eliminates a centerline cold joint.
Need a motion to hire Matt Licate as part-time labor for Streets pending
physical, background check and council approval.
 
Recreation Department:
We continue to monitor the covid-19 regulations and act accordingly.
Need a motion to hire Jessica Sheets as part-time Front Desk Support pending
physical, background check and council approval. .
Unfortunately, our 1st concert in the park got canceled due to rain. Next event
is this Thursday July 24th at 6 PM featuring The Brakes w/ The Daze. NOPEC is
planning on attending this event.
We are planning a September 11 Blue Grass Festival at the Covered Bridge
Pavilion for this year’s 20th anniversary of the tragic events that occurred 9/
11/2001. We hope to turn this into a yearly event scheduled for the second
Saturday in September for years to come. We are working on finalizing details
and I will share more about this project as more info becomes available.
 
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
Plant operations are running at fully acceptable levels.
The Wastewater plant is under pressure to eliminate all I and I from the west
side of the village. We are working with CT consultants and the EPA to renew
our permit.
The bridge and stairs projects have also been approved and we are working with
Smolen to finalize the plans. Both projects are close to being complete as far
as the engineering goes.
 
Police:
Police Cruisers: Waiting on USDA for funding.
 
Fire:
Other Items:
 
Round 36 OPWC Pre-apps have been submitted for 3 projects. WWTP renovations, E.
Jefferson-W. Jefferson paving and storms and Falcon Way reconstruction.
We continue to ask all departments to be mindful of all non-essential expenses
and we are trying to keep overtime to a minimum.
Properties with Code violations:
 
Solicitor Fairchild is working on some language changes in our code that would
allow for a better definition of junk vehicles. Changes are needed to be able
to effectively enforce removal of these vehicles. We hope to have those changes
ready by next Council meeting.

will be on August 4th @ 1pm.

Village was $2,084 for surveying and title transfer. Our priority is to correct
some of the safety issues and then come up with a plan to restore the field.
