Street Dept.  
Operating normal tasks.
Koski should be paving our 4 roads this week.
Chip and seal is scheduled for this week.
 
Recreation Department:
We continue to monitor the covid-19 regulations and act accordingly.
We have interviewed 2 applicants for the open positions at Rec. We have
selected Carlene (Kitt) Juist and Alicia Morgan for the positions pending
Council approval and physicals. See Memos for details.
We are planning a September 11 Blue Grass Festival at the Covered Bridge
Pavilion for this year’s 20th anniversary of the tragic events that occurred 9/
11/2001. We hope to turn this into a yearly event scheduled for the second
Saturday in September for years to come. Our next meeting to discuss details
will be on August 4th @ 1pm.
 
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
Plant operations are running at fully acceptable levels.
The Wastewater plant is under pressure to eliminate all I and I from the west
side of the village. We have successfully renewed our EPA permit.
The bridge and stairs projects are ready for bidding. We are going to have a
pre-bid meeting at WWTP on August 18, @ 10:00 AM and a bid opening at Town Hall
on September 1st @ 10:00 AM.
 
Police:
Police Cruisers: Waiting on USDA for funding.
 
Fire:
Other Items:
I have reached out to the Commissioners and other City Managers about crafting
a common agreement with NextSite to provide consulting services. NextSite
provides marketing information and analysis for clients that are looking
attract restaurants and retailers to their communities.
The commissioners are working on the issue. It might take some time before we
get an agreement that we can review.
We continue to ask all departments to be mindful of all non-essential expenses
and we are trying to keep overtime to a minimum.
I would like to schedule a Utility/Wastewater Committee meeting to discuss the
results of a Local Limit Evaluation. This evaluation is mandated by the EPA
before they will issue any PTI for any industry that might be wanting to set up
shop in the village. We will be looking to update our current limits with the
new limits resulting from the study. CT consultants should be helping upgrade
this part of our code.
I would also like to schedule a Buildings & Lands Committee meeting. Solicitor
Fairchild has been working on some language changes in our code that would
allow for a better definition of junk vehicles. We have draft legislation ready
for Committee review.

Visitor’s Comments
 
Todd Bendis of Lake City Plating spoke to Council regarding moving their
company to Jefferson in the old Smurf It Stone Building. Bendis told Council
That they plan to bring some of the equipment from Ashtabula to start up but
then they plan to build new equipment. By the year 2024 Lake City Plating plan
to move the entire company. The repairs to the building will cost about 2
million dollars, 4 million dollars will be put into the new equipment. They
also plan to build a brand new WWTP system that will cost about 1.8 million
dollars. There is one issue that we must look at is in Ashtabula the sewer rate
is about $4.00 dollars per hundred cubic feet and Jefferson’s sewer rate is
$6.15 per hundred cubic feet. The plan also would be by the end of 2024 is that
add 60 new jobs to Jefferson. Bendis did ask Council if they would investigate
changing the sewer rate.
 
Melissa Haney of 122 North Market Street asked Council if they could
investigate changing the wording in the zoning rules about having a bed and
breakfast in the Village of Jefferson. The have a beautiful home and would love
to make it a B&B.
 
Councilperson Damon told Haney they would have a building Land Committee
Meeting to discuss the B&B issue.

Street Dept.  
Operating normal tasks.
We will be submitting final application for the Jefferson St Drainage & Paving
Phase I project. We first applied for this last year and it didn’t make the
cut. The total project is for $ 199,900. We should receive $ 49,950 in grants
and $50,000 in OPWC loans.
The remaining $99,950 will be our local share. In an effort to stretch our
dollars, part of our local share will be in-kind work that our street crew will
be performing. Final apps are due October 29, 2021. See attached paperwork for
details.
 
Recreation Department:
We continue to monitor the covid-19 regulations and act accordingly.
The Rec Ctr is now offering a variety of classes for all age groups. We now
have Senior Fitness, Xtreme Body Pump Class, AHH Fitness, Mommy & Me, Karate
and Dance Classes. See attached flyers for details.
 
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
Plant operations are running at fully acceptable levels.
The Wastewater plant is under pressure to eliminate all I and I from east side
of the village. We are working on obtaining video footage for the Market St &
surrounding sewer lining project.
 
Police:
Police Cruisers: I received an email from our rep. at USDA. They are not able
to finance the 2 vehicles that we applied for this year. However, our
application doesn’t lose its place in line to be funded in the future.
 
Fire:
Other Items:
We continue to ask all departments to be mindful of all non-essential expenses
and we are trying to keep overtime to a minimum.
A preliminary Local Limit Evaluation is complete. We have submitted our report
to the EPA and are waiting for them to review. Once the review is complete and
the local limits are approved by the EPA, we will be looking to update our
current limits. CT consultants is helping upgrade this part of our code.
I would like to schedule a buildings and lands meeting to discuss the memo that
Solicitor Fairchild produced in regard to Zoning and B&B’s.
We have a resolution for Council tonight that pertains to the Lodge at Geneva-
On-The-Lake. As you probably know, the Lodge’s ownership is to be transferred
to the State (ODNR) at years end. A work group composed of different members
from all communities in the County has been concerned about how this State
takeover could impact the lodging industry in the County and even more how this
could impact the tourism industry and part of the County’s economy. The group
came up with a resolution, to be passed by all Cities, Townships and
Municipalities, that points out areas of concern especially when it comes to
keeping current management in place and having some degree of local control of
the Lodge. The idea is to make it known that the Lodge issue is a County-wide
issue and that all Cities, Townships and Municipalities are uniting in opposing
a State transfer that could damage the Lodge, the tourism industry and all of
the local small economies throughout the County.

Street Dept.  
Operating normal tasks.
We had Brobst in town for 2 days removing dead and dangerous trees. 1 more day
of cutting and we should be wrapped up for 2021. We plan on grinding all stumps
as soon as all trees have been removed.
Our crew has been pruning trees close to sidewalks in preparation for sidewalk
plowing. They have also replaced and repaired some sidewalks in areas of need.
 
Recreation Department:
We continue to monitor the covid-19 regulations and act accordingly.
Phase III roof replacement started today.
 
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
Plant operations are running at fully acceptable levels.
We have cleaned 1 of the 3 collection basins. After the basin was drained, we
discovered an accumulation of about 2-3 feet of rags, grit, and debris. Because
of this, we are looking at cleaning the remaining 2 basins since the last
cleaning was done about 15 years ago according to Gary. Cleaning of all basins
will reduce the frequent breakdowns of the pumps moving the sludge to the
press.
The Market St & surrounding sewer lining project is being advertised for bids
on 11/1 and 11/8/2021. Bid opening 11/17/21 at Town Hall @ 2 PM.
 
Police:
Police Cruisers: I received an email from our rep. at USDA. They are not able
to finance the 2 vehicles that we applied for this year. However, our
application doesn’t lose its place in line to be funded in the future.
 
Fire:
Other Items:
We continue to ask all departments to be mindful of all non-essential expenses
and we are trying to keep overtime to a minimum.
We have submitted our report to the EPA and are still waiting for them to
review and approve local limits for pollutants that could be generated by
industrial companies located in the Village. Once the review is complete and
the local limits are approved by the EPA, we will be looking to update our
current limits. CT consultants is helping upgrade this part of our code.
Just FYI, we have a “Lodge” resolution on the table.

Fire:
Other Items:
We continue to ask all departments to be mindful of all non-essential expenses
and we are trying to keep overtime to a minimum.
We have submitted our report to the EPA and are still waiting for them to
review and approve local limits for pollutants that could be generated by
industrial companies located in the Village. Once the review is complete and
the local limits are approved by the EPA, we will be looking to update our
current limits. CT consultants is helping upgrade this part of our code. We
should have the official limits any day now.

Street Dept. 
   Operating normal tasks.    
   We had Brobst in town on Thursday and Friday for final tree removal for
2021. As far as the stump grinding goes, we decided to push that to spring as
lawns could get damaged this time of the year.   
Recreation Department:
    Operating normally.   
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
   Plant operations are running at fully acceptable levels.   
   We had our bid opening on 11/17/21 for The Market St & surrounding sewer
lining project. Insituform Technologies submitted the lowest bid for $338,229.
We should be awarding this project in January as we are working on finalizing
financing paperwork.   
Police:
   Police Cruisers: I received an email from our rep. at USDA. They are not
able to finance the 2 vehicles that we applied for this year. However, our
application doesn’t lose its place in line to be funded in the future.   
Fire:
Other Items:
   We continue to ask all departments to be mindful of all non-essential
expenses and we are trying to keep overtime to a minimum.   
   The local limit calculations for industrial pollutants is complete and in
the hands of the EPA. They are going to advertise these limits in the papers in
the form of public notice. The public notice will run through January 6th. Our
solicitor has prepared a new ordinance with the new standards. We plan on
introducing the ordinance for a first reading at the second council meeting in
January.    
   First reading a resolution to allow the mayor to execute documentation
regarding the Johnson & Johnson opioid settlement.   
   Tyler Maylish has completed his 6-month probation as Operator Class I
effective 12/09/21. Need a motion to end his probation.   
   Blaze Burr has completed his 6-month probation as Utility/Maintenance for
Streets effective 12/9/21. Need a motion to end his probation.   
   Need a motion to promote Blaze Burr from Utility/Maintenance to Equipment
Operator for Streets effective 12/21/21 (see memo).   
   Bill Hitchcock has completed his 6-month probation as Working Forman for
Streets effective 12/9/21. Need a motion to end his probation.

Mayor
State of the Village 2021
2021 continued to be a challenging environment with issues related to Covid.
However, the Village has ended the year with a healthy financial carry over due
to the watchful spending of taxpayer dollars by Village Administration,
Council, and each department head.
We have been very busy this year, here are some of the major accomplishments
for 2021:
The new Fire Truck was delivered. We would like to thank USDA for the $100,000
Grant and for financing the balance at a very competitive rate.
We applied for 2 new police cruisers to get funded by USDA which would provide
about $42,000 in grant funding and finance the balance at a very low rate.
Unfortunately, USDA was not able to fund this project in 2021 due to Covid
budget related issues. We remain on their list of projects that should get
funded eventually in the near future.
The Village was able to close on the purchase of the Memorial Field and will be
developing plans to restore this facility for public use.
We closed on the Cunningham small land purchase for the purpose of rectifying
the sharp curve between South Poplar Street and Falcon Way.
Necessary maintenance was completed on the Village Hall with painting, new
doors, new plumbing fixtures, flooring, and a new set of steps. We also
installed 2 new “Welcome to Jefferson” signs at Village’s entry points to
welcome people coming and leaving town.
Our crews also did a very nice job repainting the Rec Center with some new
colors to give it a fresh and crisp look. The last phase of the roof
replacement was completed as well.
We hired Jason Fairchild as our new Solicitor. He has been doing a tremendous
job for the Village.
Chief Tom Lachey was recognized for applying and receiving a 2020 Fire
Department Training Grant ($2,741) and a 2021 MARCS Grant ($22,978).
We cut down about 40 dangerous trees in the village and we planted just as many
new ones.
In June, we had 2 long time employees retire, Curt Stone (Streets Supervisor)
and Police Chief Dave Wassie. I would like to thank both for the many years of
service and congratulate them on their retirement.
Last year we resurfaced 4 roads in the Village. West Ashtabula, Maplewood,
Dorset, and Brittany Lane.
As part of an effort to reduce I&I and to improve sewer function, we completed
a $550,000 project to reline about 8,800 linear feet on W. Jefferson St and
surroundings.
We also submitted and received final approval for the Market St & surrounding
sewer lining project. This project is very similar to the one above, same
amount $550,000, just a different area of the Village. We expect to have it
completed first part of 2022.
The Jefferson Street Drainage & Paving Phase I project was also approved for a
total cost $ 199,900. We should receive $ 49,950 in grant and $50,000 in OPWC
loan.
The remaining $99,950 will be our local share. In an effort to stretch our
dollars, part of our local share will be in-kind work that our street crew will
be performing. We expect plans to be completed in the next few months.
The bridge and stairs project at the WWTP was approved and awarded for
construction. We expect this project to be completed by mid-2022.
We began using our new Covered Bridge Pavilion for Music in the Park events. We
received $1,500 from NOPEC to be used for this purpose.
The Village, in conjunction with Larry Covey, SOCC, The Gazette, Montrose and
Wall Street Coffee Shop, sponsored the first annual Bluegrass Festival in honor
of all first responders that lost their lives on 9-11. The plan is to have this
festival every year on the second weekend in September. Hopefully we can get
more sponsors in the years ahead, so we can grow this festival and attract more
and more people to our Village.
In the fall we received a request for information from Ashtabula County Growth
Partnership pertaining to utilities available at the old Stone Container
building on S. Sycamore. We were later informed that Lake City Plating was
looking to move their operations to such building. After several meetings with
LCP, the OHIO EPA and CT Consulting, we commissioned a Local Limit Study to
determine if our WWTP could handle the addition of LCP to our system. The study
was completed, and the results were positive for the additional load from LCP.
The new industrial local limits will be made part of our code in early 2022 as
soon as allowed by law. The addition of LCP is exciting news for Jefferson as
it represents a great opportunity for our community when it comes to jobs and
growth in general.
Spring curb side clean up, brush pick up, leaf pick up, property maintenance
efforts, the condition of our roads and sidewalks helps make the Village a
desirable place to live, work, visit and enjoy. This year we are going to try
to focus even more on roads and sidewalks that need repaired or replaced.
The Budlings and Lands committee worked with our Solicitor to create stronger
ordinance language to enforce property maintenance codes. We constantly monitor
properties in the Village that are not in compliance with our maintenance code
and can now more effectively deal with junk cars.
I want to thank all our employees for their dedication and hard work that makes
this village a safe and welcoming place to live and visit.
I would also like to thank our residents and property owners for working co-
operatively with us to make our village a great place to live.
We are all looking forward to a great 2022 in Jefferson. I wish all a safe and
prosperous New Year.
Mayor Brian Diehl

Street Dept.  
Operating normal tasks.
Street crew is busy cleaning up trees and brush in areas of need.
We have truck #22 in the shop for repairs. We hope to replace this truck with a
new one once we have a 2022 budget.
Truck #23 also had to be fixed as a transmission sensor failed.
Recreation Department:
Operating normally.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
Plant operations are running at fully acceptable levels.
Police:
Police Cruisers: I received an email from our rep. at USDA. They are not able
to finance the 2 vehicles that we applied for this year. However, our
application doesn’t lose its place in line to be funded in the future.
Fire:
Other Items:
We continue to ask all departments to be mindful of all non-essential expenses
and we are trying to keep overtime to a minimum.
Mayor and I have met with a website designer to create a new website for the
Village. This is an exciting project, and I will keep everyone posted on
progress.
We had a meeting with the Commissioners about the Bicentennial Bell and where
to position it in the village. After viewing the bell in storage, Mayor Diehl,
Ginger Whitehead, and I surveyed the grounds at Giddings Park. We agreed that
it would be best to install the bell inside the new Covered Bridge Pavilion. It
will be installed centered on the back wall about 12 feet above floor level. It
would be under cover and visible to all park visitors. All is needed for this
type of installation is a custom-built bracket. I would be happy to contact a
bracket manufacturer, meet with them to come up with a design and provide the
Commissioners with a cost estimate. The bracket needs to be strong enough to
hold at least 500 lb. I would also suggest installing an LED spotlight to keep
it lit and visible at night.
The local limit calculations for industrial pollutants is complete, a notice to
the public expired on January 6th 2022. On January 7th EPA officially approved
the industrial local limits for Jefferson (See attached letter from EPA). Our
solicitor has prepared a new ordinance with the new standards. The ordinance is
on the agenda for a first reading tonight.

Street Dept.

new one once we have a 2022 budget.
We have an ordinance tonight regarding our new tractor-mower combo. We had
ordered this equipment last year and it finally showed up at the end of
December. After further consideration and discussion, we have decided to sell
this equipment and use the proceeds to purchase commercial sidewalk snow
removing equipment that can also be used year around for other tasks. We have
had numerous issues with the sidewalk plow, snowblower and tractor so far.

Fire:
Other Items:

and we are trying to keep overtime to a minimum.
Mayor and I have met with a website designer to create a new website for the
Village. We should have a framework of the entire website by this Wednesday.
After the framework is complete, we will begin adding pictures, content, and
links.
As part of this new website design, Patty, Roni, and Mandy have been working on
options that would allow for residents and customers to pay for most village
wide services with credit cards. We believe this would be an added convenience
for the customers and it would reduce some manual entering of payments.
LCP has been doing some work at the old stone container building. They will be
focusing on getting permits from the village for sewer tap and from the county
for some structural work and for a new sprinkling system. Work in progress and
moving forward.

Street Dept.  
Operating normal tasks.
Street crew is busy cleaning up snow on streets, sidewalks, and fire hydrants.
We have truck #22 in the shop for repairs. We hope to replace this truck with a
new one once we have a 2022 budget.
We are advertising for the sale of our new tractor-mower combo. Bid deadline is
tomorrow February 23rd. Leroy township is in the process of submitting a bid.
If we are not able to locate appropriate commercial sidewalk snow removing
equipment, we might use the proceeds for other items in the streets budget. I’m
finding out that, due to the supply chain issues, it is very hard to find any
equipment in stock.
We had to terminate employment for Reese Mabry as of 2/17/22. Reese was hired
in December 2021 and was in his probation period as Utility/Maintenance. We
will be advertising to fill the position.
Recreation Department:
Operating normally.
I have submitted a memo to increase the Rec budget for the purpose of securing
a full-time director. The idea behind this move is to have a fully dedicated
Village employee that would be responsible to ensure that our facilities are
being used to full potential and to develop services and activities that are
needed in the community and can generate revenues to offset Rec’s financial
burden (please see memo).
Cheryl Riggleman has successfully submitted and obtained a phase 1 Child Care
Stabilization Grant in the amount of $10,110 for our preschool. She is going to
apply for the next 2 phases planned (About $20,000 to $25,000 each).
Patty, Pat, Mandy, and I worked on gathering information and submitting for a
T-Mobil grant in the amount of $50,000 for a phase 1 Memorial Field renovation.
The focus is on the entryway building for now.
Effective March 1st, 2022 we are going to change our gym membership fees to a
single rate for both Village residents and non-Village residents. We hope that
by lowering the fees for non-residents we can pickup more participants &
memberships.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
Plant operations are running at fully acceptable levels.
We have a signed contract with Insituform for the Market Street and Sundry
sewer lining project. We should start soon as the weather improves.
Police:
Police Cruisers: I received an email from our rep. at USDA. They are not able
to finance the 2 vehicles that we applied for this year. However, our
application doesn’t lose its place in line to be funded in the future.
DC Dumperth has obtained $3,160 grant to pay for police training.
Fire:
Chief Lachey has obtained a reimbursement training grant in the amount of $900.
He is also working on several other grant applications.
Other Items:
We continue to ask all departments to be mindful of all non-essential expenses
and we are trying to keep overtime to a minimum.
Mayor Diehl is working on our new website. Thank you Brian!
LCP has been doing some work at the old stone container building. They are in
the process of finalizing a village sewer tap application. Work in progress and
moving forward.
Patty has applied for 2 NOPEC grants. The first one is for music and movies in
the park for $3,000 and the second is for energy efficient upgrades in the
amount of $8,228.

Mayor
Memo on Executive Sessions
Date: 03/07/2022
To: Members of Council
Re: Executive Sessions
Members of council,
In my years on council prior to 2021, executive sessions were a rare
occurrence, and were focused on serious issues affecting the Village – land
purchases, legal issues, and serious personnel issues. Since the start of 2022,
a total of five executive sessions have been held, including one special
session outside of the regularly scheduled council meetings, totaling nearly 8-
1/2 hours of council time outside of public view. These are listed below.
1/18/22
7:46PM – 9:37PM
ACTION - Approval of Deputy Chief removal from probation
2/7/22
7:49PM – 9:33PM
NO ACTION
2/22/22
7:51PM – 8:14PM
NO ACTION – Presentation of follow up information from 2/7 ES
8:15PM – 9:52PM
ACTION - Tabled Mayor’s recommendation regarding Officer Nelling and Officer
Pierce
2/28/22
Special Meeting   
5:31PM – 8:23PM
ACTION - Approved Mayor’s recommendation regarding Officer Nelling and Officer
Pierce
All of these sessions have either resulted in no action, or approval of the
recommendations that were presented in the public portions of the meeting.
I am writing to remind council that the use of the executive session should be
infrequent, and serious consideration should be given to public perception
relating to closed door meetings. Given that none of the information discussed
can be shared with the public, this can lead the public to believe that there
are nefarious motivations behind keeping discussion outside of public view,
especially given the length, frequency, and that the outcomes of each have
resulted in status quo action on the motions published on the agenda.
While there is a purpose and need to use the ES from time to time, I ask that
moving forward, you give serious consideration to the motivations behind these
sessions and how the use of them reflects on public perception of our local
government.
Thank you,
Mayor Brian Diehl

medical insurance and the increase in wages? Also felt the Pat Bradek and
Rhonda Stiles should have been asked first if they wanted the position. When
Pat Bradek was hired, she did not want the Medical Insurance or to be put on
payroll. Pat Bradek has been in the position for six year and has always had a
positive attitude. Brabender was concerned the Pat Bradek and Rhonda Stile did
not have the opportunity or enough time to apply for the position. Brabender
asked who does the postings and why was the posting done internally and
externally at the same time. Why was the internally posting not done. Brabender
stated that Rhonda Stile applied for the job but did not get it. She has worked
hard for the Village for years. She did get a letter stating someone else got
the job. We are in a small Community, (human factor). Brabender told Council

Council if they would table the vote.

Councilperson Szewczyk asked the Mayor question regarding the interview Process
for the Fulltime position at the Police Department.
In his memo that he read he stated It seems that in past practices the
Chairman of the Safety Committee  was always
part of the interviewee process for Jefferson Police Department. You stated in
an email dated March 23, 2022, at 6:03pm
"The Deputy Chief and I will be interviewing Jeremiah Polz for the full-time
position and another candidate for a part time position later this week. Since
these are non-supervisory positions; they will not be panel interviews. If
there is
anything in particular you would like us to ask or discuss with the candidates,
please share your questions via email."
Councilman Orvos and I supplied you with questions and this morning you
returned to us a vague response. Then, in this week's Council packet your Memo
to Council states that you did create a panel for the interview process and
added Sgt Nelling to the panel. In past practices the Safety Committee chair
was involved.
May I ask you why you choose to exclude me or Councilman Orvos from this
process and replace one of us with Sergeant Nelling?
Shouldn't this be part of the due diligence that I'm entrusted with?
You brought this in front of Council tonight for a vote.
How can I 'VOTE' on something that I was not made a part of and for which I
received 'NO' answers to the questions that you asked me to provide.
Considering this, I have no option but to ask council to table your
Recommendations.
Mayor Diehl told Council that the scheduled meeting was the Deputy Chief and
myself. Sargeant Nelling just happened to be there when the interview was being
started and I did not feel it was a problem to have him at the interview.
Mayor Diehl also told Council that the hiring for a supervisory role we have
had a panel in the past. Diehl also stated the hiring falls on the
responsibility of the executive branch.
Councilperson Szewczyk stated that in past practices Councilperson Rick Hoyson
Was always part of the hiring process. He said he understands that this is new
time and a new Mayor.
Councilperson Szewczyk asked the Mayor why don't you want me to participate  
in this process? Is it because myself or Councilman   Orvos could be asking
uncomfortable questions in pursuit of identifying the 'Best' interests of the
Village?
Mayor Diehl told Council the Councilperson Szewczyk was reading more into it.
He told everyone he was impressed with both candidates and the recommendation
is coming from Mayor.
Councilperson Szewczyk asked Council to bail the recommendation to a later date
to answer some if his question and bring the recommendation forward at next
meeting.
Councilperson Damon said he feels very uncomfortable about all of this.
Councilperson Szewczyk stated that he had some questions and concerns he wanted
to ask the candidates.
Mayor Diehl told Council he would not change the process if he had to do it
again and his recommendation will not change.
Deputy Chief Dumperth told Council he had no other candidates for the position.

Mayor Diehl asked Council if they wanted his memo read publicly Council agreed

Memo
Date: 04/18/22
To: Members of Council
Re: Memo re: Administrator Memo
Members of Council,
Earlier today you received an email from Administrator Martuccio which I feel
requires a response.
First and foremost, I fundamentally support and respect the jobs of law
enforcement, fire, and first responders. The safety and protection of this
Village is my first priority and I will not waiver in this. This involves both
supporting the police in their work, and working with the Deputy Chief to
identify opportunities for improvement.
Secondly, myself, the Administrator, council are required to perform our duties
in the best interests of the Village residents.
The discussion that the Administrator and I had on April 14 that was shared
with you arose out of those two fundamental concepts. The Administrator was
made aware of an issue on April 6th involving the JPD and failed to contact me,
taking it upon himself to investigate with only partial facts. When I expressed
my concern and reminded him of the chain of command as written in the Village
Ordinance, he replied that he cannot trust me to act appropriately with matters
regarding the police department and he would continue to conceal information if
he felt it was necessary. He refused to acknowledge that not informing me of a
potentially serious issue regarding the PD was a violation of the chain of
command. (Note that an external investigation revealed no wrongdoing in this
subject matter and the investigation is closed).
The conversation escalated from there. I will admit that the conversation was
heated, I was out of line and unprofessional, and for that I apologize to the
Administrator, Council, and Village staff.
However, there is for reasons unknown to me, there is an appearance of a
coordinated effort by the Administrator and a handful of council members to
actively work against the Police Department. I recognized tension between
various departments at the beginning of this year, and asked all parties for
time for me to work through it, and for them to put forth significant effort to
work together and operate in the best interests of the Village.
This has not happened, and disappointingly these issues seem to most often
originate from the Administrator.
The Clerk Treasurer has stated to me that on several occasions this year she
has had to remind the Administrator to focus on his departments and stop
looking for problems with the police, reminding him that I had asked for the
departments to start fresh and work together.
Imagine my shock when one of the first tasks I had to contend with was a
discussion in the safety and finance meetings about reducing police department
staffing. Defunding the police is not something I support, and will not support
in the future. This was initiated by the administrator in a letter to the
committee prior to the meeting.
Further examples of actions against the police department include:
On June 21, 2021, the Administrator requested quotes from the Sheriff’s
department to determine the cost of coverage if the Village PD were to be
eliminated.
Resistance to the removal of the Deputy Chief from probationary status, despite
a recommendation by the previous Mayor.
Resistance to the removal of Sergeant Nelling from probationary status, despite
my recommendation.
Resistance to hiring of Officer Jeremiah Polz, despite good qualifications, and
a demonstrated work history to train with the department, and my
recommendation.
Resistance to hiring Officer Jeremy Cusano, despite my recommendation.
And other items I cannot discuss due to executive session confidentiality.
In the Administrators own memo he states that “a train is headed your way and
you can’t or won’t see it” but when pressed for specifics in our discussion,
was unable to provide any. I have legitimately no idea what he was talking
about.
All of these item’s stem from actions or accusations originating from the
Administrator and a handful of council persons. No other department in the
Village has had to contend with this constant barrage. In fact, hiring and
promotion of every other employee during this same time period has progressed
without question.
The Administrator implored me to “clean house” in the police department shortly
after taking office this year. I entered this role with a fair and impartial
view on all departments and will continue to do so. Nothing I have observed
regarding the PD would justify “cleaning house”.
I will address some specific comments in the administrator’s letter. He stated
that I made a comment about not losing. What he failed to mention is that I
stated that I would not take on a challenge unless I had my facts in order and
was on the right side of the argument. In all challenges to date against the
police department, I have ensured that I diligently investigated each issue,
and this is demonstrated by the eventual outcome supported by council.
He also comments that I stated putting Council persons Szewczyk and Orvos on
the safety committee was the worst mistake I have made and that I would correct
that in the following year. I stand behind this comment as I was unaware of the
deep anti-policing bias with these two individuals.
After council approved of the removal of the Deputy Chief from probation, and
after I had the solicitor review sunshine laws in council, the Administrator
asked Councilman Orvos in the hallway if he was ok as he seemed irritated. The
councilman responded that he was not, disappointed that he couldn’t have side
discussions outside of public view. He also expressed disappointment that he
was forced into a vote regarding the Deputy Chief, stating “now we’re stuck
with this monster”. This phrase still rings in my head as I’ve wondered how he
could make such a determination.
Council rules permit the mayor to reassign committee membership at any time and
I am giving this serious consideration.
I am asked to be neutral, but in the very first paragraph the Administrator
states that what I decide to do will show where I stand, trying to force me to
take a position. The fact is, that even after this, I will continue to be
neutral and operate with the best interest of the Village residents in mind,
looking at each issue presented to me on a case-by-case basis.
I was angry in our discussion. But at some point, when it becomes clear that
members of Village Administration are working against the best interests of the
Village, concealing information from elected officials, and fail to recognize
the issue with that, I needed to ensure the message that this was unacceptable
was clear.
It should be noted in conclusion that I fundamentally believe that the
Administrator is good for the Village and does excellent work with regard to
areas under his responsibility.
Mayor Brian Diehl
Attached at the end of the minutes are the redacted Police Report and the
redacted Administrator Report.

daughter to suspend any discussion on the matter.

Memorandum of Concern
To: Fro: CC:
DatRe: 
Mayor Brian
Diehl Councilman John Szewczyk Jefferson Village Council 26 February 2022
Personal attacks on council members; Unbiases of Managerial Oversight of
 Jefferson Police Department
Comments: Decline to enforce policies and ordinances of Jefferson Police
Department, Influence council members through discrediting of other council
members, The use of clout and personal bias to persuade Village Council of
personal  agenda.
Dear Mayor Diehl,
Ensuing councils last meeting and the events that took place, I feel obligated to point out some concerns from that evening meeting.
The items in question were on the procedural aspects of the Jefferson Police
Department (JPD). This has not been the only instance of concern referencing
JPD, where your
focus has been to downplay the concerns. These instances include half-
truths to the public, mis­ reptation during hiring practices, misuse of JPD
equipment for personal use, unauthorized use of JPD equipment, with holding
personnel information and creating a department of non-accountability.
Your response to these incidences is 'they were generated in the past and need
to be let go'. Through your own admission you do not know anything about
law enforcement but consider yourself an expert in managing. Unfortunately,
this leaves you venerable to mis-guided
information on practices and policy that you oversee. Why is this important
because you were trying to divert attention away from JPD and single
out myself and Councilman Orvos.
It appears that Councilman Orvos and I are obstacles to how you like the JPD to
look in the future. You even stated the future placement of a chief. Regardless
of the deficient inabilities of the current leadership in that department and
by your own words 'not that smart'. Let me be clear and concise that our jobs
as Council is to do the checks and balances for the Village residences. The
fact that some people personally like a
person should not be a factor in career progression. Does that person have the knowledge, skills, and ability to handle all aspects of a certain position. This will be debated in the future.
The subject matter of the meeting was not me and yet your personal attacks to discredit, dismiss and cast doubt about me by stating 'you
had heard awful, awful thing'. I would like to remind you to be careful and
look in a mirror first. This strategy was an attempt to divide and conquer
approach was to influence other members of council. For the record, when you
were on council you praised my questions about matters of concern.
The expression you used was 'You go John!' to signify that I was not afraid to stand for what I believed. This is how I work; it's called closing the loop. I check dates,
times, signatures and supporting documents to everything. I don't rubber stamp
things and I will look into everything because some information can be
manipulated, and I don't assume anything. Your attacks on me and your direct,
repeated question to Councilman Orvos 'what do you want me to do?' brings into
question your ability to evaluate, be objective and impartial in managing
the JPD.
It is both sad and disappointing to think that pur NEW leader would stoop down
to this level so fast to push his agenda. Your actions reflect your prejudice
towards me and anything I might think or say. You are choosing to ignore
documented or material facts, ignoring different ideas, approaches and
experiences and most discouraging
different viewpoints which you try to discredit. All because they don't support your wishes.
Honestly, I am having a hard time understanding why you are making certain
choices when it comes to the JPD. Why are you downplaying and
condoning certain behaviors that are clearly not acceptable? If the Village
Residents knew everything that has been discovered, do you think they would
appreciate 'Let it Go' mentality? This is not what I expected from our new
leader of the Village. I thought the days of withholding information from
council, turning a blind eye, and rubber-stamping things were in
the past. To this day, you have failed to produce any concrete
evidence of certain matters that you claim to have investigated. Your
explanation was unsatisfactory and inconclusive findings. The time has come to
stop accepting excuses, denial of knowledge, victim mentality and counter
accusations for short comings as justification for improper
conduct and breaking Village ordinances.
I hope once this all air's out that you and I can concentrate, communicate, and
move forward for the betterment of the Village. All I expect is transparency,
accountability, and  standards.

Street Dept.  
Operating normal tasks.
We have truck #22 in the shop for repairs. We hope to replace this truck with a
new one once we find one.
We are looking into fixing Falcon Way. Working on engineering.
Our crews have picked up 40 Hot Wings Maple trees and 2 Flowering Pears to be
planted throughout the Village in the next couple of weeks.
I have a resolution with emergency language for the purchase of a Kobelco SK35
Mini Excavator. This piece of equipment will be very useful for sidewalk
replacement, storm, and utility work. We should move quicky on this purchase
because of the supply chain issues and equipment availability. (see attached
quote)
This particular unit has arrived at the dealership, and they are just waiting
for some of the attachments before it would be available for delivery.
After some extensive research we feel that we have found the most appropriate
equipment to be used for sidewalk snow removal and for mowing large open areas
like our parks. I have a resolution for the purchase of a Steiner 450 and
attachments. The resolution has the emergency language for the same reasons I
just mentioned about the Kobelco purchase. Delivery for this tractor is
expected for June 2022 (see attached quote).
Brobst was in town and started grinding the tree stumps left from last year.
They will be back to complete the job as soon as the ground dries up.
Recreation Department:
Operating normally.
We are working on getting estimates for the installation of automatic dusk-to-
dawn gates for East Park (dog park). We have confirmed with NOPEC that they are
willing to finance this project. We would have to front the expenses and submit
to NOPEC for 100% reimbursement.
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
Plant operations are running at fully acceptable levels.
The Market Street and Sundry sewer lining project has started. They are now
cleaning and televising the main lines in preparation for relining.
Housel construction is making very good progress on the bridge replacement
project at the WWTP. New support walls and new bridge deck has been installed.

We continue to ask all departments to be mindful of all non-essential expenses
and we are trying to keep overtime to a minimum.

resolution for tonight’s meeting to authorize the Administrator to enter into

Clerk-Treasurer spoke to Council regarding Juneteenth Day. She stated that a
few employees had questioned if the Village was going to honor it. Fisher told
Council that some municipalities that she talked with are honoring it and some
other have not.
Solicitor Fairchild told Council that Juneteenth was made a federal holiday and
then subsequently a state holiday. However, it is the decision of Village
Council as to whether the Village wants to add Juneteenth to the already
recognized list of paid holidays for Village employees under Village Ordinance
§ 254.05(f). Just let me know if I need to prepare an ordinance to make that
change or not.
Councilperson Szewczyk told Council he is personally against Juneteenth, just
because it's radical reckoning against the Confederate and stuff. It's about
the history of the United States and I don't think that's right whatsoever. So
I am saying no, just looking at a on the internet quickly it says right there
it is a part of the American radical reckoning, which includes removals,
removal of statues of Confederate soldiers, no, because that's all part of
history. And I think today, especially in this Community here, we need to know
history. We need to learn from history we need not to repeat history
Solicitor Fairchild told Council the federal government declared it a federal
holiday. And the state of Ohio has or has not an Ordinance but has a statute
that incorporates all federal holidays as state holidays. State employees
celebrate this because of that statute, the Village Councils and other
municipalities it's really up to them as to whether or not you want to have had
it as a holiday Fairchild told Council that the General Assembly did pass a law
that's specific to school employees, it mandates only for certain types of
school employees but not for others based upon their length of employment. It
is entirely up to counsel whether you want to add this as a paid holiday for
employees.

Visitor’s Comments (five-minute limit per council rule #13)
Visitor’s Comments
Stan Zwaduk of 259 East Jefferson Street Jefferson spoke to Council about the
issues with the dog park. He told Council that something has to be done with
the dogs barking all the time. His house is right next to the dog park and it
is very disturbing hearing dogs. Zwaduk also spoke to Council about people
going into the park and staying after dusk. The gates are not put up and down
consistently in the morning or the evening.
Administrator Martuccio told Council that he is looking at gates that will be
dusk to dawn. This will help prevent people being in the park after hours.
Cayce Baxley of 245 East Jefferson Street thanked Administrator Martuccio for
coming down to the Senior Center and calming down all the Seniors with the
confusion of the Village Table meal site. Baxley also thanked the Village
Streets Department for all the help setting up the garden sale again.
Terry Wolcott of 326A Woodland Way talked to Council with the issues on
Woodland Way Road. It was to the understanding that Woodland Way Road was
dedicated to the Village. With the Road being dedicated that would mean the
Village would take care of the roads. But recently have been told differently.
Administrator Martuccio told Council that the Village in the past helped plowed
the road to help out with the snow.
Administrator Martuccio told Council a Building Lands meeting need to be set up
to resolve the issues with Woodland Way.
Also present:  
Stephanie Wessell of the Gazette, Jake Morgan, Josh Lewis, Ken Fertig, Cayce
Baxley, Stan Zwaduk, Terry Wolcott, Riley Wood, Kaycee Saari, Patrich Beebe and
Reed Edgar

Street Dept. 
   Operating normal tasks.    
   We are looking into fixing Falcon Way. Working on engineering.   
   Our crews have picked up and planted 40 Hot Wings Maple trees and 2
Flowering Pears.   
   The Kobelco SK35 Mini Excavator should be ready to be delivered
tomorrow.    
   I have submitted the order for the Steiner 450 and attachments. I’m waiting
on the dealer to advise on a possible delivery date. Unfortunately, it might
take longer than originally anticipated since the city of Dayton just purchased
5 of the very same tractor we are looking at buying. I will keep council
informed on possible developments moving forward.   
   Brobst was in town and completed the grinding of all tree stumps left from
last year.    
Recreation Department:
   Operating normally.   
   We are working with Thomas Fence on planning installation of 2 automatic
gates for the dog park. NOPEC is willing to finance this project. We would have
to front the expenses and submit to NOPEC for 100% reimbursement.    
   I would like to recommend hiring Alicia Morgan and Katelyn Cross for the 2
Part-Time job openings at the Rec. Center. Please see attached memos for
details.    
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
   Plant operations are running at fully acceptable levels.   
   The Market Street and Sundry sewer lining project is progressing. They have
completed the cleaning and televising. The actual lining is next.   
   Housel construction has pretty much completed the bridge replacement project
at the WWTP.   
Police:
Fire:
Other Items:
   We continue to ask all departments to be mindful of all non-essential
expenses and we are trying to keep overtime to a minimum.   
   Working with Waste Management on drafting a contact for the next 5
years.

Street Dept. 
   Operating normal tasks.    
   We are looking into fixing Falcon Way. Working on engineering.   
   Working on crack sealing.   
   Rotary installed all dog bag dispensing stations.   
   Working on fixing a collapsed storm pipe on West Beech.   
   Cleaning and leveling playground areas in preparation for mulch.   
Recreation Department:
   Operating normally.   
   We are working with Thomas Fence on planning installation of 2 automatic
gates for the dog park. NOPEC is willing to finance this project. We would have
to front the expenses and submit to NOPEC for 100% reimbursement.    
   I’m please to announce that starting June 6th until July 29th, our Rec
Center and Country Neighbor are going to be offering free lunches to kids ages
1-18. Thank you, Katie Sweeney, for working on this project. See flyer for
details.     
   Also, in the months of June & July, we are having music in the park.
Jefferson Summer Concert Series 2022 consists of 6 nights of music at Giddings
Park. The events are free, and the dates are June 2nd, June 16th ,June 23rd,
July 7th, July 14th and July 21st. See flyer for details.   
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
   Plant operations are running at fully acceptable levels.   
   The Market Street and Sundry sewer lining project is progressing. They have
completed the cleaning and televising. The actual lining is set to start 6/29/
22.    
   Housel construction has completed the bridge replacement project at the
WWTP.   
   We have submitted a pre-app to OPWC for needed upgrades at the WWTP.
Concrete work and renovation of one clarifier will be part of the Phase I
submission.   
Police:
   Would like to thank DC Dumperth and JPD for helping with our efforts to
speak with residents with tall grass/junk cars violations. It seams like this
year, more than ever, we have several properties that are not being maintained
properly. We will be doing as much as possible to address these issues in the
coming weeks.   
Fire:
Other Items:
   We continue to ask all departments to be mindful of all non-essential
expenses and we are trying to keep overtime to a minimum.   
   Working with Waste Management on drafting a contact for the next 5
years.    
   We have sent out Tall Grass letters. Many complied and a few more need
work.

Visitor’s Comments (five-minute limit per council rule #13)
Visitor’s Comments
Citizen Chip Ashcraft of Jefferson Township read to Council a letter he had
sent to them in an email.
Jefferson Police Department
It has come to my attention that recent incidents involving members of the
Jefferson Police Department and the manner in which they have conducted
themselves and handled these incidents are, to say the least, concerning. As a
lifelong resident of the Jefferson area, and a past/present business owner in
Jefferson Village, these incidents need to be addressed rather than ignored.
The initial incident in which I am referring to, and those that follow, date
back to February 15, 2022, in which Deputy Chief Aaron Dumperth sent a
patrolman from the Jefferson Police Department to the Jefferson Area Junior
High Gym Class to watch Deputy Chief Dumperth’s daughter to make sure she does
not get bullied or harassed. (Information obtained through Administrator
Martuccio’s correspondence with Mayor Diehl) Please keep in mind, at this time,
no complaint or police report had been filed, so why is Deputy Chief Dumperth
ordering a patrolman to go look after his daughter? How is this not seen as a
gross overstep of power by Deputy Chief Dumperth?
Also, at this time, nor at any time after, did the school’s gym class teacher,
Junior High Principal, School Resource Officer contact the Jefferson Police
Department regarding an issue or request assistance from the Jefferson Police
Department. (Information obtained through ACSO incident #22-05219) In summary,
not a single person from the school requested assistance from the Jefferson
Police Department but Deputy Chief Dumperth ordered a patrolman to go there.
March 2, 2022 – Two weeks after Chief Deputy Dumperth orders a patrolman to
“look after his daughter” at Jefferson Junior High, Tina Dumperth (wife of
Deputy Chief Aaron Dumperth), and their daughter file a complaint with the
Jefferson Police Department citing sexual harassment & bullying alleged to be
taking place at the school.
A couple of red flags that arose in examining this complaint/report:
Is there record of a call log from Tina Dumperth requesting to meet with an
officer from JPD to file a complaint?
Why is the complaint submitted from Tina Dumperth (or at least the copy in the
police report that she signed) typed and not handwritten, and why is it not on
a JPD statement form?
To date, the school had not made contact or request for assistance to JPD
regarding any type of behavior described in the complaint
March 2, 2022 – After taking the complaint from Tina Dumperth regarding sexual
harassment & bullying accusations at Jefferson Area Junior High, Sgt. Brandon
Nelling conducted follow up on the complaint at the home of Joshua & Rachel
Lewis. Per Sgt. Nelling’s report, he advised Joshua Lewis of the nature of the
complaint from Tina Dumperth, which named their son as the “suspect.” The
parents agreed to let Sgt. Nelling speak with their son, on the front porch of
their home, regarding the allegations, but from there the actions of Sgt.
Nelling seem to become questionable.
Sgt. Nelling places handcuffs, on a 13-year-old boy, and escorts him to his
patrol unit
Sgt. Nelling questions the juvenile in his patrol unit without his parents
present Sgt. Nelling, in his interrogation tactics, repeatedly uses the term
“Suck my balls” to the juvenile
After the interrogation of the juvenile, Sgt. Nelling tells Joshua & Rachel
Lewis that “it is because of kids like _____ that cause school shootings”
It is of my opinion that this type of behavior shown by Sgt. Nelling is
unacceptable and unforgivable. Let’s take a minute and look at the big picture
in this whole scenario.
Deputy Chief Aaron Dumperth orders a patrolman, under his authority, to go
“look after his daughter” at a public school while on village time.
Not one individual, not a teacher, not the principal, not the SRO, contacted
the Jefferson Police Department and asked for assistance regarding a situation
between Deputy Chief Dumperth’s daughter and another student or students
Deputy Chief Dumperth “recuses” himself from the incident but sends his
Sergeant Brandon Nelling to do follow up with the Lewis juvenile. Keeping in
mind that Deputy Chief Dumperth claims the Sgt. Nelling to be “my very best
friend” and “Uncle Brandon” to Deputy Chief Dumperth’s children. If that is not
a justified case of conflict of interest, I’m not sure what would constitute
one.
Sgt. Nelling, after taking the complaint from Tina Dumperth does no additional
follow up aside from arriving at the Lewis home and interrogating their
juvenile son.
o One would think that the proper investigative process would be to first go to
the school, speak with the teacher in who’s class this harassment and bullying
was alleged to have happened.
o Speak with the Principal of the Junior High School to determine if/what had
transpired
o Discuss the complaint with the School Resource Officer and determine if he
was aware and/or involved in any of these alleged incidents o Upon arrival at
the Lewis’ home, take the time to speak with Joshua & Rachel Lewis regarding
the complaint and give them an opportunity to respond and provide information
to combat the allegations if they had it, instead of using what was termed as a
“Scare Tactic” to coerce information from a juvenile.
Repeated request from the Joshua Lewis for body cam footage from March 2, 2022,
from Deputy Chief Aaron Dumperth, Sgt. Brandon Nelling, and the “ride along”
Sgt. Nelling had with him at the Lewis’ home. These requests have been denied
from the village stating they cannot be released because it contains juvenile
information, but the juvenile in the footage they are asking for is their own
child.
  And last, but surely not least…. There was NO CRIME committed to constitute
the actions of Deputy Chief Dumperth to order a patrolman to the Jefferson
Junior High School, and nothing to constitute handcuffing a 13 year old child,
placing him in your patrol unit and using “Scare Tactics” and telling him
repeatedly to “Suck my balls” to coerce some type of plea of guilt.
I have reviewed the reports submitted by Lt. Steve Murphy of the Ashtabula
County Sheriff’s Office, Sgt. Brandon Nelling of the Jefferson Police
Department, and several correspondence documents between Jefferson Village
government officials and council. Although I realize that the report from LT.
Murphy states that no criminal activity was committed, but it doesn’t take a
judge or lawyer to understand ethics and inappropriate behavior in those
empowered at the Jefferson Police Department who were involved in this
situation.
I completely understand looking out for your children and doing whatever you
can to protect them, but this incident is a direct overstep of power by Deputy
Chief Dumperth and Sgt. Nelling and shows a complete lack of integrity in the
leadership at the Jefferson Police Department.
I look forward to hearing the input and opinion on this situation from every
councilmember and Mayor Diehl at the upcoming July 5th Council Meeting.
Respectfully Submitted,
Chip Ashcraft
Citizen Chip Ashcraft then looked at all of Council and asked them how they
would feel if a two-hundred-pound individual handcuffed your son put him in the

is unacceptable.

this will never happen again? That is all I am asking.
Solicitor Fairchild advised Council again statements made can be used against
Council. My advice is not to speak and limit what you say about the situation.
Citizen Tina Dumperth wife of Aaron Dumperth told Council that she has gone to
the school about the harassment to her daughter from the Lewis child. That she
had asked to talk to principal Hoyson. He was not available. She then asked
that the school resource officer sit in the gym class so her daughter would be
safe. No one from the school called her. Dumperth told Council that her
daughter does not deserve to be the victim of constant sexual harassment,
disgusting comments and telling her to suck his ball and feel his balls. Is
that acceptable? Dumperth told Council that because of all this she has taken
her children out of Jefferson School and has no intentions of putting them in
the Jefferson School district next year. Dumperth told Council that the school
never documented anything. So that is why she went to the Police Department to
have the whole situation documented.
Citizen Andrew Dumperth spoke to Council that enough is enough and bullying is
ok from what Chip Ashcraft wrote. That is what I am getting out of all of this.
He told Council that bullying is being done all the time to children at the

Citizen Chip Ashcraft told Council that in his letter he did not condone

Citizen Josh Lewis spoke to Council and said he has been attending the Council
meeting regularly to see if any punishment will be handed down to Officer
Nelling. He states he is in complete shock not a single word is mentioned. And
how serious the situation was and now it has disappeared like nothing happened.
Seems the Mayor is satisfied with the verbal warning that Deputy Chief Dumperth
gave Officer Nelling. I am not satisfied and a lot of the residents in this
town are not satisfied. At the very least this is a fireable offense. Someone
must be accountable for these actions. Officer Nelling should have never come
to our house and he should have never let us believe he went to the school.
Lewis told Council he should have never let him speak to his son. It is strange
how fast he showed up at our home once the complaint was filed. No
investigation was done he did not even go to the school and talk with the
principal. Looking at the times stamps of the report he was at our house before
the ink was dry. I just hope if I ever need the assistance of the Jefferson
Police Department, they will come that fast. There is no doubt in my mind that
this was premeditated. Officer Nelling’s only objective was to come to my house
to intimidate my son. Why did he not ask the hear my son’s side of the story?
He had already had his mind made up. He did not let him tell his side of the
story. Officer Nelling would not let me tell him my side of the story or say
some of these things this girl did to my son. He continued to ask him the same
question over and over. When he did not get the answers, he wanted, he
handcuffed him and put him in the back of his cruiser and interrogated him more
and told him to suck his balls. When he was done, he came up to me and told me
it is because of kids like my son is what causes school shootings. Bottom line
is laws were broken and rights were violated. Deputy Chief Dumperth said he
recused himself from the situation. Why did Officer Nelling, his best friend,
not recuse himself. Deputy Chief Dumperth children call Officer Nelling Uncle
Brandon. So how can he be objective. I hope this situation gets revisited and
the Mayor will let Council have some say. I know this is trying to be swept
under the rug and go away. I hope this would have been handled internally. Many
other parents have come forward and saying how Deputy Chief Dumperth’s daughter
has been abusive to their child. They did not want to get involved because they
feel intimidated because the child’s father is a police officer. Inclosing I
just want everyone to know we are not out to get the Police Department. We
support the Police Department. But our family does not support this kind of
abuse. Where were or sons’ rights through all of this?

Street Dept. 
   Operating normal tasks.    
   We are working on fixing Falcon Way.   
   We completed fixing a collapsed storm pipe on West Beech.    
   Playground received a much-needed facelift with repairs, painting, and new
mulch. A big thanks to those that helped with this project.   
   Blaze Burr has completed his 6-month probation as Equipment Operator for
Streets effective 06/27/2022. Need a motion to end his probation.   
Recreation Department:
   Operating normally.   
   Thomas Fence has completed the installation of two automatic gates for the
dog park. The gates are set to open at dawn and close at dusk.   
   Also, in the months of June & July, we are having music in the park.
Jefferson Summer Concert Series 2022 consists of 6 nights of music at Giddings
Park. The events are free, and the dates are June 2nd, June 16th, June 23rd,
July 7th, July 14th, and July 21st.    
   Katie and Alicia have organized a series of movies in the park. There will
be three events this summer with the first one scheduled for July 8th at dusk.
Admission is free. I would like to thank Jake Morgan and Molded Fiberglass for
making this possible. Please see flyer for details.    
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
   Plant operations are running at fully acceptable levels.   
   The Market Street and Sundry sewer lining project is progressing. They have
completed the cleaning and televising. The actual lining was set to start 6/29/
22 but, because of subcontractor issues, we had to postpone starting in a week
or so.

Resident Todd Mullen of Jefferson spoke to Council stating he does not know all
the parties involved of what is going on. Mullen told Council he has known the
Dumperth family for a long time. He stated he does not know the Lewis family,

everyone in front of us because they are not getting what they want. They are
not getting transparency. Everyone here tonight has not gotten a resolution and
do not think things were managed right. It is not happening, and they deserve
it.
Resident Todd Mullen told Solicitor Fairchild that he was extremely
disappointed in him. Jefferson is a small Village where everyone knows
everyone. We should be able to sit and talk things out. Council is not
commenting since you advised them not to. We are transparent everything should
be on the table. Everyone should have the access and the ability to get things
done and have a good solid Village.
Resident Todd Mullen told Council if mistakes were made, and someone
overstepped their bounds they should be reprimanded. And if they did not there
should not be a reprimand. But at least all the information should be made
available, so everyone understand why the decision was made. Not just closed
lips and everyone questioning what happened. Not have all these horrible
meetings where everyone voices their opinions and they get nothing back, that
is not right. This is a small town and where people do not have to lock their
doors and walk around town. The last thing this town needs is this what is
happening. The town needs leadership and transparency, those are the things
that is expected. This is more of a school issue. But it does seem like it is
being swept under the rug and if it is not talked about it will go away. There
are heated emotions on both sides. A lot of the people here tonight are not ok
with what is going on. This is not good for the Community, being a business
owner and a resident, this is not going in the right direction. We cannot have

mistakes were made talk about it fix the problem and move on.

Visitor’s Comments
Jake Rice of the Jefferson Emergency Rescue District spoke to Council in regard
to the Village of Jefferson to giving the Rescue District $16,098.00 ARPA Fund
to purchase a heart monitor referred as a LifePack-15. The County Commissioners
told the Rescue District if they could get the Village of Jefferson and the
Jefferson Township to donate $16098.00 from each entity the County would give
them $32,196.00. Jake explained to Council that the Jefferson Emergency Rescue
District does not qualify for any ARPA Funds because they are an Ambulance
District.

Mackensen, Warren Dillaway the Start Beacon, Frank Snyder, Thomas Ricker, Joe
Edison, and Jake Rice.

Street Dept. 
   Operating normal tasks.    
   I had a meeting with our County Engineer regarding the projects that we
submitted a pre-application for. Our Falcon Way project scored high meaning
that it has a very good chance of receiving final approval once that final
applications get submitted.    
   We are still completing crack-seal of E. Jefferson St in preparation for
paving. OPWC just activated this project. The paving plans have been completed
and we are currently advertising for bids. Bid opening is scheduled for Monday
August 29th at 11:00 AM. Once the bids get tabulated, I will need an emergency
resolution to award the job.   
Recreation Department:
   Operating normally.   
   Katie and Alicia have organized a series of movies in the park. The last
event had over 300 parents and kids attend. The next movie will be Sonic 2 on
August 19. Before the movie there will be a safety forces water war between the
kids and our safety forces. We hope for a hot day and loads of fun. I would
like to thank Jake Morgan and Molded Fiberglass for making this possible.
Please see Rec Center Facebook page for details.    
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
   Plant operations are running at fully acceptable levels.   
   The Market Street and Sundry sewer lining project is in progress.   
   We submitted a pre-application to OPWC to rehab our WWTP. The pre-app
received a good score to qualify for Small Government funding. More details
will be known once final application is made.   
Police:
Fire:
Other Items:
   We continue to ask all departments to be mindful of all non-essential
expenses and we are trying to keep overtime to a minimum.

resolution to award the job.   
   We are also advertising for bids on paving sections of S. Spruce, S.

scheduled for August 24th at 12:00 PM. Like the project above, once the bids
get tabulated, I will need an emergency resolution to award the job.   
   Our Steiner tractor is almost ready for delivery. We hope to have it within
2-3 weeks.   
   Chip and seal is scheduled to start at the end of August. We are going to
cover most all streets north of West Beech Street. This year we are going to

replacement, however, due to the lack of inventory, I’m having a hard time
finding something that would meet our needs.

Michael Roach of 132 East Jefferson Street said he is retired from the
Ashtabula County Sheriff’s Department. He spoke to Council in regards of hiring
the new Police Chief and the results from the way it was handled and results
that may occur. Mike Roach told Council that maybe a wage study should be done.
The Amount that is being paid is to the Village Chief and the amount being paid
to other Cities and Municipalities in Ashtabula County. Mike Roach asked
Council and the Mayor if they have ridden with the Police Department.
Mayor Diehl told Roach he has.
Councilperson Sekanina also told everyone that he has done ride alongs with the
Police Department.
Mike Roach went on to sat to Council; that out Police Department deal with
allot more than the bedroom Community. He told Council that one officer has had
another job offer and at least two more are looking. The Village has been a
training ground for Police Officer’s and Jefferson Police Department has never
felt the support of the Village Council. Roach told Council to go out and ride
with the patrolman and see what they do daily. The Village is a desirable
Village to live in. If the Police Department falls apart and we start having
some of the city issues in this small town. Roach said he does not know the new
Police Chief that the Village is hiring he did do some research and he does
have a lot of administrative background. The Deputy Chief Aaron Dumperth does
not have a lot of administrative background, but he does have extensive
training. Roach said that as a Police Chief he feels Aaron Dumperth would be
the best candidate. He said that if Aaron Dumperth does not get the Police
Chief position it would be a big mistake.

Safety
Motion by Councilperson Szewczyk to approve the recommendation from the Hiring
Committee to hire Christopher Mackensen as the Police Chief for the Village of
Jefferson starting at the rate of pay $59,592.75 per the wage Ordinance.
Upon completion of passing background check, drug screen and physical.
Councilperson Drier read a memo to Council about her feeling in hiring the new
Chief of Police.
Aaron Dumperth has been Deputy Chief for the past 14 months without acting
chief pay. My understand is that the candidate picked was primarily chosen
based on having more experience. When comparing the resumes and experience, you
see that Deputy Chief Dumperth has 12 years of experience, three years as
sergeant and 14 months as Deputy Chief. Sgt. Chris Mackensen has 16 years of
experience, it'll be 17 years in December of this year, not 18, 5.5 years as
sergeant and has served as acting chief on occasion. How does this justify as
more experience, or being more highly qualified? Furthermore, I cannot agree
with adding an additional member to our police department with a combined
salary and benefits package in the amount of $99,792.00, when we already have
someone successfully fulfilling the duties of this position,'' Dreier said.
.'Where is this money coming from" I would like to ask the Mayor, in the last
14 months, has Deputy Chief Dumperth given you any indication that he would not
be a good candidate for this position?''
Mayor Diehl told Council and the public. He did not know Deputy Chief that
well. I developed a relationship with Deputy Chief Dumperth. Last year in July
Council decided to move him into to the Deputy Chief position and give him a
year to develop to be Chief. Diehl told Council he has been a pleasure to work
with. He has done well in the role. Most of all he has a passion to serve and
protect the Village of Jefferson and develop relationships in the Community. A
hiring Committee was put together with myself. Councilperson Damon and
Sekanina. That decision process was not taken lightly. After the last interview
the committee was at the town hall until after midnight. In the end it was not
an easy choice. The Decision was decided by the committee to go with Chris
Mackensen base mostly on experience and supervisory time.
Mayor Diehl also told Council with experience and outside knowledge, hopefully
we will have a stronger force from this decision.
Councilperson Roderick asked the question as to what the Village is gaining
from hiring someone from the outside. Mackensen is coming from a town that is
very similar to ours.
Councilperson Sekanina told Council the Conneaut Ohio is not like Jefferson.
Conneaut the 27 square miles and Jefferson is about 3 miles. Conneaut has a
population of 13 thousand and Jefferson has a population of about 3 thousand.
Sekanina went on to tell Council in Conneaut a Sergeant man’s his own platoon.
Because they are much bigger and have a bigger Police force. He manages his
crew that is the same people the Deputy Chief manages here in Jefferson. He
also stated the he feels we are getting someone with allot of experience
managing the whole platoon. Mackensen is certified with FTO training. He brings
allot to the Village of Jefferson. Hopefully Deputy Chief Dumperth will stay on
as second in command and will have a strong department. Furthermore, the
Village has set a precedence. In the past David Wassie served as the Deputy
chief for years.
Councilperson Roderick asked Chris Mackensen why Jefferson.
Chris Mackensen told Council lots of reasons. We chose to move to Jefferson
three and half years ago to make Jefferson our home. We have set our roots in
Jefferson. We have a Ranch just outside of Jefferson. We spend a lot of time in
the Village we go to allot of events in the Village. It is a wonderful little
Village. We are invested in this Community. I come to the Council meetings to
find out what is going on in the Village not to get the job. I care about this
town. I know most of the people at the Police Department and I hope they stay.
I am coming in with a open mind. And hopefully open communication between the
department. It is not about the money. If I wanted money I would not be here. I
am vested in the Community, and I care about the Community.
Councilperson Roderick read a statement.
In today’s Society were accusations and miss communication can lead to ruin a
person’s reputation or career. Aaron Dumperth took an oath to protect and serve
our Community and he has never quit. That shows commitment and dedication to
the Community.
Councilperson Damon told Council that he tried to take a job at the Sheriff’s
Department. Please add that as record.
Mayor Diehl did tell Council that there is a Finance issue that must be
resolved. This position is not budgeted.
Councilperson Sekanina told Council we have a Finance Committee Meeting set up
to discuss it. The meeting is set up for September 19, 2022, at 6:00 p.m.
The new Chief needs to come on board and sit down with Council and see what he
needs and work with the Finance Committee and make a proper recommendation.
Mayor Diehl asked for Roll Call.
Damon yea, Dreier nay, Roderick nay, Sekanina yea, Szewczyk yea, Orvos yea.
Motion passes. Fours yea’s and two nays’

Mayor – Swearing in of Police Chief Chris Mackensen
Chief Chris Mackensen spoke to Council and all in attendance.
Let me start by thanking my family, friends, community members, and colleagues
who took time to come here and support me. Your presence means a lot to me.
I would like to specifically thank Mayor Brian Diehl and council members for
this opportunity and honor to lead this department.
As well as having the faith in me to do so.
I would also like to thank Deputy Chief Aaron Dumperth for his continued
dedication to the Village. I look forward to collaborating with him on
department and community needs.
 
I would like to thank my family for the support they have provided that has
enabled me to take on this role.
Anyone in law enforcement knows you cannot do this job successfully without the
support of your family. Whether it is the long hours, extra shifts, the numerus
missed holidays, family events, or birthdays over the years.
I am so fortunate to have such a supportive family. So, I thank; my wife,
Diana; my son, Sean who was unable to attend tonight; and my daughter, Sara.
Thank you for your continued support and encouragement.
 
As most of you know I have spent the last 15 of my 18 years in law enforcement
working in Conneaut.
Just over three years ago my family and I moved to the Jefferson area. Since
then, we have come to love and cherish this community.
Until a few months ago I had no plans on leaving Conneaut. Then a once in a
lifetime opportunity to become the Chief of Police in a community we live near
and spend so much time in became available. This is an opportunity I could not
just let pass by.
 
To all the members of the Jefferson Village Police Department and this
community:
∙    As I step into the role of chief, I bring to the department a few core
values which I hope will make every day enjoyable and rewarding not only for my
department members and staff, but also for the community, business owners, and
visitors to this beautiful village.
To the department I ask that you embrace change and not fear it.
You will find me to be direct, fair, and honest.
My commitment to you is this, if you do what is right, I will support you at
all cost. I will give you my best, and I expect that you give your best in
return.
We together will continue the work of community policing and community trust,
while striving to protect the integrity of this office with core values in
mind.
These values are:
   ∙    Professional accountability   
   ∙    Consistency   
   ∙    Community collaboration   
   ∙    And Transparency   
It is important that all of us come together not only as a department but as a
community to keep the Village of Jefferson a safe, friendly place to live and
work, as well as a destination attraction for visitors.
I cannot wait to get started and I am ready to serve the people of Jefferson
Village.
Thank you all so much.
