In the Village
 
Reminder of the Aqua watermain and waterline project is in progress. First
stage is above-groundwork with minimal disruption. Minor road closures and/or
detours will be needed throughout the project, which is going to last
approximately 8 weeks. We are currently in week 6 of the project.
 
 
Street Dept. 
 
They have been servicing stormwater drain basins. Checking the foundations and
correcting any water flow issues prior to the wet seasons.
 
There has been an increase this month in brush removal as well. Crews have been
busy clearing curbs sides of brush from residences. It should be noted, if your
brush is not collected promptly, please be mindful we do have other village
business and scheduled work to be completed with higher priority, but I assure
you that all brush will be picked up.
 
Assisted Wastewater crew in fixing a drain on Woodside, where Brightspeed
contracted services covered a drain and disturbed the runoff into the drain.
Brightspeed will be getting a bill for the work.
 
Zoning:
 
Permits issued since the last council meeting: 2
Total permits 2025 = 34
Recreation Department:
 
New ceiling tiles have been installed in banquet room.
 
Haunted Woods will be happening again this year. It is scheduled for October
10th and 11th from 6pm-9pm on both nights. I am asking those who attend to be
mindful of parking and please be extra careful with your children due to
increased traffic.
 
Trick or Treat will be October 25th from 4pm-6pm. The Fire Department will be
hosting a fundraiser, passing out candy and selling hot dogs as well.
 
Wastewater Treatment Plant:
 
Plant is running normal. No issues to report or new business to report.
 
Other notes:
 
I want to extend my sympathy to Colucci’s Pizza, Mr. Hero and Steven’s Coin
Laundry for the fire that occurred there in the early morning of September 3rd.
I am thankful no one was injured and hope those businesses can get back on
their feet soon. I stopped in and met with Mr. Colucci and offered to help in
any way that we are able.
 
I want to thank our Fire Dept. for their quick response and courageous efforts
to minimize damage. I spoke with Fire Chief Tom Lachey, who explained the fire
had about an hour and a half head start until emergency services were even
dispatched. Preliminary findings believe the fire started smoldering about 11:
30pm.
 
An Asbestos survey was completed on the Memorial Field restroom building.
Results of the test indicated Asbestos found in 4 areas of the structure. These
included caulking around windows and doors and ceiling panels. A Jefferson
company, Medico, has been contacted and are confident the remediation will be
routine and at minimal cost.
 
Lastly, the bid for the Village Street paving program was open for bid on the
12th. I have not received a bid yet and final cost should be expected this
week. Unfortunately, due to the program getting started later in the season
this year, I will be asking Council to approve this on an “Emergency Status”
due to the paving season coming to an end soon. I do not like pushing things
through like this unless it absolutely necessary. As soon as this information
is obtained, I will supply it to Council members immediately for review.
 
I also want to alert council I have received a Community Reinvestment Area
application for 337 Frayer Dr. Once the build is completed, I will have the
total amount for tax incentive and submit that application to the appropriate
entities.

Mayor
 
Mayor Chiacchiero read a letter for the appreciation of Thomas Lachey from the
Fire Department for his years of Service.
 
It is with the highest respect and gratitude that the Village of Jefferson
formally recognizes Fire Chief Tom Lachey for his 53 years of dedicated service
to the Jefferson Volunteer Fire Department, serving not only the Village of
Jefferson, but also the communities of Lenox Township and Jefferson Township.
Chief Lachey has exemplified the very best of leadership, sacrifice, and
unwavering commitment to public service. For more than five decades, he has
been a steady guardian of our community, answering the call at all hours, under
all circumstances, and always with the courage and honor that define the fire
service. His guidance has shaped generations of firefighters, instilling in
them the values of integrity, service, and brotherhood.
The legacy Chief Lachey leaves is not only measured in the countless
emergencies responded to or lives protected, but also in the example he has
set–an example of humility, perseverance, and extraordinary devotion to the
safety and well-being of others. His 53 years of service represent a lifetime
of sacrifice that has strengthened the very foundation of our community.
On behalf of the Village of Jefferson, Lenox Township, and Jefferson Township,
we extend our deepest appreciation to Fire Chief Tom Lachey. May his remarkable
career stand as an inspiration to all who follow, and may this commendation
serve as a lasting reminder of the impact of his service.
 
The next Village of Jefferson Council Meeting will be on Monday October 6,
2025.
